title: What I expected from a film named "Star Wars"
review: And did I ever! This was much better than Episode One. More action, good acting, and showed us just a sample of what is to come. The only flaw so to speak was the terrible one line gags involving C3PO. And some poor dialogue. With that aside, Episode Two was a blockbuster action film worthy of the name Star Wars. Much better effort this time Mr. Lucas. Let's hope Episode Three is even better, and brings together the story lines for the events to come. Rating 8/10

title: Utterly boring
review: I found this entire movie to be one of the most boring experiences of my life. The acting seemed forced and most of the plot was aimed towards the fanboy faction. The graphics were visually stunning but, overall they were to constant and blatant. Many of the scenes seemed to scream "hey look CGI, LOOK AT THE CGI", as though it was some how supposed to be able to draw your attention from the boring dialogue. The one scene seems to have Anakin spouting awful gothic poetry. I personally give this movie a three out of ten. There were a few action sequences i found enjoyable but for the most part the whole movie dragged along too slowly.

title: at least it's not episode I
review:
So i was skeptical, but it turned out pretty good. The action sequences were pretty cool to see, and parts that i thought would be stupid looked pretty cool. I liked this movie, i am surprised by how much i enjoyed it. I expected it to suck. Don't get me wrong. George lucas has no ear for dialogue and the scenes where people are talking are pretty rough because of it. Acting is bad in this movie for several reasons, ewan mcgregor is straight jacketed into an alec guiness impersonation. Everyone seems to have trouble working with the huge amounts of computer effects. It seems like no on really has any idea what is going on in the shot. Hayden Christensen would have been good, there is a scene where he starts to get angry, but unfortunately George Lucas lacks Cajones and doesn't show anakin skywalker go insane and kill a bunch of tuskan raiders. That would have been cool to see, but Lucas had to make it kid friendly and that hurt.

Also, the effects in the movie are way overdone. I read some where that it had a shooting schedule of 60 days, which i totally believe. The rest is computers. Maybe Lucas should ignore the computers and focus on people, his movie would have benefited from it. The effects kick butt though, so hey!

I did like this movie. Despite deficiencies in the script and acting and a dependence on computer graphics that rivaled robert downy JR.'s dependence on drugs, it has a great plot. Real confusing, pretty complex, rather impressive. And the abundant eye popping action sequences are cool. I gave it a 7/10, Jar Jar Binks still sucks though. He is only in it for a few minutes total.

title: Digital Projection
review:
I saw Ep2 at midnight on film then saw it today at a theater with digital projection. Holy cow! What a huge difference. The sound and clarity was unbelievable.

Now for the movie, I loved it. My only beef was the love story between Anakin and Padme. It was a little plastic and somewhat barf-conducive on the part of Anakin. Now if it did have chemistry those "comfortable" outfits Padme sports would've been more effective to me.

The thing I liked about Ep2 was the implications of it all. Before I saw it I was a little confused about Dooku's role but it all made sense in the end. Great way to weaken the federation! I love the part when they show what they were planning on building. Hint: they blow up 2 of them in The Trilogy.

See this film but do not expect this to feel like The Trilogy because it's not. These are the prequels...people need to remember that!!!

title: Redeems Phantom Menace
review:
Though little shallow in plot, it is what movies are supposed to be...ENTERTAINING. Which Phantom Menace wasn't. It is definately worth the wait and when you see the cast of "old friends" in this episode you are reminded of why you loved the orignal series.

DO GO AND SEE IT.

Jar Jar only has about 10 lines in it, and the twist with his character will almost make you like him....almost.

!!!!!!!SPOILER ALERT SPOILER ALERT!!!!!!!!!! Yoda kicks some severe @$$ in this one, which alone is worth admission just to watch him do so. You see why Yoda IS THE JEDI MASTER.

title: Briefly: different but better than Episode 1
review:
I just came back from one of the sneak-previews of Episode 2 here in Germany. Before I start, this: I generally hate dubbed versions of movies in English language although I'm German. I can't wait to have the possibility to watch it in the original language -although the dubbing team here in Germany did a really good job as far as sound quality is concerned. Back to the movie itself: Stunning special effects, brilliant sound, very good score (thanks to John Williams). After Episode 1 I honestly thought "With what can Lucas top this in the sequel as far as technical stuff is concerned?". Hmm, seems as if he could do it. The story(board) of this episode seems to be better than the one of the first. Although I liked Episode 1 I was a bit disappointed. Attack of the Clones was much more appealing to me. I think Lucas learned many things from The Phantom Menace. It seems as if he is on the right way to deliver a masterpiece in form of the final prequel.

I really can recommend this movie, a must not only for Star Wars fans. I give it a 9 out of 10.

title: Major Improvement Over Episode I
review: Thank god for all of us out there! Due to our over all displeasure with so many aspects of Episode I George Lucas has listened and delivered a true winner! An almost complete lack of Jar Jar Binks, increased action sequences, better acting and actors and most importantly a much better script. The film is not without its flaws, but never the less it is quite an achievment that all will enjoy. Personally I still feel that "A New Hope" and "The Empire Strikes Back" are superior but this film far supercedes "The Phantom Menace" and "Return Of The Jedi." With plotlines being carefully interwoven, loose ends being tightened up and new questions being raised I feel this feel will stand the test of time and prove that George Lucas has indeed not lost his touch. All he needed was to get back in the swing of things.

title: Mediocrity .. but better than Menace
review: After sitting through almost two and half hours of special effects I have gotten some new respect for Lucas.  Not for his overall storytelling which is mind-numbingly weak, but for his overall insistence on using special effects to sell the movie.  For parts of the movie, it is actually quite engrossing.  However, I was disappointed in the overall movie as I expected a much better effort following the disasterous Menace.  Anakin and Amidala do not come close matching the fire, the spark, the wit (basically everything) of Leia and Han and Anakin is actually quite a drab character overall.  Thankfully, Jar-Jar is an inconsequential bit-player in this movie and for that, we can all be thankful.  I would rate this movie a 'C' and going by the 1-10 scale .. a '5' is a fair value for the movie.  Not as dreadful as Menace .. but not as satisfying as the original trilogy.

title: Back in Form
review: With a somewhat bland opening scroll I thought I was going to be disappointed.   It sounded more like C-span than Star Wars.   Then there were the first lines of dialogue between Padme and her chief of security that sounded as wooden as a high school production of a comical whodunit. I sat with disgust in my plush stadium theater chair with 32 ounces of artificially flavored lemonade drink and thought that its insipid flavor might be the most enjoyable part of this experience.   Well, I was wrong! Yes, this movie has some faults that are easy to spot; they may even reach distracting and annoying to most fans of the Star Wars saga.  However the compelling action, visual artistry, and mythic scope of the original movie are back and pushed up to modern standards.   This isn't just Star Wars redone, but a Star Wars for those who came to the move to see the trailer for the new Matrix films.   What is the Matrix you ask? Yoda is the Matrix! Yes, as you probably know by now, Yoda is a bigger part of this film and the little green sprite shows why he is afforded so much respect. Lucas has made a film that will satisfy all his fans on some level.  Just remember when C3PO's highly annoying banter is making you hate what Lucas is doing, that the developmentally disabled guy next to me in the theater laughed his ass off.   C3PO will quickly go away for at least a few more scenes of glorious Jedi combat, or perhaps for the harsh moment that turns the heart of a little boy named Boba so ice cold.  When C3PO returns, or Jar-Jar, or whatever, just gloss it over and remember that it is not there for you.   The rest of the film is for you.    Stick to appreciating the parts you like and you will find this one of the most satisfying films in the series.  If you go into this film hating Lucas for Phantom Menace, then you will find faults and you will hate this film.  Just remember, had you never seen Menace, and if this had been the first film after more than a decade of waiting, that you would be singing Lucas's praises as the greatest producer ever. This film establishes several facets that the previous film failed to do. Most importantly is a couple of villains that are more than just the ugly and scary looking threat of Darth Maul.   Sure Maul looked cool, and his moves were a highlight of Menace, but he was just another Jedi warrior with no real character, no real sinister side, a real one-dimensional bad guy. Here we have both Jango Fett, and Count Dooku/ Darth Tyranus.   Jango is a proud father, a cunning warior, and a unique link to the original series. Count Dooku is a villain with charm who can cunningly use lies to seem to be a hero of sorts.   Not only that, but his skills as a dark Jedi seem greater than our young heroes can match.  In Menace we knew our hero's skills were greater than an inept trade federation, and even a more than fair match for Maul.  There was never any threat.   AOTC delivers threats that seems more dire and real. The next improvement is an Anakin that is just about perfect for his part. He is the essence of teenage hormones running amok and as rash and stupid as real teens are.    To adult fans of the series the quick, rash, and sometimes nonsensical romance between Anakin and Padme may seem stilted and false.   Just think back to when you were just learning to date and remember your own rash and nonsensical behavior as a rebellious teen. There is a bit (which would be a spoiler, I will just hint that one of Anakin's actions would probably wind up tried at a tribunal in The Hague) that seemed right for the development of Vader, but comes at a place in the movie where both the audience and Padme must gloss over it and still consider him a hero for the rest of the film. Finally we have a real increase in the wonder factor.    Menace gave us a muppety two-headed alien announcer that talked like ABC sportscasters, more of the same old Hutts, and an annoyingly earthbound, and downright offensive, patois spoken by Jar-Jar.  AOTC gives us a goul/insectoid run robot factory, a waterbound race of supermodel thin, globe-eyed scientists, and a capitol city/planet that takes off where Bladerunner left off.   To be fair, Naboo still looks too much like the renaissance Italy right down to a gondola, and Tatooine isn't exactly a stunningly original local. You still can't ask for much more wonder than an all-out land battle between Jedi, droids, clones, and fearsome alien gladiatorial beasts. All in all Star Wars fans should rejoice and enjoy a fine addition to the series.   If you find this film annoying and faulty, that perhaps you should sell your vacuum-sealed collection of mint in-package Star Wars action figures and go get a real life.

title: Not what I expected and it wasn't Jar-Jar's fault this time
review: Attack of the Clones is a little better than The Phantom Menace, but still does not even come close to the original trilogy.  Even Return of the Jedi was better overall.  I've been a huge fan of the originals for years.  I was definitely a Star Wars fanboy up until the release of the disappointing Episode I.  My expectations had been set so high and I just felt so let down.  The initial reviews of Episode II gave me a little bit of hope, but when the majors gave it mixed reviews I went into it with lower expectations.  And I still feel disappointed with this one.  Don't listen to the fanboys who like to flame the negative reviews.  This film deserves every one of them.  It's not a bad film at all but it's nothing great. The acting is mostly stale and the dialog is mostly weak.  The effects are fantastic but they seem overused.  This is most definitely an animated film starring humans.  *POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD* - - The last hour of the film is full of waaay to many different droids and forms of technology that does nothing but put the older sequel trilogy to shame as far as effects go. Most people agree that Yoda's role in the end is the best part of the film. But I think the Yoda character was dumbed down in Attack of the Clones compared to what we see of him in the original trilogy.  And not even the end of the film redeems his role in my opinion.  Plus, that particular scene is just too short.  My main gripe with this film is that it doesn't explain much of anything!  It does very little to move the story along.  Episode III has A LOT to explain...  There are things I enjoyed about this one.  I actually liked the humor with R2-D2 and C-3PO. I really enjoyed the end of the tatooine scene with Anakin.  It was very powerful.  I have yet to see this film digitally projected, but that won't change anything I've said about it.  I saw it on film.  The film was a little bit dark, but it still looked like film to me.  I look forward to the next episode and hope that George Lucas truly redeems himself.

title: Highly Enjoyable, but not without flaws
review:
First off - I must stipulate, I am a movie buff, but not specifically a Star Wars buff. I have enjoyed the first series, but like most was let down by TPM. I went into AOTC with few expectations, and was more than pleasantly surprised. The action was swift, easy to follow, and there were enough silly one-liners. The effects in the fight and action scenes were superb, although were occasionally poor in the dialogue sections. The acting was highly appropriate - just over the top enough to fit in well with the rest. As a Kiwi, it was a bit odd seeing Jay Lagai'a (sp?) and Temuera Morrison on the big screen, still looking and sounding like kiwis, but they acquited themselves well.

All in all - an enjoyable 2 1/2 hrs, although the dialogue in some areas was worse than weak, and occasionally the film felt a little too "knowing" about what was to come (in IV, V and VI).

title: The best movie in the series!
review: The critics have said that this is a dull, uninteresting story, with uninspired performances and overwhelming CGI graphics.  The critics who report that are missing the boat on the Star Wars phenomenon.  This is Star Wars where the story and the action go hand in hand and predicate each other.  The characters draw you in not by their acting but by their uniqueness and flaws.  Take Boba Fett by example, this character has less than 10 lines in the entire saga, yet is one of the most beloved Star Wars characters.  Jar Jar Binks is universally hated, and what does that say right there?  Usually people can't agree on much at all.  It's difficult to compare performances by any of the artists in these movies.  I'll agree most of Star Wars is hype and marketing, but in the end it lives up to it's billing.  Have you ever noticed that when people talk about the Star Wars movies they say what they like and didn't like, and everyone is instantly part of the conversation.  This is a universal truth that Star Wars has brought together a generation of people.  I don't know anyone who's never seen each of these movies, nor hasn't an opinion on them.  Everyone has they're favorite characters and sometimes they are villains.  As for this movie, it's probably the most compelling, at times its slow and you yearn for the trademark action sequences, but you also feel drawn to the destruction of Anakin.  Hayden Christenson is either a real talent or "The Force" George Lucas did a masterful job of directing him on how to link his performance with Jake LLoyd, there is a strong resemblance, as well as some of the same facial expressions that work well.  Ewan McGregor is much better as ObiWan this time and links his performance to Alec Guiness very well. It will be interesting to see how the relationship between ObiWan and Anakin/Vader unfolds.

title: A gripping sequel to a disappointing prequel...
review: After seeing this movie the opening day (wow I feel like a trekkie...), I must admit that it definitely does not disappoint. I won't give away any key elements of the story, but I'll give a few points on why I believe that it was one of the best Star Wars movies. First off, this one, unlike Episode 1, had an interesting plot. There was lots of action, and enough inaction to balance it out. The Anakin/Padme issue actually added to the movie, as opposed to making it worse and bogging it down. Another point I'd like to make, is that this movie had some wonderful puns and inside humor that Episode 1 sorely lacked. It was enough to keep the audience laughing in some parts, which is almost unheard of for a Science Fiction movie. My third point, is that the visual effects and new races were simply stunning. These are some of the best special effects I've ever seen. To make my last point, I have merely one word: Yoda. I highly recommend this movie, even to non-science fiction buffs.

title: A fast paced action flick with substance to boot.
review: The first installment of star wars left a lot to be desired and was in George Lucas own words a tad "infantile". Thankfully this has be redressed with Episode II:Attack of the Clones. In AotC the characters introduced in Episode I are fleshed out some more, we catch up on young Padawan Anakin Skywalker, and how he has developed under his Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi (suitably played by Ewan McGregor) as they are assiged to protect Padme ( the beautiful Natalie Portman); the former Queen Amidala from unknown ruffians.The story unfurls steadily towards a dazzling climax, carried in no small part by the sublime special effects ,certainly the most advanced yet seen, and Lucas' trademark dissolves. Lucas has created a magical Universe populated with as diverse and colourful characters as imagination will allow. Whereas Episode I left a sour taste of "scorchio" , Episode II the viewer gagging for a sequal. A thouroughly enjoyable film. And Starwipe to Episode III.

title: Bring Back The Glory That was Taken By Episode I
review: This movie simply ranks right up there with the last 3 episodes (4-6) and offers a great story-line,amazing visual effects and a rather unlikely (and somewhat flimsy) love story. Still This movie is a must see - not only for the star wars freaks but for everyone who saw episode I and was disapointed.

title: Excellent - Star Wars is back!
review:
I'll be brief as those of you reading through the reviews would have already read the plot synopsis many times prior to my review.

I went to the 12.01 screening of Episode 2 last night and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

After reading the critics negative reviews, much anticipation on my part and three years wait, I thought it was excellent.

I loved digital Yoda, however could not notice any visual difference in the fact that the movie is filmed in Digital (of course it may not have helped being seated 4 rows from the screen).

I hope you enjoy it as much as I did.

title: I forgive Lucas for Episode 1
review: This movie was so intense, and over the top it brought George Lucas back into a positive eye for me. After he dissapointed almost everyone that saw The first prequil, I thought this would also be dissapointing. He brought us as far as modern cinema can take us, while still having enough suspence to keep us dying for what is next. In this movie he had incredible action sequiences, but still had a strong story as a base. Compared to Episode 1 the acting was top notch. It shows the story we have all put pieces of together in our minds from the bits and pieces that he gave us in the original trilogy. The directoral style includes all the transitions we loved from the Original three, while making it way more of an epic movie. The story flows and tells us that this is not a movie that can only be enjoyed by our kid brother and sister. Everything about this movie is so fulfiling, and perfect that all i want is Episode Three. Plus there is only three minutes of Jar Jar. I will wait for Episode 3, but not get my hopes up, just cause this one is good, doesent mean the next will. Lucas just do what you did with this one and we will all love it.

title: Much better than Phantom, but we need space battles
review:
Overall, a much better movie than Phantom Menace, and also slightly better than Return of the Jedi. Obi Wan and Dooku excellent, Yoda goes offf. But it lacked one thing, there was no significant space battle, besides Obi Wan pursuing Jango through the asteroid field on Genosis. We need Tie Fighters and X-WINGS!!! hopefully they spawn in part III.

ps. It was cool to see the schematics of the Death Star. George, get the dude who directed Empire or Steven Spielberg or someone to direct Episode III, you just dont have it.....

title: Go see it because its Star Wars (you'll need SOMETHING to talk about at work on Monday)
review: Although the movie wasn't that bad....it wasn't that good either.  Like the empire strikes back, this movie was basicly a little filler until the next movie.  Although Yoda with a lightsaber is worth any price you pay to see the movie!!! GO YODA!!!!

title: I found this really starts putting together the pieces
review: Early critics have already condemned this movie, but do they understand that these movies aren't meant to stand alone.  George Lucas has really taken the time to not only provide great graphics but also provide a story that is well thought out.  My son and I raced home to watch the original Star Wars just to recap all the pieces.  Great Job!

title: One of the Best SW Films
review:
Go see it. There are plenty of people that will say it's a flop simply because that's what they want to say. However this movie is really good. Plenty of action.

This one's better than the first and is good as any of the other Star Wars films. Highly recommended.

title: I'd watch it again!
review: I've read the low reviews critics gave this movie, and went in expecting little.  But after watching it, I became involved into AotC. I really think the critics went a little too tough on this movie. The acting is a little stale, but I didn't think it was bad. The plot was good, and the ending was excellent. I'd love to watch this movie again!

title: A disappointment
review: Weak dialogue, weak acting, and plotholes the size of Wyoming hurt this film tremendously. While the final half hour is riveting, the first 90 are painful to behold. Particularly groanful are any and all scenes between Padme and Anakin...they are directed as if in a high school play, and because of this their "romance" seems forced and contrived. Kenobi's half of the story came off much better, since McGregor was actually instilling some fun qualities into his character. Perhaps the biggest flaw the film has is having characters with whom the audience may invest emotion in. It may be true that Anakin will become Darth Vader, but it is still the film's obligation to present him as sympathetic and someone whom the audience should care about. Here the film failed. Though Christensen's wooden performance did not help the cause either. 5/10

title: Darth Lucas
review:
In the original "Star Wars" trilogy, Darth Vader was a man who had to wear a mechanical suit in order to survive. He had given in to the Dark Side of the Force, and lost contact with humanity.

Something similar could be said of George Lucas. Over time, he has become encased in technology, and has completely lost touch with his beating human heart. He has given into the Dark Side of Hollywood movie-making, and is now both smug and defiant about that fact when he is interviewed. There seems to be little hope of winning him back to our side.

This movie is even worse than "Phantom Menace". I was actually embarrassed for Lucas. How could a man with his instincts allow such a noisy travesty to be shown in public? The audience in the theater with me was laughing uproariously AT the movie--and definitely not WITH it. I cringed for the man who is trashing his own legacy.

Chase scenes to nowhere, amateurish wooden acting, execrable dialogue, unbearable "love" scenes, pointless action sequences. Everyone stranded, gasping for air and life, in a galaxy far, far away.

I was tremendously embarrassed for Natalie Portman, who was forced to all but bear her breasts in the last portion of the movie. Shame on you, Darth Lucas!! Exploiting this young woman's body for your nefarious purposes! You bloated, deluded, dirty old man!!

Save your money. Do not give in to the Dark Side. Spend the time you have left over renting the videos of the original trilogy. Throw this movie onto a one-way garbage scow into hyperspace.

--GM

title: A very well directed film!
review:
After a pretty dismal Episode I, Episode II comes as an extremely pleasant surprise. George Lucas has done a fantastic job with "Attack of the Clones". The story is full of those successful elements which makes a good story - heart pumping action shots (great light sabre fights!), well developed characters, great themes, and a lovely musical score which ties in themes from previous and "future" Episodes.

The cinematography was well done, ranging from the busy and sprawling Coruscant, to the beautiful planet of Naboo, and rocky planet of Genosis and the wet but high tech Kamino.

The character development was also very well done. Lucas focused on the relationships between his key characters and the transformation of Annakin's character. Jar Jar Binks is a lot more subtle, and there is the interesting Jango and Boba Fett.

Episode II is fantastic story telling. George Lucas - you have done a great job!

title: Episode 2 - Attack of Bad Writing
review:
Like so many other die hard fans, I waited in line for the midnight showing to see this film, and now I am completely regretting my decision. While it was better than Phantom Menace, as a life-long Star Wars fan, I take offense that Lucas thinks he can get away with putting the worst love story ever into an otherwise interesting action movie. The film would have been so much better if 90% of the dialogue that Amidala and Anikin have together was cut from the movie. Star Wars fans are smarter than Lucas thinks. WE KNOW that Anikin and Amidala fall in love when they're not supposed to. Otherwise, Episodes 4, 5, and 6 don't make sense. Just showing scenes of them enjoying each other's company in the beautifully landscaped scenes would be enough to get the point across. Instead we have to endure crappy lines like "Everything here is soft and smooth", and "I am haunted by the kiss you shouldn't have given me." It sounds like Anakin is making an awkward pass at his sister.

It's also this clumsiness towards Amidala that makes Anakin a spoiled little brat, rather than an arrogant and extremely talented Jedi. When Anakin fights, he is arrogant and rushes to judgment. But this arrogance doesn't carry over to his relationship with Amidala. If he was truly the arrogant hero, then he wouldn't fumble around making awkward passes at her through the entire film. It would be more romantic if Anakin just knew that they were supposed to be together. Lucas meant for Anakin to grapple with his emotions throughout the entire film, but we don't need to see the angst he has with Amidala, we needed to see him grapple more with the death of his mother. Unfortunately, we are wisked away from a crucial scene with Anakin and his mother's kidnappers before we truly grasp what he is doing that is so wrong. Instead, Lucas has his characters map out all their actions with words, instead of letting the actions speak for themselves. This is his main fault as a script writer. He is so good at letting the scenery and locations speak for themselves, but all the actors have to say what they are going to do first, then do it, or vice versa. Just because actors have mouths doesn't mean they have to use them.

Case in point, during the final (and very cool) battle between Tyrannus and Yoda, Tyrannus (Christopher Lee) says "Clearly this battle will not be won by our knowledge of the force, but by our abilities with a light-saber." Well, thanks for clearing that up for me George. I've just seen a very cool fight scene where both characters try to defeat each other by using the force to move objects and kill their opponent, and you had to ruin in by having someone talk. If Tyrannus and Yoda had just pulled out their light-sabers and started fighting, we would have understood perfectly. No one would have thought that when they pulled out their light sabers that they were going to have a cooking contest. Let the action speak for itself. This is what Lucas needs to learn as a script writer, and a director. Action speaks louder than words.

title: Much better than Episode I
review:
***Warning: Minor/Moderate Spoilers*** The underlying problem with reviewing any major "franchise" movie such as Star Wars is you'll always have two kinds of reviewers. Some will be absolute, die-hard fans, and they will overlook any and all flaws in the movie. And others will play the devil's advocate, and dog the movie for flaws that they would otherwise overlook in any other summer action movie.

All that not withstanding, I must say I was much more impressed with Act 2 of this line of Star Wars prequels than the first one. Performances varied across the board this time... Natalie Portmann (Padmé Amidala) and Hayden Christensen (Anakin Skywalker) both played quite well independently, but the two have virtually no on-screen chemistry. Their relationship seems driven not so much by love, but by the necessity therein to retain the continuity with characters in Episodes 4, 5, and 6. (such as their kids, Luke and Leia)

The student-turned-master Obi-Wan Kenobi is probably one of the better performances by Ewan McGregor, being able to portray his character with a much more serious air than the first movie. (to Anakin: "I have a feeling you're going to be the death of me")

Christopher Lee, notable for doing an awesome job as Saruman in Lord of the Rings, once again delivers a decent performance as the villain Jedi, Count Dooku. (And a duel between him and the now-butt-kicking Yoda had the whole auditorium cheering)

As for the action scenes, this movie was quite mind-blowing. It seemed a lot of times as if the game was seeing how many special effects could be displayed on-screen at a given time. And a "Gladiator"-style duel-turned-battle toward the end will prove quite entertaining and memorable.

Enjoy the film, and may the Force be with you

-Juansmith

title: My Review Of Attack Of The Clones
review:
Just got back an hour ago! The cinema was packed! When I say packed, I mean packed! I went for the 9:00pm showing, but I turned up at 8:00pm to be safe. There was already a massive queue! But luckily most of the people went to the top left hand side of the cinema, so I got a lovely back row seat on the right side :D

Well where do I start!? Well I'm think I'm going to have to start with the 2 actors that shine through out of all the cast; Ewan McGregor and Hayden Christensen.

Don't believe all the rubbish that the reviewers have been saying about Christensen's acting ability, it's complete rubbish. I was shocked at actually how good he was! You know when you watch a film and you can see they're acting? Not here! He does all the tones, facial expressions, EVERYTHING perfectly; completely believable! (I studied performing arts for a year, I know how difficult it is). With that little bit of cheekiness, strong will and evilness in his eye, it is easy to see how he becomes Darth Vader. Hayden is one of best actors I have ever seen. I'm shocked that he has never done any film work pervious to Attack Of The Clones!

Secondly Ewan McGregor. He was absolutely fantastic! I would go as so far as to say, that he was actually better than Alec Guinness! He brought a humanness to the role, very genuine. Like what I said about Hayden. Ewan is undoubtingly one of the finest actors I have ever seen also.

The chemistry between Christensen and McGregor is both fabulous and comical.

I have to say I didn't find Natalie Portman's performance very outstanding. I think she has proved in this film that she is just a run of the mill Hollywood actress. It is easy as an actor or actress to do roles that are at one end of the emotional spectrum. I know from my experience that it is easier to do characters that are at one end of the spectrum. You know, like really happy or really sad, a drunk, a nurse... you get what I mean? They are the parts Portman has played in the past. It is a lot harder to play a flat part. Portman's role in Attack Of The Clones called for a more natural form of acting, which takes more acting ability, and unfortunately, unlike McGregor and Christensen, I don't think she managed to pull it off. There was one cringe worthy part where she looks over Obi-Wan's (McGregor) shoulder, supposedly surprised to see Anakin (Christensen). It was a pretty bad piece of acting from her :\ But besides that she was good in the rest of the film.

The chemistry between Anakin (Christensen) and Padmé (Portman) was extremely convincing. Just the way they looked at each other, and kissed. It was SO convincing it makes me wonder if there was actually something going on behind the scenes with Christensen and Portman.

There was some very funny classical lines from C-3PO (Daniels) that had the whole cinema giggling.

So what was the best part of the film? Well Yoda (Oz) kicking butt of course! :D There was a look he gave to Count Dooku (Lee) that made the whole cinema roll with laughter, and again when Yoda (Oz) began fighting Count Dooku (Lee). This little green thing bouncing about with a lightsaber, hehe :) Then at the end he picks up his walking stick and hobbles again. Hehe :) It was very funny :)

At the beginning I was a bit dubious about the animation for Yoda (Oz). But it seemed to be a lot better towards the end of the film. Which makes me wonder if they had 2 different animation teams working on him. *shrugs*

The background graphics throughout the film were amazing - as always. All those tiny details you don't even notice.

There is one part, where Anakin (Christensen) is having a lightsaber fight with Count Dooku (Lee). That was just breathtaking. The way the light from the lightsabers reflects on their faces. The way it should have been when Luke fights Darth Vader, but they didn't have advanced enough technologies back then.

So overall what do I rate it?: - 10 out of 10!!! :rollin

But if you are going to be all critical of graphics and script etc, then I would give it: - 8 out of 10

But as a complete film definitely 10/10!

It has now made the #1 slot in my favourite Star Wars films. It has also reached my favourite films ever list! It's amazing that it was all filmed completely digitally!

Highly recommended people! Go see!!!

title: Stop the insanity!
review: This film was awful, pretty much as bad as the last installment, albeit in a totally new way. The last twenty minutes, particularly the Yoda - Dooku duel were impressive...most impressive, but the "romantic" scenes between the two leads were just WRONG!  When Anakin blurted out to Amidala: "Are you in as much pain as I am?" the audience burst into spontaneous and embarrassing laughter!  Lucas has been living on his ranch too long. He's a man out of touch.  That said, I freely admit, I wish I had one iota of his genius!  I can't say I could make a better film, but I as a fan I have a right to be disappointed.

title: Real entertainment - A very interesting piece in the Star Wars Puzzle!
review:
Let's make it clear, Star Wars is not "Apocalypse Now", "Requiem For A Dream", "2001 A Space Odyssey" nor "Solaris". Star Wars is Star Wars. I am a hard critic on movies, but I am always objective. Star Wars was always intended to be spectacle with depth. Attack Of The Clones is a fantastic spectacle. Though it is hard to judge as a single movie, it is easier to review when seen as an EPISODE of the Star Wars Saga. Attack of the Clones brings strong and important elements to the Star Wars whole while offering to the viewer a non-stop, very entertaining chapter to the Saga. I strongly suggest the first time viewer to watch the previous Star Wars chapters in order to fully appreciate this film. No film since the late Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut have offer me that kind of visual stimulation. Simply beautiful. Critics that says the film is slow-paced must be living on another planet. That is the fastest (can I use the term for cinema?) movie I have ever seen. The 2 and a half long movie was still too short for my taste, I hope a longer version will soon be available on DVD.

The best of all Star Wars episode ? No. Most thrilling, yes, darkest, yes. Still, falls second to the sophomore Empire Strikes Back.

Spider-Man, released earlier this year, looks like a visit to the dentist compared to Attack Of The Clones.

Star Wars fans will just go crazy about this movie.

A+

title: IT'S BACK!
review:
.. the not so family-friendly violence.. the lack of Jar-Jar .. the horrific, dark moods.. the long-lasting, tranquil landscape sequences.. This time, George Lucas has let the CG-people take care of the details in stead of the plot! Excellent.. and how many details there are! Good work, CG-people!! Your work is in the scenes, and when you do that well - and only do that - it's so awesome, nothing short of art!

OK; this film has it's flaws (like all the SW-movies actually), for instance, C-3PO's hilarously neurotic character is exaggerated - to the point where it's far too much.. why, I don't know. Lucas seemed more restrictive in the cutting room on the earlier films.

Yoda is also portrayed on the boundaries of what might be considered disrespectful, but it actually works so well! I mean, he is (one of) the most powerful jedi. Everyone on the premiere started applauding Yoda, and I did too. Excellent stuff! :) I'm going to watch THAT scene again..

But there are other flaws - for instance, the romantic scenes with Anakin & Amydala were far, faar too cliched & romantic! I started laughing :D But it worked. The robot factory - where fast paced action timed between menacing machines, was attempted - failed a bit and became VERY "computergame"-like.

Anakin's transition towards evil is very well handled, both scriptwise and actorwise. Also, the annoying kid from SW1 is given new depth as we see he wasn't supposed to be simply "the cool kid" - moreover arrogant and ambitious.

Anyway: the film doesn't have the "hurried" feel that the Phantom Menace had. It had a lot of good stuff in stead. Lots of moods! Good moods and dark moods. Excellent! Good action scenes. REAL good ones.

Another film like SW1, and the series would have been screwed. I would then have had to ignore the I-II-III's and just go for the originals. However, this saves it all. It really does! Woohooo! Good work, Lucas! Get it even better for the next one, and it'll be the best in the series (hoping for all 9 to be made.. :)~ 9/10

title: Long live the Jedi!
review:
***hopefully doesn't spoil anything***

The good news is the Force is back. This is a wonderful adventure, visually, sonically, emotionally, and intellectually. The sights and sounds are no surprise; these films have a history of taking us to new and wonderful places we have not seen before. Emotionally, the film is also strong. We see the young Anakin gaining his emotions and not knowing what to do with them. He feels love, fear, hate, and anger... all things which he is told a Jedi should not have. For anyone who has passed through the gate of the teenage years, this confusion is all too familiar. And, the film suggests, that the supposedly all-knowing and unfeeling Jedi are partially to blame for the course we know Anakin will take, since the depth of the advice which they give him is: "Don't think those things; they're beneath you." Again, how familiar.

Perhaps the most pleasant surprise is that this is a film with an actual plot. There is an enormous amount going on in this story and it actually takes some effort to keep up with everything. While some viewers may criticize this aspect, I always welcome a movie that requires me to think about what is going on.

The greatest thrill of the movie, though, seems to come in watching all of the elements of the original films click into place. What happened to create the world in which the original three films took place? Characters and locales we know from those movies turn up here in earlier incarnations, and the result is often thrilling. One of the great delights is when C-3PO and R2D2 have one of their trademark little bickering sessions in the midst of some enormous danger. At that moment, it truly feels like the old "Star Wars" is back, if only for a moment.

It must be confessed that the film is hit-and-miss in many areas. Some effects look more like computer games than otherworldy visions. Some of the actors have the hang of this "Jedi-speak" while others sound foolish. (The great actor Christopher Lee is a standout as the villain.) Those who do not enjoy these sorts of movies will probably not have their minds changed by this one.

But if you do get goosebumps whenever you hear John Williams' classic theme, have no fear. The Force will be with you.

title: A Long Review - But It Goes Somewhere
review:
Now, it's only been out for, two days, maybe? Already a lot of people are saying they loved this movie, a lot of people are saying they hated this movie, but what's confusing me most of all is the sudden consensus that Episode One sucked. Where did that come from? Three years ago, Episode One ruled the school. Everyone was walking out of theatres everywhere more or less satisfied. Most, more.

And if you read that and cringe, think at least of the fight between Darth Maul and the two Jedi Knights. Now that was FUN.

I saw Attack of the Clones today, and I came out of two minds of what to think about this movie. It's certainly doing nothing to reverse that unseemly Hollywood trend of doing EVERYTHING on computer. But that's a given anyway, I would have thought. It's Star Wars.

There are a lot of things in Clones that seem a bit out of place. The Jedi

Knights don't seem to be the passive, peaceful negotiators in this episode they have been portrayed as in all the other flicks - one memorable moment towards the end of this movie has Samuel L. Jackson's character hold his lightsaber to someone's neck, to force a resolution. That's not a bad thing. That's just a thing.

In the end, Attack of the Clones IS worth seeing, even if you do end up hating it. Personally, I didn't think it was as good as I thought it was going to be, leading up to it - but that didn't detract from my enjoyment of it. Does that sound strange?

There are a lot of ideas that are underdeveloped, and a lot of ideas that are overdeveloped.

CONSIDER MY NEXT PARAGRAPH SPOILER CITY.

Jango Fett, for example, is referred to always as a "bounty hunter." He is used as the model for a mass cloned army, and you can see why. Not only is he a man of many talents, but he's got more tricks up his sleeve than a swiss army knife. But why is he referred to as a bounty hunter? We all know Boba grows up to be one. But Jango never catches anyone for a bounty, no one ever refers to him catching anyone for a bounty - it's not that it's WRONG for him to be a bounty hunter, it's just not necessary. He could be a general warrior. I also agree with something someone said in an earlier review - he dies the way of Darth Maul, eg: too easily.

AND THE NEXT PARAGRAPH IS PRETTY BAD TOO, ACTUALLY.

The scene with Anakin exacting his passionate revenge on the Tusken Raiders, that could have been one of the most powerful ideas ever presented on the silver screen. In the end, it still packs a punch, but you can't help thinking it could have been milked for all the evil glory it could get. How Darth Vader would it have been, how positively evil would it have been for Anakin to look into the eyes of the woman he loves, and say to her, "Don't ever ask me again: what happened out there today."

That's just what I think, anyway.

But I think that's why people are taking such an extreme stance on this movie - either loving it, or hating it. Some ideas are overdeveloped, some ideas are underdeveloped, the point of the matter is, THE IDEAS ARE BRILLIANT, and if you let them fester in your brain, they will move you.

Let's hear it for Darth Tyrannus - a bad guy who ACTUALLY SURVIVES!

-ant

title: Why oh why...

review:
Viewed film Thursday 5/16

Keep in mind the 2nd half is much better than first half.

Fett family space chase scene is awesome with tremendous sound.

It makes you realize how flawed 'Menace' really was (with the exception of Darth Maul saber duel which I still enjoy watching). It is really that good and so much the superior to ep 1.
