review: Very gripping film.  Blows away Episode I.  Perhaps the most dramatic of any Star Wars film, well acted by all.  Excellent use of comic relief (though C-3PO uses puns a little too much) far better than non-stop Jar-Jar in Episode I.  Overall, very, very good.

title: I miss Ford!
review: I'm a child of the 70's and grew up waiting for the next installment up Star Wars (just like many children are doing today) However my wait was for different reasons: The characters. I actually went into a trance like state for weeks wondering, between star wars and The Empire Strikes Back, if Han Solo was dead, whats to become of Luke, and who is Darth Vader? However with the new trilogy well under way what drives us to wait (what seems like light-years) for the next installment. It cant be the story. We all know where it's heading. So it must be the effects. My gripe is this I sat through 2 hours of an unknown personality (and not a very refined one yet) wandering through his mid-jedi crisis, as well as his Louis Lamourish love story, just to get to the special effects. All I could think of when I left the cineplex (other than the sharp pins going through my butt) was that I'm glad DVDs have chapter selections. Because I cannot imagine a child becomi ng as immersed in the last two films as much as I was when I was a child. So if your listening Lucas: Give me Han Solos dad in the next installment, oh and if it's not to weird a casting call let Ford play the role.

title: One Of the Greatest, If not the One...
review:
This is the movie which brings balance to the Force.

For many, The Phantom Menace was a disappointment. But it was not for me, I thought it was not a flawless movie, but there was some magic, some cool stuff inside it, so I was really loving it. And I still do. But I have to admit it, that chapter is far beyond Episode I.

Everything is better, the story is told in such a perfect way, taking us on a trip through the galaxy and we can follow beloved characters that have flaws, pain, doubt and courage. Three Characters played exceptionally well by the three actors, even if Ewan McGregor is the weakest one. Christensen is giving to anakin the ambiguity that Anakin needs, Natalie Portman is great, intelligent, et really beautiful (and she has many nice outfits too!) and Ewan McGregor is so cool playing a Jedi Master that is always close to fail with his apprentice.

The movie can be split in two parts. The first part concerns the investigation and the political plot is very interesting and complex, we feel that there's a mystery behind all those negotiations. The second part is about the beginning of a conflict. This one is breathtaking and mesmerizing, I was feeling pain for those Jedis getting killed, I was thrilled by the unexpected fights between characters of the movie.

So this movie has an epic style and this was the most exciting experience I ever had in theaters for years. I mean it!

title: Great Movie -> Star Wars Or Otherwise
review:
I read almost all of the reader reviews (without spoilers) that I could before going to see Episode II. I went in with a sense of dread, half expecting to be full on let down by the latest installment of the Star Wars saga. I had many key phrases from those reviews dancing through my head. I looked for the "wooden lines" spoken by the actors, I looked for a "jumbled" or "muddy" plot. I looked for everything that I heard was bad.... and it wasn't there. This movie returns the series to the Star Wars that most people know and love. I must admit I'm a Star Wars fan, but you can lump me in the category of people that did not like Episode I (at least the first time I saw it). Episode II delivers everything I hoped for and then some.

Although I am a Star Wars fan, this movie is a good movie in its own right. If you haven't seen any other Star Wars movie, and you're not cynical about the series because of nerd-dome that is a lot of times attached to fans, you'll still like this movie. Lucas creates a universe of characters and places, he sticks to it, and it's immersive.

I don't want to say anything specific about the film because most of the plot points have already been leaked out and the things that dropped my jaw may not drop yours. My best advice is to see Episode II (cheap prices if necissary) and judge for yourself. I honestly think the vast majority of viewers will not be disappointed. I also think that the vast majority of Star Wars fans will hail this as one of the (if not the) best installments into the Star Wars saga.

title: that stunk
review: i know everyone was dying for AOTC to be good after the last load of crap that Lucas dumped on us, but there's no need to lie to ourselves or to anybody else. it sucked. i'll admit that it was better than the Phantom Menece, but is that really saying much? the acting was the worse thing this side of Keanu Reeves. literally, everytime that Christensen kid opened his mouth i cringed. Portman, as lovely as she is, didn't do much better. Ewan McGregor did his best Alec Guinness impression, but they all seemed lost acting in front of a blue screen. acting has never been a strong point for Star Wars films, but it has hit a new low this time. i'm not even going to get into the terrible script. i wish Lucas had done what he did for Empire and let someone else handle all the real film making work. he's obviously more focused on "dazzleing" special effects. but to me they were about as dazzleing as watching my lame room mate playing video games on a friday night. maybe i'm old fashioned, but i miss the old days of puppets and creative makeup. they seemed much more realistic. as far as technology has come, alot of the scenes stilled seemed about as real as Mary Poppins dancing with cartoon penguins. i could whine all night about this and that, but what good would it do. yes, i'll be there when the next one comes out on opening night just like i was this time. but untill then i'll be watching the origanal three movies to try to reclaim what's left of my childhood after seeing the last two.

title: CONTAINS SPOILERS!! EP. 2 is the BEST apology perhaps EVER!!
review:
Contains Several Spoilers!!!! Contains Several Spoilers!!!!

Should have been Episode One. Despite some bad compositing of characters leaping on or off of CGI animals and such, and some (read: all) painful romantic moments with Amidala and Anakin, and some action elements that seem to have been orchestrated to either immolate video games or inspire the expected Star Wars video games, despite those elements this thing is pure sugar, and I've no regrets dumping out the cash to see it opening day. Loved the improved characters, the massively improved loyalty to continuity with the first trio of films, the re-creation of Owen & Beru's crib on Tattoine, the Jawa spread, the inclusion of Boba's backstory (and I'm shocked I dug this one, but if you're going to do it right, do it fully over the top, and they did, all the clones are based on Jango Fett including li'l Boba, out of control). Found the similarities of the Tusken Raider camp to a Native American village a bit unnerving, and I'd love to know where the raiders got bamboo to tie up Anakin's mom on a desert planet. Loved the violence of the opening, uncanny and beautifully rendered. Loved the arena monsters, especially the crab thing. Loved the Jedi fight with the Federation droids (which no longer act nearly as boring as in Ep. 1, although the "Roger Roger" gag is used again, and yeh, I chuckled again). Loved that 3 or 4 of the surviving Jedi were female, and 2 of those were the clearly Asian women, and the others were Hindu and Green tentacle alien respectively (there may have been more, but these four need action figures IMMEDIATELY!). Didn't laugh at the C3PO one line gags "This is a drag." Ow. "I'm beside myself." Double ow. Mixed feelings about R2-D2's leg thrusters. Found seeing R2-D2 use his third leg to climb stairs a bit distracting (although I've had to do that a few times, so I can empathize with the little guy). Loved Yoda doing the Jet Li action. Loved seeing Anakin getting his arm lopped off. Why stop there, I wondered? Loved like a mother the city stuff, the vehicles, the centipedes, the high speed traffic, the seedy bar, the scantly clad alien babes, the diner with the femme waitress bot. Awesome! Loved the Jango Fett fights, including the outcome. Nothing says good entertainment like a beheading! Love that Jar Jar became a stooge for the political agenda of the Dark Side. Love the bald lady standing next to Supreme Chancellor Palpatine. Love the symmetry of having Christopher Lee being handed the plans for the Death Star when his old Hammer Films buddy Peter Cushing was in command of the actualized Death Star back in 1977. Love the parallel moments and shots to the previous trio of films, like the ending shot of this one parallel to the ending shot of Empire Strikes Back, complete with robotic hand. Love the alien world where the clones are being produced, and dig the aliens doing the producing. Love the whole business with Jango's rapid firing machine in the asteroid belt. Love the leader of the bugs, love the Techno cyborg guy in the Federation camp even more. Kit Fisto is also the bomb, by the way. And last of all, simply adored the clones at war with the Federation robots. Tons of cool stuff in this that'll give Hasbro years worth of figures and vehicles without repeating themselves.

title: Begun this Clone War has!
review:
I was lucky enough to get tickets to the opening night of "Attack of the Clones" and let me tell you it did not disappoint. As bad as the name of the movie, I was expecting something along the lines of Phantom Menace. This is far from the truth! While Phantom Menace put emphasise on the special effects, AOTC goes into much more story detail. Without ruining it for you all, basically it starts off 10 years since Phantom Menace. Anakin Skywalker is older and more arrogant and Obi-Wan is more efficient at being a Jedi Master. This sets and backgrounds of the movie are unbelievable, and the music totally rules. John Williams has once again put a masterpiece together and used it on another master piece. Not only that, but he uses known tunes to signify important parts, such as the Imperial March.

What is also good to see are a lot of Australian Actors in it. Mainly because it was filmed in Australia, but it is still good to see recognisable faces. One thing that really made it stand up against Phatom Menace is the storyline in the movie. In Phantom Menace, the storyline was basically to introduce a few characters, but never really had much of a story. In ATOC, it is very easy to see what will connect with what. As a major Star Wars fan (although I didn't dress up), i noticed a lot of references to all the other SW movies, such as one funny quote that Obi-Wan says, "Honestly, one day i believe you will be the end of me!". But not only are the jokes references, but also character references and story references. But not only is the storyline good, but the jokes are many and plenty of laughs are had (look out for Yoda!). I believe that George Lucas truly wrote this one for the SW fans, not just anyone who happens to go see it.

However, be you a Star Wars fan or not, i thoroughly recommend you go see this movie. The action, storyline, music and even the romance, work well together to produce a terrific movies. May The Force Be With You!

title: Attack of the Yoda
review:
George Lucas is very fond of effects and it shows. And when the first two hours has very little action, but just a lovestory with bad dialogue, you start thinking, what am I doing here.

Then there is a war, and the series is back to it's former greatness. Lightsaber-fights not with one, nor two, but every jedi in the universe. Even Yoda lights his saber, and gives us the absolute highlight of the movie.

In episode I Jar-Jar broke up great actionsequences with stupid gags. This time around C3PO and R2D2 has teamed up again and interrupts some of the greatest Star Wars action ever. Uneccesary again, but more bearable.

The actors of the Star Wars movies have always had to work with bad dialogue. The actors in episodes IV to VI managed it better than the performers in these newest films with only Ewan McGregor as the exception.

Without the ending the film would get a rating of 2 from me. With the ending it manages to reach the area between 3 and 4. Not really bad, not great, not even mediocre. As pure entertainment: it works.

title: Begun, the Clone War has...
review:
...and now we have to wait for another three years to see its conclusion. WOW. Episode II is definitely MUCH better than Episode I. I would even say it's better that Return of the Jedi. If Lucas keeps up the good work then Episode III will be on a par with A New Hope and Empire Strikes Back.

You can see the plot elsewhere so I'll just try to summarize what was good about it and what was bad about it.

Good:

1. The characters. Almost every one of them (with the notable exception of Amidala - I'll get to that below) delivers a superb performance. I was especially pleasantly surprised by Hayden (Anakin). He fits the role perfectly: the impetuous young Jedi padawan, reckless, impulsive, ambitious, overly confident of himself, lacking patience, determined to be the greatest Jedi ever. But we see as well his occasional bursts of fury, his inner torments and demons, which predict his eventual fall to the Dark Side. We see as well all temptations and trials he is subjected to - his forbidden attraction to Amidala, his love for his mother and how what happens to her affects him - and we can understand how his fall to the Dark Side begins. All the others are good as well: Obi-Wan, Yoda, Mace Windu, Count Dooku.

2. The plot. There are actually two epic lines: Obi-Wan discovering the hidden clone army and dealing with the conspiration and Padme vs. Anakin. The first one is VERY good. The enemy (Sidious) is almost unseen, he doesn't have more than a couple of lines in the entire movie, yet you can feel his presence everywhere, see the shadow of his actions begging to take shape. His is a masterful plan to take over the Republic which nobody sees; he fools all with intelligence. This is the kind of bad guy I love. Also great are all the scenes on the planet where Obi-Wan discovers the clones and his confrontations with Jango Fett. Suspense, adrenaline and an eerie feeling of outworldliness.

3. The special effects - settings. Each planet has its own distinctive individuality and is created in such detail you cannot believe it is not real. Coruscant: high towers, lights, traffic, agitation. Naboo: beautiful landscapes, waterfalls, pastorality. Clone planet: water, white, rain. Conspiration planet: red, volcanos, machinery, inhabitants which resemble giant flies. Absolutely stunning.

4. All the small tidbits which are SW trademark, which give us old-timers a feeling of home coming: movie opens with a ship in space, somebody has a bad feeling, Artoo saves the day, Threepio gets into trouble, Obi-Wan jests to Anakin "I've got a feeling you're going to be the end of me" - how true...

5. Lightsaber duels. They are PERFECT. They are shot continuously (not like in TPM where they were always interrupted by other epic threads) and are suspenseful. They even manage to make Yoda duel without him becoming hilarious - he's great, in fact.

Now for the bad parts:

1. Except for the race between Obi-Wan and Jango Fett in the asteroid field, there isn't any space battle at all. All battles take place on the ground.

2. The love-story between Anakin and Padme is clumsily done, rushed and forced. I kept comparing it to Han/Leia and it doesn't stand a chance. Also, Padme was the greatest disappointment in the movie. She is downgraded from the stately royal presence and aloofness to a good-looking young woman who does nothing but get herself into trouble. There were some plot holes here as well: she keeps telling Anakin how they shouldn't be together but keeps provoking him by wearing the most revealing outfits. She is supposed to be traveling undercover in order to avoid her enemies but keeps wearing the most shining costumes.

Oh, but you can skip over the bad parts and enjoy the movie. It is really something.

P.S. In case you were wondering: Jar Jar has less than 5 minutes screen time.

Rating: 8/10

title: I don't care what the critics say, I loved it!
review: I was so excited to see this movie i didnt get any sleep the night before. I have to admit that there were a few slow parts but what movie doesnt have those.  I wont go into plot because you can find that anywhere but regardless of what ppl are saying on here there is a plot and it is carried along decently.  But the action is where this film realy shines.  There are great chase sequences, huge armies, and of course lightsaber battles.  If you have ever wanted to see more of the lesser known Jedi's and their talents you will love this movie. I give it ****1/2 out of *****.

title: Disappointed again...
review:
I was hoping that I was going to enjoy Episode II considerably more than I did Episode I. I'm afraid that wasn't the case.

I found the first 1/2 to 2/3 of the movie to be almost painful to watch at times. I normally can be appeased by special effects and eye candy, but even these were lacking. I think that Lucas tried to hard to animate everything and just couldn't get that amount of work done given budet/time restraints. I was more impressed with the special effects during the last 1/3 of the movie though.

If you are a Star Wars fan, you should go see it... who could resist?... but I don't think I will be paying to see this one a second time in the theatres.

title: I didn't expect much, and it delivered
review:
To be honest, after the horrid Episode 1, I didn't expect much from Episode 2. Because of that, I can't say I was disappointed. Lucas delivered about what I expected.

It was gorgeous, and it truly sets a new standard for special effects in film. The problem was that it doesn't integrate the actors well in places -- it looks bluescreened.

To complain about the normal stuff, the dialogue was hokey (Yoda's lines sounded the most natural), the acting was stiff, and the directing was non-existent. For the most part, the actors do an OK job of pretending to see something that isn't there, but it's a stretch at times.

Natalie Portman has established herself as a fine and powerful actress, but I kept feeling like she had to dumb it down for the role and play down to the more limited talents and experience of her costars.

Hayden Christensen is pretty, but that's about it. He looks pompous and spoiled when he's supposed to be immature, and he looks constipated when he's supposed to look dark and brooding. Forget about the "sexual chemistry" between him and Portman that supposedly won him the role -- it didn't translate to film at all.

Ewan McGregor is the film's one laudable success. He character has matured since TPM and he has adopted a style and accent that could conceivably grow into Sir Alec Guinness. The lines are trite, but the performance is admirable.

The faults for this film, ultimately, lie solely on the shoulders of George Lucas. With the budget, the franchise, and the guaranteed returns, this movie could have commanded all the might of Hollywood, yet he retained the script and directorial reigns. A good script and a solid director could have made this movie work. Lucas is a brilliant mind and a top-notch visual effects guy, but a writer and director he is not. A perfect example is the event which really marks the turn in Anakin to the dark side. They hint at it, they talk briefly about it, but the single most significant event of all six movies wasn't shown for the true horror that it was supposed to invoke. Sure, it might have taken some careful editing to avoid the R-rating, but we're talking about the event that sends the innocent blonde kid down the road to Darth Vader.

Even he has conceded that TPM was a disappointment, but rather than purge the worst of the first, he tries to salvage them. GEORGE - IF YOU'RE READING THIS -- JAR JAR NEEDS TO GO AWAY. A "limited role" isn't good enough. GONE. GOODBYE. NO MORE. There's also the Pod Race II -- same ole thing in 3D with guns. Admit mistakes, let them go, and move on.

Perhaps the worst element was the misplaced attempts at suspense. This is a prequel, so we know that Anakin, Obi-Wan, and Amidala will live. To go through extended action sequences which place their lives in jeopardy is insulting. We all know they're not in any real danger, so don't waste our time. There is only one fight sequence that's worth noting, and that's the much commented-upon light saber fight at the end. (And no, I'm not talking about Yoda -- that was tacky.) There was an element of mystery because we didn't know if the bad guy was going to buy it, but it's notable because it was simply gorgeous -- perfectly choreographed and visually stunning.

I'll grant that the Star Wars franchise is a difficult task to undertake. It's a much-anticipated epic with a religious following. I can only hope that Lucas will focus on what he's truly good at, and let others handle the rest. Peter Jackson might be a good source of input -- he's got some experience in such matters.

title: A huge step forward
review: I will say that I didn't expect great things from this film, and I was pleasantly surprised.  It seems like Lucas really listened to the griping about Episode I and did his best to not commit the same mistaked.  He's never tried to write a love story before, and in my opinion he needs some practice.  Don't get me wrong, it is necessary for later plot developments, I just found it a little weakly constructed.  My other complaint is that there are certain scenes I felt were delivered in such a way for no other reason than to get cheers from the audience (which they did), although in my opinion they might have been more appropriate a little less overdone.

title: Visuals 8.2, Plot 7.4, Acting 4.5, Dialog 4.1
review:
(No spoilers) The summary says it all. I read another review where someone said they will go back and watch the movie while listening to some music so he won't have to hear the dialog. That's a great idea.

The visuals are quite good. I don't think they are better than Lord of the Rings but they are quite good. There are several good action sequences. One near the end is amazing.

I think the whole story line ties in well with the future episodes, gives a very good story/history and there's some excellent irony (not the literal kind but the kind that people normally us the word for) in what happens throughout the movie.

There are some scenes where you can almost read on the face of the actors "Do I really have to say this line coming up?" There are several scenes where the direction given to the actors does not seem congruent with the situation. Adding to this is the fact that several characters are mostly/entirely computer animated, so the eyes don't line up (either in the real actors or the animated actors).

I think they used some previous characters well, if not a bit forced. Unfortunately, some of the jokes/puns were so very, very bad I literally heard my wife saying (quietly) "they did not just say that."

It's the start of the summer movies. This one is OK. I went in with moderate expectations. I was somewhat disappointed. I won't rush back to see this one again.

title: Stop the comparisons
review: The vast mojority of people should judge episode 2 as a film on it's own and please stop marking it against the other Star Wars films, you can not and if you have any intellect what so ever should not. You cant compare totally different films it's just impossible to do, you can say which you enjoyed the most but don't rank the films in a table.  My advice to anyone who doesn't know what to think of it is, don't listen to anyone else just judge it as a stand alone film.

title: Behold the return of the Force
review:
The only thing that could possibly have pushed this film farther towards perfection is if Lucas had titled it in a way that let us rearrange the letters in the title to call the film 'Complete Redemption and Deliverance'. Episode I soured many fans, despite it not being entirely worthless--there were good parts in it, and overall it was a decent movie. But anyone who insists that it had no weaknesses whatsoever is quite possibly due for a cat-scan.

Rejoice.

Unquestionably, a complete lack of weaknesses is the case with Episode II.

The acting isn't as campy. Shakespearean at times, but never strained.

The raw passion between Portman and Christensen would have prompted me to have somebody quietly keeping tabs on them off the set--with a set of rings at hand.

Lucas has made every scene's purpose and story foundation solid enough to shame Mt. Everest. Characters don't just do something. They have a deeply moving reason behind what they do--and it's always a reason that would probably drive you or me to do the same thing.

Every frame, every image, every picture of an idea that graces the screen is part of the story. Lucas isn't showing off ILM's latest and greatest; he has taken them up arm in arm and given us the product of two master storytellers weaving a magnum opus.

Passion, beauty, grief, unreleaseable pain, tension, unimagineable energy--all of these threads are perfect, seamless, and awe inspiring to behold. They will leave to you ecstacy of a story so rich and powerful your very soul with reverberate.

George Lucas, I bow to you as a man I respected, lost faith in, and have regained an endless, profound admiration for. The Force is with you once more, and you have shared it with us all.

title: Great movie
review:
Great story, great acting, great dialogue, great scenery and great effects.

5/5 stars from me. Many reviewers have panned this film, I suggest you do yourself a favor, see the film, and decide for yourself, it is one hell of a ride.

title: George keeps getting better
review:
I just saw Star Wars: Attack of the Clones.

Whew.

There are not too many words I know of to describe how excellent this movie really is. But I will try.

This is by far one of the best movies, including Star Wars movies, I have ever seen. And this is coming from a guy who secretly played with Star Wars toys well into his teens, and who stopped counting how many times he's seen Star Wars after the 150th time.

Before tonight, my official ranking of favorite Star Wars movies went, from best to worst:

The Empire Strikes Back, Star Wars, Phantom Menace, and Return of the Jedi.

Now.

The Empire Strikes Back, Attack of the Clones, Star Wars, Phantom Menace, and Return of the Jedi.

And if were not for Harrison Ford's excellent portrayal of Han Solo and Irvin Kershner's superior directing in the `The Empire Strikes Back', `Attack of the Clones' would rank #1 easily.

I will not give away the story for you. But just a couple of comments.

Unlike `The Phantom Menace', which relied mainly on special effects to drive the movie, this film actually has suspense, drama, romance, and a story. There is a lot of 'edge of your seat' suspense, which I like very much. The special effects are stunning, even more so than `The Phantom Menace'. George really let his imagination explore new territory on this one.

At first I was worried that newcomer Canadian actor Hayden Christensen was not a good fit for the most popular villain of all time, being the great Darth Vader, of course. I was wrong. Hayden proves to be a good fit for the role. Despite his good looks, Hayden can be dark and mysterious.

Natalie Portman also does a great job of her portrayal of Padme, except this time, we get to see some skin! Woo hoo!

Ewan McGregor does a great job of portraying Obi-Wan-Kenobi. This is probably because his character was allowed to grow and take center stage, with Qui-Gon Jinn's character out of the way. In fact, it is my feeling that this film could actually give Ewan a boost into more mainstream leading roles.

George Lucas, after bombarding us with the fluffiness of those damned Ewoks in `Return of the Jedi', and the cuteness of Jar Jar Binks in :The Phantom Menace', has finally got the message: 'Silly Lucas - Star Wars is for adults!' Yes, it is true. This installment of Star Wars is serious enough to bring back those wonderful glory days of `Star Wars' and `The Empire Strikes Back'. Kudos to George!

My final thoughts are -- Please. Please! . PLEASE! Go see this movie! Hurry! Just drop what you are doing and go! Quickly!

title: Ok, Lucas, I forgive you
review: Everything that was wrong with Phantom is cleared up.  The actors are better at their parts (and Anakin is much better as an adult then a kid), Jar Jar is mostly absent (and a little better spoken when he is on stage), the battles are cooler, the plot faster and less "aaaaw, isn't annie a cute kid".  The lines between Amidala and Anakin are a little stiff, but hey, I wasn't very suave when I was nineteen either... heh.  But the way they look at each other.  It is to die for.  And the music, especially the Imperial March (Vader's Theme) haunts Anakin through the film, to the best sceen, where it thunders across the theater.  Wow!  (It was much better than Cats, I'm going to see it again and again)

title: joyful and breathtaking experience of dumbness
review:
I loved Episodes IV, V, VI. I loved 'The Phantom Menace' and watched it three times on big screen and countless on VHS and DVD. Yesterday I saw 'Attack Of The Clones' and have no wish to see it again. Why? This is not because Episode II worse than earlier Episodes. It's not truth. 'Attack' is the same breathtaking outstanding FX show as the early ones. This is just because the times are changing. And after the such startling epic movie as we got with 'Lord Of The Rings' there's no more chances for Star Wars to make the same enormous, fabulous impact. George Lucas, your time is gone. Sorry. Affected sci-fi dumbness is no funny anymore.

7 out of 10, 2 of them - bonuses for previous services.

title: I can't believe it could get worse than Episode I
review: I just got back from this movie. It was horrible. I'm sure a lot of Star Wars fans will argue, and it's good knowing the backround of the characters and whatnot, but the acting, script, and general plot was disgusting. Hayden Christenson cannot act and is definately not worthy of playing young Vader. I think the acting would have been better if they had cast Freddie Prinze Jr. or even Keanu Reeves. That is how bad it is. I adore Natalie Portman, but she was just too dull in this. I can't even think of someone I can give credit to as 'stealing the show,' although I'm glad Samual L. Jackson got more screen time. He deserves it. I'm rating this a 2 out of 10, and I will never in my life ever watch this again, nor will I ever recommend it to anyone, even my worst enemy.

title: Unforgettable and epic
review: Just a couple of words to describe ATOC: unforgettable and epic. Lucas returns back to the right emotion, action and philosophy of The Empire Strikes Back. The CG work is amazing and far from other pictures. It is a must see for everyone. Now, the wait for Episode III starts...

title: Really good but it could have been great
review: I liked this film a lot.  It has all the good elements of the original trilogy, and Lucas has managed to at least downplay Jar Jar and the Trade Federation so that it doesn't interfere with the story.  Sadly, the worst oversite, the need of a new director, has not been remedied.  All the elements are there; the actors are all in top form, the special effects are quite good, and the plot, well, that is why we keep coming back.  What this film needed was someone, other than Lucas, to bring it all together. Someone has to restrain Lucas from throwing in way too much computer animation than he knows what to do with.  Sure the droid/clone battle may be the coolest thing we have ever seen, but it is the failures that really stick in your mind.  The beginning of the "coliseum" seen is one of them. This seemed to just scream fake to me.  Don't get me wrong; the movie holds water, and time only makes an audience more accepting of the problems. Still, in the end we wonder what could have been.

title: Fabulously entertaining. Critics should check their history text books.
review:
--SPOILERS-- From the moment it's kickstarted (that being when a Jedi leaps out the window of a miles-high building) to the much-too-soon ending, this movie left me breathless.

I didn't expect to see Oscar caliber performances here, so I pretty much ignored every critic who has panned this film.

Such critics who say, "too much exposition... and boring political dialogue..." Perhaps they aren't up to snuff on their storytelling.

When Star Wars (that being Episode IV) begins, we are informed that it's a period of GALACTIC CIVIL WAR. How does this begin? Looking to what we've learned in history class, civil war comes about due to political disputes.

Attack of the Clones had me riveted for every frame -- if there weren't three hundred things blowing up on screen, we were being let in on the reasons which lead up to there no longer being a Republic or a Senate.

We see Palpatine already guiding Anakin Skywalker toward the dark side, hooking him, and feeding him the lines that lead Vader to serve at his master's side.

We see that even prior to the events of The Phantom Menace, Palpatine and Dooku have been coordinating their efforts toward a civil war, knowing that it takes these sorts of massive events to force sweeping changes such as the replacement of a Chancellor, or granting "emergency" powers.

We smile, knowingly, as Palpatine says, "When this crisis has passed, I will gladly lay down this power."

Perhaps the critics don't get it. Perhaps they don't understand that only two "good" Jedi will remain at the end of Episode III -- Obi-Wan Kenobi and Yoda will be in hiding, while the Emporer and a scarred and nearly-destroyed Anakin Skywalker will hold the places of power.

title: It's no "Empire", but it comes pretty close.
review: As soon as the music hits and "Star Wars" blazes onto the screen, you are thrown back to a time long ago, when you only knew of George Lucas from American Graffiti. This excitement builds whenever I see the intro, and I am always reminded of the first time I saw A New Hope. You realize this is going to be a great theatrical experience but then you remember... The Phantom Menace made me feel the same way too, that is, until those three paragraphs faded out of view and the movie started. Without giving anything away, I want to say full out that this film is NOT THE PHANTOM MENACE. This is old school Star Wars with new school special effects, plain and simple. We have everything, good guy gusto and bad guy brashness. From the first thrilling scenes to the final close that leaves you wanting more, I felt a tingle that kept with me long after the final credits rolled. But... with all reviews, I have to give some shortcomings. First, the characterization is better (much better) than Menace, but it still feels like Christiansen and most obviously Portman actually have to dumb down their acting skills to play these characters. They don't overact... it's just that they have traditionally played more in depth roles (Life as a House for Christiansen, and Portman's enitire catalog except Menace). Aside from this and one other shortcoming (Yoda is all animated... I miss the puppet. The puppet worked, and looked real enough. Yoda actually gives the movie a cartoony, video game feel.)The movie is fantastic. Most other performances are done extremely well, and for those who think this movie will ruin the classic star wars experience, it won't. I feel it will enhance what you already love, because like I said before... IT IS NOT THE PHANTOM MENACE.

title: FAILURE ON A GRAND SCALE
review: This film is a disaster of cinema on a scale that could probably rank up there with 'Cleopatra' or similar botched attempts at "epic" cinema. George Lucas has, indeed, "lost his touch", as some people have said but it could be more easily explained this way: George Lucas has simply decided that the scripts of his STAR WARS prequels don't really matter that much and can be developed "along the way". In my opinion, and most REALLY GOOD FILMMAKERS would probably agree, this is ASS BACKWARDS. In LucasLand, apparently, you can start with an "idea", pay a huge staff of VERY creative graphic artists and painters to design vehicles, make models, choreograph scenes on the computer without ever having seen THE SCRIPT. Don't agree? Check out THE ART OF STAR WARS: ATTACK OF THE CLONES and you will see pages upon pages of beautiful renderings and designs that were completely wasted on a film with no script. Don't agree? Read the sorry ass excuse for a script at the back of said book. This script is so bad, it is unbelievable. It truly shows how much contempt Lucas has for the written word and this man should never be allowed near a typewriter. If I were one of the designers on this film, or The Phantom Menace for that matter, I would quit. I wouldn't want my BABIES, ships and locales that I slaved over to be used in service of some of the most haphazard and shoddy storytelling this side of Corusant. Don't agree? Watch Anatomy of a Murder. Psycho. Mr. Smith Goes to Washington. Kramer VS. Kramer. Star Wars. Alien. These films all had one thing in common. Before there was a CHECK cut to anyone, there was a script. Before a date was scheduled, there was a SCRIPT. It's too bad that we give Lucas so much power- somebody really needs to say no to this guy. "Sorry George," I would say if I were THAT GUY, "but you may not start this new series of films until I see AT THE VERY LEAST a script for the FIRST ONE. Oh, and most people do five or so drafts and have other people LOOK AT IT so they can tell you when you are being a dunderhead (Jar Jar, or all of the dialogue in AOTC, for example). THEN AND ONLY THEN MAY YOU COMISSION THE ARTISTS NEEDED TO PULL THIS THING TOGETHER! Not before, no, not before." Lucas has put the cart before the horse, my friends and so that is why these films are classically bad. We are witnessing failure on a colossal scale. I'm not talking box office. If these films were good, they would be pulling down twice as much- AT LEAST- no, I'm talking about QUALITY. I'm talking about LOVE. WE LOVE STAR WARS because the first ones (or at least the first two) were made with LOVE. Like Grandma's chocolate chip cookies. The new ones? Apparently Grandma's gone crazy and decided to ALTER THE RECIPE. She is now adding the sugar AFTER BAKING THEM. See how crazy it is?

title: Are you all fools?
review: Everyone seems to be getting sucked into the hype...... All these 'as good as original trilogy' comments are annoying me. This film is bad.  Simple as that. It's not just rose-tinted nostalgia for the old films that makes me dislike this one so much - i can see the good bits, but they are far too few and lost in a sea of CGI crap. I don't want to watch 100 computer generated guys fight another 100 computer generated guys..... when they actually got into some one-on-one lightsabre action with Dooko (or whatever his bloody name was) was much more like it...... If Lucas wants to focus on the lovey dovey bit, fine by me - BUT at least find a pair of actors who have something resembling chemistry.  I found it impossible to believe that Portman and rubbish bloke had any feeling whatsoever for each other - it was like watching droids kiss, it was so mechanical. And if this is indeed a kids film, i wonder how many 8 year-olds out there are itching for heavy discussions about inter-planetary politics.... OK, there were some very pretty CGI bits, but the minute a human actor was in the midst of it the effect was ruined - it reminded me of Who Framed Roger Rabbit, only not as funny.  We liked the Millenium Falcon because it was wobbly and the actors were actually in it, we don't want shiny silvery things that exist only on a hard-drive. This rant appears a bit form-less and random, so I'll shut up now. I hope you all enjoy the film, but doubt you will.

title: Finale worth the wait!
review:
It takes it's time to warm up - Attack of the clones - but the last 30 minutes of so is worth the wait, the 3 year wait, that is.

The only other worthy mention which many people have ignored is Hayden Christiansen's brooding Anakin - watch the way he mimmicks Darth Vader's gait and mannerisms. Unfortunately, the plot is confusing, the acting is amateur, and the digital monsters disappointing, but... The Clonetroopers were cool!! My rating: 9/10 for the final 30 minutes and forget the rest...

title: My view of Star Wars Episode 2
review: After seeing this film i just wanted to see it again. This is more like it, unlike Episode 1 this time its Star Wars. This latest film has more depth and a much better story more like the original films. This one isnt just for the kids it a great action adventure story. The Jedi fight scenes are great bringing all the excitement of the earlier films. My favorite scene has to be Master Yodas fight near the end of the film. I seemed to drag a little in the middle with the romance scenes and most of the kids in the cinema were beginning to get a little impatient, but it is well made up for with the rest of the film. I cant wait now for Episode 3 but its not going to be out until 2005. This is a must see film for anyone, even if your not a Star Wars fan you will love it. i am going to see it again as soon as possible.

title: Better than Phantom Menace...
review:
Okay...so it's not "The Empire Strikes Back," arguably the best Star Wars movie. I will say that it's way better than Episode I - The Phantom Menace.

The action was cool, the story was better, and Yoda, 'nuff said. The acting could've been better, I must confess. Other than that. It was okay.

I'm eagerly awaiting 2005 for the release of Episode III, which I think will be the best in this new trilogy. Keep it up, George.

title: Very Cool, But Tedious At Times (spoilers)
review: This is by far superior to episode 1 and in my opinion just as good as return of the jedi however it does not live up to the empire strikes back. Jar-Jar Binks has a much smaller role in e2, even so people booed at his every appearence at the screening i saw. The tedious part part of the movie is in the numerous drawn out love scenes with flat lines and flatter acting by Hayden. My other complaint would be that Obi-Wan seems a little weak in the movie, easily getting captured and putting up almost no resistence to Count Dooku. However the shortcomings of the film are made up with a cooler than ever jedi battle royale with an army of droids and Samuel L Jackson triumphantly chopping off the head of his foe. However the coup de ta comes when we finally get to see Yoda kick some Dooku but, and exclaim "You have much to learn!" The ticket price is worth it just for this scene alone. The entire audience was cheering when yoda made his hobbling entrance. George Lucas has the force back.

title: Not as good as Episode I
review: Now before you start tuning up, let me get my story finished. I was in the clear minority thinking PM was not that bad..Dont get me wrong, AOTC is great. It just takes too long to get there.. The first half of the movie is really slow.. Finally, it gets going, and it really ends with a bang. Its nice to have just the one piece remaining(Ep III), so now we can say... "How are they going to do this". I will agree with some of the things I have seen already.. George is trying to put in too much. Some of the lines in this script are almost too hammy. There are times when he needs to heed by the idea of "less is more".What made the  first trilogy so terrific, was that you felt what you were watching was  truly about another place, another time.. Here again, just like with the pod race, there are human conventions, trying to make things seem more familiar.These aren't really needed.. John Williams score again is great. Not quite the power of EP I, but the music in the grand finale was really moving. The plusses here were the transformation of Anakin.. You could really see what will turn him in the next chapter. Also, Yoda is incredible!!! When you see him wielding a lightsaber, you'll go nuts!.. His attitude is wonderful in this chapter.. He really takes control of the Jedi council, and acts more as a leader than you have ever seen. This chapter also begins to explain a lot of lore of the first trilogy.. I dont want to give anything away, but prepare to have questions answered. The only real con I have for Episode II is that it cant seem to get out of first gear, But once it gets going... HANG ON!!! 7 out of 10

title: Better than Episode 1 but still not very good.
review:
It looks as though George Lucas has learned from his mistakes in Episode 1. This time around he's upped the action, reduced the politics and brought Episode 2 more into line with the feel of the original trilogy.

Clearly this in itself is enough to keep the fans happy but it does not make Attack of the Clones a good movie by wider standards. Stilted dialogue, wooden acting and a strangely washed-out feel to most of the CGI graphics made the first half of this film in particular, a chore to watch. Can anyone genuinely think of a memorable quote from this one?

Episode 2 did just enough to keep me hanging on for Episode 3 - let's hope George Lucas hires a decent script-writer next time round!

title: Quite Probably The Best Movie I Have Ever Seen
review:
George Lucas has outdone himself this time. If you want to know how good this is, get this: It's better than Episode I! I didn't believe it was possible.

Saruman's appearance wasn't really a surprise, it had to happen eventually. I'm so glad George Lucas has discovered one of the three perfect characters. Lets just hope that Peter Jackson discovers the other two (Captain Typho and JarJar Binks in The Two Towers would be too good).

Jimmy Smits' performance was one of the best I have ever seen, not just by Smits but by anyone. Other stellar efforts were: Temuera Morrison and Hayden Christian. Honestly, where do they get these ingeneous casting ideas?

The fighting was also superb. Especially by Mace Windu and Saruman. Saruman appeared to just doing some weird conceptual dance and Windu had no idea! Most entertaining.

My only real complaint about this movie is that Natalie Portman's outfits weren't quite revealing enough, hopefully Lucas will pick up on this for Episode III: Even More Temuera Morrisons Than Last Time.

title: At last! Another jewel from this franchise!
review: As a major fan of these films, I was elated that this film finally delivered on all cylinders what the past two haven't: an equal to the first two movies. Lucas crams all the excitement and flash of "A New Hope" into a film which somehow manages to also provide enough soul-searching and romance to rival "The Empire Strikes Back". After two efforts that seemed to be aimed toward a younger audience, Lucas gets you excited about Episode 3 again by making "Attack of the Clones" a true gem. Ewan McGregor and Natalie Portman turn in grade A performances as Obi Wan and Padme, and Hayden Christensen does as well as can be expected with such a complex role. In one scene, Christensen gives us a fine preview of a dark-force immersed Anakin when he lets anger get the best of him. Lucas seems to have been stung by fan criticism of the Jar Jar Binks character, as Binks is a very minor player in this one. Jimmy Smits as Bail Organa also has a very small role, but will likely have a much bigger role in the next film. The droids provide a few light moments that are enjoyable. Watch for a part where 3PO says "I'm scrap!" I got quite a laugh on that one. Christopher Lee plays Count Dooku (Darth Tyrannus) with ease, endowing the character with the same strength of presence that Sir Alec Guinness gave "Old Ben" Kenobi in the original series. Samuel L. Jackson gets a much bigger role as Mace Windu this time around, and is up to the task. The fight scenes are, once again, finely choreographed and well shot, and if that isn't enough to get you running to the theater: YODA WITH A LIGHT SABER! No spoilers here, but let me say one thing about this scene: if you saw it in person, you might want to laugh....but then you REALLY wouldn't want to tick Yoda off! Minor complaints: A few of the supporting actors seemed cardboard and stiff at times, but that's been true with all the Star Wars films. All-in-all, a very fun movie that leaves you wanting more.

title: You'll like it or you'll LOVE it
review:
I can't wait to see this movie again. There's too much to take in the first time. The visuals are amazing, the characters are colorful, and the complexity of the situations is interesting. The only way to improve on this movie would probably be through some of the dialogue.

The content of the story presented by this movie gives one a lot of food for thought. I feel like watching Episodes 4-6 again to re-evaluate them based on the new information presented by this movie. For example, I think this movie gives us more insight into Darth Vader's motives and why he turned away from the dark side in the end.

If you wanted more Jedi action after seeing Episode I, this movie will give you an eyeful. As a matter of fact, by the end of Episode II, I found myself starting to take the cool Jedi abilities for granted.

title: Lucas is a Genius!
review: What a great film. It was visualy stunning, it had a great story and YODA ROCKS! I felt the Star Wars of old in this one. THe action is totally awesome. I cant wait for Episode three. Why are you still reading? Go see the movie. Now!

title: Great Action/Slooooooow Dialogue/Still Worth the $8
review:
Wow, talk about mixed feelings about a movie. At some moments, it was:

"Impressive..."--Darth Vader, Episode V

At others:

"I've got a bad feeling about this..."--Episode IV, V, VI, I, II

First, the good--some of the best fight sequences they've ever had, good inside jokes and references, and best of all, we clear up some of that Trade Federation v. Republic v. Jedi Council, who's what where from Episode I. And it was nice to see the opening credit scroll without a mention of an economic crisis in the galaxy--that threw me for a loop at the beginning of Episode I. Hey, it's Star WARS! What's with this economy stuff? And for you Jar Jar haters, he's only in 2 scenes.

As for the bad--in some parts, it is slooooooooooooow, in particular, Anakin's courtship of Amidala. And some of the dialogue between action sequences is not particularly interesting. In those sequences, it often feels like you're watching a Shakespearean play, "And now, I will take leave of you my good lady, but I shall return in a fortnight." Kind of missing Luke and Han's regular guy kind of talk. And though the FX are on the whole magnificent, state of the art, certain CGI images looked a little fakey, though nowhere near as bad as Spiderman.

So, in the end I'd have to say 2.5 stars. But definitely worth seeing--the payoff was so good after long stretches of dull dialogue that it was definitely worth the wait.

title: Better than the last one, thank God
review: It's opening night of this movie and I've just come home from the theater. Sadly, Jar Jar Binks is still in this movie. I tried to use the force myself to have his character killed, but it didn't work out. As far as storyline goes, this movie was pretty good because it really brought a lot of things together. People and events of the original 3 movies (IV, V, and VI) start to come together in this one. The problem with it is that Lucas still felt it necessary to include the lame, infantile one-liners that make people over the age of 10 cringe. Shoreline Theaters was overrun with little children who have probably never seen the original films, and who probably can't appreciate any plot developments (yes, it has some). So as I expected, I was struck by the commercialism of the movie and at times I felt as if I were watching an infomercial, not a film. Lucas included some garbage that made it hard to take some of this one seriously. All I can say is, thank God it wasn't The Phantom Menace again.

title: Short Changed, and possibly worse than TPM!!!
review:
George Lucas needs to start listening to the fans!! I can understand that the films are HIS and therefore he makes them they way he wants. But the rest of the world doesn't live in a fantasy world. Anyway.... Disappointed would be an understatement as to how I felt when leaving the cinema on opening night. Short Changed would be more accurate, and I feel I was not the only one for whom "The Force" did not come home.

Okay, so there's action - but you have to wait 2 hours to get to it, and it still doesn't stand against the opening attack in "Empire" or even the assault on the Death Star in "Jedi". A lot has been said already about the so-called acting in AOTC - and I agree with the negativity. But that's not the fault of the actors, it's largely to do with being placed in front of a Blue-screen with nothing to look at. Poor performances from Hayden, Natalie & Christopher Lee. Outstanding performance from Jar Jar - as he's barely in it!

The scenery and SFX are good, but I want something more like Episodes IV, V & VI, where it feels like you're involved. George GIVE US A STORY!!!

I read the book first, and it's 10 times better. Maybe the DVD release will include a far better opening (speeder chase on Tatooine according to book), more "family" scenes between Jango & Boba Fett etc. There's just no emotion in the movie at all.

But I can't be ALL negative - seeing Yoda fighting is AWESOME. Sent a wave of euphoria through the cinema and rightly so. In summary, wait for the DVD! The book left me wanting more NOW, sadly the movie didn't! Episode 3 has to be SPECIAL to make me see it!

title: The Greatest Space Saga in the Universe Continues......
review: This movie is absolutely awesome. The special effects are excellent and the continuation of the story seems much deeper and meaningful this time around. Seeing the developing life of Anikin kept me rivited for the whole movie. I loved it. :)

title: Certainly better than Episode I and a true Star Wars movie!!
review:
If you're a Star Wars fan, you won't be disappointed with this movie. It seems that George Lucas learned the lesson with Episode I and brought back the action and thrill on this one.

Yes, the dialogues are often lame, the "love story" is an unbelievable collection of clichés, but hey, this is supposed to be a FUNNY movie, not art, and as a funny summer movie Episode II delivers.

I rate this one the third best Star Wars movie overall, after The "Empire Strikes Back" and "A New Hope".

title: Bad acting, slow pace.
review: While this one was better than the first, it was still poorly acted and paced way too slowly. There were too many times you could tell that it was just a guy acting in an empty room. There were at least a couple action scenes that were either direct references to other Star Wars movies or completely gratuitous.  Heck, even the actors sounded bored.

title: I am thankful that I was one of the first in the world to see this.
review:
Star Wars Episode 2 - Attack of the Clones has reawakened the joy of Star Wars in me. I live in New Zealand and we were favoured by the time zones, to see the world premiere of this before the rest of the world.

I can only image what it was like to see the advances in technology in the original Star Wars film (afterwards renamed Episode IV - A New Hope), but I feel that this was a similar leap in audio visual entertainment. Industrial Light and Magic have outdone themselves yet again, though I am beginning to feel that Skywalker Sound is giving the sound effects a bit too much of a sameness... when will R2 say something other than the soundbites from the original movies?

The backgrounds are stunning and the plot I found was a little easier to follow than the previous episode. I don't know whether this is because the film is structured better or because characters that we are being introduced to are ones that have already been involved in later episodes. I certainly get the feeling that chunks of the Star Wars "jigsaw puzzle" are coming into place.

Fans will notice that a lot of dialog is delivered in similar fashion as the other films we have already seen; some of Amidala's lines are reminiscent of things that Leia says in Return of the Jedi, and we hear the usual verbal jousting... "join me and together we will..." etc. This seems to follow Lucas's intent that everything "rhyme". Themes and constructs are mirrored throughout the Star Wars story to give a semblance of wholeness. I don't think it's cheesy, but some may disagree.

Speaking of cheese, many critics will be happy to know that the role of Jar-Jar Binks is peripheral at most, and when we do see him he is being less of a twit.

It's about time we saw Master Yoda in action. We've heard people rant and rave about how he's so powerful, and you'll be happy to know that we finally see a slice of what he is capable of.

My only problem and I don't know if it is a world wide one was that the film looked grainy (I guess I'll have to see it a few more times to see whether or not it was just the theatre that I was at ^_^).

Throw in some gorgeous critters, more highspeed chase scenes that you can shake a stick at and light sabers everywhere and you have a high paced romp that is leaving me (at least) primed for the next installment.

title: Looks good, sounds terrible
review:
When an audience gasps at an amazing looking backdrop, thats nice. When the same audience laughs out of shock at what they have just heard in the scene, thats not so good.

This film looks great, no question. And the action is certainly well directed apart from the usual video game friendly inserts. But the script is beyond a joke.

At times I thought that I was watching a set of big budget Monty Python sketches. The dialogue only had two settings; acceptable and dire. I don't expect hip irony - but watching Anakin chew through more poorly written adolescent wailing is not entertaining in the least.

At the end of the film some parts of the audience were starting to clap, but the instinct was immediately snuffed out by the sense of disbelief felt by most of us.

And yes, Yoda rocks.

title: Almost there...
review:
• Those of us who hated Phantom Menace had several reasons to do so, few of which pertain to Attack of the Clones. Lucas apparently has learned from his previous errors and has taken steps to reclaim his empire. Clones breathes new life into a saga that a lot of us feared was spiraling into irrelevancy.


  • Attack of the Clones brings with it not nearly as much childishness or silliness that burdened The Phantom Menace. The new tale is better written with a plot that is a lot less hazy than the first prequel. The acting has improved considerably as well, but this is probably a benefit from having a better screenplay.


  • The film opens strongly enough with an assassination attempt on Senator Amidala. When the visually eye-popping speeder chase gets the action started nicely, it is obvious that Attack of the Clones is a different breed of movie. As the night darkened, Bladerunner-esque buildings wizz by, thoughts of The Phantom Menace begin to slowly fade away.


  • The ensuing mystery propels the plot forward, with the Amidala/Anakin romance not bogging things down nearly as much as rumor may have it. Their scenes with each other (most set in front of spectacularly beautiful landscapes)are playful and warm but not as touching as they should be. Though the script drags here and there in the middle, there isn't much time to worry about that before the final act commences and we are again deeply entrenched in Lucas' universe.


  • Though not perfect, the final 45 minutes are a study in science fiction filmmaking, each minute rising higher and higher to fever pitch. The surprises here are numerous and breathtaking. These last scenes hold the key to what Star Wars fans have been yearning for. Even though Lucas doesn't use this key to unlock the brilliance of the original trilogy, he leads us dutifully to the door, where we will can wait comfortably until he opens it in Episode III.

title: Fantastic Adventure
review: If you loved The Phantom Menace, this is nothing for you. The Phantom Menace was a kid's adventure movie, this is a dark story of passion and pure evil. Anakin Skywalker is now a grown-up, and he is well on his way to embrace the dark side. The love-story between Anakin and Padme is central to the story, the rest is merely essential to tie this trilogy to part IV-VI. It's a great adventure movie, and I really recommend it!

title: The Star Wars saga just died for me tonight.
review:
[Contains one plot element that is not really a spoiler. It is a happy moment in an otherwise dismal experience.]

The Star Wars saga just died for me tonight. Episode II is dull and lifeless. The only scene that roused the crowd was when we finally got to see Yoda in action. Yet, even this moment was cut short, as the few true moments are, while the rest is either painfully stagnant or a blur of incomprehensible action. The vaunted digital effects are overwhelming and actually detract from the advancement of the story. You could forgive Episode I as the difficulty of getting back in the saddle after 20 years just like the ponderously bad first StarTrek movie. Episode II is a violation of the very spirit of adventure that Star Wars brought to us all.

If I had not been so depressed, I would have cried.

title: Excellent!!!
review:
I went to see this at a preview midnight showing on Wednesday night/Thursday morning of opening day - the movie was showing in 3 or 4 screens and all appeared packed out - The 2+ hours that followed were a VAST improvement over episode 1(which i liked, but could have been better) and appeared to have been enjoyed by all who attended.

I've heard some people say that they thought Anakin was acted badly, but his arrogance and annoyance was apparent as i had expected for his character, and all the other characters were played brilliantly by a great cast - Yoda has been replaced by a completely computer generated character which works even better than what i feared when i heard about it(jar jar, although not as annoying to me as to others, just didnt looks right in some scenes of episode 1), but most of all was Ewan McGregor's absolutely flawless performance as Obi Wan Kenobi and a nice performance from Samuel L. Jackson as Mace Windu - the two actors clearly showing how much they are enjoying playing their parts and are completely comfortable with their roles. Also a lot more subtle an introduction for characters which will play an important role in the following episodes(Bobba Fett, Owen Lars, Bail Organa), having them actually be included as part of the plot and not just because they need to be worked in for continuity with the back story as in episodes 4-6.

A HUGE improvement over episode 1, and surely a sign that even better things are to come in episode 3. Overall, story wise(the love story, though not perfectly handled, worked within the story), acting wise(some nicely timed touches of comedy make the characters more believable in their situations), and effects wise(the chase in coruscant, and the huge conflict seen in the film looks absolutely amazing, and is hopefully only a glimpse of the clone wars from episode 3).

Overall - 9/10

title: Lucas delivers at the fifth time of asking
review:
Anyone who comes to watch the six Star Wars episodes back-to-back, in chronological order, in a few years time will be able to appreciate just how far we've come in twenty five years of special effects. Here Lucas moves on from the contrived set pieces of The Phantom Menace, and uses his Industrial Light and Magic company to breathe life into the world of the Galactic Republic. Finally, Star Wars has context, vivacity and depth, and this for the first time in five mega-grossing movies.

The story is perfunctory, but just about sufficient to justify the 140 minute running time, while the dialog is as wooden as we've come to expect. There has been some unjust criticism of the performance of the leads, but there is only so much an actor can do when he has to repeat the line "I really don't like flying" four times in one film.

The point is that Attack of the Clones has excitement, pace and human interest. It is worth remembering that Star Wars was never supposed to deliver Olivier-style dramatic monologues, or bucketloads of existential angst.....it's a straightforward story of cowboys and indians: goodies and baddies in space, with the odd twist thrown in for good measure.

What's missing of course is a sense of consequence.....in the same way that we knew the Titanic was doomed, we know where Anakin and Padme's romance will lead them, something Lucas is obviously conscious of when he inserts lines that foreshadow later events, as when Obi Wan asks Anakin, "Why do I get the feeling you'll be the death of me?" Similarly, it's hard to take Christopher Lee's character seriously as a baddy when we only introduces to him and his story at the point when the climactic battle scenes begin.

But these criticisms pale besides the visual achievement that this film represents. It is truly possible to feel that you are soaring through hundreds of different worlds as McGregor makes a serious of sweeping visits to other planets, and even to a vast library that stores every kind of information about the galaxy. For the first time since Jurassic Park introduces us to the possibilities of CGI, this is a film that can be rightly described as breathtaking. Towards the climax there is a sense of effect overkill, and you have to ask whether this visual feast spills over into an orgy, but even then there are enough dramatic events to keep the viewer riveted through to the end.

3/5

title: Wonderful action, terrible love story
review:
Thank you George Lucas for continuing the saga continued from the Phantom Menace. The action sequences in this movie are awesome, the graphics are spectacular. The love story between Anakin and Padme is lacking in depth of acting (or was it the directing?), and dialogue.

I really enjoyed the use of digitally placed graphics to create aliens, spaceships, weapons, etc. This added to the entire movie. Lucas' special effects unit has come a long way in making digital graphics look believable.

The action sequences were exhilarating! The Jedi standoff is spectacular, worthy of any action film. The light saber duals are well choreographed, especially the one with Yoda.

While Senator Amidala's dialogue is poor through most of the movie, Natalie Portman delivers it the best that a actress could. She is stunning and radiant, brightening any scene that she is in.

C3PO returns as the comic relief. Jar-Jar is much more enjoyable in a small role. R2D2 is sturdy and present as always.

I commend all Star Wars die-hards to see this film, you might be a little disappointed, but not like you were with Phantom Menace.

title: George is forgiven!
review:
That really was something else. I went into the cinema with low expectations after the Phantom Menace but I was over the moon with Episode 2.

The film does have a few slow spots as they try to build the romance up between Padme and Anakin but the last half hour or so take you on a rollercoaster ride in the battle on Geonosis.

There is a lot more humanity in the characters this time round with quite a few enjoyable one liners between ObiWan and Anakin, and as for Yoda, wow, now we know why he is the master!

And yes, JarJar is in the film but luckily his screen time is probably less then five minutes, although he does play a very key part in the commencement of the Clone Wars.

Roll on Episode 3!

review:
