title: Episode III is going to be amazing on this evidence
review:
I saw episode II last night, and after the disappointment of Phantom Menace, went in with slightly lower expectations this time around. I needn't have done so. This is a much, much better film than Menace.

The best compliment that I can give to this film is that it feels like a star wars film. Thematically, it is very much in tune with the original three films, with more explicit lines beginning to appear between good and evil. You get a real sense throughout the film of the break up of the republic and the start of the problems which will eventually destroy it.

Hayden Christensen is excellent as Anakin, managing to be pull off being the most powerful jedi in the universe, whilst also a sullen and arrogant teenager. It is an extraordinary performance that points the way nicely towards his fall from grace in the next installment.

Relationships are also explored more deeply in this film, particularly between Anakin and Padme, and Anakin and Obi-Wan, the latter being particularly interesting, with a mixture of love, respect, lack of trust and Anakin's wayward behaviour making for compelling viewing.

The action sequences are unlike anything you have ever seen, I wish I could say more, but believe me, your jaws will collectively drop and you will find yourself just grinning like a schoolboy for almost and hour. (Just like me) In addition to this, Yoda........ Oh My God!

Despite what I have said, there are problems with this film. Of course Lucas cannot write dialogue and that is evident here, there are a couple of moments which make you wince at the cheesiness of the lines, but they are not bad enough, or often enough to detract from the pleasure of the film. Surprisingly, the direction is not all that bad. I always felt that Empire and Jedi were better directed movies than Star Wars, and this was confirmed by Menace. However, this is a rather better affair, with (reminiscent of Jedi) several plots progressing simultaneously, keeping the pace quick and the audience interested.

Although the dialogue is dodgy, the bearded one has got it right in a big way this time. C3PO and R2 are here, Jar Jar is not for very long, the fighting is excellent, bloody excellent and the new actors excel themselves. Christensen as Anakin is a believable future Darth Vader and Christopher Lee as baddie Count Dooku bring a touch of old school class to proceedings. Jackson is cool again and has a bigger role, and Jango Fett, (father of Boba who also makes an appearance) is a cool bad guy and one of the many links that this film provides with the original trilogy.

This film has me salivating at the thought of Episode III. I truly believe it is going to be absolutely unbelievable. Enjoy

title: True Star Wars
review: This Star Wars movie is simply fantastic. It definitely lives up to my expectations of it. George Lucas is really good at building up stories and I cannot wait to see how the last of this trilogy ends - well, I know how it ends but I cannot wait to see how Lucas describes it. And then I must say that Yoda is THE MASTER!

title: Yoda kicks butt...
review: While not perfect, it's a worthy entry in the Star Wars Saga... Sure there are some slow scenes (i.e. the whole love subplot) and some less than perfect CGI effects, but there are so many great things in this movie it's easy to forgive the lesser parts. When the pace picks up and the clone war breaks out - it's pure movie magic, so just sit back and enjoy the ride... Oh one more thing - Yoda kicks butt!!!

title: Roll on Episode III
review:
Like many others, I have been waiting to see Attack of the Clones with eager anticipation. I have avoided (or tried to avoid) the trailers, and any TV spots, so that I could see it fresh.

I was looking forward to it so much, probably too much...

The special effects and set pieces are phenomenal and it's good to see George Lucas back on form. The effects are so good, that they are unnoticeable in many cases, and that is excellent. But what is unfortunate is that it seems as though the time and consideration has been put into this at the expense of the script.

The dialogue is clunky and laboured in many cases - these are not bad actors, they are just dealing with some really awful lines.

The first hour of the film is very slow, but it is worth the wait. From then on we move from one set piece to another - the introduction of new characters into the mix is great and very enjoyable. Jango Fett and Count Dooko are great villains!

There are many references to the future in this film - from the Death Star plans, to the clone army / stormtroopers; and Bail Organa to Owen and Beru. Episode III certainly holds a lot of promise.

It is a clever film, both enjoyable and thrilling, but I was expecting more... Maybe at 28 I'm just too old for Star Wars...

I think the pull to the dark side (Lord of the Rings) is just a little too strong!

title: Much better than The Menace, but not enough
review: The Attack is much better than the Phantom Menace - with well-developed story, more detailed characters, better acting, much more action and sense. But it is still quite enough dull and shallow. In 70-ies it could be fantastic movie, but now, when we have The Matrix, Spiderman etc. it is not so easy to impress. And all these "copy-and-paste-from-another movie" moments... "Gladiator", "The Fifth Element", "Lara Croft", "Blade Runner". We have even some "Titanic" moments. Scale: 7 out of 10 at most, maybe 6 and a half. Waiting for The Matrix 2 and 3...

title: A better script and this might have been the best one yet!
review:
There are so many mixed reviews of Episode 1, but my stance is that it was pretty poor. I came out of the cinema wanting to like it and went back 2 times in an attempt to enjoy it, but at the end of the day was left cold. The dialogue was clunky and poorly delivered by pretty much everyone, Obi Wan was stiff (ooer) and uncharismatic, the Young Anikin was just young and unintresting, Ja Ja Binks was annoying, the Pod Race wasn't as exciting as it should have been and the end was absurd with Anakin saving the day by complete accident! The main saving grace was Darth Maul and the lightsabre battle, but it was not enough for me to save the film from being a major disappointment.

So onto Episode 2. One of the inherent problems with this saga I feel is that, where the original 3 were set amidst an Empirical rule, the Jedi's all but wiped out, they were able to concentrate on a bunch of misfits coming together to fight evil. Thats part of what made them work so well, thier simplicity. In this proceeding trilogy though there is so much more politics involved in the development of the story and politics is rarely intersting, even when discussed by Jedi Knights. This is a problem that I feel Lucas really needed to focus on, if he had got a better sreenwriter to write the dialogue for these scenes, as well as some of the slower parts between Anakin and the the Queen, then he might have really kept our interest throughout the whole film. As it is we have to sit through a mis-paced and clunkily scripted mid section in Episode 2 before things really get going. I have to admit, I was on the verge of being a bit bored at times, during the mid section involving Anakin and Amidala's blossoming love and Obi Wan's investigation of the strange Cloners. I didn't even think the episode 1 suffered from poor pacing quite as much as this lengthy section of the film did.

Which is a shame, because for the rest of the film Episode 2 is up there with them all, even matching The Empire Strikes Back at times!! There I've said it! Hayden Christensen is excellent as Anakin, he is likable and has a good screen presence, yet we are unsure of him as he expertly shows flashes of the arrogonce and anger that will take him to the dark side. Ewen McGregor is much much better as Obi Wan, though at times he slips back into his stiff and forced speech, but during the fight scenes he really makes up for it. Natilie Portman is a lot better and seems to come to life more away from her royal duties and there is definatly a chemistry between her and Anakin that, whilst not quite rivaling that between Leia and Han Solo, does help us empathise with them. As for the rest of it well the list of positives is endless..Tusken Raiders, Jawa's, R2 and 3P0 (though be prepared for some really cheesy comedy oneliners from 3PO!!), JangaFett and the story of how BobaFett was created, Jedis kicking ass, Yoda kicking ass (I really wasn't prepared for this bit, a real crowd pleasing moment!)and loads of new monsters and creatures. In terms of relentless breathtaking action then there is no doubt that the final 45 minutes or so of Episode 2 outclasses the whole series by far, the effects are awesome, the fights are amazing, the good guys are likable, the bad guys are cool....Its darker, louder and faster for most of the film than the others and this time I came out of the cinema knowing I'd enjoyed it.

So to sum up, the beginning is promising, but you will have to risk being slightly bored before that promise is delivered on in the final hour. But what an hour! An hour of Star Wars done how it should be! Plus I think Episode 3 is really gonna be good!!

title: Wow - George is back!
review: This is by far the best of the Star Wars films to date, there is a great balance in the force here. The story is good, the humour is funny and dry, not slapstick. The action is spectacular and only used to enhance the story, not as a set piece to wow the audience. The final battles are amazing, Yoda is one cool M.F. (as is Samuel L.) there are some unexpected twists and turns and even few 'in jokes' (try to spot the X-Wing, TIE fighter and Millenium Falcons).

title: Much better, thank you George...
review:
A considerable improvement from Phantom Menace. The back story continues and we start to see some maturity developing in the characters and their interactions. R2 and 3PO seem to be getting on well, the Anakin/Padme relationship is developing nicely and the start of Palpatine's influence upon Anakin is shown. Finally, Anakin's opening to the dark side is witnessed and we recall Yoda in TESB - "Anger, fear, aggression; the dark side of the Force are they".

Solid performances from Ewan McGregor, Natalie Portman and Sam Jackson who all appear far more comfortable in their roles. This is supported by charismatic turns from Christopher Lee and an impressive Temuera Morrison. The only slightly wooden performance was from Hayden Christensen, though I get the distinct feeling that his creativeness was rather "pruned". Still, he plays it by the numbers and I have hopes for the next instalment.

The set pieces keep you on the edge of your seat, though there is a distinct feeling of deja-vu. A chase through Coruscant leaves one thinking of Bladerunner and The Fifth Element; the ampitheater scene has obvious Gladiator overtones about it. However, Lucas always makes nods to other films and there are plenty of other references. Overall, it has an "old fashioned" feel to it - a 50s matinee type.

Humour is also used well through the film and there are nice nods to the other films in the series - a ledge scene for Anakin and Padme similar to Luke and Leia's in the original film; Anakin having "a bad feeling about this"; Anakin's injury at the hands of Dooku; Padme's costumes and hair becoming increasingly like Leia's etc (and George - you did Carrie a favour with the tape in Star Wars, the least you could do is to extend it to Natalie...).

OK, so Jar Jar is still there, but his role is less. Seeing Yoda go to work with a lightsaber (green of course!) more than makes up for his inclusion in this vastly improved chapter. Looking forward to chapter 3...

title: A vast improvement from Episode I, but not quite there yet
review: A darker tone than in Episode I and a more serious note (all those who hated Jar Jar and cute little Ani will be pleased) makes for a step very much in the right direction compared to the messy kiddy movie  that was Episode I. The characters benefit from a deeper profile and a fuller content in terms of a story (although not yet close to the consistent and easily followed storyline of episodes IV - VI) that does a credible job of teeing up the evolution of the character of young Anakin Skywalker and providing additional background to the rise of the empire. The movie does however suffer from sub standard acting performances by almost all parties involved (with the exception of a brilliant Christopher Lee), but on the other hand it's Star Wars, who cares?  Fantastic effects and camera work as usual, but the good Mr. Lucas is becoming too smitten with the possibilities offered by digital imagery. Every shot is overloaded. Overall not bad, and certainly provides faith that Episode three could be just right.

title: Visually superb,but..............
review: This film has some of the best special effects since The Matrix but this alone cannot make a film. Lucas seems to want to make us see the loving side of Skywalker but unforunately these scenes are quite awful especially the one with the two rolling around in a field - this is meant to be Star Wars where are the light sabres. In the end they did make a superb appearance with possibly the Star Wars fight EVER yes EVER it is Yodas fight with Count Dooke. When the script failed a joke was stuck in some worked others didn't. As usual Ewan McGregor was very good with Samuel L Jackson proving again that he is one of the best actors around. In the end i looked at my watch to notice just how quickly the mega 150 minutes had gone by only then to think what has actually happened no much the answer! but then again it is Star Wars!

title: The first one was annoying, the second one just boring.
review:
I saw the movie yesterday in a sold-out theater in Paris. Although the audience seemed to like it, it was a very disappointing experience for me. I didn't like the actors, the dialogue was flat, the love story didn't function at all. There was no sense of timing or suspense in this picture.

I really think the first STAR WARS - Episode was annoying, but the second one is just boring. Who cares if the Special Effects are great when there are no likable characters.

Lucas is an untalented director and a really bad writer, nevertheless he is going to write and direct the next one... I don't think that anyone in the right mind is looking forward to Episode III now.

*/****(one for Yoda)

title: So Much Fun
review:
The plot is convoluted and confusing. The narrative is full of holes. The acting is functional at best. The script veers from the sublime to the ridiculous The FX are stunning. The fight scenes are thrilling. The lightsabres go zzzzzzsssswwiiiiiinnng.

I loved it.

title: Disappointing
review:
I have seen the Episode Two on its premiere night in Zagreb, Croatia. Apart from it being organized as a very exciting event, I was disappointed. The new prequel of the Star Wars saga lacks in many things that would make a good movie; good story, good acting and good dialogues. Yes, special effects are great. Yes, the movie is almost perfect _visually_, but other than that...

Hayden Christensen looks fine, handles the sword in a very cool way, moves well, but his acting is horrible. Ewan McGregor, who is normally a good actor, has such stupid lines that he couldn't show off his acting skills even if the Force has inspired him. Samuel L. Jackson, otherwise a cool dude, is very pale and his role is quite uninspiring. Christopher Lee looks like a retired count Dracula, i.e. not a least bit scary or threatening (but ridiculous), while Nathalie Portman, apart from being beautiful, doesn't really deliver anything that would be convincing, including her supposedly great and tortured love for Anakin.

The dialogue is shallow, love story seems more like a reckless fling between two spoiled teenagers than the deep and passionate affair that it was supposed to be, and one can hardly escape malicious satisfaction derived from the knowledge that it will NOT end well. The worst part (and here comes a tiny bit of spoiler) is when Anakin tells Padme about his slaughtering spree, which sounds as if she told her: "Honey, I'm sorry, but I am a war criminal!", and her reaction to that is almost as if she said: "Oh, well, who can blame you...you were SO stressed out!".

All in all, bad. Better than "Phantom Menace", but...what isn't?

title: Much Better
review: Episode II is much better than Episode I.  The action, acting, story, and even Jar Jar (note that I still hate Jar Jar) was better.  Though Jar Jar messed everything up for the entire galaxy thats ok, this is a must see and I give it 2 thumbs and 2 big toes up.

title: Very happy about this movie
review:
A huge success. This movie had adventure and excitement. For those who crave not such things, however, it also had intrigue, character conflict, insight, emotion, and an extremely well constructed sense of helplessness.

Of all the criticisms that are dogging this movie, wooden acting and and bad dialogue seem to be the most common. I just want to say that I didn't find the acting wooden, I found it suitably restrained. Christenson (sp?) and Portman are portraying characters that are being forced to suppress their emotions and I felt that they did that quite well, hinting at their reactions rather than wearing them on their sleeve, and allowing their emotions to show when the plot called for such developments.

As for the bad dialogue, I think there's a difference between bad dialogue and dialogue that is not naturalistic. Although some of the lines may make hardened cynics wince a tad, I have no objection to giving Lucas the creative license to be a bit of a Romantic. This is a galaxy far far away after all, not a slice of life love story set in modern day New York.

Although 3PO's punny sense of humour is shamelessly awful in this movie, I have an odd sense of humour and admired Lucas' sheer gall in injecting such bad jokes into the movie.

After one viewing,I think this is the second best movie in the series (after Empire of course). Easily far better than the two movies it is sure to be compared to: Lord of the Rings and Spider Man. An absolutely fantastic movie.

title: The worrying is over.
review: All concerns that this film would fall into the same traps that Phantom Menace suffered from were banished in the first half hour.  'Clones' delivers plot and action in spades, the visuals are outstanding and the soundscape is very impressive.  Sure the dialogue and acting aren't great, but hey this is Star Wars!

title: It -feels- like Star Wars.
review:
AOTC's greatest triumph is highlighting how non-Star-Wars TPM was. AOTC feels like Star Wars. Moreover, it is a better film than ROTJ and TPM.

It's not as visceral as ANH in terms of emotion... it closer to the greys of ESB. But its also about repressed emotion, so it does feel cold. But, to quote Besson, emotion comes from the resistance to emotion.

Forget the nitpickers and naysayers - especially those who ignore the failings of the original trilogy, in favour of a myth about the SW myth - the flaws in AOTC are the same endearing flaws found in all the SW films. Sure, it shares somes flaws with TPM that the others do not have (Jar Jar, less charismatic actors, slower pace) but they're far fewer in number.

My biggest gripe with AOTC is John Williams' score. I'm not a fan of JW but his score in TPM was my fave aspect of that movie - it was barely noticeable here.

P.S.

To those, like Roger Ebert, who are using AOTC a rallying cry against HD... get over it. You may be an adequate film critic Ebert, but I doubt you know your ASA from your F-Stop, yet alone your HD from your 2K scans. I wonder if you managed to spot the HD footage in TPM? Besides, AOTC is an incorrect gauge on that debate given that it was mostly bluescreen... and the actors were extracted from a 'matted' HD 16x9 frame and placed in a high resolution 2.40 frame.

P.P.S.

To those who want Peter Jackson to direct EP3... 9 months ago I would've agreed with you. But GL has done something remarkable in AOTC which PJ failed to do in FOTR. GL resisted the temptation to telegraph every moment as a big event. He had restraint.

title: WAYYYY BETTER THAN TPM, "ALMOST" A RIVAL TO ESB IN ITS TONE
review:
well first off.... it was wayyyyy better than TPM. Better effects, faster paced, longer (gives a little more time to develop the story), and of course.... less Jar-Jar.

The really great thing about jar-jar being in this one is ..... it's all his fault! all of it! NONE of the things that unfold in this film and the remaining ones would have occured if jar-jar hadnt been on the senate floor to put forth a motion. So now i can rest easily knowing that as annoying as he might be.... the emperor's rise to power is all his fault. I like him a lot better now.

After watching the film 6 times now, I still cannot tell for sure if N*Sync is in the film or not...... i "think" i recognized a few of them though....(i suppose i should be happy that i don't know exactly what they look like) but if it was them, it wasn't all that bad either. Hell.... they were only extras anyways. I'm actually jealous... I would LOVE to be an extra.

The acting is as cheesy as the original trilogy.... Hayden does some wonderful mood swings throughout.... giving us a real preview of what is to come. Ewan is pulling off a GREAT obi-wan.... I could really beleive that this man will grow up to be Guiness.

The occasionaly one-liners and puns made it fun. As did the effects, which were great except for a few of the CG creatures. Great job on yoda though. ILM has come a long way since digitally reinserting Jabba into starwars IV.

The only problems I had in general were the score (somewhat a rehash of the previous 4 scores), not enough screen time for the clone/jedi/droid battle, not enough screen time for the lightsaber duels and the one thing thats really been missing...... a huge space battle. There is a small little scuffle between Obi and Jango.... but as good as it was, that really didnt do much to quench my thrist.

I wouldn't say that it's darker than ESB.... but it does come close. There are a few disturbing images... like Yoda hanging out with the clones, the aliens of Camino were kinda eerie, and of course the tusken camp adventure..... i think something that added a lot to the overall dark tone in ESB though was the use of lighting and environments. The icyness of Hoth, the blackness with blues and orange-red in the carbon freezing chamber, the bleakness and barren feel to the asteroid belt, the darkness and fog of Dagobah. Those lights and envoirnments just intensified the dark events that occured in ESB. AOTTC on the otherhand, offers only a brief glimpse of the darkness of space (also with asteroids) and the rainy planet of Camino. Everything else is clear weather and bright lights for the most part. This doesnt do much to intensify any tone or events. Had the environments been better selected.... had Coruscant not been in daylight hours, had the lighting been more blues and blacks...... i think it would have far surpassed ESB in the emotional tone.

I look forward to three years from now.... meanwhile I'm going to try to find a digital theater to watch AOTC in now.

Critics are such idiots.....I dont know why people put so much faith in them.

title: Darth Vader was a teenage weenie.
review: It's totally unbelievable that this Anakin-kid becomes the most evil person in the galaxy. Obi Wan should have slapped this weenie a few times in the face and Darth Vader would have never existed. Save yourself some cash and watch the original trilogy at home.

title: Bring in the Clowns, Bring in the Clones...
review: hollow dialogue, winded love scenes, but Yoda rocked?!?  Did you feel this way too?  George give up writing man!  Windu the purple light saber makes me feel as though you're working your way toward a red saber...?  A Jedi is selfless did you need to have a purple saber so badly to see yourself? Hmm, all in all we've grown far more mature than our childhood fantasys.  I loved the effects, I wanted to love the characters but couldn't alas, George, I will only see the next one because I have to.

title: Simply the best Star Wars ever...
review:
If Episode 1 was a kid movie, which was for most fans a failure, this one has nothing to do with it. No more Jar Jar Binks, no more midichlorian stuff, no more playstation-podracer championship.

Remembre that in the first trilogy, Empire Strike Back was the second one... This one, the dark movie seems also to be the second one. "Expecting the third with great impatience, I am..."

title: it could have been a good movie...
review: in my opinion amidala & anakin are very weak actors. absolutely there is no "pathos": in "return of the jedy" you can see luke skywalker fighting against himself and the dark side of the force, but anakin is just a spoilt kid angry for the loss of his mother. some locations are ridiculous (the city at the beginning of the movie, the pursuit with  the speeders... just a bad carbon copy of blade runner). I liked very much Yoda's fight against christopher lee and some scenes of the war.

title: Lucas Strikes Back With Ep-II But Still...
review:
Ep-II opens with Anakin Skywalker as a young man. We don't know much about his life since Ep-I except that he is the padawan (pupil) of Obi-Wan Kenobi. They care about each other but have frequent mentor-pupil arguments even in the presence of others. Queen Amidala is now a senator representing her people. Nothing much is told about her life either. The plastic painted face of the Queen is thankfully missing.

George Lucas seems to be strongly influenced by criticism of Ep-I as we see very little of Jar Jar Binks and nothing of the kid Jake Lloyd. Looks like nobody told him that the pod race was way too long (not to be interpreted as bad). The chase sequences in Ep-II are long too and leaves you with a DEJA VU. First we have Obi-Wan and Anakin chasing the assassin (interesting only at the beginning). Then we have Obi-Wan chasing the Bounty Hunter. I cannot help comparing Ep-I and Ep-II every time I see a glimpse of similarity.

Hayden Christensen was a pleasant surprise. Frankly, I did not expect him to act well at all (haven't seen him in anything important, that is). He turns out to be an intense actor (a rarity nowadays). At times he is stiff. You gotta check yourself, Hayden. Natalie Portman, on the other hand, needs serious acting lessons. I didn't see much of it in Ep-I. I thought may be her inch deep make-up and ridiculous head-gear were making it difficult. I was proved wrong. She is just dull and CANNOT emote. There is absolutely NO CHEMISTRY between Christensen and Portman. The romantic scenes look deliberate. Queen Amidale should seriously consider change of wardrobe to match her figure.

However, it was a delight to watch Ewan McGregor as a more mature Jedi Obi-Wan Kenobi. Do I hear a Alec Guinness accent in his voice? I look forward to seeing more of him in Ep-III. Samual Jackson, though an excellent actor, seemed a little uncomfortable handling the lightsaber. Christopher Lee is impressive as Count Dooku. But I missed Darth Maul terribly. The movie is not entirely lack luster. It does have its good moments (you will have to see it yourself)- Check out the confrontation between Obi-Wan and Bounty Hunter, the Jedi in action and above all Yoda. But overall the story lacks depth. It seems like a 12 year old's fantasy ride. Only a Star Wars fan, like me, would give it some credit and consider watching it for a second time!

A SUGGESTION to George Lucas for Ep-III: Try spending more time on the story line and character building than on special effects.

title: better than episode 1
review:
One word: ACTION No jar jar (oke 2 short scenes) not to much love scenes and yoda who fights against the dark side what do you want more?

Attack of the Clones is a 10 movie

title: Average Start, terrible middle and an incredible ending
review:
The movie starts with some nice racing scenes, not too bad but nothing you haven't seen before in "Blade Runner" or "The fifth Element". Then it seems to fall into a bottomless pit of boringness for about an hour!!! I don't know what George Lucas had in mind, when he blew the whole romance thing to a whole hour. Obviously it had to be in the movie because it belongs to the plot, but 10 minutes would have been more than enough! I read somewhere that the audience was laughing in some cinemas when they saw that "Heidi"-like love affair on Naboo. When I saw it, nobody was laughing! At first everybody seemed to wait patiently for the action to start up again, then the "BORING"-chants started and finally a lot of the people started to leave the cinema. Only those who couldn't believe George Lucas could make such a crap and who were still waiting for a good ending were rewarded with an incredible and furious final battle.

The last part was something, every Star Wars fan has been waiting for since the first movie appeared on the big screen! For those who read to this point and who haven't seen Episode II yet and who still want to see it after all, I won't spoil the best part in years (Although it seems to be "stolen" from other movies like "Gladiator", "Starship Troopers" and even "Return of the Jedi").

Those who have already seen it, they will know what I mean anyway (If they were strong enough to survive the terrible middle)!

I would like to say the ending would have saved the movie and I really would like to give it a high vote. But although the ending is worth a 12 out of 10, the first part is even with the hunting scenes and with a whole lot of Good-Will a 2 out of 10. That makes only a 7 altogether.

May the force be with you, George Lucas, and may it clear your mind!

title: Better than I expected, not quite on par with the original trilogy
review:
I'm regretting my cynicism a little - it was better than I expected. The effects were of course very nice, but this time, they were used for considerably better effect - Lucas' formidable skill with visuals has obviously returned. My favorite scene, cinematography-wise, was definitely the chase scene at the beginning. The digital effects were stunning, and absolutely necessary for a scene like this - the number of speeders, buildings, and people in the scene couldn't have been achieved without CGI. This time, it seems that Lucas' cinematic vision hasn't been outpaced by the power of his computers. I also very much liked the visuals in the scenes on the water planet (can't think of the name). They impressed me a great deal.

The dialog was quite poor, though - filled with clichÃ©s (Samuel L. Jackson: "I don't think so!" being only one of many examples.) The scenes with Anakin and Padme were almost sickening in their sweetness. I'm glad the teenage romance wasn't as important in the movie as the preview I saw made it look because George Lucas at his best is not a skilled director of romance, and here he is positively ham-handed. Leia and Han Solo were funny, had good chemistry, and Lucas used a very light touch. Anakin and Padme, on the other hand, said lines like "I've been dying day by day since you came back" (paraphrased) and didn't manage to convince me at all.

Thankfully, those scenes were fairly brief, and Jar Jar was also present briefly, although in his perhaps 5 minutes of screen time, he did manage to put into action the destruction of the Republic.

The scene with Yoda was, of course, extremely crowd-pleasing, even obsequious - perhaps an apology for Episode I. It was also, however, very well done - although I don't know that it would have the same meaning to those who haven't seen the first three. I wonder about the young folk who haven't necessarily seen the original trilogy. The end of that seen, when Yoda picks up his cane, was a classic moment for the series.

All in all, it was a good movie, but it didn't quite live up to the original trilogy. His visual skills are on par with IV-VI, the effects were much better, but the cast was not the equal of the originals, including, surprisingly, Ewan McGregor. The dialogue was mediocre, and the acting was mixed. Definitely a worthwhile addition to the series, but nowhere near its peak. It is sure to please the diehard fan, especially after Episode I, but to someone like myself, who enjoys Star Wars but isn't fanatical, the flaws are visible. I give it 8 out of 10.

title: Wow!!!
review:
Two and bit hours of bombs, blasts, light sabers, lasers and flying.

What more could you ask for?

Brace yourself for some really corny dialogue - I really cringed, but some shocking romance gives you time to catch your breath from the most spectacular special effects extravagance scenes I've ever seen.

Some people have just forgotten how to have fun. No, this is not Schindler's List or Citizen Kane. No, Hayden Christensen will not win best actor at the 2002 Academy Awards. It's Star Wars. George Lucas made it to make money from the blockbuster movie to Yoda shaped lunch boxes. And he has me sucked right into the craze.

title: Visually stunning yet lacking
review:
This movie exactly fits the expectations set by the four preceding Star Wars movies. The acting is mediocre at best, grating against the cheesy script: for example, in a near death situation, Anakin states, as though it were the most serious thing in the world, "I have a bad feeling about this." The graphics are, of course, incredible, and the adrenaline rushes were worth the $5.75 entrance fee, and some of the scenery was fabulous, but if the movie had to stand on its own without being part of the Star Wars mania, it would be barely memorable at all.

Basically, I think that everyone who is the least bit curious as to the continuing saga of our Skywalker heroes should see it, but newcomers to the series shouldn't buy into it simply because of the publicity. The plot moves too quickly for that, and the scenes are so spliced that it's sometimes hard to remember what's happening. However, I rated it seven out of ten stars simply for the effort it must have taken to produce something so large in scale.

title: George Lucas tells a beautifully crafted story rich with fine acting, witty dialogue, and amazing special effects.
review:
Despite what critics have said, "Star Wars: Episode II-Attack of the Clones" is a wonderful, fun filled adventure from a galaxy far, far away. There are a few problems with the script, and the acting is stiff in places, but George Lucas has, for the most part, succeeded with creating a visually compelling, dramatically focused, and very emotional film. Much like "The Empire Strikes Back", Lucas has dwelled into darker territory with "Clones", as we begin to see Anakin Skywalker's inevitable descent to the Dark Side. We also get to see the beginning of the end for the Galactic Republic, and its transformation into the Empire.

At 142 minutes, "Clones" may seem like a long movie, but it moves at a ferocious speed, and it's over almost as soon as it begins. For me, this was a bad thing. Not enough time was given to specific scenes. The love story between Anakin and Padme Amidala feels rushed, and loses some believability because of this. The scenes with the Homestead on Tatooine had the potential to be great, but Owen Lars and Beru Whitesun, Luke's uncle and aunt from the original "Star Wars", have very few lines, and their roles in this movie seem rather pointless. I was really anxious to see this part of the film, but I was ultimately disappointed.

As for the acting, it's mostly pretty good. Ewan MgGregor does a fine job as Obi Wan Kenobi, and offers a couple of pretty good laughs during the film. Hayden Christensen is terrific as the young Darth Vader. He brings a lot of intensity and emotion to the role, and, at times, you can't help but feel sorry for him. Natalie Portman is only ok with her role as Padme Amidala. She delivers some of her lines in a dull monotone. The rest of the cast is excellent, especially Ian McDirmid as Supreme Chancellor Palpatine. He's devilishly sneaky and corrupted, and it's amazing to watch him in action. Samuel L. Jackson is also back as Jedi Master Mace Windu, and, as always, he's a pleasure to watch. Christopher Lee manages to bring us a truly memorable villain with Count Dooku, who's light years ahead of Darth Maul. His skills with a lightsabre are incredible, to say the least.

All of the technical aspects of the film are a wonder. The special effects, the sound, everything, are fantastic. The battle at the end of the film is truly one of the best action sequences ever put on screen. John Williams has also given us a dazzling musical score, his best since "Empire", I think. The love theme is amazingly beautiful.

For me, the best part of the film was the story-telling. It's absolutely masterful. The missing pieces of the saga begin to fall into place, as Anakin slowly begins his transformation into the evil Darth Vader, the beginning of the Clone Wars, the fall of the Republic, and the rise of the Empire. The final sequence of the movie will no doubt send chills down your spine, as it gives you the feeling of the impending doom that's about to be unleashed upon the galaxy.

Even with its faults, "Attack of the Clones" proves that George Lucas still has it in him to create an epic story that not only offers a huge treat for the ears and eyes, but a film rich with exhilarating emotions, raw intensity, and beautifully crafted drama.

Final Grade: B+

title: Lot better than Episode 1
review:
WARNING - POSS. SPOILERS

After the Episode I love/hate relationship (I guess I am one of the few who actually liked it) Episode II goes someway to address the storyline issues from the last film. Episode II kicks off straight into the thick of things with a number of action sequences.

The storyline too detailed to write uses a lot of inferences in all the others films to cobble together the Attack of the Clones. George Lucas has pushed out the boat as far as computer generated graphics in the movie but you can't help feel its too much (maybe we are just too used to the look of the low tech Star Wars Episode IV).

Enjoyed the film immensely however the Yoda fight sequence is laughable. Hobbling on his stick one moment. Jedi super athlete the next. Back to hobbling on his stick.

title: There is No Hero
review:
The whole Star Wars Prequel (both I and II) has been one big disappointment. All that movies seem to rely on these days are special effects. I found Star Wars: Episode II to be as confusing as Episode I. The genius which Lucas had drawn from the works of Joseph Campbell in the 1970s is highly lacking in the new episodes. Maybe it's for the simple fact that one has no interest in relating to any of the characters in the movie because there is no true hero and no real character involvement. Though George pushes for it, we all know where Anakin is headed and we are loathe to identify with this future traitor. The glory of the first Star Wars trilogy lay largely in the hero, Luke, who embodies the noblest and most ideal qualities of humanity. Luke Skywalker inspired the audience with his naivete, integrity, growing wisdom, lofty idealism, and his eventual journey towards Jedi glory. The viewer lived out Luke's experiences vicariously. But in the new Star Wars triology, there is no one to take on the responsibility of our imagination.

Certainly not the illaudable Anakin, who is surely the greatest known disappointment, nor the personality-less Jedi Council and grammatically challenged Yoda. Not the uninspiringly fallible Obi-Wan (his folly being his conceit). And definitely not the passively hyper-feminine Senator Padme (at least Leia had an attitude on her--thanks to the saving grace of the Women's Liberation movement). These characters provide little fodder for an audience's yearning for heroism with a greater purpose. Though the prequels provides the history to Star Wars IV, V, and VI, they are unlikely to appeal to mass audiences who care less about science fiction and more about universal themes of human growth, change, and triumph over adversity. In Star Wars I and II, Lucas fails to engage the audience with these crucial elements that comprise a great heroic epic.

title: Great action, effects, story elements, and some humor carry this one past eps 1 and 6
review:
Some spoilers ahead, some of a general, some of a specific nature, no overall plot summary:

Here's what I liked about Ep II:

1. Redeemed virtually every issue in ep I. 2. Fantastic effects, especially in action scenes 3. Involving plot with elements that worked well together 4. Christensen's portrayal as a frustrated Anakin 5. Interplay between master and padawan 6. Much of the humor was funny and not annoying

Here are some things that bothered me about Ep II:

1. Uneven tone. Self referential (to the series) humor here, grave seriousness there, general humor there, attempts at serious romance here, I expect variation, but the way it was done felt inconsistent within a single movie and the selection did not work perfectly for me of 2. Romantic chemistry is all off (Christensen's great frustrated tone doesn't even work well for me when it involves Portman much of the time, not all) 3. Some CGI scenes, usually static, sweeping into view, broad landscape views, look totally faked, like matte paintings as another user pointed out. 4. The scene after the attempted assasination explosion looked like video instead of film, kind of jaunting b/c the rest of the film looked like film (I know it's shot in DV but it still looks like film). There was another scene where this was the case, but I forgot what it was. 5. Many lines still delivered flatly, even one from Christopher Lee where you can see him waiting to react, instead of reacting naturally to a comment (only one from him, everything else is perfect from him) 6. Ending had some of thrown together feeling that TPM had. "Begun this clone was has," "Where is Anakin?," (getting married), we should watch senator palpatine, etc... Too much too soon without enough explanation. 7. Too much of the writing was just bad. Anakin's line about not liking sand was pretty lame. They gave Samuel Jackson some bad lines too, also Yoda had some bad lines... 8. Yoda fight was impressive, but it was a little silly looking also (probably impossible for it not to be with the little guy bouncing all around) 9. Agree with guy calling it a circus about some scenes. Should have been obvious to Obi-Wan that someone deleted the planet from the computer. I thought he was looking for some cosmic explanation about what could have happened. I assumed the part about the planet (and solar system it was in?) disappearing was obvious and he wanted more explanation. 10. If Amidala was going to vote against an army of the republic how could even someone as easily mislead as Jar Jar think she would want to vote the Chancellor emergency powers when he would obviously create a republic army, even despite the separatist threat? 11. If Count Dooku is the most powerful jedi, why is Darth Sidious his master? Or is Dooku yanking Yoda's chain, knowing he's not the most powerful? 12. Some explanations/background are not provided that would help and don't seem to be left out deliberately where I'm supposed to guess, just seemed like an oversight. In addition to the above, who the heck are the Sith? What's the Jedi/Sith rivalry all about and why was Sidious involved with Maul and the Sith in ep 1 anyway? What is Jango's relationship with Sidious and Dooku? Why did the weird seemingly peaceful scientists/business ppl the Caminos have weapons? Why would such a simple little barbed dart be so unique? 13. No sword fighting has perfect viewpoint like fight in ep 1. Never felt like I could see any fight as well as that one in any movie.

Some highlights:

Obi-Wan flying around the asteroid belt around Geonosee (or whatever it's called) Huge end battle Jango Fett Yoda fights Palpatine creating civil war and influencing everyone around him to like and manipulating Anakin (guy keeps busy) Jar Jar was not annoying this timeC3PO was pretty funny Clever hints about Anakin becoming Vader (helmet shadows and the machine stapling his arm down and adding circuits to a part that he's stuck under, I thought he might even want to slice off his own arm)

Overall:

I liked this film better than Eps 1 or 6. I thought the action was very good and the plot was interesting, though I would have liked a little more explanation on what people were trying to achieve, how they planned, etc. There was nothing so obviously annoying or marketable as the Ewoks or Jar Jar Binks being a bungling dumbass and it didn't have any dialogue as bad as the Leia telling Luke to run away instead of facing his destiny speech in ROTJ. I forgive much of the flat delivery b/c I think that's what Lucas gets, he's not a great director, and hey, I was entertained despite it all. This film is unquestionably better than TPM. I was never a huge Star Wars fan, but I did like the ANH for much of its fun, and TESB is still one of my favorite movies for being so well done overall. I thought the action in ROTJ was good, but this film has much better action and I think is overall a better film. It obviously rides on the coattails of its predecessors for much of its interesting lines (repeated in this one) and is well received because it is quite a bit better than TPM.

I'm really looking forward to seeing the beginning of a real separatist movement (The Rebels), what becomes of the clone army (storm troopers?), when the Mandelorian Guard comes into play (Boba Fett's group, army type), how look is fully seduced to the dark side, when the Jedi council finds out Anni slaughtered a Tuskan Rider settlement, and what happens with Anakin, Padme, their kids and Dooku/Sidious.

Overall, good job Lucas, you've improved everything and directed better than other Star Wars film thus far (Kasdan did ANH, Irvin Kirshner did TESB). Work on the dialogue, delivery, and those obviously fake CGI/matte painting scenes, and you'll be even better, possibly repeating the glory that was TESB.

title: Simply Amazing
review:
"Star Wars: Episode II- Attack of the Clones" is downright amazing entertainment. Lucas held no punches back in this all out assault on the senses. This film is filled with enough imaginative images and sounds to fill a summer's worth of movies. From the computer generated characters to the different planets to the lightsaber duels, Lucas has created a terrific and entertaining blockbuster.

Star Wars films have never been about Oscar caliber acting, rather they are more like an experience; dropping you into a world and taking you for a ride. I saw in several reviews by major critics, that some are attacking the script and even going so far as to say the film has no "heart".

All that can be said is this film has a heart, a child's heart. I'm 22 and this film gave me the same chills as I had as a little kid watching, "Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade", "Star Wars: A New Hope" and "Jurassic Park". AOTC reminded me of what it was like to sit in wonderment and awe at the world on the screen.

The film begins with Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) and Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen) meeting up with Senator Padme (Natalie Portman) after someone tries to kill her. The events unfold as Kenobi and Skywalker split up as Anakin is assigned to protect Padme, while Obi-Wan is investigating the situation. The film packs a punch of both humor and visual splendor along the way. "Attack of the Clones" is like a firecracker with a long fuse, slowly burning at the beginning and eventually exploding at the end into a dazzling treat.

This film also has a deep connection with the other films in the series. (For example, Darth Vader and Boba Fett's histories become more complete, yet complex.) Lucas gives a film that the fans of the series can laugh at (especially the scenes involving C-3PO) and cheer for, while the average filmgoer can still appreciate the originality of the world before them.

I have always wondered about the critical harshness for films such as this one. Since when have science-fiction or fantasy or even action films had truly daring, creative and original scripts and dialogue? These genres have been and probably always will be visual genres as opposed to verbal ones. "Attack of the Clones" explodes with a creative visual awe that surrounds you and leaves you begging for more. A 9 out of 10.

title: Why This Movie Doesn't Work
review:
Warning - some plot spoilers probably contained herein.

Lucas has manufactured an interesting trap for himself. By telling episodes 4, 5 and 6 first and then going back to the first three, he is essentially telling us a story we already know. Some of the details are new, but every Star Wars fan knows all the broad strokes already.

Granted, there are only a dozen plots in all of literature and success or failure stems from the way in which the plot has been told. But this very point dooms Lucas to failure because his strengths have never included writing dialogue or directing actors. Given the exposition-heavy nature of this film, he clearly needed both a better co-writer and needed to hand this over to another director, as he did so successfully with Empire Strikes Back.

Beyond that, one reason that the original Star Wars movies worked so well was the influence of Joseph Campbell and the way Campbell's theories on mythology were applied to give an incredible back story to the characters and action. It's one of the reasons Lord of the Rings always worked so well for so many. Now we're seeing that back story on film, but it needs its own back story to give it resonance, and that's not provided.

We are left with two hours of really embarrassing dialogue and acting, in some cases from some excellent actors who are truly wasted here, especially Samuel Jackson. Plus a final half hour that basically gives us what we want and expect from a Star Wars (tm) franchise vehicle. But by the time you get there, you may not care.

Other problems:

Throwing away logic for convenience. As one example, in this film R2-D2 flies. He never flies in 4,5,6. So how could he fly now and not later?

Lack of suspense. Lord Dooku is carrying the only plans for the Death Star. We know the Death Star is built in #4. Therefore, we know that Dooku will escape in his duel with Yoda and Obi-wan. And since we know that both Yoda and Obi-wan will appear in future installments, we know that they are not in mortal danger either. (And frankly speaking, that hurling of electric bolts back and forth reminded me of the cheesy wizards' battle between Karloff and Price in Roger Corman's 1963 "The Raven".)

I'm sure Clones will gross 400 million in the US and double that globally. That does not make it a good movie. The joy that was in every frame in the original Star Wars is completely gone, bogged down in a $140 million 2-1/2 hour trailer for the technical capabilities of ILM.

Clones' guaranteed success means that Lucas will follow the same path for episode three, and it will fail in the same ways. Lucas needs to open up, release an iota of control, bring in a stronger collaborator or two. Right now all I can do is hope that he will not make a 7, 8 or 9. And I'll sit back and wait for future installments of Lord of the Rings and Matrix instead.

title: A visual feast that puts Episode I to shame.
review:
I used to be a hard-core Star Wars fan. Hell, I grew up with it. But when Episode I came out, the disappointment- combined with the saturation of licensing, truly put out the light for me. I couldn't stand Star Wars after that. Sure I still liked it, but I had immersed myself so much in the release of the new film that it actually left a negative effect on me. In fact, I had no idea when Episode II was coming out until about a week ago.

On to the movie itself, I truly, truly enjoyed the entire movie. Although the acting was a bit awkward at times, there was really no chance to notice those moments, as the movie is steeped in action, action, and more action. I'm not going to spoil anything for anyone here because I hate it when people do that. Let me just say that the movie moved me in ways that Empire moved many people. Some reviewers gave the film a bad grade but I surmise that those people had no true knowledge of what Star Wars is about and thus could not appreciate Ep.II's many references and generally, it's direction. Star Wars, as many know, isn't about all the aliens, it's not about Han Solo or Luke or any of the Jedi. It's about one man- Anakin Skywalker aka Darth Vader and his redemption. It's about triumph of the human spirit over darkness and about man's triumph over the coldness of machines. I think this movie sets up a very dark scenario to be played out in Episode III, in which Anakin will turn to the Darkside and complete the sextet of films. The visual effects were incredible and I really only noticed a couple of parts that seemed CGish. The rest was very smooth and well integrated. The plethora of characters and aliens didn't seem to be as distracting as they were in the previous movie- like I said, it's all about integration within the story and with the human actors. The ship and technology design was amazing and even in this department was the last movie put to shame.

I'd say that anyone who likes Star Wars in the remotest, or likes love stories, or just likes shoot em up action should go see this. Don't listen to those idiotic critics, listen to people like me who don't pick it apart and instead enjoy the film for what it is- entertainment.

title: Lucas has redeemed himself
review:
Like many Star Wars fans I was deeply disappointed with The Phantom Menace. However, Attack of the Clones has completely restored my faith in the series. AoTC is a darker, more complex tale than its predecessor. This installment provides Star Wars fans with what we want to see -- action. Anakin (Hayden Christianson) and Obi-Wan's (Ewan McGreghor) exploits are on

full display in this film and they will not disappoint. Mace Windu (Samuel L. Jackson) finally gets off the Jedi Council's couch where he sat during TPM; Mace beautifully wields his purple lightsabre and shows us why he is a venerated Jedi Master. In fact, we finally get to see an entire legion of Jedi Knights doing what they are supposed to do, defend the galaxy.

But what good are heroes without villians. AoTC introduces two very compelling bad guys. Jango Fett is a bounty hunter who proves to be a formidable adversary. Fett employs toxic darts, concussion grenades, a missile and a grappling hook during his battle sequences. Count Dooku (Christopher Lee) is chilling as a former Jedi who has fallen to the Darkside. He pulls out all the stops against Anakin and Obi-Wan.

In fact Dooku is so powerful that only Yoda can successfully stand up to him. Yes it's true! After 22 years of speculation about the extent of Yoda's power, we now know why Yoda is the most powerful of all Jedi. The little green guy can do much more than foretell the future, dispense advice and free X-Wings from mud puddles. Yoda, when left no peaceful alternative, can fight. In the most exhilerating sequence in the Star Wars saga to date, Yoda and Count Dooku engage in one hell of a great battle.

Besides the action there is also romance between Anakin and Padme. The romance was a little bit corny but nonetheless it works. More importantly, the quiet moments in the film provide an opportunity for Anakin's character to develop, foreshadowing his inevitable transformation to Darth Vader.

AoTC delivers what Star Wars fans expect and deserve from the series. In Episode II: Attack of the Clones, George Lucas and company return us to our favorite "galaxy far, far away" for a fantastic adventure.

title: George is still looking for an original idea
review:
Let me begin by saying that this film is way better than Ep I.

Way back when the world was younger and more naive, along came a young filmmaker called George Lucas who created a fantasy world in which adult and children could immerse themselves. They were good times, happy times, analogue times, where puppets and stop motion ruled.

But now times are much more cynical, and filmmakers have less respect for their audiences. We live in a world where major plot lines can be altered at the whim of the film maker for convenience, and all those things that have been foretold in future episodes can be changed to suit substandard story lines.

At least in Attack of the Clones, Lucas does not mess with the well-established story lines set out in the original series, but he is still in search of an original idea. Clones is full of cliched dialog, characters and ideas that he has lifted from numerous other science fiction works.

Some of the story is laboured, particularly those sections set on Naboo. And as usual, Lucas manages to get very wooden performances out of some very talented actors. I also felt that the film was about 30 minutes to long, with the inclusion of some gratuitous special effects.

Now for the positives. Its fun. My 3-year-old son will love it. There are no truly annoying or cutesy characters that seem to be regular inclusions of late. The special effects are very special. The film has lost no definition by being shot on a fully digital media.

I think that Lucas has tried harder to be less condescending with this film, but at times we are still spoon-fed, probably for the benefit of younger viewers.

Overall worth a look - 3 out of 5.

title: Hayden Christensen IS Jake Lloyd
review:
I simply can't believe that Hayden Christensen was cast in this role. He is absolutely atrocious, and makes the wooden Natalie Portman look like Audrey Hepburn. The two have NO chemistry--they get together because the plot requires it. The dialogue is hackneyed from beginning to end, and if not for Ian McDiarmid and Christopher Lee, no human actor would stand out at all...(Ewan MacGregor tries, but he can only do so much with lines like "my Padawan still has much to learn.") The only heart in the movie comes from the digital actors--Yoda (who is unfortunately a source of unintentional comedy at the movie's climax), Watto, that fat fry cook at the beginning, and god forbid, even Jar Jar. George actually lets them ACT...what a concept.

Attack of the Clones looks and sounds great, but the action scenes now run together in my mind like a blur, and most seem like commercials for the upcoming video games (particularly the scene in the Droid factory). I never felt that the characters were ever in true danger.

Wouldn't Anakin have been a better character if he was a Han Solo-type in this film--a swaggering, charming, hothead that's difficult not to like? Of course, but nowadays Lucas take his story so seriously that the main characters are humorless, and deadly earnest--and the light touch is left up to the strictly-comic relief droids (and I'm sorry to say that the C-3PO/R2-D2 schtick is really starting to get old, and is very much out of place in the epic final battle).

All in all, the movie is clearly a spectacle, but is it good? Unfortunately, I can't say for certain...I'm afraid this movie will always bring with it for me the thoughts of what might have been.
