title: It was so worth calling in sick!
review: This movie was awesome.  The lightsaber battles, the chases.  It had everything i could've asked for.  I've been a Star Wars fan for as long as i can remember, and it just keeps getting better and better.  The thing about Clones is that it starts to show the history of where everything in the original movies came from.  It shows primitive star destroyers, and answers some burning questions Star Wars fans might have. Overall it was worth calling in sick to see Episode 2.  I went to the first show in the area, and it was packed.(I hope it breaks Spider-man's record)  The only complaint i have is that we have to wait until 2005 for Episode 3.

title: oh thank goodness
review:
Don't worry, it's good, very good indeed. Not great, but definitley worthy of Star Wars fame.

Although the movie does have some painful dialogue moments, on the whole the acting is very solid. Christensen & Portman effectively carry their romantic scenes, and have a real on-screen chemistry. Lucas made the RIGHT choice for Anakin.

The effects are as spectacular as you would expect, the movie's plot effectively foreshadows the events that will take place in III and the 4-6 trilogy, and the music is as brillaint as ever.

On another note, Yoda is the man. I will say no more and you probably know what I'm talking about anyway, but he rocks. Viva La Yoda!

Can't wait for Episode 3. All you doubters, Lucas has the touch. This movie probably won't make as much money as Spiderman, but it is a more rewarding cinematic experience as a whole.

title: STAR WARS ROCKS !!
review:
It is safe to say that Star Wars gets better and better every episode. Personally, I believe that this has to be one of the greatest episodes in the entire Star Wars saga with exception to Episode III which has not been released yet. Episode II reveals a lot of what happens through the course of Anakin Skywalkers transition phase to the dark side of the force. The film takes place ten years after the events that occurred in Episode I, in which Anakin has grown older and has become Obi Wan Kenobis jedi apprentice. Most of the characters from Episode One return in this movie, however Jar Jar Bink has a rather short but important role in Episode II. This film reveals the life of Anakin Skywalker while he is in the process of becoming corrupt by power and anger as well as it being more of a love story. Samuel L Jackson and Ewan McGregor are awesome in this movie, but Yoda steals the entire film. The droids also have a solid role in this film. Natalie Portman is so hot and she gets better and better in the series.

Attack Of Clones shows how Episode One and the events that will occurr in Episode III are releated to the original trilogy. Some people believe that George Lucas has ruined the series by creating these prequels to the orignal trilogy because they say how can technology be more advanced than in the original Star Wars, which is an opinion that I disagree with. I believe George Lucas is a genius for creating these films and he keeps making Star Wars better and better. This movie is terrific in pretty much every aspect. The sound effects blew me away, I couldn't expect them to be as spectacular as they were. The music which was composed by John Williams is terrific as well as the acting and visual effects. I give this movie 4 stars and I say that Star Wars just keeps getting better and better. If you have any interest in Star Wars definitley catch this movie over the summer.

title: Outstanding
review: This movie far exceeded my expectations. Hayden Christensen is perfect as the tormented Anakin. Yoda was the coolest, everybody cheered when he lit up that lightsaber. Ewen Mcgregor was great and Natalie Portman is just beautiful and exciting to watch.The comedy was strictly left to C-3P0 and R2-D2 like it should be and not to that other thing(can you believe he is a senator now.) The battle scenes were thrilling and of course the final lightsaber duels were great. If you didn't like this movie then you should get a life and stop complaining. No movie that Lucas makes today will compare to the original trilogy, ever. So just accept it for what it is today and stop complaining, because critics and fans will always find something wrong. Enjoy the movie and don't analyze it, its just fantasy anyway.

title: Better than Episode 1
review:
Saw Episode II - AOTC at a special showing. Definitely better than Episode 1. Action sequences and sets are great, which has been George Lucas' strength. However, his weakness is using actors who came with good reputations - Samuel L. Jackson, Natalie Portman and Ewan McGregor has won praises for other movies before this but their acting in this movie leaves some room for improvement. Hayden Christensen just tries too hard but falls far short of say, Elijah Wood's performance in LOTR: FOTR. It says a lot for the acting when one of the best sequences had Yoda doing a Jackie Chan turn.

That said, as a package, AOTC is more in line with Episodes IV to VI, where the audience will feel more involved with the Star Wars universe developments. More non-Star Wars fans are going to watch this by word-of-mouth.

title: Well Worth It
review:
AOTC was a solid installment to the Star Wars series. The movie was very entertaining, and was certainly worthy to be part of the Star Wars family. It is filled with action, a solid story line, beautifully done graphics and a bit of humor.

If you are looking for answers, you will find them in this movie. We begin seeing the circumstances that lead to later episodes, and get a better understanding of Darth Vader, Storm Troopers and Yoda among other key themes. I actually thought the movie could have been a bit longer, and should have explored the details of the story and characters much more. I thought the 2 hours went by fairly quickly.

About the only disappointing thing to me was the acting. The 2 main characters (Obi and Anachin) are not very good actors. I was particularly disappointed in Christensen (Anachin). His lack of acting ability was apparent, and I was left scratching my head on how he ended up with such a key role.

Outside of the "B Team" actors, the movie was very good. It is well worth the price of admission, and it was great to finally see Master Yoda show his Jedi prowess.

-- DP.

title: It has brough balance to the force...
review:
Being a rather big STAR WARS fan, i was extremely happy when viewing this film. It fit nicely with the OT (original trilogy) by using many more inclosed sets. It was as big and open as TPM was. It captured the same essence and 'force' that Episodes 4, 5, & 6 all have. It's filled with emotion and wonderful shots of the start of the CLONE WARS. Anakin is nearing his faithful down fall to Vader. Obi-Wan is becoming more and more of that mindful old man we see in A NEW HOPE. This film has it all, including many good jokes/puns by C-3PO near the end, which makes the line "WITH ALL THAT WE'VE BEEN THROUGH, IT'S AMAZING WE'RE IN AS GOOD OF CONDITION AS WE ARE" in EPISODE 4 more understandable and reminisciant.

STAR WARS EPISODE 2: ATTACK OF THE CLONES is a winner and a fav amongst STAR WARS fans like myself.

title: Breathtaking visuals
review:
If they gave Oscars for eye-candy then George Lucas would already be getting a space ready on his mantelpiece. Episode 2 provides a series of backgrounds, landscapes and scenes that serve up a rich, deep tapestry of colour and vivid imagery.

Lucas has both a problem and a boon with the plot - we already know largely what has to happen to the principal characters, so the fun is in how we get there. Episode 2 definitely serves to make one strongly anticipate the third installment, with the scene set as it is for Anakin's final descent to the dark side.

This leads to the inevitable question - if this series had not been going strong for 25 years, would this film be so popular? Well, the acting is not as bad as has been made out - Anakin's character is well played (although not overly likeable or sympathetic) and the other performances are solid. The dialogue is not award winning but serves its purpose.

The major problem with the story is why Anakin and Amadilah fall in love - there is no chemistry there at all and for the most part Anakin is quite unpleasant.

At the end of the day however, one can simply sit back, soak up the visuals and enjoy two of the finest moments of the series that allow C3-PO (humourously) and Yoda (violently) respectively to take centre stage.

title: Salvaging the trilogy
review:
After being thoroughly disappointed with "The Phantom Menace", I had come to the conclusion that Lucas was in a very undesirable position of having to deliver a knockout punch with Ep II - or possibly face a failed trilogy.

So, I came into "Attack of the Clones" with extremely high expectations - knowing Lucas had to deliver.

After watching the movie, the very first thing that came into my mind was that this was easily the most complicated Star Wars plot of all of the Episodes - easily. If I had been 8 years old in the theater watching this film (as I was when viewing the original Star Wars), then I would definately had been confused during this movie - and I have NEVER been confused during a Star Wars movie. The plot is quite complex.

However, that is a good thing. The plot needed to be complex when considering the nature of the storyline. This film is taking on the difficult task of explaining how the Star Wars universe went from being a democratic Republic to a hardened dictatorship-based Empire. That's not something you can explain without deep plots that might not make immediate sense. However, the more you think about the plot and the more you realize the level of political back-stabbing that is going on by Palpatine then you realize this is very well written script.

Sure, there are awkward moments. The romance is clumsy & extremely awkward. But who cares ? I mean, is that REALLY what you go to see a Star Wars movie for ? The only reason the romance is so prominant here is because it carries such important consequences in the next trilogy (Luke & Leia).

As far as the action scenes go, I just do not see how anyone could ask for more in a film. The visual effects are just overwhelming. Even two viewings of this film would not be sufficient in appreciating the effects. They are just that extensive.

So, in the end when judging this movie you have to ask yourself : am I looking forward to Episode III ? I believe after seeing this film you will be, and therefore Lucas succeeded.

I can't believe people are being so enthusiastic about SW II. The dialogue is ridiculously bad, Portman and Christensen cannot act, most of the movie is slow and boring. There's no humour, no interesting plot twists, no character

As a devoted Star Wars fan, 'Attack of the Clones' I would say is not only the best installment in the prequel triology so far, but THE BEST STAR WARS MOVIE CREATED!

Despite terrible acting by Hayden Christensen (Anakin) and Temuera Morrison(Jango Fett), it had great performances by Christpher Lee, Natalie Portman and Ian McDiarmid! (Christopher Lee being the best)

title: A Good Movie
review:
The title of my post is as straightforward as they get. This film, which is far superior to Episode I, was a good movie. I cannot say that I was thrilled with it, despite its good plotline and superb special effects. I had nothing which I could point out to say that THIS is what was bad about it.

I will say that it did drag on from the beginning somewhat (which, I guess, is a staple of all Star Wars movies besides the Empire Strikes Back), but the combat sequence in the end made up for that. After all, what good is brilliant action when no story is told.

I think that the special effects were better in this picture then in Episode I as well. I think this is a good, though not great, movie in the Star Wars line.

title: More Story, Less Mindless Violence/Action
review: As a fan of Marvel Comics (Spiderman, X-Men), versus Dell Comics (Superman, Justice League), I found this episode of the Star Wars movies more satisfying.  It had more substance in the story.  I got a better view of the characters as people, not just ornaments in the actions of the plot.  This was not as true of the earlier ones, which even while I loved them a great deal, I found them more one dimensional. The only disappointment was a couple of the computer generated characters looked computer generated in their actions.  I much prefer the Frank Oz muppets.

title: Better story, same problems (Spoiler Alert)
review: Infinitely better than the last outing, but that's still damning it with faint praise.  To be fair, there are some wonderful moments here: the thrilling bounty hunter chase through Coruscant; Obi-Wan and Jango's rain-soaked one-on-one; and the chillingly vicious Lightsaber Round Robin finale  Yoda's 'Matrix'-style moves notwithstanding.  Jar Jar is mercifully relegated to the minor (and rather apt) role of unwitting traitor, and Christopher Lee brings some much needed gravitas to the whole affair. Though the story drags in places, it's reasonably well-structured, balancing the action with the necessary (though soggy) romance.  And the motivation for Anakin's descent into evil is credible, even if Hayden Christensen's performance isn't.  Yet, once again, Lucas sabotages what could have been his masterpiece with what is now clearly a CGI-obsession bordering on clinical insanity.  Entire sequences, such as the droid assembly line (Coming soon to a Playstation near you!) and the 'Gladiator'-inspired arena battle, are plainly motivated by nothing more than the desire to do something cool with effects.  But they aren't cool.  They're mind-numbingly boring.  The climactic battle between droids and clones is so self-consciously spectacular that the audience is left feeling more alienated than engaged.  Sure, CGI played a role in every scene in this film  even the ones I loved.  But that wasn't what I loved about them.  For me, it was one or two of the humans who nearly saved the day.  In particular, the performance of Ewan McGregor, with his wryly humorous Alec Guinness impersonation and his ability to wring some semblance of credibility from even the most banal of Lucas's lines, was almost enough to salvage the entire production.  But not quite.

title: A Retread
review: Sorry Folks, After sitting through this most recent installement I can only think of how I have seen most of this before.  The massed troops in Ants, the flying craft scenes in a Bruce Willis movie of a few years back, and the saber battles in any Hong Kong Kung Fu Movie.  Great special effects but nothing really new.  No magic like the orignal Star Wars. The Doc

title: Really good fun sci-fi movie with priceless entertainment value.
review:
Absolutely thrilling Episode of Star Wars, a few good funny jokes and amazing action sequences. There's great lightsaber duels. I think that people who are complaining about the acting and dialogue are missing the point entirely as Star Wars has never been about plot or dialogue.

That said the mythological undertones are all in place, setting up Episode III to be possibly the best of the series.

Attack Of The Clones is a really good fun sci-fi movie and its entertainment value is priceless.

title: Just as bad as Episode I
review:
I am amazed so many people find this to be the "redemption" of the series. Everything I disliked about Episode I is still alive and kicking in this entry. I firmly believe Lucas has misunderstood what made his original trilogy so popular and timeless: good characters. These cardboard cut-outs of heroes and villains are simply set decoration for the real stars: the effects (which I thought were rather poor...it was like watching a video game). Anakin has to be one of the most unlikebale character on celluloid. Is anyone going to care when this kid goes bad? No way. Let him have it. I can't stand him. I read a review which brought up a great point: imagine if Anakin were a Han Solo type brimming with charm. Watching a character like that become seduced into the dark side would be far more tragic and interesting.

Acting has never been the strong point in a Star Wars film, but it's reached new lows. Given the caliber of actors Lucas has employed I must assume the corniness of the film is from bad writing. The dialouge in this film is vomit inducing. I cared for none of the characters, nor did I find the story that good.

What this new trilogy is missing is a good bad guy. Don't say Palpatine. That guy is given nothing to do. No, what I mean is a good Vader type antagonist. What they should have done was kept Darth Maul around through the first three films instead of killing him off. Replacing that very un-intimidating Dooku with Maul would have made this film much better. Just some consistancy is all I'm looking for.

The pacing in this film is more akin to the original trilogy...it actually feels like a Star Wars film. But I will NEVER compare it to any of the films in the original trilogy. It simply does not begin to compare. Many say with this film Lucas has made up for the mistakes of Ep. 1. I say he's dug himself even further into a hole. I don't expect much out of Episode III.

title: Superb!
review: From the opening scene of Coruscant (a homage to Asimov's Trantor) to the end on Genosis, this was the best Star Wars of them all. Like George Lucas, I discount critics, what good are they really? This was a superb, lively, action filled film that shows Anakin on the path to the dark side. But it also highlights the other Characters; a more mature and humorous Obi-Wan, an evil Count Dooku and a mighty, force using Yoda!  This was just a great, fun, pleasing film to sit through. The only bad thing is, like the rest of the Lord of the Rings, I have to wait years for it to be done! At least I have hobbies...

title: Lucas has followed his story exactly, whether we like it or not
review:
I mean this in George Lucas' defense. One of the major complaints I see with AOTC is that the Jedi are dull and lifeless, as well as everyone else in the Republic. They're supposed to be! That's the life of the Jedi, being the peacemakers of society. Even Ben mentions in ANH that before the Empire, everything was more civilized and sophisticated. The reason everything/one is so relaxed in the original 3 movies is because there in no Republic, just a band of freedom fighters called the Rebellion who are trying to overthrow the Empire. The scenes of the Imperial army in the old trilogy were boring in the same sense the Republic political scenes are boring. We're seeing AOTC through the eyes of the good guys who are still in charge, not the little group of bad guys trying to overthrow the good ones. It's the opposite of what we saw in the originals, a totally different perspective, and it works great in the overall story.

The story belongs to Lucas and he's presenting it exactly the way it needs to be shown. Whether we like it or not is our problem. I admire the way AOTC turned out. It's way better than TPM and even that movie wasn't so bad, it's part of the story. I give this one an A- overall.

title: This is not only the best Star Wars movie but also one of the best sci-fi films to have been made
review: George Lucas has made a breathtaking film that will easily rank as one of the better Star Wars movies. I watched in awe at the beautiful images in Attack of the Clones. And Yoda's fight scene??? It was simply amazing. I do not have enough praise for this. . It leaves you wanting more. A definite 10/10

story behind this movie?Lucas is the best storyteller??What is the

story here? It was sad that there was progress in the story as everyone was

expecting to see how Anakin will evolve to Darth Vader.

title: Attack of the Clones Drones on and on
review:
I expected great things from this movie. Episode I had been slated and George Lucas has had three years to put the Star Wars express back on the rails.

To be fair, it must be difficult to write a story that we all know the ending to. To that ends Hayden Christensen's portrayal of an increasingly dislikeable Anakin Skywalker is probably the highlight of the film. However, quiet what the eminently sensible Padmé sees in him I'm not sure. Ewan McGregor may be trying to hard to play Sir Alec playing Obi-Wan but I like it.

That said the film jumps back and forth across the galaxy. The locations appear disjointed, with no real flow between them. Lucas seems more interested in creating wacky aliens and grand CGI scenes than plot and story, which plods along at snails pace. Stunning special effects don't cover the fact that Lucas has just lost his way.

I know it's now possible to put thousands of sprites in complex backgrounds but do we have to see them all the time? Thousands of flying ships; thousands of clones; thousands of droids. When Lucas, and moviegoers had to use their imagination to imply this, we seemed to get better films.

Better than Episode I, which isn't saying much.

title: First the franchise lost its soul, now it has lost its way.
review:
This film is Dawson's Creek in Space, with special effects sequences thrown in for no particularly coherent reason.

Perhaps you could forgive the leaden characterisation, the pointless dialogue between McGregor and Christensen, stupid Ominous Lines being forced out of Christensen's mouth, C3PO being reduced to a comic-relief cipher; but what you cannot shake is the total lack of wonder, mystery or fundamental sense that these might even be individual protagonists with motives and personalities and suchlike, instead of riding a flagging merchandise bandwagon to dramatic hell.

Why must Portman and Christensen hop irrationally from danger to danger... who cares, The Plot demands it. And you thought Episode I was contrived.

Don't bother seeing this or the next high-tech soap opera that follows it. Portman and McGregor should be ashamed.

title: Absolutely Phenomenal
review:
Believe the hype! Episode II will go down as one of the signal most thrilling and satisfying movie-going experiences I have ever enjoyed in my life. In fact, it may be the most wonderfully entertaining film I've ever seen period.

This film will not disappoint. It is truly a wonder to behold. Like most everyone else, I was quite disappointed by "The Phantom Menace" but "Attack of the Clones" really delivers the goods. It is all that and then some. I was completely blown away.

While I understand those who may say that the acting is stiff and the dialogue is cliche, personally I believe this is necessary in order for the film to translate to a global audience. The greatness of this fim does not derive so much from spoken language, but visual language. The images are what make you feel. The moments are what you'll remember, not the dialogue. If you surrender to it, this film will immerse you into a fully-realized universe so tangible, so palpable, that you may find yourself feeling the same emotions as the characters on screen. What more can you ask? Honestly, this movie is an epic of, dare I say, Titanic proportions.

Will you appreciate this film more if you're already a Star Wars fanatic? Of course. If you're not a Jedi-enthusiast, will you be able to enjoy this film on its own merits? Absolutely.

This is a film that has everything you go to the movies for: vivid images; thrilling action; warm, heartfelt moments shared between characters we care about; dazzling special effects; humour; insight; and a tightly developed, carefully plotted storyline.

The skeptics will hem and haw, but this is the real deal. Is it better than Spiderman? Much, much better. Is it better than "The Fellowship of the Ring?" That debate will go on for an eternity. Does it measure up to the three original Star Wars films? In my opinion, yes. In fact, as sheer spectacle, I would say it exceeds them. It may not be as adored as those films were, but technically and artistically, I think this film is better than any of the others.

See this movie for Hayden Christensen's terrific performance as the seething young warrior, Anakin Skywalker... See this movie for Ewan McGregor as he comes into his own as Obi-Wan Kenobi, mentor and father figure to a child more talented than he... See this movie for the disarmingly beautiful Natalie Portman, who brings more spirit and sensitivity to a more mature and sensual Padme Amidala... See this movie for Samuel L. Jackson as Jedi Knight Mace Windu, who brings his signature air of coolness to the Star Wars universe as only he could... See this movie for Christopher Lee as Count Dooku. With Sauron already under his belt, this man will soon become a cult idol for bringing to life two of the great screen villains in any sci-fi/fantasy film... Lastly, see this movie for the beloved Jedi Master, Yoda, as you've never seen him before. This movie has it all. It is a classic. I could not be more pleased with the job George Lucas has done. He has made a film of which both he and his legion of fans should feel more than proud.

Thank you very much, Mr. Lucas, for taking me on such an incredibly moving journey. I'll never forget it.

title: Still not quite back on form, are you Lucas?
review:
As a whole, it's pretty much the same kind of movie as Episode 1; Overly dependent on CG; bad casting and bad acting, as well as very cheesy dialogue.

It does have it's moments though. Ewan McGregor is consistently good throughout the movie. Samuel L Jackson, although stiff as a cardboard cut-out, is good in his fight scene - and so is the very CG Yoda in his. Not Crouching Tiger impressive, mind you - but it gets the job done.

One thing that's notable is the successful casting of the villain. Christopher Lee did a great job in Lord of the Ring, and he does a good job in this one as well (playing the same character in alot of ways).

One thing that really got to me was the very noticable CG and lackluster compositing. CG can never replace a good movie set, and this movie proves just that.

It is a reasonably enjoyable movie though - for the most part. One thing thing that really sticks out is how horrible Lucas is at writing dialogue. He's attempt at "Shakespearian" romantic dialogue is too much too bare.

Here's hoping Episode 3 redeems the series.

title: Best Star Wars since Empire Strikes Back
review:
Awesome! This movis is better than Return of the Jedi and Episode One! Episode Two has an even paced story that offers little surprise but guess what, who cares. Most fans already have a very good idea of what's going on. A definite treat for Star Wars fans!

For all you critics out there, you can't compare this to Oscar hopeful movies, that's not what Star Wars is about and you should know better.

For those who want to see a fun and exciting movie, check it out!

title: GEORGE LUCAS GOT IT RIGHT! IT DELIVERS!
review:
Everything that went wrong in Star Wars - Episode I - The Phantom Menace... this time George Lucas did it right! The real Star Wars feeling with all the romantic twists, technical details, fun and playful alien arts are just right. It finally feels like REAL STAR WARS like 1977.

Visually stunning special effects (SFX) through out the whole movie make it virtually impossible to tell what was computer generated and what was real.

Boombastic soundtrack from the master composer John Williams make this film an experience.

Yoda in a light saber fight: REALLY COOL STUFF. The worlds look great. The aliens are really well portrayed. They got unique look and feel. Hundreds of races! Cloned storm troopers. Jedi fighting a whole army of androids. You name it.

The love story is well embedded and the story is quite ok (for Star Wars).

I will go to the cinema and watch Episode 2 several times. IT DELIVERS. YES, SIR! SATISFACTION GUARANTEED.

10/10 - A perfect 10.

title: I came... I saw... I almost fell asleep.
review:
Wow. I saw a screening with some friends last night... and boy was this a lame attempt of Lucas trying to regain his PERMANENTLY LOST creative talent. I have to admit, it WAS better than Phantom, but it will never beat the old trilogy.

I must say it had some great affects... better than Spider-Man's. But at least in Spider-Man there was character development, a GREAT plot, GREAT acting (save Ms. Dunst), and great directing skills.

There was no character development. The worst plot yet... since when were Jedi like priests? They can't have girlfriends? Utterly bull. Lucas is trying to come up with better ideas. The acting was...hmmm...how do i put this? oh yeah: AWFUL. Ewan M. and Samuel J. were the only good parts. The directing is the same as the acting, it would have been better off made by retarded monkeys.

The action was good, well coreographed, as always. But I didn't get the same adrenaline rush as I did in Spidey. Who does Haden C. think he's fooling? He should be a clothing model... so he wont have to open his mouth and make an idiot of himself. The Yoda fight was cool, like most of them. But the clone attack thingy was pretty lame. The title sounds like a bad political statement.

In the end... this was the worst movie of the summer. Still better than Phantom. If you are a die-hard fan don't expect much. Spider-Man is much better. All Clones is is Battlefield Earth with a Star Wars makeover, good effects, and two more good acting jobs. If you need to see a movie this summer... see Spidey while you can. But of course if you must cure your insomnia, see Clones, it will do just the trick.

2/10

title: The Force Returns in Full Power
review:
Dear Star Wars Fans!

I just saw the premiere of Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones at my local theater... If you lost your faith in Lucas's last work and if you thought that he was not able to tell stories anymore, well... you are completely wrong. This picture is just UNBELIEVABLE - this is the first actually real STAR WARS film - battles of incredible scale that you have never seen in a Sci-Fi film before. I must admit also that this is the first episode of the saga that made me cry like a child. Now I realize why Anakin will become Darth Vader some day... Perhaps the complete answer will be in Episode III but now I saw that Anakin's character has a human heart - he loves and he hates with such strong feelings that a person like you and me could have, if something really beautiful or terrible happens in our lives. We feel love and anger all the time and we cannot stop it because sometimes it happens that we lose someone precious for us and we cannot bring him back. We are not God. And we cry and we bleed. We are just people. That's why I cannot blame no one... even if he is meant to be a Jedi. Next wonderful presence in the film is Obi Wan Kenobi - very different form Episode I, now he is more confident, more powerful - he is a knight! No more, no less. Perhaps the most entertaining feature in Episode II is the tandem Yoda-Mace Windu. Now i see what the Jedi Council is capable of. Mr. Jackson is far more convincing as Windu even than his character from Pulp Fiction. And if I was a part of AMPAS, next year I would vote with two hands up for Yoda as Best Supporting Actor - this time you will forget that the small Jedi Master is actually computer generated.

This film will touch the most unreachable parts of your fantasy and your hearts... Please, see it on big screen and you'll never forget it.

THE FORCE IS HERE AS NEVER BEFORE AND THE CLONE WAR HAS BEGUN! Now we have three years to survive...the wait for III.

title: Fantastic, A 10 out of 10
review: I just got back from a showing of this movie, and my God, what an event. Everything and more was in this movie, from the romance to the high powered action scenes.  Some people still are naysayers (mostly due to the Phantom Menace), but you have to love a movie in which Yoda kicks some serious ass and Jar Jar Binks brings about the destruction of the universe (you'll just have to go and see).  This movie was incredible.  Those who complain about the bad acting, wooden dialogue, and lack of story apparently haven't seen the original trilogy, which in itself is incredible.  All in all, a fantastic movie.

review: I have one thing to say, I will personally take on anyone who dares to knock this film. I will be kickin' it Yoda style on their ass. title: Bad acting, writing, directing. Great renderings of boring battles.
review:
More and more of the movies I see lately make me wish silent movies were still popular. The score and sound effects were fine, but the dialogue was just plain awful.

Like the funeral scene in Spider-man, I had to wince every time an actor opened his or her mouth. Just notice Hayden's portrayal of what a person sounds like while having a nightmare.

Did you like the acting in Titanic? Yes? Then you will probably disagree with me about this movie.

Yoda this and Yoda that... His big scene was ridiculous, kung-fu-theater fair.

Turn off your brain and you're still not going to like it.

The major battles look fantastic, but do nothing to advance the story. We just get to see a bunch of machines blowing up other machines (and faceless clones.) There's no pathos in watching extras fall. Even when they are Jedi extras.

Forget my money, I want my two and a half hours back.

title: Unfeasibly cheesy (but great!)
review:
Just got back from seeing Episode II. Great movie, thoroughly enjoyable, but cheesier than a ploughman's lunch.

I've read comments about this being not a 'fans only' film but I couldn't disagree more. To me this seems like George Lucas looked at a list of what the fans wanted from this movie following the differing responses to Episode I (which I liked) and tried to fit as many of them in as possible.

Much of the action, locations and dialogue has been taken from the original trilogy and given a new twist, which means any fan will be smiling, nodding and chuckling knowingly at the events that occur. There are loads of humorous elements (some unintentional) and possibly a few too many times when they have tried to explain future events in the saga which in one case leaves a gaping plot hole.

These may sound like criticisms but they are what make the film enjoyable. It's a little too in-jokey and fan-friendly to fit snugly in the saga - it's almost a 'best of Star Wars' compilation/tribute - but it's still good fun, which is what movies are all about.

A final word about the development of Anakin's character - really good in my view. There are plenty of moments where you see the dark side come across him, and I think Hayden Christiansen did a good job of portraying him...

Roll on Episode III, where things should get really nasty!

title: The Greatest Saga of Science Fiction back with a bang!!!
review: All elements of this film build on the foundation of the first film.  I felt also when watching this that the new trilogy is gathering pace towards it's climax.  The cast is improved from the first film with Christopher Lee giving a glorious performance as the machiavellian Count Dooku.  It's great to have a classic English actor playing a central role in a Star Wars film again.  I have to say that in the lead up to the film I wasn't convinced but well done to Hayden Christensen for pulling it off.  He has given the role of Anakin Skywalker the requisite brilliance, impetuousness and petulance that will ultimately lead him to the Dark Side of the Force.  Padme is again played almost as a "mini-Leia" by the gifted Natalie Portman (we await her performance in the last instalment of the trilogy).  The relationship between Anakin and Padme is dealt with tenderly and with clarity over their difficulties.  For very different reasons they struggle to deal with their feelings for one another.  By the end of the film the light sabre battle has to be seen to be believed and if that is all your interested in then you will not feel short changed.  All in all a magnificent follow up to the low-key Phantom Menace and I await the time when I can watch all six films back to back at my local cinema!

title: Overall entertaining, but someone needs to take away George's CGI toys....
review: I won't give any plot spoilers here, but just my general impressions after seeing the film at 12:01 last night.  High points were definately the music (although I didn't recall any new themes being introduced, rather variations on old), the costuming (Natalie looks spectacular in everything), the creatures (although one needed to be attacked with some lemon and drawn butter rather than a blaster *grin*), and the ships (the first big one being very reminiscent of the prop plane in Casablanca).  The droids were very entertaining, and Yoda kicked his little green butt into overdrive for some seriously Jackie Chan-type action! Who knew?  However, while overall the plot and storyline started coming together, I felt that similar to Episode I the dialogue and acting really have taken a backseat to the special effects. While I can't deny that they are indeed beautiful, I have two specific issues with them.  First that they are indeed so perfect as to not have the somewhat gritty reality quality that the first films had.  They feel more like a video game or a cartoon at times than a film.  Secondly, that there are so many separate elements included on the screen in some scenes that it becomes overwhelming and scatters the focus of the scene itself.  Also, in re-watching the first films, I was struck at how much edgier both the dialogue and the characters were then.  While many of us could recite and quote the great lines from the first three films, the lines from Episodes I and II seem to be forced and in some cases are simply recycled poorly. Amidala could have been edgier with better lines, and a more intense, less "American Pie" teenage boy to play against.  The audience laughed in places that it obviously wasn't intended, and it was unfortunately due to the hormonal rather than anguished/love-struck performance that should have been.  Ewan was good, but again needed to be more edgy and less wishy-washy....the interaction between Obi-Wan and Anakin fell flat for me, particularly since it was supposed to be taking place after they'd been together for 10 years.  10 years training as a Jedi would certainly have ingrained far more maturity and tact in Anakin even if he would have still had the ego of a 20 year old.  They would have been more like partners of mutual respect, rather than the relationship seen.....one that could have been undermined in a far more effective subtle fashion than occurred.  It was actually this relationship that was the key to the entire plot of this film.....Anakin's desire for respect and praise of his abilities, to be thought of as an equal while being egged on by the Senator who played to his ego.  Unfortunately, it simply didn't succeed.  I know some will think it blasphemous to say so, but it seems to me that while George Lucas has continued to develop his skills as a director of special effects, his skills of directing actors and his writing seem to have atrophied a bit over the years.  I was reminded of the adage that simply because you *can* do something (i.e. with technology) doesn't mean that you *should*.  Less is more, and using effects as enhancement and backdrop rather than making them the overwhelming star would have instead made this a film at least equal to the original three.  I feel that Lucas is truly visionary, has blazed the trail for the present movie industry, and will bring them finally into the age of digital projection that has so long been overdue.  However, in regards to this film, I think that perhaps to have done this as a collaborative effort with another strong director (such as the "Raiders" series with Spielberg) would have achieved a far more effective end result.

title: Bad movie, great implications
review:
As a Star Wars universe fan, I found myself concentrating less and less on "Attack of the Clones" as a movie in and of itself; the dialogue (terrible!) love scenes (cringe-inducing) and CGI (rubbery) made it hard to applaud this work. However, the ideas in the movie, and the plot threads that connect it back to "The Phantom Menace" and, especially, forward to the original trilogy definitely make this worth the eight bucks. Go with friends who've read all the novels and discuss amongst yourselves afterwards.

Fortunately, there's no talk of mitochorians or virgin births; instead, there's an angry, smoldering (tall) Anakin intensely seducing young Amidala in some dimly lit, almost creepy scenes; but hey, else would Darth Vader court, anyway? The actors do the best they can with the lines they've been forced to read, but that doesn't stop you from wanting them to just Be Quiet. The action scenes are good, and fast, and if you don't mind that everyone, Jedi or layman, seems to defy physics and basic concepts about matter and acceleration, you'll be suitably impressed.

The new worlds were cool, if a bit too reminiscent of past movies; though if you played "PodRacer" you'll really appreciate the scene where Obi-Wan and Anakin chase an assassin through Corscecant (sorry, can't spell). Yoda kicks some serious gravity-defying butt, Palpatine gets more and more evil, and Boba Fett! he's Australian! who knew! Yes, all in all it's worth seeing, kiddies. Banish "The Phantom Menace" from your mind and get thee to a theater. George Lucas is in my good books once again.

title: I am only "partially" disappointed...
review: What can you say about a cultural phenomena? Yes, again the special effects were mind blowing, but again, special effects don't make a film great. Episode II follows Anakin trying to deal with his conflict: should he love Padme, even if it means breaking his Jedi oath; while Obi-Wan investigates a multi-layered plot against the Republic and its Jedi guardians.  Fans of the series will love seeing more back story revealed (meeting Boba Fett's father, seeing C3P0 and R2D2 first teaming up, seeing the first plans for the Death Star, meeting the aunt and uncle who will raise Luke), watching Anakin slowing changing to what will become the Dark Lord himself, and a cool battle between the Jedis and their new enemies. But too many flat spots, sprinkled with flat acting, scenes that reminded me of "Blade Runner," and pedestrian dialogue, grounded this latest installment on an earthly plane. When the action finally comes, the film is over and I felt cheated. If it wasn't for the best scene in the film (watching Master Yoda fight with a light saber), I would have been "totally" disappointed. With the Yoda scene I am only "partially" disappointed as I cautiously await Lucas' last shot at redeeming his pop culture crown.

title: The Force is Strong with this one.
review:
The developing story lines are now bridging the gap from The Phantom Menace to A New Hope, and I'll be giving Attack of the Clones a second viewing.

No matter what the critics say about it I thought it was spectacular entertainment, and a fabulous roller-coaster ride, and all the while like the other Star Wars movies it still remains essentially a people story, of friendship, commitment, love, honour and fortitude in the face of adversary. Star Wars is now truly a classic movie saga that will be enjoyed by people of all ages in the years to come.

Oh how I just wish the galactic society of the Star Wars saga was for real.

Well done George, your back on track, looking forward to on Episode 3.

title: Really enjoyed this movie

I can't wait to see what the 3rd movie will bring, since that is going to be the most important one. It will bring all the movies together, too bad we have to wait until 2005.

Anyway, hope you all enjoyed this one as much as we did.

title: Better than Episode I
review: This second episode of Star Wars is stunning visually, amazing in sound effects, impressive in scenery and interesting in plot. Several amazing sequences are state of the art. For example, a scene involving a meteorite field is even more impressive than the pod racing of episode I! I truly enjoyed it for all the adventures that happen to the well known characters of Star Wars. Watch it and you will see why Yoda is such a great Jedi master! You will discover Boba Fett's background. You will witness the events that affected Anakin Skywalker's life. "Attack of the Clones" has more weird & wonderful aliens which of course is all part of the Star Wars universe, which I particularly liked in this episode.  For those of you who were disappointed by "The Phantom Menace", or just annoyed by Jar Jar Binks' character, make sure you watch "Attack of the Clones". Jar Jar's character only has three scenes. And for fans of the original episodes IV, V & VI: you should enjoy R2-D2 and C-3PO's roles and the battle scenes as impressive as the snowy "Empire Strikes Back" ones.

title: THE FILM'S COOL, BUT COOL MOMENTS ARE NOT EXPANDED!!!
review: Well folks, I have just returned from the premiere here in Riga and if I might say it in one word - THE FILMS IS FANTASTIC. The early critics and press that said that the force is STRONG with this one were right! Completely! Or Almost... But first the good bits: A) The film completely satisfies both in term of action, eye candy and just everything you hear and see. B) It's definately stronger than PHANTOM MENACE and it really shows to a die hard STAR WARS fan, what a good star wars movie can be. This film definately worth seeing. I try to avoid spoilers, but there were just everything you, a star wars fan need: lots of action, cool fx, the scale of everything is fantastic, the love story behind is great. For example the Jango Fett fight or finale lighsaber duel - THEY ARE GOOD, but they seems to be short, far too short. They should have been more expanded. I love them and for me there is not enough time given to them. I could give more examples. 3) The whole movie you wait for something big, and when it seems to be coming- the movie ends. So that's of a minor complaints. But heck, bollocks to complaints. Go and see the movie! It's still rules.

title: The Best Star Wars Movie Ever!
review:
Let's get one thing straight: Attack Of The Clones is better than The Phantom Menace. Far better. Things start off a bit slow-paced, although there are a good few lively bits to keep people interested. However, things start to really pick up in the second half, with the pace building gradually until the explosive finale. I need to talk more about this ending. Without giving away any details, it makes the climactic battle in Episode I (the one good thing about the movie) look like Ben Stiller's battle with the dog in "There's Something About Mary". It kicks ass.

Anakin Skywalker (now older and much less annoying) makes a far more interesting partner for Obi-Wan Kenobi than Qui-Gon Jinn from Episode I. Obi-Wan seems more developed in this movie, and Anakin, whose dark side is just beginning to show, is a joy to watch. His relationship with Amidala is actually quite touching, and not as sickening as I thought it would be. Both Yoda and Mace Windu (yes, that's Samuel L. Jackson) have bigger and better roles, especially Yoda, who could very well steal the show by, without giving anything away, playing a part in what has to be the best moment in the Star Wars saga. Thankfully, Jar Jar Binks is only in the film in a cameo role, but the annoying character in this part is C-3PO, with some of the most cringe-worthy one liners I have ever heard. George Lucas will never learn.

Now for the bad guys. Jango Fett is, sadly, no Darth Maul. Jango, a bounty hunter, may have a bigger role than Darth Maul, but Darth Maul's smaller role was more effective, and had a bigger impact. But Jango Fett still manages to look cool. The film's best villain, however, is Count Dooku, played with sinister excellence by Christopher Lee. While Jango is the villain everyone thinks is cool, Dooku brings in the boo-hiss factor with the thankless role as the villain everybody will love to hate. It is he who surpasses Darth Maul, and (I'm about to make a bold statement I may regret) whose presence could even come close to matching that of the legendary Darth Vader.

With fantastic battles, and the choice to give great characters more screen-time at the expense of bad ones, this is a big improvement. Unlike Episode I, Attack Of The Clones can be placed side by side, perhaps even on a higher level, than the original trilogy.

10/10

title: THE WORST OF THEM ALL!!!!!

title: Don't worry so much
review:
After reading many reviews of AOTC and their harsh criticisms of the dialogue and plot, I have a question: How many Star Wars fans, on the news that prequels would be made, thought "Yes, I can't wait to hear some of that great dialogue once again"? Hell no, you wanted great special effects, a journey into new and exciting worlds, and to find out how Anakin succumbed to the dark side. I enjoyed AOTC thoroughly, and although it is a bit esoteric and may alienate non-fans, Star Wars lovers will find that this is what the hoped for in Episode I.

Yes, the dialogue needed another draft, but it wasn't nearly as bad as everyone is making it out to be. The romance isn't the cringe-worthy affair I thought it would be. It was awkward, but young romance is suppose to be awkward, you can't expect Anakin to as smooth as Han Solo, it wouldn't fit the character. Well, now that I think about it, Hayden Christensen will never be as smooth as Harrison Ford, but he's a capable actor. Portman, on the other hand, needed to loosen up. Sometimes she acted like she was in one of those old Calvin Klein commercials.

But the Brits and Yoda steal the show. Ewan McGregor commands authority, and Christopher Lee plays the slick and slimy villian as only he can. And yes, Yoda's lightsaber duel lives up to the hype. I thought Samuel Jackson was pretty good too, but he does look uncomfortable when he can't say motherf---er all the time. Oh well, I'll watch "Pulp Fiction" for that.

Anyway, just sit back and enjoy the 3rd best Star Wars film to date.

title: Lucas goes back to basics with lots of surprises
review:
In "Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones ", Lucas goes back to basics: staying with a simple story and great special effects; ties several loose ends (or rather unanswered questions); and most importantly expands the story and sets up the next and final episode of the prequel trilogy. Reviewers were rather divided on the movie, some screaming "A+" and some screaming "bloody hell". Without a doubt this part is superior to "Episode I", with faster action, more spectacular special effects and more character development. And while I believe that critics nowadays are completely unreliable (consider the Sony Movie Studio's fake critic) and the major ones tend to vote in blocks (Olympic skating comes to mind), I do agree with one of the common arguments from the negative reviews: "this movie will appeal much more to the true fan of "Star Wars" saga"... except that I find nothing NEGATIVE in that comment: Why in the world would anyone who is NOT a fan, ever go see Part II of a series? Even universally praised and accepted movies like "Gone With the Wind" or "Citizen Kane" don't appeal to everyone.

For the true fans, a lot of fun moments await: subtle hints tying the story or re-creating the mood of the original series (for example: a certain theme being played at an appropriate time, a preview of person appearing later in the series or an event which was mentioned in the original series but happened beforehand). I won't spoil anything, except to say: watch everything carefully. Just as in "Phantom Menace", when you notice the Wookies sitting in the Galactic Senate only the second time you see the movie, just so in "Attack of the Clones" there are events and tie-ins that you will certainly miss while watching the movie for the first time. Myself, I intend to wait a couple of weeks until the crowds clear out a bit and will go see the movie for the second time. Good job George, and good luck at the boxoffice (although you most likely won't need it).

I give it an overall 9 out of 10 ranking it right after "Empire Strikes Back". Story-line and that intangible "feeling" get 7.5, but the action, pace of the movie and special effects get a perfect 10: the best in the series so far.

title: The Force Needs Character
review:
Well, this film can be reviewed as two seperate movies, really. One is a visual treat on a level never before seen in the cinema. The other is a character play that clunks along like cinematic artereosclerosis.

Fans who hope for an "improvement" on "Phantom Menace" may be thinking quite a bit over "Clones". The story continues to be an explanation of the first trilogy rather than a story on its own. It reads like a backstory. The implication is always that the first three films are the reverential material, and "Clones" (along with "Menace") is merely the prolog. Consequently, none of the characters have any of the charm that the first films had. This is a problem that will persist into "Episode III". It is a major dramatic weakness that no amount of special effects can cure.

Hayden Christensen does his best to present a conflicted Anakin. The character has to play against a continuing wooden Ewan McGregor, who has yet to capture the gravitas of Alec Guinness. Christensen also has to contend with Nathalie Portman and convince the audience that we should believe and care that the two are falling in love. I don't. I can understand Anakin's obsession, but not Portman as the object of it. In order to be three dimensional and empathetic, one must be more than an object. And there's that lack-of-charm thing again.

Lucas has repeatedly said that this prequel triology is meant to find an echo with the first three. Obi Wan is Obi Wan, Anakin is the Luke replacement, Amidala is the Lea replacement, Jar Jar is the Chewbacca replacement, jango Fett is the Boba replacement, and so on. Where's the Han Solo replacement, the "rogish" character that personified the charm of the first three films? It isn't there.

The story itself could be compelling, but is bogged down again by explication. Apart from a pretty good car chase scene in the first quarter of the movie, nothing really happens. The plot revolves around an assassination attempt on Senator Amidalla, but we the audience never get a sense of urgency because we don't care about her. The only interesting thing is the tension between Obi Wan and Anakin, and if anything, we empathize with Anakin. Obi Wan is a priggish ass.

I'm not quite sure what to make of "Crouching Tiger, Hidden Yoda". It seems to me that his inability to perceive Palpatine's machinations, along with his generalling at the end of the film is out of character. But it got a good laugh (one of the few the audience had).Personally, I would like to have seen more seducing between Palpatine and Anakin, and this promises to be the one true character play of this trilogy.

Now, let's look at the other film: the visuals. Nothing on this scale has ever been seen in the cinema. The digital video photography is almost on par with celluloid. Almost. The only fault is the washed out palette when the filming moves into sunlight. The definition is as good as traditional 35mm, and signals a final death knell for the latter medium. Technical Oscar for ILM.

The production design is what one would expect from Lucasfilm. Apart from nods to Bladerunner, Metropolis and Gladiator (to name a few) the vistas are magnificent and well worth seeing the movie over again.

All things considered, though, when I left the theatre today, I wanted to load my VCR with some recent tapes of "Enterprise" and watch characters I really care about. The story might be a little smaller in scale, but "Birth of the Federation" is a more interesting story than "Birth of the Empire".

title: The Thrill Is (Going, ... Going,...), GONE!
review: What happened???  Bad acting, bad dialogue, bad directing!!! How did George let this one get away from him?  After four real thrillers, this one is a dramatic let down. I can only hope that Episode III will approach some of the greatness of Episodes IV, V, & VI.

title: Not quite there yet... but getting close.
review:
Note: I'll try to keep this review spoiler-free.

I've just returned from the "world premiere" of Star Wars: Episode II. Us Finns got the rare opportunity to be amongst the first in the world to see Episode II in the theaters; don't know why or how, but there you go.

In short: it's better than Episode I. Still, it suffers from many of the same problems which haunted The Phantom Menace; Lucas has definite problems directing actors, some of the dialogue is bizarre to say the least, the characters and the storyline appear to be secondary to the massive amounts of CGI, and that peculiar sense of detachment is ever present. We are shown people struggling, fighting, talking and loving, but it just doesn't really do anything for you.

Most of the film's good points have to do with technical merits. Visually, it's often breath-taking. We visit the street level at Coruscant and and the frame is filled with almost a sensory overload. It's not Blade Runner, as the city appeared to be suspiciously free of filth, pollution and grime, but it was definitely a living and breathing city somewhere far, far away. The wizards at ILM truly exceeded themselves on this movie, as one couldn't help staring in wonderment at several of the film's large sets and action pieces. One exception though: CGI Yoda. Nope, didn't buy that at all. There was always something a bit wrong about his movements and his facial expressions when talking. Completely CGI characters just aren't convincing yet. Which reminds me of Jar Jar. He had a really minor role and the gibberish he spouts was mercifully kept to a minimum.

Alas, everything's not perfect in the land of digital filmmaking. I noticed at least one scene where the background was far too bright, draining the foreground of contrast and detail. There were also numerous scenes were people's faces were severely underlit, resulting in almost a silhoutte-like face with only a very small amount of detail. This couldn't have been intentional, since the scenes in question required the characters' emotions being visible on their faces. I'll be sure to make comparisons when watching the movie digitally projected (yes, we've got one of those theaters in Finland now).

Ben Burtt's sound design reminded me very much of The Phantom Menace. Burtt seems to be very fond of sounds that go "chak-chak-chak", "wrap-wrap-wrap" and "woop-woop-woop". All the various spaceships and other vessels have their own distinctive sound, but they all share the same chattering characteristic. I got really annoyed when even the monsters couldn't howl properly; instead they went "skreek-krek-krek-krek". You'll see, no, hear what I mean :)

Much has been said about Star Wars' sense of adventure and how it's back in Episode II. There's a lot of action, yes, but it still doesn't have that same wreckless feeling of high adventure from episodes 4 and 5. Ideas ripped from video games do not equal adventure, they equal easy conversions to Game Boy Advance titles. Still, that said, Episode II has its fair share of fun action sequences, big explosions and beautiful tracking shots through alien cities and environments.

My biggest objection has to do with the love story. Where Episode I was made for kids, this one's for teenagers. Or would be, if it were handled properly; I'm afraid teenage girls with posters of whats-his-name on their walls are walking out of the theatre with dry eyes. You all know that Anakin and Amidala become lovers, so that's not a spoiler, OK? But the way it's presented gave me the willies. Apparently, all it takes is one practical joke, some rolling in the hay and intense staring into the other person's eyes and hey presto! Cue that wonderful Williams love theme! I simply didn't buy the love affair; there was nothing to make it a reality.

Both Christensen and Portman have already garnered criticism about their performances. It's not quite Night of the Living Dead out there, but yes, both are somewhat wooden most of the time. Christensen manages a couple of really convincing stares, foreshadowing the character Anakin will become, but for most of the time he sounds like he's having trouble with pronounciation. Take that sponge out of your mouth, I felt like shouting.

The main storyline with the clone wars... I liked it, even though Lucas sprang Count Dooku out of thin air. It was nice to see bits and pieces which set up episodes 4-6. The plot was easy enough to follow and left enough questions unanswered to make Episode III interesting. But I promised no spoilers, so no more of the plot.

All in all, I give Episode II 7 out of 10. The story actually made me look forward to Episode III, while I was almost ready to give up on Star Wars after Episode I. Here's hoping that Lucas can keep this upward trend going and we'll end up with a good movie in two years' time.
