title: Lucas blows the audience away again.
review:
Well, for the first time ever, I went to an opening-day showing of a Star Wars movie. The crowd was into it from the beginning, as I have not head a crowd into a movie since Empire Strikes Back. When the opening titles came up, everyone cheered. And there were many more cheers to be had, especially during he climax, where the audience roared its approval more than once. When the end credits came up there was a final ovation as people got up to leave.

This was perhaps the best of the 5 movies so far, but it is hard for me to say after only one sitting. There is so much going on in every scene that it will take at least 2 or 3 viewings to catch it all. I am certain I missed little tidbits here and there. But of course I was able to follow the movie just fine and enjoyed it thoroughly. The scenery and effects are breath-taking. Once again a Lucas movie sets the standard as the greatest effects achievement to date -- which will stand probably until 3 years from now, when he beats himself yet again.

Many people, particularly critics, have complained about the acting and dialog. I do not understand the problem. I thought Hayden Christiansen in particular was an outstanding Anakin. In one scene in particular, where he recounts some very un-Jedi-like behavior to a stunned Amidala, he shows definite signs of the future -- the fall to Darkness and his transmogrification into the evil Lord Darth Vader. Oh, he's not there yet -- but you can see he's well on his way down that road, and perhaps so far that even if Obi-wan realized it, he wouldn't have been able to stop him.

The other actors turned in fine performances in my opinion. The dialog was a bit stilted at times, but in what Star Wars movie, including the "classic" three, was this not the case? I am not sure why people who know and love these other movies, have found fault with the very same items in this movie, that appear not to bother them in the others.

The story is good in this movie, perhaps the most intriguing of all. You will see, as things unfold, the seeds being laid for many things. You will find out why many of the things that existed in Episode 4 (Star Wars) but not in Episode 1 (Phantom Menace) came to be. After Episode 1 it seemed odd that in so short a time we could have Star Destroyers, Stormtroopers, Bounty Hunters, and Dark Sith Lords. In this current installment, some of that is explained, some is hinted and foreshadowed.

In all I found many of the scenes excellent, and of course the lightsaber battles are wonderful as always. I am still not sure if the "primary" saber battle in this movie or in Episode 1 (with Darth Maul) is the best... I think I will have to view it several more times to be sure. But it is very close, and it is exciting and fun to watch. The crowd cheered multiple times at this part, too.

I have only good to say about this movie. Not one thing was bad about it. It had a great balance of action and drama, fast scenes and slow, excitement and tense personal interaction. It was visually stunning. The sound was great. The sound track was, as always, magnificent. In all, this movie is a proud addition to the greatest series of movies ever made.

Great job, George. Hats off to the entire cast and crew. I can't wait till Episode 3.

My score: 10/10

title: It Was Okay
review:
Great? No. Acceptable, yes. C+/B-. Go see it for what it is, not for what it's not (a religious experience).

Portman and Christensen were better than reviewed. But there were some moments that just kind of made me want to gag. The effects weren't really any more impressive than Phantom Menace's--except of Yoda's duel at the the end.

I've watched the first two movies many times. Will watch this one again? I doubt it.

title: Dazzling
review: This is better. Much, much better. A striking piece of science-fiction, a dazzling piece of cinema. A vast improvement on Episode one both in tone and in quality, Episode II is a far meatier prospect and more than meets (almost unrealistic) expectation. For all the (excellent) CGI, this is dark, tough, grim storytelling, full of deceit and betrayal. Along with Empire, Clones is the most adult chapter of the saga. The odd clunker of dialogue and stale delivery aside, this is strong, satisfying stuff. Jango Fett was underused (as always, Lucas seems uninterested with his most complex character), but that is not a big complaint. The force is very, very strong with this one. Watch it and see a master visual artist unfold an interesting chapter in his epic saga.

title: What a great fit in the saga!
review: I have been hearing people complaining about how uninspired this film is emotionally. I believe this is for good reason. We have seen how ships in Phantom Menace had beautiful lines and style, but as we move through time towards A New Hope it becomes utilitarian and functional. This has been explained as a move from an age of the Republic's beauty and art into an age of Trade Federation cold capitalism and ultimately into an age of Imperial totalitarianism. I believe a similar thing is happening with personality styles. We have a republic that is sick and dying and being torn apart, and much of it is based on the fact that the politicians are mostly bureaucrats and passionless, and that a Jedi's guiding principle is restraining emotions. Since these are the people who are getting the wool pulled over their eyes by charismatic separatists like Dooku and Sidious, you can see why they are destined to fail. Like many civilizations in decline, they are apathetic and listless, and they are bound to be boring in comparison to their descendants Han Solo, Leia, Luke Skywalker in the coming rebellion who have a reason to light a fire in their eyes and hearts. They are like the revolutionaries that fought for freedom in America. They are the Jeffersons and Reveres of Star Wars. Comparing a Naboo Senator and a pack of cool headed Jedis to the gang on the Millenium Falcon is unreasonable. It is like comparing George W. Bush to George Washington. It all depends on whether you are trying to defend freedom from a position of power, or fighting for it from a far off empire's "Most Wanted" list. Remember, England promised the death penalty for anyone who signed the Declaration of Independence. America is an old republic now, I see no passion in leadership here either. To sum it up. If Han, Leia, and Luke were running the Republic, I doubt they would have been all that interesting either. Eddie Keever

title: **1/2 out of five. It has some good moments but in the end its style over substance.
review: Boy, is the dialogue bad! Aswell as some of the acting. But the great Samuel L. Jackson is good. And the scene in the arena is breathtakingly awesome. But at times the film drags and it feels as if Lucas thought up of some special effects before the script. And that title is pathetic. All n' all a mediocre film.

title: Up there with the originals - and Yoda fights!
review:
Brilliant, excellent, as good as all the original 3 movies. Having been a huge fan of Star Wars since my childhood I was a little disappointed by Phantom Menace. Not so Attack of Clones, it had everything - The humor, the action, the special effects, the dramatic plot, the immense sets with thousands of extras, etc. Star Wars fans, go see it as soon as possible.

Yes, perhaps the acting is wooden at times but so were the originals, no-one cared then except critics. Ewan McGregor is far less annoying as Obi Wan, having grown into the part well, and Christiansen portrays Anakin with a lot of maturity, he finds the schizophrenic nature of the character perfectly. C3PO and R2D2 are back with their double act, amusing as ever and Natalie Portman is better than in Phantom too, not as stilted, I felt. Plus Jar-Jar is hardly in it (although he plays a pivotal role in the war).

For the Star Wars fan there are a lot of extra plot points too. I found myself thinking 'Oh I see!', 'So that's why...' and 'I know that name!' all the way through. Very satisfying.

And it's a real treat to see Yoda displaying his skills with a light-sabre at last. Go see it, if you loved the originals then you'll love Attack of the Clones.

title: Film of the year!
review:
After seeing the latest Star Wars film, I can't believe just how good it is. I enjoyed The Phantom Menace but didn't think that it was as good as the original trilogy. Attack of the Clones however really is as good parts 4,5 and 6, no matter what some snotty critics may say. I saw it in an (obviously) full cinema and everyone seemed to be impressed by it. The only part that drew a groan from the audience was the appearance of Jar Jar Binks; but that was more than made up for by the amazing action sequences, each one better than the last - the speeder chase on Coruscant, Jango Fett vs.Obi Wan Kenobi(in the rain!),and finally the battle between Jedis, Clone troopers, droids and monsters in a gladiator arena.

Added to that was an exciting mystery thriller involving Obi Wan(another great performance from Ewan McGregor after last years fantastic Moulin Rouge), and a well handled and believable love story between Anakin and Padme.

This movie also explains how Anakin starts his path toward the dark side which will eventually lead to him becoming Darth Vader, and Hayden Christensen handles the role very well.

The best performances however come from Christopher Lee as the evil ex Jedi Count Dooku, and Ian McDiarmid as Supreme Chancellor Palpatine who's understated performance as the master political puppeteer is excellent.

Plus if all this doesn't sound good enough we actually get to see Yoda wield a light sabre and prove why he's a Jedi Master!

George Lucas is back on top form and the worlds and characters he has created are as entertaining and exciting as ever.

See it and enjoy! 10 out of 10!

title: Great continuation of the Star Wars saga (spoilers)
review:
Today, the day after opening I bagged school to see Star Wars- Episode II: Attack of the Clones. After three years of waiting the question is does it live up to potential and I can happily say that it does. The action sequences are simply amazing. The Battle on Geonosis was by far THE best battle I have ever seen in a Star Wars film. The acting unfortunatly was weak (from a few characters) but it is in every Star Wars movie so I can dismiss it for the excellent story. As a big fan of both Star Wars and Movies I can honestly say this is one of my new favorites.

STAR WARS, My opinion so far (FAVORITE TO LEAST FAVORITE) 1. The Empire Strikes Back 2. A New Hope 3. Attack of the Clones 4. Return of the Jedi 5. The Phantom Menace

title: A worthy Star Wars movie.
review: Excuse for a minute the sometimes laugh-out dialogue.  Excuse for one-second the convoluted plot.  With great pleasure I must report that "Attack of the Clones" for the most part captures the spirit of the original trilogy, while creating a new feeling for the new ones.  Listen, Star Wars has always had comic book dialogue, this one is no different.  The love story is a little weak, but it is a small part of this movie.  For Star Wars fans, the thrill of seeing the relationship between Obi-Wan and Anakin, the creation of the Clone-troopers,  and the breathtaking action is enough to make everyone forget the dissapointing Episode 1.  And there is one scene that everyone should go in knowing absolutely nothing about, but alas, most reviewers seem compelled to spill the beans on what is one of the most thrilling sequences in Star Wars history.  I knew of this scene before going in, and wished I hadn't.  Spoiler free for Episode 3 is my motto now.  So Star Wars fans, our series is alive and well and 3 years from now it all comes to and end. Episode 2 is a great set-up for the final chapter, and last piece to the legendary Star Wars saga.

title: Yoda and Obi-Wan Kick Some Serious Butt
review:
I was blown away by this movie. I realize that the professional critics have had a field day with this one as they have with all the previous episodes. I'll briefly give my response to their comments.

The acting was wooden--dialogue too formal. I think that at least some of that is intentional. It's mainly the Jedi who speak without using contractions and that may be to help show that they are 'outside the norm'.

No spark between Amidala and Anakin or Why would she fall for him? Oh come on. Those blue puppydog eyes? The hint of danger? The old "he needs me to help him change"? I think Lucas also lets us know, albeit subtly, that Padme isn't very experienced herself romantically.

No surprises. Well, we do know who makes it alive to Episode IV so it's kind of hard to make us believe Obi-Wan might die. Still, I thought the fight and chase scenes were very well done. I also liked the view of 'normal' life on Coruscant. The diner, the club, the advertisements on the street were nice reminders that this is a complete universe.

No memorable lines. That one came from Roger Ebert. Please. "Good job." "I don't think so." "Why do I feel you'll be the death of me?"

That's all from me. I have to go get ready to see it again.

title: a few words for the critics
review:
In my opinion, Episode 2 is either the second or third best installment of the Star Wars series. That having been said, I feel somewhat inspired to mount a defense against the film's critics...

1) "The acting is bad" -- give me a break. Have you ever watched the original trilogy? "But I was gonna go to the tashi station to pick up some power converters!" "No... that's not true!!! That's impossible!!!" Every line Luke says until ROTJ is in a long, drawn out whine!!! Is that the good acting which we're to judge Attack of the Clones by? The acting in this film is excellent in comparison to the acting in the original trilogy.

2) "This movie is one big computer effect" -- name me 1 hollywood sci-fi film over the past 10 years that hasn't been a computer effect. What was Lord of the Rings, one of last year's best picture nominees... but a computer effect? Would the critics of this film prefer that Lucas go back to using stop motion miniatures? Or better yet... cut/splice spaceships in so that we can see the black boxes around them when they fly? That would certainly be thrilling.

3) "We already know Anakin's going to become bad, why foreshadow it?" -- this might be the single dumbest thing I've ever read in a review. If you go into episodes 1 through 3 with that mentality, you may as well not go in at all. What do you think the point of these installments is, exactly, if not to show how Anakin turns to the dark side? Should there be no indications that he is going to turn evil before the moment that he actually does? Aside from making his transformation completely fantastic and without any rational basis, what would that accomplish?

I'm sure that there are other reasons out there for people to continue to berate George Lucas' recent installment in the Star Wars saga... but let me close this defense with one comment. Without George Lucas, there would be no Star Wars saga at all.

title: The Best Summer Blockbuster in Years!!`
review:
Ok, I'll keep this short. I thought movie was incredible. It's lightyears beyond Phantom Menace and it's everything a summer blockbuster should be. I did not walk out of this one feeling cheated or empty. Instead, I simply felt like I'd had an awesome evening at the movies.

Yes, Star Wars is finally back. This one doesn't really feel like the originals. It feels more like a hybrid between between Menace (very appropriately named) and the originals. We are slowly moving toward the universe of Luke, Leia, and Han.

Anyway, I can't wait for III. Lots of questions, and the ride just got fun again!

title: Complete entertainment
review: I must admit, I left the theatre wondering if there was anything else I could ask for in a film.  I could think of nothing.  Though I have always enjoyed the Star Wars saga, I consider myself difficult to please in regards to films.  I found this film had everything I enjoy in entertainment: great characters, solid plot-line, brilliantly choreographed action sequences, a very human element, love.  This is a fantastic film.  Better yet, the Star Wars story just keeps getting better and better.  The highest recommendation.  Go have a blast.  Cheers.

title: Fantastic!!!!
review:
This was a wonderful treat to behold. What a great follow up to a not so great PHANTOM MENACE. Natalie Portman and Hayden Christensen are astonishing as the two lovers. I can not speak enough about how great this movie was. The action was great and the story very complex and intriguing.

This film introduces us to some of the more complex characters from the original three movies. We get to see how some of the characters originated and how they are all intertwind.

title: No complaints here.
review: I don't understand the complaints about how the dialog is poorly written and the acting is wooden. These are Star Wars trademarks. Have any of these people watched the first three movies at all? All three first movies had the same problems and they are thought of as classics. This movie Rules. Why you ask? Because it's a lot of fun. Sure the hour after the Coruscant chase is anywhere from talky to boring, but look at the bright point of this all: Less Jar-Jar and no Jake Lloyd. When Jar-Jar is on screen, he's helping out the bad guy. Then the movie becomes a lot of fun. The end fight scenes have a lot of stuff happening and it's awesome. The best part about this movie is that it avoids having like 3 different battles happening at once and it sticks to one at a time. It goes from having the arena battle, to the attack of the clones, to the fight with Dooku. The previous two movies had too many battles happening once. Going from one battle, to the next then another one then cutting back to them again. Then Yoda comes along and steals the movie and makes just his 5 minutes in the sun worth the price of admission alone. The best part about this movie is that it sets up the next one perfectly. I can't wait to see it, if this movie is any indication, Lucas hasn't lost it; the force is strong with this one. :-)

title: Lucas is working it out... ****
review:
I found this movie to be very entertaining. I have heard complaints about the acting and the dialogue. I see their point, but I feel it (acting, dialogue) to be appropriate. Hayden is a good actor, but Anakin, if he were real, would probably be a bit wooden. He grew up a slave, was whisked away from his mother and placed into strict discipline and training. Were he real, he would probably be confused as who he really was and his behavior around others would be awkward. Hayden plays that well.

To the Star Wars fan... the allusions made in this movie are incredible. You are really starting to understand how Vader could be. You can see the stage is set for the Empire. The seeds are also sown for what will be a small, but effective rebellion. I loved this film.

title: An Epic of Suspected Proportions
review: Star Wars has returned to the screen and this film is truly epic, but in ways that fans and even casual viewers expected. It is without a doubt a marvel to behold, despite stretched dialogue, a slightly forced romance, and some occassional moments when things seem out of character for most characters. Still, the film holds your attention well and will appeal strongly to fans of the franchise or even to casual movie goers. An improvement on the Phantom Menace, but still slightly lacking that element that made us cheer on Luke despite the odds... maybe, however, this is because we know where Anakin is heading, where the toher offered an element of surprise. Regardless, this film holds water, it functions, and is truly fun to watch. What it lacks in new concepts and character development, it more than makes up for with a fast few final minutes climaxing in setting up what will no doubt be a free for finale in episode 3.

title: Excellent plot, some clumsy dialogue
review: This is probably the third best Star Wars movie after Empire and a New Hope, and the action scenes are quite outstanding as is the plot, which draws you in. The only drawback is rather clumsy dialogue, especially in the 'love story' part of the movie - some parts looked like they were straight out of a Harlequin romance novel - but even this part got better as the movie progressed. All in all very good movie.

title: Lucas does it again!
review: For all those thinking that George Lucas had lost the Midas touch, think again.  Attack of the Clones is one of the most exhilarating, breathtaking cinematic experiences I have ever had, and more than does justice to the original trilogy.  The film looks incredible, the action sequences are mind-altering, and the acting, from Sam Jackson to Temuera Morrison to the great Christopher Lee, is top notch.  The question on everyone's mind has been, what about Hayden Christiansen?  His performance will be the most hotly debated aspect of this movie.  Your like or dislike of this film hinges on your like or dislike of his performance.  I feel he nailed it. This is a boy, not yet 20 years old, who is aware that he may one day fulfill the prophecy of bringing balance to the Force.  He is brash, cocky, impulsive, and arrogant, almost like a star athlete in high school who knows he's one of the best in the country.  His awkward interaction with Senator Amidala is what you would expect from a teenager trying to impress an older, mature woman.  Couple that with the fact that, because of his code as a Jedi apprentice, he has less than zero knowledge of women, and you find a boy trying to be a man without understanding the responsibilities a man must undertake.  I fully bought Anakin and Padme's love story, and could see the undercurrent of destructiveness inherent in it.  Overall, this movie is unbelievable.  Go and see it 5 or 6 times.

title: Maybe better than the first trilogy...
review:
I had a once in a lifetime opportunity...

and it was to see star wars episode2 attack of the clones six days prior to its release. Ã½ live in Istanbul and they organized a special premiere for the movie. I was one of the lucky persons to squeeze his butt to a seat in the theater. George Lucas shows us that he really is a supreme director. The movie is filled with emotional and political scenes. Dont ever think that it is a love movie. The trailers do not reach to its magnificence and makes it look like a stupid romantic film. Indeed the movies has a slower pace then episode 1 but its action scenes are really breathtaking. I had to hold my breath in the coruscant chase scene. I dont want to reveal much about the plot. As a star wars fan i would want to learn everything in the theater so i respect that aspect. But i can say that all comes together. Why Jar Jar was in the series in the first place? Because it was necessary for the reason you'll see in the movie. Why the hell a crippled and dwarf Yoda is a Jedi Master? Can he ever fight? Yes but you'll have to wait a few day for more details.

My biggest wish now is to live long enough to see the third installment... I feel like watching Empire for the first time and craving for some more.

Tasslehoff

title: better than Phantom Menace, But that's not saying much
review:
I was completely and utterly, thoroughly disgusted with Phantom Menace. However, George Lucas has redeemed himself somewhat.

The major downside to this movie, is that it is sad to see that this movie is not the first in the new Star Wars trilogy. Hayden Christensen is Anakin, a Not great character but better than the boy in Episode I...

The music is excellent, and some scenes made my mouth open wide in amazement, whilst others chilled me

Overall I did not like it. Why? Because: bad acting, stunted dialogue, boring plot... It's got one good part. The part where they get put in the coliseum. Count dooku is OK. Flying/jumping Yoda is silly and the overuse of cgi makes it look fake

title: He did it!
review: He finally made another star wars movie to rival the greatness of Empire Strikes back.  Lucas really out did himself this time!  I highly recommend this one to all fans out there who have forsaken the trilogy due to the childlike nature of Episode 1.

title: Two Words: Yoda Rocks!
review:
I would never make it as a movie critic; they said the movie was slow paced, I looked at my watch 30 minutes into the movie & was surprised to see 2 hours had actually passed. They said the dialog was awful and the acting stilted; I watched Anakin struggling with his feelings throughout the film and saw my own teenagers on the screen. Lucas and Hayden nailed teen angst perfectly.

The one thing the critics and I agree on is the special effects. The movie is stunning with mesmerizing action. The digital characters are amazingly realistic; Portman and MacGregor had better watch out, George may not need them next time. I'm waiting for the spin-off starring Yoda, because in "Clones" Yoda really rocks!

The only thing I didn't like was the sound effects. Apparently all spaceships, speeders, etc. sound exactly like pod-racers. You would have thought Lucas could have varied that a bit.

title: Impressive - they did it right this time
review:
This time Lucas and Co. bring back some of the feeling from the original series, and manage to get the pacing right. This movie was just fun to watch from the opening frame to the last, and I am very disappointed with some of the official reviewers, who seem to be ultra-critical(looking for some of the mythological undertones of the originals I assume, and not looking deep enough, while simultaneously forgetting that movies are about entertainment and other forms of art, and don't necessarily have to fall on the same side of the tree as their predecessors).

This movie was simply too short.

title: Almost killed by the acting
review: Let me start by saying I am not a big Star Wars fan.  I did however go to see this because it was the premier showing of a movie with DLP here in Wichita, KS.  I was most interested in seeing that above everything else, and I feel horribly let down in that aspect right away.  From there, the movie did not seem to visually entrap me like was promised with the hype. What really killed the film for me, however was the horrible acting/dialog. I found myself laughing outloud at many parts simply due to the acting being so bad.  If you are true film buff and bad acting/dialog pains you, then skip this movie!  However, if you can forget about those requirements, then the ending of this movie is worth sitting through the horrible acting.

title: More fun than, well ANYTHING.
review:
I was a midnight showing for AOTC and didn't have the highest of expectations for this film, especially after Episode 1. I can honestly say I have NEVER had such an amazingly good time whilst watching a movie. Some of the best action scenes I've ever seen on film (be it digital or otherwise).

So many amazing movie moments, #1 being Yoda's fight scene. Nothing will prepare you for how amazing it is. At my showing the ENTIRE theatre was cheering madly during these scenes. I've never seen that kind of reaction before.

Yes, some of the dialogue is horrid, but don't let that worry you. Go see it and have the time of your life.

title: No, really, it is pretty good!
review:
I was really not keen on seeing this film after seeing The Phantom Menace (which was like Jurassic Park - lovely to look at but devoid of any content). In fact, I was dragged against my will but it turned out to be a pleasant experience.

This film (again) looks beautiful and is CGI-tastic, but it does have a story and some plot. It makes you wonder why they spent so much time and money making The Phantom Menace which has nothing (other than Natalie Portman) to recommend it.

So, it should be fun to see how many hours of junk they stick on the DVD triple pack deluxe edition (available in this format for the very last time - until we release it again with a different cover to milk the fans for some more cash).

But enough of that - it's pretty good, and a vast improvement on the last one. Give it a go - you won't be bitterly disappointed. Even if it's just to see Natalie Portman and to see the little green guy kick ass, chew bubble gum - and be all out of bubble gum.

(An overly generous 8/10)

title: Anticipation Builds...
review: Star Wars first captivated my soul back in 1977, when I was young Anakin's age of 9; you can imagine a young boy's anticipation of each and every sequel...I felt that same anticipation ever since I first heard of George Lucas' plan to release the trilogy of pre-quels to my all time favorite Star Wars films. While I did enjoy Episode I and watched it over and over again, my enjoyment came not necessarily from the film itself, but more from what it represented: a filling in of the gaps of what is Star Wars the saga. I must admit, some elements of Episode I were a disappointment (J.Binks & A.Skywalker), but overall I did appreciate the film. I hoped and prayed that the next film would redeem some of Episode I's weaknesses and after just having viewed the film for the first time on opening day at 12:01 am, I can say to you that I can't wait to add this film to my collection so that I may watch it over and over as well. In just over 12 hours, I will be viewing this film again and I can't wait! Natalie (Amidala), a stunning beauty, and Hayden (Anakin), a gorgeous young man, were perfectly cast in their roles; they definitely fit the look needed for episodes IV, V, and VI, and their acting is wonderful. I accept the gaps in the development of their relationship as necessary in order to keep the film under 2.5 hours; besides, anyone that has ever been in love can easily fill in all the details. My favorite part of this film has got to be seeing youthful, strong, properly trained Jedis in action! I was blown away by their skill and the wonderful cinematography. Now, I wait in anticipation of the final installment of the Star Wars Prequel Trilogy...And for that I thank you, George Lucas--for making me feel 9 once again!

title: The darkest episode since Empire Strikes back - a powerful film, as good as the original trilogy.
review:
No spoiler review....

Star Wars:Episode II- Attack of the Clones continues the epic story of Anakin Skywalker, the tale of a young man tempted by power and forbidden desire, a man whose personal conflicts and choices will affect the course ofan entire universe.

In this, the darkest episode of the series since 'The Empire Strikes Back', we see a young man who has abandoned his family, his home, and the chance for love, to follow the spiritual code of the Jedi Knights, the ancient guardians of the old republic.

Attack of the Clones is a powerful, spellbinding thrill-ride, set against a sinister web of intrigue, in a universe increasingly threatened by an unsettling spiritual darkness.

We see far more of Coruscant, the planet that is entirely a sprawling megalopolis, from the great giant skyscrapers to the murky depths of the underworld, we are introduced to two new worlds and many more incredible species from this entirely original universe.

The special effects are, for my money, the greatest seen so far in the history of cinema, but they only serve the plot, which is driven by a serious story and decent acting - Hayden Christiansen as Anakin is believable as a conflicted young man with a serious dark side, Ewan McGregor as Obi-Wan delivers some great sardonic wit and exudes Jedi coolness, and Christopher Lee is a compelling Count Dooku.

The action and the humour are more sophisticated and satisfying than the Phantom Menace, the first episode, and beneath the romance between Padme Amidala (Natalie Portman) and Anakin, is an interesting underlying darkness.

We have come to expect a lot from Star Wars films - they have become the mythology of a generation - and where you judge films such as Spiderman against popcorn crunchers like Godzilla, Planet of the Apes etc, here today gone tomorrow merchandise franchises, the expectations around the Star Wars series are higher than for any movie.

But this does the truly remarkable in that it does not disappoint. There may be a few more slower scenes in the middle than I initially anticipated, but, as with the other Star Wars movies, they will only serve in time to mature and further the understanding of the full, six movie story. There is so much to take in, so much 'meat' in this film, and any negatives are not even worth mentioning due to the wide open mouth awe of the film and the excellent way the plot unfolds.

This is 'up there' with the original three Star Wars films - indeed there are moments that surpass the great Star Wars moments - and this intriguingly sets up Episode Three to be a powerful ending to the saga. But for now Episode Two is here at last and I am going to need another four viewings at least to get everything there is to get out of this movie. How many other films can you say that about?

Attack of the Clones is a worthy addition to a timeless movie series. And what more could you possibly ask for?

title: A great film, and obviously, a must-see for Star Wars fans.
review: Attack of The Clones is a significantly better film than The Phantom Menace, and even the original 3, in many respects.  George Lucas summed it up perfectly in 3 words: "The plot thickens."  Everything you saw in Episode I (Jedi battles, new worlds, amazing creatures, grand armies, etc.) is magnified.  The characters of Yoda, Mace Windu, PadmÃ©, Anakin and Obi-Wan are well-developed, and Jar Jar is only on screen 3 times.  Cinematically it is technically superior and visually more interesting.  There are still minor, noticeable difficulties with interaction between the actors and CGI characters.  More specifically, when an actor is pictured touching or riding a CGI, and there is quite a lot of this.  Suspension of disbelief comes easily.  The CGI creatures in Episode II are the scariest yet, and may be a little much for the younger viewers.  Nevertheless, this may be the best of the five movies, simply due to its overall importance to the story, the well-written script, and the technical achievement.

title: That's more like it.
review:
Here's my quick and spoiler-free take on the new Star Wars movie: It's good. Very good. Far from perfect, and not as good as the first two films, but better than the last 2.

The usual Lucas deficiencies are present: Sometimes awkward dialogue, mediocre to poor acting (Christopher Lee and Frank Oz provide the film's best performances) and the blatant swiping of scenes from other films (THE SEARCHERS again, this time). The romantic sequences between Hayden Christensen (who's awful) and Natalie Portman are the cinematic equivalent of a toothache.

However, this time Lucas drowns out those flaws in a flood of eye-catching, edge-of-your-seat action sequences that dominate the final two-thirds of the film. The tone this time around is darker, more downbeat and less kid-friendly than the last 2 films (a return to the tenor of EMPIRE STRIKES BACK). In a bold choice, Lucas allows Anakin to be portrayed as an arrogant jerk most of the time -- troubled and somewhat sympathetic, but not warm or wholly likeable; clearly, Anakin is on his way to becoming Darth Vader. (If only Lucas had cast an actor in that key role, instead of Christensen.)

Also, Lucas does a masterful job of putting to good use the wealth of characters introduced in the previous film, as well as new ones we meet here. Mace Windu and Yoda are especially prominent. Lucas even uses Jar Jar Binks wisely. He's not in the film much, but he contributes to a pivotal moment. How he's used in this short but key sequence almost redeems his presence in PHANTOM MENACE. There's a lot less comedy in this film than in the last 2, and most of it is actually funny (thanks to our old pal C3PO). And, as you'd expect, the f/x are staggeringly good.

Episode II is also loaded with little tidbids for geek boys like me. We watch situations develop, see for the first time locations, meet characters and glimpse other elements that we recongize will become important later. I don't want to give anything away. Let's just say that if you're a big fan, there's tons of stuff in here for you.

Oh, and one more thing: Yoda kicks ass.

title: Easy on the eyes, hard on the ears.
review:
How can it be that the same director that got subtle, nuanced human interactions in 'american graffiti' cannot now direct a love scene to save his life (or his series)?

And do the amazing (and they *are* amazing-- the final Yoda scene alone will redeem this film for star wars fans) special effects and plot innovations counterbalance the urge you'll have to laugh (or worse) during those times Anakin and Amidala are stuck on-screen together alone?

These are questions which just might be worth a viewing or two to answer, but expect some unintentional snickers among the cheers.

title: Might be the best of the bunch
review:
Frankly, I don't know what some of the early critics are talking about. This is an amazing movie in almost every way. It bridges the two series for the first time in ways 'Menace' never could and is more exciting than any Indiana Jones movie. And then there's the special effects....they are by far the best I've ever seen. Not to say there aren't some dull moments- some scenes simply do not click and so therefore the movie isn't perfect? WHO CARES!!! Was 'Empire' PERFECT? NOOOOOOOOOO (I have always found the Dagobah sequence a little boring). 'Jedi' (Jabba laugh)- certainly not. 'Menace'? Let's not even go there.

So no, 'Clones' is not perfect and I don't know why some critics feel the need to bag on it when it is so wonderful in so many ways. It's their loss, really, because they decided not to enjoy this film which is so rich and delectible it begs to be enjoyed.

In short, the love scenes are not as annoying as some might think. They are actually rather sweet- especially the later ones. Anakin is showing some definite 'Vader-esque' traits here and C3P0 has his best moments yet. It's a wild ride and is just waiting to be enjoyed by every man, woman and child on this planet. AMAZING! 10/10

title: A Dramatic improvement
review: I will have to admit I was skeptical going into my viewing of Episode II, after the disappointment of Episode I. However, I was pleasantly surpirsised by the film. In many respects, Lucas has returned to those elements which made his prior films a success. As you would expect, there are familiar faces, as well as new characters, and an explosive action finale. While no one may be surprised at the superior effects, it is actually the story of the inner struggle of Annakin, a momentous task to handle, that the film captures well. Performances are not as stale in this film, and it is a great improvement. This is a film Lucas can take some pride in. 7/10

title: Better than TPM but still leaves something to be desired.
review:
Well, at least it it heaps better than TPM but not perfect Star Wars...

I do think that one of the problems is that we who saw the original trilogy when we were kids, early-teens or teens tend to forget that we have grown some after that, so it is natural that this new trilogy wont have the same effect now, sad as it is.

Anyways I would say that the worst bit in AotC is Hayden Christensen, as he's acting is horrible at places and average at best, also while I understand that the jedi knights could talk like they do in the movies just because their training and ethos I hardly understand why the rest of the galaxy has to do so also, some of the lines are truly horrible (especially the love scenes between Anakin & Padme.)

On the bright side the movie has more of the spirit of the original ones, it's mood is rather more dark (yipee)and "flows" better than TPM. Ewan McGregor does a good job here (although he seems to try imitate Alec Guinness at places, otherwise fine but he doesn't pull it off) and Christopher Lee is another jewel in the cast of AotC.

While it might not be a earth shattering experience I do recommend that you would see it, it's fun, it's entertaining, and it's always fun to joke with your friends about some of the more stupid lines in the movie, in short good clean summer entertainment.

title: George Lucas: once was lost, but now he's found
review:
Okay, George Lucas was once lost, but now he's found. Remember how cheesy Phantom Menace was? Not this one. This film is darker and better and it doesn't pander to children. Phantom Menace seemed to be a kiddie movie, but this returns as a film that can be enjoyed by all ages.

Of course, the effects were spectacular. They were tastefully done this time too. The CG on Attack of the Clones really didn't bother me. One can say that you know when you're looking at computer graphics, then criticize for it, but remember when watching the first three films you knew when you were looking at a matte painting, a model, or a puppet. So get past that and enjoy the film.

I was very pleased to see that Mace Windu is in this movie a lot, and Jar-Jar isn't. And just wait until you see what a badass Yoda is.

One complaint, if I may, is the love story between Anakin and Amidala was just plain awful. Of course, it had to be there for the story's sake, but I think it could have been done much better. Also, this film seems to drag a bit at first, but hang in there. It does get better!

This movie completely blew away my expectations too. What you expect to happen, doesn't, and that's a good thing. This film was a treat to watch. As good as Empire, better than Jedi, and a whole lot better than Phantom Menace.

title: equally as good as the original trilogy films
review:
not only does it make up for every obscene invective ever uttered against jar-jar, it even gives us an objectively legitimate reason to hate him now.

the cinematography, as always, runs the gamut from serviceable to hyper-kinetic during the action sequence, of which there are many.

but better, the sense of innocence and wonder which i felt was sorely lacking in TPM is back, in spades. the plot is much tighter and it's paced quite well, although admittedly the mid-section could "stand to lose a few pounds" and the lovers' dialogue was, well, if you can't say anything nice...

but that isn't what star wars is about, and neither is this movie.

and this can't be said enough: yoda rocks. and i'm not talking about his climactic scene either: throughout the film, yoda rocks. he's hysterical! lucas appears to have re-discovered his sense of humor and it's there in spades.

there's been much discussion about why boba fett is so popular. this movie gives you a whole host of reasons why the galaxy's most notorious bounty hunter deserves that respect.

there are weak points, to be sure. but they're definitely in the distinct minority. go, see it, and be a kid again.

title: Very much a prequel...
review:
(*SMALL* SPOILERS)

First things first: Yes, the special effects are amazing, and yes, Yoda kicks ass. Fett and Son are a good double act too.

Unfortunately though, the middle prequel in the modern Star Wars trilogy suffers from being just that. Between the lush scenery we are mostly given explanations about what happened to the characters from the Phantom Menace, and introductions of characters and situations that occurred in 1977's A New Hope.

Of course, much speculation has surrounded the circumstances of the fall of the Jedi etcetera, and now no longer are some of these matters speculation. Lucas has taken great care to make credible and thorough explanations of how these events transpired. In fact, so much care has been taken to ensure this that Episode II has, as a standalone film, less substance that one may like.

The relationship between Anakin Skywalker and Obi Wan Kenobi is a very successful one, and Ewan McGregor is very convincing as a younger version of Alec Guinness' character. Less convincing, however, is the love affair between Skywalker and Senator Amidala, played by Natalie Portman, which appears rather flat.

The turning point of the film is when Skywalker's Dark Side destiny shows it's head. Hayden Christensen does gives a good portrayal of a (slightly stroppy) proto-Vader here when he raises his sabre in anger - a chilling part of the film that is maybe underplayed too much.

The battle at the end is as epic as we've come to expect, and the final light-sabre fight is astounding. Yoda will never seem the same again. in the closing moments, we see a glimpse of the Empire-to-be, setting the scene nicely for the final film in the Star Wars franchise.

My feeling is that, as with Episode I, this is probably a film that will improve with repeated viewings. Although lacking in new characters of any depth, it is rather complex in scope and there are certain aspects of the plot that manage to confuse, like exactly how the titular clones actually fit in. One can't help thinking that if Lucas would've taken more risks with his characters and shocked the audience a little more, he could have made both this, and possibly even the awaited Episode III, better films. As it is, just by comparing Episodes II and IV, it's pretty simple to work out what's going to happen next.

title: A classic
review: Special effects, action, plot all amazing, George Lucas has done himself proud. This is was of the best films I have seen. It was really a joy, I had two kids with me, they were in awe. We talked about the film all the way home. Only two years to wait to find out what happens next!

title: Great film, must see!
review: Now this time (if you compare it with Episode1) George Lucas really made a great film. The main thing which was improved in my point of view is the great, interesting story. The love-story element was included such as a funny jumping-around Yoda and some nice fights against the monsters in the arena. Although it is wellmade, many elements and ideas are taken from the first 3 films, thats the only thing where I thought that it could have been made differently.

title: This is the best starwars film ever? Not!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review:
This is the best starwars film ever? Not!!!!!!!!!!!!

What a disappointment when I saw the first 15mins of this film I thought it will be an improvement from the last one (The Phantom Menace) I was wrong. After the flying car chase it got really slow and boring. What makes this film so boring is romance between Anakin & Padme it so slow and dramatic. It takes about 1hour and 45min to get in some action. Also what was a disappointment was Samual L. Jackson he was not even in the movie at all and he was just boring. Also a disappointment was that the fight scene between Count Dooku & Anakin & Obi-Wan it only last about a minute & I thought it would be good when Anakin has two light sabres and fights Count Dooku but it last about 1 seconds. The bit when Yoda fights Dooku it started to get good then it become a laugh & when Yoda got his light sabre out and started to fly about it was so stupid he look like a hamster flying about with a light sabre. The best thing about this film some of the storyline connects with the old trilogy & the battle between the droid army Jedi nights & clone army.

Summary

The first 15min was good then it started to get all crap and it took 1hour 45mins to get some action. How say that the old trilogy will always be the best and people called Episode one a disappointment what till you see this one. I saw just one thing it is a film to rent. One thing I love starwars and this.

title: darn good flick... but something wrong...
review:
Star Wars' newest installment is a darn good flick, it was definitely better than TPM. There's more than enough bashing of TPM to go around, so I won't add to it. Though, one thing did carry over from TPM into AOTC, that it's under the direction of George Lucas.

I loved the original series, I think they were well done. ESB and ROTJ were much better probably b/c Lucas was not in the director's chair. Don't get me wrong, I think he's usually a decent director. For the current prequel series, I think he should have stepped down after TPM like he did after ANH, maybe brush up the dialog a little. I don't think he has the chemistry with the current actors of the prequels to get the job done.

I know that Natalie Portman is an excellent actress, probably my favorite. She does have great acting ability, but for some reason that ability wasn't able to present itself most of the time in this movie, and I think that reason is Lucas. This argument can also be applied to the other actors, though I don't know Hayden Christansen's previous works.

As for the movie itself: I know I'm nit-picking, but I didn't enjoy the constant back-and-forth of the Kemino & Naboo scenes. Must have gone to and fro about 6 times, got really annoying. The fight scenes were excellent, particularly Yoda's and seeing Windu in action is pretty cool too.

I don't know why this only got a PG rating, there's a few scenes (a few decapitations, plus some dismemberment -- neither were bloody, but you see them quite well) that would have warranted a PG13 rating back in the 80's.

I give it 7/10 stars. The story is enjoyable, it has a few lulls, but what story doesn't. It does a great job of setting up the background story for the next 4 episodes. The end of the movie will allow you to leave the theater happy, feeling you got what you paid for... but then again, it's Star Wars, so it doesn't really fall into that type of category :-)

title: It told the story well
review:
I have not yet read the accounts of any other reviewers, and have only heard rumors of their dismaying reports; so mine is a perspective biased only by my love for the Star Wars universe. I went with the expectation of being told a story-- a story which I, as well as any true fan, already well knew-- a story of love, intrigue, anger, and war. I was not disappointed. Already knowing what was going to happen-- what had to happen, to lead into the next story, and eventually, the story which we all know-did not spoil the telling of this story for me, for it was told in a way that captured my attention like few films have. It was a story that I loved-- so how could I possibly be disappointed?

The music was magnificent; the special effects were spectacular; the action was first-class; and the acting and dialogue served the story well. Much welcome and well-administered comic relief was provided by everyone's favorite pair of droids. Hayden Christensen much exceeded my expectations; he gave an excellent performance, for a pair of boots that are hard to fill. Natalie Portman had to grow up fast to fill her role, something that she's always been good at, and she was impressive, as always. Ewan McGregor also aged, to become a more mature Jedi Master, and did so splendidly. Ian McDiarmid continues to chill my bones as the evil mastermind with a silver tongue.

My verdict: It rocked. It ruled. I loved it.

title: Dud installment rescued by great finale
review:
Even when you hear the negative pre-release buzz for a new Star Wars movie, you have to say to yourself "Hey, It's Star Wars, how bad could it be?". Well, for the first three quarters of "Attack of the Clones", George Lucas sets out to show you just how bad it could be. The dialog is weak and the story moves at a snail pace.

Hopefully, it is not too early in the movie season that critics will forget Hayden Christiansen in their year-end lists of "worst actors". This guy barely changes expression during the entire film and seems programmed to spit out the lines. Even normally good actors like Natalie Portman get sucked into his wooden vortex.

If I had to sum up the theme of this movie, I would say "George Lucas likes when people fall". Obi Wan falls about a mile after letting go of a flying droid, Anakin jumps from a flying car and falls even further and the Princess falls from a fast moving spacecraft. Did I mention that this never has any ill effects? Apparently folks are much tougher in a galaxy far-far away. Those aren't the only scenes at which I laughed out loud, check out the scene between Anakin and his mom for some great unintentional humor.

Anyway, I was prepared to come here today and scathe this movie as the year's worst, when along comes the final half hour. Once Anakin returns to Tatooine things pick up a bit thanks to evoking some fond memories of the first Star Wars. After that, it kicks into high gear with a great "Gladiator" scene that has some neat computer generated creatures. The ensuing battle involving the Jedi Knights, bad guys and a bunch of clones is very exciting and visually stunning. Even the obligatory light saber fights have some nice new twists that make them seem fresh.

In summary, the first three quarters of the film gets a D rating. The last one quarter is worthy of an A. Final rating C.

title: Star Wars and classical themes are alive and strong.
review:
The movie was great, one of the ten best movies in a long time. First off let me say that at the time of writing (approx. one hour after seeing the film) my head is still swimming in the turmoil of this movie. This installment of the Star Wars saga is the most involving chapter to date.

AotC suprised and scared me in that i could empathize with Anakin's issues of love, hate, duty, and revenge. This got under my skin because it made me realize that all those undesireable traits reside in us all. Hayden Christensen played his part to the hilt in one scene you saw the sixteen year old child who only understands the now and acts on raw emotion in the next scene we see that same child learn about sacrifice and greater needs than our own. Anakin seems a little stiff at times but i think any actor would have trouble portraying a charecter with that much going on in his head.

Obi-Wan is the true essence of the jedi, he understands that he isn't perfect. This installment of Obi-Wan as a Jedi Knight does a great job of bridging the gap between the reckless padawan and the wise old sage he will become. I say knight because he is still a little rough in his teaching skills, not quite the gentle teacher we see with luke much later. Obi-Wan is a true greek hero. He has faults but attempts to overcome them rather than give in to them.

Amidala gets a much more fleshed out role in AotC. We begin to see where Leia gets her spunk. Natalie Portman is a beautiful actress does quite well as senator and also gets into the action. Like mother like daughter.

One of the best and subtle themes in the movie is when you find out which jedi trained which dark jedi before they turned to the dark side. this gives a more human quality to classic Star Wars charecters, whose wisdom and abilitys were thought to be beyond reproach.

After watching the movie and writing this review I must say that a little catharsis is a good thing. This is a great movie because it is a greek tragedy in its purest form. The heroes all have flaws the villians all have qualities you can empathize with, and in the center you have Anakin who could make Oedipus look like the best decision maker ever.

title: poor dialogue, but that was never lucas' strength. brilliant otherwise.
review: "the clones" gets off to a great start, moves slowly in the middle act, then brings us home with some brilliant sequences.  it has been criticized for its lack of meaningful dialogue, but look back on the other four "star wars" films-- lucas does not seem very interested in it.  the love story angle of the film works only because it has to-- there are many uncomfortable scenes between anakin and padme.  visually, "episode II" is great, and it was fun getting to know old, familiar characters better through action.  lucas wisely leaves out the things that made "phantom" weak-- jar jar plays a very minor role, the word "meticlorene" (sp.?) is not mentioned, and there are no jokes involving bodily functions.  "episode II" is strong, and it sets us up for a great adventure in "episode III."  i rated it an 8.

title: In one word ...Yoda...
review: I'm not not a Star Wars fan to start off. While I like the movies they have never been something that is in my movie collection.
