title: The Young and the Restless..IN SPACE!
review:
When George Lucas announced the title for his second prequel of the six-part epic that is "Star Wars" many fans scoffed. It was far too reminiscent of a cheesy Hollywood serial from the 1950's. If only it was that much fun! With Episode II Lucas reconfirms his inability to tackle important directorial chores that should be taken for granted, primarily casting and dialogue. There is considerable effort placed on the minutiae of every frame and detail yet all this work can't help piece together a cohesive structure or interesting narrative (like the first trilogy did), even with "Clone's" overwhelming visual proficiency.

The Phantom Menace has finally been acknowledged for the dull and flat film that it was. Fortunately it can be reported that this film is in every way more interesting and watchable, even if for less than desirable reasons. The story picks up the story 10 years after Episode I left off. In fact it overloads the audience with plot. The majority of the film is exposition. Unlike the first trilogy where the narrative was linear, accessible and seamless, the plot here feels contrived and overly complex. Lucas, instead of telling an interesting forward-moving story has the task of unraveling a tangled knot of a story. He has to make sure that he covers his bases and justifies everything that happens later in the series. Not all of this is totally uninteresting (the political intrigue and treachery in the picture would make even Tom Clancy proud) but it doesn't appeal to our emotional connection with the characters the way Lucas has before. The story of Luke Skywalker's journey from boy to Jedi appealed to our collective unconscious in a Jungian fashion. Audiences could be absorbed into that story for there own personal psychological relation to it. Lucas has the opportunity to do the same here, appealing to our deep understanding of fallen angel mythology so prevalent in classic western literature, from Paradise Lost to the Godfather. Instead, Lucas ties up plot points and creates a web of complex fictional politics that only increase the "geek"-factor of the series. It is the sort of information that 8th graders might debate about at school lunch tables across America.

At least the political aspect of the film maintains some intellectual interest. The heart of the problem with Episode II is really the stale love story between Padme (Natalie Portman) and Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen.) Dialogue like this has not been seen in a mainstream motion picture since the golden days of Jeanette McDonald and Nelson Eddy. If only these two actors had a Romberg ballad to save them after their interminable scenes. The performances don't help much. Natalie Portman continues to confirm her status as the worst working actress with the best career. (Her turn as Nina in the Seagull on stage completely destroyed any lingering doubts about her talent or lack therof.) Opposite her is Hayden Christensen as Anakin- one of the most unlikable characters in the Star Wars cannon (Jar Jar may take the cake in that debate.) His Anakin (the "chosen one" as we are oft reminded!) is a spoiled obnoxious brat who is setting up his descent into the dark side as little more than misguided product of teen angst and inflated ego. When he and Padme discuss politics he comes of as merely ignorant and unintelligent. In the original Star Wars ("Episode IV" as Mr. Lucas would have us call it) Anakin is described as a "good friend" of Obi-Wan Kenobi yet little evidence of that is seen here; their relationship is that of a temper tantrum prone child and nagging mother. One only longs for the day when the much more enjoyable and entertaining Darth Vader takes the reigns, though it is hard to imagine this interpretation of the character ever evolving the sense of austere grandeur and cool menace that the man in the helmet achieved effortlessly.

Other actors in the film fare better, especially Ewan McGregor as Obi-Wan Kenobi and Christopher Lee (playing the exact same role he has in the Lord of the Rings Series). As for the effects, they are polished and carefully constructed without a doubt. The new fully computerized Yoda allows the little green man to attack Chritopher Lee's villainous Count Dooku with joyous abandon in the films much hyped climatic duel (Clones' best scene by far) Yet seeing the computerized sheen on Yoda's face the entire picture reminds one of just how much more realistic the puppet looked, when it was still powered by Frank Oz hidden just below the camera frame. Outside of the battle, Yoda does little more than say perfunctory things in a profound manner by reversing the grammar in his sentences. "Begun the Clone Wars Have."

Despite the complaints, the films last half-hour is immensely entertaining, among the best in any of the episodes. It is no wonder that this segment is almost entirely dialogue free. Hopefully by Episode III Lucas will either get around to hiring an actual writer or making a film with nothing but action scenes. Just please--no more mushy stuff. Star Wars should not be daytime television.

title: That's Star Wars
review:
I guess I won't find enough words to describe my emotions, but after viewing the movie yesterday I was just as excited as I was 20 years ago.

I saw the old (new) Episodes when I was about 8. Actually it is nearly impossible to compare movies from different centuries, but I see similarities between Episode I and ANH, and Ep II and TESB. If you watch the old Episodes in an objective way, you have to admit that there are a lot of trashy, ridiculous or boring scenes (especially in ANH). But you have the Star Wars feeling because of the whole story, characters, the "diving" into another world or whatsoever. And that's exactly what you get here. With modern technics of course. What would it look like if George still used vaseline on the lenses?

There is more to say, but ... just watch it.

And ... yes! Yoda rocks!

title: The force is Strong with this one
review: I just saw this at a press screening and can happily say that at Last, Star Wars returns to the heady status it reached with Empire strikes back, one of the best sci-fi films ever produced. The film takes a while to get going, after a fabulous chase sequence, it appears to steer down the path of exposition, and becomes heavily focused in politics. However it soon picks up again and the last half hour leaves you with a strong desire to see more. There are other problems, at times the CGI is glaringly noticable, and you can't help feeling that Yoda doesn't quite look right, no where near as good as the puppet. Similarly there are some scenes which are a tad on the long side, and some of the dialogue appears to be lifted straight from the Carry On leftover bin, primarily C3p0. Yes Jar- Jar is Back and annoying as ever, but at least he gives us an official excuse to hate him. Despite the gripes however, this remains a solid piece of entertainment, highly enjoyable, with great acting, and a wonderful script.

title: One of the best Star Wars Films to date...
review: As a loyalist to Star Wars, I have nothing but great remarks for the movie. Nonetheless, I will try to make an objective critic of the movie without giving away details.  First, this movie has more action sequences than any other Star Wars film; incredibly action packed.  The movie puts you on your feet with the opening chase sequence, and then settles you down telling the love story between Anakin and Padme, then you're strapped on a rocket and away you go.  This movie is the link between Episode I and the older Trilogy we respect so well. Not to get into detail, but it starts to show how Anakin will take down the Dark Side and how the human Anakin starts to become the mechanical Vader.  It shows how Bobba Fett will begin to follow in his fathers steps.  How Luke Skwalker ends up with his Uncle Owen Lars and even when plans of the Death Star begin.  All these things come into play. Lucas did a marvelous job with the story, which is what Star Wars has always been about.  In the midst of the story, Lucas throws in some hardcore battle sequences unlike nothing ever seen.  The ending leaves you waiting for the third film.  I am not on the academy award staff, but there were some one liners that did not seem to belong in the film as far as dialogue.  But when you look at it, those are the little things that are in all films.  These professional critics are hell bent on trashing movies because there were clichés in the movie.  What movie doesn't have clichés?  In all, Star Wars has never targeted audiences for Best Actor, Best Actress categories, it has always been about telling the story.  Ask yourself, why did you go see Star Wars?  You went because you want to finish learning about the story or you went because it's going to be an action packed movie with special affects. You did not go because you wanted to see how well some new actor said `I love you'.

title: makes you wanna see episode 3 (very small spoiler)
review: i saw the this movie on may 16 in dubai. firstly i was amazed that dubai (which is a city in the UAE) got the movie soo quickly. usually it takes 3-4 weeks or more for a movie to come out her. i thought the movie was excellent. the graphics and visual effects were very good. the acting could have been better and that is one of the negative points from the film. anakin had too many corny lines. but overall okay acting. the story line was good, however i think if lucas got rid of the love sequence it would have made the film better. i mean star wars is an action and adventure film, adding i love story just makes it look boring, plus the love lines were corny. i felt the end was the best part of the movie. it had yoda fighting with darth doku, that part was probably the best part of the movie. lucas made an excellent decision of making yoda fight. they really showed yoda's speed and accuracy. when the film finishes it really makes you want to see part 3 because it doesnt tell you what happens. it doesnt really give you an ending. you know whats going to happen but how you dont know. i feel that lucas can do a very good job for part 3 and im really looking forward to seeing that movie. sadly its going to come out in 3 years time.

title: Appetizers and after dinner drinks...
review:
This movie... what can I say... it is visually stunning in many places, but, as also happened in Spiderman, it sometimes was TOO visually stunning... I just don't see what this film does to advance anything besides a plot that is bordering on mechanical... it is almost as if a 3rd grader wrote a story, and then was given 200 million to make it into a movie.. there is no depth, there is no intellect, there is nothing that does not move as if it were operating simply to move from plot point to plot point...

The obvious comparisons are to Empire, which advanced the plot, but took you along for the ride... Empire had the most to do of any of the first three, and it did it with grace, wit, and suspense... Simlarly, Clones had the most to do of these three, and it did it, but only through wooden dialogue, wooden performance, and stunning visuals...

This movie is like starting a meal with a light appetizer, and ending with a triple espresso, but skipping the main course entirely...

title: George Lucas' Empire Strikes Back in grand fashion!
review:
SPOILERS I just got back from seeing it and I've got to say that this one rocks! This is a huge improvement from the last Star Wars outing "Phantom Menace",and a far better display of character development and the best action/sci-fi sequences since Lucas' three original Star Wars trilogies.

Yes,ladies and gentlemen...STAR WARS IS BACK IN FULL FORCE!!!

"Episode II:Attack of the Clones" has all of the excellent,at least great and astounding things that I liked in the film,and could had some things that could have been better. Overall,it will be the thrill ride of the summer.

George Lucas takes several risks with this lastest installment,and the one that pays off the biggest is the structuring much of the first two-thirds of the film as a classic mystery. We think we know all of the answers because we have seen only the last three episodes of the six-part space saga. Half of the fun of Episode II is figuring out who's who,what their relationship to each other is,what their motives are,and what part will they play in bringing about the downfall of the Republic and the rise of the Empire. Lucas has come much closer to hitting the precise target with this one,but in all he had made up for his mistakes in the last outing and on this one its a much more mature and very "intense" film that will pleased purists and newbies alike.

As far as the love story between Senator Padme and Anakin it could have been better since Lucas is voyaging into new territory here. And it shows. Hayden Christensen and Natalie Portman are astounding actors and their characters are physically attracted to one another,but overall it was a bit corny. Some of the scenes are fine,but if I were Lucas I could have gotten Lawrence Kazdan instead of Jonathan Hales to redo some of the dialogue.

As for the villains here,Christopher Lee AND Ian McDiarmand were FAR BETTER and more sinister too than that lame Darth Maul from Episode I. But the scene that had audiences cheering for here is no one than man Yoda. For anyone who loved Yoda,this is te movie to see! Here Yoda,walks,Yoda talks,and Yoda KICKS BUTT! He has two of the best scenes in this film--the one where he is gentle(a touching scene where we see him as a teacher of young padawans-Jedis in training),and the other(which will always be my favorite part)fierce as he battle the sinister Count Dooku(Christopher Lee) in a attempt to save Obi-Wan and Anakin from great danger.

Long live Master Yoda....his Green Badness of the force!

At the end of the movie,Padme and Anakin are married on the planet Naboo with C3PO and R2D2 looking on,but also you can tell where the movie will picked up in the next installment(Episode III),but they showed where his hand was cut off dueling with Count Dooku,and this is where the foundation of Darth Vader and the evil turn of Anakin will come in. Also it furthers the rise of the Sith into controlling the galaxy and it will give us a taste of what the Clone wars will be all about.

Overall,this was sci-fi and its finest and I can't wait for Episode III. Some of the characters do get a chance to show their stuff here....For one,Natalie Portman gets to KICK BUTT here and a far better character upgrade than her last go-a-round from the first installment. She shows her tender side,her romantic side, and her fighting side. As for Ewan McGregor's character as Obi-Wan,(who looks and sounds like Alec Guinness)he has never been better. One scene has Obi-Wan dispatched to a distant water planet(which is incredible to see,an amazing effect!!!) to get to the bottom of things,has a showdown with bounty hunter Jongo Fett(Temuera Morrison).

Samuel L. Jackson's character Mace Windu has a much larger role here. The film's climax brings it all of these characters together beautifully in a gigantic,eye-popping battle royale on the remote,Mars-like planet of Geonosis.

Overall,you have lightsabers,giant monsters,fantastic cities and even a alien diner thrown in for good measure. As for John Williams' musical score...you ARE THE MAN! Long live,Master John Williams!!! As for the rest of it,I would probably go back and see it again for good measure since this is the best ever!!! And it really,really,shows!

Indeed the FORCE IS BACK! MAY THE FORCE BE WITH YOU!

title: Lot's of eye candy
review:
Lot's of eye candy but that's it. All candy and no food left me sick to my stomach. A good movie has a well-told story with solid acting. A great movie has this and the candy too. Sorry, 1 out of 3 just doesn't cut it, especially when the candy is the main course.

Special effects- yes Story- no Acting- no Good- no

title: Lucas redeemed!
review: Like many fans, I was sorely disappointed with Episode one.  So much so, that I wasn't too interested in seeing this one.  A friend talked me into it, and it was worth it!  This movie is as far above Episode I as Episode I was below the originals!  Epic battle scenes, that unfortunately will be criticized by the same people who criticized the CG battle in Fellowship of the Ring.  My only complaint, and it isn't really fair, is that all of the vehicles (although they do begin to resemble the vehicles used in Episode IV, as logic should expect)look more advanced than the vehicles that replace them (ie., in Episode IV and beyond).  I know, I know, no one wants to see a movie made in 2002 that uses technology from the 1970's.  But if I'm designing vehicles for a movie supposedly set BEFORE the original, I'd see it as a challenge to make them look interesting, but becoming obsolete, to be replaced by the next generation (which happens to be 25 years older). Fans who felt they wasted their money on Episode I will not feel that way with this one.  The Yoda fight scene alone was worth the money!  Yoda kicks BUTT! Gets around pretty good for a decrepit old...er...man.

title: Some Good Comments about the film with only few criticisms.
review: Seeing the movie at a press preview before it's release, many people were asking me what i thought of it and wether it was worth watching. I said 'Hey, it's Star Wars, it's always worth watching!' And i was right. The second installment of the epic is a great movie to watch. It's fun, has great action sequences and, occasionly, funny. The strong point of the film is the action. It's brilliant and better than it has been before. The final battle at the end of the movie is stunning, pitting 200 Jedi against Count Dooku's droid army. the clone soldiers are brilliant, the design of their uniform is cleverly close to that of the Storm Troopers, showing what is going to happen to them in the end. The special effects are also a brilliant feature in the film. But what did we expect from Industrial Light and Magic? ILM are ahead of everybody else when it comes to computer graphics. For the first time in all of the Star Wars films, Yoda is no longer a puppet but computer generated. At first i was think that this would ruin the movie, but it is superbly done and i have nothing bad to comment on it. What is hugely dissapointing is the script. It lacks that certain thing that is seen in the original trilogy. The lines that Obi Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGreggor) finds himself saying are utterly rubbish some of the time. I found myself laughing at a couple of them at the very most. Then the scripting leads onto the acting, which is done consideringly well. Newcomer Hayden Christensen portrayed Anikin very well, showing his love and anger (both should not be shown by a Jedi) very well. Overall, the new installment of the Star Wars saga is a great movie. Certainly better than Episode 1 in most areas, fans of the Star Wars universe should not be disappointed. Movie Goers who arnt that involved with Star Wars should still enjoy.

title: Excellent as always
review:
Well, what can I comment now, before the movies' official worldwide premiere? I'll stick to what has already been mentioned in the press I guess, since I don't want to spoil this movie for anyone, just like I had Episode I spoiled for me (some jerk told me which people dies at the end of the first episode).

The movie resembles Episode V in a lot of ways. The only way I can mention without spoiling anything is that just like Episode V, it is the typical middle-step of a triology, where nothing REALLY majestic happens, but rather it's just a drive-in to the final part of the triology.

However, since this was also the case in the first triology, which is now an immortal classic, I dare to give this movie 10 points.

title: Better than the first?
review: Well, I check out the movie last night, and I must say about 45 minuets into the film, I thought I would be whole heartily disappointed.. Again! but have no fear, after the pretty long drawn out plot development, that nearly put me to sleep, The movie Picked up big time, the action scenes where amazing and Yoda, well he was just amazing. All in all, if it wasn't for the first 45 minuets of boredom this movie would have been a 10, but it gets 8 from me. Better than the First? Well Jar Jar has very few lines, and the action is much better, so I would have to say yes, but by much? Nope.

title: The Force Is With GL
review: After the disappointing Episode I is the force back.ATOC has not only the missed Star Wars-feeling, also the acting and of course the special effects are great.This film is not only for fans it´s a film for everyone who wants to plunge into a phantastic world.

title: Good but an empty feeling?
review: Well just got back from watching ep2. I did love it, the special effects were the best ive ever seen and for cgi movies this has set the standard. The action was as fantastic as we always expect from Star Wars, fast paced, flowing but unfortunately not too frequent. The love story between Anakin and Padme' was at times a little frustrating but for me just kept itself inside the lines of taste. I think Lucas has done well with a very tricky story and managed to keep the ideology of the trilogy alive. At times i felt the audience were shifted back and forth between scenes a little too much, in ep1 it built up alot before reaching the final climax, yet in ep2 the build up doesnt seem to link together as well. Id rate this just behind Empire as the best Star Wars film to date, for me it just seemed to miss something and be over too quickly. I cant complain though, the die hard fans will love it, the die hard sceptics will hate it and the people in the middle will enjoy it for all that it is, good old fashioned storytelling that packs a hell of a punch. Overall a worth the wait score of 8/10.

title: well..
review: I do not agree with the harsh comments on Hayden Christiensen.He played his role how it should be.After his evil smile and his unstable character (some say unstable acting),I can't think of anyone playing to-be Darth Wader instead of him. I do not know what people who havent liked this movie had been expecting, but this movie is going to be one of the classics,time will show. After watching the old movies hundreds of times of course this one is yet too fresh. This movie has one of the epic battles you can see in star wars movies. I am very pleased with this movie and i can't think of any other way this movie could have been done. You can't expect,of course,and unexpected story with unknown characters,since this is a sequal.A kickass one.

title: It was awesome
review: My wife and I were lucky enough to see it last night at a premiere.  We both loved it.  Lucas sure is making Anikin and Amidala look like their future children (Luke and Lea).  The ending is intense.  Everyone in the theater cheered at the end.  Do go see it if you were not planning on it.  I liked it better than any of the other Star Wars movies.

title: Absolutely Mind Blowing!!
review: This is by far the best Star Wars of them all.  It was very good and the special effects were fantastic.  The part I probably enjoyed the most was the fact that Yoda got to fight with a light saber.  He moves so fast and it is very entertaining.  When he pulled out the lightsaber everyone in the audience starting cheering.  If anything you should see this movie as soon as possible.  It is literally one of my favorite movies of all time.

title: Far superior to Phantom Menace
review: Attack of the Clones is an excellent movie, and is far superior to Phantom Menace (which is still a good movie). It is more fun than Episode 1, has a faster pace, has a more interesting plot, and less Jar-Jar. This is a visually stunning film (it didn't hurt to see it in a digital theater). The action scenes are fantastic, and it was nice to see Mace Windu and Yoda receive more screen time; the audience cheered every time they were onscreen at the end of the movie. Hints of dark things to come kept popping up throughout the film, which added to the fun. The film has its flaws. It is a little slower at the beginning of the movie, and the dialogue IS a bit flat or corny at times, but that is something one hears in all of the Star Wars movies. I will have to watch the film again, but after the initial viewing I feel that this film ranks up there with the original trilogy, and I can't wait to see it again.

title: Better than Episode I
review: One is sure - Attack of the Clones is much better than Episode 1. There's no children in this part, there's no funny creatures either. But, too bad but there is BUT. First 30 minutes of the movies is a bit boring. It reminds me brasilian soap-opera...how does he wants her and how doesn't she give him..... The real movie begins when Obi Wan comes to the cloners planet and when we see the first real fight between Obi Wat and Jango Fett. Too bad that George Lucas once again kills the bad guy, whos one of the best character of the movie (the same was with Darth Maul). Overall Episode II is much better than first one, it's darker and we've got lots of fights, but Lord of the Rings is better anyway :)))

title: WOW!!!!!!!
review: People who want to have fun at the movies will love this.  Don't be fooled by the over analytical bores that hold this movie to higher scrutiny then all others.  The original STAR WARS believe it or not got a lot of mixed reviews.  This movie was fun, actioned packed and decent story. Yoda ROCKS. Go see this for fun and not with a critical eye and you will not be disappointed.

title: As good as Episodes 4, 5, and 6
review:
First, let me start by saying yes, much, much better than Episode I it was. Where Menace was overindulgent in its special effects, cheesy characters (Jar Jar, anyone?), and chunky dialogue, Clones was much more character-driven. In addition, the largely reduced roles of the Digitally Animated characters led to a movie that felt much more like Episodes 4-6.

I won't bother explaining the plot  you'll either already know it or won't want to, but rest assured, it's a doozy. By far the most memorable battle in all of Star Wars occurs at the end of the episode, and the Midnight showing I went to had fans wildly cheering throughout the battle. If you're a fan of Star Wars, this battle is everything you've wanted to see. Yoda also gets by far his largest role in any of the films, and he even kicks a little butt.

Haydn Christianson was quite believable as Anakin, and he definitely portrayed the internal anger well. Natalie Portman was surprisingly flat as Amidala  she's usually the best actor in any movie she's in, but I thought both Christianson and Ewan McGregor, reprising his role as the young Obi-Wan Kenobi, were better. Jar Jar Binks was actually likeable  yes, likeable  in his role as an assistant to the now-Senator Amidala.

The plot explains a lot of the origins of what you see in Episodes 4-6  the death star, the storm troopers, the rise of the Emperor  but it was also slightly confusing. Just which side is the good side, anyway? If I have any complaint with the movie, it's that exactly what makes it so exhilarating is also what makes it so flat. The huge digitalized battles were awesome to watch, but they were much less personal than the smaller battles of 4, 5, and 6. You never saw armies of thousands fighting at once which makes it hard to understand why the battles would be so much smaller later on.

Nevertheless, this movie is definitely up there with the best of the Star Wars series, and will go down as a much, much more satisfying encounter than Episode I.

title: Not as completely awful as Episode I - but close.
review:
Not as completely awful as Episode I, but it makes up for it with dialogue to daydream by. Sets were great. Acting was uneven. Story was boring. Surprises were few and far between. I maintain that NO ONE could save this prequel-trilogy since by definition -- the audience knows what's going to happen, knows who will live or die, etc. It was just a completely stupid decision to make these 3 films. Instead, why not do episodes 7, 8 and 9? Pick up with the sons and daughters of Solo, Skywalker et al... At least then I wouldn't be yawning through death-defying scenes -- knowing that the character HAD to live to be in the future stories.

Want to see a fun film this summer? See Spiderman. Want more fun? See Spiderman again. :)

title: That was awesome
review:
I was absolutely elated after seeing this movie. It was far better than anything I expected. It matches up well with the first two films in the trilogy. I loved every moment of every scene and found no problems. Natalie Portman was the most beautiful thing in it. Hayden and Ewan both gave competent performances. The special effects and battle scenes were truly awesome. It was easily the best film I have seen this year.

I first saw Episode IV when I was six years old and Episode V when I was 9. This films takes me back to that greatness. Anyone who fails to see the brillance of this movie is blind.

Here is how I rank the films in the series:

1. The Empire Strikes Back **** 2. Star Wars **** 3. Attack of the Clones **** 4. Return of the Jedi ***1/2 5. The Phantom Menace ***

title: Lucas is back on form and this time the force is with him!
review: The Clone wars, treated with such high regard in the first trilogy.  Who would have thought that they would begin with such a bang. The Phantom Menace has been slated as the weakest movie in the Star Wars saga, many had fears for Episode II, let me assure you the force is strong in this one. Its a love story, its an action film and its a Star Wars film finally. With new worlds, new societies and exotic characters.  The evil Count Dooku is more than a match for Darth Maul as a true movie villian.  While Jango Fett is amazing as the hired gun. This is a must see.

title: Good Duels, Horrible Dialog
review:
As many people are, I'm a big fan of the original trilogy. Before waiting in line at midnight to see this movie I had read three reviews of AoTC, each pointing out how badly flawed this movie is. So I just went in anticipating to see at least some good saber duels. And those were delivered ... during the last 20-30 minutes of the movie.

But the relative slowness of the movie isn't the major gripe. Its largest flaw is that very few of the actors seemed to actually be in character. The cast is a greatly talented bunch, but they're left unguided, and it comes off on screen. There are few believable emotions shown in this movie. Most dialog is very articulate and without emotion (and therefore not believable). Again, not because of their acting talents, but because of the script and, in my honest opinion, a bad directing job by Lucas. There were many times that I couldn't help but laugh at the horribly written and delivered dialog.

For the most part the story unfolds without direction. There are some interesting twists and references to the original trilogy that I did not expect to see near the end. And really, that's where the best of this movie is: the end. The action is very well done, and the duels will please most.

6.5/10

title: What we've come to expect
review: Ah, the simplicity of the original STAR WARS: A standard McGuffin (the Death Star plans) to set the action in motion, a few heroes trying to rescue a princess, a bad guy in black.  It's hard to believe that the writer-director who so masterfully conceived this space western could muck things up so much, both with complicated politics (who are we really supposed to be rooting for?) and inane dialogue.  The film nearly comes to a standstill whenever Hayden Christensen, as Annakin-cum-Darth Vader, spills his heart to dear Padme' (Natalie Portman).  As I suspected after LIFE AS A HOUSE, Christensen is a sincere and intense actor, but not a very good one.  His face is boyish and flat, without any character, definition, or shadow: he's like a breathing Ken doll.  But despite being a magnet for complaining fans, I won't trash the film.  I went to see it eyes-wide-open, knowing what Lucas's obsessions have become: It is not even a "film" in the technical sense -- the whole thing was shot digitally -- because Lucas has turned into a techno-geek.  His way may be the future of how movies WILL be MADE, but it is not how they SHOULD be FELT.  Just as FINAL FANTASY reminded us why actors usually are needed to make audiences care, CLONES stands as an important and fairly entertaining example of the potential of technology, without doing much damage to the promise that good screenwriting and actor trump all kinds of glitz.  Of course you should see it; but don't be seduced by the dark side. (c)

title: Star Wars is the greatest
review: George is the man; episode II is a stunning movie.  The visuals are breath taking, the action is intense, and the Empire is coming.  What else needs to be said? Okay maybe one more thing.  May the force be with you.

title: Not the best...Not the worst!
review: Well it's here -- the eagerly awaited next instalment of the 'Star Wars' saga. The last one - 'Episode I' - was decidedly average and this one clocks in just above that. Anakin Skywalker (the new kid) is annoying and the love story between him and the Senator Padmé Amidala is lacking in chemistry and believability. The effects are as good as you'd expect from a 'Star Wars' film -- the flying and fighting sequences are great -- but if anything they go overboard with them -- as you can just see the video game footage being churned out straight from the movie! The only other real complaint I had with the film -- is all the bouncing around can be a bit tiresome and confusing. C3PO isn't in it nearly enough but when he is, he steals the show. Yoda's quips and 'Crouching Tiger' moves were enjoyable as was the always delightful Ewan McGregor. At the end of the day, the movie will be HUGE and it is better than the last one. "True" 'Star Wars' fans will no doubt enjoy this and see it again and again. Once was enough for me, I think, though. If you do go see it, stock up on plenty of food as it clocks in at nearly 2 and a half hours! Enjoy! :)

title: Leaden and disappointing given the potential
review: The only thing really worth seeing was the lightsaber fight between Yoda and Dooku.  That was really cool.  Unfortunately it was also really short.  The other lightsaber fights were pretty lame.  They should have gotten a better actor to play Anakin Skywalker.  It might be an ok teen movie, but for any adult the alleged love scenes are not at all convincing.  Obi-Wan Kenobi is strangely a weakling in this film.  He should know by now that Anakin is turning to the dark side.  Samuel L. Jackson is a good fighter but is oblivious to what's going on around him and makes bad decisions.  There is no hero in this movie and Yoda is the only great character.  That none of the Jedi realize that the chancellor that they work with every day is the dark emperor is a little hard to believe at this point.  The acting is generally stilted, which is forgivable but they sure could use a Harrison Ford--someone who clearly enjoys both the humor and adventure of his situation (being an actor in star wars) and makes light of it enough to bring some spirit into his character.  Some parts of the plot don't make much sense.  After dazzling heroics, a promise to never fail again, and a compelling reason to protect Padme, Anakin seems to get bogged down in weak enemies and give up his responsibility to protect her in the conveyor belt scene, for example.  Padme goes on vacation as soon as she gets home, does no work as a senator and doesn't even keep up with news, and spends most of her time emerging from doorways dressed to allure to meet her spurned Jedi protector.  Anakin shows her that he is turning to the dark side and that he has killed indiscriminately out of hatred and vengeance, and yet she does not seem concerned by this and never brings it up with Obi-Wan or Yoda as you would expect her to do.  Samuel L. Jackson has Boba Fett and Count Dooku under the sway of his light saber, but he leaves them to go fight drones. It seems clear that Yoda could have kicked Count Dooku's ass, but he waits too long to strike a blow and Dooku escapes.  And the way the jedi kill seems inconsistent with the struggle between Luke and Darth Vader in the original Star Wars series.  If Luke kills darth vader he becomes him.  When Vader strikes down Obi-Wan, Obi-Wan becomes stronger than ever before.  Why doesn't this struggle between the light and dark have meaning in the actions of the jedi in episode 2?  Indeed, where is the struggle between good and bad?  It seems that good is really just a confused few led by Yoda.

title: Ugh!
review:
Well, I saw the latest of the Star Wars films (at 12:01am local).

When the first film came out in 1977, the actors threatened George Lucas with the torture of having to repeat his own lines.

In this film, the *audience* should do the same. What passes for dialogue here has got to be some of the most stilted language I have ever heard. Guaranteed-- you *will* wince when you hear it.

The characters all appear to be foreground material for the CGI effects that are scattered throughout the film.

Lucas appears to be straining himself in an effort to tie up loose ends and connect as many dots as possible with this movie because he knows he has limited himself to exactly one more film to complete the cycle. Contrary to his original vision in the 70s, that will be no more Star Wars films after the next one.

Will you enjoy this film? Probably. Remember that we're not talking about William Shakespeare here--and try not to grimace during any scene that involves dialog.

You have, however, been warned.

AOTC is an action packed adventure in the true Star Wars style, with lightsaber fights like you've never seen them before. Oh and for those who might have doubted why they call Yoda a jedi MASTER, the movie will show you why.. Only bad thing I have to say about it, is the dialog. As usual it sounds like something off a sitcom, but hey after you've seen Jango Fett and especially Yoda in action, I think you'll forgive George for the dialog..

title: The Greatest Installment Of Star Wars
review: I really want you to believe me, but I know you won't, because what I'm saying is ridiculous, but, hand on heart, that's how I feel right now, Attack of the Clones is not only the greatest single instalment of Star Wars I've had the pleasure of seeing, but the best damn 2 hours I have spent in a movie theatre. It helped of course, that the movie theatre I was in, was London Leicester square, the night of May 15th, the official Public Premiere of the movie, yes that helped, the gang of guys dressed as rebel pilots, and the cardboard jango fett, that helped too, not to mention the appearance by Anthony `C3PO' Daniels and Rick `Da Man' McCallun, sure all these things were contributing factors, least not forget to mention the amazing Digital projection and the sound, all these things are fillers, gloss, a little nibble of bread before the roast dinner, and what a roast dinner my friends, what a roast dinner. From the moment the camera pans up instead of down after the opening crawl appears on screen, this movie feels different, we linger on shots, we flow with the crowds, I get to analyse the buildings as they beautiful cut threw the clouds, I admire them, my heart swells. I was so scared that I knew too much about this movie, id bought the graphic novel, read the script, read the SCRIPT, but nothing, nothing prepared me for the sheer joy and wonder I saw on that beautiful digitally projected movie screen. I loved every single digital frame of this movie, every single one, this movie is destined to be watched by me hundreds, no, thousands of times. Attack Of The Clones excelled in every single aspect I could every judge a movie on, storyStory, I loved it, I loved seeing the clones conception, I loved seeing what becomes of Anakin, how all these things are set in motion, how the Emperor will tempt and convert him, how OBI-WON will live on after death, all the clues are here. The Acting, this has seen the most criticism, and you what, I don't understand what people are talking about, even if, even IF, you thought the acting was bad, the whole love section of the story, its gone even before its started, its quick, its painless, and It didn't bother me at all. Hayden Christenson was so much better than I was expecting, There are two stand out moments for me in this movie, and both of them are the brilliance of John Williams mixed with acting I never thought I would get the pleasure of seeing in a Star Wars movie, the first, the moment Anakin looks down at what the tusken raiders have done to him, and looks up, the music starts, we know the s**t is going to hit the fan, and then BAM! Chaos. The second, Anakin's painfully poignant and haunting confession, over the top of the Imperial March theme, and you know, you know that mask is only another 4 hours away, and the worst part is, you can't wait. I'm not sure I actually have words for how fantastic that end battle is, but the seamless blend of CGI at last with live action is incredible, are those Clone Troopers Real/CGI? Do I care? Hell no, I was having too much fun, I loved the Obi Won/Anakin confrontation here, no one seems to be talking about it, by I was on the edge of my seat, I half expected Anakin to start waving a lightsabre in old Obi Won's direction, but no, Lucas is saving that for later, you big tease. And yes the Yoda fight scene, this prompted the loudest roar in a cinema I've heard, well ever, every fan knew it was coming and now, now it was time, now it was time to see the Master lay the smack down, and prove why he's at the head of that council.  As soon as Yoda force pulled his sabre out of his belt, everyone, and I mean EVERYONE around me was in geek spasms they were having TOO much fun, TOO much, and the moment Yoda picks up his walking stick at the end, after running rings round Dooku, fantastic, brilliant, comedic genius. This movie promised everything and delivered, I can't wait for Episode III, its going to be the longest three years of my life.

title: The force is strong in this one............
review:
It's ten years since the events that took place in 'The Phantom Menace'. Queen Amidala (Natalie Portman) is now Naboo's representative in the galactic senate and the target of a bounty hunter. Obi Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) and Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen) are assigned to protect her and find out who is trying to kill her. Meanwhile former Jedi Count Dooku (Christoper Lee) is banding together various planet systems to try and break away from the senate. Something Chancellor Palpatine (Ian McDairmid) will do anything to avoid, including starting a war.

After the lacklustre 'The Phantom Menace', Attack Of The Clones is a real return to form for the Star Wars franchise. Gone are the attempts to pander to the kids in the audience (for the most part, more on this later) and the comedy characters. Jar-Jar Binks, the bane of so many peoples problems with the previous film is reduced to a mere bit player, but he does bear some major importance to the plot. Indeed, Clones has an altogether darker tone that is more akin to 'The Empire Strikes Back'.

Another complaint levelled at the last film was the amount of time spent standing around and debating politics, 'Not enough action' was the cry. Well, Clones does have some political scenes, but these are in the middle part of the film and are kept brief enough for the audiences attention to stay focused. Cleverly these scenes are cut with those of Obi-Wan on his investigation and they provide a nice balance to the talky nature of the Senate scenes.

The film opens with a bang, an attempted assassination and a high speed chase through the crowded traffic lanes above Coruscant. ILM have done it again. Just when I thought it couldn't get any better after Weta's work in 'The Fellowship Of The Ring' ILM go and pull one out of the bag. Taking a leaf out of Blade Runner's book, ILM has created a living breathing metropolis, Giant towers adorned with Neon signs, seedy bars and brooding industrial zones all make this city jump of the screen.

Perhaps the biggest achievement for ILM in the film is the fact that you don't notice their work. Whilst filming, the vast majority of the sets were blue screens, they were then added later by ILM. It's testament to their hard work that apart from a couple of occasions you can't tell what's a set and what was created in the computer. The final battle scenes are immense, the sheer scope and audacity of the battle is amazing. Lucas has such an amazing vision and he has the team at his disposal to realise this vision.

The world he has created is populated by such a wide and varied selection of creatures and animals that it takes on a life of it's own. From the city planet of Coruscant, to the dusty Tattoinne and Goenosis, to the lush and regal Naboo, to the rain soaked Kimono. All have separate environments and all are created with such attention to detail that they are believable as places that people (or things) live in, leading everyday lives.

The film seems to ditch the ill advised midichlorian nonsense that was dreamed up for Episode I and harks back to the force that we know and love from the original trilogy. Yoda feels pain and suffering when something happens light years away and a scene with Jedi children (or younglings) is just delightful. The climatic lightsaber duel is breathtaking and easily matches the final duel from Menace. There are moments during the final duel where it I got the feeling I get when I watch the original films, it just 'feels' right.

I touched on the comedy aspect of the film earlier. To go with the darker tone of the film Lucas has cut back on Jar-Jar and any other comedy characters. However that's not to say that the film is a laugh free zone. Ewan McGregor flexes his comedy muscles and has some excellent lines. His dry wit is a welcome bit of light relief. C-3P0 and R2-D2 fill the roles that they did on the original films (and didn't in Menace) as the hapless duo get into more tight spots. Some of the stuff from C-3P0 was quite unexpected and was a nice touch (although I heard some cries of derision from round about me).

The film however really is about Anakin and his slow turn to the dark side of the force, before he eventually becomes Darth Vader. It's a part that really needed a good young actor in the role and Christensen delivers. About halfway through the film he has a really powerful scene, the first signs of the dark side in him and he nails it. It's a fine piece of work from a young man who is going to find the world as he knows it turned on it's head in the next few weeks.

If I was to nitpick I would say that the relationship between Anakin and Amidala, whilst necessary in the long run, held the pacing of the film back. Christensen and Portman seem to have some good chemistry (rumours were rife on set that they were an item) and there scenes aren't horrible, but they were getting in the way of the more interesting plot of Obi Wan tracing the bounty hunter. One particular scene on Naboo reminded me of 'The Sound Of Music', not quite sure where George was going with that.

Aside from that small point I loved Clones and it can be mentioned easily in the same breath as the original films, as it's better than 'Return Of The Jedi' and almost as good as 'A New Hope'. Hell, maybe my judgement is clouded by my undying love of all things Star Wars (or maybe the dark side?) so feel free to knock a point of my score if your not a fan. At any rate for sheer spectacle and vision Clones is a must see, highly recommended.

5/5

title: A great return to form!
review: After the disappointment of Episode 1, I was in no rush to see this one. However, I was lucky enough to attend a preview screening, and was blown away. title: Simply Amazing!
