title: Short, but sweet
review: You'll be COMPLETELY amazed with just how great this story is when you see it for yourself.  I went in thinking it would be just okay, but I was quite taken by how the movie blended a love story and an amazing war story.  Of all the Star Wars movies, I can now easily say that this is my favorite of them all.  I wasn't so big on the first one, but this one has DEFINITELY energized my interest in the Star Wars series.  If you want to see one movie that will get your blood pumping and touch you with a great story, see Star Wars episode 2.

title: truth
review:
unbelievable, such cynical people. i don't listen to critics, i've been to film school myself and film students are snobs, critics are just hybrid snobs. I realize it's a generalization, but it's an accurate one. just remember that those who can- do, those who can't- just gripe... Critics are often completely inept of a creative drop of blood in their body, and yet they so freely critique the creative work of others. They're failed screenplay writers in alot of cases, and failed film makers in other cases. Yet, we listen to them? why?- Would we ask a high school drop-out to take the bar exam? Think about it, was anyone honestly blown away by A Beautiful Mind? - The critics' pick for this year's best picture; a decent movie, but unoriginal and stupid. Russell Crow would have done a pretty good job- if his character had turrets, because his nervous impulses weren't indicative of schizophrenia (which was what his character really suffered from). Film is art, which infers creativity and yet one of the most creative films that we will likely see this year is slammed, why? A man with money and influence tries to do something to advance his profession into the 21st century so they're not using ancient methods of filming. His methods would allow for longer lasting and better quality film. Yet, he is condemned for this, why? Film is entertainment 1st and foremost, and George Lucas has made movie-going into an event again with the Star Wars series. Yet, he is trashed for this as well, why? Is it jealousy? Are those who "can't do" jealous of the one who so obviously can? Perhaps that's too simple an answer. Don't make the movie going experience into something it's not, there's no need for such pretension. No one should let critics b.s. them into believing that a grainy film which is long and boring is worth the 10 bucks over Episode 2, which is built for the soul purpose of entertaining. In the end all that critics are doing is giving opinions and opinions are subjective. I am sure many films are better examples than Star Wars of aesthetically perfect movies, but it doesn't matter because movie making is about one thing, the audience. Not the reviews. Critics are not the final word on movies as much as they might like to believe they are, the box office has proven this fact time and again. I've seen Episode 2 and it was a truly amazing experience, the electricity in the room was like a rock concert, the effects were wild and fast, the story was good and I walked out with a smile on my face and a heart beating fast. That's MY opinion. It's fun to go to the movies again, let's keep it that way.

Sincerely, Tired of Cynicism

title: The saga continues beautifully!
review: Ok, I just left the midnight screening of "Attack of the Clones," and all I can say is WOW!  This movie was absolutely gorgeous.  Hayden Christiansen was a brilliant Anakin Skywalker, Ewan McGregor was great as usual and Yoda... well, see the movie yourself and giggle like a giddy school girl at Yoda.  Now, I am one of the few defenders of the Phantom Menace.  I think it was lighter than the other films because Lucas was trying to portray a much more peaceful time in the galaxy.  Yes, Jake "Mannequin Skywalker" Lloyd was not the greatest actor and yes, Jar Jar Binks brought out the dark side in us all.  But one thing I think happened was just what I said would happen. Phantom makes a lot more sense now!  Now we know that Jar Jar was there for a reason: (spoiler alert) To bring down the Republic!  The master plan of Darth Sidious is much more clear now, Anakin's path to the dark side has become more evident, and the birth of the Empire is imminent.  I think I can slip my Episode 1 dvd in now and breathe a sigh of relief, knowing that Lucas, the emperor himself, has everything mapped out and everything is going according to plan.  So I urge everyone to see Attack of the Clones and if you didn't like Phantom, go back and watch it again after seeing this great movie.  Maybe you'll smile, shake your head and say, "Ok, I get it now."  Well done Mr. Lucas.  Well done.

title: Seems to go on and on and on...
review:
The pre-release critics who were baying for Attack of the Clones' blood were justified to a large extent. Or may be it's a prejudice after reading all those reviews (most of them -ve).

You just feel like you're caught inside an XBoX game and can't get out of it for 2.5 hrs (luckily this wasn't as long as LOR)! Duration (considering how little story is being said) of the movie may be its biggest handicap.

I guess the problem with the movie seems to be the predictability of the movie's flow and the graphics overkill. We've just seen some much of this cloning business (a small group fighting a large multitude of beasts/mummies/ghosts/insects/robots/droids.... in the recent past that the only great feature (the visual extravaganza) seems to get boring and monotonous at times.

Even the most enthusiastic fans who were cheering at the start for almost anything that moved on the screen, where walking out of the theatre like they were following a funeral procession when the closing credits were rolling.

Can't complain about the acting, nor about the music, but the movie as a whole was a let down for me. Definitely, Lucas is much more capable than this and we deserve a better value for the 8.95 ticket + long wait in the line and the anxiety to see another Star War episode which lives up to the old spirit and storytelling prowess.

title: Superb! The Force Is Strong In This One
review:
Like Star Wars? Then you'll love this. Other reviewers have commented on how much better this is compared to the Phantom Menace - and it is.

In a word, Attack Of The Clones is stunning. From the moment the music begins and you see the opening crawl, you feel the hairs on the back of your neck rise. As the film progresses you find yourself thinking, yep, Star Wars is back, we've returned to that galaxy far, far away - and you never quite got that with the Phantom Menace.

Of course, the visual effects are everywhere. From the digital landscape of Coruscant (watch out for the Blade Runner homage during the chase scene) through to the completely realistic CGI Yoda, there's no escaping the fact that this is an effects movie.

But certainly not at the expense of the plot, which (as well as Jar Jar Binks) was a failing of Episode I. There's intrigue, mystery and - very pleasantly for a Star Wars movie - some very real character and plot development. You'll see events and characters here - even starships - that come to fruition in the original trilogy. You might even find yourself thinking "Aha! So that's where that comes from... that's why they do what they do..."

Jar Jar only appears for a total of about a minute. And you get to see him make his biggest blunder yet. It's also not hard to guess who's gonna be after Mace Windu in Episode III.

This isn't an X-Files movie where you leave the cinema feeling frustrated and cheated because you've had more questions thrown at you than were answered. You leave the cinema wanting to go back in and relive it again. You leave the cinema thinking "Have I really got to wait another three years for Episode III? When can I get this on DVD???"

I gave this 9/10 so there's gotta be flaws, right? Well, two immediately spring to mind. Much as I love John Williams' music and much as I appreciate that a Star Wars movie (more than others) has it's themes, the score seemed to rely too much on the music from the other films. In particular, it seems the score for the big battle sequence at the end was nearly identical to the big battle score for the Phantom Menace.

The other flaw - a very minor one - is that you do need to know the back story and the events of the other films to really be able to appreciate this. Otherwise you'll be wondering what the hell is going on.

Having said that, I'm going out on a limb here to say this is probably the best Star Wars movie yet. Better than even the Empire Strikes Back. And yes, I'm a fan too, that's my favourite as well. Or at least it was.

I'm very much looking forward to 2005 - if Lucas stays true to his word and his winning formula then Episode III should be well worth the wait.

title: The Young and the Restless..IN SPACE.
review:
When George Lucas announced the title for his second prequel of the six-part epic that is "Star Wars" many fans scoffed. It was far too remineicent of a cheesy Hollywood serial from the 1950's. If only it was that much fun. With Episode II Lucas reconfirms his inability to tackle important directorial chores that should be taken for granted, primarily casting and dialogue. There is considerable effort placed on the minutiae of every frame and detail yet all this work can't help piece together a cohesive structure or interesting narrative like the first trilogy did; even with "Clone's ` overwhelming visual proficiency.

The Phantom Menace has finally been acknowledged for the dull and flat film that it was. Fortunately it can be reported that this film is in every way more interesting and watchable, even if for less than desirable reasons. The story picks up the story 10 years after Episode I left off. In fact it overloads the audience with plot. The majority of the film is exposition. Unlike the first trilogy where the narrative was linear, accessible and seamless, the plot here feels contrived and overly complex. Lucas, instead of truly telling an interesting forward-moving story has the task of unraveling a knot. He has to make sure that he covers his bases and justifies everything that happens later in the series. Not all of this is totally uninteresting (the political intrigue and treachery in the picture would make even Tom Clancy proud) but it doesn't appeal to our emotional connection with the story the way Lucas had before. The story of Luke Skywalker's journey from boy to Jedi appealed to our collective unconscious in a Jungian fashion. Audiences could be absorbed into that story for there own personal psychological relation to it. Lucas has the opportunity to do the same here, appealing to our deep understanding of fallen angel mythology so prevalent in classic western literature from Paradise Lost to the Godfather. Instead, Lucas ties up plot points and creates a web of complex fictional politics that only increase the "geek"-factor of the series. It is the sort of information that 8th graders might debate about at school lunch tables across America.

At least the political aspect of the film maintains some intellectual interest. The heart of the problem with Episode II is really the stale love story between Padme (Natalie Portman) and Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen.) Dialogue like this has not been seen in a mainstream motion picture since the golden days of Jeanette McDonald and Nelson Eddy. If only these two actors had a Romberg ballad to save them after their interminable scenes. The performances don't help much. Natalie Portman continues to confirm her status as the worst working actress with the best career. (Her turn as Nina in the Seagull completely destroyed any lingering doubts about her talent.) Opposite her is Hayden Christensen as Anakin- one of the most unlikable characters in the Star Wars cannon (Jar Jar may take the cake in that debate.) His Anakin (the "chosen one" as we are oft reminded!) is a spoiled obnoxious brat who is setting up his descent into the dark side as little more than misguided product teen angst and inflated ego. When he and Padme discuss politics he comes of as merely ignorant and unintelligent. In the original Star Wars Anakin is described as a "good friend" of Obi-Wan Kenobi yet little evidence of that is seen here; their relationship is that of a temper tantrum prone child and nagging mother. One only longs for the day when the much more enjoyable and entertaining Darth Vader takes over, though it is hard to imagine this interpretation of the character ever achieving the sense of austere grandeur and cool menace that the man in the helmet achieved effortlessly.

Other actors in the film fare better, especially Ewan McGregor as Obi-Wan Kenobi and Christopher Lee (playing the exact same role he has in the Lord of the Rings Series). As for the effects, they are polished and carefully constructed without a doubt. Yoda is now fully computerized and while this is necessary for the much hyped final duel sequence (by far the films best moment) seeing this creation only reinforces how much more realistic the puppets look. Outside of the battle, Yoda does little more than say perfunctory things in a profound manner by reversing the grammar in his sentences. "Begun the Clone Wars Have."

Despite the complaints, the films last half-hour is immensely entertaining among the best in any of the films. It is no wonder that this segment is almost entirely dialogue free. Hopefully by Episode III Lucas will either get around to hiring an actual writer or making a film with nothing but action scenes. Just please--no more mushy stuff. Star Wars should not be daytime television.

title: Good film, but the worst film of them all (spoilers in my summary)
review: The hype was definately there for this movie. I was at a theater here in Henrietta (Regal Henrietta) and all 18 showings sold out. But the film didn't live up to it. It was good, but that's because it was saved by the last hour. Most of the movie was boring and the acting was pitiful. But acting in all of the Star Wars movies has been bad. Hayden Christianson is an unknown, and judging by his acting in this, he will only be known as Darth Vader in his acting career. Natalie Portman wasn't much better as Padme. I guess George Lucas is to blame. If it were up him, I think he would rather have the next one with no actual humans acting. Ewan Mcgregror does a good job as Obi-Wan. Samuel L. Jackson has a much bigger role in this than he did just stroking his chin in The Phantom Menace, but once again, he is doing Lucas lines. I was waiting for him to tell Christopher Lee "Can you dig it", like he was Shaft. Speaking of Christopher Lee, he was very good in the short time he was in the movie. The best character in this movie was Yoda. YODA?!!!! That midget? This film proved why he is bad-ass. A character that should have been use more was the Emporer, I mean Senator Palpatine, I mean Chancellor Palpatine, I mean Darth Sideous. His theme music is cool. Another theme song used in this film is the best theme of the Star Wars movies, The Imperial March, courtesy of Annakin and the Clone Troopers. Boba Fett was cool, even though he is only 8-years old, and Jango Fett is a character not to get too attached to. Jar Jar Binks is only in the movie for a couple of minutes, but he does one of the biggest things in the Star Wars movies. The japanese alien, Nute gunray (the Visceroy) is only in it a little bit. All in all, the movie is an 8 out of 10.

title: The Magic is Back!
review: Getting back to basics with a 21st century flavour never tasted better. Attack of the Clones rises far above The Phantom Menace.  Why?  A great script, good characters, lots of action and that all powerful force in many Star Wars movies: a sense of wonder.  This is truly what Star Wars is all about.

title: Tremendous Film Flowing Full of the Force
review: What can i say, It's a breathtaking movie indeed. The movie was much better than Episode 1 in many ways which you will observe by going and viewing the movie yourself. Over all the love scenes in my opinion were under acted but the Incredible battle scenes and duels make up for it. Over all the movie is well worth the money and I would encourage you to go and see it soon.

title: words can't say enough
review:
words simply cannot justify how great of a Star Wars movie EpII is. For as much as I though that Lucas could not beat Empire Strikes Back, he has.

Yoda is a badass, Anakin is a pain in the ass, Boba Fett is going to kick some ass in the next episode, and Natalie Portman...well, she's rather attractive.

I really cannot say more, for I am still in awe.

title: Well worth the wait...
review:
In this fifth installment of Star Wars, George Lucas delivers a visually stunning thrill-ride through the galaxy. While I believed there were script problems from day one that show in the picture, it is easy to overlook. Action packed from start to finish, Attack of the Clones makes for a most enjoyable movie experience.

There are several stories going on at one time. The main story covers the love between young Jedi Apprentice Anakin Skywalker and the now mature and Senator Amidala. A love forbidden by the Jedi order that could put both of their lives, and the lives of everyone they care about, in jeopardy. Even in the Star Wars universe, true love is not something that comes around often and should never be taken for granted. Hayden Christiansen was perfect for the role of Anakin Skywalker. The chemistry between Christiansen and Natalie Portman sizzles the screen making for a truly believeable romance.

After the assassination attempt on Amidala's life, Anakin is assigned to protect her, Obi-Wan Kenobi is given the task of discovering the hows and whys of this. If Kenobi is not doing battle, he is interacting with interesting characters. Most interesting of all is Count Dooku, played by the charasmatic classic actor, Christopher Lee. George Lucas has developed many more interesting characters than he did in Episode I and introduced ones that appear later in the saga such as Boba Fett and Bail Organa, Princess Leia's adoptive father.

I waited in line for 1 hour and in the theater for 5. It was well worth the wait. After The Phantom Menace, my expectations were low and demands were extremely high. He met all of the requirements for a wonderful Star Wars picture and then some. Many of the action sequenses were better than anything I have ever seen in a Star Wars film. None could have been done without ILM's surpurbly improved digital animation. For all fans of any part of the Star Wars saga, from fairweather to hard core, this film is a must see.

title: Perfect!
review: Like "The Empire Strikes Back" before it, this "Episode 2" jacks the wonder up a notch. This is a film that will simply strengthen the new generations of SW fans further, while reminding original fans like myself what all the magic was/is about. Thank you George Lucas for creating a masterpiece that will snowball into an unprecedented movie event: Episode 3! Movie-goers of Summer 2002 are the luckiest in 20 years!!!

title: Yoda rocks!
review:
I was just six years old when the first "Star Wars" came out. Didn't really understand the whole concept of sequels and such and "Episode IV: A New Hope" totally confused me at the time.

Well, I'm older now and can give a whole litany on prequels, sequels and such.

Last night, I went to see "Attack of the Clones" with a group of people from work and in two words, "it rocked."

The excitement in the air was palpable as the lights went down in the theatre. When the Lucasfilm logo appeared on the screen, applause broke out among the packed house.

In true Lucas fashion, we saw a story with seemingly different plot lines emerge to bring all the characters together in the end for a spectacular battle.

The cinematography was awesome, but then again it WAS shot all digitally. The character development was tremendous and gives a perfect entrance to episode three. (It'll be a long two and a half years)

I personally enjoyed Episode I, even with Jar Jar. Of course, he's back in the movie and unwittingly starts a war.

Overall, I give this movie a solid 8.5.

title: Return To Form
review: Just went to see the film at the Warner Village in Cambridge and I think it's a great film. The action scenes especially. Yoda absolutely rules!! You could feel the crowd get more and more excited as the action scenes came. The love story was alright but dragged on a bit and was not very convincing but I thought Hayden did a good job as Anakin. Amidala (Portman) looks really hot and as the film progresses loses more and more clothes which I was thankful for. I think the film could surpass the Spiderman movie in it's opening weekend. Unfortunately it has been released on a Thursday meaning the first day's earning don't count towards the weekend gross. A lot of critics have slammed the film but I figure they're all wrong. Go see it whether you are a star wars fan or not.

title: Fun-Filled & Action-Packed, But Lacking That Star Wars Magic
review:
Why are the critics bashing this movie? If critics, like Chicago's Roger Ebert for example, can give good reviews to a movie based on its `popcorn value,' why can't they do the same for `Clones.' This was arguably the most entertaining and the most fun of the Star Wars movies. All moviegoers, fans or not, will enjoy this movie. (Yoda alone is worth the price of admission.) But the praise ends here.

Anyone can argue which of the original trilogy is the best. Mine personally is `Jedi' for the simple fact that everything came full circle. One can argue for `Empire' for its plot twist. One can argue for `Hope' for a variety of reasons. Any and all of these reasons are correct. The original trilogy had that `Star Wars Magic.' `Clones' unfortunately does not.

After the travesty that was `Phantom Menace,' I was rather pleased by George Lucas' second offering. This movie contains wall-to-wall action that is unheard of in a Star Wars movie. That would be all, though, that fans will remember of this movie. It's an action movie with a Star Wars theme, instead of a Star Wars movie with action. It just didn't have that `Star Wars Magic.'

I could still, though, watch this movie over and over again. - 7/10

title: The fans get what they want.
review:
We spoke, Lucas listened.

With over two hours of 'back to the basics' Star Wars, Attack of the Clones easily outdoes it's previous counterpart, "Menace."

Nothing like Phantom Menace, this movie is sure to bring a smile to the face of the most casual of movie goers, and satisfy the minds of the most die-hard fans.

I'll keep this short, and without spoilers: Attack of the Clones was worth every minute.

title: Critics of this film are way too jaded...Good vs Evil has never looked this good.
review:
I honestly don't know what people are thinking when they criticise this film. It is an stunning epic in every sense of the word. While most ordinary fans love it, movie critics in magazines and newspapers blast it. Don't listen to them, they wouldn't wouldn't know entertainment if it splashed into their cup of latte.

While it may miss the mark in some places, the misses are small. But when it hits (and it does so often), it hits hard.

I think the problem is a lot of the fans of the originals are adults now and have forgotten that the last films also relied heavily on effects and often poor dialogue.

But it is the wonderful storyline (that spans all episodes and is now even clearer), the amazing FX, and pure soul of it that sucks you in.

It's the way it appeals to everyone who loves the everlasting clash between good evil. And Episode 2 has this in spades and much, much more.

This prequel is what Episode 1 should've been and is equal to episodes IV, V, VI without a doubt.

Why are you reading this? Go see it.

title: An excellent followup to episode 1 and introduction to episode 3!
review:
The second episode brilliantly starts to piece together the beloved episodes 4, 5 and 6. The special effects no longer seem native in this film - everything fits and doesn't seem to distract as it may have in Episode 1. Jar Jar Binks made a respectable reappearance that is sure to give the character more respect than in Episode 1.

Hayden Christensen does a fantastic job in portraying older Anakin Skywalker, and being able to seamlessly relate the similarities to Anakin's boy-hood traits, played by Jake Lloyd in Episode 1.

The movie holds many surprises and is sure to keep you on the edge of your seat. George Lucas has truly finished another masterpiece that should easily gain acceptance and respect to Star Wars fans, despite the order the six episodes have been released, and the technological changes since then.

Without revealing any more, see the movie. It will certainly take the crown for one of the best movies of 2002.

title: 10/10 A great movie for everyone.
review:
This movie is a huge improvement on the Phantom Menace! There is almost NO Jar Jar which should make you want to see it more. The audio and visual effects are awe inspiring. The story comes together and it becomes clear to everyone why. Hayden Christensen who plays Anakin Skywalker surprisingly fills the role well and it is totally plausable that he will become Darth Vader. Natalie Portman is totally beautiful and her character is allowed to do so much more. Ewan McGregor even if he did look like he was from the Bee Gee's displayed a more mature character. There is too many to go further into their performances! The climatic battle rocks but the highlight is the light sabre duel between Master Yoda and Darth Taranus. Where Yoda proves that the dark side is not stronger and that size matters not.

Overall I think it is a great movie. My nephew who is 18 months old watched the entire thing (at the midnight screening) without uttering a word (well except saying stuff about Anakins mummy in one sad scene). My parents who are almost 50 were also there and everyone loved it.

title: Even better than the real thing
review: Attack of the Clones is without a doubt the most enjoyable cinematic experience in a long while.  For the Star Wars fan this is the film you have been waiting for....for the partner of the star wars fan this is a movie you can really sit back and enjoy, unlike Phantom Menace, and we all thank you terribly for sitting through it with us.

title: This time they did it
review: I was sceptical about this one after episodeI, but to my surprise this one really lives up to the original ones, and I even think that this one might be the best one yet (might take a couple more viewings though). It was a much darker movie than episode one, and in many ways resembles Empire in its style. It also has a great sense of adventure like the original ones along with multiple story lines also like Empire. The sound track was the best I've ever heard and the score great with a few new themes along with all the good old ones. I hated EP1, but this one I will definitely go see again and again and again. It does have a few weak point on the acting especially Hayden Christensen is not always too believable, but hey - he's a Skywalker - being a bad actor must run in the family. Oh, and watch out for Yoda - the little green guy can be pretty surprising. If EP1 had been this good, it would have met all the expectations and more. Even my wife, who has always hated the original Star Wars was crazy about this one.

title: Finally a Star Wars Movie
review:
Lucas must have listened to input on Phantom Menace.

Gone are the patronizing, blandly delivered lines, and excessive kiddie humor.

In is a somewhat darker, much more detailed story and universe.

I have it a 9/10, since I couldn't give an 8.5/10. A must see if you have any interest in the Star Wars story, even if you were turned off by "The Phantom Menace".

title: in one word.....WOW!
review: After I got home this morning at about 3am from watching the midnight premiere here in Miami.  My face was still glowing from the pure delight of watching such a great peice of entertainment.  I do not think AOTC will win any acting or screenplay awards, but the special effects were outstanding and the story line was simply brilliant.  The tie-in's from episode I and to the nostalgic trilogy were great.  The movie had very minor flaws and perhaps a few scenes we could have done without and even went overboard with some of the characters (ie. Yoda, C3P0) but watching Yoda doing his thing was a good laugh. I have always been a StarWars fan and I was a bit dissapointed with Epidode I but George Lucas is back to form with Epiode II. From a fan's point of view I give the movie a 10 of 10.  But from the critics perspective an 8 of 10 (there is much room for improvement in the movie).

title: Exciting and dull at the same time
review:
I'll be brief, the movie is a hit and a miss. The actions sequences are some of the best action I've ever seen on film, but the dialogue is frightfully dull. The love scenes in particular could have been so much more, and perhaps the development could have been given to a more experienced writer.

Anakin comes off as being too immature for a Senator, which could have been okay if we were given something to show why Amidala would have respected him. It might have been improved perhaps if generally speaking Anakin showed immense maturity for his age, but you saw glimpses of his emotionalism. Subtle hints would have fared much better than the obviously childish antics of Anakin.

However there's no doubt that Star Wars fans will love the film. There's been so much talk about this and that throughout the previous four films, and finally the fifth film does the walking! Especially nice to see the king of talk: Yoda, finally earning the right to spout all that annoying rhetorical philosophy.

I give it an 8 for enjoyment, an 8 for plot, a 7 for the acting and a 5.5 for the direction and script writing. George has some great ideas - but sometimes I wished that someone else did the directing.

title: The Magic is Back!
review:
Someday in the future I may have as good a time at a movie as I did tonight seeing 'Attack of the Clones' - but I doubt it. While some fans were dissappointed with 'The Phantom Menace' - Lucas has won them back in a big, big way with AOTC.

4 stars - the best Star Wars film yet. Everything you wanted to see happens, massive war scenes, incredible jedi fighting, Mace Windu and Yoda in action! This film has everything it needs and everything you always wanted - all bow to Lucas - the Magic is Back!

We have come to expect fantastic special effects in the series but somehow AOTC makes a huge leap forward with absolute mind blowing action and visuals created by Lucas' special effects team. Incredible! I can't believe it will be even better tomorrow when I get to see it digitally!

Go see this film now!

title: The Best Star Wars Ever
review: I just saw this movie, and it's worth the wait and the long lines.  I'll definitely see it again.  George Lucas really improved on episode I and returned to the traditional Star Wars we have been expecting, Enough action, battles and Light saber fights to satisfy even the most demanding Fan.

title: "Clones" not original, but certainly fun. *MILD SPOILERS*
review:
I should let you know that, as I write this review, my brain is still reeling from the complete sensory overload this movie inflicted on me. It's slow to start but once it gets going, the excitement doesn't end until that final iris-out to the credits.

I should also warn you that if you are not a fan of the Star Wars saga, there's very little in this movie that will change your mind. It's a film for the fans of the saga

***MILD SPOILERS BELOW***

The movie opens with a bang (literally), and for that I was thankful. Then it lags a bit, with the dialogue focused on the politics surrounding the attempts on Padme's life. It's at this point you'll think Lucas will make all the same mistakes he did in Episode I: The Phantom Menace. But once the chase through Coruscant begins, it's all classic Star Wars until the final battle on Geonosis.

I was reminded very much of The Empire Strikes Back in this movie...not just because it is darker, or because it is the middle chapter. It's the pacing and the storytelling that makes it feel more like ESB. In Episode I, the two Jedi meet Jar-Jar on Naboo, who accompanies them on their journey to rescue Amidala, who then (along with her faithful guards and handmaidens) tag along with the Jedi and Jar-Jar to Tatooine, where they meet Anakin, who goes with them to Coruscant, then they all go back to Naboo. Episode I was much too linear, and the characters all seemed to be together at the same time, hoping to accomlpish the same thing. In ESB, Luke was off on Dagobah while Leia, Han, Chewie and the droids were on Bespin. In Episode II, each character has separate missions and motives, and it makes for a much more interesting story.

The acting was much more solid in this film than in its immediate predecessor. Ewan McGregor IS Obi-Wan Kenobi now...the role truly belongs to him. Hayden Christensen is strong as Anakin, his subtle looks providing the depth his character requires that the sometimes-ridiculous dialogue can't. His first dark-side experience is a truly frightening one...you'll realize just how on-the-edge this young man is, and how little it will now take to turn him into an agent of evil. Natalie Portman is merely adequate, but the writing is at fault there...her character isn't given much room to grow on her own. Samuel L. Jackson was excellent as Jedi Master Mace Windu, whose powers are only rivaled by Yoda. And Yoda's performance, strictly CGI now, is without a doubt the strongest in the film. It's frighteningly good stuff...Rob Coleman's animation team deserves a Best Actor Oscar for their work. I know it sounds ridiculous, but it's true. Yoda's performance is brilliant.

As for the action...well, need you ask how good the action is? It's Star Wars, for crying out loud. If you thought there wasn't enough action in Episode I (as I did), then the action in Episode II will suit you better. As I said earlier, the final 40 minutes of the movie are non-stop action, and it is far better than almost anything we've seen in the Star Wars saga, save perhaps for the pod-race in Episode I (two-headed announcers excluded). Yoda's abilities will have your jaw on the floor, and you'll never ask why he is called THE Master.

If you're a fan of Star Wars, you'll love this movie. If you're a fan who was disappointed with The Phantom Menace, your faith in the saga will be restored. If you're not a fan? Well, at least give it a try. You should be able to find something you like here.

title: the best Star Wars yet....
review: I have to say, I went into Attack of the Clones with extremely high expectations.  My expectations were blown away.  I caught the earliest showing I could on opening day, and I left the theatre feeling like a million bucks.  Without saying too much, it was just amazing.  The cliffhanger at the end of the film , makes me feel like I cannot wait the three years for the next installment.  Hayden Christensen was absolutely awesome.  His ability to portray Anakin was absolutely perfect.  Natalie Portman was great, she did a far better job with this then she did with Phantom Menace.  Ewan McGregor was superb, he really played Obi-Wan to Alec Guinness perfection.  Christopher Lee was absolutely amazing.  If you love movies, see this.  The cinematography and special effects are breathtaking. If you love Star Wars, see this.  Any Star Wars fan will leave the theatre more than pleased.

title: George, we miss the passion from the originals.
review:
As a child, I must have seen the original three episodes about 100 times. The movie was presented to me in a way that was easy to understand and the characters were well defined. You knew who the bad guys were...and who were the heroes. The effects were awesome, yet simple compared to today's standards. At the end of "A New Hope", I couldn't wait to see the next movie. At the end of "Empire", I was jumping out of my seat...applauding and cheering.

But now....

My good friend and I saw it 'this morning' at a midnight showing. When it was over...no one clapped, or cheered. We all just walked out. I could sense from the other viewers the disappointment I also felt. The effects were wonderful....but almost TOO much. Where was the heart of the movie like "A New Hope"? My friend quoted it perfectly..."They should call this sequel 'Anakin Creek'".

AOTC is a good movie, but is far from reaching the standards we have come to love from the originals. It is much better than Phantom Menace (easy enough). I feel that Mr. Lucas has chosen to ignore the cries from his fans and decided to simply make a movie for himself. So many of the action sequences are OVERDONE. He might like all that eye-candy, but fans like us want a better story....not a city of floating cars.

We all have learned in English class the term "KISS" or Keep it Simple Stupid. There are too many plots going on that are poorly defined. The love story (or lack of it) is worse than a TV daytime SOAP. Finally, there is just WAY too much animation. My guess...you could easily cut out 30-45 minutes of the stuff and still have a great movie.

Please Mr. Lucas, review original Star Wars episodes. Create that type of energy and plot line for us when you make the next one. We like simple stuff like light sabers, tie-fighters, good guys, bad guys, and Han Solo. Leave the digital effects for Pokemon.

PS - Delete Jar Jar Binks.

title: Amazing!
review: I saw this movie at 12m today (Thursday May 16th- Opening day) and was blown away. This movie is great! George Lucas has done it again. The story was great, building up to Episode 4+ beautifully and the graphics were insane. The best part of all would have to be Yoda and his moves in the light saber battle with Count Dooku. It's about time we get to see all the skills that everyone has been saying Yoda has- they weren't lying. Amazing movie...I'll be seeing it again.

title: Better Than Episode 1
review: Wow, I went to see Episode II opening day, Thursday may 16, at 12:01 AM, the first showing on the east coast. I loved the star wars movies, but I wasnt seeing episode II because it looked particularly good, just on principle for a lucas film. I was in for a great surprise, episode II was freakin' awesome. Between Kung-fu, lightsaber-fu, jedi force powers, spaceship battles, clones + droids, Padme's tits, Samuel L. kickin ass, and Yoda.... i wont spoil that but I gave the movie a 9(not a 10 just because Jar Jar was back AND unmaimed) Hayden Christensen's acting was very unconvincing and his kiss with Nadalie Portman (if you didnt know that they're going to kiss, your dumb)was poor. It might've just been that as actors and their characters are inexpierienced but - shrug - that's not what your seeing the movie for anyway. All in all a great movie expierience, i recommend it to all star wars fans, or movie fans in general, I can't wait to see it again, or until it comes out on video.

title: Great only because it's Star Wars
review:
SPOILER: Yoda does more than save Anakin and Obi-Wan; he saves the entire movie.

If you've seen it then you understand that comment - if not, go see it.

It seems more and more that Mr. Lucas has become part of the Hollywood Machine, as much as he likes to say that grosses and ticket sales don't matter to him. This movie could have been more than it was, but fell short on many levels, mostly due to a lack of true chemistry on the screen.

Sure, we can all watch A New Hope and laugh at the fuzzy special effects, the models zooming on wires in front of a painted black "starfield" and the corny and sometimes badly delivered dialogue ("I was gonna go to Tashi station to pick up some power converters.") However corny it seemed at the time, there was something in all of the original trilogy films that is sorely lacking in the new ones: emotion and chemistry. It seemed that Hamill, Fisher and Ford actually CARED about their performance and their films. They had to; there was no multi-million dollar fan base to back them. The film depended on them, not a computer generated cityscape, as pretty as it may be.

When Luke and Obi-Wan spoke, you felt the father-son connection between them. When Han and Leia kissed, there was true passion between them, not some trite rehashing of recent Freddie Prinze Jr. films. The characters in Attack of the Clones (AOTC) don't really seem to be enjoying themselves but rather just going through the motions. It appears more often then not that Lucas shot each actor reciting their lines alone on a stage and then spliced them together at a later date with ILM wizardry. I realize that it's very tough to make interesting characters when 90% of the audience already knows their ultimate fate, but that doesn't mean the actors should try any less hard just because the audience already "knows" their character is good, evil, stupid, mean, etc. They still need to make us BELIEVE it, and unfortunately in AOTC that falls short more often than not.

The dialogue, while not quite as pompous as in Ep. I, is still much too prolific. I kept waiting for them to get somewhere with it. True, the action sequences leave nothing to be desired, but I should not have found myself wondering when the talking was going to end and the action begin. The "romance" between Anakin and Padme takes trite to a new level. (Please - rolling in a grass field? "Truly, deeply, I love you"?) George, if you're trying to make more $$ than Titanic, you don't do it by imitating it.

Speaking of imitation, and not that this is a completely BAD thing, but did anyone else notice the blatantly obvious parallels to Empire? There were points when I felt like I was watching that movie instead of this one. (The romance, chase through an asteroid field, Anakin's loss at the end of the movie, the last shot!) Still, I guess there is no law against ripping off your own films...

Ok, enough bad. Beyond the emotionless acting was a pretty fair plot, and I must say that the movie did take the story where it needed to go. The action scenes of course stole the show (How long have we all waited to see hundreds of Jedi fighting with lightsabers?) It goes without saying that Samuel L. Jackson is a BAD, BAD MAN. You walk up to him and tell him purple is a fruity color...I dare you. And while I think there was entirely too much CGI through out the film, Yoda's display of what a Jedi MASTER truly is would not have been possible without it. As I said before, he made it worth the price of admission.

I realize this movie, like Empire, is supposed to end on a sour note, and that everything will be resolved in Ep. III (though not for the better, as we all know) but I hope that Mr. Lucas brings the emotion and the chemistry of the first three films back for the last. Yeah, yeah, we know Anakin is evil, but I want him to act EVIL, without assuming that we already know it. I say "great because it's Star Wars" and that goes a long way, but if I wanted to watch puppets on the screen I'd buy episodes of The Muppet Show. It's too late for AOTC, but maybe Ep. III - quite possibly the most emotional and exciting chapter of the saga - will be allowed to show some of that emotion to us loyal fans.

title: BEST STAR WARS YET
review:
The best star wars movie yet. It has something for everyone, A love story for your girlfriends or Wives, action for the guys, a great story line much better than Episode 1. The Graphics were Undescribable.

The ending was perfect, everyone got to see Yoda do what he does best and fight. Don't go see this movie once but go see it twice.

title: THE MOST AWESOME MOVIE I HAVE EVER SEEN!!!!!
review: You guys I just saw this movie at 12:03am on opening day and it kicks ass. It is better than episode I, not that I found anything wrong with that one but apparently some people did, and is right up there with 4, 5, and 6.  I really can't choose a fav but I can tell you that you won't be disappointed by this movie.  Lucas has really out done himself this time.  It leaves you dying to see episode III, which is ages away :(  The fight scene at the end is just incredible.  YOU MUST SEE THIS MOVIE AS LEAST ONCE!!  Believe me I will be seeing it quite a few more times.  Star Wars Rocks!!!!!!!!!

title: Incredible!! (and better than Spiderman)
review: Attack of the Clones is everything Lucas Film promised and more.  The movie has the most tenacious action sequences of any other Star Wars film, and is rewarding to the patient audience who knows that a spectacular ending is near.  AOTC is a teaser for Episode III to come and leaves the audience feeling empty, as did Empire Strikes Back in the original trilogy.  There is a class and sophistication that reemerges is Episode II because of the contribution that Christopher Lee makes to this feature, similar to contribution that Alec Guinness made in Episode IV, V, and VI.  The love aspect of the movie is fair, but troublesome because we know what is to come of Anakin.  Do not miss this movie, even if you have never seen Star Wars before.  This movie will expect a prior knowledge to the Star Wars universe, but seeing this movie will make you want to jump back into your childhood as the story unfolds and the actions sequences emerge.  This movie's contribution to the strength of the Star Wars saga is immeasurable.  Also, I loved Spiderman, but AOTC makes Spidy look elementary.

title: If it wasn't the Star Wars brand, it would be another Battlefield Earth
review:
Stiff, boring movie, and, worst of all, unconvincing special effects. At least they could get that right. CGI just doesn't look as good as real-world models, and CGI creatures just don't look as good as costumes and masks.

Dialogs are terrible. They includes lines such as "Don't let your personal emotions get in the way".

This is a movie for small kids. If you're not one, there's gonna be a lot of eye rolling and not much fun.

title: I really liked the movie
review:
This movie definitely had some interesting plot twists to it. The Senator is an absolute baby doll!

Not to forget Yoda who really is "never under estimate the power of the Jedi"

title: One of the all time greats.
review: Having received an invite to a press screening, I am happy to report that the Star Wars saga is back on track. After the wobbly Phantom Menace, I can say hand on heart that Attack of the Clone is a good film. No, its great. The effects are amazing to say the least. Its has a story, you bond with the characters and its very well made. Towards the end of the film you begin to remember the first time you ever saw a Star Wars film, and it takes you back to then. The actors were, I'm sure, aware that they had to put 110% into the film and they do. Phantom was a big let down but, George, your forgiven. To qoute Austin Powers a couple of years ago, If you see one film this summer, make sure its Star Wars - Attack of the Clones.

title: Go see it! you won't regret it
review: The first hour is a bit boring, and you start to think where is this going to, it is too much of a love story. But the second half makes it up, what a nice action scenes, especially, when all the jedi's come together in the arena. I am gonna see this movie at least 5 time's i think. another fine job.

title: WOW! Yoda kicked ass!!!
review:
Lets face it. The Phantom Menace was very flat and so thin it makes a supermodel look obese! I went to the first midnight showing last night in Canterbury (it finished just 7 hours ago) and all I can say is George Lucas has redeemed himself. Whilst TPM was mainly all talk and little action, ATOC was all action. I mean in the first ten minutes, you see a cool scene of Obi Wan and Anakin chasing an assassin.

It had better wit than the TPM. Less Jar Jar Binks and Anakin got some hormones!

Ewan McGregor showed a more mature personality. Whilst in the TPM, he seemed moody and unlike how Obi Wan should be, he was more like Sir Alec Guiness in ATOC. Could be just the beard but he fitted better into the part.

Samuel L Jackson shined as well. He showed his movements as a Jedi and proved to all critics of TPM that he was not all talk and no action.

One of the funniest scenes was when Palpatine is given all the emergency powers, one line will always remain with me. "I love the Republic"- thats a lie but it was done so good, the audience roared with laughter.

But my absolutely favourite scene was when Yoda came in to face count Dooku (played brilliantly by Christopher Lee). I never knew the little guy had it in him! Those flip flops, those light sabre moves- we saw a very different side of Yoda!! And when he went for his stick afterwards-the roof caved in with too much laughing!

I give it a 10/10! Good work Lucas. Now if you can top that with Episode 3, then you are some genius. Come on, bring it on!!

title: A superb, if flawed, return to form
review:
Midnight, 16th May. A theatre darkens and we all sit back to enjoy a long-awaited sequel, and praying that the disappointment of Ep.1 would be purged. Oh it was.

I cannot spoil in this section, nor would I, but I can tell you that only bits that seem to drag are the love story scenes. Far too many and too silly. C3-PO and R2-D2 are given some comedy at last, but not the wise stuff of the old films. This is rather silly stuff and you WILL groan.

The battles are incredible, the scale huge (see this on a massive screen!), and at last things are HAPPENING, rather than the political posturing of Episode One.

There are some great one-liner in-jokes and little snatches of musical themes at certain points. (The Imperial March, for example, which sent a shiver down my spine). The "old theme" return in certain segments too, which jolts you right back to 1977. There's a lot to see in this that links to Episode IV. Padme's hairdos showings a distinct leaning towards Leia's "big headphones".

I give this 9 out of 10 because it wasn't perfect. But now that Lucas is on a roll, I have HUGE anticipation for the final film, Episode II, where Darth's saga will at last be complete.

Who would have guessed that this 6-film series was a protracted biography of Darth Vader/Anakin Skywalker way back when??

Oh, and finally, Yoda kicks ass. Seriously!

title: SWE2 is far superior to The Phantom Menace.
review: ATTACK OF THE CLONES is a return to the feel of the original trilogy. The characters and the story are far more interesting. The weaknesses are definitely in the dialogue and the acting between the two leads, Christensen and Portman, especially during the love story scenes. But the rest of the film is very entertaining, with striking visuals and memorable scenes. The action sequences, from chases to lightsabre battles (especially with Yoda), is Star Wars at it's best. I would place the film as my third favorite in the series behind EMPIRE STRIKES BACK and STAR WARS.

title: No mistakes this time. Pure pleasure
review:
As a die hard fan of Star Wars, I was one of the, I guess, few who really liked Ep. 1 (yes I even liked Jar Jar (although not as much)). And not just because I am a die hard fan. I liked it because of a lot of things. But the general opinion was that it wasn't really that great. So I was really nervous about Ep. 2 because I knew that if it also weren't really great enough, the public opinion about SW would decrease drastically.

But I must say I have nothing to fear. Apparently Lucas listened to the public opinion, and made the movie based on, not only his own vision, but also the vision of the great mass of fans. He created what I would describe as one the ultimate Sci Fi, if not just movies, of all time. It includes so much that will leave one speechless. Acting, effects, story, and it makes so much of Ep. 1 that may have been confusing, clear as daylight. It has many a great reference to the later movies (ie the earlier ones in our time), and so much saber battle one could easily catch oneself drooling :)

The young Anakin is doing a great job with the task of turning an otherwise good and clever boy slowly towards the dark side. The plot thickens, if you look at the overall triology in this one. It is Ep. 2 which is really a tough position, because it lacks both a proper start, and a proper finish. It is darker and more vile than Ep. 1, just like we saw it with Ep. 5.

But all in all, the movie will leave one really visually numbed for hours. Like the brain hasn't got enough capacity to store all the impressions it gets... Solution: Watch it again and again... and again.... and :)

title: To care or to sleep?
review:
I cannot believe how bad this movie was... First lets get the discussion of the visual effects out of the way. Of course, they were stunning. It's George Lucas, after all. And if visual effects are all you care about you'll enjoy this film.

But the love story, which takes up the majority of the plot, was so stale and dull be aware that you might fall asleep in your cushy theatre seat. All of the actors, especially Natalie Portman and Hayden Christensen, were extremely stiff, which is to be expected, what with the cheesy and archaic dialogue. But, even so, I expected better performances from these two. Natalie has definitely proven that she is capable of turning in a marvelous performance (i.e., Leon) and Hayden was nominated for a Golden Globe for Life As a House. Why then were these two so terrible at convincing us that we should care about their characters' supposed "love" for one another?

I found myself staring at the screen thinking, "NO. These can't possibly be the future parents of Luke and Leia. I'm suppose to believe that two cold fish could have produced such lively and intelligent children?"

Episode II has really confirmed my belief that George Lucas, as talented as he is with visual effects, should not direct. Leave it to someone else, please! And for the third film would it be too much to ask that Natalie be given some sort of intelligent senatorial speech? This way we can all believe that she is someone worthy of Jedi protection. (And perhaps Hayden's dialogue should be kept to a minimum next time.)

Final Comment: You know a film is bad when the best performance comes from Yoda, a little digitally created green guy.

title: Great! Classic! -- No Spoiler
review:
This reminds me alot of Episode 4 and Episode 6. It is thoughtful and deep, well acted. I can almost forgive Lucas for Episode 1.

We left the movie with some questions answered with more questions raised! (Classic Star Wars feeling).

Fight scenes were well choreographed, and special effects were not the best, but the story was excellent.

title: The force is back!
review: I loved this movie.  After being extremely disappointed by The Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones restores any faith I had lost in George Lucas. It's not quite as good as A New Hope or The Empire Strikes Back, but it's leaps and bounds better than Phantom and even Return of the Jedi.  What I enjoyed the most, other than the action, was the way it advanced the plot and connected to the Original Trilogy in more ways than one.  We see several people, things, and weapons that will eventually pop up and play major roles in the original three films.  This film was so much fun.  Did I mention I loved it?

title: Keep your spirit up during the terrible first half, it'll pay off in the fantastic second
review:
The problem Star Wars has always had is with the screenplay, and this is no different. The first half is filled with cringe-filled dialogue and one-liners, and when Jar Jar Binks appeared early on my own thoughts echoed Han Solo's: "I have a bad feeling about this". However, Jar Jar's appearance is brief though it will have you burying your face in your hands until its over.

Though the special effects are impressive they tend to get in the way and are at times distracting. Luckily the chemistry between Anakin and Obi-Wan works very well, though it still doesn't come close to the charming relationship that Obi-Wan and Qui-Gon had in Episode 1. The build up of Anakin's and Padme's relationship is the major thing that slows this movie down, and its hard to care about them at all. While Obi-Wan is investigating the creation of a clone army this subplot intrudes which is frustrating since we already know the outcome. Unfortunately its important to the plot and the future of Luke and Leia so we must grin and bear the melodrama. The action later moves to Corruscant where CLONES really begins to pick up.

From that point onwards the bad dialogue (for the most part) is left behind and the fantastic action begins.

From the introduction to Count Dooku, the suspiciously familiar Gladiator battle, the Jedi Battle, and especially the final battle between Yoda and Dooku, which works fantastically, will leave you impressed.

The problems with this movie are mainly pertaining to the plot and dialogue, however as many Star Wars fans know, it was never the dialogue that made Star Wars - it were the space battles, wonderful locations and the climatic Jedi duals and when these eventually make their appearance it will make you remember why you loved Star Wars in the first place.

title: Oh My God Go Yoda
review: That was the sickest( in a good way)thing i have ever seen i cant tell you but your jaw will drop when this little green devil whips his thing out. the performance was decent and the story was above par but im sick of lucas limiting himself to a pg rating get some blood with the fight scence. im not talking black hawk down here but take it up a knotch.

title: Oh yes! Star Wars is back on track!
review:
This film really heightens the anticipation for Episode III, it also adds a little credibility to Episode I. The Star Wars saga is really coming along and you can make up your own mind as to what Episode III will bring.

The Romance: much slated as part of an action movie, but it builds on the saga (rather than film) plot lines. There are also indications to Anakin's temperament in the love interest scenes.

Anakin: you can see how he will develop, but we'll leave it to Lucas to finish the story.

Yoda: Tops! Yoda really comes alive in this film.

Effects: Excellent, but not as jaw dropping as I had been led to believe.

3PO and R2 are back on form as a comic duo.

Boba Fett, Tattooine, Death Star, Uncle Owen etc. all the stuff from Episodes IV onwards are starting to be in the plot lines more. This is a Star Wars movie in the true sense of the word, rather than an "stand alone" effort that was Episode I.

In summary - very much back on track.

title: Episode II: The Apology
review:
I'm going to take a little different approach here and comment on other people's criticisms...

1. Is AOTC's love story "clunky?" Well, on a scale of "Say Anything" being a 10, and "Pearl Harbor" being a 1, I'd give AOTC's love story about a 6. It's not great, sometimes it's even a little stilted, but unlike PH, at least it doesn't grind the movie to a halt.

2. Does the dialogue seem forced? Sometimes, yes. But not distractingly so. It's not as colorful as some of the earlier Star Wars movies. It serves mainly to advance the plot (and boy, is there a lot of plot). But at least it's not stupid. Stilted I can handle. Stupid I hate.

3. But does it look good? Two words: Eye. Candy. You've never seen anything like it. And ultimately this is its strongest suit. Yes the love story and dialogue are average, but the plot and action are great. And admit it, that's what you want to see, right? 8 out of 10.

title: It's Star Wars, and it does just about everything right...
review:
To keep this review short and sweet, it's Star Wars, and it does just about everything right. While sometimes I feel odd because I really enjoyed The Phantom Menace, I will say wholeheartedly that this movie surpasses Menace in many ways.

There are a few shortcomings in Clones, as the story hits a few bumps in the road on an otherwise steady course of action and solid dialogue. There are a few scenes where the CGI is slap-you-in-the-face obvious, but for the most part it blends wonderfully with the live action and actors.

One thing that will be hard for people to do is compare this movie to the original Trilogy, which is something I think is not fair. These last two movies (and the one to come) have a very different feel, pacing, and obviously a different style of action. This is not your older brothers Star Wars, but it's still a long time ago in a galaxy far, far away.

title: Worth the wait
review:
After the Phantom Menace, many felt that Star Wars could only get better, and waited for Episode II expectantly, but with trepidation.

When the name was released many were disappointed - I thought, well The Empire Strikes Back doesn't really smack of originality in the title department, nor does Return of the Jedi. The difference is that these films have been consigned to the 'legend' section of film history, thus sealing their fate regardless of silly titles. Thus, Attack of the Clones will similarly be consigned.

For this film outdoes The Phantom Menace tenfold. Nay, a hundredfold. I thought The Phantom Menace an accomplished, (if somewhat angled to the children), film which set out a base for what is to come. Many were bored by the politics involved, here we see they were setting up for what is a fantastic film.

Romance, tragedy, humour, a Jedi craves not these things. But you can be sure that Episode II has them. Oh, and action. Shedloads of it. George Lucas seems to have pushed back his spectacles (if he wore them) rolled up his sleeves (checked of course) and got back on track with a wonderfully sweeping epic. Amidala is more alluring, Obi Wan is more assured, Mace Windu gets in on the action, (as do others, but I'm not going to spoil it), and Anakin. Well, Hayden Christensen does a remarkable job after poor Jake Lloyd botched the 10 year old incarnation of our anti-hero. Many levels to the character, he is not obviously drawn to the dark side, yet we see cracks forming. A wonderful portrayal.

Sure, the dialogue is cheesy at times, but then, that's nothing new to the Star Wars saga ("Aren't you a little short for a storm trooper?"), the love story could have been better written, but the musical score (John Williams of course, back on form after Harry Potter) the action scenes, and the larger plot of the film more than make up for it.

C3-PO and R2-D2 reunited, the introduction of Uncle Owen and Aunt Beru, and the reduction of Jar Jar Binks's part will have die hard fans pleased, and the rest of the film will have the rest of us delirious.

It's better than Episode I. It's better than Episode VI. It's arguably better than Episode IV, the one that started it all.

Now it's just a long wait for Episode III: The One Where Everything Makes Sense At Last, but before then, we have umpteen viewings of Episode II to attend.

As for me, I'm off to the cinema again - this film demands to be seen more than once. And it sits well next to the others.

See it, not that you need my encouragement, for this is a brilliant film.

title: A major leap from Episode I
review: My god was I shaking when i exited the theater yesterday. This movie is just so full of everything I ever loved about Star Wars. Episode I was a bit long at times but this one almost ended before it began, or so it felt. I had heard a little about Yoda's light saber fight, and feared it would be too silly, and in every other movie it really would have been, but in this one, nothing seems more right. I can't wait till 2005 to see how they're going to end this spectacular adventure. Imagine if the quality leap will be as wild from Episode II to Episode III as it was from Episode I to Episode II!

title: May the hype be with you
review:
I'm not usually a believer in hype. The only premieres I have ever been to were Batman, Interview with the Vampire, and Gladiator. After Batman didn't quite live up to my expectations, I decided to choose my movies more carefully from then on. NOT THIS TIME!!! I pre-ordered tickets. I stood in line. Finally, I stayed up until 2:30am watching "Attack of the Clones." I can proudly say it was worth it.

I was surprised at the unusually slow pacing of the movie in the beginning. Scenes were held in frame for nearly too long. Almost as if Lucas were painting a picture; albeit a mediocre one. The acting was a little stiff, but overshadowed by the story development and mind-blowing special effects.

It was worth the admission just to watch multiple Jedi in action -- lightsabers blazing, clones firing, ships exploding. A much better accomplishment for ILM and CGI developers everywhere compared to Episode I.

I recommend this film to everyone. The genre needs films like this. It is not anything cutting edge or groundbreaking, but definitely entertaining.

title: the force is back big time
review:
the force is back big time, a slow start may cause tripidation, but after twenty minutes we are off, the first chase with anakin and obi wan after an assassin sets the pace, which never really lets up. i am not going to go into plot details as this would ruin it for anyone who has not seen it. but just to say there are scenes which make you leap out of your seat. a great tag line would be "more light sabres than you could shake a stick at@.

go and see it i shall be going at least another three times.

as for the usual boring critics, who never understood the films ignore them

title: Another Disappointment
review: I'm pretty rare, I think this film was worse than Episode I. The dialogue is dreadful, with odd gaps and no natural flow. The plot is still too reliant on the episodic sequence, it doesn't stand alone. The romance is cringingly awful, Amidala/Padme refuses Anakin's advances then all of a sudden says she loves him. There is no consequence for Anakin's evil deeds. There are plot holes (landing in a vent of steam and walking through it would be deadly). The end battle is spectacular, but you don't really care about any of the characters. The film's over long and some of the set pieces drag. There only good performances come from Yoda, Christopher Lee and the bloke who plays Django Fett. And Jar Jar's still in it. You want some deathsticks? (groan).

title: AWESOME for Star Wars Fans!!
review: Attack of the Clones is a great movie. Yes, it is easy to "attack" some of the sub par acting and shoddy dialog, but people should not expect a Shakespearian drama, that is not what the purpose of these films is. It's supposed to be about entertainment. AOTC is terrific in that it draws up part of the story of a transformation of a good character to evil, while also telling the story of how a republic crumbles. The CG effects are terrific as is the spectacular battle on Geonosis. I hate to say it, but I think I may have liked it more than any of the other Episodes. Just AWESOME! Star Wars lovers, if you haven't already, go see this film!

title: The best movie ever!
review:
For all of you boys and girls who grew up with Star Wars, this is a dream come true. This movie was everything the first trilogy could have been, and everything PM should have been. A golden work of art on the part of Lucas. The camera angles were reminicent of the first trilogy, and there was eye candy everywhere. Cast was great and there were enough subplots to keep an active mind busy. I want to watch this several more times today, but first.....MUST SLEEP. I stood in line for 6 hours for the best seat in the house (which I got) and it was worth every second. Can no one understand the passion behind waiting for something really great? I was so amazed at this movie. I came in with high expectations, very excited, and even so, my ever wish was fulfilled, I couldn't have asked for more. George Lucas has outdone himself again. If you should see one movie this year, this decade, ever, this is it.

SPOILER*****************

I just want to say that Yoda is SERIOUSLY kickin' butt and I LOVED it. C3PO is still making those corny lines, R2D2 is still just as courageous, and WE GET TO SEE YOUNG BOBA FETT!!!!! Enjoy this movie you will.

title: George lucas renews faith in the Force
review: George Lucas has created a quality sequel to a much maligned episode 1. the story line and pace is better as well as characterisation. Episode 2 is full of action and humour and ILM have out-done themselves with the special effects. If your faith in the force was rocked by the Phantom Menace then it will be renewed in Attack of the Clones. Thank you George Lucas.

title: A lot better than Episode I
review: This was much better than Episode I.  Jar Jar lives but with only a bit part.  The jokes are corny but that is OK too.  The romance between Amidala and Skywalker might be a little confusing since they don't seem to fall in love too quickly.  Hayden Christensen plays the tortured young Jedi well. This movie is much darker than Episode I and its tone and even plot bring to mind Empire Strikes Back.  Overall, a good movie and a good addition to the Star Wars legacy.  I was not disappointed.

title: Kick @$$!!!
review: I want to warn you folks that i may spoil some things for you. That said, Star Wars Episode II is one of the greatest Star Wars so far. One may even argue that it's the best since "The Empire Strikes Back". Unlike Episode I the story takes a while to develop but when it gets going it takes off. The characters are very well developed this time around (and more good news, minimal Jar Jar). The main story in the production of it all was new comer Hayden Christensen who did a very good job with the evil building up in Anakin but not so good on the love for his mother and contempt for Obi-Wan (but maybe I'm just jealous because I didn't get picked for the part). Like the originals the comedy comes in the form of droids. The banter between C3PO and R2D2 was one of the things that made the originals so great and it's brought back to life in this showing. And of course Yoda and Mace Windu (Samuel L. Jackson) live up to the hype (infact Jackson delivers the best line of the movie, a line only HE could deliver). So my overall rating is a good 9. If you were weary about this one because of Episode I, like I was, don't be. Go see it. This one was well worth the 3 year wait.

title: All effect, subzero substance
review:
Anybody wondered why Aliens, Blade Runner, Predator were such good movies ? a) a good plot and decent dialogs, and b) great acting. How could Mr. Lucas hire Hayden Christensen for a lead role - he should have remained in Canadian sope operas, who is so wooden he could make up for the Yoda's missing cane. All he does is glimpses from underneath his eyebrows to express some emotions. There is no substitute for acting school, expierience or well, talent for that matter.

The movie itself deserves a "Alternative Cut" for DVD which would not include : the superficial and totally unconvincing "romance plot" between Anakin and Amidala, their entire time away when Anakin is suppose to protect her, their picnic when they exchange their angry views of a 6 year old on current state of intergalactic politics, which are absolutely intelligence insulting to anybody older than 10 years old.

To sum up : Bad casting(Hayden), lousy, trivial, nonsense dialogs, sudden rushes of action interleaved by a dull, boring, soap opera-like filling and CGI-everywhere - apparently a good mix these days for making half a billion dollars.

title: Open your eyes wide and think tight.
review:
You guys seem to be blinded by the grand name, "Star Wars" How this movie could be rated as high up as 7.8? This is just an avg movie deserves only 5.0 points.

Blurry screen due to CG, awful acting, then the "funny" script. I'd say Star Wars EP1 and EP2 are just another avg SF movie. Yeah, EP4,5,6 are a bit childish too, but they are tight storyline-wise. And they've got the legendary status in the movie history.

Wake up, men, don't let the name value blind you.

title: Master George Lucas
review:
Well, So far I've seen this movie 2 times. The first time I hated it! I really don't know why, maybe it's because I went with a friend who has never seen Star Wars, so I was bored. Anyway then i went with my aunt, who is a mega star wars fan, (and so am i) and wow!! I enjoyed it so much!!! This one is way better than Episode I, yeah we don't have Liam Neeson this time, a real shame, it would have been great to see him as an spirit, you know, lie Obi Wan in Return of the Jedi. Anyway this movie has a lot of cool moments and lame moments, a lot of cool special effects and explains a lot of things that you wanted to know since you saw episode IV, V or VI. here are some cool things:

******** SPOILER *************

YODA RULES!!! he gets to fight the bad guy in the end, Anakin and Obi Wan tried to stop Dooku (sp?) but Obi was wounded and Anakin lost is right arm, and then Yoda comes.. WOW!!! who could have ever imagined to see that little guy doing so many cool things?? Kamino is a creepy planet isn't it?? Well the whole "falling in love" part between Anakin and Padmé is really lame and boring, the landscapes are great, but Anakin and Padmé are just boring there! The part when Anakin rescues his mom, that one is great! it gives you an idea of why Anakin became Vader.. A jedi is not supposed to feel hate, Anakin was full of hate and anger, and a Jedi is not supposed to fall in love, Anakin gets married for God's sake! what kind of jedi is he anyway?? *******************************

All performances are great, Obi-Wan is cool, as always! Once again, Ewan McGregor plays his role very well! Padmé is much better in this one than in Episode II, we get to see her in action! Natalie Portman makes her performance really believable. Anakin was really annoying!! which means that Hayden did his job well because young anakin is supposed to be arrogant, and believe me, he is! title: Attack of a clone of 'Empire' & 'Gladiator'
review: Well, as I wrote 3 years ago, there is much hype and there are many expectations for this film, yet it just barely comes through.  I saw a midnight showing last night and almost had problems staying awake at times. Sure, the visual effects were stunning (with almost too much going on in the backgrounds), but this was the most poorly acted of the 5 films.  Hayden Christensen ("Anakin Skywalker"), Sam Jackson ("Mace Windu"), and Christopher Lee ("Darth Tyranus") sound like they are reading lines right off of cue cards.  And there are WAY too many love (or, 'pre-love') scenes between Anakin and Amidala.  I know that's a huge part of the entire story, but I found them sooo boring.  Some of the light-saber fights are good, but many other scenes were unintendedly funny (like Yoda fighting Darth Tyranus).  C-3PO is hilarious - probably the most redeemable character in the film, though Ewan McGregor does a good job as "Obi-Wan"...   After the film we all discussed how this was too similar to "Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back" and "Gladiator" (I kept waiting for Russell Crowe to pop up in that scene).  I will say that Lucas does plant the seeds for Episode III very well, as everything will be connected between the trilogies in 3 years. At least Jar Jar's role was limited in this one...   Overall I'd rank this one 3rd (behind 'Empire' and the original) and give it a 6 or 7/10.  Maybe if I see it a few more times (I'm sure I will), it will improve in my eyes. Still, you HAVE to see it because it is what it is:  part of our film culture...

title: Not as bas as Episode 1
review:
It wasn't as bad as Episode I. And, I'm happy to see that "death sticks" make it to the future.

What to say? What the heck happened to George Lucas? The first thing I said, after the lights came up, was "That's the longest trailer I've ever seen for a movie." The dialogue and directing was laughable. The effects were stunning as usual. How can a person go from creating so much good, to creating so much crap?

One of the nice things about the original series, was the timelessness. Right from episode one, Lucas's social commentary and religion have been on the movie's sleeve.

The movie does rival "Godfather III" for most laughable death scene.

It was better then Episode I.

title: Good, but not mind-blowing
review:
As readers of my Spiderman review will know, I saw this movie, with a bunch of my friends. Half of them were still in the habit of judging a film on its SFX or last half hour alone (shocking I know). The rest of us (probably through years of watching "classics" as recommended by our parents) need a little bit more from our cinematic experiences.

I'll admit the SFX were excellent, but I did notice one UNFORGIVABLE mistake. During one of the highly annoying love scenes (which I will talk about later) Anakin hovers across a piece of fruit towards Padme. The bite appeared easily noticeably early. And after seeing some of the earlier scenes in which i found it hard to differentiate between real and CG. I wonder know if he(Lucas)meant it, as it would make more sense.

The acting. Christopher Lee, well, he could make Cage's character in 'Gone In 60' look like he had depth. Ewan MacGregor, good as could be expected. Samuel L. Jackson, except the cheddar line that was: "This party's over!" was on par. Now, for the two main characters...... Natalie Portman, however hot she looks, cannot use looks to increase her performance.

And now for the man, who, had it not been for the rest of the film, would have sunk the whole saga. Hayden Christensen, with his attempt at (what should have been at least) a subtle transgression to the dark side (of course this could have been Lucas' fault, which i doubt), I have never seen a more obvious change in character when it need not have been so. It kinda went like this: (note the KINDA)

I'm Anakin, I'm happy, I've once more met my soul mate. Oops, I maybe got a little bit angry while talking to said soul mate, but it happens. I'm going to my home planet, to find my mother (wonder why, with all my "powers" I didn't think of this sooner). I've found out from my step-father she went missing, I'm getting a little peeved now. I've found her, I'm really peeved. Wow, it was lucky I found out it was their bad treatment that caused her to die (but, also luckily, she didn't die until after I had seen her) otherwise I wouldn't have been able to completely psycho and kill all the sand people, and their dogs. Now I'm Anakin but I'm OBVIOUSLY not happy since said event.

I'm sorry to you Star Wars fans, I am a very sceptical person. And everyone has the right to an opinion.

But apart from the few niggles, the very few niggles. It was quite good, 3rd best so far, behind 'A New Hope' and the excellent 'Empire Strikes Back'.

Personally, my favourite character in this movie was Jango Fett. Unfortunate that he had to die in such a sudden way.

7/10

review:
Anakin Skywalker Hayden Christensen

I still remember seeing the first Starwars movie at the theater. I had just graduated from High School. I thought it was the most exciting movie ever!

Well, I have seem the latest version, Episode II, Attack of the Clones several times. Not only was it exciting, but it was one of the most emotionally charged, dramatically shocking movies I have ever seen. It left me rivited in my seat.
