title: Enjoyment, or Overcoming Your Disturbance with the Force
review:
**BIG-TIME SPOILERS AHEAD**

For a more certain path to the light side  the side that refreshes  it helps to divorce one's mind from the original trilogy and consider the more recent Star Wars movies on their own merits. While bearing the same name, they differ from the first batch in some respects, and comparing them too much can lead to frustration. Frustration leads to anger . . . anger leads to hate . . . and hate leads to . . . well, overheated message boards and chat rooms across the galaxy, I guess.

So as the lights dimmed I settled in with relaxed expectations, ready to have a good time. And to the extent that I followed my own advice, it served me well  and I had fun.

Like an aging warrior with occasional constipation, the story takes a little while to get going. Apparently the Dark Side (along with an air of heavy self-importance) clouds all things as the Jedi Council convenes. Senators commiserate about matters of Great Concern to the Republic. It's kind of like watching a C-SPAN video signal broadcast from a long, long time ago in a galaxy far, far away. But I kid the Jedi Knights.

Soon enough the teen Jedi-in-training, Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen) is thrown together with an ex-royal in peril, the lovely Padme (Natalie Portman). As has been widely reported, the ensuing romance is not exactly one for the ages. Acting tends toward the stiff, and the dialogue ("I hate the sand") wanders into ludicrous territory at times. While there is the beauty of Natalie Portman to consider, you may find yourself wishing for some emergency dialogue assistance in these patches. The budding couple amuse themselves by riding and rolling  on alien beasts and in fields of waving grain, respectively.

While the kids get reacquainted, a still youngish Ben Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) shoots off to track down Padme's would-be assassin and stumbles upon a greater threat to the Republic. There is a waterworld here curious to behold, with Kevin Costner thankfully nowhere to be found. Along with the heavy rains, a showdown is precipitated between two of the most cool-headed dudes around: one a bearded Jedi, one a bad-ass bounty hunter whose armor looks awfully familiar.

An hour or more has gone by, and you may feel you've had a moderately good time, owing largely to visual pleasures. Your eyes have feasted on some intriguing backdrops, perhaps lingering also on the good looks of an actor/actress. Your ears have welcomed a few familiar names, noting some (occasionally clumsy) references to future events of the original trilogy. So far it may not be a great outing, but a nice diversion.

Suddenly, the movie finds that its hyperdrive is operational after all, and an action extravaganza ensues, gladiator style. Action? Adventure? Yeah, I know, a Jedi craves not these things; but even the most gentle souls may be ready to chuck that philosophy as the movie pulls the light saber out of it's a** and really gets moving.

And yes, Yoda reveals why he's called Master Yoda in a battle sequence which now has its own television ad campaign. The little guy bounces and hops his way along the fine line between terrific and totally ridiculous, and in any case he seemed a real crowd-pleaser at the showing I attended. Having shrewdly concealed his true powers in the great tradition of singularly-named heroes from Jesus to Columbo, Yoda also manages to emerge as the movie's Master Thespian. His acting is rivaled only by that of Christopher Lee (Dooku), who exudes a wonderfully easy-going sense of menace, suggesting `Yes, of course I'm evil . . . surely there's no problem with that?'

To sum up: While you may find yourself missing certain elements of the original trilogy -- the iconic characters, the fun ensemble chemistry, the use of real (non-CGI) sets, the simpler plotting, the cynical-everyman-quality of Han Solo, the - okay, okay, I'll stop it, you're right, it's not healthy -- there are surely pleasures to be had here: (1) visual backdrops, (2) light saber battling, (3) the thespian stylings of Christopher Lee and Yoda. (Add an areola or two if you find one of the leads especially attractive.) Despite its flaws, you may very well emerge from the latest Star Wars episode pretty jazzed, ready to swing a light saber and kick a little dooku yourself.

title: Nostalgia value aside, really quite pointless
review:
Overall, I enjoyed the movie. But then, I have a bad habit of enjoying bad movies, so perhaps I can be excused... What I did not enjoy about this film was the acting - or rather, the lack of it. In an effort to bring depth to their roles, the actors have valiantly over-emoted and over-acted what minimal basis there is to base a character upon. Ani is your stereotypical teenager, chafing at his chains of underdeveloped independence. Padmè is also stereotypical, the strong woman who is eventually overwhelmed into love. The bad guys are all very, very bad, and the good guys are all very, very good. Except of course, Ani, who is a bit of both. I can see what Lucas was trying for in his script, I really can, but in his bid for technology and digital imaging he has lost the very thing that made the original Star Wars episodes so appealing, the very humanity of the characaters. Instead of Ben Kenobi as a man who has become wiser through the years, we are given an advice-spouting mother hen of a Jedi who can barely control his apprentice. (Don't they learn about discipline in Jedi school?) Instead of Luke we have Ani (whine for whine, question for question, they basically balance eachother out). Instead of Leia we have Padmè, who near the end of the film shows some of her daughter's chutzpah, but then just falls back into "I'm a female bossed around by men except when I'm really determined to do something utterly foolish" mode. Yoda has turned from old wise guru to incredibly agile spinning-top type small guy with a short future. Where is the equivalent of Han Solo and his trusty side-kick, Chewbacca? There is no "slightly on the wrong side of right" guy for us to cheer with, jeer with, or just plain watch as he wreaks havoc amongst all his friends. There is no risk-taker. The two droids are among the best acted of the characters in this film, only because through the simplicity of their roles, they can't become more wooden (metal?).

But back to what I liked about the film. I liked the story. No, I really did. I find it fascinating to see the background to the story we all know so well - to watch the parents of our future heroes meet, to see their characters reflect so well what their children will become. I find it interesting to suppose what will happen - what will make Ani finally turn to the dark side? We have seen him tempted by power, we have seen him torn by emotion. But at heart, he's a good guy with no emotional control. What makes him snap? We don't know. (Well, I don't, and refuse to find out until the next installment.) My guess is that something along the lines of an early death after childbirth for Padme, followed by a withdrawal of the right to raise his own children by the Circle of Elder Jedi (due to what we all recognize as a rather heated temper and unpredictable nature) Ani decides not to trust the "good guys", and goes with the only other option open to him. With the blandness of the personalities on the side of good, I can't really blame him. My advice to Lucas would be to get away from the cool digital stuff (sigh - boys and their toys!) and get back to what made the first films such a success...a great story told through interesting acting.

One other note...I believe I read somewhere that this is a kid-friendly film. Not in my opinion, no sirree. Too many boring love scenes, too many violent fights, no characters at all that I would like a child of mine to identify with. (I'm sorry, but I don't see the future Darth Vader as a role model.) The effects are cool, the droids at the end spectacular. But this is something that will not go away, children will still be able to see it in the years to come.

title: A Slightly Flawed Thrill Ride
review:
In nearly all the reviews of "Clones" seen thus far---from reviewers both professional and amateur, and reviews both scathing and exalting---people seem to take great delight in excoriating its predecessor, "The Phantom Menace". The opportunity to verbally eviscerate Jar Jar Binks is reveled in by most. One could very easily forget that the latter film set and held box-office records which were only broken recently. (Am I to believe that NONE of these 'Phantom'-bashers were among the millions of repeat viewers or DVD consumers? Allow me to scoff, please.)

I point this out simply because, having seen "Episode II" twice now, I'm left with a polar opposite view from current favor: "Episode I" had at least as much fun and personality as "II", if not MORE...largely thanks to the oft-reviled Jar Jar. Yes, that's right, Jar Jar helped "Phantom" work rather nicely. What's that? You were annoyed by his voice and mannerisms? Fair enough, but I'll take a goofy digital Gungan any day of the week over the comatose deliveries of Hayden Christensen and Natalie Portman in "II". Granted, these young actors are saddled with both inanely clunky dialogue and George Lucas' seeming inability to coax performances from his actors. This would be a far less unsightly blemish if the Anakin/Padme romance were not the core of the story. Alas, it is, and we're thus subjected to far too many of their after-school-special scenes.

Lucas struck gold in 1980 by relinquishing the pen to Lawrence Kasdan and the lens to Irvin Kirshner for "The Empire Strikes Back". "Clones" and "Phantom" (to a lesser degree) are flawed by the use of a less-talented wordsmith and Lucas' directorial rustiness. The overall storyline of "Clones" is grand and well-conceived, but it mires down in wooden dialogue and uninspired performances. In "Phantom", Portman is the only one seen to be phoning it in. (At least Jake Lloyd and Ahmed Best---the two most-maligned victims of reviewer wrath for that film---are clearly giving their all.)

There's far more to be said about "Clones", both good and bad, and much of it has been said here at IMDB already. Here's hoping that Lucas will alter his approach to "Episode III" by allowing actors to act (even the scenery-chewing of the first "Star Wars" would be more welcome than the blank stares of late), and by enlisting a proven script doctor for the final draft. Surely he's got Carrie Fisher's phone number...

title: 2nd best
review: Saw this at midnight, and I'd rank it behind Empire and before A New Hope, it IS that good.  CPO was funny as hell, Yoda ruled, Anikan was creepy and cocky.  A great fun time.  I liked Menace, but this showed how bad Menace was(I still like it, a movie dont make $900 billion and no one likes it).

title: No...noo.
review:
After seeing this, I wished Lucas would stop using the name "Star Wars" and call these something else.

The Star Wars movies (4-6)were brilliant for so many reasons. Episode 1 and 2, miss the magic and danger entirely.

Since the bad outweighs the good, I'll start with the good. Special effects. This is all about computer generated effects. It has a good number of terrific sequences due to the effects.

Ewan McGregor rocks again. His portrayal of Obi Wan is a total compliment.

Now, the bad. Grab a drink and take off your shoes.

CGI is either a movie's compliment or it's crutch. In this case, it was a wheelchair and a respirator. It kept the movie rolling and breathing. Some scenes felt to me like they were filler to get to the next special effects sequence. Not to mention, a couple of the effects were quite fake looking. And come on, if I really want two hours of computer effects, can I just play a video game and get it over with before going to a movie, where I'm supposed to be told a story? (I'm not bashing CGI entirely. Shrek, Monsters Inc., and Fellowship of the Ring come to mind as recent brilliant CGI.)

The acting was horrid. The cast is filled with talented actors and actresses, but they were directed wrong. Like Sam Jackson. A great actor that is, well, boring in this. And Hayden Christensen is a good actor, as proven in Life as a House. I hope this train wreck of a performance doesn't hurt his career as a serious actor.

The dialogue is another contributing factor to the flaw. In the old days, it seems to me anyway, Star Wars dialogue was short, simple, and sweet. Here, it drags along. Most of the conversations are presented in what felt like a neutral pitch. After a while, I didn't care too much what they were saying. Nothing ever seemed to come from it.

There were also some ridiculous moments where a great special effects/stunt show should've been avoided. A time consuming scene involved characters on a dangerous assembly line. Well, the thing that bugged me was, it was a conveyer belt. Two steps to the left or right, and you're off the belt, avoiding all of the big, curiously evil-looking machines on the line.

The timing was bad. Some things, many things, went on too long. Others, very few others, were too short. SPOILER ALERT, GO TO THE NEXT PARAGRAPH TO AVOID A SPOILER. The scene where "Anny" grieves over his mother and goes crazy was way too short. I really woke up here, then actually became mad when it cut away. This is DARTH VADER we're talking about here. He becomes a guy who kills more of his commanders than any rebel ever dreamed of, and we can't see him go bezerk on faceless characters who barely resemble humans? Man, I wanted to see him frothing at the mouth, raving mad. Instead, I get to hear about it. I quote Homer, D'OH!

-------------------------------

Finally, the super-hyped Yoda fight. I actually guffawed when I saw "computer" Yoda acting like a gunslinger getting ready for a fight. With a little bread, I could've made a big cheese sammitch. Once again, there was a sequence where Yoda flipped about the room in a manner that made me ask, "How're those moves helping him win the fight? Oh wait, Lucas is showing off the CGI..."

(They showed a little clip of this on a TV commercial a little over a week after the movie was out. The stinger was, they used Spider-Man font and said..."If you only see one action hero this year...", then showed Yoda drawing his saber. What's that say about faith in this film when STAR WARS has to be compared to another movie in an ad?)

Okay, it's all off my chest. I gave this movie a four, based almost solely on Ewan McGregor and the special effects. If you have an extra two hours, and don't feel like watching paint dry, watch this.

title: Welcome back Lucas!
review: In Episode 1: The Phantom Menace, we did not see the remnants of the George Lucas that we were used to and hoping for.  The storyline was ok, but not enough good acting and too much CGI.  Also, perhaps, Lucas was just a little rusty doing the whole "movie thing."  But lest we dwell on the past and observe our present and look forward to the future....(especially 2005 when Star Wars Episode 3 comes out!).  In Attack of the Clones, Lucas has generated a movie masterpiece.  He worked with an excellent and perfectly fitting cast that carries you through the movie, from start to finish. This is a VERY complex movie, and I get headaches trying to imagine how Lucas was able to put this together.  The story is curious, compelling, and complex; a perfect combination for modern film.  I was disapointed with Phantom Menace, and was reluctant to see Attack of the Clones (because of the failed first attempt), but after seeing Attack of the Clones (3 times), I cannot wait to see Episode 3.  This film was not just a movie, it is a work of art and true genius.  Great job Lucas! -chaz

title: I loved this Movie!
review:
Lucas can't write romantic dialogue. Anakin Skywalker is a real snotty and whiney teenager. That aside, the rest of the movie is worth double the price of admission. I thought the battle scenes and light saber battles were awesome! Yoda Kicks A--!

Anyway, despite a few squirms during the Padme/Anakin scenes (ok, a lot of squirms and groans) I had a great time and would like to see this movie again. Thanks George Lucas. I can't wait for Episode III.

title: It's getting there...
review:
Episode 4-6 was great! Episode 1 was just about as bad a job as one could do with such an awaited movie. So what about episode 2?

To be honest: It linked up the horrible episode 1 with what we know will happen in episode 3. The first half might be a good movie, but not with the name "Star Wars" associated with it, but perhaps with a title with the word "Love" in it.

However the second half almost makes up for it. The scene with Yoda fighting with his light sabre was worth the ticket on its own, but couldn't save the movie from a mediocre grade.

But, thinking of the end of episode 2 and the beginning of episode 4, I can't imagine that anyone could make anything but a GREAT episode 3!

So, in my disappointment over episode 2 I'm left with a certainty that in three years we will be witness to one of the best movies ever made! It must be!

title: I just dunno!
review: I grew up watching the Star Wars trilogy.  I liked them then, as a kid. Nowadays, I fail to see the attraction of the prequels.  There's hardly any mystery. Lucas (the uncontested  pioneer of the special effects industry) fails to impress with his current batch of effects.  They are good but in a film industry that has given us Matrix, it's hard to get ooohhh and aaahhh ed by some (now) very basic special graphics.  And unfortunately, that's 90% of Attack of the Clones.  Regardless, the under 30 generation will make Episode II a box office success, despite the movie's shortcomings.

title: Ra ra for Yoda!
review:
Well, having managed to miss Ep 1 at the movies, (made up for it a bit by watching it on a widescreen tv with surround) was glad I made it to the picture house for this one, which was better. Although still not a patch on the originals, particularly Empire Strikes Back.

The action sequences were great, (although lifting the speeder chase straight from the fifth element and the clone factory from the matrix was a little beneath Mr Lucas I felt), Ewan McGregor seems to have relaxed into his role this time, Samuel L Jackson was fab as Mace Windu and good old Christopher Lee nearly had me fooled too.

The big letdown was the romance... I couldn't help but compare it to Han & Leia... (i will never forget watching Empire Strikes Back when she calls him a scoundrel, and.... oh you know the rest). My heart strings were not pulled even a bit, and when Annikin goes off and kills the Tuscan Raiders... not the slightest bit of sympathy did I have... a shame, because a better actor would have done it for me. George, you should have gone for a young actor with some real big movie experience, there are a few out there y'know. We wouldn't have minded, honest! Natalie tried, and she was doing alright, but Hayden Christensen just didn't do it for me, I just wanted to smack him around the head.

My bestest favourite bit though, was Yoda... wow! What a star! Although I kind of miss the muppet, I don't think the Creature Workshop could have pulled that fight off with strings and sticks somehow...

All round good fun, but my nostalgia did get in the way a bit I think... perhaps if I was still 10 I wouldn't have minded so much.

title: It is a great movie after all.
review:
I must admit that I am a fan of Star Wars. While I don't consider myself a freak about the series (I managed to wait three weeks before catching "Attack of the Clones.") I do consider Star Wars and The Empire Strikes Back as the greatest movies ever made.

I read most of the reviews and was going into the movie expecting a lame love story (and it was) and a great action scene at the end (and it was). I was not prepared for the rest of it and I'm really not sure how I would rate this movie outside of the Star Wars universe. I guess as a movie in it's own right, if you knew nothing about Star Wars it wouldn't hold up very well, but it's not meant to be seen that way. It is meant to be seen as the fifth installment of a series of movies with a grand scope. In that case the movie worked.

It never bored me, I was hanging on every word. There was plenty of action throughout and lots of good references to what was going to happen in later (earlier?) movies. I found myself moved several times, but the emotions were when I was considering the sweep of all the movies.

I left very satisfied. While the movie didn't leave me as excited as Star Wars did or as transfixed as Empire did, I was very happy with it as it just seemed to fit the arc of the whole series perfectly.

I think my review comes accross a little more lukewarm than I intend it. I really do think the movie deserves a 10 out of 10 as I'm sure I'll want to see it several more times in my life.

title: Its the 3rd Best Star Wars Film!
review: Ten years after the 'Phantom Menace' threatened the planet Naboo, Padmé Amidala is now a Senator representing her homeworld. A faction of political separatists, led by Count Dooku, attempts to assassinate her. There aren't enough Jedi to defend the Republic against the threat, so Chancellor Palpatine enlists the aid of Jango Fett, who promises that his army of clones will handle the situation. Meanwhile, Obi-Wan Kenobi continues to train the young Jedi Anakin Skywalker, who fears that the Jedi code will forbid his growing romance with Amidala... Amazing Vissual Effects an Breath-Taking Moments will leave you on the edge of your seat. I think this is one of the Best 100 Movies I've seen. Ranking at Number #17 its good enoff. Maybe Star Wars: Episode II did relate to other movies on my list like GLADIATOR the #1 Best Movie for 2 years. Episode II ends in a way like that with Ewan McGregor looking like a Gladiator with the moves. GOOD MOVIE Folks.

title: A good film, it is. See it, you should.
review:
There was a very excited full house in Dublin at for the first showing in Ireland. There were a few hard-core fans with light-sabres and other merchandise. I have never witnessed a better atmosphere in a cinema during the 25 years I have been a regular attender.

This is a very good film for both Star Wars fans and newcomers alike. It started with plot development and exposition and built up gradually to a frenetic and exciting climax. The plot is rock solid and fans can easily see things heading towards the start of Episode IV. The motif of the film is quite dark and therefore could be compared to the other "middle film" Empire. There was a some quiet grumblings from the crowd as Jar Jar appeared but thankfully he hardly figured in the movie. "Meesa people going to be written out?".

This must be the most humorous episode film so far. There are many moments worthy of a giggle and these are often quite subtle which is unusual for Star Wars. Watch out for the "bar" scene on Coruscant.

With regard to the actors performances I thought Ewan McGregor moved up a gear for this film and did a great job. Likewise Samuel L Jackson and Christopher Lee. Natalie Portman and Hayden Christensen had to work with some corny dialogue at times but they had good chemistry on screen.

All in all I'm already planning a second viewing of this most satisfying installment. I'm already looking forward to Episode III.

title: Fool me twice, shame on me
review:
I should have known better than to fork out money at the box office to see Attack of the Clones, but I had to. It had the words Star Wars on the poster, and I just had to. It's like the way I had to buy those crappy plastic toys in 1978 - they weren't just crappy plastic toys, they were STAR WARS toys, I tell ya!

Okay, I thought that Episode I was appalling, but this one can't be nearly as bad, right?

They've got rid of the annoying wee brat and replaced him with an annoying adult that behaves like an annoying wee brat.

Almost every line of dialogue is raw untreated exposition, without the slightest hint of sincerity or character. And where the characters aren't blandly explaining the plot to the audience, they're spouting cliches so rank as to be often hilarious. Not one character is believable - let alone likable - and the whole affair reminds me of Evan Dorkin's Fisher Price Theatre (only without the intelligence or wit).

The action sequences are annoying too. They're so obviously designed to be copied as computer games, I often felt like I was watching a computer game. But the thing about games is they're no fun when someone else is pushing the buttons.

Special effects were good and bad. The ships and cityscapes were marvellous. The CG creatures stank. Still, Lucas (or, more accurately, his cinematographers and effects departments) succeeded in giving us a rich canvas to look at. But in the absence of characterisation or any real drama, that rich canvas soon starts to resemble dull wallpaper - especially when you've been staring at it for almost two and a half hours.

But I really can't blame anyone but myself for this disappointment. Episode One had already convinced me that George Lucas has lost his touch as a film maker - and as a writer, he shouldn't even be allowed to write an envelope.

I was the one stupid enough to spend money at the box office, and I'm the one contributing to the colossal takings that will ultimately persuade Mr Lucas that he can go ahead and make another movie just like the last.

Shame on me!

title: This could be the Best Movie in the History of.......
review:
What......? Episode 2 should be have called attack of the 50' Tall Lucas Ego. Honestly, George Lucas should never be allowed to Write or Direct ever again, period (Yes,and I am one of those people who loved THX-1138)! Attack of the Clones marks the end of Cinema as we know it. This movie has done nothing to elevate the art form on any level. From it's less than uni-dimensional characters, (by the way the cast is made up of some amazing acting talent none of which is realized in this movie) to the overall story. It's even living under the guise of entertainment... Ha !

Obviously, we as the movie going public felt compelled to see this movie after Episode 1. Chalk that up to the Dark Side. Some strange and malevolent force which emanates from down low at the SkyWalker Ranch facility in California.

So I call all to arms, to rise up against this evil and return Cinema to it's rightful place. Back to 1977 standards when all was once good and the future never seemed brighter for the Movies.

title: I guess George Lucas dosent need a good script anymore
review: Attack of the clones is 2 hours of special effects which are fantastic and nothing more, the story is nothing more than fill to lead to the next effect, the acting is wooden the dialog is terrible. The first two movies from Lucas in this current trio makes us realize how all around great movies star wars, the empire strikes back and revenge of the jedi were. I guess George knows he can make money with just special effects and this is what we are gonna get. 7 out of 10

title: Good Flick, Excellent and Dark
review:
The worst parts of this movie involve two characters talking to each other. (Any two - it's all bad. But the Anakin-Amidala sequences are the worst.) That said, this is a great movie for visual effects. The mood is dark; the urban scenes are reminiscent of Blade Runner. And, of course, there is a lot of neat supermanesque sequences involving Jedi Knights. (That's why everyone likes Star Wars, isn't it? Because the movies have good superheroes.)

One minor complaint, and I hope that it's not too much of a spoiler: I almost laughed out loud during the Yoda duel. I've always thought that it would be hilarious to see the muppet use a light saber, and the reality turned out to be even more ludicrous than I imagined. I doubt laughter is the mood Lucas intended though....

title: Yoda rules! =)
review: It was a really good movie. It is worth the money to go and see it! i want to see Episode 3 now! :) I think about to go and see it again.

title: Just go and watch it already!
review:
Well, George seems to have gotten it right this time. Star Wars 2 is a blast. My Rating:

8/10

The good:

Yoda Fights! (If thats not enough to entice you, read on) Natalie Portman Scantily clad Natalie Portman Massive battles Awesome skirmish in an asteroid field Light shed on certain characters (namely: Bobba Fett and Anakin Skywalker) Lightsaber fights galore Jaw-dropping special effects Great acting

The bad:

Cheezy Love scenes (knock off 1 point) Some scenes with cheezy acting, although the acting is great overall Jar Jar is in it

The ugly:

Some scenes they went for the el-cheapo special effects instead of the good ones

Even with the bad and ugly, the movie is worth seeing twice. If you see it for the Star Wars, you'll be delighted by the battles and pleasently suprised by the story and the deep characters. If you see it for Natalie Portman or Yoda only, it's worth seeing.

Oh, and bring the kids. It's a kid friendly movie, but it doesn't stop it from being a great epic.

title: If George Lucas had the technology....
review:
If George Lucas had the technology, I'm sure he would be using digital avatars instead of actors.

Episode II is full of fantastic digitized imagery, but is devoid of any real feeling. It's like a non-participant video game where the game plays itself and you just sit there watching the action unfold. A prime example of this is the part where several of the principal characters end up in a battle droid manufacturing facility. There is dangerous machinery pounding and slicing away all around them and they have to time their actions to avoid and then proceed through said machinery. I wouldn't be surprised at all if this scene was recreated in an upcoming video game release from Lucas Arts.

Maybe it's because I'm all grown up now but, like The Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones for me retains none of the "classic" Star Wars appeal that the original three films had(fuzzy ewoks not withstanding). I wanted to like this film. I really did. But as it wore on and I found myself constantly checking my watch I realized that, at least for me, the magic is gone. The characters have no real chemistry and the story exists simply to bridge the gap between the early episodes and these new ones, having no identity of it's own to make it stand out.

I still want to see Episode III for posterity, but it won't be until after all six films have been released on DVD.

title: Good, but not the best Star Wars ever
review:
OK, so it's smashed the box office, even next to Spiderman. That's got to be worth something, right? Well, Star Wars films have always smashed the box office. Most of you (like me) probably only went to see it to find out why Anakin becomes Darth Vader. But, yet another episode went by without fully answering this.

Surprised that Anakin and Padmé hit it off? I don't think so. In episode I, dispite the age gap, the two hit it off quite well, so what else could they do? My main complaint about this film is the love scenes. Particularly that four hour speach (well, it felt that long) by Anakin, in which he confessed his eternal love for Padmé, and the pain of not having her, and the haunting of a previous scenes kiss ... He just wouldn't shut up about it!

There's only one more episode left until a good jedi-night becomes a half man, half robot Sith Lord. We never will find out why he is in that suit, will we? Because it'll only be at the end that Anakin crosses over, won't it?

All the other episodes had someone in the team who wasn't a Jedi, and actually didn't spend the entire film going on about the force (Han Solo in the earlier ones, Jar-Jar in Episode 1), but this time, only Padmé isn't going on about it. That's not enough! You need the clumbsy idiot or the rouge warrior.

I will say this for the film, the special effects are awesome! And the action is impressive. There's a lot more violence this time, as well (yippy!), including Anakin beheading a groupe of Tuskun raiders (I had no idea what they were, either, but they were sort of Planet-of-the-Apes rejects).

The mystery of the film is the plot. Who created the clone army? And why is it, if they were created by the dark side, did they fight for the Republic, and quite well, alongside the Jedi?

Tye action finally errupts properly in the last hour, after Anakin reaches the planet. I liked the fight with the monsters, but didn't Luke Skywalker have to do that in Return of the Jedi? Still, none of the others had an army of Jedi nights start having a mass brawl, Star Wars style. Pretty impressive, but could Padme really have survived that? I don't think so.

By far the best part of the film was the Yoda fight. This little sweat guy, who everyone thinks is halmless, apart from telekenesis, pulls out a light saber twice the size of him and fights with it. I don't think one person in the cinema could move for laughter. I hope that was deliberate, I mean who can take a guy who jumps around like that and still needs a walking stick seriously?

My only problem with the last hour was that the light saber battle between Anakin, Obi and Count Duku wasn't good enough! It just didn't last long enough.

Overall, it was entertaining, but lacked the feel of the older Episodes. Also, it was too long.

title: Lets forget about the Phantom Menace.....
review:
This is worthy of the Star Wars name. I am not going to go on about the Phantom Menace as much as I'd like to. A film that when it was released did very well only because of the Star Wars badge and not because it was any good.

This time round lets look at what Lucas has got right. He has captured a decent story line that is very simple but effective and likens itself to the original trilogy. He has created some stunning actions sequences and set pieces some of which nobody else could have dreamed of and he has got rid of Jar Jar Binks (well almost).

The film starts very well and makes you sit back into you chair knowing that the next couple or hours are going to be very entertaining. The film moves at a decent pace and never gets too slow or too hectic. Even in the battle scenes towards the end, everything is done with the utmost clarity and accuracy and to think that people were impressed with the battles in Episode 1, it doesn't even come close to what is in this.

The dialog acting is at best a little poor, which of course is to be expected. Anyone going to see this film expecting Oscar material has never watched any of the others. And to be honest I thought Ewen McGregor was better than in Phantom Menace and the only real let down was Hayden Christensen who was trying to hard as far as I'm concerned.

A couple of minor critical points about the film are the obvious plot lines that eventually turn Anakin to Darth Vadar. He tries his hardest to show how angry he is getting, and of course we know what anger does to a Jedi. When Padme tells him that he is not `all powerful', he replies `well I should be, and one day I will be the most powerful Jedi of all' or something like that. Its laughable, I bet even he burst out laughing then when George shouted cut at that point. The other is the brief moments of Christopher Lee. I expected him to play a bigger part and when you watch you can see why he doesn't appear for the first hour-an-a-half because there is no need for him to be there, however I still would have liked to have seen more of him. These are obviously minor points to an otherwise very enjoyable film and I am really looking forward to the next instalment.

title: about Lord of the Rings
review:
First off great film but disagree with comment that without George Lucas and Star Wars there would be no Lord of the Rings or Spiderman, surely there would be no Lord of the Rings without J R R Tolkien and no Spiderman without Stan Lee.

Star Wars was heavily influenced by Tolkien's novels and many other works which came before A New Hope, notably some of Akira Kurosawa's work. This does not make it a bad film as all works of literature reflect on or are influenced by what came before.

The originality of a work of fiction should be decided by how the author takes his influences and changes them enough to create a new spin on them.

George Lucas achieved this with the original Star Wars and the creation of the Star Wars universe and although i think he has set himself a difficult task of getting 40 years worth of back story into three films Attack of the Clones (poor title) is an enjoyable enough film and let's face it is better than both The Phantom Menace and in some respects A New Hope and Return Of The Jedi.

title: Very Ordinary
review:
I haven't seen the older movies, unlike most of the planet and I am taking care that I watch the movies in their correct order.

I enjoyed Episode One immensely. It is a shame then that I nearly walked out after the first 45 minutes of utter rubbish that George Lucas offered this time. The storyline was slow and trudging, flicking about between the pitiful excuse for a romance story and the deathly dull build up to the action, with some horrible acting from Hayden Christensen.

Thankfully, I decided to stay. After about 45 minutes the film suddenly burst into life, with dynamic acting, purposeful action, fast paced script etc etc. In the end I found the rest of the film gripping, entertaining and what one would expect from a Star Wars film, apparently.

But, the first 45 minutes force me to give it only 6/10.

title: ONLY ONE THING WRONG! WE HAVE TO WAIT 3 YEARS TILL THE NEXT ONE!
review: Right in sinc with the triliological mind of George Lucas this one left me feeling dark and wanting more. Just like The Empire Strikes Back we see prime examples of the definite line between good and evil. I love how diabolical Count Dooku's character is. How confused Anakin is about everything. With his loyalties to the Jedi order, and Padme at the same time, no wonder he's so moldable by Palpatine. We will see the definite fall and transformation of Skywalker in Episode III. This is a captivating tale for all ages. Shame on any critic for saying bad things about something so beautifully scripted, portrayed, and directed. Maybe they're jealous of Lucas' success. Nah they just don't really love movies like the rest of us do. They probably haven't had fun at the movies...well... ever.

title: 2nd Best Star Wars film..............
review:
I went with a fair bit of trepidation to see this film owing to the mixed reviews (again). Many of the bad reviews come from the so called high brow journalists who prefer artsy french film noir then a good action film.

My fears where proved wrong, this is without doubt up there with Empire Strikes Back, not as good but good enough.

I wouldn't want to give any of the film away to those who aint seen it but out look out for the Death Star, Yoda fighting, a Luke style prosthetic limb, Anakins first turn towards to dark side on tatooine and Jango Fett's head.

Those who like me have followed Star Wars since the start will see all the pieces start to fit into place, this will give a greater sense of what is to come in the 3rd film.

title: Painfully humorous
review:
It is movies like this that actually make me angry when I leave the theater.

First and foremost, consider the fact that the script for this film is essentially a 25 year work in progress. I can appreciate the attractiveness of the underlying story, but give me a break. A sixth grader with a free weekend could have hammered out the dialog that was present in this film. So many lost opportunities to further develop the story.

I am also sick and tired of hearing about the amazing effects. CGI, while remarkable when used properly, has become a substitute for true artistic inspiration. There is simply nothing new about all of Lucas' pastel toned, airbrushed backgrounds. They look pretty, they look like nothing more than a background, and they look fake. Until CGI is used in a fashion where it actually ADDS to a film, I am no longer impressed.

Finally, the acting in the film was truly painful to watch. Hayden Christensen displayed the range of a one legged buffalo caught in a snowstorm. His hackneyed expressions and dead delivery of lines conveyed nothing more than teenage angst; his supposed descent into the dark side was completely lost. The same is true for Natalie Portman, whom I believe is an otherwise fine actress.

In several instances, the most notable being the scene in which Christensen and Portman stood in front of the fireplace and proclaimed that they would be "living a lie," the audience actually erupted into snickering and laughter. Were it not for this endlessly amusing incident, I may have gone home without a scintilla of entertainment from my evening. I also gleaned an enormous amount of amusement from the supposed death of Anakin's mother. Priceless.

Yoda with a light sabre is cool. 20 seconds of entertainment.

title: What a piece of (fun) junk! 987 words
review:
--Some Spoilers--

First off, let me say I'm a HUGE Star Wars fan--I can recite each line of dialogue from the original trilogy in my sleep. Heck, I even liked Phantom Menace--even though it was a bit disappointing. And I had a great time seeing Clones at the theatre (Mann Chinese, baby!) with my friends.

This movie, though, stinks. It stinks BAD. I still enjoyed it simply because it's Star Wars, but unfortunately I've got to put this film on my list of the top ten worst movies EVER MADE in the history of film. There are some fantastic qualities about this movie which I'll get to, but IMHO what sinks this movie are two things: script and direction (hmmm...George Lucas was responsible for both of those things!).

First off, this movie just didn't FEEL like Star Wars. Even with the disappointment of TPM, I still felt like I was in the Star Wars universe. Watching Clones was like watching a generic video game. I think most of this is due to the fact that nearly every frame of this movie is almost completely computer generated. Clones shares more with last year's Final Fantasy than it does Star Wars.

Now the script. Hoo boy, there are no words to describe how awful, how horrendous, how gut-wrenchingly putrescent it is. Good lines are few and VERY far between. I think that the so-called 'love story' portion of the movie is literally the worst piece of trash I've ever seen in my life. It is on the level of really bad community college theatre, perhaps even as low as really bad high school theatre. This isn't the actor's fault, mind you. They did an admirable job with the stinking pile of dooku that they had to work with. Can anyone tell me WHY Padme falls in love with Anakin?!? The moment he lays eyes on her he starts working his mojo WAY too hard, which she doesn't go for at all. Suddenly, and for no particular reason, she's being charmed by him and admitting she has feelings for him! All she's seen him do are whine about Obi-Wan, undress her with his eyes, and confess to slaughtering an entire village of Sandpeople! Wow, enough to woo any girl. Every scene of their 'love story' consists of them--COMPLETELY ALONE (even though she's "not interested" in him and her life is in danger)--sitting in front of some lovely and romantic computer generated image. It's as if the only reason they fall in love is because George told them to. Completely inorganic, totally forced (no pun intended). And oh man, the lines they say to each other...most of the people in the audience were laughing out loud at how stupid they were.

Oh, and did I forget to mention Anakin's 'nightmare'? Honestly, does anyone at Lucasfilm WATCH these movies before they're released?

And I'll be darned if I can tell you what the plot was. Memento made more sense than Clones. You know it's a bad sign when the opening crawl finishes and your first thought is...huh? Something about two different planets creating two different armies, one for the Republic--commissioned by some Jedi who supposedly died ten years ago but maybe not (what? I still don't get that--who is this missing Jedi?), and another droid army for the Separatists, who are led by arch-villain...wait for it, wait for it...COUNT DOOKU!!! You'd think there'd be SOMEONE who could stand up to Lucas and say things like "Maybe 'Dooku' isn't the best name for our bad guy, George, whaddaya think?"

Not only is the plot confusing, but so many of the scenes are ripoffs of every other sci-fi/adventure movie movie out there. Blade Runner, 5th Element, Matrix, Starship Troopers, Gladiator, Galaxy Quest (for goodness sake GQ was MAKING FUN of conveyor belt/chompy-thingie scenes!)--Clones steals from them all and does none of it as well (well, maybe except for the speeder chase--that kicked butt).

The direction is also uniformly bad. After two movies, it's clear now that Lucas's only concern is with digital technology. He doesn't give a rip about plot or acting. The best part is when Padme falls out of the troopship. She appears to be badly injured when some clone troopers arrive to help her. "Are you alright?" they ask. "Yes," CGI-Padme says, leaping to her feet and trotting down the hill as if nothing happened!!! I'm also really bummed that Lucas finally found a way to ruin Threepio and Artoo. Oh man does 3P0 suck in this movie!

Okay, now the good stuff:

1) Ewan McGregor. He's a fantastic actor, and the most interesting character in both prequels so far.

2) Hayden. I thought he did a good job, given the script he had to work with, of working in typical teenage angst, being upset with Obi-Wan (fighting with Dad), while at the same time showing flashes of nascent adulthood as well as the sparks of evil that will one day consume him. Props!

3) The visuals. Undeniably some of the most jaw-dropping ever put on screen. The problem is that it eventually becomes too much. Nothing is real and by the end you walk out feeling as if you just watched the coolest videogame ever, instead of feeling like you just watched a Star Wars movie.

4) Yoda. He rocks, plain and simple, although I MUCH prefer the puppet. His training the kids scene was great!

5) Christopher Lee.

6) The first 30 minutes.

7) Jango.

Not that you care, but here's what you need to do, George:

1) Figure out what you want the story of EpIII to be about, then LET SOMEONE ELSE DO THE WRITING.

2) HIRE AN ACTING DIRECTOR so you can concentrate on what you love best--the visuals.

3) And HIRE PEOPLE THAT WON'T JUST BE YES-MEN.

5/10 and that's generous because it's Star Wars.

title: The pieces of the jigsaw start to fit...
review:
Warning: Possible spoilers

Those who thought Phantom Menace sucked will not be disappointed by this film. Most of the reviews already focus on the plot, so let me just go to the good and the bad.

The good: Ewan McGregor as Obi-Wan Kenobi. Great actor to begin with, and pretty much acts just like I would expect a younger Obi-Wan to. Christopher Lee as Count Dooku (informally Darth Tyrannus). Who better to play the precursor to Darth Vader. Incidentally, it seems like his name is in reference to Count Dracu (in history, Dracu was the father of Vlad the Impaler aka Count Dracula). Yoda...now you will see why he is truly THE master jedi ("Kick your ass I will!")--has the screen stealing part of this movie, and probably one of the best "actors" in this movie. The action sequences are truly amazing...much improved on from Phantom Menace. Look for a lightsaber fight between Dooku and Skywalker which is reminiscent of the saber fight in Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi but more artistic. And the Jedi battle with the droid army is kick-ass, especially with Mace Windu (Sam Jackson) getting medeivel on some droid.

Finally, and most importantly, this movie makes a better link to Episodes 4-6 than Episode 1. In Episode 1, even though it made more name recognitions than links, it served more as a prologue than a part of the episodes (a la Hobbit and Lord of the Rings). Here, we see more important connections: How the clones came into the picture of the whole story, how Anakin's temperament will eventually lead him to the dark side, Jedi training tactics, how (and who) the Emperor will come into making the Empire, and phrases from episodes 4-6 like "He (Darth Vader)is more machine than man" and "He (Luke) is impatient, just like his father", and even minor characters like Uncle Owen and Bail Organa of Alderaan (Leia's adopted father) start to fit into everything.

The bad: The romance between Skywalker and Padme. Could have been written more maturely, but ends up like a kindergarten romance. Almost brings the movie to Phantom Menace level (the other scenes save it from this). This is my biggest gripe about the film; if this is the key to Episodes 4-6, then don't put it down by making it look like a puppy love type of romance. I understand that Anakin has a crush on Padme, but please show me that the parents of Luke and Leia were more mature than this when they fell in love! Secondly, Natalie Portman is totally miscast as Padme. Don't get me wrong...she is an excellent actress, and very beautiful, but quite frankly, she doesn't have the pizzaz and feistiness of Princess Leia/Carrie Fischer to spice up the movie. It seems like Padme is more of the damsel in distress who dresses up pretty /kinky than a leader in this film. Then again, you can also blame Lucas and other screenwriters for putting her in this situation. Third, Hayden Christansen is appropriately cast as Anakin, but he is wrongly directed. Like Natalie, a very good actor with good screen presence, but except for the scenes where he is angry, impatient, or in action, he comes across as more wooden than human.

So pretty much, if you want to be entertained, or if you liked Star Wars when it came out and want to know more, you will like this film.

Now my only concern is with the liberties Lucas has taken with these prequels. I feel like he has included characters like R2-D2 and C-3PO more as a way to make a connection to the original episodes than as characters to be developed. I mean, if you recall in Episodes 4-6, they have no idea about Skywalker being their master, and don't really know Kenobi well. Do they have their memories erased in Episode 3? How about the fact that in Episode 5, Kenobi tells Luke that Yoda trained Obi-wan, but in Episode 1, Kenobi is the apprentice to Qui-Jonn Jin? If Lucas and his screenwriting friends are going to draft Episode 3, then I really suggest they view Episodes 4-6 again and fill in the gaps in Episode 3 as to not make the prequels as looking like different movies than Episodes 4-6.

The writing must have been dumbed down significantly for kids. The acting, even by actors who are normally really good, was the worst I've ever seen. The 50's diner and characters, the Fifth Element city scenes, the advertising in city streets, the bar with sports games on monitors, the Arrival/AI/X-files aliens, etc...none of it looked or felt like the Star Wars universe developed in the previous movies. It just didn't feel like a Galaxy far, far, far away - it was like everything else we see in movies now. He just relied way too much on the 3D, which I didn't think was very good either. I still like the old models much better than 3D, you just can't get the same detail and lighting quality with 3D. The fight scene with Yoda was the only cool thing in the whole movie and it was very short. The battle sequence was one big cheesy 3D fest, and the jedi knight army wasn't much of an army. What happened to the much talked of jedi knight army in the original movies. This movie destroys all of the grandeur talked about in the original movies of the Clone Wars. The scenes with Anakin and Amadalla were just plain silly - "Hi Annie, I love you and even though you just told me you slaughtered innocent women and children and liked it, I love you and want to marry you. Now lets go frolic in a meadow together.". The acting and writing in this movie, believe it or not, was worse than the garbage we were forced to sit through in Battlefield Earth. No depth or chemistry between any of the characters. I much prefer, despite Jar Jar and the little kid, Episode I. At least with Episode I they gave us great scenes like the beginning with Liam Neison and Ewen McGregor fighting together, the fight at the end with Darth Maul, the deathstar-like space battle at the end, etc. I'm just so upset with the crap he expects all of us to accept, especially now that we have new standards with The Lord of the Rings series. title: I want to love it more
review:
I enjoyed the film very much and look forward to enjoying it in the future. I would certainly say that if someone else invites me to come and watch it with them I would definitely say yes. I would however say that in many ways I don't consider it to be a good film. We have come to expect fairly cold heartless scripts from the Star Wars series, but as this had more than just action in it, the romantic element stood out like a sore thumb, and made those scenes insipid and boring to watch. Its not exactly like there was any suspense involved in the romance. We knew all along that they were going to come together. I just felt like shouting "Get on with it!" from the back of the cinema "Just shag each other and get on with the plot!".

It was nice that there was a little humour in the film, but most of it was very poor and did nothing to enhance the viewing experience. The low humour point in the film by far was the C3PO head swap fiasco. It detracted from the exciting action scene and in itself served absolutely no purpose to forming the climax of that stage of the battle. Surely there were many more interesting things that the bodged together mechiniod could have done with the advantage of being in an armed stronger body. Although my own sense of humour can be very cheesy at times the, sorry to give away a line but, "I'm beside myself" line didn't even get a groan in the full 1800 seat auditorium and although I was deeply into the action it dragged me straight back from the coliseum like amphitheatre, into my seat, while I sobbed into my popcorn! C3PO was the episode two equivalent of the universally hated jar jar, whom thankfully didn't appear very much as he was even more annoying than before.

One can understand that Aniken was at the uncomfortable teenage part of his life and that that was what they were aiming for, but the acting of what is effectively the lead character was more wooden than Roger Moore! I'm not quite sure exactly what they were aiming for with some of the characters and some how, even though I already knew and loved the Jedi and Pad Me characters, I found it hard to really care what was going to happen next. Rock on Yoda though. Nice light saber action!

At the end of the day though there were many things good about the film and at times I was on the edge of my seat. It ultimately a Star Wars film and for some reason the way the action scenes are played out and direction during these are pure Lucas and there is nothing quite like it. If only he had handed some of the bits he is rubbish at out, for more competent direction. OK yes. You may ask "What did I expect?", but I do honestly believe that with all of the things that make Star Wars so wonderful and good other bits, this could have been one of the best movies of all time!

In the end the bits that I didn't hate I loved and for some reason, that I feel hard to justify, I want to see it time and time again. Anyone free tomorrow?

title: engaging and enthralling
review:
By George he's done it!

After the dismal Phantom Menace all seemed lost. With the spectacular Episode II, George Lucas has resuscitated interest in the Star Wars franchise.

By now you're probably aware that this film has polarized audiences across the globe. All I can add is that this is a film for Star Wars aficionados only - it is steeped in Star Wars lore and has strong intertextual relationships with many aspects of the Star Wars universe.

I suspect much of the criticism this film has attracted is a more a reflection of the viewer than the maker. The mob is whining that Anakin is wooden, that the romance lacks romance, that characters aren't developed ... etc ad nauseam

If you're a knowledgeable Star Wars fan, ignore this and smile ... they just don't get it!

If you're a true believer, you will adore this film. You'll realise that the Republic has grown stale and ponderous, a dull-witted beast on the verge of extinction. It will occur to you that Palpatine is a Machiavellian dissembler who simultaneously plays the role of protector and assailant. You won't be outwitted by the Shakespearean double plot that Lucas has employed. You'll appreciate the delicious irony of Yoda leading a clone army purporting to save the Republic.

Visually, the film is stunning, eclectic and provoking - I especially enjoyed Dooku's sailcraft - artistically, the Star Wars universe is significantly enlarged.

My recommendation - if you know Star Wars intimately, enjoy! If you don't - read the literature, see the films, do some research ... and then see Episode II.

And thanks George ... looking forward to Episode III.

title: It's not perfect, but it's pretty damn good!
review: Like any Star Wars fan that grew up with the original trilogy, I looked forward to Episode II with a great deal of excitement, and I must say, having seen it now 5 times and having had many opportunities to digest its pros and cons, that it really quite extraordinary. As with anything that has such hype and historical success attached, viewer can't wait to tear it to pieces. After all, initially people complained about the title. For God's sake, was the titleThe Empire Strikes Back so inspiring, Return of the Jedi something special? And what does the title title matter anyways? After my first viewing, my initial feeling was wow!! What degree of imagination, design, craft and sheer graft must have gone in to creating such a movie? it is probably the closest to George Lucas' far away galaxy that we've yet seen. The characters, far-away-worlds and their applicable religons or beliefs are phenonmenal. And to think that this has all been brought forth from the in of one man is even moreso. If nothing more, George Lucas deserves praise for his vision and perseverance. As for the movie, sure it has it's faults. But what film doesn't? Some of the dialogue is a bit clumsy, but don't forget that it is designed to appeal to all ages. It's not Shakespeare and it's not Rugrats and neither is it meant to be. The enduring success of Star Wars is its universal appeal - and that may mean simplification, particularly where speech is concerned. The story is superb, especially when wee links to the original trilogy are thrown in. I particularly enjoyed Obi Wan's remark: "You'll be the death of me". Visually, the film is astonishing! The cityscape of Coruscant, the damp Kamino and the mysterious Geonosis all look fabulous. The action scenes including the early changeling chase, the Obi-Wan and Jango Fett battle and the always anticipated lightsabre showdowns were amazing. The performances were so-so. I can't still quite get used to Ewan McGregor's "Guinness" accent, Natalie Portman seemed a little bland while Hayden Christensen was good. For me though, the presence of Christopher Lee made all the difference. His brief scene with McGregor clearly showed the difference between "master" and "apprentice" in the acting stakes. As a fan I was thrilled. Whether you are a fan or not, cut the film some slack. Sure, note it's shortcomings, but recognise its merits, as there are many. And above all, just enjoy the fun, because it is after all, just a movie.

title: Though imperfect, Episode II has renewed the faith.
review:
First, I would like to say that anyone who hasn't seen Episode II yet should go see it and come to their own opinions about the film, there are a few spoilers in this review. That said, everyone must admit that this new installment in everyones favorite intergalactic saga proves that The Force is indeed back. With no mention of mitichlorians, relievingly few "meesa think..." comments, and an action packed storyline that keeps the audience at the edge of the seat the whole 2 hour length of his latest opus, George Lucas has renewed the faith feared lost after the glaring shortcomings of Episode I. This is not to say everything in Episode II is perfect, but rather to say that the film is comparable in overall quality to the first three.

Allow me to point out the flaws I found in the film first: -Hayden Christensen, though far more believable as the tormented Anakin than Jake Lloyd was as the child, does not deliver the kind of performance I think the part necessitates, though this may also be due to the dialogue he had to work with, which was, for the most part, uninspired language that does not fill the potential of one of Lucas' most compelling characters. -the dialogue and acting throughout the rest of the film was generally mediocre, most evident in the love story between Anakin and Padme which fell far short of what it could and should have been, but thankfully does not take up very much of the running time of the film

-one shot--with Anakin's shadow falling on the sand igloo of his stepfather's home while talking with Padme, making a silhouette that looks just like Darth Vader--lasts far too long and feels like an insult to the audience's intelligence. Right before this shot, there is a quick shot of Anakin's shadow, looking like Vader, which is enough, the rest is overkill

Now the good: None of the above matters all that much. -the sets, worlds, aliens, action sequences, cinematography, score, video and sound FX, and character development are all top notch.

-the plot and execution of the plot onscreen really drew the audience into the movie, which episode I did not accomplish

-The overall feel of the film is much more mature than episode I was, with a lot more self-awareness.

-the film managed to convey numerous ideas and images to the audience without being pretentious--especially the eerie people of Camino and the perennial storms therein, an ominous foreshadowing of the battles to come as a result of the cloning factories on this world.

-many of the cooler powers granted by the force but left out of episode I make a return--the blue electricity fired by the Sith, the modified telekinesis all Jedis use, the pre-cognition granted by the force (i.e. the little laser-firing orbs and a whole bunch of kids learning how to trust their intuition and block the shots with their lightsabres), and many other skills

-Yoda rules.

-Jango Fett, played by Temuera Morrison, and his "son" Boba add so much to the film. Boba Fett, everyones favorite sinister bounty hunter, gets all the attention (no to mention background story) he needs. When Jango gets into the thick of the action with Mace Windu (Samuel L. Jackson rules.) and gets his head chopped clean off--a fittingly ironic end to such a sinister bounty hunter-- Boba, played (very well) by Daniel Logan, watches on in anguish and hatred. After his shot holding his fathers helmet (head?), one of the finest in the film, I simply cannot wait to see what he does in Episode III.

-The setup of Boba losing his father works so well in conjunction with Shmi Skywalker's death at the hands of Tuscan Raiders. It brings to mind the scene in Empire when Vader sends Fett on bounty missions against the rebels, one can only hope their relationship is strengthened in episode III.

-The shot with Yoda surveying the battles against Dooku's forces with the symbol of the empire emblazoned on the storm trooper's helmet just behind the badass little muppet is just perfect.

-Yoda RULES.

-Ewan McGregor is a fine actor who brings the kind of life to Obi- Wan few others can, especially in one hilariously deadpan scene with a barfly in Coruscant

-there is much more to say, but i dont want to ruin the WHOLE movie for all those who still havent seen the film

In short, Episode II has brought back the fantasy and wonder of the original series, and I strongly encourage anyone and everyone to drop what they are doing and go see this fabulous film. I promise it won't disappoint.

title: the force is with it
review:
A great film.

Other viewers have complained that the romantic dialog is poor. True, it's not modern. In fact it's just different, in the same sort of style as Victorian novels or the Arabian Nights. Which is quite appropriate and credible in the heavily stylised "Galatic Republic" in which the film is set. Other viewers have complained that the politics are complicated. True, the goals of the factions are not spelt out explicitly. But we're an intelligent audience, able to put two and two together, and can understand with a little effort precisely what is happening and why. More viewers have complained that Anakin is whiney. I think he exhibits very well the arrogance of youth and power. You see him encountering his own limitations, and the limitations set by others, and straining against both. There's one particular scene where he gives in to his rage. In the aftermath, the recriminations are like those of God to Cain: "what have you done?"

title: Yoda kicks a** - but otherwise ordinary
review:
Aside from Yoda opening a can of whoop-a** there is little excitement in the film as action yields to character development but even then it could have been more interesting.

On the plus side some of the key plots that were evident in the earlier films are being revealed. The casting of Hayden Christensen is very well, portraying the early traits of his conversion to the dark side in a convincing way. Portman again does nicely in the role of the former queen now Senator. Some have said that the romance between them is too cold, no chemistry etc. Given that Anakin is a Jedi living with the same principles of that of a priest it is understood in the film that he has to be reserved. The pace moves nicely although some may find it slow due again to the development of the characters although the movie is driven out of the lull by spurts of action. The movie moves toward its big scenes at the end revealing that Yoda didnt always seem like the lovable and venerable character in the Empire Strikes Back.

On the not so plus side, special effects galore: the problem with computers being used in film is that now complete sets are being built on microchips instead of on real physical foundations. Attack of the clones suffers on this point. Lucas could have layed all the digital stuff because at a certain point you start to realize how fake looking it looks and also because it seems that the new films are now showcases to how much Lucas can pack in the film with the plot being a minor character in the movie. Even Yoda is now digitized, he doesnt display the same physical presence that he did on the Empire Strikes Back when first seen.

In the end it was entertaining but not extraordinary - some nice surprises. For the real fans it will have been a great improvement over the Phantom Menace.

title: Cool but
review:
This has some brilliant parts: Anakin when he goes ballistic in the Sand people camp Battle scene Light Sabre fight Yoda! Music!!!

Bad parts: I did not like Jedi's falling through the air. Too incredible. I wanted the fight with Jango and OB1 to be more!!!
