ps I would go to the Dark side for Nat

title: Without Anakin this movie would be great.
review: It´s a cool movie, much more Star Wars than Episode I, including great fight scenes (especially Joda of course) and with the guys who designed the clone-army the best aliens I have ever seen in a movie. But from the first moment where Anakin appears George Lucas screams in your face: "Watch out, this guy will become very evil". The storyline offers so many possibilities to let the character of Anakin develop, but Lucas simply completely failed with this part of the movie, since Anakin does not develop at all: From the beginning he is arrogant and bigheaded. Together with completely primitive dialogs ("I should be the most powerful Jedi of all time!") Anakins story simply destroys the good impression the rest of movie gives: If you take a look at his behavior, nobody can understand why Padme should love him at all and the moronic death of his mother makes you just shake your head. Not even the best actor could have made Anakins character and his story seem believable (because of the crappy script) and thus Hayden Christensen has not a chance to succeed. Does George Lucas think his audience only consists of idiots or why does he have to present Anakins tale so clearly that you feel insulted and without leaving room for any imagination. I will give this movie a 7, which regarding my harsh stricture shows how good many parts this movie has. But I am still disappointed because I know how good this movie could have been. The way it is it´s cool, but far away in quality from Lord of the Rings.

title: Splendid It Was!
review:
AOTC is a GREAT movie. In fact, the more I watch it the better it gets. The FX are breathtaking, the acting is contextually solid, and the story is a thrill ride that solidly binds together four other episodes and advances the entire saga. I am a Star Wars fan. I loved it since it originally came out in 1977. The critics didn't like it then either. Urg! Now many do...!?

I find the three major criticisms of this film astounding, primarily, that the first half lacked action (I don't think that they were watching the same movie that I was), that there were no memorable lines (Ebert what gives?)... how about "I call this aggressive negotiations." Lastly, people seeing this movie on film are seeing and hearing noticeably inferior picture and sound. Subsequently, they are being disappointed (little visual/auditory snap).

Anyway, I think that this is the second best movie of the Star Wars Epic (The Empire Strikes Back is still number one). However, after seeing this film for the third time (once on film and twice digitally) I can say that the digital version is SO TOTALLY SUPERIOR that a fair review can not be made unless the digital version is reviewed.

I also think that AOTC has filled in so many plot points (and in a fluid-action oriented way) that Star Wars may not be fairly judged as individual episodes. Only when Episode III is released, will we be able to objectively judge this collective thing called "Star Wars." When Lucas is done, we will have a complete 12+ hour SINGLE movie/epic that will be exactly the way the maker originally intended it to be.

I think that the whole of Star Wars is already much MUCH greater than the sum of its parts, and its parts ain't bad!

AOTC is SPELLBINDING!!!

title: Can't say I liked it
review:
Although, as most people have said, I think episode II was better than episode I, the movie was still rather disappointing.

First of all, I can't understand why people are praising the special FX. CGI just don't look real to me. Especially the computer generated creatures look weird, technology today just isn't good enough for this exaggerated use of CGI. To me, the special FX of the old star wars movies look better than the new movies. Stop motion rules. I'd even take ranchor over the ugly execution-monsters. I can't for the life of me understand why they have useD CGI for almost everything. Even when there is just one clone talking to Amidala, he is computer generated. To me, the second half of the movie felt more like an extremely long playstation cut-scene, than a star wars movie.

Also, C-3PO was a great disappointment, since he did nothing more than say stupid comments, that weren't remotely funny. He was almost as bad a comic relief as Jar-Jar was in the Phantom Menace. Old 3PO was funnier in the old days.

Yoda reminded me more of a bouncing ball than of a Jedi Master.

I liked the other Jedis though, and the lightsaber duels are pretty much the only things I like better with the new movies than the old.

All in all, I think the movie was more or less ruined by its special effects.

title: Steven Spielberg once said...
review:
Steven Spielberg once said that he rued the day when it would be more practical to design huge sets with a computer, rather than going to the trouble of building them. This film shows he had a point.

Think of your favourite scenes in a James Bond film: Blofield's mock volcano in You Only Live Twice, his alpine lair in On Her Majesty's Secret Service or perhaps Hugo Drax's space station in Moonraker. Now imagine if all of Ken Adam's set pieces had never actually been built, but done with CGI, as with Attack of the Clones. It would lose something, wouldn't it?

With actual set designs your enjoyment is on two levels. There's a sense of admiration at the real-life feat of having designed and constructed it. I'm not saying that CGI design isn't skilful, but it doesn't impart the same kind of enjoyment somehow - and, of course, it doesn't always convince. The same goes with stunts. 007's ski jump in the pre-credits of one Bond film is an audacious idea, made more enjoyable by the fact that we know a stuntman actually performed it. You could fake it now with CGI, but again, something would be lost.

That said, George Lucas could have a trick up his sleeve here. As noted, the effects in Attack of the Clones are far more advanced than those of Star Wars: Episode IV, which had a more beat-up look. But what if Episode III contains a scene of apocolyptic destruction, plunging the universe into the Dark Ages? That would account for the "backward" look of Episode IV. And the drift of events in Episode III foreshadows this - the overpopulation, the hi-tech prevalence, the sense of impending destruction, the fall of the Roman Empire and all that...

Just a thought.

title: Decent plot, Horrible acting
review: This movie is truly a dissapointment.  Some of the worst acting I've seen in a long time.  Lucas obviously wasn't looking to see if his characters were feeling the force.  Most of the scenes in the first half of the film look like the actors are reading their lines.  The actor who plays Anakin is terrible, and Portman looks like she's saying a line for the umteenth time. The action gets going in the last 45 or so minutes, but go to the concession stand for the first half, nothing really important really happens anyway.

title: The "fantasy" of Star Wars is alive and well!
review:
Since first seeing Star Wars around age 12, I've been fascinated by that scene on Tatooine when Obi Wan Kenobi is telling the young Luke Skywalker about the fate of his father...describing how Darth Vader hunted down the elder Skywalker and murdered him...alluding to the Clone Wars. For 25 years we've waited for a glimpse of the time when the Jedi kept the peace until, as fate had it, war broke out. We've been disappointed by Episode I (which was not THAT bad). Now comes Episode II: Attack of the Clones.

"Clones" brings the fantasy alive. Sure, it has some of Lucas's now trademark awkward dialogue (but wouldn't we all soil our pants if a Star Wars movie were nominated for an acting oscar...c'mon)! This movie tells us the story that we've waited 25 years to see, hear, and feel. And it does it damn well. I like these characters, and I believe them, too. Hayden Christensen plays Anakin Skywalker as well as Jake Lloyd did poorly! I feel the pain and anguish. As the movie progresses, Lucas employs the actors and the special effects to create a darker more ominous feel and look to the movie. Pieces of Darth Vader's theme and the Imperial March from the first trilogy are woven in artfully. Digital actors and sets are integrated seemlessly into this film.

History will not look kindly upon Episode I, but when the hype clears and the cynics go home, Episode II will be regarded as a classic right up there with The Empire Strikes Back and the original.

title: The force is with George this time!!!
review: George Lucas's film The Phantom Menace seemed good at the time, but after Attack Of The Clones was released it looked like a big disappointment. The acting, special effects and basically the whole plot seemed at least 10 times better. Anyone agree? And the bit where Yoda turns out to be an amazing acrobat was pure genius. You wouldnt expect it from a 500+ year old impish green dwarf, would you? But Mr Lucas did in my opinion, go a little overboard when he decides to have Jango Fett killed by Mace Windu while his son was watching. Seeing your fathers head been sliced off isn't very nice for a 7/8/9 year old child.(Boba Fett) I end by saying: "Go and see this movie. It is the best of the lot so far and it can appeal to everyone who likes a SciFi/Romance/Adventure film."

title: What a rush - next time Lucas, add personality to the actors
review:
This second of the new Star Wars movies is a great adventure, which easily makes you forget the terrible Phantom Menace. The movie is filled with great action scenes and Natalie Portman is always a pleasure to watch.

The only problem with the movie is the lack of decent personality in most of the characters. Ewan McGregor as Obiwan is good, but way too decent. His character definitely needs some more substance. Natalie gets the most out of Amidala as she can, but again the character needs some more depth.

Hayden Christensen however, must rank as one of the worst actors I have ever seen. He is seriously awful and is hopefully replaced for the third movie.

I never really understood, why Samuel Jackson agreed to do the part he did. Quite uninteresting part to play for such a great actor.

Yet, all in all, the movie is great and everything is now set for the grand finale, the third movie, which should be even better than AOTC.

title: Excellent movie, fine addition to the Star Wars family
review:
I am a huge Star Wars fan. First off, no movie could live up to the original Star Wars. As great as Empire and Jedi were, they weren't as good as Star Wars. Maybe technically or artistically they were better, but the original is just that, the original and it is very rare to eclipse an original.

Attack of the Clones is 50 times better than the Phantom Menace. It's story line is close to the standards set from episodes IV - VI. The visual and special effects are the best yet by far, which makes sense given it is 2002. The fight scenes were great, there was almost constant suspense and action. I really loved this film. And as you know, almost no jarjar (who ruined the first movie).

It can't match episides IV - VI in acting, or at least it wasn't given the chance to. There were great actors in the IV - VI. The actors in I & II are good too, some of them great (Sam Jackson), but I & II rely more on action than plot/character developement. I think this is more towards the times, in 2002 Lucas can do whatever he wants with the computer effects, something he couldn't do in IV-VI. So he had to rely more on acting and characters in the others where he didn't have to here. I would have like to let the actors do more acting in Clones, but all in all it was an excellent movie.

title: A fun fantasy thrill-ride across a galaxy far, far away...
review: Awesome in scope and breathtaking in execution, ATTACK OF THE CLONES leaves you wanting more!  The story of STAR WARS is coming together, characters become more developed, and the suspense mounts for the conclusion of the prequel trilogy.

title: Impossible to Compare with Original Trilogy
review:
Those who are the most disappointed with "Attack of the Clones" fall into the trap of comparing it with the original three Star Wars movies. By this standard, there is no way any of the prequels will ever succeed in fans' minds -- not so much because the product is inferior, but because many of the people who quibble the most with these new movies seem to forget they were 10 years old or younger when their beloved "Original Trilogy" came out.

The first of the original trilogy that I saw in a theater was "Return of the Jedi" -- I was 7 years old. Over the next several years, those three movies became larger than life for me, and I still believe they are as fun as any I've seen.

But anyone in their 20s or early 30s who hate these new movies because they are "inferior" to the previous three should remember that we came to love the original trilogy as impressionable young kids. This is not to take anything away from those movies, but it is the truth.

There are elements of the original trilogy that are just as "juvenile" as this one. If they were released today, some cynical Twentysomething like myself would laugh at characters such as Chewbacca, Admiral Ackbar, and Jabba the Hutt. (A lot of people snicker at the name "Dooku"; what about the fact that Han Solo's sidekick was nicknamed "Chewie"?) We would scoff at the acting skills of Mark "But I was going to the Toshi Station to pick up some power converters" Hamill. And we would probably even consider some of the special effects overkill, overcompensating for a lack of actual direction of live, human actors.

I still love those movies because they make me feel like a kid again. Many adults my age and older -- especially film critics, who seem to love movies that stroke their intellect or are self-important -- refuse to allow themselves to be 10 years old again when the curtain opens and the movie starts.

All this cynicism... and then look around the theater when you watch this movie again and take a glimpse at the kids who are watching it. They are the same age we were when we saw the original movies. And they are absolutely glued to the screen. Ten, 20, 40 years from now, they will love these prequels the way we love the classic trilogy.

This is not "The Godfather." It is not "Out of Africa," "Gandhi," "On the Waterfront," or "The English Patient." The fact is, as a 26-year old reviewer, with the experience and pretension an adult my age has, I must admit that objectively it may not even be "The Empire Strikes Back." But it sure looks, feels, smells, and IS a "Star Wars" movie and a worthy successor to the others. And I think if we were 10 years old -- and if we allowed ourselves to think like it -- we'd enjoy it just as much as we did the first three movies. When we saw those movies for the first time we were not nearly as cynical as we are today... and we were happier for it.

8.5/10

title: Candy for the eyes
review:
I really enjoyed the movie. Digital photography has come a long ways. The battles were a lot fun to watch. I liked the way Yoda looked in ESB better, more realistic. But, we are just seeing the birth of this digital stuff. Have much confidence will get better I do.

Sure, some of the acting was cheezy. Hey, so what. They did a good job considering most of there time on the set is probably in front of some sort of "blue" screen or something. I won't rip on it to much, they did a pretty good job.

Some of the one liners were bad (or has been heard a billion times now). They need to be a little more original. I'm just a big fan of "one liners".

It's definitely a movie to see on the big screen, it's candy for the eyes. If I watched it for the first time on my television, It probably wouldn't of made my heart pound as much and such.

Overall, I recommend this movie. I'll give it an 7.9 (not quite an 8).

title: A return to the Star Wars bread & butter
review:
I will not attempt to go into a painstaking critique as their others out there more qualified than I to do so. However, like many I was left a little incomplete in my expectations after watching Episode I. I am pleased to say that I did not leave with the same feeling of disappointment after watching Episode II.

Attack of the Clones sees George Lucas return in foundation to what made Episodes IV & V so fantastic & legendary. The darkness of this film is something we should have had more of in Episode I, and the development of Anakin's character was so much better weaved into the plot of the film then in the last installment. Ewan McGregor shines on the screen as Obi-Wan and we get an eerie introduction to the famed Storm Troopers, the Death Star and the roots of Anakin's eventual seduction to the dark side. Padme's striking similarities to her eventual daughter's are striking and well crafted. As always, John Williams does an outstanding job with the score - although he did recycle music from Episode I perhaps more than I expected!

Looking forward to 2005 and Episode III!

John Schmitt PA., United States

title: Great dialogue, acting, romance, plotwhere was it?
review:
**POSSIBLE SPOILERS** Before going into the cinema to watch the latest George Lucas franchise, I had pre-conceived expectations  and after leaving 140 long minutes later, they hadn't changed. Was this the best looking video game I just saw? The special effects and locations were undeniably spectacular, but a successful film needs story, pacing and acting first and CGI not to get in the way. The love scenes and the lulls with senators sitting around in circles had me looking at my watch, which can't be a good sign for a Star Wars movie. And the less said about the poor actors spouting such banal and cringe-worthy dialogue the better - who says the word `dreamy' anymore? And Anikan comes across as a spoilt brat and not a tormented soul on his way to becoming evil dictator Darth Vader - a missed opportunity. But what about the positives, as there are some visual treats. The last half an hour turned a mediocre movie into an entertaining ride, the Gladiator style monster battle was visual eye candy to behold. OK you knew none of the `good guys' was going to die not even a sense of danger, but please bring a little tension and unpredictability next time. There is however a great scene of Yoda putting down his walking stick to kick 80 year old Christopher Lee's butt. A crowd-pleasing moment that needs belief suspended, as judging by Yoda's highflying moves, why does he need a walking stick in the first place?

So to sum up - don't expect too much from the latest Star Wars movie and you're be entertained if not overly enthralled for a couple of hours. And it's still better than The Phantom Menace, oh yes, much better - A generous 7/10 rating

title: great effects, shame about the acting
review:
Saw it last night. The scenes between Annakin and Padme are terrible. The CGI is great. Yoda was done very nicely. last half hour is great.

However when Yoda gets moving (When you see it you'll know what I mean) He moves just too fast. I thought It would be great after reading some of the reviews here, but it was bad. Looks like there will be some cool games come out of this movie. Basically sometimes it feels like one long games advert. Hopefully George Lucas will not direct (At least not the real live actors) in episode III.

title: No more a movie for the guys
review:
I went to see the movie yesterday and I was frankly quite disappointed. Star Wars I was so bad that it is a good thing Lucas did not start off with that. That movie is targeted at "dad and his kids" which is quite brilliant from a marketing perspective. It is no coincident that Mr. Lucas is - to say the least - quite wealthy. For a normal guy I was sadly disappointed as I had hoped for an action movie with a humoristic twist, as I had seen in episode 4 and 5.

In episode II, Lucas fortunately tried to focus less on the kids-appeal. That is good, however, the romance theme (which I think makes out approximately 50% of the movie)is so boring that I had trouble staying awake. But I guess this is a way to get your girl-friend to see the movie. Any way I have never before heard so many men undergoing spasmodic yawns at the same time.

To sum up, episode I and II are terrible and totally unnecessary. It seems that Lucas has trouble in matching his own previous success. Having seen the movies I must admit that the marketing staff is very good, as they actually got me to waste my time at the cinema. However, I prefer a movie that keeps you awake and hooked. THAT is not the case with episode II!!

title: Totally redeems the franchise after MENACE !!!
review: I thought it was amazing! The sheer spectacle, it's like they filmed a documentary about the rise of an empire in another galaxy! Sure, there's some wooden lines and cliches, but if you can't get excited about some of the scenes in this movie, you are not there to see a STAR WARS picture! Spiderman (who I always liked) eat your heart out !

title: Very heavy on the irony...I loved it!
review: some of the lines in this film were laugh out loud funny! Obi-wan Kenobi: Anikan, why do I get the feeling you'll be the death of me?" Everyone in the theater laughed at that line. I enjoyed this Movie alot. Corusont was a lot like a futuristic Los Angeles, complete with a 50's style diner and cocktail waitresses! the car chase was very impressive, one of the most breathtakingly beautiful sequences in the whole saga. excitement started to grow in me, watching Anikan and Padme's romance blossom, because we were witnessing the begaining of the Skywalker Family, and hearing the imperial march again was a real treat. and it's just been confirmed that James Earl Jones will return in episode three as Darth Vader! I'm looking forward to it. title: Visually stunning piece of rubbish...
review:
I nearly walked out of this film. If it wasn't for the gladiatorial scene and what followed I would have. The actors did their job well considering that they were required to imagine their co-stars. Yet one wonders whether or not Natalie Portman and who-ever played Skywalker were required to do the same with each other! Honestly, the chemistry between them simply failed to materialize! I knew that the 'love' story was going to be insipid but non-existant!

The movie contains what is probably the best Sci-Fi battle scene ever. But, imagine if you will a beautiful maiden (Effects and Conceptual design) who is dragged into the mud by the Swamp thing (everything else)and you have the movie in a nut shell.

What I feel needs to be said however is that the worlds created are wholly convincing. Understand that I mean WORLDS. Populated with imaginative and stunningly realized characters, beasts, buildings and vehicles. It just had a lousy film made in it.

title: Best Movie
review: This is the best movie I have seen in a long time! I love the thesbians - Hayden & Natalie - they were very realistic! Hayden Christensen is very hot, and keeps a straight face all the time. I respect Natalie Portman very much! But the whole Star Wars is still bit confusing w/ me - 1st they go backwards, now they're going forward!

title: This movie is... *gasp!*
review:
*** RISK OF INCLUDING SPOILERS ***

I've got a confession to make (no - not about my crappy English...): I love Star Wars. Star Wars for me is the ultimate movies about the fight between good and evil. The only movie that has been able to threat the saga until now is Lord of the Rings - but that hasn't got anything to do with what I am going to write here, so I'll skip that for now.

To start off, I'll admit, that I didn't think, that The Phantom Menace was a huge mistake - but on the other hand I wouldn't call it the best in the saga either. But already after the first trailer being released ("Breathing"), I could see, that this film would be something... different. And all the following trailers only confirmed this ("Mystery", "Forbidden Love" and "The Clone War"). So when I went in to see the movie, I new the basics of what I was going to see, and I was not disappointed at all. When I came out of the cinema, I felt relieved, and realized, that Lucas is still on the roll even after 20 years of vacancy.

There are so many scenes in that movie, that I would like to talk about, but don't have time for. Yoda, Count Dokuu/Darth Tyranus, Boba & Jango Fett, the Clone Army and so on...

But I must admit, that the full potential of the movie is only released, if you know some of the background stories. E.g. that Dokuu was part of "The Twenty", which explains why he left the Jedi order. Also many of those parts of the script people point at as major holes in the story can be explained by using the knowledge in the background stories. E.g why does the specter of Yoda, Obi Wan and Anakin appear, but not Qui Gonn's? Why could Luke become an apprentice as a 20 year old, when Anakin was too old as an 8-10 year old? And so on. But without that it is still a very entertaining movie.

I've noticed, that many of the reviews are giving the movie very low marks because of the acting. And I agree - the acting is not on the same level of e.g Se7en. But let me ask you this: Who watches the StarWars saga because of the acting??? The acting has NEVER been the primary part of the saga. Only some of the actors have been able to give a decent level of acting, while the rest is below average. I won't consider Christopher Lee, Liam Neeson, Ewan McGregor, Frank Oz (OK - it is limited how much acting he is doing...), Harrison Ford and Ian McDiarmid as being bad actors...

Also by seeing the prequels to the original 4-6, the characters in the original trilogy makes much more sence after seeing their story before we met them for the first time. Why Vader is as he is. How did Sidious/Palpatine get all that power? Who is Yoda, and what is he doing in that swamp? And why is he a Jedi Master, when all he is doing is waddling around? And so on and so forth.

Yes - I have seen this movie more than once, and yes, I am going to see it again. And I am looking very much forward to Episode 3 - where Anakin will take the final step towards the Dark Side and become Darth Vader as we now him from Episode 4-6.

The grade? 9½/10.

title: Looking for a love story? Skip "Episode II."
review:
As a movie standing on its own merits, "Attack of the Clones" is an exciting, memorable action flick. I was on the edge of my seat nearly the whole time, and just when I thought things were going to settle down, the energy fired up again. However, as a member of the Star Wars saga, this movie is sadly a let-down. Gone are the witty one-liners and quips that define the original trilogy. And yes, there's actually a male-female relationship. I don't dare use the words "romance" or "love," because the acting is so stiff that it's impossible to believe that Anakin and Padme really care about each other. Though considering that Anakin is growing into Darth Vader, the idea that the whole thing is just teenage lust is a little more believable. I don't think it would be possible for Padme to see anything good in Anakin because he was so shallow, bitter, and downright disgusting to her. What was she thinking? I could swear there was a jedi mind trick in there somewhere.

I was really happy to see Jango Fett in "Attack of the Clones" because I'm one of those weird fans of Boba. Unfortunately, he seemed way too clumsy and unsure of himself in this movie, and his reputation as a bounty hunter who never fails was unconvincing. Plus, he died in the first movie he appeared in! What a rip-off! I find it tough to believe the greatest manhunter in the galaxy was defeated so quickly. Especially with all those cool gadgets. If I had a suit like that, I could've beaten Obi-Wan. Boba was in the movie too, but he was just this ugly little kid having a bad hair day. Certainly not what I was expecting! I hope he grows a lot before Episode III.

One thing that always set Star Wars apart from other Sci-Fi sagas (like Star Trek) was that its technology was so different from everything else. In a way, the Star Wars universe was far more high-tech and cool than the 24th century of Star Trek. But it's so gritty and REAL that it's a lot more likable. The ships looked like real vehicles, assembled by real people, with function over form. I could really picture those things cruising through space. But lately the ships are getting so shiny, sleek, and smooth that it's hard to believe Episode II is a prequel to the original movies. What we have now are glossy yellow "Flash Gordon"-esque pods that streak across the screen effortlessly. Pretty stuff. But this is how many years BEFORE the beige behemoths of "A New Hope?" The galaxy seems a lot more populated in "Attack of the Clones" too, but I think that's just George Lucas flexing his CGI muscles. I think we've got a few anachronisms here.

I could write for a long time about this movie. But I'll stop now. It's a decent movie, bottom line, but not really worthy of bearing the "Star Wars" moniker. And the acting is ridiculously cardboard, especially the "love" scenes. Yuck.

title: everything we love about star wars
review: Attack of the Clones reveals how beautifully complex the star wars saga is. There is a whole level of complexity that the original three movies lack, and this movie delivers completely.  It is obvious why Lucas waited to do the first three episodes.  The  intricate battles and sequences in episode II would have been impossible to do with the limited special effects they had, nor would a new audience be as appreciative of the significance of the actions that happen in episode II.  Knowing what will eventually happen attaches so much significance and awe to the actions in Episode II.  Lucas delivers but he also leaves plenty of mystery with episode III.  We STILL do not know what will happen.  This movie reveals the most information out of any movie before it, but at the same time becomes the most personal.  We care about the characters because they are people not because they are heroes in a movie.  It is the reason the star wars movies are a success because it reaffirms everything we love about the previous four.  A gem

title: get over yourselves
review: Star Wars is what it always has been. I am a huge Star Wars fan, and I will admit, Star Wars is cheesy. It always has been. Anybody who wants to complain about bad acting had best recall the originals. Anyone who wants to complain about cheesy lines had best recall the originals. And if you fell in love with Star Wars when A New Hope first came out, but want to now say that the story just isn't any good, then you are fooling yourself. Nobody loved A New Hope because the story was great. People who fell in love with it in the 70's did so because of the special effects and anybody who says different is either a bad judge of good plots or a liar. I admit, the special effects in The Phantom Menace were, for the most part, not up to par with those of the originals. This movie is different. In this movie, they are better. If you did not like this movie because of any of the above reasons, then what the hell were you doing watching Star Wars in the first place. And if you feel like blaming George Lucas for doing such a bad job, get over yourself, it's not his fault that you are a sucker. Way to go, George! Here's to Episode Three!!!

title: George Lucas is raping his own corpse
review:
I think I've only read about 100 of the reviews for AOTC, and there seems to be a mostly even division regarding the film's worth. I'd say about 40% pro, and 60% con.

There are 4 groups of people I want to address in my review, since every conceivable spoiler has already been revealed (not very difficult to do for a movie with a $2 plot) and the many flaws have already been pointed out.

PEOPLE WHO WERE VAGUELY DISAPPOINTED WITH AOTC: You are not alone. And it's not that there's anything wrong with you; you didn't like this movie because it was truly bad. Don't let your standards slip so low that you can no longer separate good movies from dross like this. Be ever vigilant. Demand better films.

PEOPLE WHO HATED AOTC: My brothers (and sisters)...seeing your reviews does my heart good.

PEOPLE WHO LOVED AOTC: Please do not tell other, unwitting filmgoers to see this dud. It is cruel to trick people into throwing their money away. Attack Of The Clones was NOT a good movie, no matter how much you enjoyed the original trilogy, no matter how many figures you own, no matter how good your Darth Maul costume was last year, and no matter how many times you've paid for Jeremy Bullock's autograph. This movie was bad. (See other reviews for details on HOW it was bad.) For anyone to give rave reviews to a film with so little going for it is like a child saying that a restaurant served "good" food when all they offer is chocolate bars, cotton candy, and Jolt cola; you don't really know what "good" is. Attack Of The Clones is the cinematic equivalent of junk food. You will receive no nourishment of any kind from seeing it.

Contrary to some of the posts I've read, the acting wasn't even remotely decent, the storyline was NOT compelling, and George Lucas is NOT, in fact, "back." We all enjoyed the first three movies, but we're big kids now (I hope); we should be able to recognize a 120-minute commercial for ILM or Kenner toys when we see one.

PEOPLE WHO HAVE NOT YET SEEN AOTC AND ARE TRYING TO DECIDE IF THEY SHOULD: Trust me. This is not worth your time. Go see Spiderman if you really need to get out of the house and see something on the big screen. Don't believe the hype about Episode II, because the people who will tell you that it's anything more than eye candy have standards that are shamefully low. They wouldn't know a good story if it was served up on a silver platter for them.

But...if your curiousity simply won't let you rest, and if you MUST see what all the fuss is about, let me help you to enjoy it as much as possible...

1) Expect to laugh where you shouldn't. Anakin's range of emotions is more limited than Stephen Hawking's vocal inflections, so his serious lines are sometimes unintentionally funny. 2) Don't look for continuity. There are holes in the story big enough to pilot a B-wing through and things that simply won't make sense if you stop to analyze them for longer than a few seconds, like two people who met as children confessing that they've thought about each other constantly over a period of TEN YEARS, even though one of them was a queen and then a senator (presumably, she was kinda busy) and the other was undergoing rigorous training to become a Jedi Knight. (How did "Annie" ever manage to learn to levitate fruit when he was oh-so-smitten with a girl he met before he hit puberty?) 3) Don't expect anything "big" to happen to save the movie. Yoda's fight is entertaining, but it's almost like watching his more subdued cousin play the part. You will find yourself asking how a CGI-generated character could be more expressionless and dull than a puppet. 4) Don't expect to be dazzled by the visuals. Yes, they're good, but FX can't save a movie, and we've seen stuff like this before. As one reviewer put it, we see the same thing just by playing computer games.

And finally, one more tip; if you're going to go, take some psychedelic mushrooms beforehand, sit way in the back so you have a good view, and surround yourself with people who won't mind hearing you say "Whoa" a lot.

I'm really really really really hoping that Mystery Science Theater 3000 tackles this one, because that's about the only way it could be worth watching.

title: So close and yet so far
review:
So close and yet so far, this is exactly how I felt when I left the cinema. This is the only way I feel best to describe this latest installment of the Star Wars trilogy. This is because it almost fulfilled my expectations but always seemed to let me down when I felt it was finally getting somewhere.

Now before I get into the film I do want to make it clear that I am a Star Wars fan and I had great expectations for Attack of the clones and I also enjoy watching a good film and like to be fair with what I watch. So when I went to watch Attack of the clones I felt that it was only fair to give it a chance after the watching the previous installment of this prequel trilogy (i.e. The Phantom Menace) which to be quite honest was disappointing. Attack of the clones however, was not disappointing but more of a puzzlement to me.

By that I mean Im unsure whether I like it or not. The film has so many good qualities but these are matched by the bad ones as well. The film starts off well enough by reaquainting us with some of the characters and starts with a plot situation that is a bit more easier to follow than the previous installment. The galaxy is still in turmoil and the republic is on the verge of collapse, the Jedi are also struggling to keep the peace in the galaxy. In comes Natalie Portman as Queen Amidala who is dispatched two Jedis (Obi Wan Kenobi and apprentice Anakin Skywalker) to guard her as she has become the target of assassination by an unknown assassin.

Ewan McGregor steals the show with some of the wittiest dialogue the film has to offer (that is, he has all the great lines) and great action scenes, an improvement over his last performance as Jedi Knight Obi Wan Kenobi. But its business as usual for the acting veteran Christopher Lee who plays the mysterious Count Dooku and puts in his usual creditable performance.

The film is packed full of CGI and is very impressive at that. There are baddies a plenty on offer including the deadly bounty hunter Jango Fett. There is enough lightsabre swinging and laser blasting action to keep the average film-goer entertained and the star wars fan impressed.

So now you wonder, what can be so bad about the film? Well to begin with, the use of CGI was impressive but after a while it all seems too fake. The plot after a while seems a little confused and even left me wondering at the end what was going on. The dialogue is also of a poor standard which after a while becomes very tongue in cheek and at other points cringe worthy!

The acting from the new Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christenson - I hope thats spelt right) is a bit sketchy at times. For the first hour of the film he seems to overact and moan too much for my liking, but I will give him his credit as well because he does manage to pick it up later in the film when he goes back to Tatooine and performs well in some key scenes, I wont spoil it for you!

However, as necessary as the love scenes were, there appears to be no chemistry between the on screen couple Portman and Christenson. It all seems to corny and forced at times. Also, in some instances you wonder what the attraction is between the two (in terms of personality).

The lightsabre battle at the end is more adequate than impressive. Yoda has more of a presence in the film but again you wonder after a while if this is a good thing or not.

Now this is the sort of film you could pick holes in all day about plausibility but its star wars, its supposed to be fantasy, so I wont even consider attempting to do that. If you are looking for the kind of film that can just go straight over the top of your head and keep you mildly entertained with its action spectacle than this is your film. Its not bad for something to watch on a night out, but I would'nt rush to see it.

However, I think other star wars fans like myself will walk away feeling slightly confused with how they are supposed to feel about this film. That is, was it great or average? Better than The Phantom Menace but it just falls short many a time of being a truely great film. I'm gonna hold out till the next installment to see whether or not George Lucas truely deserves the credit for his prequel trilogy.

title: Thank god for the battle scene at the end.
review:
The thing that made the original series great was that, even though it was sci-fi, it was believable to a large extent. Episode 2 (and Episode 1 for that matter) both throw the notion of believability out the window. From about 5 minutes into the movie until about the last 1/2 hour was nothing but fluff; all cute little things put in by George Lucas to sell tickets....just tell the story.

Because I am such a die-hard Star Wars fan, I still think it was worth the price of admission, but I would have much rather have seen Lucas return to tell the dark story that the Star Wars series really is.

title: An improvement but not up to snuff-- awkward love story
review:
Warning- this review may contain a slight spoiler to those totally unfamiliar with the premise of the Star Wars movies.

Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones is a clear improvement over Episode I, but it leaves much to be desired. Lucas continues his love affair with great and not so great CGI, which is sometimes incredible and sometimes incredibly fake looking in this film.

The movie started interestingly, despite some truly cheezy dialogue during the first action sequence. The situation established and the character tension seemed truly strong. However, as the movie progressed the tension slacked, and what was youthful defiance in Anakin turned to selfish, immature poutiness. What was a sense of guarded independence in Padme turned to a completely unbelievable and rather sudden 180 turn in character.

We all knew what was going to happen, and it seemed like the film was going to include a truly interesting battle of two strong people submitting to their passion. But instead, Anakin seemed to whine his way into Padme's heart, and it thoroughly compromised all of the buildup of her character. People in our audience laughed at what should have been a very touching moment because it was presented so poorly.

Other than my problems with the plot of the movie and some poor CGI, I enjoyed this movie. Once I quit looking for bad CGI and let go of the hope that there would be minimal cheezy "Lucas Dialogue" as my husband calls it, I had fun. Which is how a Star Wars movie should make one feel. Fun.

The plot was interesting, and Yoda was awesome! Other than whiny Anakin, there were no characters in this movie who were gratingly annoying (not to name names from Episode I). The premise was good and left a lot to look forward to in Episode III. And Padme's wardrobe was gorgeous!

Hopefully, the upward trend will continue.

title: For Best Results: See This Movie TWICE
review: When I first saw Episode II, I spend too much time analyzing it and finding the flaws in the movie.  I saw it again a week later, and just sat back and enjoyed the movie.  One reason it was better is that I saw it on the DLP screen.  If you have the means to do so, please make the effort to watch this on DLP.  It is awesome!  The acting seemed better the second time around, especially with Christensen (the "attitude" threw me off the first time, but he really does a great job portraying the role).  If you were disappointed with this movie, give it one more chance.

title: good for star wars
review:
Ok, you can probably guess from my one line summery that I actually like Star Wars. I've seen episodes 4, 5, and 6, but i didn't enjoy them, in fact, i hated them - yes you are going to verbally assult me for that statement, but it takes me a long time to get my head around fantasy (second time round for Lord Of The Rings as I couldn't get my head around the hobbits being smaller than everyone else and that thy were played my real people - ok, going off the subject, so...) for this reason i did not enjoy the original Star Wars films. I never seen episode one, but I would like to so that I actually understand some of the things that went on in episode 2.

Onto what I thought of the film, I thought that it was quite slow moving with not much action, only the development of the love between Anakin and Padma (? spelling? Natalie Portman's character anyway), I may be a girl but I do like films to have some action in so that I don't get bored, so I really enjoyed the action scene in the arena with the Jedi's fighting the droids which Count Dooku manufactured, that had to be one of the best parts in the film, and the touches of humour from C3PO had me in stitches, however the fight scene between Yoda and Dooku was hilarious (SPOILER), Yoda hobbles in there leaning on his walking stick, uses the force against Dooku, then they fight with their lightsabers, Yoda is flying around, levitating and generally acting as if he is not ancient, I was in hysterics at this point, because (even with my limited knowledge of Star Wars, I know that Yoda can barely walk around), so this was slightly hypocritical, but even more so after he has (SPOILER) saved Obi Wan and Anaklin from getting crushed as they lie passed out on the floor of the hanger, he goes back to hobbling around on his stick - it was so funny, if you don't like Star Wars, you have to go and see it just for that.

It is amazing what Yoda can do when he hasn't got a hand stuck up his a*se, and he, and the absolutley gorgeous Anakin, are my favourite characters and I hope that I will be able to go up to Leicester Square to see episode 3 as I am now curious, like everyone at a guess, to see how Anakin goes 'to the dark side', but I could see hints of it in episode 2. I give this film 7/10, very good entertainment

title: Possibly the finest in the series
review: Some might complain about the love story and pace of the first half of the movie, but they fail to see how it helps to develop the story which ultimately leads to the original trilogy. No doubt that the action in the last half of the film left you stunned and waiting for Episode III to come out.

title: I don't want to say that I am disappointed but I really expected more!
review:
Saw the first show of Episode 2 on this side of Atlantic last night in a special preview after midnight. And man was it an event, but that's expected I presume of every Star Wars movie. Anyway getting back to the point, I really expected more than what the movie eventually offered. I heard people saying on television movie programs, those who had seen it in the Trebecca film festival in New York, that its better than Episode 1: The Phantom Menace and so on. But I beg to differ. I am sure that its not. Though I feared a complete love story after watching many many rushes in the last few weeks but luckily it has a lot more. Unfortunately it all doesn't seem to be linked to each other that well.

Now I don't want to give away the story so I would just say that it's about the attack of the clones :) On what and by whom I wouldn't say. And though it is the main theme but the actual attack was only one of the many sub plots in the movie. In my humble opinion the real story is the turning of Anakin Skywalker to the dark side. He is, as all know, the hero of the recent trilogy as Luke was in the first but he has to turn to a complete villain by the end of the next episode and George Lucas has tried for the first time in this movie to explain this transition. Anakin is shown to be suffering all the time by his new found love and by the nightmares of his pained family ties. Add to it his growing disenchantment with the system and the jedi order and the desire to be the most powerful. In the flow of emotions he does some things untypical of a jedi and the process takes him closer to the dark side. This transition as I wrote earlier is the sole purpose of this movie.

I found many a times during the movie an out of the ordinary effort by Lucas to explain things which he supposed or presumed in the original trilogy and I think any close viewer will notice this as well. As for the performances, I would say Hayden Christensen didn't make a really bad debut but he could have been a lot better. He looked stone faced and emotionless in many scenes. Natalie Portman was good in her role that was more realistic than the pomp and style of the queen she was in Episode 1. She seem to be the dominant partner in their relationship as she has more control because of her position as a senator and being more mature of the two because of their age difference. Rest of the cast did well but if there is a real star of the movie, it's got to be Ewan McGregor. He was really good. Visual and sound effects are outstanding and I found a marked improvement in the background score as well. The screenplay, though a little better than Episode 1, leaves a lot to be desired. If one had to point out one major difference with the original trilogy it has to be the strength of the original screenplay.

Now just to give a little away.... the high point of the movie comes right at the end, and the die hard fans will surely enjoy that.

My recommendation will be to go and watch the movie as every other fan would do but don't expect a lot or you'll really be disappointed. Enjoy the visual extravaganza and you may end up liking the movie. My rating 6/10.

title: Just not good - admit it!!
review:
***********Warning Spoilers****************

I decided to take a few days after watching this to post my review, giving me time to mull things over. Frankly this film is a disappointment.

When you have an almost unlimited budget, the best CGI specialists working for you, no time pressure to deliver the finished product and actors queuing round the block in their desperation to work for you, then really there is no excuse for this being presented as the final product.

I'll start by tackling one of the good' aspects of the film. The idea that Palpatine has created this false separatist movement to enable him to effectively usurp the Senate and put to use a clone army of the Republic is pretty neat. Excellent, terrific, well done George! It's hardly the most cunning plot idea ever but it's good enough and explains well how Emperor Palpatine comes to power. Some however have suggested that this somehow makes up for The Phantom Menace  that it explains why the first instalment seemed so disjointed and frankly amateurish. This is utter tripe. The TPM storyline / plotting was just rubbish and the events of AOTC should not be used as some sort of figleaf to cover this. But heck I'm man enough to let bygones be bygones.

Now I've read a few of the reviews on this site that have been of the get real' variety. I agree wholeheartedly, this is Star Wars not Shakespeare or some deep, weighty film about the human condition. Thus I would suggest George Lucas remember this. It seems obvious to me that old George, in his quest for the creation of a mythic and enduring morality tale, has forgotten something  a myth or fable need not be childish. Emotions do need to be writ large upon the screen and character traits and ideas of fate and destiny conveyed via a bludgeon to the audience. I mean the pseudo-Noo Yawk caff with the chummy short-order cook / owner - urrrghhh...I mean please, please, please try and treat me with a little modicum of respect. In fact who the hell was this aimed at? Children under a certain age would not care, teenagers would think this was just lame - this is just an example of sheer self-indulgence at the cost of the audience.

This is what annoyed so many people in the audience when I saw it and which resulted in laughter at some of the supposedly deep moments'  I mean for chrissakes did Anakin's mother really have to die in his arms  that got a real good laugh, which I assume wasn't the aim. Or do evil characters really need to have names like Sidious, Tyrannus? I await the formidable presence of Darth Eee-Will next. Does Anakin, to show the dangers of power without maturity, really need to whine like a 7 year old when he's supposed to be 16 or so? Even children over the age of 8 would be insulted by such idiocy. It is really necessary for Mace Windu to suddenly do a Samuel L. Jackson Bad-Man patented moment with This party's over'  again raised a laugh not of delight at recognition but at the sheer stupidity that made the director think this was a good idea when filming or editing.

I really want to know the answer to one question  is there anyone in world of cinema who has the balls to tell George that this cut or that edit is frankly crap  a classic is when Padme is lying, apparently dazed and hurt on the sand  along comes a helpful clone trooper and suddenly she jumps up and with an I'm o.k.' shakes of the moans and groans. The audience creased up at that one and so did I.

I really can't blame the actors in this for the fact that Yoda comes across as the most coherent, real character and he's CGI. The only human actor who came near was Temuera Morrison as Jango Fett and that's because to be the Boba Fett's papa, nay even clone is just too cool for school. The only person who can really take the blame is George Lucas.

Is this utter tripe like Phantom Menace? Not by a long shot. But if the next episode, Nemesis I believe is the title, is the same degree better than AOTC as AOTC's is better than PM then we may have a reasonably good film on our hands. Whether I go to see it is another matter as you have to wonder if you want to be a chump 3 times on the trot.

Yes the effects are great - big deal, that's what we expect now. yes Yoda fights - whoopty-freakin-doo. It really has been overhyped. A heartfelt plea George, a guy you may have heard of (and ripped off actually) called JRR Tolkien wrote a story that he hoped was a morality tale disguised as fantasy - luckily this other chap called Peter Jackson came along and made a damn good movie out of just one part. If you really insist on following your vision, let someone else put it on screen for you cos frankly you have stopped doing a good job of it. Yes, we're too jaded and cynical - so you had better change what you deliver instead of expecting the audience to revert back to how they were when Star Wars came out and forget some 25 years of films in between.

title: Another rather negative comment.
review:
** THIS COMMENT CONTAINS SPOILERS **

When I went to see Episode II, I had rather high expectations. This because I had been told it was considerably better than Episode I, with much less Jar Jar presence etc.

During the first 1 - 1.5 hours of the movie, I thought it was rather slow most of the time. Especially so during the scenes with Amidala and Anakin. At times it was actually slow to the point of being outright boring.

When I left the cinema after the movie, someone asked me what I thought of it. It then struck me that the thing I liked the most about the entire movie, was the sound effect used for the seismic charges among the asteroids.

Naturally, there are other good things about the movie, but that was the one thing in the entire movie that felt "perfect", or close to it.

One part of the movie I liked was the water world with the tall aliens. These felt "right" (quite possibly because they look like aliens are "supposed" to look like according to other movies etc). They didn't feel so over-the-top like some other creations in the movie do (the thing Obi-Wan talked to at the diner for example).

One other thing. During some scenes, I almost started looking for the gamepad controller infront of my seat. The whole look and feel of the scenes presented, was very close to those of a platform game. I'm refering to the scenes with Amidala and Anakin in some processing facility.

And Jar Jar ... well, he wasn't in the movie that much. But everytime he's on screen, and especially when he's talking, I feel that I'm about 20 years too old to be in the target audience for the movie.

I think Jar Jar is something that only young children can really appreciate, and I'll go out on a limb and say that pretty much every other viewer of Episode I thought that his presence made the movie worse than it would have been without him.

So ... why am I not so thrilled about this movie? Well, I think the plain truth is that I've become too old for Star Wars. I was 10 years old when I first saw Return of the Jedi on cinema. I was blown away by the movie, and found the Ewoks fascinating instead of annoying. Now, 20 years - and thousands of movies - later, I'm expecting much more from a movie. Now, I can detect sub-par dialogue and acting.

Episode I and II, to me, feels like movies that are made almost exclusively for children (unlike, for example, LoTR). They have lots of fancy effects to make them go "WOOOW!!", but other aspects of the movies has been given secondary priorities to a degree that makes it harder for me to enjoy them as an adult.

*** (3) out of of ***** (5)

title: The first theatre movie in 25 years
review:
I haven't seen a movie in a theatre in 25 years. My kids made me go see this one. As a matter of fact, one of the last moves I saw in the theatre was Star Wars.

It was too loud. Oy ve, I sound like my grandfather.

But it was exactly what I expected. No more, no less. Great effects although out of focus when rendering large cities. The work on Anakin was overdone but not too much. I would have deleted about half the storylines. But you could see images of Vader and you said "hhmmmmm..." quite a bit. That was nice.

But for sheer entertainment, two thumbs WAY UP. It really was fun to watch although I would have preferred it on a TV screen. It was SO intense at times. Like a roller coaster that goes on too long but you still enjoy it.

I predict this will be a big hit on video. It's a good chance to show off the $5k home entertainment theatre.

title: Anakin is whiny? How about you nay sayers are whiny.
review:
Yes I must admit that I like the new Attack of the Clones and Phantom Menace films. I think for saying that I will be pelted with rotten fruit from critics who thinks that the new Star Wars films are wretched. Yet friends I am not the Star Wars geek that you might label me. No I am simply a lover of movies. No not a film auteur just a fan of entertaining films. I happen to find the Star Wars films very entertaining. I'm afraid it is you critics out there, who complain that the new Star Wars films fail to hold a light to the original trilogy, who are the Star Wars geeks. You nit pick about how it is not well acted or it is not well written, or the special effects are fake. The latter of complaints are...well...just plain slander or come from people who need to get glasses. One complaint, "Yoda is not the same as CGI." No I have to say he's a lot better.

As for comparing the new films to the original... In 1999 when the Phantom Menace came out I went in knowing that in no way was Lucas going to be able to recapture the magic of the original and he hasn't. But that's OK. Star Wars was made in a time when such films like it were a rarity and thusly Star Wars appeared as a breath of fresh air. Most films in the 70's and most of the 80's were dull, gritty, and low key, not to mention vulgar. Star Wars in some way changed the summers at the cineplexes and now every film out there is trying to be the next big thing. And that is fine too.

Yet the original Star Wars trilogy was not the best acted series of films, or the best written, or for that matter the most original. They were not designed for you to serious ponder the meaning of life, or the conflicts of this world...No they were simply meant to transport you to another one. A galaxy where fantasy thrives and where good and evil duke it out with colorful lightsabers and lasers. To get majorly upset over such a thing is rather petty. And to hear grown men at the end of the movie yell out loud how much Attack of the Clones, "just sucked," is rude and becoming of a true whining brat.

In all fairness I will say that yes these news Star Wars films are flawed but so is just about every other film out there. And for the love story, yes it lacks some charm that was found in Empire Strikes Back, but I'll take it over that three hour mess that was Titanic.

In its defense I will say that Attack of the Clones was adequately casted all the way. Hayden Christansen, Natalie Portman, Ewan McGregor, and Samuel Jackson all get high marks. As for George Lucas...True, he is a better producer than he is a director or writer but he is still a good movie magic maker, and John Williams still has the force when it comes to bringing the music of the film to life.

Over all I give Clones a strong B+

title: Attack of the Fanboys is more like it.
review:
All right, let me get this out of the way first. I LOVE Star Wars it is one of my favorite franchises of all time but, I'm not the stand in line for 386 hours, believe The Force is real type of fan. That said I'll now put my reputation and quite possibly my life on the line here. I LOVED Episode I!!! It had what this film is missing, that Star Wars feel. Lucas has always said that he made Star Wars for 13 year old boys. Episode I had that feeling. While, yes, I did find Jar Jar annoying, he was no worse or more distracting than the Ewoks from Return of the Jedi. The only true complaint I have with Episode I is Jake Lloyd, too hyperactive.

To me it just seems that Lucas has tried to silence all the fanboys, who are now in their 20's and beyond, I fit this age bracket yes, but again, I accept the films for what they are, fun action filled, corny dialogue, kids movies. The fanboys distracted Lucas from making his fun filled movies, to make a movie that is too heavy handed and loaded with WAY too many inside references. Chances are that half the audience that's now seeing this movie, are actually the 13 year olds that he intended, and they are lost because they may not have even seen the original trilogy. While the action was fast paced, more plentiful and awesome, the story itself was just lacking that mystical, magical, kiddy-movie feel that the other five films had. So, if any of the fanboys read this and are po'ed at me, or thought that the movie did suck, remeber, you only have yourself to blame.

title: Well, I can say this much
review: It was better than Lord of the Rings. There, I said it. Sacrilege? Nah, not in my view. I didn't have the patience to sit through LOTR (left after 50% of the movie), but time just flew by with this movie. But then, I'm a sci-fi buff. All that dungeon and dragons stuff I leave to the roleplaying geeks. Anakin has grown up now, and isn't the stuckup little brat that saved the day in the previous movie. Also, the almost total absence of Jar Jar was total bliss. It was also satisfying to see the plot thicken regarding Anakins fate. I give it 8 out of 10. Return of the Jedi still tops my list though. I anxiously await episode III.

title: Best Animated Film of the Year!
review:
I'm not really being a smartass when I say that "Episode II" could qualify as the best animated film of the year. I feel that one of its major flaws is that it has people at all! Honestly, pay attention to the parts with actual humans in them--the actors in Lucas' film stand out against their computer-created environments almost as obviously as the ones in "The Golden Voyage of Sinbad."

Well, maybe I'm being a little bit of a smartass by claiming "Episode II" could qualify as the year's best cartoon--the computer environments and animation really aren't even as convincing as those in "Stuart Little." This is mainly due to overkill--I mean, there wasn't a single "set" in the film that wasn't absolutely massive. Distractingly so. And when Lucas' characters are replaced, in long shots, by computer animated versions of themselves, they move in that unnaturally smooth, underwater way that computer-game characters do (also one of the few flaws in this year's "Spiderman"). This lack of "flesh actor time" is no huge loss, however--Hayden Christiansen and Christopher Lee give the only real performances in the movie, anyway.

On the positive side, even though the backgrounds are invariably busy and distractingly mammoth, the actual action taking place is wonderfully easy-to follow. Lucas' simple editing and framing, influenced by action serials of the 1930s and 40s is a refreshing change from the incomprehensible action sequences in recent action flicks like "Lara Croft: Tomb Raider." For the most part, Lucas just pulls back to a medium shot with the major participants in full view, and has them do their (often computerized) thing.

If only he could take a lesson from himself and simplify his epics instead of making them ever larger and more scattershot. He needs to pull in the reins on the FX department and concentrate making movies instead of big-screen, non-interactive videogames.

title: Poor title, great film
review:
Just about the only thing I didn't like about this film was the title.

I'm 38 so I've followed the series right from the start, and I'm pretty sure that after I've seen this film a few times it'll become my favourite. Yes, it's even better than "The Empire Strikes Back".

The film had a really good pace, much better than "Phantom Menace" where I remember checking my watch a few times in the cinema. I was quite surprised when it had finished, I thought there was still some time to go!

The effects have come on so far since the first trilogy that I'd be willing to bet my last shilling on Lucas re-vamping IV, V and VI again, otherwise they're going to look a bit clunky if watched in episode order. Perhaps then he'll finally release them on DVD.

I'm really surprised at some of the criticism aimed at the film. The acting is no worse (although admittedly no better) than IV, V or VI. Product placement seemed a bit more restrained, and there was some good humour in the film (C3PO aside).

The reason I like "Empire" is that it really fleshes out the mythos and the story, and "Clones" is fantastic for the same reason. The effects are mind-blowing too, but it needs the storyline to make the fight and chase scenes have any real meaning. This film has Yoda with a light sabre and an attitude, how could it possibly fail?

"Phantom Menace" really grew on me when I saw it a few times on DVD, and if this does the same then I think this will become THE classic Star Wars film.

Can't wait for part III.......

title: The Force is in neutral
review:
This is primarily a love story, and not a very good one! The clones don't really get involved until the bitter end. I know it's tough to do a sequel, but bigger and more don't cut it. The plot was thin, acting bad and there were no real villains.

George, go back to your original formula - it worked. Maybe episode three will have better characters, less computer design, a better plot, better acting, a real hero or two, and a bad guy we can all hate.

The action was ok, but there were too many participants. Even in the first three you didn't have thousands of soldiers.

I will probably go see episode three, but only to complete the cycle. Give it your best.

Had this been the first movie there wouldn't have been a sequel.

title: George, you did it again!
review: As someone who had seen Star Wars Eps.II 5 times already, I'd just like to say how much I enjoyed the movie. I think George Lucas did a wonderful job. He manages every time to produce a wonderful movie and have people go back multiple times to see it again! After seeing this one, I just can't wait 3 YEARS to see the 3rd and final eps. He also managed to get the 2 most perfect people to play Anakin and Padme'. I'd also like to say that John Williams did an awesome job with the music. The love theme was out of this world. He was able to make it hauntingly romantic and fill it with so much passion and emotion. I'd go back again just to hear the music in-person (and of course for the whole movie! lol) I also think that Natalie Portman and Hayden Christensen did a tremendous job. It always helps out the movie when the 2 most important characters (who are in-love) have...oh, what's the word...CHEMISTRY! (which they had ALOT of.) The two did beautifully! And for those few...very few people out there who maybe didn't like the story.... just the whole Yoda "fight" scene would be enough to get anyone to go back and see it again. I was very pleased with this movie and can't wait until it comes out to DVD.... I'd recommend this movie to anyone who has any taste whatsoever! Awesome MOVIE! :)

title: Lucas has made a Star Wars film for adults...
review: Star Wars Episode I was made for kids.  I firmly believe children will hate Episode II.  It is the anti-Phantom Menace, and not a kids' movie at all. It isn't action-heavy.  It has a lot of plot and dialogue, foreshadowing, and mystery to it...and romance (I fear more than a lot of people can stand).  ATTACK OF THE CLONES is quite a film.  From a technical standpoint it is superb (although I'm sure I prefer a puppet-Yoda to a CGI-Yoda).  It does have a few magnificent action scenes.  Its not what you'd call a "fun" movie, though.  The original 1977 STAR WARS ("Episode 4") film was fun, as was RETURN OF THE JEDI and THE PHANTOM MENACE.  ATTACK OF THE CLONES fits in better with EMPIRE STRIKES BACK, and is a very dark film.  (How this movie didn't get a PG-13 is a mystery up there with the Kennedy Assassination and Jack the Ripper.)  It has doses of humor, action, and fun, but those elements are overshadowed by the suspense and mystery of it.  If you go into the film with that mindset, you'll enjoy yourself and be quite pleased with ATTACK OF THE CLONES.  If you're expecting another Episode 4, you'll be disappointed.

title: I liked the Second of 6 Star Wars Movies
review: I have heard a lot of negative things about Star Wars Episode 2, and I frankly don't think that the reviews I have read have come from die hard Star Wars fans. I myself am not a die hard Star Wars fan, but I loved this movie more then anything else that has been released thus far other hen Spiderman! I will admit that it was a little slow in the begining, but giving what the meaning of what the story tried to tell people it was well done. And I don't think that it is fair to compare in great detail the stars of 4,5,6 to the stars of 1,2,3. If u like Star Wars in any way, please go and give this movie a chance, please don't go by the reviewers. Thanks :)

title: Lucas needs to let go
review:
He has shown again with Episode II that he can't handle both producing and directing these pictures. I'm guessing that he's concentrating too much on perfecting the look of the scenes to be able to concentrate on creating a captivating story and script which ties us in emotionally to the characters.

I'm not a hard to please moviegoer. I can forgive the occasional plot hole and bad acting as long as I'm emotionally drawn to the character. This was the main difference between Episodes 4-6 and the prequels. In the original episodes, I was totally rooting for Han, Luke, and Leia to kick some ass. When Lando betrayed Han and Leia, I was thinking, "What a b**tard!" In the new prequels, I was just watching the characters on the screen doing stuff and I wasn't that interested in whether they prevailed or not.

You'll notice that Lucas let others direct Empire and Jedi, perhaps because he knew that making those films would be such a monumental undertaking that he wouldn't be able to both produce and direct them. They both maintained the fun and emotional investment in the characters as Star Wars. Hopefully, he can do the same for Episode III so that he can at least end the series with a bang.

title: well done!
review:
A lot of bad things have been said about George Lucas following the mildly annoying Star Wars Episode I. Two of them are definitely not true: That he doesn't listen to critics and that he `has lost it'.

Honestly, I did not expect much from Episode II. I hoped for a state of the art display of CG which was not so obnoxious you would want to turn away. But I was pleasantly surprised already a few minutes into the film. There was a lot of CG, but not just for the fun of it. The atmosphere was dense and gloomy and as the plot unraveled, there was a real sense of danger and, almost too good to be true for the action movie it basically is, it actually started developing some depth. The force is no more an infectious disease and Jedi are finally something more than well coreographed martial artists. There was a mystical undercurrent, brilliantly displayed by Joda in two very different pivotal scenes. There is the overall sense of corruption and doom, a very well done hierarchy among the Jedi and finally a really interesting geneology of people to play a role in the original Star Wars.

Also the characterization and acting was quite good overall. I even found the love story well done. It was so ridiculous and juvenile - if by accident or by design - that it provides a firm background for Anakin to be thrown onto the dark side, as it inevitably has to come.

Some things could of course have been done better. Obi-Wan for example was a little too weak and uncharismatic in my opinion to make Anakins rebellion against him believable. And, if queens are elected on Naboo, do they really vote for one that is a mere 16 years old? But these are minor glitches that do not substantially undermine the general soundness of the plot and characters.

On the technical side I liked the action sequences a lot. In contrast to the now usual action fare, they are not cut in the 2-second pieces that make you want to throw up after a minute. They actually allow you to follow what is going on to a large extent and, although quite frequent, they do not cut the movie into disconnected pieces. And, what is really nice, they are lacking the totally unbelievable two-people-against-a-whole-army-scenes.

And finally, there is one little detail that I almost admire Lucas for: He managed to dispose of obnoxious Jar-Jar Binks in a fashion, that both his fans and opponents will approve: He is there in the movie, but he is not only told to shut up once, but, as it turns out, he is the one formally responsible for the death of the republic and the creation of the empire!

Overall, I really liked this movie and even a little more. George Lucas has grown up - and that is meant as a compliment. Back in 1977 the now `Episode 4' seems to have hit the nerve of that time. For me at least it seems, that Episode 2 has done that again.
