review:
They did it. This is the best of the series.

The critics are looking to recapture the thrill of Star Wars. Star Wars was so unique in 1977. It was a spectacle. If it were released today it would not do as well. The audience has become more sophisticated and expectant. Lucas Films delivered. Can't wait for Episode III.

title: A new low (SPOILERS)
review:
Awesome, spectacular, fantastic! The special effects were breathtaking and the fight scenes were incredible! And now for the other two thirds of the movie.

What a piece of crap! Hayden Christenson should go back to hockey. The only thing worse than his acting was the idiotic dialogue. Particularly his. I'd rather watch Jar Jar and Yoda have sex for an hour and a half than this drivel. Endless amounts of poorly conceived, glib repartee, mercilessly interrupted by frequent thousand foot leaps from speeding hover cars (with just in time rescues from certain death) and so many light saber battles that my eyes are still seeing flashes of blue, green, and red (oh yeah, and Mace's purple helmeted warrior - I mean light saber).

The whole romance thing between Anakin and Padme had me cringing and saying "yeesh" more times than I could count. The part where he talks about how sand is rough or something and that she was soft and smooth was one of his better lines, if you can believe that! Her confession of love for him just about made me puke. I hope I can forget it.

C3PO gets his head chopped off. Miraculously, he stumbles into a conveniently empty space in a robot assembly line and his body gets a new head while his head, again miraculously, gets a new body. Geez! Talk about suspension of disbelief! Later, R2D2 takes his head and drags it back to his body. C3PO says, "what a drag" - groan! Then, when his head is lying next to his body, he says "I feel quite beside myself". What the...?

Other brilliant lines included "I hate it when he does that" and the clever variation "You know I hate it when you do that". Or how about the oft repeated "I've got a bad feeling about this" or the frequent references to Obi-Wan's hatred of flying. I'll go out on a limb and say that there was better acting and dialogue in Hercules in New York.

Obi-Wan constantly demeans Anakin and Anakin constantly acts like a complete jerk.

Jango Fett was pretty cool and I liked the big battle with all of the Jedi. Count Dooku (Saruman) was pretty nifty too. What makes the whole movie worth the price of admission is Dooku's fight with Yoda. Man, that was one of the funniest things I've ever seen! This little muppet whipping back and forth, twirling through the air was comedic genius!

I'll be generous and attribute special effects and fighting to 40% of the movie. I'll give it a 4 out of 4 here. As for the rest, somewhere between a 1 and a 2 out of 6 for a total of 5 or 6 out of 10 (I'm pretty easy on movies). I actually think this might not be better than TPM. AOTC was both fantastic, in some aspects, and utter crap in others.

title: I tried to be objective....
review:
I viewed this film with a critical eye, I tried to be objective, but I couldn't for the life of me understand the criticism this film has received. I tried to hate Hayden Christiansen's performance, I tried to hate the bad dialogue, I even tried to hate that space water horse Jar Jar Binks but I couldn't. Aside from a few laughable moments I was completely satisfied with every aspect of Attack of the Clones.

I am 28 years old; those 3 films define my early childhood. I am not a raving Star Wars Freak, I may watch the films, including The Phantom Menace about 3 or 4 times a year but I would not wait in line for more than an hour to see any of them. My favorite one of course is Empire, but there is definitely a soft spot for A New Hope and without the ewoks and the labored acting by Harrison Ford (especially on Endor) Return of the Jedi has a flawless ending. I love the story, I love the characters and I couldn't wait for the prequels to be made.

Well, The Phantom Menace was released and I could sense a difference. I didn't hate the film like a lot of people but I could tell that for the most part it didn't feel like Star Wars, too much babyish add ons and stilted dialogue and of course that sea horse Jar Jar. I did however understand the reasons why. I knew that the next one would get more into the meat of the story and it does. Its disappointing to think that some critics and viewers just looked at the acting and dialogue which really wasn't that bad at all and I would even go so far as to say that as clichÃ©d it was it was pretty damn good for a Star Wars film. The acting was also just as good as the originals, because, what is the real draw is the story the world Lucas has created the characters and why things are the way they are in episodes 4,5 and 6. I loved the chess game being played in Attack of the Clones and watching it made me like The Phantom Menace even more.

I also loved the little hints of what type of guy Anakin is, he is ruled by his emotions and he feeds off them. My favorite part was after wiping out the Tusken campsite he is talking to Padme about his frustrations with OBI WAN when he reveals to her what he did. This worked very well and it made more of an impact, on me anyway, having him speak of the slaughter rather than showing it. I think Hayden is great as Anakin, and I think there is chemistry between him and Padme which leads me to Natalie Portman who is so hot, I mean that face and her acting is way better than some would have you believe. The comparison to Carrie Fisher is imminent but they are both quite different yet very much the same, if that makes sense. The characters are similar but the motivations are different and both are great, I love Leia's no bulls*** attitude and she is pretty sexy but I am absolutely in love with Portman can't wait to see what happens to Padme and Anakin.

Now for Ewen Mcgregor and his performance. George Lucas with the help of Alec Guiness has created one of the most interesting characters in this genre of filmmaking, Obi Wan Kenobi. In The Phantom Menace Ewen wasn't given much to do except wait around and follow Liam's lead, until the final light sabre battle with Darth Maul and there you get a glimpse of where Ewen Mcgregor is going to take this character. Well, in Attack of the Clones Ewen becomes Kenobi, he is phenomenal! I just wish there was more, but I guess I will have to wait for Episode III. His moment with Yoda discussing the missing planet Kamino is great along with the banter between him and Anakin. The bar scene is great too, Kenobi going to get a drink and then using the jedi mind trick on a weak minded drug dealer, priceless. I have always been a big fan of Ewen Mcgregor and knew he was perfect to play a young Obi Wan and boy was I right.

Yoda, as everyone has noted, kicks ass. This is a unanimous feeling whether you loved the film, thought it was all right or hated it, everyone agrees Yoda kicks mother****in' ass. He is the master, how do you fight something like that. I guess that's why Dooku just says f*** this and gets the hell out of there. I can't wait to find out why he ends up in the Dagoba system. Mace Windu is pretty awesome too; his take out of Jango Fett is great. Some people thought it was too quick, but, s***, he is second to Yoda on the Jedi Council so some bounty hunter is not going to put up too much of a fight. Which leads me to Jango, I loved seeing what that mandalorian suit can do and having temuerison play him was awesome, too bad he didn't last too long.

Finally, Dooku, Sidious and clones. Christopher Lee is brilliant this guy plays the best villain. Every moment with him shines, his little game with Obi Wan, his duel with Obi Wan, Anakin and then Yoda, his calm escape riding that speeder bike and that little look he gives when his right hand man Jango gets decapitated, Christopher Lee ROCKS! Palpatine/Sidious is not featured as much this time but Mcdierrmond is still great, I liked the little passive aggressive approach to getting Jar Jar to propose the full power bill to the senate.

Now for the special effects. I didn't see this in a digital format but it still was great, the speeder chase through Curascant was thrilling, the kamino stuff was visually stunning, except the waves, they looked pretty fake. Obi Wans chase of the Slave 1 through an asteroid field was very well done especially the seismic bursts, the sound was very original. The introduction to Geonosis was a little video gamey but I was glued to the action, I loved the design of the Geonesians and the arena monsters where pretty fun especially that cat thing, it was actually pretty freaky looking. The battle itself was awesome although it did look at times like a playstation role playing game, especially when they showed all the Jedi Fighting, some of them just looked stupid. I don't understand why no two jedi can look the same. One looks like a tiger man, another looks like whoopee Goldberg the next one looks like the Quaker oats dude and some Asian squid head. Anyway the worst CGI offense was Anakin riding some fat cow thingy in the fields of Naboo, that was terrible.

Aside from those poorly done effects, here some other aspects of the things that just didn't quite do it for me. C3P0, his accidental inscription into the arena battle was stupid as hell. Anakins nightmare caused quite a burst of laughter in the audience and a couple of long speeches by him induced some major groans. That's about it, oh yeah a couple of scenes where a character would seem incapacitated one moment and then all of a sudden jump up and be alright, not to mention that fat jedi that couldn't get into the gun ship without a helping hand.

Overall I absolutely loved Attack of the Clones and definitely can't wait for Episode III.

title: The movie's OVER-WHELMING imagination makes it worth!
review:
This is a very un-equilibrated movie. Scenes of UNSPEAKABLE beauty and imagination are followed by scenes of acting that is average at best. I gave the movie a 9 without a regret because of its imagination and also because of its action scenes.

The script is average/decent and did not manage to ruin the beauty of the images, which the acting did in some cases. The love story is made up of NOTHING but cliches (and bad ones!) and the acting of the others is rarely average (most of the times, is under average). Humour is as good as inexistent (except for a line or two).

But most of this loses in relevance as to the overall quality when put together with the INCREDIBLE imagination present in just about every picture of this movie. The worlds created here are like nothing you've ever seen (even in Phantom Menace) or you're likely to see anytime soon (except, hopefully, in 2005, in Episode III). There are so many of such worlds, each of them both different from the others and incredibly rich in details, that the feeling is that you are overwhelmed. I will see this movie again and again, bearing the parts of awful acting, just so that I can be "exposed" to the overflowing imagination of this movie, so that I can see new things. Pictures that can make up poster one could watch for hours and not have enough are here present for just a few minutes... and such pictures are by the dozens. This is truly an UNIQUE film.

And, of course, one must not forget sounds. The music is excellent, and re-interprets the music theme of Phantom Menace (remember the fights towards the end of the movie...). But the sounds of the movie manage to suprise even a StarWars fan, accustomed to the imperial fighters and lightsabers from the first trilogy. Bombs explode in space with sounds like you've never heard (no more average booom! explosions), light sabers please the ear once again and so on...)

Unfortunately, what could have been a truly genius movie is drawn back by the acting. Without the slightest intention of making a joke, Yoda has been, by far, the best actor in this movie, followed by Ewan McGregor (who does a decent job) and Samuel Jackson (average). Otherwise, plain awful...

In short, you want acting and story... rent "Ladri di biciclette". You want imagination BEYOND ANY DREAMS YOU EVER HAD and andrenaline rush action... go see Attack of the Clones. Again and again and again...

title: Better than TPM and Jedi, almost as good as Empire
review:
This movie succeeds in every way that The Phantom Menance failed. The story is more cohesive and compelling and the performances are uniformly better (Samuel L. Jackson especially redeems himself after his terrible cameo in episode 1).

I had feared that Hayden Christensen would be an absolute zero as Akakin, but I was wrong (Lucas must have chosen all of his worst moments from the film for the trailer). Natalie Portman and Ewan McGregor finally get to show at least some of their considerable acting chops. Horror movie legend Christopher Lee looks like he's having a blast in his role as Count Dooku.

None of these performances are going to start any Oscar buzz but they are more than acceptable for this type of movie. People who view the first trilogy through rose-colored glasses often forget that neither Mark Hamill nor Carrie Fisher were grand masters of the thespian arts.

Some have panned the romantic dialog as sophomoric and awkward, but even at its worst, it never descends to the depths found in Jedi ("I have it... my sister ... has it."). I was less troubled by the sometimes purple prose than I was by the occasional uses of American slang. It wasn't often, but when it happened, I was briefly jarred out of my suspension of disbelief.

Making a welcome return to Star Wars universe is a sense of humor. I mean real humor, not forced, unfunny Jar-Jar slapstick but character-driven dialog humor. What little physical humor there is in AOTC is at the expense of C-3P0 (as it should be in a Star Wars movie).

The effects are uniformly a step ahead of Phantom Menance. The final battle scene is just plain spectacular. Yoda's fight scene (I won't say more) is a sight to behold, getting the biggest cheers from the audience.

After the Phantom Menace, I was only mildly enthused about the release of AOTC. After Episode II, however, 2005 can't come soon enough.

title: I love it when a plan comes together.
review:
Just saw ATOC at Disney Downtown at the weekend. We saw it on DLP, instead of 35mm. Looked and sounded great. The movie was a heck of a lot better than TPM.

The main plot is good, ... after all its like real history to some people, but the love story lacks everything. The acting made me feel, that we all should apply for lead roles in the final movie cause George Lucas doesn't know good acting if it slapped him in the face, fortunately though he does know about a good story and special effects.

I can't wait for the final movie, but I still feel that Lord of the Rings has the edge, more film magic and wonder.

C Lee is good as always, Ewan M takes us through the story and keeps us awake while Anny (still a brat, just taller) and Amidala (who falls in love the instant she thinks she might possibly die, now that's romance!) play doctors and nurses like two elementary school kids.

How Boba Fett came into being though is very cool. Samuel L J ..... is Samuel L J ... one CMF

Senator Palpatines master plan though is everything to this movie, .... I love it when a plan comes together.

R2D2 and C3PO provide humour like Jar Jar never could. And Joda, well I've not laughed so hard in quite a while, its pure genius, like Kermit on Ecstasy.

From the moment it feels we've just entered a scene from Gladiator this movie just keeps getting better. Unfortunately of course that's over half way in, but worth the wait nonetheless.

Hope you all enjoy it too.

title: Acceptable...***Possible Spoilers***
review:
I had hoped to see the movie again before I tried writing a review, as I generally like to do, but I found the desire too great to deter myself any longer.

First of all, I thought the movie was okay. There are many people who are up in arms about the loose ends that seem to have no real connection to the original movies, but what we have to keep in mind is that there is still another film before we finally catch up to Star Wars, Episode IV.

I was pleased with Yoda's fight, quite pleased. In the words of a friend of mine, "I was waiting to see why Yoda is the 'all-powerful' Jedi. His fight kicked a$$! Show some respect, Bee-otch"! I have to agree. For a little guy, he certainly can move!

Secondly, I thought the chemistry between Natalie Portman and Hayden Chrsitiansen was fairly good. I mean, it was along the same level as Laia and Hans, almost...it's difficult to compare.

I did feel that the movie encompassed the essence of Star Wars, as did Episode I, once you get past all the blunders, such as Jar-Jar Binks.

Continuing on, all they need do is cut him out of the first movie, and none of this crap would have happened! Hahaha... (If that doesn't make sense, see the movie, and you'll know).

And, I must mention the car scene. I know people have been raising Hell over this scene, but when you try to compare this to the original three movies, it was a necessary sequence. Think about it...the original movies had space ships zooming all over the screen, and the models they used then CAN be compared to the digital age in which we now find ourselves. It also showed us how crowed Corosant has become.

There is one scene I think should be eliminated. The scene reminiscent of "The Sound of Music". I think there is even a musical trill from the movie itself wedged in there! Nasty...

Overall though, I liked the film, and will likely see it again before it leaves theaters.

I rate it an 8/10.

title: Attack of the Senses
review:
The movie is worth seeing mostly for the effects and to be prepared for what I hope to be an improved Episode III. However, Lucas really stumbled here. This should have been a character movie. This is the centerpiece of a trilogy concerning the rise the good, Anarkin Skywalker, and his fall into evil, Darth Vader, one of the movies greatest bad guys of all time. This is the movie where we should have learned along with Amidala to love Anarkin. That would make his fall, that much more personal and involving. He's not really very lovable here. Hayden Christensen does the best that he can, but he's just not right. We needed a cross between Errol Flynn and James Dean, a swashbuckling hero with a hidden inner angst. We don't get that, and that's a shame.

Luckily, Lucas still has a great feeling for special effects. It's here that the movie shines and keeps people in the seats. We all want to see a glimpse of the 'future' that Lucas continues to create. The detail and completeness of the dynamic backgrounds is definitely worthy of praise. However, the special effects end up being more believable than the actors or the story. The pace is quite fast, but seems more rushed than action packed. I think that is mostly due to the difficulty in relating to the heroes.

Anarkin's arrogance, which will obviously be part of his movement to the darkside, is not at all appealing. He's petulant, moody and really too good-looking to be a believable action hero. This combination of preening good looks, and whiny attitude makes him difficult to identify with.

I couldn't understand why Amidala even likes him, much less falls in love with him. His early meetings with her after a 10 year lapse were either trying to countermand her decisions, or complaining how Obi Wan doesn't appreciate him. Is she really a closet Jedi groupie?

Maybe she's just not very smart. My opinion of her, and anyone who helped to make her a planet representative, fell as low as it could go, as soon as she passed her senatorial duties to Jar Jar Binks in her absence. Huh? Wouldn't that type of decision be reason enough for impeachment? Jar Jar's character is used like an old pair of shoes by Palpatine and is, thankfully, barely seen again.

Obi Wan is also hard to relate to here. His character, which was in my opinion the most appealing in Episode I, seems out of place in II. He's just not as engaging playing the mentor as he was playing the Padawan. He comes off as cool and patronizing, showing very little emotional range as a character.

Who else can we cheer for? As mentioned above, the big three are whiny, unbelievably dumb and one-dimensional. Who else is there? The Jedi Council? Please. By their own admission they are getting weak and disjointed. Yoda? His action sequence is entertaining but also a bit unbelievable. He comes in and out of the scene obviously relying on his crutch. Between the beginning and the end of that scene, he has more power and ability than anyone else in the movie. Come on, who's he fooling. Us?

I looked forward to Episode II with high expectations, hoping that the feedback from Episode I would help to bring the series closer to its roots. Sadly, instead of moving back toward simple stories where a few intrinsically good individuals hesitantly make brave contributions toward the betterment of galactic society, we get a morass of convoluted politics, a forced no sparks romance, and an endless exposition of unendearing heroes taking unthinkable risks.

title: Lord of the clones
review:
Episode II is, as could be expected, an example of how far Lucas and ILM have taken special effects and computer animation. But it's also an example of how much you lose if you are too focused on and impressed by visual effects. And it's sad, because the story behind Attack Of The Clones is actually quite good. We have the young soon-to-be-intergalactic-lord-of-darkness Anakin Skywalker, who is trapped between his jedi training, `the woman he loves' and the desire to go back to his home planet and save his enslaved mother. And we have the political disturbance in the republic, with the deceiving Palpatin pulling the strings, and a bunch of very distressed jedi-masters pondering and wondering.

But all of this is just not working as it should... or as good as it could anyway. First of all: Anakin's character lacks development. All the way through he just appears as a frustrated teenage boy, with a grudge against his master, and this makes him and also his interaction with the other characters quite unbelievable. Especially the love affair with princess Amadela seems contrived.

Then we have the whole part with the jedies, and most of all the jedies fighting! A part of the movie I really looked forward to. And it does look extremely great when fifty jedi-knights light up their sabres and come the rescue. And Christopher Lee is quite good as the renegade jedi-master Dokuu, although he plays exactly the same role as in Lord Of the Rings, just with a shorter beard and a light sabre instead of a magic wand. But that just completes the circle, because the original Star Wars movie also had a lot of elements from Tolkien's novel. And in general Episode II: Attack Of The Clones HAS borrowed quite a lot from other films, although I doubt that there is self ironic joke in the title.

So. to sum up: The new Star Wars chapter is a beautifully made adventure movie, better than Episode I, but it lacks some essential storytelling elements and actor directing, which could have saved a lot. But worst of all, and a lesson for future Star Wars films: Thou shall not have Yoda fighting with a light sabre! Imagine a frog on speed with long green ears and a glowing green stick, flying around Christopher Lee, while making Darth Maul moves.

Anyway. It's Star Wars, so you have a tendency to accept more, than you would with other films. At least that's how I feel...

title: Technically Perfect but Poorly Plotted
review:
I will certainly admit that this film's special effects and cinematography are nearly flawless; however, I cannot say the same about the plot and dialogue. The plot is dry, predictable, and damn nearly juvenile (the whole thing plays out like a Saturday morning cartoon).

The movie lacks importance: the film's lack of interconnectedness, character development, and good dialogue are really just symptoms of this: We have no grand moral conflicts, no clashes between duty and self-interest(would Yoda, for example, allow himself to use clones just because his friends are at risk?), between good and evil (the evil characters in the first films seemed motivated by a need for order; here they are evil just because the good guys need somebody to fight with), or between love and hate [the abduction of Anakin's mother and the subsequent slaughter of the sand people border on this kind of importance, but they fall before hitting the mark]. Consequently, the events of the plot seem only loosely related; there is no sense in the air that a great catastrophe is building (compare this with say empire where we get the sense that Luke's undisciplined, irrational love of his friends may lead him into darkness). The movie is all exposition followed by an obligatory special effects/action sequence. The film simply lacks intensity---the true intensity that is the product of rising tension and good character development. Even the Anakin character (who ought to be fascinating as he is Darth Vader, one of the most ominous movie characters of all time) seems dull. The other characters hardly exist. This is natural given this film's lack of relevance; why should we care about characters whose actions and words do not speak to the struggles in our own lives? Why should we care about this film?

title: Yes, it *IS* as bad as "Phantom Menace"
review:
Everyone currently talking about how much better Part II is than Part I are going to experience a tremendous *POP* in a few months, as their heads come out of their asses and they realize how they've fooled themselves.

Cast your mind back to "Phantom Menace," and remember the wishy-washy way everyone was talking about the wonderful images and effects, and trying not to focus too much on Jar-Jar, Jake Lloyd, and the god-awful script. It took a few months before a consensus was suddenly achieved that hey, it really was bad. No one wanted to believe it.

Well, the same thing is happening again, with far less excuse.

Yes, it has some cool moments, particularly towards the end (and Christopher Lee, I'll give you, is awesome)--but this movie SUCKS. Sucks sucks sucks suck sucks. Sucks like a Hoover. Has high levels of ambient suckiosity. Stop trying to convince yourself it's good--you've been taken for your ticket price, and you might as well admit to it.

Yes, there is less Jar-Jar, but we have the Padme/Anakin love story to take it's place. Yes, we don't have an unconvincing child as the hero, but instead we get a whiny, self-pitying adolescent. (I'm undecided as to whether Hayden Christiansen is a terrible actor; he was given a part that Olivier couldn't have played.)

By the time you start get the big action scenes, towards the end, it is impossible to care about the characters. For the first hour and a half the movie is boring and forgettable, except for the few scenes that are so dire they become unintentionally funny, and memorable for all the wrong reasons.

When Anakin, in an overheated moment, tells Padme that he loves her so much he's "in agony," someone in the audience with me muttered, "So am I."

This is a film that cries out for two robots and an astronaut down in the right corner, making wisecracks as it spools out.

The acting was a wonderful improvement over its predecessor, and Hayden Christensen stole the show.  I was captivated by his portrayal of a man teetering on the edge.  But all the characters, not just Anakin, seemed more real this time around.  The story is much more emotionally charged in Attack of the Clones, and the film itself is an action movie, love story, whodunnit mystery and a story of deep personal conflict all rolled into one.  The special effects are fantastic, it being a Lucas joint and all, but what makes this film such a marked improvement over The Phantom Menace is that the storyline, not the CGI, really drives the film.  This movie offers something for everyone of all ages and is well worth the price admission (several times, at that).  Its only drawback is that now I have to wait ANOTHER three long years to find out how the whole story comes to a close.

title: An expected disappointment, but with some upsides.
review:
Like many others worldwide, I went to see Episode II on its pre-premier here in Israel. Remembering the burning disappointment from Episode I, I went with a pessimistic approach. This was almost a week ago, and only after much contemplation with myself and my friends, have I managed to establish an opinion on what the movie succeeded, and failed, in doing, at least for me.

The Clone Wars is quite an improvement from Episode I, which I consider a true flop and a disgrace to the Star Wars saga. But I do not intend to discuss the first movie here, only for comparison where needed.

It is clear that Lucas learned from some of his mistakes and went on to create a movie that is much more reminiscent of the old Trilogy. The movie feels a lot closer to the Trilogy we all loved, using many elements and methods that fit this forgotten style. There was great attention to detail in most plot-elements, greatly reducing the number of plot-holes seen regularly in Episode I. The world created in this movie feels true, and behaves as one would expect. However, I cannot say as much for the characters in this movie. Allow me to elaborate:

I am an actor myself, and one of the first things that I understand is taught in any acting and directing school is that actions must always be justified. Any movie- or theater-goer automatically tries to find a logical explanation for the events that take place in a movie or play, because this is our human nature. However unreasonable an action is, if the character has a good reason to do it (no matter how bizarre), then the action immediately becomes believable, or at least acceptable, by the viewer. In this way, the viewer can relate to what goes on.

I have great respect for many, if not all of the actors that participated in "The Clone Wars", and have in the past admired their great skills in other movies. Sadly, in this movie most of the actors failed to come up with any motivation for their actions, any justification, and to me they give the feeling that acting scenes were made hastily, or that little or no work was done by the actors to ensure that their characters hold a steady and logical line of thought and action throughout the film. This phenomenon appears in most acting parts of the movie, noticeably so in the romantic scenes between Anakin and Padme, which appear to have been literally FORCED on the actors. They simply show no emotion to each other, and the resulting romantic interludes appear foney and tacky. The melodramatic music and gorgeous scenery (indeed!) and sets used in these scenes can barely make up for the loss of tension between the characters.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying that the actors have gone sour! I'm simply suggesting that there might have been a lack of time spent on understanding WHY the characters do what they do. The computer-animate characters, like Yoda and Watto displayed much more acting skill, in my opinion, than their flesh-and-blood colleagues.

George Lucas may have noticed this problem. Weather he did or did not, an awful lot of money and work was directed at the digitally-created CG scenes, which were spectacular and colossal in any scale. However, special-effects, no matter how grandiose, cannot constitute an entire movie. While watching the film, I had a strong feeling that Lucas was trying to IMPRESS me... The sheer amount of special-effects scenes was astonishing, but to me it seemed to mask the fact that very little attention was given to the problem I described above.

Again, most of the FX scenes were mind-blowing, including the hovercar chase, the Jedi-to-droid fight in the arena, and of course the Yoda-Lightsaber-Fighting scene which clearly showed how state-of-the-art computer graphics can create magic like never before. Sadly, as I've already stated, even all these scenes combined together cannot begin to compensate for the lack of a believable chain-of-events, that seem to "trigger" suddenly out of thin air without any reasonably explanation.

To sum it all up, I think that George Lucas has made a positive step forward to achieving another brilliant picture that comes close to the Trilogy, but he has to drop the notion that Special Effects are more powerful than an ensuing plot, and the magic that happens between characters. I think the film was targeted to a young audience, much like the Trilogy movies, but gave them format instead of contents. "A New Hope" won the affection of millions worldwide by telling a fantastic story, not by its toy-model animations, even if they appeared futuristic at the time. If he can come to understand this, perhaps George Lucas may turn the third film in the series into a hit that may match or surpass the greatness of the previous films.

Oh yeah, and R2D2 CAN FLY? HUH?!?

title: Better than Episode I, but still disappointing
review:
At first: I'm a great fan of the old Star Wars trilogy. "Return of the Jedi" was my second movie ever seen after "Jungle Book" and it made me a real SciFi-Freak. Ok, now let's take a look at Episode II: It is really much, much more better than that Kiddie-Style Episode I !!! It has a lot more of the elemts that made the old trilogy that famous and great it is: Great Battles, extraordinary creatures, a basicly much more dark mood than Episode I.

But: Remember the Millenium Falcon, elegantly swinging around asteroids, pursuited by some Tie-Fighters in Episode V... 20 Years old and still stunning. In Episode II we have the same scene, but even (or because) they increased the speed and added missiles, it looks like a video clip or game. No elegance, just effects.

Remember that great idears of George Lukas in past: A spaceship, so huge it looks like a moon. Topped by the idear to fly in it an destroy its core. AT-AT Walkers and to kill them by twisting their legs with wires.

And now ? Flying cars like in "Fifth Element". Creatures copied out of "Starship Troopers", "Harry Potter" and "Lord of the Rings" An arena fight inspired by "Gladiator" And an Yoda, fighting like in Matrix or Chackie Chan Movies. It was so dishonoring... just made to please teenagers, with no respect to the fans and the venerable old Yoda.

The same Teenie-Thing with the dialogs. Dialogs have never been the strength of Star Wars movies. But they always were short and most time seriously and that was okay. Now we have to suffer awkward things like "I hate, when he's doing that". (That was the German translation of Obi-Wan, after Anakin jumped out of the car - don't know if it's the same in English) Whatever, that has the level of B-Movies or of series like "A-Team".

But the worst thing: casting and directing of the actors.

It's Lukas basic mistake still to be unintersted in his actors (This is his own opinion): Ewan McGregor, boring like he always was, trying to be as wise and charming than the old Obi-Wan with no change to reach his level.

Hayden Christensen, boring too, with no charisma, no depth, no one likes that guy, he's just arrogant. Why should Amidala fall in love with him ?

Now the talented ones: Remember Natalie Portmans stunning performance in "Leon - The Professional" - and that was years ago when she was a little girl... what a waste. I guess a good director would have led this unexperienced actress to an outstanding performance. Christopher Lee: Looks like a neewbie, if he never played the great roles of "Dracula" or Saruman in "LotR". Samuel L. Jackson, the unbeatened Mr. Cool: No chance for him to develop his strength because of the missing depth of his character.

And than this love story... (I guess Lukas revenge to the lack of understanding of the fans for Jar-Jar Binks) So mediocre, so trashy, so unimotional, so cold.

No one awaited a love story like in Braveheart or Casablanca. But compare with Han and Leia. They were funny, playing with each other the old cat and mouse game. Solo the charming warhorse and Leia the tough but sweet Princess. So simple but so effective. Everybody knew why they loved each other, even they never told us really. Has anybody an idea why Anakin loves Amidala ? Or why Amidala is falling in love with Anakin ? ...I don't know and i couldn't see or feel why.

Once upon a time, in a galaxy far far away.... there was an director, fulfilling his dreams and the dreams of his small but fast growing fan community. Now he only lines his pockets, by creating 100-million commercial spots with only one goal: maximize the target group.

title: Gets better the more you watch it!
review:

title: What everyone said... but better. grin.
review:
I had a look at other comments and critics opinions on Episode 2. THe general consensus seemed to be: - Visually Amazing. - Crummy Dialogue leading to wooden performances. - Better then Episode 1. Everyone seemed to agree on this, no matter what final score they gave the film.

So i wandered along, with fairly low expectations after ep1, and I have to say that all the comments above are perfectly true... 8.5/10.

TO SUM IT UP: on the way out of the cinema my mate asked me "what are you grinning about?". i couldn't answer, just mutter something about "film" and "yoda". I was still grinning when i got home. What more recommendation could you want?

spoilers may follow:

Visuals: Some of these are stunning... but better than that, they are artistic. I got the impression that episode 1 was just trying to show off what it could do... but episode 2 has much more interesting shots, such as the droids vs clones in a cloud of dust, and the final saber battle in only the light of the sabers.

Dialogue: Much better than i was expecting. Not as dire as Ep1, and without any of the stupid sounding americanisms ("Yippee!", "are you braindead?", sports commentators). But it is still pretty clunky in places, allthough i like jonathan, his shakespeare type backgroud isn't really what is needed to counter georges lack of feel for dialogue. They need someone with a flair for sparky interplay (like the leia/han stuff in the originals) like Joss Whedon or Shane Black. A compromise between their styles and Lucas' would be about the right feel.

Characters: Anakin came across as a spoilt, whining kid for the 1st half of the show, but as soon as they headed for tatooine he picked up and really started to be the sort of interesting, emotional, torn character that i was expecting. Ob1 came across as being a bit to stern and overcritical about anakin, and fairly uncharismatic. Natalie portman was much more interesting in this one, as we actually got to see a bit of her personality... she still needs a bit more of leia's cockiness, but she is getting there. Samual L. Jackson was wooden as hell. Looked bored. Jar Jar is cut down to size, but i liked the fact they gave him a pivotal role. Christopher Lee was cool as always, but the film is stolen by Yoda. Between them Frank Oz and ILM's character is by far the best acted, most charismatic and most interesting character in the film. It must say something about Lucas that he can only really get a great character out of a digital effect. Yoda in the school room "lost a plant, obi-wan has, how embarassing" and in his final fight make the film worth watching on it's own.

Plot and pacing: On the whole the plot is pretty good, more epic, dark and ambiguous than episode 1 (which didn't really have a plot). George never explained about disappearing jedi (which he promised!), and he forgot about all the annoying stuff from ep1 (immaculate conception, midichlorians etc...). The main problem i had with the film was the INTERCUTTING OF THE OB1 AND ANAKIN PLOTS and their effect on the pacing. Too often we were just getting to a good bit in one, then we were cut over to the other. ANd to often we cut from a dramatic ob1 scene to a romantic ani scene. Or just as we were feeling the anger and grief of anakin, we cut to the other side of the galaxy. Personally, if i could have made one change it would have been to cut out naboo altogether (anakin suddenly running off to tatooine felt false) and had anakin hide padme on tatooine from the start. It would have made more plot sense and been less jarring in the cuts. Also, ob1 turning down dooku straight felt wrong... at that point dooku sounds like he has a point, trying to save the senate from sidious. The political statements are as subtle as a sledgehammer and lead to some of the most cheesy and boring parts of the film ("the moment we stop believing in democracy is the moment we loose it!" etc..). I think we could have got the point on our own george.

Better than Episode 1: YES, in every way. Almost as good as return of the jedi in fact (better because of the darker tone, not as good because i can't care as much about the characters, and x-wings, tie fighters and the millenium falcon are still cooler than droids and the ships in ep2, no matter how cool they look)

title: If only the humans were animated!
review:
Awesome FX! The humans were stiff and the dialog was flat. How many hairdos can Padme have in how many scenes? Even the over actor (Samuel Jackson) was stiff.

The computer generated characters and action saved the day.

The big picture story was adequately told, but the sub-plots and character development stunk big time.

title: enjoyable,but christensen was terrible
review: I saw Star Wars episode II last night on digital projection and it looked unbelievable. I had a good time,but I think Lucas needs to bring in another writer for the next episode if not for the fact that the dialogue especially between anakin and padme was stiff and wooden. Christensen was terrible and not convincing as the arrogant young jedi. But I think a lot of the problem was he was miscast. Joaquin Phoenix as a young jedi would have been PERFECT. Even Portman,who is usually a great actress, looked stiff. Macgregor was good as Obi Wan and his sequences of investigating the planet Camino and finding out about the clones and Jango fett was fun. I wish Lucas had gone deeper into the Clones themselves and why Jango was the host for these clones. The fight scene between Jango and Obi Wan was awesome. Jango kicked butt and was one of the best parts of the movie. Really slick character. The flow was hurt by the budding romance scenes and not enough on the clones or Yoda. The fight between Yoda and Dooku was cool,but too short. I guess we have to just enjoy the prequels for what they are,technical marvels.

title: The middle chapter is always the best!!!
review: Lucas returns to the real world!  What a way to come back with possibly the second best Star Wars film of them all (after Empire). Empire's darkness returns as does the more varied pace and non formula plot. The sweeping, all conquering music score is back once more after a weakish 1st episode.  Christensen is superb as Anakin, if limited by an overall simplistic dialogue.  There's a dangerous, sinister undercurrent beneath the good looks, which makes the closing scene all the more unsettling.  We know where they're heading, but they don't.  Yet!  Portman and McGregor can't quite rise above the material, lacking the dynamism of Christensen.  Two much CGI in places, and the Coruscant scene is a little overlong and far-fetched.  But the battles are first class, particularly the closing conflict.  And Christopher Lee is supreme as Dooku.  Never has an actor belied his age (almost 80) to such an extent.  Roll on part 3, but do we have to wait three years? And George: Make a final trilogy!  You'll see it in your dreams!

title: Fantastic!!!
review:
Excellent performance by Natalie and Hayden. Anyone calling the dialogue wooden, does IMO not know anything about teenage love. Yoda rocks!!!

In conclusion: Best Star Wars movie yet. Thank you George.

title: One word: Fantastic!!!!
review:
Alright then, what can I say about this film?

I will not talk about the plot, since most of you will know the plot by now. I am going to talk about how this film made me feel while seeing it. After all, that's what's important.

First of all, the acting was very good. The lines are sometimes a bit stiff, but Hayden, Natalie and Ewan in particular shine. At times, their plight really made me grab the seat and hold my breath in excitement.

The story, although talky in parts, is always engaging and interesting. And most important of all, very emotional. Especially during the last hour, which is some of the best cinema I've ever witnessed - funny, sad, suspenseful, desperate, romantic, scary and truly captivating.

The music is way better than in Phantom Menace. The new love theme deserves special mention, since it is so rousing and beautiful, it can drive a grown man to tears.(trust me, I know this from personal experience!)

All in all, a fantastic film that brings balance to the Force. I cannot wait for Episode III.

Rating: 10/10

title: Better than Episode 1, but will pale in comparison to Episode 3.
review:
I don't know why everyone is so gung-ho about this being the movie that puts Star Wars back on track. The franchise never got off-track!! I LOVED Episode 1, but I'll admit, I LOVED AOTC a little bit more. (SPOILERS AHEAD)!!!

I'll analyze the characters one by one and you can fit the story together as you go along:

Obi-Wan: Ewan friggin owns this role. OB1 has been a Jedi Master for 10 years at the telling of this story, and it's begining to show. His senses are sharp, lightsaber skills have increased, and he's just awesome. We see him give a lot of aggrevation to Anakin by constantly talking down to him, and we all know where that'll end up leading to. He goes to Kamino and ends up finding out about the clone army and is the first to Geonosis. It's kinda hard to place his role in this one, but it's definately bigger than in Episode 1. Just can't wait for him to put Anakin in his place in Episode 3.

Anakin: Hayden pulls off the most important role in this entire franchise suprisingly good. Although the romance scenes on naboo were pretty dull, watching him slowly turn to the dark side gives me goosebumps. He claims a dictatorship (the yet to be formed Empire) should be the way politics are handled, his meeting with Palpatine and his view on Tusken Raiders are spine-tingling. His whining about OB1 was a little annoying, but hey, he's still a teenager.

Amidala: She was kind of passive in this one to me. Yes, the Trade Federation was still behind attemps to kill her, and yes these attempts end up inadvertantly triggering the clone war, but other than that and her relationship with Anakin, she really didn't have much to do.

Mace Windu: If Mace was a Sith, he'd be Darth Bad-Ass. His role as it pertains to the Jedi counsel and the Senate is huge in this movie, and he's one of the best with a lightsaber, second only to......

Yoda: Words can't describe the feelings that went through my body when Yoda stepped out of the shadow to face Dooku. WOW. Although I'm torn on whether I like the goofy, outlandish Yoda from Empire and Jedi or the serious, cautious Yoda from I-III, he definatley is one of my favorite characters of all time.

Count Dooku: Can I just say that Christopher Lee should be recognized as an acting GOD!!!! This guy is the ultimate bad guy, the only others I think come close are Willem Dafoe as Green Goblin and Jack Nicholson as The Joker. And Lee has these guys beat cuz not only is he an awesome Dooku, but a flawless Saruman (LOTR). Anyway, Dooku ends up being in cahoots with the Trade Federation and Palpatine. Interestingly enough, we learn he was Yoda's Padawan, Qui-Gon was Dooku's, and we know OB1 was Qui-Gon's and Anakin is OB1's and later Palpatine's.

Palpatine: This is probably one of the best written characters ever. You see him pulling the strings behind the scenes, putting himself in complete control, with no one the wiser. Observe-1.Given emergency power (basically Dictator control), 2.Puts the clone army at his fingertips, which I predict he will turn bad in Episode 3, killing all but 2 Jedi and turning clones into Stormtroopers, 3.Is behind all the attemps on Amidala's life. Awesome.

Jango Fett: The man being cloned thousands of times to formulate the clone army, was hired by Sidious to whack Amidala. Other than that and a couple cool fight scenes, nothing too special. Although, he does have the best line in the movie: "I'm just a simple man trying to make my way in the universe". Vegas, baby!

In conclusion, this movie exceeded Episode 1 and 6. In order it'd be 5, 4, 2, 1, 6. But just wait. This movie is the perfect set up for Episode 3, which if it's done as good as this, will be 3 hours long and will be the greatest movie ever made. AOTC=9/10

title: This is no Spiderman movie, AOTC leaves you waiting for the next prequel
review: I watched Spiderman on its opening weekend and by half the movie I was ready to leave, it looked a copy of the Original Superman motion picture.  AOTC brings back the magic and myth of the original Trilogy, without leaving you the sense that it is a replica, and is almost as good, or tops, the Empire Strikes Back -- with two clear plots carrying over to the next prequel. The last 45 minutes looked more like only 10 minutes, time goes by that quick since it is that good! Not to mentioned that also right at the beginning you are jumped into action. Hayden Christensen carries to perfection Anakin's role --- anxious and impulsive, best reflected in his eyes. I am also glad Mindu (Samuel L Jackson) had more active screen time. George Lucas had the hard job of showing how the Republic looked before the raise of the Empire and the role of the Jedis in that "old Republic" and he clearly mastered it. After watching AOTC I came out of the movie convinced that "Return of the Jedi" is not named after Luke Skywalker come to mastering of the Force, but for Anakin (Darth Vader) conversion back to the light side of the Force. In short, I will highly recommend it.

title: George is simply put.....THE MAN!
review: OK so you have this story to tell....you know how it is suppose to go and you know what it looks like.....you can hear the sounds and voices and just thinking about it sends chills down your spine because it is so real. George took this epic story from the depths of his brain and revealed it's innermost secrets in the most stunning fashion that pushes our senses so far into it that reality is just a faint crackle of popcorn from the guy next to you. Now I could go into detail about how this story is one of the best ever told.....but that could take a while. Instead I will just say that this movie is the epitome of why we go to movies. You feel the entire spectrum of emotions while completely immersing your physical senses and bringing you away from the harsh reality of life. But this is just my opinion.....

title: Less Jar Jar!
review:
Midnight showing; Pittsburgh.

Much better than Phantom! more serious and more directed to original Star Wars fans. Great effects, even though they are digital.

Longing for the days of actual physical construction of ideas. But still great movie!

title: Better than Episode I
review:
The exciting action scenes pretty much make up for the two dimensional acting performed by Hayden, Portman, ect. George should of replaced some of the actors with CG impersonations. Although the movie is fun and exciting the dialouge does make you want to take a lightsaber and whack Lucas's head. Some of the performances were also very weak. If Lucas gets a good writer to come up with a better script for EPIII the movie will be a lot better than Episodes I and II. Lawrence Kasden would be an ideal choice for Lucas to write the script.

If you are discouraged by the many negative reviews about AOTC you shouldn't be because it is much better film than they think. When you see the Jedi light their sabers and Yoda kicking Christopher Lee's ass you will know seeing this movie was worth viewing.

title: If it's BAD, why is everyone watching it?
review:
I was a fan of the original Star Wars trilogy (heretofore known as Episode IV, V and VI, nuts huh?). Great story telling, magical feel with real actors in brilliantly crafted suits (Ewoks, Stormtroppers, etc.), puppet characters manipulated by humans (Yoda, Jabba, etc.), and most of all, very like-able actors in very like-able roles (Harrison Ford as Han Solo, etc.). George Lucas was a visionary in his time.

Then came the news that he was going to make a trilogy of prequels. That didn't sound right but I thought, hey, more of the same magical stuffs. Great! Hype and anticipation preceded Episode I, the Phantom Menace...I went to see it with great expectations, came out of the theater feeling nauseous. From great looking villains like Darth Vadar, to roadkill resurrection Darth Maul. From like-able characters to unlike-able spittoon resident Jar Jar Binks.

I thought Episode II might be different and gave it a chance. Went to see it but again came out nauseous the second time. For sure, it's better than Episode I but it's way off the standards of the original three. The magic is gone - in place of neat puppets, we get CGI, lots of it. There are no like-able actors (should have asked Leonardo DiCaprio or anybody to be Anakin Skywalker instead. There's something about Hayden Christensen and how he looks so wrong in that hair-cut) or characters (where's the wise cracking Han Solo persona? and what the heck is John Shaft doing in a Star Wars film, sans the shades and the face hair?).

In short, a disappointing film that did not match up to the original films. Definitely not worth the hype nor the cash to go watch it. Only the fight scene between Yoda and Dooku was not too shabby but if I had known that to be the only scene that would crank my gears, I would have waited for it to come out on DVD or video to rent it.

Final comments - I'm still willing to give George Lucas the chance to make amends for what I perceive to be a sacrilege of the original films. Re-employ some good old fashioned Star Wars film making for Episode III and you might get back the countless of fans you lost for the next trilogy of sequels to the original films.

Rating 3 out of 10 (3 for the fight scene between Yoda and Dooku). Spider-Man was a much, much better film. If you have the cash to see one film, go see Spider-Man.

title: Bad writing, worse effects.
review:
As I was watching this film, I kept Roger Ebert's immortal words in mind, that he "couldn't recall a single line of memorable dialogue."

This is exactly what's wrong with this film. The writing is atrocious. In the original, where the lines were original, witty, and delivered with great effect, in this film, I dreaded every time a character opened their mouth.

For example, C3PO to R2D2: "Idiot!"

Wow.

In fact, R2D2 is the only one with a shred of their future/past dialogue.

Also, Ebert helpfully pointed out that what lines there were were culled from every single cliche ever made. Again, he was right.

For example, Annakin on his mother's death: Mom, I'll miss you...soOoOoOoO much.

Regarding the "look and feel" of this film, I would say it lost too much using digital effects. The actors have no environment to play off of. Many of the animated characters lack weight and physical presence, without even the slightest hint that they actually exist.

But now it's time to say something nice about this film: It didn't suck as much as phantom menace. For that, I would say it's the 2nd worst film in the series, or 4th best, depending on how you look at it.

title: Obviously good, but...Dunno yet
review:
I dunno... I just know that the first watching of these big, spectacular movies full of ideas usually makes me disappointed. It was the same with Harry Potter (reading the book first, it killed the movie and I had to see it once again to like it), Men in Black (seen the trailer thousand times), and even Lord of the Rings (I heard so many praises that I was expecting some orgasm-generating thing while it was *just* very-very good).

Also, I always expect something impossible; I expect the miracle that SW1 provided, or at least the miracle I felt when I saw the first giant dinosaur in Jurassic Park. Of course these miracles can't be repeated; we won't see any f/x so earth-shattering, won't see any incredible good new story elements in this crowded marketplace of movies - I was just so young when I could see SW1 I did not know it was a chain of quotations from other movies and books (Lord of the Rings).

Probably those who say this is the best of the five Star Wars movies watched Empire Strikes Back only on video or the SE in cinemas. Which is not a problem; it seems Lucas is able to make something digestable for the next generation too.

I enjoyed watching the movie, it was incredibly spectacular (even if the f/x was not always the best, sometimes it was better than anything we've seen before). I like the story, actually this non-Black&White movie seems to be more mature than any of the series. I like the sign of the future empire on Obi Wan's ship. I like the irony of the speech of our wise old kung fu master...C3PO is sometimes a bit annoying, but he has the funniest sentence of the movie as well. The love dialogue is really epic. I can't say I really love it; it actually annoyed me a bit, but I can accept it as it is an emotionally really serious part of the movie. I love the usually present background stories (like the droids replacing a window).

I can't say more now; I know I have to watch the movie again to have a more developed opinion on the case. I know I did it wrong when I spoiled the movie for myself reading the book and the comics, watching several trailers before going to cinema. I just wish Lucas forgot marketing aspects and kept everything secret. Of course this is really nice to see these large numbers and records but... PLEASE DON'T DESTROY THE THIRD PART FOR ME, PLEASE!!!!!!! Without seeing any trailers, pictures, books etc. in advance, I promise I will watch that three times, OK?

review: Part of the expectation arisen around Episode II..., is owed to the love story between Anakin and Padmé. title: Just another blockbuster
review:
Many people feel George Lucas has vindicated himself solely because "Attack of the Clones" is superior to "Phantom Menace." That's similar to saying a lemon is better than a totalled automobile.

Now, I'm not going to say that Episode II is a horrible movie. Aside from the incredibly inane romance between Amidala and Anakin, the rest of the movie is quite watchable. The last half hour alone is worth the price of admission (if you can get past the O-so boring second act). But does it have the same sense of fun and adventure as the original trilogy? I'd have to say no.

Watching Episode II the day after I watched "The Empire Strikes Back" again, I realized what's wrong with the new trilogy: no Han Solo. The characters in Episodes I and II are all clean-cut elites--none of the main characters are scummy or dirty or even charmingly roguish. Thus, all the attempts at humour are not witty or clever but just immature and stupid.

Lucas has made another entertaining blockbuster. Ironically, he's become part of the blockbuster phenomenon he created. A few years from now, the new Star Wars trilogy will be as forgotten as other recent blockbusters: Independence Day, Stargate, Men in Black, et al.

title: Maybe I Need To See It Again...
review:
Um, it was ok. For some reason, the Anakin/Padme romance didn't click for me. And let's face it, that's what this movie really turns on. And if you don't buy that, the rest is hard to swallow. What in the world does she see in him? She: a young but experienced Senator, and ruler of a planet. He: an immature, mixed-up, narcissistic, teenage Jedi wannabe. He almost made me long for the kid in the first movie! It isn't until after he slaughters the sand people camp that she pledges her love. No wonder Leia likes scoundrels...she gets it from Mom! And the scene where Anakin's mother dies...I almost laughed it was so cliched. It's a good thing it wasn't a wide shot, or I'd half-expected her feet to fly up at the moment of truth (a la Shemp of the 3 Stooges).

The movie is kind of confusing and does drag a bit. A 2nd viewing will probably clear things up, but I'm still a little unclear on Count Dooku, where he came from, and how creating clones helps Senator Palpatine. I THINK it's because Palpatine is using the "clones are needed to protect the Republic" argument, when he actually plans to use them to overthrow it. I have a feeling a "Special Edition" will come out in the future with new scenes and new editing to make this movie more comprehensible. If so, I hope they throw in some scenes to make Anakin more appealing. And I'd gladly throw away some of the high tech special f/x for better characters, truer emotions, and a more comprehensible plotline.

I'm going to go see it again. That helped with "The Lord of the Rings", which was a much finer movie. Although, even THAT wasn't quite up to the original "Star Wars" and "Empire" (forget the "Jedi" furball fiasco). Note to George: if Lawrence Kasdan and Irwin Kershner are still alive, let THEM handle the 3rd flick! Heck, even if they AREN'T alive, let them handle it! I was between my junior and senior year in high school when "Star Wars" first came out, and I can tell you from experience and seeing audience reactions that neither one of these new episodes comes close to measuring up to the first 2 movies in this series (SW and TESB). People walked out of those movies in awe of what they had just seen. If these movies were as good, they would easily surpass "Titanic" in theatre grosses. 6 out of 10.

Oh yeah: Yoda kickin butt was almost worth the price of admission! THAT was cool!

Thank goodness we didn't have another intergalactic C-Span for a movie.  The local Washington Post reviewer here said the movie lacked a plot.  This is why almost everyone I know ignores the Washington Post reviewers.  Plot and intrigue galore.  And here's hoping Lucas somehow finds the humility to ask his good friend Steven Spielberg to direct the last of the prequel series. Spider-Man was a better movie.
