title: Simply Stunning!
review: When you read the other reviewers of AOTC saying that George Lucas has redeemed himself after the much slated Phantom Menace, they are absolutely right. I was never one to negatovely criticise Episode 1 but I have to admit that it had lacked the essential Star Wars feel of the later episodes. This, I thought was down to the fact that I have aged 25 years since the original Star Wars and even though I attempted to view it with some of that childhood wonder, I felt perhaps that something was lacking. Any preconcpetions I may have had prior to seeing AOTC quickly disppeared though and I add my vote to the many who say that George Lucas has definitely returned to form. Attack of the Clones is, quite simply, stunning. Mainly due to the incredible effects but also due to the fact that Lucas seems to have returned to his grass roots. Perhaps, he tried too hard with Phantom, attempting to create something that would satisfy the fans' 25 year old hunger. An impossible task but here, he has settled back down into what he does best: simple storytelling. For a start, AOTC "feels" like proper Star Wars. In episodes 4,5 and 6, there were a number of story threads throughout each film which met to a conclusion at the end. Phantom Menace didn't seem to pull this off and followed the same characters from the film's start to its finish. In AOTC, there a number of different stories going on: Obi Wan's quest for the truth behind Senator Amidala's attempted assassination, the conspiracies happening behind the scenes in the Galactic Republic, the love story between Anakin and Padme, and Anakin's struggle with his own feelings and his role as a Jedi. This made it a much easier film to digest as each story was broken down into small pieces and alternated throughout before meeting for the conclusion. Hayden Christensen did a surprisingly good job of the maturing Anakin and although it took him a good while to achieve empathy to his character, once comfortable with his his role one could really get into the head of soon-to-be Darth Vadar. His feelings for his mother, he's uncontrollable love for Padme and his rebelliousness in the Jedi Order.  One of the most frightening scenes had him slaughtering Sandpeople, his rage uncontrolled and vicious. If Lucas maintains the passion of this character then we are in for one hell of an Episode 3 as we find out his fate. Ewen McGregor seems completely comfortable with his role as Obi Wan and looks and acts more like Alec Guinness with each passing scene. I also loved the many references to the later films, especially meeting a young Owen Lars and his girlfriend Beru. What a joy to see Luke Skywalker's future home, with Anakin sat in the refectory where we met a disillusioned Luke many years ago! And what about the young Boba Fett? Now we finally find out why he hates the Jedi so much. The young lad who plays him carries off the look of revenge so well as he realises his life-long vendetta. Watch out too towards the end of the film, a hologram of the Separatists' new weapon off-camera ... the Death Star. And did you ever want to see what Yoda really could do? Oh my god! His fight scene with Count Dooku (Christopher Lee) was a genius piece of work. The audience roared with laughter too when after putting his light sabre away, he hobbled away as normal on his walking stick! The effects are quite simply stunning. Lucas, comfortable with his art has created a universe of unparalelled beauty. We get to see more of Coruscant (watch out for the deliberate reference to Blade Runner), Naboo, Tattooine and new worlds such as Kamino and Geonosis. One of the most stunning scenes is the quite simply amazing chase sequence through the asteroids of Geonosis. Remember how impressed you were with Han Solo guiding the Millennium Falcon through asteroids after its flight from Hoth? You ain't seen nothing yet! And I was overjoyed to see one of my favourite Star Wars vehicles, The Slave I, doing its stuff. The final battle sequence too, with a million Clone Troopers fighting battle droids is perhaps one of the greatest sequences ever filmed. Attack of the Clones from my perspective as a Star Wars fan, more than excceeded my expectations and I know that I need to see it at least twice more. This is REAL Star Wars, overdosed on steriods and the best two and half hours I have spent this year. If you're a fellow fan, you'll love it and I would even say that to those who claim Empire is the best of the lot ... there's a new guy in town. Keep up the good work George and bring us an Episode 3 that you have set up so well with this installment. 10/10

title: Simple Stupid Poor
review:
I can't see why the average rating of Episode 2 is 8.2 today, because this movie has so many obvious mistakes in the logical structure, that it sometimes hurts to watch it (Jango Fett kills the women, who was supposed to assassinate Princess Amidala by a poisoned arrow, while she's lying in Obi-Wan's Arms. Why doesn't he just kill Obi-Wan himself, all his problems would be solved when doing so?!?!?/Why does Anakin's mother immediately die after his arrival in the tent where she is locked up in??!!!?!?!/Why does Obi-Wan say that a planet is south of another one while watching a map of the galaxy? Of what use is south of' when describing a direction in space?!?!?!???! )

Additionally, I can't see any depth in character development in this movie. Anakin is influenced by love and hate and so he can't accomplish his mission like hes supposed to do and he'll finally becomes a menace to the republic, hoooh, that's clever and this was told in episodes 4-6 before. The scene in which his hate is shown is really primitive; he kills the murders of his mother, that's the level of character development in a B-movie. In addition, whenever homage is paid to the original trilogy, this is done obvious and simple, to make sure that even the biggest idiot in the cinema gets it. And of course, those scenes are always followed by a few seconds of silence to underline the brilliance of such a clever allusion.

What finally remains are some impressive sets and special effects and the brilliant, but mismatching Yoda-Fighting-Scene.

And OK, I confess, that some of the old magic and atmosphere of the episodes 4-6 returned, which makes episode 2 much better and entertaining than the terrible episode 1.

But in the end the unbelievable stupidity and simplicity of the story and character-development are too annoying to recommended this movie and it's impossible to give more than 5 points for a movie, which sometimes doesn't even reach the level of a Trash-Movie.

title: Attack of the Clones is just as good as the classics!
review: I was floored by Attack of the Clones, and can easily say that it is now in the top 2 favorite Star Wars movies for me.  I am not sure if I prefer Attack of the Clones or the Empire Strikes Back -- its that close.  I can honestly say that I have greatly enjoyed each of the Star Wars movies -- not because they gave me more of what the previous films gave, but because each one has covered new ground.  I have read a lot of the other reviews posted here by people slamming this movie (and its predecessor, The Phantom Menace, which ALSO rocked) and saying that it didn't live up to the interplay between Han, Luke & Leia from the classic trilogy.  News Flash:  This is 30 years before the original trilogy!  It is about TOTALLY DIFFERENT PEOPLE. It is asinine to expect the prequels to give us the exact same feel & chemistry as a group of characters who DO NOT EVEN APPEAR IN THIS PART OF THE STORY!!  Don't get me wrong -- Han, Luke & Leia were awesome in the classic trilogy, but Padme, Anakin and Obi-Wan are just as compelling if you give them a chance.  George Lucas has done an amazing job giving continuity with the classic trilogy.  He has also created interesting new characters, and is giving compelling reasons why Anakin is about to Darth out.  Attack of the Clones was technically superior to ALL of its predecessors, & the story completely lives up to the Star Wars name.  Perhaps the people who do nothing but lambast the film have built the original trilogy up so high in their minds that NOTHING George Lucas did would please them anyway.  The point of Star Wars is to sit back, enjoy the spectacle, & lose yourself in Lucas's Universe again, just like we did when we were children -- not to pick it apart because it wasn't custom made to YOUR perception of the classic movies.  As for the complaints over CGI, the special effects in the new trilogy are no more noticeable as artificial than the muppets & stop motion from the classics.  It is sad that so many people have COMPLETELY lost the childlike nature that Lucas's films are designed for.  I, for one, am not willing to let the modern world kill the wonderful escapism of Star Wars for me.  If you can watch this film without any preconceived notions, then you will enjoy it.  If not, then maybe you should ask yourself why you bother to go to the movies at all.  If you hate something because it doesn't give you more of the same, then perhaps you should stay home & watch re-runs.  Personally, I am glad that George Lucas has chosen to delve into new areas with the same eye for fantasy & detail that he has always had. Attack of the Clones is not only a worthy successor to the previous movies, it is an excellent film in its own right.  Give it a chance.

title: critics not quite right
review: All of the critics' comments I have read say that the characters are cardboard, there is no good dialogue, and all the rest of the favorite this-movie-is-not-all-people-make-it-out-to-be cliches.  While perhaps the acting was not as impressive as it could have been, and there may have been the occasional cheesy line, Episode II was not only a great Star Wars movie, but a great film on its own.  The romance subplot alone brought an emotional level to the movie unmatched by any previous Star Wars episode, while I thought the characters in general had a more natural, human aura to them than before. Okay, the first, very political portion was a small exception, but it was only small.  This was a very dynamic movie; in addition to the benefits that the romance story brought, the action was just as intense as--if not more intense than--that of previous Star Wars movies.  Nobody should regret seeing this.

title: Everything I'd hoped for and more! The force is strong with this one!
review:
Simply amazing.

The action was fantastic. The worlds were breathtaking. The technology is mind-boggling.

I give this movie a 9.9 of 10 since Empire is still my favorite. I have to say this is a close second.

I wonder if Christopher Lee ever thought in his wildest dreams that he'd be on a box of cereal at the age of 80.

MTFBWYA

title: I Loved it!
review: If you go into this movie expecting it to be like the original trilogy you might be disappointed, I myself after being disappointed with Phantom Menace Did my best not to have any thoughts about what I would have done or what I thought should happen. I went in knowing I could not change what's in the movie, and did my best not to compare it with the emotional feelings I feel for the Original 3 films. It's never going to give me the same feelings. With that said I really liked this movie, and loved it the second viewing. The acting is fine, R2 and 3po are funny and the effects are awesome, You need to see it twice to really enjoy everything.

title: What a relief!
review:
Well, I must say that this film is a drastic improvement on the last. And with that said, I'll also say that it's even enjoyable, very enjoyable! There are a number of moments where the dialogue is rather atrocious, so bad in fact that the whole theater burst out laughing, particularly scenes between Anakin and Padme. So, no, it's not a perfect film, I wouldn't say it's as good as any of the original three, but you can now begin to see the transition from this trilogy to the 4-6 trilogy.

Whereas Episode One was very flat and the characters where very deadpan, Episode Two's characters are much more interesting, with a lot of conflict to keep the plot moving along. The wide shots of all of the planets are beautiful, although I still felt like the CGI was a bit too much at spots.

Overall, an entertaining film, especially so for Star Wars fans/fanatics. Let's hope E3 is even better.

title: Dazzling CGI effects a good Star Wars do not make
review:
Don't get me wrong - this film is awesome. I was really blown away, especially by the closing battle sequence with Count Dooku. Possibly the best of all 5 so far but the continual onslaught of millions of CGI's at 0.5 past light speed are very hard to get to grips with at times. With the exception of light-sabre confrontations, the large battles scenes in the original 3 movies were alot more gripping.

Using small groups of combatants makes for better audience involvement, such as the chase through the Death Star in IV, the classic asteroid field sequence in V and the speeder bike pursuit in VI - which is why the light sabre duels always come across well. I used to think Stormtroopers were a dumb bunch but they're elite forces compared to the dime-a-billion battle-droids.

Quality, not quantity and well-used, not over-used CGI would make for a flawless Episode III.

title: The story continues in a brilliant film
review:
If you had not seen any Star Wars films before, this film is brilliant with great acting and special affects. This is the only reason I could not give full marks because as a film on its own the story may seem a little confusing. However, as most of the world have seen episodes I,IV,V and VI this film is a masterpiece. It does the job that is requested of it. Not only does it continue to tell the story but it tells it incredibly well. The film has everything including Lucas' first real venture into a love story which he pulls off extremely well.

Christensen and Portman are exceptional lead roles and McGregor and Jackson follow up well with performances that deserve the highest accolades.

There will be the usual critics mouthing off about the soppy love scenes and the return of Jar Jar but as George has said all along, he is just telling the story as it is. In my opinion he could not have told it better.

title: Doesn't engage you like the originals.
review:
Thank you, George Lucas - for giving me the opportunity to use the word "humdrum" in everyday conversation.

After being disappointed by The Phantom Menace, I was very careful not to let my expectations get too high for this one. Unfortunately I failed, as I was stupid enough to listen to people who said it was an improvement.

You may have heard that Jar-Jar is much less in evidence in this film. At first glance this is true, but his irritating slapstick role is taken over by C-3PO. I know there was a touch of this in the originals, but this is too much. The film cuts from a life-and-death battle between Jedi and droids to a silly head swap joke that is carried on far too long, and then back to the battle. Maybe things like this are put in for the kids. If that is the case, have a little faith in the younger generation George! The original series worked just fine without scenes like that.

By far the biggest disappointment is the complete lack of tension in the film. I can still watch the asteroid chase from Empire and be on the edge of my seat, while the attempt to repeat it in Clones is just boring. When the Rancor is released in Jedi, it is a convincing and impressive monster. The creations released to kill Padme, Anakin and Obi-Wan look appalling. They look "cartoony" whereas the Rancor is scary.

Furthermore, whoever had the bright idea of putting Yoda in a lightsabre duel should be taken outside and given a good kicking. The overriding impression in my mind was Gizmo's Rambo impression in Gremlins 2. I nearly laughed out loud.

To whoever directs Episode 3, please remember; the success of the original series was not down to flashy special effects or childish humour, but good characters and chemistry between the actors. Let's face it, the plots weren't particularly original and the scripts (particularly the first) weren't that amazing. What made them work was good film making, something that has been sadly lacking in these instalments.

title: A little disappointing, but would still recommend seeing it.
review:
As a huge Star Wars fan, I was happy to see the movie just to see the characters progress from the last movie and see the "history" of the previous Star Wars films finally being played out. However, as I have seen better come from George Lucas, I was disappointed in the movie as a whole.

In an article about the film, one writer stated that the obsession Skywalker has for Amidala is driven by the fact that a day hasn't gone by that he hasn't thought about her. I thought this was an interpretation of the drama. Instead, that's exactly what Anakin says: "Obi-wan, I have been thinking of her every day since I met her." And things like that pepper the entire screenplay - they tell instead of show. I believe the movie was too talkative. Things can be said without actually saying them and that gave a very immature flavor to the entire movie for me.

As it has been said many times in reviews and articles, the best part of the movie is Master Yoda's lightsaber duel. THAT alone makes the movie worth seeing...that along with the wonderful visual effects and artistry of the movie.

As a Star Wars fan, it's impossible for me NOT to purchase this movie for my collection when it comes out on video/DVD. I can't have an incomplete collection. I will say that Episode I: The Phantom Menace was a better movie...and I've yet to see any of the Star Wars films top "The Empire Strikes Back". Perhaps Lucas should get his writing partner from THAT to give this final movie (Episode III) the grand exit this series needs.

Signed, A devoted, but truthful fan

title: Impressive Special Effects
review:
This is technically speaking a very impressive film. The level of detail evident in the special effects shows that an enormous amount of work must have gone into producing them. If you're not a Star Wars fan, but you like watching "cutting edge" special effects, you won't be disappointed with this.

As for the plot, acting etc., this is all pretty much standard Star Wars fare, so expect a story which moves at a pace designed for a hyperactive 5-year-old with a severe attention deficit disorder and acting as wooden as Yoda's walking stick. And women beware - there's really only one significant female character in the entire movie and in this one there is a token ripping of her costume to excite the boys/men at whom this film was so obviously targeted.

And for all those who moan that it's not as good as the original three films, your memory is playing tricks on you. The acting in "The Empire Strikes Back" and "Return of the Jedi" in particular is absolutely appalling and the plot of the whole series is contrived, paper thin and full of holes. The dialogue in "Empire" (particularly between Han Solo and Princess Leia) often borders on the excrutiating.

Sorry to burst your bubble - it's just that when the original three came out, you overlooked this because the special effects were so groundbreaking and you were probably young and impressionable when you first saw them. Either that, or you were and still are the sort of Sci-Fi geek who won't watch anything

Not that I think the current film is any worse for its faults. It really is a spectacular audio/visual experience. Just don't try and look for anything deeper because it's simply not that kind of movie.

title: Better than Episode one, but still not Star Wars
review:
I'm not sure why Star Wars fans give praise to either episode I or II. I've watched IV, V, and VI a hundred times and episodes I and II do not even scratch the surface of the level of action, acting, suspense, storyline, and drama evoked by the originals. I understand people perceive things differently, but I just wonder, what was it about the originals that Star Wars fans liked, that made them huge fans? Is it just the fact that people carry light sabers, or that when blasters are fired they make a certain sound that is unique to Star Wars movies? Or maybe because they were movies that used the word "Force." If that's the reason, then Episode II delivers. But if you're looking for anything that resembles the level of artistry that went into the Original Trilogy than Episode II ain't it. It's hokey, badly plotted, it seems to poke fun at its own campy premise, and the last 20 minutes of action are not enough to redeem the film. Some of the problems I specifically have:

****SPOILERS******

1) I didn't originally like the fact that Boba and Jango Fett were going to be a father and son team when I heard it. Watching it on film seemed really hokey. They're supposed to be merciless bounty hunters yet Jango carries his son around with him everywhere he goes. OK, I'll buy this, but what's with the sinister cliche laugh coming from a 10 year-old boy. It seemed goofy. And the writers seemed to be setting up a premise that Boba Fett wants to avenge his father's death at the hands of the Jedi. But the original triology painted him to be a paid mercernary, not a man on a vendetta, and he barely had any contact with Jedi. Seems like a sensely reason to weave him into the storyline.

2) Perfect example of bad directing and acting. Padwe's thrown from a ship, lay hurting in the sand. A clone soldier comes up to her and says are you all right. Suddenly, her grimace is gone and she's like I'm fine. Is this make-believe acting or is this a homage to those old A-team episodes where the car would flip over fifty times and the guys would come stumbling out merely coughing. Sheesh.

3) I heard from previous movie goers that the movie was worth seeing Yoda fight. So I patiently waited. But no, at first they have to set up the showdown between Yoda and Count Dooku as a bad western. Count Dooku says. "Well it seems we have to settle this with, light sabers." Did a fanboy write this line, sheesh. Then Yoda throws open his robe, like he's about to throw down. Come on now. Just take this a little seriously please. Would it seem so hard to have Yoda act a little more in character and kick ass? What's up with the Kung Fu stance he gets into. Then he goes jumping around the screen like Mighty Mouse, you could barely see him. It looked hilarious actually not like look how magnificently Yoda's fighting. Yoda was a reverant character and they reduced him to a Dragon Ball Z warrior in two minutes, the CGI was so bad.

Those are some of my big concerns, that's not to mention the horrid love scenes or the overall horrible dialogue, the fact that Padwe's skin tight outfit was ripped perectly around her abs although the CGI creature only scratched her back, or the fact that she was supposed to be in disguise but her clothes were very regal. I actually thought the movie started out decent, and I liked the detective story, but the movie got swallowed up by its own campiness. The fight scene between Obi Wan and Jango Fett was good. The fight scene between Obi Wan and Count Dooku started out descent until they were fighting so close you couldn't see anything. And I even liked the initial battle of the Force between Count Dooku and Yoda. But overall, the Star Wars prequels are nothing but bad impersonations of the Originals.

title: Don't listen to the critics
review: The problem with critics is that they are just that.. they'll deny the greatness of a movie because by itself, it is lacking.  But that's just it about the starwars saga.. you are not to watch just one movie by itself.. the entire entity that is the (soon to be) 6 movie epic is -1- story.. it's just too long to tell in less than 30 years. :)  Watch this movie in that light, and you'll realize that this is so far the greatest installment yet, and it does nothing but point the way to the next movie and how amazingly phenomenal it's going to be..

title: A case of spectacle over substance.
review: An anti-climax, a disappointment. Disbelief can only be suspended so far. My issue with this film is that while the spectacle - the effects, the sets, the costumes, are superb - someone forgot to write a decent script. Ewan McGregor is wooden and looks as if he's reading from an autocue. Hayden Christensen (who?) never seems to have acted before this film, is this his first feature? Even Samuel L Jackson seems to groan inwardly has he spouts Jedi rubbish. This is great if you're 12 years old and part of the Jedi religion, if you're not either of these you're screwed. Get a grip Lucas.

title: Novelty crap!
review:
If it wasn't for the fact that this is a Star Wars film, this would have been one of the worse films I've seen in the cinema (the worse one is "The book that wrote itself").

The whole film was based upon the "myth of Star Wars", but with itself being a Star Wars film, the film is an utter failure.

Some scenes were blatantly there to promote future computer-/videogames.

The only positive factor with this film was the fact that I ate some nice chocolate while watching it (you see, I haven't had chocolate for a while).

title: This is a spoiler of AOTC.
review: This is a spoiler. Star Wars Episode II AOTC was very disappointing. The best part of the movie was when Yoda went ape turds on Count Chocula at the end. The plot and trying to figure out who is who is so confusing it's ridiculous- the empire, the republic, the senate, the trade federation, the commerce guild, the separatists, the clones, the drones, the schmones. In the first trilogy, there was just the empire and the rebellion- simple and clear cut. Lucas does a poor job of developing the main characters- you have no vested emotional interest in Amidala or Anakin. Why should we care about them? Why is the title Attack of the Clones? Weren't the clones fighting with the Jedi and for the good guys? Is Senator Palpatine Darth Sidious? Is he the Emperor?Who is Chancellor Valorem and what do these guys have to do with anything? Which side is fighting for and with whom? Plus, Lucas assumes that every creature in the universe has a humanoid form with a head, torso, two arms and two legs. There is no scientific basis to support or assume that. Jar Jar Binks makes me want to retch. Does the republic become the empire? What about the separatists and the trade federation? What the frig is going on?

title: No drama, little acting, nice effects
review:
For an average film it was A-OK. For what should be a blockbuster, it was below par. The biggest problem was there was nothing compelling except the special effects... and they didn't have the "wow" factor the original did with surround sound.

There are no surprises. Nothing to wonder what will happen next. The love story is not made interesting and, when you add in dialogue that is simply without pizazz, you are left waiting for battles and effects to make it worth your while - and it doesn't.

title: By George you've got it!
review:
Managed to catch the 12.05am opening session last night and the atmosphere was electric.

The movie? 3 thumbs up!! Absolutely fantastic.

Being an old school star wars fan (30 y.o.) I was quite nervous we would see another 'kiddie' flick like Phantom Menace (my rating about 6/10), but AOTC was miles ahead in terms of, well.., everything! Hayden did a great job and Portman was OK - she looked a treat but her facial expressions and speech never really matched her performances in Leon and Beautiful Girls. Action sequences and storyline were superb. I'm seeing it again on Friday night.

Good work Mr Lucas, "most impressive"!

title: the force is strong in this one
review: I enjoyed the movie a lot. I have to admit that I was a bit afraid before I entered the Cinema but 15 minutes into the movie I realised that I won't be disappointed. Not just because of Yoda, or Obiwan's sence of humour, or the purple lightsaber or the evil that actually talk, or the similarity to Empire, but because of everything!

title: Get Over It!
review: I'm so sick of people slagging off the two recent Star Wars movies, it's as if they expect a completely soul-changing experience. IT'S JUST A MOVIE!!!!!! All these people saying that TPM and ATOC 'don't have the depth and emotion of the original three', I'm sorry but the Star Wars films are (and always have been) the epitome of saturday afternoon popcorn-munching flicks. Don't get me wrong, I love the original trilogy, (any films that can contain some of the appalling lines that they had and still be enjoyable has gotta be good) but they weren't these deep, philosophical masterpieces that everyone seems to think they were. I think the obvious reason for the hatred being thrown at these recent prequels is that most people saw the original three when they were children, so they remember them as being fantastic, whereas now they're grownups and expecting these ones to be just as good, but they can't be because people are now seeing them from an adults point of view. Children at the moment love the new films, just like we loved the first trilogy. All you whining nerds out there, get over yourselves and get out more! They're George Lucas' films, he should know what's right.

title: A huge improvement!
review: Ah... relief.  After a somewhat disappointing Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones was superb.  The plot revealed several connections to the first trilogy that I often wondered about.  Yoda's fight scene was simply astounding.  The only real question that was brought to mind was "Why is Mace Windu (Samuel L. Jackson) the only Jedi with a purple-hued lightsaber?" I did not see it in Digital format yet, but look forward to do so sometime in the next few weeks.  If you have not seen this... WATCH IT!

title: George, next time let someone else direct.
review: 3D animation doesn't do it for me any more, and that is all Episode II was, visually beautiful, but what about the story? The movie was 1 hour longer than what it should of been. I think it comes down to bad directing, George Lucas should stick to writing the story and directing ILM, but he should let someone else direct, like he did in his previous movies. He is not timing his scenes properly, they ar way too long, he is definitely not directing well his actors, but I guess that it's not easy acting in front of a blue screen. What happened to the magic, where are the interesting characters, the great dialogs. The characters are so dull, not even Samuel L.Jackson could put energy to his character. And the dialogues are cliche after cliche. I did not like this movie at all.  It could of been a great movie but I think Lucas messed it up

title: Next time, use the force, George
review:
Star Wars II: Attack of the Clones missed the Oscars, but maybe more importantly, the Raspberry awards. Although it is improbable that the hype and its immense popularity would endanger a solid performance at the Oscars.

The good part of this film lies in the truly amazing special effects and the excellent use of all kinds of sf goodies, like sailing spaceships etc. This makes the film stand out from any of the recent productions.

However, watching the film as what it is, a story in its own right, you cannot help but notice how deeply flawed the script is. This isn't helped in any way by Lucas' sloppy direction. Important scenes are unceremoniously expedited without the necessary buildup and leave you feeling robbed. For example, the courtly atmosphere and the pomp of the Senate are contradicted by Amidala's entry: instead of being given the appropriate honors of a senator (and, more importantly, of a key character in the film), everyone starts talking to her at once. Invariably, a character will advance in a grand manner, and have nothing noteworthy to say. This makes it hard to believe a story that is told on such an epic scale. The romance between Amidala and Anakin is just as hard to believe. There are no sparks coming across. The fact that neither of them make us believe in their respective characters doesn't help. Natalie Portman has a squeaky voice, reminding you of a spoiled teenager rather than an important senator cum adventuress. She is miscast for the role. Christensen is solid as an insecure but intelligent Jedi, but his internal motives are too vague and his agony doesn't come across convincingly.

From the freshness and inspiration of the subject matter in the first two Star Wars films, little or nothing is left. Lucas has built up an aura which is consolidated by his special effects gurus. But for them, the emperor would be naked for real and probably for good.

title: The story of a young man with the potential for greatness who falls into bad ways - George Lucas, I mean
review:
An improvement on The Phantom Menace. I was entertained for most of the way, but a lot of the flaws of "Episode 1" and in George Lucas' films generally are painfully apparent. In the end it was disappointing to see so little interest in characterisation and good story-telling, and it all felt a little bit second hand.

In 1977 George Lucas and Star Wars were the leader in a field of one. The Seventies was a time for some fascinating cinema but no one was making the kind of swashbuckling entertainment or films suitable for children with anything like the verve and charisma of the "old days." The splash that Star Wars made on its release was heard around the world. A phenomenon was born and a trend was set, even if purists were alarmed that one day there would be no room for thoughtful adult fims among the blockbusters. At the end of the day, though, "Star Wars" was entertainment for all ages, with adventure and excitement to the fore and everything else second - and throughly enjoyable on that level. The next two instalments showed a real talent (especially in "Empire") but a talent all too ready to forget good cinema and concentrate on juvenile fodder (like "Jedi"), but he still did it better than anyone else.

When "Phantom Menace" was released people were full of expectation, hoping to see the mythic storytelling of the first two films taken to a pulse-quickening max by state-of-the-art special effects. What we got was a few good sequences and a succession of nicely rendered CGI images and nothing else. Lucas obviously found characterisation and the human side a distraction from the technology that he was more interested in. There was no way Lucas could live up to the reputation that the early films had rather spuriously gained as classics to rival the all-time greats, but he was supposed to be able to make a straight-ahead entertaining film instead of an infantile effects picture that tried to pass off its lame plot and funny names as ambitious mythic cinema. Worst of all, it just seemed like a procession towards Episode 2 with almost no sense that anyone was in any danger or that anything bad was going to happen unless our heroes save the day.

"Attack of the Clones" is a big improvement on "Phantom" but still suffers from stunted ambition in terms of story and character, with the usual clunky dialogue that pervades all Star Wars films less easy to forgive when you haven't got Harrison Ford and a walking carpet making it fun for us. At least there is more of a sense of danger and people who have to be rescued or confronted, and there is more variety to the scenes instead of the endless, boring sunny backgrounds of Naboo in "Phantom." However, it is very hard to forgive how utterly perfunctory Lucas is with the characters and the story line. OK, Anakin is angry and rebellious, but we know WHAT'S going to happen to his character because we've all seen the "first" three films, so how about making us interested in HOW it happens? Also the true identity of one of the characters is kept a "secret" when it's fairly obvious who the person actually is, which frankly felt like an insult to the intelligence. I don't mean to sound like a moaner and wanting every film to be a piece of Indie Art, but by the same token Lucas seems to think that he is producing an epic saga that rivals "Lord of the Rings" and "The Godfather", and let me tell you George, you aren't even close.

The biggest problem for George Lucas is that there is a big body of opinion ready to forget that he (like Spielberg to a lesser degree) always shies away from applying his considerable talent to something more complex instead of serving up puerile goo to five-year-olds, and will say that he is the greatest film maker of all time. He thinks what he does is good enough for his audience, but it isn't and it is a shame to see a talent go to waste. It is put into even sharper focus by the fact that "Lord of the Rings" and "The Matrix" provide entertainment, story and action for his older audience that puts anything he has ever done to shame, and the likes of "Toy Story" and "Shrek" are much better as films for children.

In the end what we got was an OK movie, but I couldn't get over my disappointment that it could have been so much better and more entertaining.

title: stunning visuals and actions but marred by an unconvincing cast
review: I was disappointed with Lucas's previous movie Phantom of the Menace as I found it to be flat with a slow development of the storyline. Lucas used a new approach to this movie and wastes no time in getting the audience straight into the action. You can almost compare this movie with those of James Bond where a simple storyline is woven with lavish settings, visuals and actions. There are some spectacular scenes of cities and locations shot on the various planets but the overall feel appears slightly artificial. The alien characters  also appear animated and not as lifelike as one would have expected. Acting is also somewhat sub standard and was particularly disappointed with Samuel Jackson's somewhat muted performance. However, performances by the old veteran Christopher Lee and the voice of Yoda (Frank Oz) lifted this movie. There seemed to be an urgency in the film as the scenes were shot in quick succession in various locations and so tended to depart away from the central theme of the story. Normally the musical score gets unnoticed in most epics but in this case it appeared more pronounced which could be argued as good or bad. The intimate relationship between Anakin Skywalker and Senator Padme Amidala was tackled early in the movie with the premise that that the Star Wars saga will continue.   The final battle scenes was by far the best part of the movie. The complex mechanics of machinery, robots, humans and aliens battling on the desert was very well captured on screen. Like all good spirited action movies we see the supreme republican members of the council also engaged in hand to hand combat. Stunning visuals with good actions are let down by a weak cast but entertaining to watch nevertheless.

title: Kind of good stuff...except for that dialogue thing.
review:
So you've waited three years after seeing "The Phantom Menace" and ended up bleary-eyed and with some trails of snot escaping from your nasal passages, well, don't worry, Episode II is actually a decent film.

As traditional Star Wars would have it, the movie is and has not only political themes but the audience once again has the opportunity to see more of the workings of the Jedi Order as is. Episode II's story line and plot are strong, held up by an elaborate and wonderful world that George Lucas created all those years ago. Another strong point to add is that, like in all the others in the Star Wars saga, we have a bevy of characters which we get to see. This adds to the diversity of the story and the plot and gives the movie watcher something more than just Character A and Character B...yay.

"Attack of the Clones" is visually stunning. Worlds, planetary systems, cities, everything is marvelous in the movie. Lucas' team of special effect afficionados do an extraordinary job of creating intense scenery and brilliant battle scenes. CGI characters and backdrops are at times shaky though, but it still does not do away with the kudos they deserve.

Some of the films weaknesses though are big ones. The dialogue in the movie is rather horrid, at times, almost childlike, laughable. It leaves the moviegoer with the question of whether Lucas can write or not. The acting at times is weak, Hayden Christiansen at times sounds awkward speaking his lines and overall demeanour don't seem natural at other times.

Overall the movie is quite enjoyable and is decent. Some of the jumps in plot and character development sometimes leave you with a cocked eyebrow but nothing so terrible that it will ruin the movie. I give it a 7.1/10.

Oh, and the musical score is great...

title: Go see the digital version!!!...
review:
I saw the digitally-projected "Attack of the Clones" high-definition version. and I was ASTOUNDED by it!

You won't believe the difference.

The visuals are MUCH more vivid. The effects seem to leap off the screen.

Cineplexes need to jump on the bandwagon and join the digital revolution. The cost to upgrade is well worth it.

title: Superb
review:
Not being a truly true fan of the Star Wars saga (I have only seen episode 4-6 four times each, I found Episode II to be the best of them all so far. The feeling was there, a perfect mood was set and the action was great. The sound and setting was so powerful, I sat i awe throughout the whole movie.

I got a bit sceptic when I first saw the "love story" trailer a while ago, but when I saw the movie, the whole love story fell nice into place with the rest of the plot. I got some of the same feelings as I did watching Lord of the rings and with Episode II still fresh in mind, I'm not sure which one I liked more. I think in fact Star Wars.

So don't mind some of the bad reviews. The people who don't like this movie, probably never understood what Star Wars was all about anyway.

title: This movie did so many things right...
review:
Nuance...Subtle...many words (big and small) can be used to put this movie in a positive light.

These are not the words of a Fanboy...I gave up on the franchise after Episode 1 like most fans of the series. Mr Lucas has won me back.

title: Yoda fights!!!!
review:
One thing that made me love this film. Yes you got it Yoda fights. It's cinematic history now we know why he is called master Yoda. Even though there were some idiots behind me in the cinema that started laughing when he walked into the room in still wasnt ruined when he whipped out his almighty lightsabre and rocked the party. They seemed to quiet down after that.

Another good sequence is when Anakin kills all them crazy looking things that killed his mum and while this was happening yoda was meditating and can just hear the deep breathing of darth vada

classic film that will be a force to be reckon with. can't wait for the dvd

title: Great CGI, but where's the script?
review:
Once again, the CGI is fantastic and the action scenes breathtaking. However, during the first hour I was amazed to find myself actually getting bored! The acting seemed to be labouring under delusions of being grandiose, but it came across as merely wooden and unconvincing, and the romance between Amidala and Anakin Skywalker didn't have the merest hint of life or originality. Nevertheless, Natalie Portman does the least bad job of everyone concerned and at least manages to salvage some sort of dignity. Oh, and looks quite pretty as well. :)

However, things perked up a bit in the second half when the war machine rumbled into life, and the fight between Yoda and Count Dooku has to be seen to be believed! There are some scenes which are fabulous to behold. You know they're not real, but still you're stunned anyway.

But when will Hollywood learn that flashy CGI is no substitute for a decent script? There's no excuse for spending millions on a film which has a line like (and I paraphrase) "sand is rough and gets everywhere. Not like you, you're smooth all over". Good god.

title: Choice eh Bro?
review:
Nah stay at home with ya frund in the frudge!

I remember seeing Star Wars in 1977 at Aldershot in the UK when I was 9. My father thought is was going the be tripe but we were all amazed by not only only the special effects but a great story line.

Fast forward to 2002. Phantom Menace was just pulp. Attack of the Clones just cheese. New Zealand colby at that.

I cannot take this film seriously. I laughed through most of it.Who in their right mind would a) cast Kiwi actors, b) then allow them to keep their accents, c) finally clone them!

2/10 (1 for the spaceships and 1 for the alien lesbian scene)

review: What can i say,if you read this and you havent saw the movie yet..what are you waiting for?!?! go and see it now!! the effects,the sounds,the story,the jokes...he's back! and George Lucas will give you an amazing more then 2 hours journey into the beginning of the end of the Galactic Republic. A true must for a Star Wars fan,a true must for a sci-fi fan and a true must for a movie lover!

title: A solid, respectable addition to the first trilogy, at least
review:
After the initial advertisements and generally condescending reviews, I was ready to concede that the only reason I was going to see "Star Wars II: Attack of the Clones" was to fulfill a societal obligation to yield to the Lucas franchise juggernaut and keep abreast of Star Wars lore so I wouldn't be blatantly ignorant. Well, after leaving a boring birthday party early and going to see it at Showcase Cinemas in Revere, MA at 7:15 p.m. on Sunday, May 19, 2002, my final evaluation of the movie, out of 4 stars, is 3-3.5 stars. Overall, the movie is a well-crafted, intelligent, and worthy addition to the Star Wars canon. I think it falls somewhat short of the IV-VI first trilogy (but then the initial trilogy is beyond emulation anyway), but, as others have noted, it is better than "Star Wars I: The Phantom Menace". Even in its own right, as a movie disconnected from the series progression, "Attack..." acquits itself well.

As a brief synopsis, as others have noted, "Attack..." is a tad slow and ponderous for the first half and exhilaratingly frenetic and dynamic in the second. The backgrounds, CGI work, visuals, other special effects, and general cinematography are superb, especially in the coliseum and final battle sequences. Not once did I feel any artificiality or "blue matte painting" unreality. It seemed logically real. Despite Roger Ebert's grumblings of vague, grainy, and obscure visuals, the movie looked bright and colorful enough to me (and I didn't see the digital version). The set pieces involving the "Fifth Element"esque chase by Obi-Wan and Anakin of the would-be assassin, Obi-Wan's battle with Jango Fett on the eternal waterworld, the conveyor belt ordeal Anakin and Amidala endure in the droid factory, and of course the "Gladiator" beast and droid/clone clash toward the end of the movie were pulse-pounding, energetic, and ultimately convincing.

The plot was convoluted and labyrinthine, to be sure, but quite comprehensible if one paid sufficient attention. I agree that the dialogue and other verbal exchanges were prosaic, pedestrian, and dull, but I believe that was so because of the dreaded portent of Anakin's (Hayden Christensen's) future descent into Darth Vader's nefariousness. I think neither the actors nor Lucas dared to add any levity to the movie because of this solemn main plot. I admit the lack of sprightly banter so prevalent in the first trilogy was a handicap, but not a fatal one. Also, Christensen's performance was not as horrendous, IMHO, as others had opined. Sure, he was an impudent, impatient whiner at times, but at others he eerily foreshadowed the monstrous villain he would become (as in the black cloak and sinister Darth Vader silhouette he sported on Tatooine). Also remember, although an accomplished Jedi apprentice, Anakin had not yet attained full knight status; add the facts that he is still in the throes of confused adolescence and identity, and I think one could find his willful, arrogant, conflicted behavior quite natural and expected. Luke Skywalker started out as a confused adolescent himself; remember how mature and serious he became in "Return of the Jedi".

Aside from the relatively uninspired banter, all the actors performed admirably, nobly and competently, especially Obi-wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor), Mace Windu (Samuel Jackson), and of course, the inimitable Yoda (voiced by Frank Oz). I even found Anakin's fitful romance with deposed Naboo queen/current Naboo senator Padme Amidala (Natalie Portman) generally charming, sweet, and pleasant, if awkward, but again, first love is almost always awkward and first lovers are usually not a font of eloquence. C3-PO (voice of Anthony Daniels) had some amusing moments, especially during his mind/body switch with a droid, as did the utterly dependable R2-D2 (Kenny Baker), especially during his flight sequence in the droid factory (question: did he lose his flight capabilities in IV-VI?) Even the universally loathed Jar Jar Binks (voice of Ahmed Best) was rather tolerable and even subdued at times, of course considering he had only three scenes or so. He goes down easy in small bites, but how in the galaxy did he become a Federation senator? Count Dooku (the immortal Christopher Lee) was an imposing villain, especially in his unforgettable showdown with an animated "whirling dervish" Yoda. I especially found his line "Obviously this battle will not be decided by knowledge of the Force, but by lightsabers", humorous; shouldn't it be the other way around? Ah, any excuse to rouse the philosophical little gremlin from his Buddist reverie! Yoda, of course, is the most memorable character and by now transcends description. CGI suits him well. My favorite line in the movie comes from him (and I paraphrase): "A planet Obi-Wan has lost, my students. Help him find it, we must!"

In conclusion, "Attack of the Clones" is a good movie that generally has nothing to be ashamed of. It delivers on all cinematic counts except sparkling dialogue and competently and mostly seamlessly advances the Star Wars mythos. Star Wars purists will most likely cherish it. I'm glad I saw it (not solely due to peer pressure) and it makes me avidly anticipate Episode III.

Good show (detractors notwithstanding)!

title: Only The Force Will Make This a Good Movie
review:
Have you ever had relatives or friends bring over slides of their vacation or their wonderful child's last ten birthdays? They walk in with eight slide carousels and regale you with still, flat, lifeless images for two hours and seven minutes? If so, you'll have a good sense of what it's like to sit through Attack of the Clones (AOTC). The film largely moves from one lifeless (and often truncated) scene to the next.

What about the story? The dissident separatists are fed up with the empire and want to leave, building a droid army to fight the good fight. The wonderful Republic tries to quell the insurrection with a clone army that, oddly enough, was ordered at the Clones-R-Us Drive-Thru planet ten years ago (won't spoil it by telling you why). Eventually they clash. The story of this celluloid trilogy is getting more involved politically, to be sure, and on a larger scale. However, this information is related to us by people sitting down and talking with each other, using valuable screen time that could be filled with something we actually cared about. Too much time is wasted with lifeless exposition that would send the worst insomniac into a coma.

On the other hand, the characters were all over the galaxy. Everyone split up and went in many different directions, with the film jumping back and forth, here and there, one hyperjump after another. Each scene ended quickly, often before it was finished. Many of the scenes were jammed in between other scenes, and did not seem to relate to the story. The entire sequence that tells the story of Aniken searching out his mother could have been left on the cutting room floor, and told through one scene lasting 30 seconds. Another pointless scene occurs when Aniken and Amidala end up in a droid factory, evading molten steel and giant chopping meat cleavers. Whole sections of this scene were taken from Bugs Bunny cartoons (which did it much better). This entire sequence (and many others in the film) just didn't make sense. Why do I get the distinct impression that this is here only to sell an upcoming video game?

The worst tragedy of AOTC, however, is the characters. In the original Star Wars films, Lucas and the actors created excellent characters that we were interested in, that we cared about, and wanted to see succeed. They were mixed up in a political situation, much like this new trilogy, but the political story was told through the characters' more personal involvement. And what kinds of people were Luke, Han Solo, Princess Leia, and Chewbacca? They were much more real. They were funny, providing lots of effective comedy, even in the middle of great hardship. They got angry, they became sad, they were determined, they were scared, yet persevered despite the odds against them. You saw this, and you believed it, despite the Ewoks. Even the bad guys were believable and scary. Darth Vader is a masterpiece of villainy. Even Greedo, the sneaky little bounty hunter that cornered Han Solo in the Cantina seemed like a real bad guy (though somewhat rubberized).

The `characters' in AOTC, however, deliver all their lines in the same fretful, stoic, monotone. All of them, not just one actor. Hayden Christensen, who plays a teenage Aniken, did not deliver a single believable line during the entire film. Natile Portman listens to Aniken's tale of how he just committed genocide on a tribe of Tusken Raiders, and then kisses him to comfort him. These are the actions of a senator? Of a real person with a brain? Soap operas have more passion, acting, and make more sense (although, to be fair, this is as much the fault of the writer and director, both George Lucas). Any good characters in the film? C3PO and R2D2 were the only comedy in the film and the only likeable characters that seemed to have any substance. Even they were hamstrung by Lucas, having small roles and delivering lines that Henny Youngman would have turned down as being too corny.

What's good about this film? How does it compare to the first? It is marginally better than Phantom Menace, in the way that the earlier episodes of Gilligan's Island were marginally better than the later ones. The visuals (slides in our show) are more striking and complete, with sets that seem less forced and give the film a richer feel. You are placed more effectively in the setting. It was nice to see Yoda come out and do something other than sit in a chair (and the audience loved this as well). However, he looked more like a chimp on crack with a light saber than a Jedi Knight. His silly, hyperactive jumping about did not make us believe in his great power because they had no effect on the bad guy. If you can get by with flashy lights and sci-fi accoutrements, you'll be fine.

In the end, we really don't care if the characters live or die. They contain as much life as the digital backdrops created for the film, and the only thing keeping us in our seats are the stunning visuals and the hope that something real might happen in the next scene before it is abruptly cut off, whisking us away to some other part of the galaxy. Is the republic in danger? Perhaps. Are there bad guys that need putting down? Maybe. Are there heroes that will save the day? Not really. Will we get advance tickets and wait in line for the third installment? Not a chance. I've learned my lesson on that account. Maybe George Lucas will learn his and create a real movie experience next time, but don't bet on it. He'll need to Force to make the finale of this trilogy more than a rental.

title: different from the old movies but just great
review:
SPOILERS ALERT It was just after midnight (local time 9 hrs ahead of LA) when they started the movie. Since I had the chance to see the original English version, the cinema was not too crowded. Germans had the chance to watch their translated version in several other the theatre rooms in this place.

Many of them where surprised when the traditional yellow words in the beginning were in German, but as on many DVDs they show us the German version with English sound and some English subtitles were they need to be. Titles are not in English though.

The main story of Episode II tells us about Anakin Skawalker (the later Darth Vader) and his trainer Obi Wan Kenobi. The upcoming lovestory between Anakin and the Senator Padme Amidala is another part of it, but many visitors did not like the too romantic pictures. There were just too many flowers and waterfalls involved in this romance.

The main story starts with an attack on Senator Amidalas Spaceship at the arrival at Coruscant. The Jedi decide after this to give her protection by Obi Wan and Anakin. They stayed on guard in her apartment when a drone inserts two large poisoness insects through a hole in the window of her bedroom. The two Jedi saved her live and got hold of the assassin after a wild race through rush hour traffiv in 3D (similar as in the 5th Element with Bruce Willis).

After this the two Jedi split and Anakin travels with Padme to Naboo, while Obi Wan visits a hidden planet somewhere in deep space.

There are later large battles in this movie, but none of it takes place in space. I do not want to tell You everything, but it will get louder and faster through the last 30 minutes.

After the end of the movie people were sitting motionless in their chairs and watch each and every name that scrolled across the screen. I am not used to visitors doing this but I think it was just because of the overwhelming speed and action in it. They just were not ready to go home immediately. Finaly at 2:35 AM we had to go - it was over and the curtain was closed.

I will see this movie again, maybe this afternoon - you can get addicted to it, so watch out!

title: Better than Episode One, but plot-holes need to be resolved
review:
Much in the same vein as Episode 1, there were many scenes which, if removed, would've made the movie much better. However, there were fewer of these than there were in E1, and overall I thought E2 was *much* better than E1. I didn't think 3-PO was all that funny, but as a forced comic-relief character he wasn't nearly as annoying as Jar Jar. It's also ironic/very Lucas that Jar Jar is indirectly responsible for ultimately creating the Empire.

I liked the little boy who played Boba Fett; you can already tell he's going to be an a$$hole. And I thought they did a good job finally having (Jango) Fett do something. And he finally used his flame-thrower! :)

Obi-Wan was solid; so was Dooku. Anakin/Padme were pretty lame, as were all of those horrible scenes on Padme's homeworld. Take every scene on that planet out of E1 and E2 and both movies are better for it. Anakin almost redeemed himself when he slaughtered those Sandpeople, but the whining afterword kind-of spoiled it. And what is Padme thinking falling in love with this psychopath? Yoda, needless to say, kicked a$$.

There are still several large continuity plot-holes that need to be resolved between the original Trilogy and the two new movies.

Anakin to Padme: "Hey darling, why didn't you freakin' buy my mother out of slavery ten years ago?"

Why do the neither of the droids remember Tatooine, Obi-Wan, or Owen/Bertru Lars? A memory wipe at some point is really the only answer ...

But more to the point, why do Owen Lars/Obi-Wan not remember anything about these droids at the beginning of Episode 4 (New Hope)? I know it's been a long time between E2 and E4, but c'mon. Owen could say something like: "Gee Luke, that's funny, when your father was here 20 years ago, he had two droids with him that were exactly like these two." Also, why does Obi-Wan decide to hide Luke on Tatooine knowing full-well that Anakin not only grew up there, but has in fact been to the Lars' house before?

I carefully watched (geek alarm) the first hour of E4 last night, and Obi-Wan states that he doesn't remember owning any droids (despite R2D2 claiming to be Obi-Wan's property). 3-P0 clearly says that he doesn't know what planet he's on, that his first job was as a "botchi translator for binary load lifters" and that his (and R2's) previous owner was Captain Antilles. He implies multiple times that he and R2 have been working together for some time. Also, Obi-Wan is referred to as "General Kenobi" by Leia, and Obi-Wan tells Luke that his father "wanted him to have" the lightsaber. Just some things to consider.

Of course, my explanation is still that Lucas had no idea he was going to make any more movies after E4 and that therefore everything he's done since then is revisionism ... which of course gets harder to pull off the more you try to incorporate it. Especially with Lucas' unnecessary style of trying to make *everything* tie together.

Finally, I still maintain that the stormtroopers in the original Trilogy are NOT clones.

title: ouch!... but...
review: (this mentions an important , although not surprising, appearance of a major character late in the film, although it doesn't give away what happens) The first 20-25 minutes of the "love story" were soooo painful. Hard to know whether to fault the actors or simply bad writing. BUT... it definitely picked up, and actually had a Parisian audience applauding by the time Yoda steals the show.  So just bear with it, especially if you are a Yoda fan. (also problems that plagued the Phantom Menace in terms of suspicious accents continues to be a problem, although perhaps slightly less glaringly so.)

title: Getting Better
review:
It was with great anticipation and slight trepidation that I sat down to watch the latest installment of the Star Wars saga. I was desperately hoping to see a marked improvement since "The Phantom Menace" and fortunately, this was the case. At least I didn't slip into a boredom induced coma within the first half hour!

I did find myself cringing quite frequently at the irritating dialogue, especially in scenes between Senator Padme (Armadillo?!) and Anakin Skywalker. Their entire love story was such a cliche and one major cheese fest I am sorry to say. The scene with them rolling around in the grass together almost pushed me over the edge and I was expecting at any minute for them to start running in slow-motion while little bunny-rabbits skipped around their feet. Hayden Christensen (Anakin) was as wooden an actor as you could ever hope not to see. His facial expressions were so overly dramatic that I couldn't help feeling he belonged in an American daytime soap-opera like "Days of our Lives." He certainly left a great deal to be desired.

I have to admit to having a real problem with Ewan Mcgregor playing Obi-Wan Kenobi as well. I think he is a fantastic actor and puts in a valiant effort here but for me, he just doesn't cut it as a young Alec Guinness somehow.

Having said all this, I did genuinely enjoy the film. The special effects were awesome to say the least, if not somewhat reminiscent of "The Fifth Element" at times. The fight sequences were brilliant - the joy at seeing not only men, but women wielding a lightsaber in battle and I have yet to recover from the thrill of seeing Mater Yoda bouncing off the walls during his battle with Count Dooku (silly name)!

On the whole this was an incredibly enjoyable film. It is certainly not up to the standards of the original trilogy but then, nothing ever will be in my eyes. It is certainly worth going to see, if only to see Yoda kicking some arse! I am intrigued now to see the third installment and how Anakin finally turns to the dark side. I recommend watching the film with an open mind and try not to compare too much with the original trilogy as you will most likely be disappointed. Just bear in mind, while watching the love scenes, that it will not go on like that forever, no matter how much it may seem that way! "Attack of the Clones" is pure entertainment.

title: A fine return to form
review:
I will comment in two sections - the first will be a general review for those who have yet to see Episode II and the second will be a little more detailed with spoilers. Here are my thoughts:

This film is a spectacular return to form for the series. After a great-looking Episode I that seemed to lack the "fun" of the originals, Lucas brings the goods in fine summer blockbuster fashion. No, this movie doesn't have the greatest dialog or characterization but then is that what we are looking for in these things? No, we go to these films (though it's more of a "movie" than a "film") to be entertained and here Episode II more than succeeds. There is more humor this time around (courtesy of a credible performance by Ewan McGregor) and the plot twists hold your attention much better than in Episode I. But the real stars of the show have to be the fine folks at Industrial Light & Magic. Their performance is impeccable - rendering surrealities full of wonder and action-sequences that leave you breathless. Speaking of which, if the last roughly an hour or so of this movie don't get your blood racing then you may just be dead. Overall, I had a great time and it was certainly worth the $7 paid to get in. I can't say that for a lot of films these days.

*********SPOILERS ALERT****SPOILERS ALERT*********







This film isn't going to win any awards for its acting but the rest of it picks up the slack admirably. Yes, it is rather obvious that Natalie Portman and Hayden Christensen have zero on-screen chemistry (that fireplace scene is almost embarrasing and sure to be remembered come Razzies awards time). But I think Christensen had better chances than her and his admission to the Tusken Raider massacre did have a little more going for it in the emotional department (he really is a brooding guy with lots of issues). Fortunately, Ewan McGregor and Christopher Lee put their all behind their characters making up for the flatness of the two leads. I particularly thought McGregor added a great deal to the film - he really does seem like a young Ben Kenobi/Alec Guinness (with that sage wisdom starting to permeate). His quick British wit also made for some needed comic relief (the Jedi mind-trick on the "death sticks" dealer in the nightclub is classic Obi-Wan). Christopher Lee makes for a great villain while Darth Sideous has taken a back-seat in this Episode (I think he has only 1 or 2 scenes of unbridled evil - too bad since he added so much to Episode I). Of course, what everyone is talking about is Yoda's "performance" at the climax of the movie. I think it's interesting that people laughed at first at his posturing but the light saber duel he has with Lee is astonishing. The FX are, of course, top-notch with an attention to detail and fluidity that other movies can only dream of. It's amazing that ILM can make the Phantom Menace look dated (considering its only a few years old) but they do that here. John William's score is another highlight with lots of gothic themes and reprises from the original series (including the Force theme and Darth Vader's famous march set to Yoda's comment "begun, this Clone War has" with ship after ship of Clone Troopers taking off to do battle against the Trade Federation). The ubiquitous racing scene near the beginning wasn't as impressive as the pod race from Episode I but then you kinda got two-races-for-one in this movie with another harrowing run through an asteroid field (which admittedly blows away the asteroid chase in The Empire Strikes Back). The important thing is most people left the theater satisfied and excited. That is the purpose of "entertainment". I am pleased to see the "franchise" doing this well and it almost bothers me to think there will only be one more. We should get the chance to delve into the Star Wars universe every couple of years just for the escapism (something kinda like the Olympics which we could look forward to). Great job Lucasfilm and I look forward to Episode III.

title: The best Star Wars film ever
review:
Depending on your point of view, Attack of the Clones must either be the best Star Wars film ever, or the second best after The Empire Strikes Back.

Full of breathtaking imagery, sumptuous visual storytelling, genuinely epic battle scenes, a Star Wars love story AND a Star Wars detective story, plus trademark rubbish dialogue, I would find it very difficult to be friends with someone who didn't like this movie.

Why is it so good? It fulfils everything anyone would ever expect of a movie. It contains genuinely fantastic action sequences, iconic moments which you'll be talking about for the rest of your life, characters you care about, good handling of plot and story, and breathtaking special effects. The final battle makes it the Saving Private Ryan of fantasy films. Plus - and this is most important - it moves people. It may move them to tears, if they're that way inclined, but at the very least it makes people laugh out loud from sheer joy, in a way I personally haven't done since the helicopter crash in The Matrix. This is something movies can do that "serious" films cannot - inspire awe. And AOTC is one of the most awe-inspiring movies ever made. Phantom Menace doubters can rest easy, and Phantom Menace apologists such as myself are vindicated. This is the kind of movie that will win MTV awards and Empire awards, but never Oscars, because the Acadamy looks for "inspiration" and "pathos" without ever giving "joy", "wonderment", or "Jesus Christ, did you see that?!" a second thought. Sod them. Go see it, then see it again.

Star Wars perfection. Roll on 2005.

title: The Force is BACK!!!
review:
Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones was perhaps the best Star Wars film out of the whole series. George Lucas surly shows off his true talents in this film. The idea to film this movie completly digitally was sheer genius. It is a shame that Star Wars Episode I: Tha Phantom Menace wasn't shot in digital. Episode II had perhaps the best action sequences I have ever seen in a movie. The lightsabre battles were sheerly amazing. Despite all the machines that do not exist the machines and crafts all looks pretty damn real.

I also liked the fact how George Lucas used past Star Wars characters, vehicles, and space stations. By doing this it links all the Star Wars movies making the series easier to believe that it is one saga. Lucas did a good job, by not creating the image that all Star Wars movies are just different movies with the same characters. GOOD JOB! GEORGE!!!!

I am greatly looking forward to Star Wars Episode III, perhaps the darkest chapter of the saga!

title: Some additional points
review:
Just a few comments to add:

First, the title is taking a lot of heat, but remember, Lucas has said that one big inspiration for him was the early sci-fi serials, and "Attack of the Clones" is dead-on for a serial title (think Flash Gordon or Commando Cody).

Second, yes, some of the dialog is a bit wooden. But no more than that in the original three. Come on, how original is "What took you so long? Uh, we ran into some old friends."?

Third, has anyone else noticed the "Ray Harryhausen Homage" scene? The monsters in the coliseum are very close to the old stop-motion monsters and especially ObiWon menacing the crab-monster with a spear is right out of "Mysterious Island".

Overall, a great movie, especially for fans of the first 3.

title: Saruman strikes back!
review:
*Minor Spoilers*

I have to say I was very worried when waiting to get into the 12:01am showing of Episode 2: "Would it be as flat and lifeless as the Episode 1" "Will the plot live up to the original three"

When the movie began, it did start off slowly, even murder attempts and the discussions leading up to the chase at the start seemed a little flat. Thankfully the uneven pacing of the first third of the movie disappeared when the characters seemed to settle in to their roles. Christensen was quite good as Anakin, much better than Jake Lloyd. I suppose he has a lot more to work with since his Anakin is older and has more depth, even so some of his lines were a little lacking. That said I think he is a stronger actor than Natalie Portman. Many of her lines were compitent but lacked in projection, thankfully she has ditched her silly snooty accent and is just speaking normally.

On the topic of accents Ewan McGregor's is forced (no pun intended) but his lines have improved considerably.

Jar Jar has only a handful of lines, but he actually does work quite well and has the dubious honour of inadvertantly setting the empire in place.

Now I could go on for a long time speaking about Yoda's swishy jumpy saber elite skills, the clearly kiwi Boba Fett (such a little tyke), the vast array of Australians in supporting roles, or finally seeing a multitude of alien Jedi (hopefully episode III will have some dual wielding Twi'Lek's), but the part that truely made this movie a worth prequel was Christopher Lee. His portrayal of Saruman in Lord of the Rings compliments this perfectly, as essentially it is the same role hehe. Let that detract nothing from him as Count Dooku. Whereas Darth Maul was just a ninja with a scary(?) face, Dooku is dripping with evil and for a man of 80 he handles a lightsaber (or lightscimitar as then handle is bent) better than anyone in the series so far.

So with high spirits I can heartily recommend this film to all but the most cynical of critics.

title: GREAT MOVIE
review:
Episode II is really good, George Lucas did a great job and so did the actors.

I was some what disapointed of Episode I, for the acting and some of the special effects. However Episode II actors and special effects complement prefectly the story.

If I had to say a sad point, I found the "love story" in the center of the movie a little to long.

Great Job George Luca

title: Nice Star Wars feel, but does NOT live up to the hype!
review:
This film does NOT live up to the hype. It is NOWHERE NEAR on a par with "The Empire Strikes Back", and it's not as good as either "A New Hope" or "Return of the Jedi". The film is spoilt by flat acting in both the opening stages and the love scenes (Hayden Christensen is a little wooden when it comes to the film romance). There is also, once again, a heavy over-reliance on CGI; so much so that you sometimes think you could be watching "Who Framed Roger Rabbit". This film could take lessons from "Dog Soldiers" in the artistic and subtle use of computer effects, combined with excellent REAL COSTUMES!!!

On the positive side of things though, this film was nowhere near as bad as "The Phantom Menace". I actually enjoyed "Attack of the Clones" to the extent that I've awarded it a grudging 7/10. There is a definite Star-Warsey feel to the film once you get past the dreadful opening stages (spoilt by the wooden acting more than anything else) and it begins to gather momentum. This time there is a story that manages to arouse your curiosity, leaving many questions to be answered by the film as it goes along (and most of them are answered, but not necessarily in an obvious way). It was almost like watching a detective story, apart from the annoying interruptions of the flat love scenes with Christensen and Portman. The film becomes progressively darker as it draws towards its conclusion, and is permeated by undertones reminiscent of "The Empire Strikes Back". Hayden Christensen, whilst playing a wooden 'love-struck' role, becomes quite convincing as an Anakin Skywalker gradually succumbing to the dark side of the Force. Christopher Lee's "Count Dooku" (unfortunate name that) character is excellent, and his battle with Yoda is a must see. To say that Yoda is pretty nifty with a lightsabre once he chucks his walking stick away, would be an understatement! Euan McGregor has begun to shine as Obi Wan Kenobi, and Jungu Fett is also a character that assisted the film in coming together, along with little 'Boba'. Questions related to the origin of the Stormtrooper army in Episodes 4, 5 and 6 are undisputedly answered!

Anyway, to conclude, there are a couple of pointless scenes, but nowhere near as many as in TPM. Lucas has definitely put the story first this time over the imagery of his imagination. A final plus point is that you hardly ever see Jar Jar Binks (I reckon he gets about 10 minutes screen time, tops, and hardly ever speaks - thank God! All he needs now is a laserbolt to the head). His childish antics have been replaced by the tried and tested combination of R2 and 3PO, although some of their scenes are cliched from the original films which spoils things a touch.

title: It must be sad being a movie critic
review:
The original three Star Wars pretty much got slaughtered by the world press. Later, in the 90s - the 80s "Star Wars hangover" had deteriorated, and these critics must have felt criminally unhip when the 70s' and 80s' teenagers had grown to intelligent, young people who STILL proclaimed the Star Wars triology as one of the few essential film-experiences.

They must've felt so let out! And most of them - of course - later talk of the original three as movie classics.

Now, they've blown it again. As most of us SW fans agree that this movie is definitively up there with the original trilogy, and a far jump from the pathetic tripe that Ep. 1 was, they actually manage to give this movie a worse review than Ep. 1 (!!).. as well as even trying to convince us that this film "doesn't even convey the traditional Star Wars feeling for the fans". Oh, really?

Imagine working with popular film, and so obviously revealing that one doesn't have the slightest clue as to what film experiences are really all about?

Anyway: This movie is really, really good. It gave me the feeling I hoped for for Ep. 1: "Star Wars - is back". I know SW fans don't like Lucas' term "space opera" :D, but we all know that the storyline is supposed to be a bit over-dramatic and the acting over-dramatised. It is, after all, the ultimate space drama.

title: This sorry mess of a movie
review: From the unconvincing assassination scene at the beginning, to the attempt to emulate TESB at the end, this dull, unexciting movie had most of the audience in The Ritzy, Brixton, London, in fits of laughter at each fresh, clunky plot turn, or tired, dated old cliche (Anakin has a bad dream...). Although the FX are 2nd to none, and the fights, space battle and general pyrotechnics are superb, what this sorry mess of a movie lacks is a heart, a centre, someone about whom we can care. Cos God love him, not only has the Anakin character become a crashing bore, but Hayden Christiansen just cannot act. Not at all. Not one little bit. And he's more or less swallowed up by all the crash bang whizzery that surrounds him and his cohorts; Ewan Mc Gregor's Obi Wan is more dull and humourless than ever, Natalie Portman struggles gamefully with the terrible dialogue but in the end does all her emoting through her hair, and the various others involved (Samuel L and Christopher Lee especially) simply fax their performances in. One the minus side, bad dialogue, bad acting, no narrative, on the plus, top FX and a great sabre fight from Yoda. Which earns it 4 out of 10. And that's being generous...

title: Jedi Mind Tricks
review:
I watched this movie having been told by someone I trust that it was almost as good as the first Star Wars (episode IV, not episode I). I don't trust him any more.
