title: Vast Improvement over Episode 1
review:
I have seen the movie twice now and after seeing it a second time, I'm thrilled to see how much of an improvement Lucas did over Episode one. Unlike most of the overly harsh critics, I see genuine improvement in several areas. In addition to the improvements in character development and visual effects, the aspect of parallelism within the series is present specifically in regard to Empire Strikes Back. If you go back and look at the two movies, you see how Lucas patterned Attack of the Clones just like Empire Strikes Back right down to the ending. Just take a close look and you'll see.

The visual effects were excellent as always and the ending battle was probably one of the most impressive uses of CGI along with Lord of the Rings and the Matrix. The lightsaber fight once again went over the top of the beginning trilogy, but was incredibly well done. Yoda particularly puts any of the previous lightsaber fights outside of the Kenobi-Vader in Star Wars to shame.

The character development is much better and is not as stale as Episode One. Hayden Christenson does an excellent job presenting the conflicted, tormented Anakin. I actually enjoyed the romantic development between Anakin and the beautiful, alright outright gorgeous Natalie Portman as Padme. From what I remember, Anakin was 9 in Episode 1 and Padme 13, so its not that much of an age difference. Any romantic relationship during the late teens-early adult years is awkward (I would know). Lucas could have made it a little deeper, but that too is to be seen how it will develop in the third episode. Ewan McGregor is fitting in nicely as Obi-Wan Kenobi. I feel he still needs the last movie to develop into the Obi-Wan we loved as Sir Alec Guinness. Christopher Lee is excellent as Count Dooku and brings in an excellent new villain that we can all hate.

One of the best things that Lucas does is finally tie some ends together and brings about some developments that will close the entire series together. I'm sure many die hards are disappointed because of their incredibly high expectations. Let me say this, why can't people just love a movie for what it is and be happy with what we're getting. Lucas wasn't even going to do these movies and we should be thankful that he has done so much. So please be appreciative of what we're being given. Episode 3 will tie everything together and I can't wait for it. I plan on seeing the movie a few more times to finally pick up any missed references to the other Star Wars movies and see what direction Lucas is going to take in the last Episode.

title: Am I immune?
review: I am awfully sorry, but I was really hoping that Clones would be better than Menace and it wasn't.  I thought it was 45 minutes too long, too dreary, too confusing and the action too concentrated at the end...and worst of all, I didn't care what happened.  Oh...and that Anakin bloke really began to get on my nerves, especially as he was out-acted by the scenery.  Sorry!  I am 41 and maybe seeing Episode IV 25 years ago spoiled me!

title: The force is with us all now - 4 star review
review:
So, what did I think about Episode 2: Attack of the Clones? Why would you even care what I have to say? Well, I think you should care what I have to say, because I am a Star Wars Fan. I waited in line to see the 12:01 showing in Westwood at the Village MANN with about 1200 other fans and I have to say it was a blast. First, let's talk about the action sequences...

They were terrific. Here is a list of the five best and in the order I think they are in

I) Yoda kicking Dooku's butt II) The Scene in the Gladiator Hole III)The battle in the Rain IV) Obi-Wan chasing Jango Fett through the Astroids V) The opening scene with the speed racer chase

The Romance:

Though cheesy and cliched, I still found it to be a real hoot. Lines like "Your skin is soft" and "You'll always be the small boy on Tatanoone" were great, though kinda silly.

The Obi-Wan/Anikan relationship:

At the heart of the movie is this relationship. Here is where we can see the evolution of the future to come. The dialogue between them is great: "Why do I feel you'll be the death of me?" was one of the best lines in the whole serise of films. Expect great things to happen in Episode III.

The story:

The reason most people didn't like Episode I was because it wasn't a "movie", it was the prolouge for a longer movie - All the Star Wars films combined. So this one had more of an arch because the ground work was layered and the abilities of Lucus were at full throttle now that he could have some fun with rousing action sequences and a silly romance that would set forth the destiny of the Skywalker clan. So this story felt more together and richly designed. A wonderful film!

Overall rating - * * * * Stars (1-4 scale)

title: The clones strikes back
review:
With AOTC Lucasfilm did not make the same mistake as they did in 1999. The movie opened in 30something countries on the same day, and fortunately in Europe we ( first time in history ) were able to see it 6 hours before than our american friends. Honestly I did see the movie on Tuesday on the media screening.

As far as I can tell, this is the 2nd best SW movie of all time. The first is TESB of course, normally ROTJ would be the best, but I cannot forgive for the ewoks ( me dislike plush bears ).

If TPM had two good action sequence ( pod race and the "duel of fates" ), AOTC has 5 and all of them are fantastic, the chase on Coruscant, Jungo/Obi Wan, Asteroid field sequence, droid factory, and the last twentysomething minutes from the arena to the hangar scene with Obi wan/Anakin/Yoda and Dooku.Yoda is fighting, do I have to say more ? :o)

The scenic bombs ( or what are they call them ) are truly impressive, but I have to confess, the movie is nothing but a CGI orgy for your eyes and the sound effects for your ears.

Meanwhile there is some story of course :o))

The story is developing, in this episode we got some really nice backgrounds for the Ep. IV/V/VI. And I really curious about EP III. because so much to tell.

As usual Palpatine is tricky, I missed Sidious a lot ( I did hope for more than one time, I wait for the DVD ), and the actors are not bad. This is a Star Wars movie, not W.Shakespeare, so do not expect really clever dialogues with depth.

As I read here at imdb, the same thing happened as in Hungary ( and I think globally ), a lot of people liked the movie and a lot really bashing it for several reason ( the critics never liked SW at all ).

There is some thing to understand why we are like this movie ( of course much-much more than TPM ):

  • we tried really hard not to grow up


  • we would like to love this movie, with Ep I. it was not really easy, but this one delivers the stuff you expecting from a SW movie.


A lot of people would like to have the same euphory from these movies what they had, when Ep IV/V/VI came out. It won't happen. When I did see the first time the first SW movie ( Ep IV as we now that now ) I was 11 years old. That was almost 23 years ago. Since then I did not aged a bit, I am able to see the new ones with a child's eyes.

Certainly I do like movies with meaning, I do like movies with much better plot and acting.

But this is Star Wars for christ's sake :o))

This is a tale about bad and good, in a galaxy far far away.

What did you expect ? :o)

I did get what I wanted, and I am very happy with the results.

With this background Ep III will be very dark, and the hardcore fans will be more than delighted.

title: The 4th greatest of the series
review:
First of all, I regard the first trilogy (4,5,6) with such respect and awe that I really don't think that any movie will ever top the grandeur of them. Even with the amazement I have at Lucas' genius for creating the story I was one of the many who were disappointed with his Phantom Menace. It had its moments, but overall it fell far short of the most remedial expectations one could have for 20 years of story plotting. So after the 99' disappointment I didn't have very high expectations for Episode II. Even though I got the same feeling I did while watching PM - that there was just a bit too much CGI, I REALLY enjoyed this movie. And I had made up my mind that I was going to be very critical. Well, Star Wars got a little bit of its magic back. That special feeling that you only get when you watch a SW movie. There were some amazing moments in the movie that I didnt see coming that really did work - Anakins telling of the sand people incident.. the last shot of Boba.. Yoda, nuff said.. and the early reference to the Death Star was pure GENIUS.. I think either by blind luck or maybe a sudden realization, Lucas got back to what, in the end made the original series stand the test of time and it wasn't the special effects, because effects of sw were soon outdone and it wasn't the acting (never been one of starwars strongpoints with the exception of a few characters) but the friggin story!! Thats whats so amazing about the series, and I was into the story the whole time.

The main criticism of the movie thus far seems to be of the love story. True, the script does have its problems, particularly in the love scenes but it actually did not bother me that much. I just kept thinking, this guy is gonna be Darth Vader, and that kept me going during those scenes.. sounds a little strange I know but hey whatever works.

I think if I had to pick a main fault of the series thus far it would have to be lack of character development. You just don't care about these characters like you did Leia and Han and Luke and Chewy. You don't feel like you know them... particularly my biggest complaint is with Amidala, I dont think enough meat has been given to her character but perhaps I am jumping ahead of myself and should just wait till 2005.

But anyway, I think its a great addition to the series, though still far behind Jedi, (My ranking being Empire-1st......A New Hope-2nd.....Jedi-3rd........AttackotC-4th.........PM-5th..

title: If you're a fan, you should like it!
review:
I say that admirably. For all these people who keep proclaiming themselves to be huge fans of Star Wars but continually critique the saga as it unfolds, you're not really Star Wars fans -- you're Han Solo fans. If you read through these comments, you'll notice that the people who didn't like Episode 2 all had one complaint: no Han Solo.

Well, sorry kids, but he hasn't been born yet. Furthermore, this is a time when the Jedi would not converse with scoundrels like Han Solo. Everyone keeps saying Lucas is screwing up, but wouldn't it be counterfeit of him to insert a random cynical character (as a main character especially) into the universe simply because the fans desired it.

This is a different time than the first three movies. Enjoy watching the history of the universe unfold and stop wishing that Star Wars was a universe filled only with sarcasm and the void of your own imagination.

title: Thank you Mr. Lucas
review:
my favorite star wars yet! the attention to detail in this episode is...unparalleled. stunning.

just plain remarkable.

title: Except for Anakin as Pinocchio.....
review:
...the movie wasn't bad. Christensen had been so hyped, and he was AWFUL!!! Made of wood. Of course, his dialogue left much to be desired, but even so, he is simply a whiny mama's boy. Portman wasn't a whole lot better; Obi was terrific. More Obi, less Anakin, please.

and oh yes.....

GO YODA!!

title: FABULOUS ADDITION TO THE FIRST TRILOGY!!!
review:
I went into the theater hoping for the best...and what I got was the BEST!! Excellent film~if you are the most critical filmgoer who is an avid Star Wars fan~you will not be disappointed!!

The plot is marvelous! Bringing together both trilogies in characters, battles, and fantastic sequences--George Lucas has stirred the audiences once again with his tale of love, hatred, good, and bad. I do not want to give anything away. Two words--SEE IT!!! :)

title: This movie truly sucked ass.
review:
OK, so it wasn't as bad as Episode I, but what is? I can't believe all the things that sucked. The color. The dialogue. The pacing. The confused story. The non-acting.

I wasted two and a half hours just to see Yoda kick ass? That's the only thing I enjoyed. I wonder if Lucas asked everyone to act like robots so his CGI robots would look more real. Christopher Lee was the only one who actually ACTED and CHANGED FACIAL EXPRESSION in the whole movie? Did he just miss the memo that said, "Everything from starships to flying cars to actors movements will be CGI. Just stand there and don't worry about anything. Just read the script in a monotone."

And I'd ask questions about the missing plot, but who cares? It was just about one of the worst love stories I've ever seen and a bunch of washed out battle scenes.

I was told that the battle scene was good, but it looked almost cartoonish in its lack of color depth. Give Lucas some film and tell him to try it again. Digital, schmigital.

title: Brilliant, Stunning an Absolute Success
review:
Star Wars is my life. I have ate, slept, breathed and dreamed about Star Wars for the better part of my 26 years. I have grown so attached to this piece of cinematic genius over the years it's hard for me to separate Galaxy from Reality sometimes. When I was 13 years old or so My father took me to see Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade, while we were there he mentioned to me that "They" were making a movie about Darth Vader before he went bad, when he was still a kid. That day set into motion nearly a decade of anxiety and anticipation to the likes never imagined before my mortal man.

Cut to May 1999. 1st reaction was extreme and bitter disappointment. Episode One had failed. What happened to my Tie Fighters, Storm Troopers and X-Wings? After the dust had settled and I had seen the movie a couple more times, I learned to accept that there was no way a movie made 20 years after it's original was going to hold entirely true to it's roots, I faced the fact that Lucas needed to use every bit of new technology in the making Episode One as he did in making A New Hope. But most importantly, what I think we all looked past was, Lucas did what he needed to do. Episode One needed to tell a story, set a stage if you will and I think it did exactly that. Now enough of Episode One, this is the era of the Clone.

I went to the Premier at 12 Midnight and the turnout was nothing short of Grand. One by one we filed into the theater, a very surreal atmosphere surrounding the group for we all new why we were there. In a matter of minutes we would be subject to the the most outstanding display of Motion Picture Brilliance ever to be projected on the Silver Screen. From the moment that LUCASARTS faded into the screen in it's Wizard of Oz like Emerald glow to the Fateful kiss between Skywalker and Amidala I was a kid again. I watched in awe, jaw wide open, eyes bugging. Every saber clash, every note, every tone was perfect.

Three years ago I walked out the EP1 and looked at my cousin and said "I can't believe I have to wait three years for Episode II" and now I can only echo those same words again. What am I going to do for three years? Wait I guess? What else can I do?

May The Force Be With Me 'cause I am gonna be a basketcase.

title: A great ride
review: Going from ROJ to PM it seemed that ol' George found a formula...a multi-tiered finally, a "primitive" under-dog army, and angered fans...well AOTC George found his magic again !!!  A great story, paced superb, and that gut feel that you got at the end of ESB, where you can't believe you have three years.  Hopefully the ranch remembers not to "Soprano" us, and tie up the loose ends.  BTW, beware of MACE :

title: Solid improvement from episode I. Worth your ticket price!!
review:
George Lucas comes through on his sequel from his much loved Star Wars stories. Giving the fans many tasty treats in this latest installment.

Without giving away any plots (incase your one of the very and I mean very few who haven't seen this movie yet!) The fans dreams and wishes were heard by Lucas when he penned this story.

If you hated Jar Jar Binks from the first film, good news. The happy and goofy Gunjan is gone, err... not totally but he was tastefully given a very brief and should I say important role in the film.

Without wrecking the story. Let's just say he has a major historical effect on what we now know as the empire in the later film's.

His on screen presence is maybe 4 minutes total throughout the whole film and he doesn't "spech" err. speak nearly as much as his episode I role.

Special effects have to be the best that I have ever seen in a Star Wars film let alone any film of this size. If you miss this or are just waiting for it on video, that really a shame! Your missing probably the 2nd best film out of the series! (Empire strikes back is my favorite). Have fun and hope you enjoy this masterpiece!!!

title: Fun for all!
review: I am a huge Star Wars fan and really enjoyed this movie. So did everyone I saw it with.  I firmly believe though that even regular fans will have a lot of fun at this movie.  This movie is in my opinion the best Star Wars since The Empire Strikes Back, SEE IT!

title: i had a bad feeling about this.....but i was wrong
review:
Well, after the success of the original trilogy, Lucas made the mistake of...well....the phantom menace. Although it was ultimately a childrens film, it lacked any of the magic wonder and awe of the originals. With episode 2, Lucas made a truly wonderful and griping saga which shows Anakin Skywalker take a huge step towards the dark side.

Impeccably cast, this chapter of the star wars films, starts to conclude all the loose ends that were left in episode 1 aswell as bringing in and developing characters such as Jango and Boba Fett, Count Dooku and Mace Windu. The basic storyline is that federations are pulling out of the republic, influenced by the ex-jedi knight and Qui-Gon Jinns ex-master, Count Dooku(Christoher Lee). Meanwhile, a Bounty Hunter named Jango Fett (Temura Morrison) is trying to assasinate Ambassador Amidaila (Nattalie Portman). So Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) and his young apprentice Anakin Skywalker(Hayden Christiansen) are called to protect her. The love story between Anakin and Amidaila is expertly crafted and Portman and Christiansen pull it off with expert-like ease. While Obi-Wan is sent to track down Jango Fett, Anakin is sent back to Naboo to look after Amidaila. But things go wrong as Anakin is forced to go back to his home planet Tatooinne where he finds his mother dying. Once she dies Anakin looses it and kills almost everything in sight. This scene especially shows a great leap from the force to the dark side. Th emain finalle in the film is set in a gladiator like arena with all the Jedi Knights pitched againt huge Alien monsters and thousands upon thousands of trade federation droids. The clone warriors, grown upon Jango Fetts home planet save the remaining Jedi Knights from near extinction and mayhem erupts. The lightsaber fight between Count Dooku and Obi wan/Anakin does not last long as Count Dooku defeats both of them(without killing them) but the main treat in the film is watching the little green man (Yoda) pitched against Count Dooku. This is the main highlight in the film and everybody in the cinema was stunned.

The ending of episode 2 leaves plenty of doors open for what is bound to be a nitty gritty end to the saga. Altogether, attack of the clones was a very fullfiling second chapter to Star Wars.

title: Much like Empire Strikes Back, it is
review:
Yes, it's true, at least the last hour and a half. The beginning is slow, full of political talk and scenes that look like they belong in Phantom Menace. But once Jango Fett comes into the picture, the movie really picks up and is very enjoyable. Hard-core fans should be impressed, especially those who did like the Ep. I characters since most of them are back for Ep. II. It's similar to Ep. V, the middle-half of the original trilogy in some aspects.

I won't bother talking about the FX because they're incredible beyond words. But I will say that I fully support the digital Yoda, he looks so real and much better than the creepy puppet from Ep.I.

The actors are great, all of them are much more expressive and human than they were in Ep.I. Samuel L. Jackson finally gets to do something besides sit and Padme no longer speaks like a droid. Hayden was great as Anakin, very believable and into the character.

This is a must-see for all Star Wars fans, I'd rank it tied with Ep. V (Empire) for 2nd as my favorite movie in the series. Once you get past the first hour, it gets really good.

title: Lucas has not disappointed.
review: Awesome just awesome. This movie was all I was expecting and much much more. Lucas has taken his creation to the ultimate level. I only hope the next three years pass quickly so that all the answers we have always wanted will be provided and we will have a grand 6 film story to watch and love forever to come.

title: A vast improvement over the Phantom Menace
review: This was one of the two movies I chose to see this weekend in Russian because I knew the dialogue would not be the best aspect of the movies(the other one was Spider-Man). From what I could understand, the lines were a bit flat. I didnt get in all of the story, but I loved the CGI. It was very very exciting. Thankfully, Jar Jar Binks had a very small part in the movie. I was a bit confused as to the story's plot, but i still enjoyed it very much. A must-see in the theatres, just because of the wonderful effects.

title: WoW
review: What a movie .... I would have to say by far the most action Star Wars yet. Many people said that it was going to be a lame movie just like Episode 1 but it was the totally opposite. The best by far was the final battle scene bewteen Duku and Yoda. He doesnt need his cane when he is flying around and using a light saber but he does when he just walking  But over all I give it a 9. George Lucas must have had  great time working on this movie and i think it will show in the box office .

title: The force is strong with this one.
review:
Once again the power of the force sweeps the nation if not the world.

The Phantom Menace was critisised by the many, although I quite enjoyed it. However episode two captures the Star Wars universe in a way that nothing else has since Return of the Jedi. Lucas has taken his vision to the limits of CG and combined it with a great story that is now begining to fit together. What was dissapointing about the Phantom Menace was that it was about a planet that no-one knew about or cared about and no-one saw the relevence. However with this new epic in the Star Wars universe the story really comes to life.

The acting wasn't the best but it didn't disapoint. The story grew more complicated and darker than it ever has been and the effects were great. On the whole this is a great movie well worth the wait. If nothing else go and see it just to see Yoda with a light saber

title: I Can't Understand The Title Of This Wonderful Use Of The Force
review:
Now that I've seen the second Act of this great series, I can't understand its title, "Attack of the Clones".



The "Attack of Clones" in this Episode starts at the end, even Yoda said 'Begun, has the Clone wars' (Or something similar). And the attack is in fact against the Trade Federation troops, to help the Jedi, and we can see Yoda himself leading this Clone faction. I said "faction" because the Battle Of Geonosis does not include the whole Clone army, but only a part of it. With that said, in Episode II, the Clone army was just created, and only a part of it was on the battlefield for the first time.

I don't know who decided to choose "Attack of the Clones" as the main sub-title of Episode II, but the first one that was official at a time, which was "The Darkness Within", was much more appropriate, and for those who saw Episode II can understand my sayings. Well, I guess that Attack of the Clones just sounds cool...but, it does not, for me.

Besides the sub-title "mistake", Star Wars Episode II is a wonderful use of the Force.

Main characters provides more depth to their roles, dialogues are well done, Jar-Jar Binks becomes serious (Great! Thanks Lucas), Yoda proves what beeing a Jedi Master means, as well as Mr. Lee proves in his role what a good traitor and Sith "apprentice" should be...and another nice touch, we actually see Boba Fett's "father", and not only that, but we see Boba Fett's face! For the first time ever!

Battles are great in this Episode, just like all of the others. The Battle Of Yavin (Episode IV), The Battle Of Hoth (Episode V), The Battle Of Endor (Episode VI), The Battle Of Naboo (Episode I), and now, not only one, but actually 2 great battles featured in Episode II, which are The Geonosis Arena Battle, and the final, best one, The Geonosis Battle.

And I should add the fact that this new Act makes us remember some scenes from the "Old Trilogy". The bar scene on Coruscant, just like the bar scene on Tatooine (Episode IV). And at the end, Darth Tyranus blasting Anakin's body with the Dark Side powers (a.k.a electricity), just like the Emperor blasting Luke's body (Episode VI). Another example, which is the pursuit of Jango Fett by Obi-Wan Kenobi with a Jedi StarFighter ship accross a field of asteroids on Geonosis orbit, in this scene, Jango was able to take the lead on the pursuit against Obi-Wan, and tried to blast him and its StarFighter with his Slave-1 ship turbo lasers...but Obi-Wan was able to "hide" its presence to the Slave-1's radar...guess how? By landing the StarFighter itself on an Asteroid and by shutting down the ship's systems, just like Han Solo did, to hide its presence to an Emperial fleet, by landing on a Star Destroyer in Episode V.

Congratulations Mr. Lucas, you made Episode II my equal favorite with Episode VI. I loved Attack of the Clones, and already can't wait to see Episode III.

Hmmm...now I'm just wondering how Mr. Lucas will do, to connect Episode III...with Episode IV's beginning. Princess Leila should be old enough in Episode III...to be able to steal the Death Star's plans, and evading with a Rebel Ship. Well...Mr. Lucas, you'll find how, I know it. I just can't wait to see it.

Great work LucasFilm staff and eveyone involved in the making process of this Sci-Fi masterpiece.

The Force Strikes Back.

My personal score; 9/10.

title: Thousands of computer-generated foes don't scare me?
review:
We went, we saw, we ho-hummed. The visuals are terrific. They've always been that way. The story is two dimensional. The acting (or is it the directing) is one dimensional. Portman is gorgeous but has a greater ability than this film shows (see The Professional which she made when she was about 14.)Hayden Christensen is plastic. To utilize his good looks, I'd stick him in a boy band. Yoda does a better job, and he's digital.

When the high point of the movie is either a cartoon-Yoda spinning his light saber like a weed whacker (boys favorite moment)or "the kiss" (girls' favorite moment), the force has obviously lost it's force. There is little tension created. It's too predictable. Lucas has created another piece of "eye candy" but has done little to advance the "heart" of the original. It's as if he's making the sequels out of some sense of obligation rather than because of a need to delve deeper into the characters.

In interviews, Lucas admits he wishes he had the ability to do then what he can do now ... create thousands of computer generated clones. I almost wish he didn't have the computer ability. He might be forced to return to what made the whole phenomenon so great ... story, story, story.

It's still worth seeing if the popcorn is hot. We'll see the next one, too. I'm not sure I'll be alive by the time 7, 8 and 9 are finished.

My clone will be, though.

title: Yoda Kicked Ass!
review:
We Just came back from starwars epiosode 2 and it kicked total and all ass! the loghtsaber fights were better then the first one (yoda was amazing) and the story was also better then the first one. It still wasnt as good as the Trilgiy but then again what is? I strongly reccommend you see this.

P.S. To all the Ladies if you liked Ewan McGreggor i strongly suggest you see Trainspotting you get a pleaent supprise from him;)

title: The years funniest movie! Well done George
review:
How contrary of Lucas to prick at all our faux Jedi posturings by making the most hilarious Sci-fi spoof since Galaxy Quest. This movie really is something to behold, you have to see it believe it. Who would have thought that a long time ago in a galaxy far far away they would have American Diners...inspired. Yoda - known for being three foot tall and walking with a cane gets up and kicks butt (this is the best moment and will have you in stitches). Queen Amidala falls fifty feet from a spaceship, lies in the desert for a good ten minutes groaning, but as soon as someone turns up to rescue her she's up and running like she'd just taken a nap.

This is inspired stuff, it really is. Big black holes litter the plot (why were they building a clone army on Komino again!?), the dialogue reeks, absolutely reeks, and the acting is as wooden as Yodas walking stick. If you want great sci-fi stay at home and watch Star Wars on video (when did Lucas forget how to write witty dialogue exactly - probably around the time of Howard the Duck I guess). If you want the years finest sci-fi parody, with sumptuous computer graphics and a complete lack of any emotional involvement (even Anakins mum's death is hilarious, one minute she's full of life and the next she's dead as a doornail), go see Attack of the Clones...!

title: Better than Phantom menace but thats not saying much
review: Just a short review.The positive elements of episode two was the great special effects and inventive worlds that were created by lucas and his talented team.But sadly all this energy was channelled into visual elements of the movie and someone forgot about the plot,characters with depth and dialogue (a mixture of Z grade sci fi and midday soap opera). The love interest aspect of the movie just didn't fit it seemed and felt like someone added in for the cash in(titanic any one).To me it seemed like a wasted opportunity because both are promising actors but their scenes together are limp and lifeless,lacking any real intensity.I could go on but it feels like waste of my own energy and time to do so.All i can say is i hope the next episode has some backbone and remmembers that some us enjoys a movie that has a bit of heart and uses it s head and dose'nt just rely on a pretty face.

title: What we were waiting for...
review: A return to form and Lucas' strengths, namely the sence of epic mysticism and Jedi-centred action [al be it toned down for the kiddies]. Yoda finally shows the temper of his metal. Obi wan grows up into the mantel of Alec Guiness and some decent comic relief is provided by the stright man funny man combo of R2 and C3PO. The decried mistake of Episode one i.e. Jar-Jar is corrected and the Gungan only has three or four lines [although a pivotal part in events]and Palpatine grows steadily in power and menace. The groundwork for the third installment and the original three is firmly lain and we see Christopher Lee in the second of probably what will be the three biggest grossing films of this twelve month period [with Lord of the Rings - books one and two] as the menacing count Dooku. The usual quanta of colourfull aliens and ugly monsters [one of Episode one's good points] are also here and the film will have all Starwars fans grinning and gripping their arm-rests alternately. The climatic end is built up to beautifully and a bit of romance thrown in keeps the tone quite light, without detracting too badly from the pace. A definite improvement on The Phantom Menace and for a final word - Yoda is the man!

title: minor flaws but overall, awesome
review: After queuing in line for 2 hours to get a decent seat, it was great to realise that east coast Australian audiences would be the first to see EP2 in the world. With high expectations and a roaring full house, it was easy to tell that the congregation was impressed. AOTC is a huge improvement over TPM in terms of story, characters and tone yet  like EP1, it still had the flaw of woeful dialogue. With Lucas bringing on Jonathan Hales to flesh out the script, i would of expected better dialogue throughout the film, which brought much unintentional laughter. Although the humour was actually quite funny and there were some good lines, the writing and direction of the romance scenes was quite poor and proves Lucas as much to learn on executing chemistry with characters. Acting was good allround yet Christensen wasn't 100% capable of pulling off his role which to say, wasn't helped by his dialogue. It is easily seen any flaw of acting is contributed by actors not used to delivering amidst a wall of blue screens and with Lucas not having the best skills as helping actors blend their performances through the masses of fx surrounding them, the actors try their best. As far as fx, wow. The film has brilliant action sequences with the audience constantly dropping jaws no matter how much we know it's just CGI. As for the finale and Yoda..the whole cinema just erupted in cheers and 'holy sh..s' Overall AOTC is a great film and if a little more effort had gone into the dialogue, it would have been a perfect sequel.

title: star wars a triumph.
review: without doubt george lucas has exorcised the debarcle that was the phantom menace. out goes annoying, irritating young children and in comes in comes characters that are mean , moody and intense . george lucas has delivered the star wars movie that fans have been crying out for , this is the kind of movie the summer blockbuster was meant to be . the story is is a complex tapestry of political intrique and subdefuge , whilst still remaing simple enough for the younger ones to enjoy . the action set pieces are breathtaking , ilm have pushed the special effects barrier to a different level . the acting at times is a little stilted , but this is only due to george lucas's poor dialogue, he'y you cant be good at everything . all actors do the best they can with the material they have but christopher lee stands head and shoulders above the rest, an old hand showing the youngsters how its done . but the real star of this movie is yoda , without giving the plot away his final scences have to be seen to be beleived . so which movi e is the best ? clones or spiderman ? . well after seeing both it has to be star wars , but only just .

title: Fantastic return to Star Wars!

title: Love, Mystery, Clone War
review:
MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD

When the curtain went up on Star Wars II, at midnight, first Saturday screening of the film here in the UK, the audience clapped, whooped, yelled, made Chewbacca sounds. Some had come a long way especially to see it in this 2000-seat digital projection cinema. The point, for those who have criticised critics for not 'getting it' about Star Wars, is this: everyone wanted to love Epsiode II. We don't WANT to be disappointed.

In the spirit of marketing, I've split this review into 3, corresponding to the trailers that stirred up fevered anticipation.

'LOVE'

The romance between Anakin and Padme has been described as clunky, awkward. It's a funny description, because there is more chemistry between R2 and C3PO in one scene of any of the IV-VI movies than there are between our two protagonists for the whole of AOTC. This romance is not clunky, it is frankly quite stupid. Anakin comes across as a completely unsympathetic lecher, and Padme, well, as kind of dumb. By the time we saw them rolling down a hill together, the audience was groaning, and we knew we were in for a LONG wait. Their dialogue sounds fake, and for those of you who say go see ROTJ, at no point did it sound as fake as this. Campy in a fun way, but not to the depths of hell that we were dragged through in this 'courtship'. As one girl whispered, 'Can't we just get to the good bits?'

There is one touching scene: as they are wheeled out for execution, Padme whispers to Anakin her love, the love of those who are about to die. If by that time we cared, that scene would have raised a tear in the ladies.

Grade: 3/10

'MYSTERY'

What is good about AOTC? Well simple: everything in the plot involving Obi-Wan. You saw it in the trailer: "they are using a bounty hunter named Jango Fett to build a clone army." Our interest was genuinely piqued when Obi-Wan arrived at this shrouded waterworld. My skin definitely crawled when I saw clones every where. And, when the clone makers asked Obi-Wan, so when would you like to take delivery, I thought: OK. This is pretty OK. This is a mystery.

Bad news, guys. We never find out. Sure, we know its you-know-who, but we don't have the satisfaction of seeing some closure and some anticipation. What made Ep V great? Ep V was great because you wanted to see what happened next: they were already in the midst of planning Han Solo's rescue. What happens in Ep II? "Well, we should watch the Senate for suspicious moves." "Agreed." Oh man.

But its still OK. If there's one thing we're looking forward to, its the future emperor's grand design. As they say here in England, it's all coming together nicely.

Grade: 6.5/10

'CLONE WAR'

Special FX rawks! Cool, clone gunships, just like in Nam! Armies and armies of clones vs droids! Missiles, artillery barrages, troop transports, AT-AT predecessors! Did you see that landing ship unload the walker and fly off? Awesome!

And the Jedi! A huge Jedi battle! Omigod, they're DYING Jedi can't die! And YODA! (And here I have to quote a previous reviewer here at IMDB), Yoda, THE AMAZING GREEN BALL OF DEATH!

Grade: 9/10

Summary and prescription:

1. Lucas, stick to the plot, the gizmos and the vision. You invented the lightsabre, the AT-AT walker, the A-, B-, X-, and Y-wing fighters and the Death Star, to name a few. There were no gizmos we could love in AOTC.

2. Leave the voice directing and script to others. Stop being such a cheapskate and pay/beg Larry Kasdan or someone as good to write for you again. And if the fact that there's too much CGI meaning you need to be in 2 places at once and so you have to direct: TAKE A CLUE. There's too much CGI!

OVERALL GRADE: 6/10

title: What the critics are really thinking but are too afraid to say...
review:
Episode II, Attack of the Clones, brings to the table all the resolution needed to long unanswered questions. Mr. Lucas does the unthinkable once again by using the most advanced technology available in order to bring to life a screenplay 30 sum odd years in the making.

The film is a shining example of creativity, writing, production, and editing.

Sadly, there are those 'Fans', who expect the impossible. Fans who want a 30 year old film to have no similarities to movies done in the last decade or so. Ones who feel that Mr. Lucas owes them something, even though he sacrifices years of family life in order to bring to those devoted skeptics media bordering on greatness.

Shame on you all for giving the Lucas Arts production company the impression they did good work by forking out the millions of movie dollars grossed by Phantom Menace and now Clones. Those people who have the need to compare, criticize and critique should look deep into their bank accounts for the missing sense of reality.

You loved the movie, and when it comes out on DVD you will clear the shelves to own a lil slice of movie history. To those who would scrutinize Attack of the Clones as a poorly put together movie, need to give up the profession of Star Wars fanatic, and go back to being Trekkers. In short, we are obviously true believers that George Lucas will take his story to its fruition.

That he will show to us all why in his mind Darth Vader is feared throughout the universe, why there are so few Jedi left in Episode IV, and how a glorious republic disintegrated into a struggling rebellion trying to survive against an omnipotent empire.

This is movie making at its finest, no matter what the critics say, THEY LOVED IT TOO!

title: Lucas might be able to direct, but he can't write
review:
It is beyond the time that somebody took the pen out of George Lucas' hand and placed it high on a shelf beyond his reach.

Too often in Attack of the Clones, there were actions and dialogue that didn't serve to further the plot, but rather give reason for some event in a "subsequent" piece of the hexology. Too often, this didn't matter to anyone but Lucas. The "subplot" involving Jango Fett is a case in point.

Too often, the actions of the characters were illogical. For example near the end of the movie, when Yoda does his thing with the falling column. Why didn't he just move the people under it? Would that have been too too easy? And if I was Christopher Lee, I'd certainly never miss a chance to take out an opponent while he was otherwise engaged in saving his allies. And where would somebody in the middle of a flat, arid plain on a desert planet go to find mushrooms? The list is extensive, and is a testimony to Lucas' lack of writing skill. It is no surprise that without Campbell's seminal work beside him, the nuances of a workable plot escape him.

Too often, Senator Padme Amidala (obviously demoted from "Queen" and happy about it) switched clothes with a speed no supermodel could hope to emulate, although her choice of garb was at times mystifying: I still wonder at the leather corset she had donned in the evening she spent with Anakin. Surely something a little more concealing and comfortable was in order? And she has a wonderful white jumpsuit that without apparent cause can become a two-piece number that permits her to display a significant amount of midriff. But by this time I'd given up wondering why time had apparently stood still for her, whilst permitting Anakin to put on ten years. At best, this puts him at 18 and her nudging 30...

Too often, moments that should have been filled with warmth and tenderness as the two would-be lovers attempted to make the most of Anakin's personal time warp, were drab and lifeless. Just like much of the dialogue and acting.

The film wasn't without highlights though: the action sequences were handled quite well - clearly this is Lucas' forte. Yoda showed wonderful coordination at one stage, and was that a neon rendering of ET at the front door of a nightclub?

Thank goodness Lucas' seeming obsession with unusual creatures playing weird instruments was held in check by someone. Mind you, nobody seems to drink anything in the Star Wars world unless it is colored blue.

There was so much to irritate in the movie - a situation so aggravated by the length that it's best end simply, and damn it with faint praise: at least it was better than Phantom Menace.

title: NO SPOILERS
review: If you are a Star Wars fan (like me), you will love this movie. If you aren't you will love it anyway, but on a different level. George Lucas has given just about everyone a light-sabre, and there are some terrific battles, far better then anything in the other Star Wars movies. You see an entire army of Jedis, running forward and smashing aside laser blasts with their light sabres, and then crashing into an army of droids, which is truly satisfying, and the young Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan fighting back to back, which is a bit ironic really, considering what will happen in the later movies. Anyway, the battles are brilliant, and Yoda gives everyone a big surprise by turning up and showing us all just why he is the Jedi master. Unfortunately, the acting was pretty rubbish: Natalie Portman, who plays Amidala was completely flat, and Anakin Skywalker just couldn't pull off the bits when he wasn't angry. Samuel L Jackson was a bit of a disappointment too; he is an excellent actor, but was held back by the script. However, Ewan Mcgregor was excellent as Obi-Wan, and acted the part really well. No worries though, as the acting was never Star Wars' strong point, and the battles truly make up for it. There were also lots of references to the later movies: Anakin has his arm chopped off, we are shown how the Bounty Hunter Boba Fett came to be, and there is a brilliant line, when Obi-Wan says to Anakin, "I have a feeling you will be the death of me." So anyway, if you have not seen this movie, go and see it, as it is pretty damn good. Well done George Lucas, I can't wait for the next one!

title: Attack of the CGI
review:
There's nothing like watching a Star Wars movie for the first time. When the sound of trumpets blaring, and the word "Episode II" pops out, I was overwhelmed with emotion and I gripped my seat tightly ... but then I thought hold on, the movie hasn't even started yet. But boy, when I walked out from the theatre, I was consumed with an overwhelming desire to buy another ticket and walk right back in. Yes I am a huge Star Wars fan, and with Attack of the Clones, the magic is back once again and I'm loving it.

What strikes me about Episode II, is that there are more CGI in it than all the Jurassic Park movies put together. Even the venerable Yoda is no longer a muppet. All of the Clone army is done entirely with computers, even in scenes where there is only one or two of them, which is pretty strange. Can't they just get extras to walk around in suits? So I'm not sure if all this excess CGI is a good thing, but nevertheless Episode II managed to be one of the best Star Wars movie yet, even though I still miss that expressive Yoda puppet from The Empire Strikes Back ... its like casting Miss Piggy as a CGI character - its just not the same.

Unlike the previous Phantom Menace, the biggest improvement is that there is finally a good chunk of story to bite into. Now we have the pre-requisite love story of Anakin & Padme, a relationship that's destined to end in tragedy (and twin babies). Its quite nice, but however the actual story on politics is more interesting because its starting to draw parallels to Anakin's fate as the future Jedi terminator. He is portrayed nicely by the newcomer Hayden Christensen, who managed to project his dark emotions and desires very well, and there are several powerful scenes where Anakin showed his early inclinations towards the dark side. In fact, many of the movie's best moments are provided by him. When it comes to the love story however, Anakin & Padme lacked the natural spark & wit that Han Solo and Leia exhibited in the original trilogy. But it is not as bad as some people think, and they do make a cute couple together. The "romantic" dialogue is as Star-Warish as it can get; sometimes cheesy, sometimes not. But considering their young age and the period of time they live in, its perfectly acceptable and works well for me. Ewan McGregor is great, even better than before. He is becoming more and more like the original Obi-Wan Kenobi played by Alec Guinness, sporting a beard and a cynical attitude to boot. Obi-Wan even has a sense of humor on occasions, and his banters with Anakin are insightful. McGregor remains one of the most inspired casting in the trilogy.

Now for once, I can comment on the soundtrack since The Phantom Menace has hardly any - except one - memorable tracks that one can whistle to. Now we get a sweeping, haunting score reminiscent of the original love theme, plus other original tracks and delightful cameos that brings tears to those who grew up on the original movies.

But the best thing about Episode II is that it brings us much closer than ever to the third chapter, where many questions and mysteries will finally be answered. How will Anakin turn to Vader? What is the mysterious connection between Darth Sidious and Palpatine? Who exactly is Darth Tyrannus? Imagine, all of this goodies will be revealed in the next one, and the whole saga will finally make sense!!!!! George Lucas has done very well in that department, considering that re-telling a story in backward order is no easy task. Suddenly, 2005 seems like an eternity ... but hey that's exactly how I felt back in 1999. Episode II is definitely worth waiting for, and now I can't begin to imagine what magic Episode III has in store for me (besides what probably be another cheesy title). Well done Lucas!

title: Loved it - as a very biased long time fan
review:
Just walked from home from first official screening in Helsinki, Finland, and spent some minutes reading other new comments. I share many of the views, especially the ones on wooden dialogue, breathtaking action and amazing sceneries, and I honestly don't think the plot has much to offer to others than die hard fans but as such the film delivers lots of fun and enjoyment and lived up to the expectations. Don't take it so seriously - feel the Force and let your imagination do the rest! :)

More analytically as a fan I am ready to accept the fact that Lucas is more imagining than thinking kind of guy, and therefore I wont complain about the bizarre plot "development", the lack of believable characters or the action that even the Force cannot explain.

Anyway contrary to other reviews I saw Anakin as very much as Darth Vader (maybe it was his tall and dark figure, dunno), Obi-wan Kenobi was, well, just like Obi-wan, and Senator Palpatine as a rather creepy old guy. Both episode I and II somewhat lacked real villains, but Palpatine is ominous enough to keep the suspense. There were some plausibility problems with Amidala *really* falling for the "kid" but oh well.. more weird things have happened so why not this totally unbelievable romance (Hayden tho played his part perfectly as the teenager in agony over long term infatuation).

There was lots of warm, even self-ironical humour that I dearly missed in the Episode I. The dialogue was as bad as it can be, but not as bad as it could have been ;) Just shut your ears and concentrate on the otherwise beautifully choreographed and designed scenes. Anyway I couldn't care less if there was dialogue at all. I would just as well make it up all in my head as I normally do :)

As a summary: (SPOILERS AHEAD) Definite pluses (and pleasant surprises) were Boba Fett as child, Jar Jar Binks as a representative of Naboo in the senate, more action for Yoda, the weird creatures of the waterworld (not so Star Wars but cool anyway), the music actually building up the scenes and not just disturbing the story, first appearance of the Stormtroopers.

As major minuses I would include (if it didn't come clear enough) the ever so silly dialogue, still way too many throwaway characters and sites (e.g. the assassin girl), too much unnecessary show-off action, and incomprehensible (or am I just stupid?) plot development (SPOILERS DONE)

I would recommend this film to just about anyone with wild imagination and a heart open for new experiences. The child in me got a huge kick out of the film, and that is the reason I love Star Wars! It is not *a* movie, it is not even *the* movie. It is sci-fi fantasy come true :)

title: Back in my day...
review: I never thought that, at 28 years old, I would actually be starting a conversation with the wrds, 'Back in my day..' but here I am.  My wife and I suffered through the excruciatingly boring Episode II yesterday, and I realized that this movie was so slow and ridiculous it made me miss the Ewoks!  I know, fellow fans the world over are gasping in shock, but I have been a fan my entire life also.  I saw Episodes IV, V, and VI on the big screen (not the 'Special Edition' garbage, but the real movies), so I know what a good Star Wars movie is.  Let me tell you, Episode II ain't it.  We all know how terrible Episode I was (with a few moments of greatness), but I actually found myself debating which movie was worse--during one of the many endless dialogue scenes.  I know, all the die-hards (a group which included myself up until yesterday morning) will say, "He's just setting up the story details for Episode III".  Back in my day, he set up the story details during the opening scroll.  Anyone remember the set-up for Episode IV? The Princess has stolen the plans for the Death Star and is racing to get them home--then she is captured during the first five minutes--after a thrilling gun battle--and we are completely surrounded by the joy of another galaxy. George Lucas used to be able to tella story that was thrilling and exhilarating while delivering a movie that was also thrilling.  There is absolutely no reason I should have to sit through two movies that are complete and utter garbage just so that I will be prepared for the next movie.  Please people, avoid this movie, and maybe he will realize the mistakes he is making and give us an Episode III that deserves our time and money, unlike this latest installment.

title: Let stop and think, shall we?
review:
Okay.

I've been reading a lot of crap about this picture. I've been reading a lot of junk about how it's barely better than Episode 1, how the dialogue is muddy, and the performances are bland, and on and on and on. I work in the movies. I know how every take is different from each other, and I know how the director can have a profound influence on the movie regardless of the script.

So. Let's take a moment to consider something. The performances were merely average and the dialogue sounds like someone reading the menu at McDonald's? Has anyone actually stopped and listened to Lucas speak in the last ten years? There is no more boring speaker in the world. Lucas makes Stephen Hawking sound like Sinatra. It seems almost natural to me that the chosen takes would sound like the dialogue running through Lucas' head while he was writing it.

Okay. That point aside, can anybody actually sit back and take in this picture for what it was? We all entered the theater with heightened expectations. ALL of us. Was it going to be as good as Irvin Kischner's visceral "Empire?" No. Was it going to be as slyly clever as the interpersonal dialogue between Han and Luke on the Death Star? No. Was it going to be a story about people living their lives before the crushing hand of the empire controlled the universe? YES!

This movie was not about the radical feats of problem solving and improvisation during episodes 4 through 6. This was a movie about characters who have yet to realize the incredible importance they will have over the course of history. This was a movie about the human elements inside all of us, regardless of our duties and obligations. This was the movie Lucas promised us would follow in the shallow footsteps of Episode 1 and make all the difference in the course of the tale.

Ultimately, what I am trying to say by this rambling diatribe is shut up, stop pretending to be filmmakers, and enjoy watching the perpetually slighted Yoda kick some Dark Side ass.

title: Really good, what we desperately wanted from Episode I
review:
The word on the street was that Episode II was a vast improvement on The Phantom Menace, and they were right. The only real complaint I heard was that the developing romance between Anakin & Padme slowed things down. Now that I've seen it, I can say it is visually stunning, fast paced and in the end thoroughly entertaining.

Ever since the likes of Jurassic Park there has been the promise of some really eye popping, mind blowing movies thanks to the use of cgi. I think SWII is the first one to really deliver. I would go as far as to say that special effects have been overdone, there is so much to look at.. and at times (especially in battle scenes) I felt like my eyes were going to pop out of my head because they couldn't handle it :)

Now that I've started a critique, a few people I have talked to say the romantic scenes are a bit much. To me the problem seemed to be that George Lucas laboured over the whole thing... it's as if he knew the romance had to be played out, but was scared about getting it wrong. Movie romances normally flow a lot more naturally than this one.

Otherwise excellent piece of work, particularly in the latter stages of the movie where as you probably know by now, Yoda shows he can mix it with the best.. It all looks and feels like Star Wars, and there's more battles, chases and light sabre duels that we all were begging for the first time around.

It's fantastic stuff, but the hype can spoil it for you... it's just a movie, but an absolute visual and auditory feast at that.

title: Still missing the old magic
review:
George Lucas' latest installment of the Star Wars saga, Attack of the Clones, provided a bitter mixture of extraordinary special effects and stunning landscapes along with a story that is presented rather forcefully and emotionally sapped. The old combination that worked so well in the 70s and 80s has been derailed to the point that frankly, it just isn't fun anymore. For all the digital technology and the CGI creations and the wondrous imagery that Lucas paints on the screen, he is simply unable to reinvent the fascinating story that made Star Wars what it once was.

With the passing of ten years, Anakin has grown into a cocky Padawan learner who has trouble with patience and obedience. He, along with his master Obi Wan, is assigned to protect the former Queen, now Senator (strange politics) Amidala when an assassination attempt is made against her life. Upon finding that a bounty hunter was responsible for the attack, the Jedi Council assigns Kenobi to find him while Anakin remains in charge of the Senator's safety. The story takes a confusing detour into a contrived love story, full of sappy lines and cliched events, sharing time with the more interesting story of Obi Wan's pursuit. Lucas' love story is labored and missing the tension and the clever barb play that we witnessed between Han and Leia. Unfortunately, the rest of the story takes a back seat to this melodrama until the ending battle.

The action sequences are excellent. We see the full strength of the Jedi in combat and finally get to see Samuel L. Jackson wielding his purple light saber. The Yoda/Dooku battle has been discussed thoroughly with excitement by most, but I found the end result to be nothing more than a gimmick. Ironically, however, the best acting performance in the movie was by the computer generated Jedi Master himself, giving credence to the notion that Lucas is more comfortable with the technology than with the actors.

George Lucas envisioned one of the greatest movie epics ever created, but at his best, he was an influence behind the scenes and let those that excelled at writing and directing handle the details of his vision. Two movies into his second trilogy, it may be too late to rectify that mistake. I have two words that Mr. Lucas would be wise to heed before he undertakes the final chapter: Lawrence Kasdan.

title: Amazed & Disappointed *WARNING - SPOILER*
review:
**WARNING - SPOILER CONTAINED**

This is the movie that has been long awaited by Star Wars fans since Obi-Wan mentioned the Clone Wars way back in Episode 4. For those Star Wars fans who are true to the text of the chronology, not just the movies, do not expect much from this film. Sure, there are those moments where you get to link pieces together, but then there are moments when you will be stunned by the complete lack of adherence by Lucas to his own folklore.

I feel that the screenplay is desperately missing the guidance of Lawrence Kasdan. He wrote 'Empire' and 'Jedi' and his influence, looking at this, seems to have made all the difference.

Look out for the moment Mace Windu becomes John Shaft with the memorably stupid line "The party's over" while holding his saber to the throat of a bounty hunter.

Yoda becomes a saber wielding pinball in a moment many Star Wars fans have probably been waiting for but should've never happened as it turns out to be the most ridiculously farcical scene in the film. He duels a Sith. the lead up to which looks like it was inspired by Mortal Combat, full of stupid posing and macho talking.

George Lucas proves himself to be romantically inept with tender love scenes pulled straight from midday soap operas; a plummet from the quality of similar content in THX-1138. One particular moment where Padme declares her love for Anakin saw the entire theatre burst into laughter. not complimentary.

Although Jar Jar is no longer falling about for cheap laughs, Lucas has suitably found another source for comic relief during intense battles in C-3PO. Watch the droid make dumb comments and ruin a complete battle scene. For what purpose, I have no idea.

In fact, the droids from the original trilogy are pretty much introduced here so they can lamely save Amidala from a hopeless situation. In one instance, R2D2 fails to save Amidala when a nemesis manages to sneak up on her. He emits a light but doesn't SEE anything, at which point all the Star Wars fans are screaming "But he has sensors that picked up Sand People miles away in Episode 4!".

But while these are all annoying to the overall experience, Lucas does show that he still knows what he's doing.

A fantastic chase through Coruscant is visually amazing and paced with the skill of the Lucas of old. The chase ends with Obi-Wan proving yet again that barflies shouldn't mess with him! Look here for an excellent homage to Bladerunner.

Another great scene involving Obi-Wan is a fight with the bounty hunter, Jango Fett. Particularly impressive are the ways Obi-Wan gets around not having his light saber. a great example of a hero overcoming adversity without catching a break.

In short, it is visually amazing. Fantastic special effects. Computer geeks and FX nerds will be in heaven! But, for a man who has made it his life's mission to snub Hollywood and remain independent, Lucas has produced something which could have easily spewed out of the lamest of Hollywood's blockbuster machines.

It left this Star Wars fan bitterly disappointed.

title: Happy You Will Be
review:
Everything that was wrong with Episode 1 is either gone or cut back severely. Everything that is good about Episodes 4, 5, and 6, with the exception of Han Solo (Harrison Ford), is here. It was worth standing in line for two hours among people half my age, to see on the premiere.

Look, most people have already read the reviews and know the plot outline. You've already decided to see it. But let me tell you some things you can look forward to seeing.

Young Anakin is growing up and taking his Jedi training seriously. He's a great pilot and was such a reminder of Luke Skywalker except for his arrogance. He knows he's the best, whereas Luke only thought he was good. Watch the stance and the emotions that pass on Anakin's face. All foreshadowing of who he will be. Yet there is still a weakness in him that makes him more appealing.

Obi-wan is a little older and just perfect. In him, we can see the older Ben Kenobi peering out from time to time. Padme is looser this time around and we begin to see exactly why 'Ani' has been in love with her these ten years.

There are plenty of new planets, locales, and locals to give delight. Plus very little Jar Jar in this one! Palpatine uses his proximity to young Skywalker to brush that arrogant ego.

Some odd things... it is quite a surprise to see the first stormtrooper and find they are... they are the... they are the good guys! And the good side of the force is being muddied by the dark side.

The best thing about the movie, however, is Yoda. Sure, in Episode 1, we see an old Yoda, not the ancient one we are used to, but Episode 2 will stand out as Yoda's film. He rocks, he rolls, he kicks butt.

All in all, see it on the big screen at least once.

You will be happy.
