title: Definitely Not Worth A Second Viewing In The Theater (Spoilers Inside)
review:
I was by no means a fan of The Phantom Menace, but I actually find it to be a superior film than Attack Of The Clones. As usual, the trailer made the movie look great, but the finished product pales in comparison.

Since I wasn't a fan of TPM, I didn't set my expectations for this film unreasonably high. Even with that, the film failed my limited expectations.

I'll start with what I did like. Not having a strong Jar Jar Binks and a young "whoopie" Anakin presence throughout was a plus for the film. I also liked the fact that the climatic action took place with all of the central characters together instead of having to switch back in forth like in Jedi and TPM. The score was still good even though it was my least favorite. It was nice to have The Imperial March and Duel Of The Fates segments appear. The effects for the final climatic battle were well done and exciting as well as the sound effects throughout. Finally, the performances of Ian McDiarmid, Christopher Lee and Ewan McGregor were exceptional. I also thought the boy who played Boba did a nice job and didn't find him annoying like I found Jake Lloyd.

Now for the dislikes. I found Anakin to be a whiny brat 1000 times worse than Luke in ANH. The love scenes were very boring because they were so repetitive. Anakin, "I love you." Amidala, "We shouldn't." "I love you." "We shouldn't." I love you....repeat that about 4 or 5 more times. She decides to cave in when she figures they are going to die anyway. Why did she have to wear such tempting clothes that it was impossible for him not to be at least physically drawn to her.

That was also some reaction she had when he said, "I killed them all. I killed not only the men, bought the women and children as well." Some great Jedi, protector of life and the piece. If I were her, I would have told him to go away after he told me of his murderous rampage.

What was the deal with having a 50's diner with old cliche's like, "Want a cup of joe?". That was downright cheesy.

So, all of the clones are Jango Fett? That is just lame. In other words, instead of the Imperial Stormtroopers being recruited, they are just all clones of Jango Fett.

So this doesn't get drug out as long as the film, I'll just say a few general dislikes which affected the whole film. There was just too much switching back and forth between scenes that were just too short. Most of the scenes up until the climax had time to become interesting before they were cut off. None of the tension that existed in Episodes IV-VI. We know the principles aren't going to die in these installments, so there is no fear of them dying. The films are very unbalanced now. Some of the violence, which was less severe in IV-VI was toned down. We can't have Han shoot first and laser blasts to Imperial officers were altered so they would appear more family friendly, but in this film, bee-like and other creatures are dismembered left and right. Not to mention as bar patron wearing a thong with her a** hanging out.

The magic is gone. It all started on a downhill spin with the Special Editions and has done nothing but gain momentum since. I'll see Episode III since I have scene the others, but afterwards, I'll consider I-III to be a separate and inferior entity to the unaltered IV-VI.

title: Lucas concentrates too much on the story and neglects the acting
review:
Lucas is probably planning for another big hit out of this episode. The special effects are great and the story is much better than that of episode one. The aggressive negotiation scenes set up for great action. The audience, Star Wars fans or not, won't be able to resist reaction to Yoda and other Jedi.

The story also makes it a long way. From only relying on the special effects in episode 1, this episode has a far more moving story. The touch of romance is just right.

However, because of this great emphasis on the story, Lucas neglects the acting. These stars, paid to be be in probably one of the biggest hits, are not acting that way. Did they just wake up, did they not have enough time, or are they just not putting in the effort to match the supreme story? Whatever it is, the acting quality goes down and is a disappointment to the original trilogy.

Lucas manages to balance the good and evil throughout the film as not to depress everyone with evil always getting its way. Different than other Star Wars episodes, this uniqueness will make this film a success--hopefully.

title: Great Digital Work!
review:
I saw this film one minute after midnight on May,16th, and at first i wasn't very amused about this picture. To call it boring would be exaggerated, but the story begins slowly and is growing more and more. It all begins with the rivalry between Anakin and Obi-Wan and it ends with?

I do not want to tell you the end of the film, only this: it is kind of surprising, and for me overwhelming. The picture grows and grows and in the end you just hope, that it won't take too much time for Episode III! (8/10)

title: The cunning rise of both the Dark side and the Empire !!!
review: This film is what good Science Fiction really is about. It has a mesmerizing plot, great characters and interesting predicaments. It is filled with nice exotic places to visit, mind boggling action sequences and a very pleasant mood to it all. George Lucas' Episode 2 masterfully succeeds to get the Star Wars series back on the right track, compensates for the mediocre Episode 1 and will entertain even those unfamiliar to this far away Galaxy. The dark pieces, vital to the empire's rise are slowly and Insidiously coming together. There also are so many, SO MANY established or "will be" bad guys, it's no wonder the honourable Jedi knights will sadly be exterminated. The dark times are coming...

title: Quit crying!!!
review: Honestly I loved this movie.I loved it enough to see it the first day it was out and the second day it was out.I loved it from beginning to end.I loved the fight scenes,the love scenes,and every scene in between.Too many people are crying about it being "not lucas like",but i think they are just stupid.This man has wowed us over and over again.Granted,at first i hated episode one but now that i have seen this one,number one makes more sense,and thus looking better.And as for Lucas,he pretty much has the right to tell us what to like and hate he is that talented.I loved all the actors performances.They could have done without all catch lines from C-3po,but i loved the leading on quotes.Like the one from Obi "I feel you will be the death of me" to Anikin.I especially loved the fight scenes of Obi vs. Fett and Yoda vs. Dooku.the fight between fett and obi was just cool,and as for the Yoda fight scene.(gasp)Sure it might have looked kinda funny,but it got its point across that Yoda is the freaking Jedi of all Jedi.All i can say is go see this movie with the open mind you had when you were a kid,when you first saw Star Wars,when Mr. Lucas(im not worthy of saying his first name)first started the epic story that will forever be remembered when our generation is spoken on.

title: much better than 'phantom menace', hayden christensen rox!
review:
episode II was everything i hoped it would be and more. the film as a whole was very well done and interesting, with exception of a few annoying appearances with jar jar that we could have done without. although the critics may have critized it, 'clones' was much better than the past 'menace'. the story had much more substance. especially enjoyable was the romance, and the thrilling performance by hayden christensen as anakin. you can see him becoming darth vader-feel the tension and the force driving him to be evil. what probably surprised me the most was episode II's ability to hold my interest for it's whole 2 hr 22 min running time. i was completely entertained with what i saw on the screen, and while the acting as a whole isn't oscar material by any means, it's still convincing.

all in all, i say go see this film now. even those (like me) who aren't star wars freaks and haven't even seen all the old classics will still love it. if the movie itself doesn't enchant you, the stunning and handsome hayden christensen still will!!

title: The worst of the series.
review: The argument of the film is quite simple, the conversations are plain, without depth, boring.., the psychological touch has been definitively left, the story is a pretext to show big visual effects, etc... The worst of the series, as i had said.

title: Yoda kicks ass!
review:
I didn't read any of the critics reviews of this film but I think I will now just so that I can laugh at them for being so wrong. This movie is fantastic! In terms of star wars films it is second only to "empire strikes back."

I had heard from reliable sources that this movie was good but that the first half was a little dull. I went into the cinema expecting something good but, at the same, expecting to be disappointed (after all "the phantom menace" was pretty bad). I came out of the cinema extremely pleased with "attack of the clones" it is a throwback to the original trilogy; I would even rate it as being better than episodes IV and VI. The first half is not dull at all it builds up the story quite well, the scenes on the clone planet were intriguing and the anakin/Padme scenes were kept to a bare minimum, the way they should have been.

As I wasn't disappointed with the first hour in any way, I therefore had huge expectations of the second half. I was not disappointed. The huge Jedi battle is fantastic! Not only in terms of the sheer scale of the thing, but the way it grips you as well. Real edge-of-the-seat stuff!

My only real complaint with this movie would be the poor performance of anakin during the romance scenes (and to be honest the first half of the movie as a whole), he just came across as being an arrogant stuck-up twat. However, my opinion of him changed after he found his dead mother, clearly he is more suited for acting dark characters which should mean anakin is fantastic in episode III.

My final word would have to go to Yoda. Until "Attack of the clones" Boba Fett or Darth Vader were my favourite star wars characters. Now I would have to say without a doubt that Yoda is the greatest character in the history of the world. Put simply, Yoda kicks serious ass!

title: Redemption
review:
I saw Star Wars Episode II - Attack of the Clones the first day, first showing at the closest theatre, I had reserved tickets 2 weeks in advance and I was one of the 4 first people in the theatre. Why? Because I knew that Episode II would much better than Episode I. Many people including me, did not think Episode I lived up to it's expectations. The special effects were great, but it was too childish for me. Although I liked the movie enough, it lacked the bang and the excitement of the original films, save for the podrace and final lightsaber duel. But Episode II definitely made up for all that, with a more serious plot filled with excitement all the way through.

The story begins when Obi-Wan Kenobi and his apprentice Anakin Skywalker are assigned by the Jedi council to protect the now-senator Padme Amidala after an assassination attempt on her life. When Obi-Wan recieves strange information about a planet called Geonosis, he is sent to investigate while Anakin stays to protect Padme. As Obi-Wan's search leads him to a startling discovery, Anakin's relationship with Padme becomes more serious. Meanwhile Count Dooku, an ex-Jedi, is assembling a large army of seperatists, and the Supreme Chancellor of the Republic is taking actions that will determine the fate of the galaxy...

title: Casting...
review: If it is true that Lucas decided who his main cast for Star Wars (the original) would be by the amount of chemistry they displayed among each other, than he should return to this best practice. The romance between Christensen and Portman lacked. With that said, loved the fight scene with Yoda, but could have done without the Bruce Lee, martial art stance.

title: ultimately bittersweet
review:
Being a huge Star Wars fan guru, this movie contains a balance between what is pleasant and what is unsatisfactory.

I find the idea (romance as a component of Star Wars) a difficult situation to master. Because of the main spectacular battles in the previous Episodes created, we have been influenced to believe these two factors may be quite a challenge to combine, and...well...hehe..it sure was. Regardless that this is the story of Anakin Skywalker, his character portrayed in this Episode seemed to be ridiculing a stereotyped subliminal message of how teenagers act now-a-days: stubborn, impatient, spoiled, VERY arrogant,deeply emotional,uncontrollable, inconsiderate, and lets not forget the raging hormones. I cant say I take any offense to what I believe this to be a subliminal message, but you'll see what I mean after you've checked out this movie.

As far as the Romance goes,Lucas has done his part to explain the relation of how Skywalker and Amidala came to be, but dont expect this love story to be as passionately epic as James Cameron's, Titanic....you have to remember....this is Star Wars...=P

Once again ILM, like always, has proven to be the masters of computer animation and special effects. Thank goodness you only see Jar Jar Binks for about 4 brief scenes. The Design Director, Doug Chiang,also has came up with a lot of nifty space ship, droid, and other great designs that had to do with the mechanical 'eye-candies' of this Episode. This time, Yoda is remarkably all CG. As you might have guessed, yes, he does duel in this movie, 'tis quite an enjoyable scene and certainly not one to miss."I've never seen something, so old and so short, move with such rapid speed and accuracy." The clones, the droids, and 'the beginning' of the war is utterly mouth-dropping. The action is intense, 'like the Battle of Hoth on steroids.' Like Darth Maul of Episode 1, Jango Fett, a Bounty Hunter working for the Sith Lords, serves as the signature villian of Episode II, not much dialogue with this bad guy either, cool fight scene with obi-wan, but its always great to see the Slave 1 in action again.

Over all, you might call this movie not quite an impressive art of 'Love and War'. Like Episode 1 it has its goods and bads,but like many would say, even though this is a prequel,.... still, nothing beats the original Star Wars Ep. 4, 5, and 6. Now-a-days, it seems that movies compete to see who has the best CG support, yet they include such terribly weak plots. In my opinion, Lucas seems to be leaning towards that direction. Yet, do not get discouraged; this movie is still a cool movie... mostly because it is.....Star Wars, and is one of ILM's greatest and most spectacular projects. I honestly wasnt too hyped up about this movie this time, but if you want to see a good movie this summer,see...STAR WARS EPISODE II, but if you are sick of Star Wars go see..... SPIDERMAN!!

title: The best so far
review:
The WOW is back, but for different reasons from the original. The first Star Wars film, Episode IV in the saga, was a supremely delightful popcorner that succeeded because of its then ground-breaking special effects, humor and its hint at a much larger universe encompassing its story line. It was absolute perfection for what it was.

Lucas then gave us 3 more movies, 2 sequels and a prequel. This sequel to the first Star Wars prequel succeeds in showing how the story lines of the 2 trilogies mesh, and it does so masterfully. We don't have all the details yet, but things are beginning to become clear.

This film is as complex as the original was simple; more complex than all the other films combined. Its a love story, a psychological drama, a swash-buckling adventure, a space opera, mystery, and epic story of the decay of democracy all in one film. And for those interested in morality plays, its an act in one of those also. The critics just don't get it; they're too busy with their pseudo-intellectual snobbery to recognize that George Lucas's saga is a masterwork in the making.

Yes it suffers the inevitable consequence of some decline in suspense because we already know how the story turns out. But so what? Besides, Lucas continues to push the state of the art of film-making. I didn't think he could beat the eye-candy of the otherwise disappointing Episode I, but the effects here are a new high in film making. His "city of the future" setting on the planet Coruscant exceeds even Blade Runner's by a wide margin.

GO AND SEE THIS FILM. 10/10

title: Somewhat satisfying
review:
Action scenes and special effects - 10 / 10

Dialogue - 1 / 10

Storyline - 7 / 10

I was reading other user comments, and saw one where a conversation was overheard that "Great special effects can make a great movie regardless of the script," or something along those lines. I guess I have been brain-washed to believe this too, since I still gave the movie 8 / 10 !

The movie has three storylines it bounces around in telling, a little too quickly for my tastes; approximately every 2 minutes. However, after you witness the scenes between Anakin and Amidala, you'll be grateful (like me) that they don't last too long. Those scenes are painful to watch. My mom and I were gagging at the schmaltz, and we're both women who enjoy a little romantic story...but their scenes aren't romantic, just stupid. The chemistries between R2-D2 & C3-P0 and R4 & Obi-wan are better than the chemistry between the two young actors. In fact, you might be like me, and long to see more Jar-Jar!!! I'm not kidding here :o)

Another stupid element: The constant wardrobe changes for Amidala. The Senator is supposed to be in hiding / on the run. Why does she have the most incredible wardrobe around ?! (So there can be 10 different action figures sold, each with a different outfit?) Natalie Portman is a good actress, she should be used as such, not just a model for sexy-cute clothing.

As far as the acting, at first I thought it was not too great. I thought Hayden (Anakin) may have been doing a cruddy job, but a friend pointed out that he was in "My Life as a House," and I thought he did a fine job in that movie. Also, there's Samuel L. Jackson...it's pretty much accepted as fact that he's a great actor, but his character in this movie seems wooden. That's why I blame the dialogue for what seems to be poor acting performance.

Now, my husband tells me that some critics have been putting down Ewan's portrayal of Obi-wan. This is one of the things I thought was flawless! Obviously, the other thing I enjoyed was the special effects!

Overall, I'd say the movie is definitely worth seeing; not worth waiting in line for more than an 1/2 hour though. If you can't get to a theatre / showtime that isn't packed (I was able to), then see it in a couple weeks when the crowds settle down.

title: a movie that you'll be seeing not for just one time
review:
Hello reader!!

Ok, if you haven't seen this movie yet: expect a lot to see. A lot will happen in front of your eyes. And most of the time you'll be amused every microsecond. It's superb, entertaining, funny and the story keeps trying to drag you in.

On the other hand you'll say to yourself: "Oh dear! So much is happening!!". It'll be hard to see or notice every detail, to realize what things are going on, etc. But don't worry about this!! Listen up... ...after seeing it for the first time take a deep breath saying "Wow!" and let everything come to your mind. Then one other day (or the same day if you're really excited) go ahead and see the movie again. You'll notice a lot of details, and sneaky references to the other parts in the saga. In fact: you'll start loving this movie more and more when seeing it over and over again! And of course not only this movie, but the whole saga aswell :-)

So ummmm... what can I say... my point is: don't except to love the movie after one time seeing it: See this movie, see it again, see the other parts again, see this movie again, and again, and again. It'll please you in every way, and it'll grab your attention every second of a day. Until episode III arrives.

Couldn't be better!

title: Great,a lot of fun
review: very good movie finally George Lucas is back on track,great story ,great action. a little too much CGI and a bit slow in the first half, other than that Star Wars is back. i was hoping that after the Phantom Menace fiasco we will get something good and we did.The only bad thing now is that we have to wait till 2005 for the third one.

title: Amazing Visuals w/ A Whole Lot Of Terrible Dialog
review: See the title?  That about sums it up.  Your jaw will hit the ground when you first see the amazing visuals that Episode II has to offer, and then about 10 minutes later your jaw will drop even further when you witness the sickeningly embarrassing dialog that ultimately keeps the movie from being the best Star Wars picture of all time.

title: AOTC wins the award..*spoilers*
review:
for funniest death scene ever. I seriously haven't laughed so hard in a long time. Where did they find the woman who played anakin's mom? "Anakin, you're so handsome! I love...youaaach....euuuch......uuuugh..."

As for the rest, well, the movie sucked because of all the reason's previously stated. Too much CGI that doesn't follow the laws of physics, etc. There was a scene in which there was a REAL canoe on some REAL water, and it was so jarringly out of place because it wasn't CGI enhanced. Even yoda's lines ridiculous were little a getting.. its hard to sit thru too much of that. And enough with people getting their hands cut off. The only single element that was not directly drawn from a previous star wars movie was the last ditch desperation selling out of yoda's character. I admit it was the most entertaining part of the movie, but come on, it's just not yoda's style.

Also, let me just say that christopher lee should have been cast as Anakin, and that anakin's corruption to the dark side should have started when he was much older than 16. The tragedy of Vader is that he was once a great and noble jedi, who was twisted and corrupted. Instead we will get bratty and annoying teen who turns to the dark side in a fit of adolescent rage ("I WILL be the most powerful jedi ever! I will! nyah! nyah!) Christopher lee's character is exactly what i had imagined as a pre-Vader Anakin. He almost had me convinced he was on the good side when he was talking to obi-wan..someone who can be seemingly wise and yet menacing at the same time. Plus, he's tall enough. When he is walking with the emperor at the end, it's almost like he IS Vader, just without the armor. couldv'e been perfect..

title: action packed
review: loved it. great action, great effects, not the greatest acting but hey who cares it is star wars. i love how the story is coming together. the light saber fight scenes are great as usual. can't wait for the next one!!

title: Amazing. Lucas is back on form...
review:
What a great film. I was sure I'd be disappointed but this film had it all. Yes, even Yoda fighting. And he's really tough...

Basically, the plot of this film was better thought out and better paced than Episode One. While Episode One seemed to drag in parts, AOTC never loses the momentum it picks up from the very start. There is a lot less extraneous material, scenes are not just filler between action sequences.

I thought Hayden Christensen was excellent as Anakin, giving a great performance as someone who is not so much angry as frustrated. He plays the part of angst-ridden (Jedi) teenager very well.

The rest of the main cast turn in typically solid performances. Samuel Jackson is great as the pontificating Jedi Master and equally good as the galactic arse-kicker he becomes towards the end. Ian McDiarmid again pulls off the sinister Palpatine excellently.

Christopher Lee should be singled out for his performance. It's his best in years, imbuing Dooku with sinister overtones without the pantomime theatrics that he brought to Lord Of The Rings. He underplays it well until the final lightsabre fight in which he unleashes pretty well!

The effects were awesome. Loads of people are going to knock them because they are not totally photo perfect but thats just dim. The effects are neccesary to the film. Effects have never been photo real, and people who think the effects in the first trilogy are better are kidding themselves. I remember watching the Special Editions at the cinema and the effects are not a patch on what Lucas is doing now. The effects are not 100% perfect, but I'd rather that than have no films with effects.

Some of the best parts of the films were the links to the original film. The secret plans carried by Dooku are the plans to the Death Star. The Lars homestead is meticulously recreated on Tatooine.

So all in all I thought the film was amazing. Again miles better than Return Of The Jedi and in some ways approaching A New Hope. It has a similar down-beat-but-hopeful ending to Empire Strikes Back and is more similar to that film than any of the others. Lots of people won't like it simply because it's not a carbon copy of the original trilogy, but I think this film can stand alongside the others as a true action/adventure cinematic great.

title: Fantastic sci-fi, magnificent specials effects and a plot that works.
review:
As one of the world's GREAT Science-Fiction fans, I've always felt a little disappointed at the fact that I couldn't see what everybody else apparently saw in the 'Star Wars' movies.

Yes, I understood the references. Yes, I loved the concept of the 'Space Samurai' (Jedi). Yes, I accepted that from an objective, cinematic point of view, they were good movies. But subjectively, I wasn't really into them...they were just a way to fill up a couple of hours of dead time.

'Attack of the Clones' is different. In this movie Lucas has finally managed to entice me into his universe. With a script that pokes fun at itself throughout the movie, well-rounded characters, superb visual effects (with one 2-second exception of which Lucas should be ashamed), creditable performances from the entire cast and a strong storyline that moves the action along in an intelligent manner, this movie is destined to be a HUGE blockbuster and should serve as a good example to anybody of how to construct a Science Fiction movie.

Cinematically, this is a good movie. In my personal opinion, it's a GREAT movie.

title: Puts you back into the universe.
review: Great filmmaking.Ewan really owns the part and the music by John Williams is terrific. Its nice to be so reconnected to the Star Wars Universe and this film is truly a saving grace. I am very hopeful that the next film will be something very special.It is after all the ending in Georges dyslexic yet dynamic universe.

title: what is the bigger waste? my $5.50 or lucas's millions
review: unfortunately, i came into this movie with unusually high expectations.  i will try and make this concise.  the plot was lengthy and slow.  the acting was rather poor.  anakin's lines were childish and whiny rather than tortured and misunderstood.  the love scenes were similarly weak.  anakin again came up short and appeared like a little boy with a obsessive crush rather than a young adult reuniting with his soulmate.  the movie consisted of drawn out action sequences that ended in an anticlimax.  the ten minute car chase scene and the ten minute run through the droid factory stand out in my mind as particularily large wastes of time and money.  i understand that the point of the movie was supposed to setup anakin's turn to the dark side, however, the film barely develops anakin as a character, much less a likeable character that the audience will identify with or sympathsize with. am i wrong or is anakin supposed to be a tragic hero?  i cant wait for him to fall into the molten lava pit and stop with the poorly acted and written lines.  oh yeah, the c3po "humor" was by far the worst part of the movie. i dont know why anyone over the age of 5 would see it as comic relief.  ewan mcgreggor was good and natalie portman was stunningly beautiful and decent. the rest of the cast is forgettable and detestable by turns.  i think less cgi, which the movie crammed down the viewer's throat at every turn, and more quality acting, plot development, and dialogue would have been a better use of the ungodly amounts of money lucas spent. all this movie did successfully lower the bar for episode three, further depreciate my respect for lucas a filmmaker and writer, and make me depressed about waiting another 4 years for a movie that will undoubtedly be just as poorly done. is it any wonder why my friends have lovingly dubbed this movie "episode douche?"

title: An improvement...
review:
Entering the cinema my expectations for Episode II were extremely low, as opposed to three years earlier with 'The Phantom Menace'. Perhaps this is the reason I enjoyed this movie so much more, but then again, perhaps not...

'Attack of the Clones' has a lot more of the genuine Star Wars "feel" to it. Although Hayden Christensen's performance as an actor isn't too impressing, it's still interesting to see his character start growing into what one day will become Darth Vader. The love story is intriguing but unfortunately ruined by poor acting and dialogue... George Lucas could use some kind of help with this kind writing/directing as it certainly isn't his field of expertise.

Natalie Portman is gorgeous but surprisingly dull in her performance, I'm thinking this isn't her own fault, but the director's, Evan McGregor is solid but the dialect gets annoying, Samuel L does his job, as does whoever is playing Yoda.

Despite it's few flaws, the poor acting mentioned and in my opinion excessive usage of digital fx and animation, this film is very watchable for anyone who liked the old Star Wars trilogy, I tried to think of the STORY and imagine it being acted a lot better, basically this movie is essential to Star Wars freaks, not because it is an excellent movie in itself (not too bad either!) but because you want to know what happened before the first trilogy. Can't wait to see the third and final episode and find out how Lucas managed to tie it all together!

title: On C3P0's amnesia and The Beatles...
review:
Episode II: Attack of the Clones is fine sci-fi entertainment and a definite improvement on its predecessor. But does it deserve the Star Wars brand name?

Gone is the bold economy of the earlier works; I am reminded of the scene in the original film in which Moff Tarkin informs Vader that the Emperor has dissolved the senate. One line, that's all we need to know, back to the fun stuff; the background politics are sketched in and give the movie extra weight and character, but they do not intrude upon the central action. It doesn't matter if we miss all mention of the senate, or if we are too young to know what a senate is and understand the effect its disollusion will have - all we really need to know is that a bad guy has a beautiful girl locked up and she needs rescuing. In AotC, there are an awful lot of officials looking very grave and saying and awful lot of things to each other in a very grave and official way. All political manoeuvrings are up there on screen and consequently the entire film is a slave to them. Gone is the gung-ho swashbuckling adventuring of a motley band of rebels - these guys have government endorsments. (And this is significant: George Lucas is no longer the rebel fighting against the rigid and out-dated studio establishment with his low-budget motley crew, he's one of them now, he is Hollywood hierarchy.)

The plotting: The original trilogy was an epic tale of good against evil, drawn from myth and legend and ancient tales. It was elemental, it spoke to us all. Every part of it - the characters, the situations, the plot - was an archetype, and that's what made it great, a real feeling of an age-old story playing itself out against the backdrop of space. To be sure, everything about AotC is fine: the characters and story are good, the visuals superb... but it's a TV mini-series. It doesn't speak to race-memory as the original trilogy did, it merely does everything it should to take the story from point A to point B. The overwrought political machinations, the complex character motives, the somewhat lacklustre set-pieces all belong to a 10-part serial explaining to us what happened leading up to the actual movies.

The set-pieces: it's all fine fun, but where are the great, indispensable moments? Maybe, at a push, the final duel of the first film and Yoda going nuts in this one, but that is all. Do a couple of poisonous centipedes, a rainy brawl, a dangerous conveyor belt and some gladiatorial action even compare to the trash compactor, the space station which blows up planets, the assault down the trench, the snowy battle against lumbering tanks, the father-son revelation, the Sarlaac pit, the speeder bike chase etc. etc. - indelible scenes which turned cinema upside down and yet at the same time seemed to have been around forever? The original trilogy was teeming with defining, iconographical moments, whereas pretty much everything in TPM and AotC has been... adequate.

Add to the plot complexities and diluted pacing Lucas's seemingly compulsive quest for ever-tightening spirals of internal continuity. In the original film, R2D2 and C3PO were the lowly "everymen" with whom we could identify and who just happened to be in the right place at the wrong time - they found themselves parties to a magical adventure beyond their wildest dreams. They were merely two droids, any old droids, knocking about the ship at the start of the story but who ended up part of something special. They were proof that any of us could have what it takes to be heroes. But now what? C3P0 was built by Darth Vader and spent 12 years on a farm he had no recollection of sometime later when he just happened to drop by there again by sheer one-in-a-billion chance; R2D2 was in it right from the outset and wasn't in fact lying in the original film when he said that he was the property of Obi-Wan Kenobi in order to get the message to him - it seems that Old Ben (in similar fashion to C3PO) was suffering some form of advanced amnesia when he claimed never to have owned an R2 unit! So in fact, when we join "innocent bystanders" R2 and 3PO at the start of the original film, there's a whole lot they're not telling us.

In many respects, Star Wars reminds me of The Beatles. Yes, Free As A Bird and Real Love were nice tunes in an airbrushed, MOR kind of a way, but compared to I Am The Walrus, Hey Jude and Strawberry Fields Forever, they are worlds apart. And the reason is the same: like The Beatles in 1995, George Lucas is no longer lean, hungry and desperate to prove himself against the stodgy might of the old establishment with his pioneering spirit of invention - he's middle-aged, comfortable and has the whole world at his disposal... and that means a whole lot of polish for very little wood.

title: Impressive, most impressive
review:
A spectacular film that recaptured the magic of the first two episodes. When talking about the quality of a Star Wars film, it is only proper to evaluate within the context of the series. That being said, this film is easily the equivalent of each of its predecessors. The acting, which is being panned by many major critics, was as strong as that of any other Star Wars episode. The story was more intriguing and more enveloping than any Star Wars film to date, and the both the sound and visuals were amazing.

With Attack of the Clones, Lucas has recaptured the magic of the originals, its a shame that some people seem to have lost their ability to feel the magic.

This film scores a 9.5/10 for me!

title: The Force is strong with this one !
review:
After what feels like an eternity waiting for the next Star Wars film, I finally got to see Attack Of The Clones' at the midnight showing at the Odeon along with 3 of my friends.

The atmosphere was like no other that I've witnessed at a non Star Wars film. As with the Phantom Menace' the auditorium erupted into cheer when the opening titles appeared on screen, and likewise at a certain part of the film to.

As with any film, seeing it with friends can make for interesting conversation after the film has finished, although at half past 2 in the morning, thoughts are more likely to be towards getting some sleep. However, enough was said to show that opinions on the film ranged from, rubbish' to most enjoyable', of which my own opinion falls into the later category.

That's not to say, that I didn't have a few niggles, but generally they are concerning the visual aspects of the film.

As anyone who may have read previous letters of mine in the Gazette, I have before now, expressed my opinion on the continued reliance on CGI graphics in films. And unfortunately, however realistic they may look, they are not a patch on real actors. There is just something about these computer graphics, that takes away the realism. And as a result, the original Star Wars' (pre special edition) trilogy will never be bettered.

That aside, Attack Of The Clones' I felt was an improvement over the Phantom Menace' despite a fairly slow start.

If you go into watching this film remembering that it is essentially a kids film, then you'll not leave disappointed, as all the characteristics of a Star Wars' film are in place.

Roll on episode 3, I'm off a bit of sleep before returning in a few hours to the Odeon to see it again.

The Force' is definitely with George Lucas

title: Pretty decent, better than I expected
review:
I read a bunch of reviews from critics and users here on imdb.com, and thought the movie was gonna stink. Well... it was much better than I thought it'd be. Yes, 70% of the dialogue sucked and could have been better written by... well... almost anyone. A lot of the acting was wooden and "I dont care just give me my paycheck." Some of the CGI was REALLY bad and fake looking. ALL the romance scenes were either cliche, cheezy, or just plain... oh man... just BAD. Lucas should stay far far away from romance.

Spoilers ahead...

The good points: Action was fun. Was cool seeing some unexpected things and foreshadowing, as well as references to the 'future' (prior) movies such as meeting Luke's 'parents' as teenagers, Chancellor/Emperor Palpatine, etc... and Yoda is the MAN... err... creature... err... whatever he is... he kicked ass :)

Overall, I liked it a lot more than I thought I would. I give it two thumbs up. Go see it, it's worth your $8. Spiderman was better however ;)

title: Thrilling and Disappointing at the same time!
review:
***SPOILERS***

I love the star wars saga since I was 7 years old and saw it for the first time in the theater in 1977. The sense of wonder it gave me was amazing! That feeling for the most part returned with Episode I (except for Jar Jar Binks...YUCK)

Episode II is an inconsistent beast for me.

First the good....the fight scenes, action sequences and visuals are outstanding...great to see Yoda and Samuel L. Jackson and the Jedi Knights kick butt. ***Spoilers*** I love the forshadowing of things to come in the original trilogy....i.e. the death star plans and the birth of stormtroopers. Hayden played the anger and ego of Anakin very well.

What brings this film down for me is its pacing and lack of tightness in the story. The middle third of the story is slow and I was actually BORED!!!...which for me is a cardinal sin in a star wars movie. I thought the pacing in Spiderman was much better. That brings me to another point...One important purpose of this film was to establish the love relationship between Amidala and Anakin and it was completely flat! I just didn't feel the emotional connection between these two like the sweet yet corny one between Peter and MJ in Spiderman. (Yes, I know these two films are not comparable on the whole, it is like comparing apples to oranges, but I think these aspects are appropriate to compare)

In conclusion, I did enjoy this movie a lot for its visuals and action and the set-up for Episode III but parts of the story fell flat for me. Oh well, its still Star Wars and I can fast forward through the slow parts on the DVD if I want to :) 7/10

title: Lucas is still a pioneer in the industry
review:
The movie, finally here, delivers. Yes it is over 2 hours long, but in the end we all want it to be that long don't we? With another 3 years to wait for the final installment, we need all the Star Wars screen time that we can get. All the Star Wars films are around 2 hours long, so why would this one be any different?

I, considering myself an extreme movie buff who has seen literally thousands of movies, have never seen anything like this movie before. It's not just the scenery, but the depth of the battle scenes. It makes any battle scene of any movie look like fodder (including Episode I's climactic ending battle scene which was impressive).

The critics of ALL the Star Wars movies are a bunch of self-proclaimed astronomers who expect space laws to be followed to the ninth degree. Give me a break. I'm so sick of hearing about how Yoda didn't act very well or how Hayden and Natalie didn't portray their on-screen romance very convincingly. They did just as well as any. Their performance was hardly worthy of any criticism at all. Considering some of the lines of previous installments (i.e. "No I'll not leave you, I've got to save you"-Mark Hamil, Episode VI; "Let's try spinning, that's a good trick"-Jake Lloyd, Episode I), this movie has an excellent dialogue for a Star Wars film.

Lucas has really out done himself this time, though, imagery wise and story wise. Unbelievable twists, young Boba Fett (a newly sworn enemy of the Jedi), pre-technological artificial limbs, etc. We are all so glad he agreed to have someone help him write the script as you get a few extra ideas and less not-so-great lines.

In the end, the movie is excellent. I have seen it only once so far, but will definitely make it out to see it many times in the theater not as a tremendous fan of Star Wars, but a fan of the awe that the imagery leaves you with.

title: Well...that happened
review:
Went to see Episode II last night at 11:45 PM. Theatre was pretty full, although not at capacity. Unlike with Episode I, there was no spontaneous pop when the lights went out, or when the Star Wars theme started. Sort of an ennui seems to have set in after the first film.

What worked:

-- Obi Wan. I thought Obi-Wan carried the film tremendously. Ewan McGregor may be the only capable actor in the film. That is the difference between the original trilogy and the current releases, the acting is just not up to par.

-- The last 45-minutes or so saved the entire film for me. The fight scenes were are all entertaining, and Yoda going crazy got the biggest pop of the night (the only pop actually, the crowd was dead silent throughout the film, outside of a few chuckles at the cheesy love dialogue.)

--Lack of Jar Jar was good. He had like 2 lines. He was actually booed by some of the audience when he came onscreen. Ok some of the audience was me :-)

--Mace Windu. I thought Jackson was strong in his role, I just wish he would have had more time on screen.

What didn't work:

--The Plot. I know Lucas couldn't finish the screenplay himself and had to bring in another writer to fine tune it, but c'mon, this dialogue is some of the worst in any movie I have ever seen. I think half of the nutcase star wars fans on the internet could have written a more coherent script. Amidala all of sudden falls in love with Anakin, after he slaughters, women and children. Ahhh, how sweet. Don't cop out and say it'a Star Wars, it has to be cheesy, ESB and ANH were not cheesy IMHO. Yoda with the Moliere-esque Deus Ex Machina finish came across as somewhat lame to me (although expected).

--Hayden Christensen as Anakin. He was stale and rigid throughout the film. I thought he had a couple of decent facial expressions in the film, but overall he was pretty bad. I don't want to watch She's All That in Space.

--The opening city montages were reminiscent of Blade Runner in that neon glowing world kind of way. It didn't feel like Star Wars, it felt like Neo-Tokyo or something.

--Overall, the scenery with the millions of colors still feels out of place for me. There's just too much CGI in the film, I don't know how else to say it. The original magic contained the human element, whereas these films are so CGI-based that the actors are often talking or working with blue screens. Yes the film looks pretty, but that isn't why people go to see these films. Just because you can do something, doesn't mean you have to do it.

--Who are the fans supposed to side with? This may be an ancillary point to the above one. When I went to see ESB and ROTJ I went to see Luke Skywalker and Han Solo. They were my heroes. But are there any heroes here? Yoda? I really think they need to develop a strong "hero" character that the fans can associate with. It's hard to associate with Anakin when you know he becomes Vader (well actually I went into the film hoping to associate with Anakin, because that's the crazy b****rd I am, but still). The problem is that the main hero is spread out over a series of characters, Obi-Wan, Amidala, Anakin and Yoda (he did get the biggest pop out of all of them). There wasn't enough storyline for these characters to develop.

--Natalie Portman hasn't grown into a good actress yet. There isn't much more to say. She had a pivotal role in this film, but spent her entire time on screen virtually expressionless.

-- Jango Fett. I remember the actor from the New Zealand film, "Once Were Warriors" as a crazy wife-beater, I think his name was "Jake", it's been 6 years since I've seen the film. Anyway, I'm not quite sure why Fett is even involved in this to be honest. Was Lucas just bowing to the cult of Bobba? Does he have big plans for him? What was the point of having Bobba appear so sympathetic?

The film is definitely worth seeing, at least for the last 45 minutes or so. No it doesn't feel like Star Wars to me, but what does? Lucas will never regain the magic of the original films.

title: Great, but would be better if Yoda wasn't CG.
review: As somebody whose main complaint about The Phantom Menace was that it was too computer generated, it was inevitable that I would say the same about Attack Of The Clones.  With this, Episode II, the special effects are greatly improved, as is the story.  Depth is added to characters, the action is spectacular, and in short this is a great deal better than Episode I. However, this movie fails where The Phantom Menace succeeded in that Yoda is now completely CG.  He looks unbelievably synthetic and is, in my opinion, far too different from the Yoda in the other installments of the Star Wars saga.  It can be said quite correctly that Yoda need be CG for some parts of the film, but a more traditional and realistic puppet could have been used for the majority of his screen time.  Nevertheless, this is tremendously enjoyable, action packed fun which needs to be seen on the big screen...and needs to be seen more than once!

title: Lucas has run out of ideas
review:
This film is far, far superior to the Phantom Menace. However, George Lucas has left himself with too much to do from a storytelling perspective, and appears to be way out of his depth. For all his claims of having the grand storyline written all along, he suddenly has to get from point A (powerful, precocious young Jedi) to point B (most evil man in the galaxy) over the course of two films, and it doesn't look like he knows how. What results is a mess of cliches and rehashes of his own (and other people's) work, riddled with inconsistencies and contradictions, and with parts looking like the opening chapters of My First Book of Love Stories.

The special effects are, of course, astounding. It's rumoured that 95% of the film isn't real, and although that's certainly believable, you may have a hard time spotting the gaps between the genuine 5% and the rest. The Phantom Menace was technically impressive, despite its other more obvious (and less forgivable) flaws, but this film exists on another level beyond it. However, special effects do not the film make - and although poor effects can ruin a film, perfect effects do not make it a success (just look at the Final Fantasy movie).

This effort may be heralded as a "return to form" for George Lucas, but if that is the case, then it makes me inclined to go back and watch the original trilogy with a more critical eye and see if they are as weak as the most recent two. And I don't want to do that - I treasure my childhood memories.

Exciting, visually magnificent, in parts amusing, but overall it is a two-hour exposition of the mind of George Lucas, which seems far shallower, and emptier, than I'd ever considered. An improved 6/10 to the Phantom Menace's 4.

Kids should love it, if they know what's good for them.

review:

(POSSIBLE SPOILERS FOLLOW)

title: Just a ordinary movie which doesn't feel like "StarWars"
review: I just went to that movie yesterday and like Phantom Menace it was a real disappointment. Most of the people will have seen the movie by now so I won't bother about the contents of the movie. But a few thing have to be said. At first the setting is beautiful made. The locations the costumes they all look beautiful and the special effects are awesome. The music is quite good and has a nice opera effect when hearing it. But this doesn't make the movie a "good" movie. Although the landscape is beautiful made it has no atmosphere. The whole look is like seeing a normal US city in the future. The whole concept of another world with its own culture and civilization has been neglected. Those people in that planet is nothing more than the USA in the future. And all the people in the movie behaves the same. No cultural differences. The whole idea that the queen had become a senator was terrible. The whole personality, and elegance of an aristocracy have been wiped out by this idea. A chosen queen??? The whole meaning that Luke Leila SkyWalkers background is "chosen" and "special" is just gone. And the way she acts is so ordinary that you don't find her to be an important person like the people in the movie suggest she would be. The whole concept of the Jedi knight was meant to be some kind of an elite order of knights within the system. In the movie they just differ from the rest of the soldiers that they are fighting with light sabers and not with laser guns. It doesn't fell that they were special at all. They had no special customs or rites. No symbols or mythologies. And the fighting scene was very nice done but also dull. Those people are fighting robots... The excitement is missing when you know that they are just machines. All in all the movie lacks the "magic" and "atmosphere" of a good epic space opera. It wasn't epic at all.

title: 2 out of 5
review: if i preferred this film over the last installment, it would be merely because of its darker leanings.  the transitions between both stories was a bit jarring (watch "empire" to see how much more of a flow it has).  and the romance was very forced.  i found the action sequences to be too busy and noisy, preferring the essence of suspense over spectacle displayed in the first two star wars films.  yoda fighting might've been cool on a visceral level, but was it necessary?  in the end, does it take away the mystery that is part of yoda's charm?  overall, i find lucas' new direction for his saga to lack the majesty and enchantment of the original series.  it's a shame really.  but i can't be too upset.  afterall, the original three are good movies, not great ones like the mass public would like to think.  the first three have lasted this long and have made such an impact on our generation simply because we saw it as children and now they contain a certain nostalgia, something the new movies would never be able to compete with. but compared to the action films of kurosawa (who was a large inspiration for lucas), the star wars films lack the brilliance, insight, and - yes - imagination needed to be a true masterpiece.

title: Worth staying up for, mos def :)
review:
I've just seen Ep 2 at midnight on the morning of May 16, and it was worth it. I won't try to describe the film's storyline as *you'll see it very soon* (old jedi mind trick :), I just want to alleviate fears of Phantom Menace syndrome. The title, Attack of the Clones, really is the only stinker in this film.

Hayden Christiansen is so-so as Anakin, but you can see him trying to act way above his current talent at one important tragic scene. Natalie Portman has ditched that awful faux-English accent she sported in the last film, and does alright considering Lucas's famed lack of emotive directing. Ewan Macgregor is good as Obi Wan, full of wry looks and showing the ability to carry the subplot that will come to fruition in Episode 3.

The love scenes (or indeed any scene just between Amidala and Anakin) are reassuringly clunky but not too cringe inducing, the effects are as you'd expect from Industrial Light and Magic, though there is definitely the influence of Ridley Scott's Gladiator towards the end. Lots of actors, some new to the story like Jimmy Smits, have little to do but speak some bad dialogue in wait for the next film.

Coruscant looks beautiful, and the scene for some of the most breathtaking effects I've seen. A debt has definately been paid to Blade Runner and The Fifth Element, and you really feel part of the city as opposed to the rather staid wide setting shots that were dished out in the previous film.

Yes, someone says 'I have a bad feeling about this'. Yes, as many people have already stated, YODA ROCKS. The wars in this star wars movie are executed fantastically, with the action focused on one battle rather than flitting between two inequal scenes. And Threepio for some reason is given some great jokes! I'm not complaining, and you won't be either. I'm off to get some sleep...

title: God bless Lucas for Star Wars
review:
I've loved Star Wars since i could remember watching movies. When I heard Lucas was finally going to make the prequel trilogy, I was ecstatic! Episode I had obvious flaws, but it was still great in my book, it's part of Star Wars! As for Episode II. I Loved this movie!! To attack the critics reviews, here we go:

1. the acting is wooden: Yes, in parts it is. But like many before me, did they watch the original trilogy? And also, these are being modeled after the serials of the 30's and 40's, have they ever seen any of those? This is the way Lucas envisions it, don't knock his vision, we all love it. (Plus you try acting in front of blue screens and characters that aren't there!)

2. The love scene dialogue was bad: Ok, this was pretty bad and cheesy, I'll admit it needed some help. But no one is perfect. They should try writing a film saga in 6 parts sometime.

3. Too many effects: When I came into this film I was afraid that a purely digital Yoda would be a horrible idea, but it plays so much more naturally than I could ever have hoped. Some people gripe about Yoda's fight scene not being natural (if he can do that why does he need a cane?) Come on, it's the force. We've all seen the insane things these Jedi can do when harnessing the force. Love it, Yoda kicks ass!!!

Overall, I was so impressed by this film. I thought it was much closer to the original trilogy, plus loved the use of Darth's theme for Anakin at points! My only gripe is I wish they would have shot on film instead of digital. I had to sit close to the screen, and the pixels showed pretty badly. Hopefully this was just my theater.

Small details aside, This film rocked! George Lucas, thank you for your vision.

title: Why this is such a great movie...
review: There are many reasons why "Attack of the Clones" is a classic piece of movie making, and, while it may have some faults - which are few and far between, by the way - it manages to hold your attention throughout. *SPOILERS* OK, where should I begin. The film begins with an attempt on the life of the now Senator Amidala which spawns the beginning of the end for the Republic. Obi Wan and his apprentice Anakin are appointed to protect the Senator from further attacks. AOTC contains numerous references to the original triology which are sure to please fans. Many of the original triology's mysteries and plot holes are filled in this installment, such as how Owen and Beru Lars came to be Luke's Aunt and Uncle. The transition of Anakin to the dark side is magnificently done with appropriately dark music accompanying the scenes as Anakin's emotions tear him appart and force him to give in to his anger. While those who say that the film's romantic plotline are exteremely poor are not wrong, it is not something which takes away from the film's enjoyability. The acting of these particular scenes, while not being astounding, is exceptionally good when you actually look at the script which they had to deal with. The acting is perfect otherwise with Ewan McGregor performing excellently as Obi Wan and Christopher Lee playing the villain, Count Doocu, brilliantly. Fans of the series will not be dissappointed with AOTC as it contains some marvellous visual effects taking full advantage of the new digital technology available. The road is well paved for the original triology's events with the newly created Clone Army bearing a striking resemblance to the Stormtroopers, telling us fans how they came to be. The transport ships at the end which come to take the Clones look a lot like the infamous Star Destroyers. My favourite homage to the originals is the inclusion of "Jango Fett", the father of the chilling "Boba Fett" from TESB and ROTJ. The scene in which he and Obi Wan share a spine-chilling conversation had so much suspense in it that I was glued to my seat. It was clear that both he and Obi knew who each other were, but neither wanted to act yet. I read someone say that it was stupid as Jango would have killed Obi on the spot, but they are wrong. We see that Jango cares deeply for his son, and he obviously did not want to put him in danger. Finally, for those of us who always wanted to see the true extent of Yoda's power, we are not left in the dark, as he gets fully involved in the action, hurling streams of lightning and running rings around Doocu with his lightsabre. This was one of the best scenes combined with the duels between Anakin, Obi Wan and Doocu, and of course, the MASSIVE fight sequence between the entire Jedi order with the Clones, taking on the joined might of the Trade Federation's army and numerous other evil armies. We see Mace Windu showing us his power with the incredible beheading of Jango, which was sad because I liked him. There really is too much great things in this movie to describe in a thousand words. So, I will just say, go and see it. While this film can not please everybody - the critics will obviously say so - it should please those of us who like to see lightsabres, the force, digitally enhanced scenery, a two foot tall killing machine (Yoda) and a whole lot more.

title: Not the best of all but very close
review: Finally and after a long drought Episode 2 made it`s appearance. I must admit that I`am a huge Star Wars fan. I grew up with it and fell in love with the Story and the way it appeared and was made. It was a milestone something like the first man on the moon. Jackson is awsome again although he just has one of those smaller roles and even if most is computer generated it catches you and really puts you in another world. title: An old fan's viewpoint
review:
Standing in the queue to see this movie gave me butterflies like a 16 year old experiences before an exam. Would the old magic be back? No set piece battle to begin with followed by a segment that left one wondering more than in wonder. However momentum built up like a boulder careering down a hill, with the same explosive conclusions!

No-one can claim this to be a film without flaws. One line by Christopher Lee could have come straight out of B List Ninja film. However we got to see things we could only imagine before-the political backdrop, the role of the Jedi and maybe why they need to control their emotions (dangerous things those lightsabres).

No actor will be in close up when they give out the Oscars for Best/Supporting roles but the FX folks can sit smugly back at a job well done. Some of the set pieces are simply breathtaking in their detail.

And if you have seen the film I bet you're already scanning the net looking for a release date of Episode III, and you weren't doing that after Phantom Menace...

title: John Shaft with a light-saber, what else can you wish for?
review:
After early reservations, long waiting lines and a number of seat-switches (to get a bit further away from the screen) i was ready to see "Attack of the Clones", and boy it was worth it!

In "Attack of the Clones", Lucas restores his biggest flaw from Episode 1, which is Jar Jar Binks. In this movie Jar Jar is not given more than 10 lines. Personally i was hoping Lucas would have Jar Jar get shot in the first 10 seconds of the movie, but this is a good-enough alternative for me :)

The performance of Hayden Christensen was bad. Especially the supposed 'nightmare scene' was a pain to watch. The other actors did a fine job (given the weak lines they where fed by the play).

While some people critisize the 'digital Yoda', i personally found it to be an improvement to the puppet. It is well rendered and animated, allowing more emotional depth to the character. And lets face it: Without the digital Yoda, we would never have the kick-ass swordfight everyone raves about!

While the script lacks depth, the beautiful surroundings and constant flow of action in the second-half of the movie make up for it.

The special effects in this movie where good. The screen is flood with action everywhere, the backgrounds look fantastic (even better than in LOTR) and the swordfights are better than in all the other starwars movies. Finally we get to see Samuel L. Jackson in action. John Shaft with a light-saber, what else can you wish for?

All in all, Star Wars Episode 2: AOTC is an entertaining movie if you don't mind the plotholes and sometimes weak screenplay. For me personally Natalie Portman and the Yoda swordfight would be enough reason to see this movie (again).

title: Worst episode ever
review: Ok now i love star wars, but this movie was bad. The dialoge was awful and Natalie Portman was very non-convincing as an actress. Lucas should not be directing these movies, he didnt direct the empire strikes back or return of the jedi, and those are the best in the seires. This movie went nowhere. But there was some good things , like Sam jackson as macu windu and ewan mcgregor as obi-wan keniobi.

title: Finally a worthy successor to the original trilogy!
review: After the disappointment I felt with "The Phantom Menace, I am very pleased to say that the series is back on track with "Episode 2".   Yoda, R2D2, and C3P0 are finally given more screen time and Jar Jar only has about 2 minutes of screen time.  PERFECT!  The droids have always provided the comic relief and they just don't need the annoying hijinks of Jar Jar. I'm rating this movie a "9" out of "10", only dropping one star because of some hokey dialogue in the love story. But Lucas has really redeemed the series with this one and now I'm really looking forward to "Episode 3."

title: A worthy follow up
review:
Now, who would have thought! The story's starting to build up very nicely and the whole patchwork of open links are starting to make sense. Darth Sidious plan to conquer the universe shapes up and future actions are hinted.

George Lucas uses an array of spectacular visuals to set the scene for our two lovebirds and battalions of fighters to get it on. He even brings back the beloved 70ies zoom-function (through some fluid CG-created creatures).

Now I just have to wait 3 more years for the next installment... so be it...

title: A Pretty Good Movie
review:
Just wanted to throw in my 2 cents since I don't really see the comments that most people who have seen it have:

This movie has an outstanding last hour. I was extremely satisfied with the entire last part of the movie.

But the first 90 minutes of it are full of cheese, bad acting, unmemorable dialogue, and extremely slow-moving plot. I'm not sure if it was a case of bad directing, or just plain bad acting. I was yawning my way through the whole first part of it.

That's about as much detail as I care to go into because I don't want to give up any spoilers. I want to finish by saying this movie is definitely worth seeing. The last hour is that good. But keep your head on your shoulders going into it. Overall it's a good movie, but it suffers from some serious dragging for a large part of the movie.

title: What's missing? Jar Jar. Woo Hoo!!
review:
I saw this movie while in the States for a short stay. Opening night in Kentucky lacked all the colorful characters of a big city openening, but none of the excitement.

Opening credits rolled to cheers and the exctacy of another Star Wars film.

From the start, one would be skeptical of the quality of another movie after some of the disastrous choices in the first episode, but the presence of the infamous Jar Jar was short and fleeting, leaving a good taste in the mouth. Unfortunately, Lucas needs to maybe re-think what the character of Annikan Skywalker should be at young ages. This Christiansen guy should be doing soap commercials rather than starring in one of the most beloved movie sagas in history. ("Wow, my skin really does feel cleaner!") He is predictable, and his emotions of fear and rage are laughable.

Putting aside the young Jedi's performance, this movie overall does not lack in other categories. We see wonderfully exotic places and sets, experience incredible, but not intrusive, CGI displays, and witness fight choreography that we can still be amazed at. The light saber duel starring our fuzzy-eared green friend was worth a 15 hour plane trip alone.

Overall, you will get your money's worth out of this installment. It rivals the first in my mind, putting aside sentimentality. Well I got to run down to town to get some power converters. I hate to leave with a corny cliche like "may the Force be with you", but I can't resist.

May the Force be with you!

title: Go see this movie, my Padawan Learner
review:
Okay to start this off, I just want to state the fact that I am one of the biggest Star Wars fanatics in the world. Star Wars is less of a movie and more like a religion to me. So when Episode I ended (and slightly disappointed, but I understood it was just a start), I began the three year anticipation for Episode II. Thankfully, the anticipation was WELL WORTH IT. I consider Episode II not only to be a great Star Wars movie...but (some may say I'm wrong) I consider it to be my second favorite in the series (sandwiched by #1 Empire, and #3 ROTJ). Episode II starts off with a big bang, literally. When there is an attempt on Senator Amidala's (Natalie Portman) life, the Jedi Council assigns Master Obi-Wan Kenobi (Ewan McGregor) to protect the headstrong senator. Lo and behold, Obi-wan arrives with his padawan, a 20 year old Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen). From the offset you can see that Hayden tackles the role very well, bringing a depth that Episode I lacked. The Jedi have a mandate that states they must protect the queen, but in doing so they pursue her assassin. I won't spoil, but suffice to say, the pursuit leads them into deeper...and darker, things. So what everyone wants to know: Is this movie less one dimensional than Episode I? YES. It has everything that Episode I had (EXCEPT JAR JAR, HE ONLY SHOWS UP FOR ALL OF 10 MINUTES-GOOD STUFF), knockout special effects, incredible lightsaber fights (Let's just say that an little green Jedi master fights), great action sequences(Great Clone War sequence). But it also took a note from Empire and built on subtle underplots and love themes. Anakins transgression to the Dark side pops up in Episode II...but wait till Episode III for the full transformation. This movie did not disappoint this Star Wars junkie at all. The Force is strong with Lucas and his team once again. I'm very happy to be a fan of the greatest movies of all time. So to sum it all up...go see Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones. It's more than worthy of your time. Whereas Episode I was all killer,no filler; Episode II is a Pie of buttkicking.

May the Force be with you.

title: You aren't George Lucas
review:
I saw Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones last night. I thought it was fantastic! However, this morning, I logged onto the IMDB, and started reading the comments the other users have posted. I was a bit troubled.

After reading through these comments, I have a few of my own.

First of all, the critique of the acting is acceptable. I don't agree with most of the points made, but that's a matter for personal translation.

Second, the people who are deriding the effects...were you watching the same movie I was? The effects in this movie far outshine anything else I have seen...including the Matrix and LOTR, and definately Spiderman. Maybe that is simply because it the newest, but if you didn't like it, watch the battle scenes again. Wow.

Third, the "Attack of the title". Leave the title AOTC alone. You don't get it, do you? Yes, the clones fought with the good guys in this movie. DUH! All part of Palpatines master plan! He hasn't revealed himself as evil, yet....he's getting the good guys to do his dirty work for him! DUH!

Fourth, and most importantly, the critique of the plot and the love story. I have a question: CAN I SEE YOUR DRIVERS LICENSE? DOES IT SAY "GEORGE LUCAS"? NO? THEN WHO ARE YOU TO CRITIQUE ANOTHER MAN'S VISION. IF THIS IS WHAT LUCAS BELEIVES HAPPENS IN ***HIS*** STORY, THEN THIS IS WHAT HAPPENS! SO SHUT UP! The love story is necessary. Otherwise, how would Luke and Leia ever be born. The sub-plot involving the cloning facility is necessary. The clone wars are an integral part of the Star Wars universe history! Even the much derided Jar-Jar Binks has his purpose in the whole storyline revealed. Amidala would never have done what he did while acting on her behalf. Jar-Jar has a purpose. Still annoying, but he has a purpose.

In conclusion, I'd just like to say that those who hated it so much should just shut up and go watch "A Boy's Life"...obviously more your speed.

title: George's got it back on track that certainly isn't a cloned film!
review: Attack of the Clones is simply not as good as Star Wars, but then again that's our problem..... we are expecting the impact of A New Hope. But this is Star Wars in 2002. The special effects are outstanding. The crew has to win the special effects oscar or I'm going to cut my feet off!! Obi Wan flying through the air dangling off an assassin droid is simply a new achievement in special effects. Hayden Christensen shows off a fantastic talent, especially in his reunion with his mother. Superb. Portman's acting is a little wooden especially in the "by the fire" scene. But what points she loses in acting, she more than makes up for with sensual, lingering looks & fantastic costumes (well done the costume dept). It's in this film that we first get a taste of everybodies favourate Star Wars character. Although he's still only a young child, he still manages to give off a "I wouldn't mess with me if I were you" aura. Boba Fett of course is being bought up by himself (or rather he's a clone of his older, slower self), that is Jango Fett. & Yoda..... wow. Imagine a squashed, green, angry Bruce Lee & you've got everyones favourate Dagobah resident. Just cool! Well done George for jetesoning (One of his favourate words)the tight plastic atmosphere of Episode 1 & making Episode 2 one of the best films of the year! Finally, is Dooku good or bad? I'm sure there's a couple more surprises up Master Lucas' rather big Jedi cloak sleeves.

title: Going going and...nowhere
review:
I would classify myself an enthusiast when it comes to Star Wars. I read 2 reviews on IMDB before seeing it. The 2 reviews said this was much better than Phantom Menace (PM). I quite enjoyed PM and gave it 7/10 (therefore still a disappointment when it comes to legend that is Star Wars). The prospect of seeing something better got me very excited.

Maybe it's because I'm getting older and more cynical... Attack of the Clones (AOC) disappoints in many ways. The love story is a major failing. Was the magic between Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher recreated? Far from it. What about the nice romance in Spiderman? Not even that. Natalie Portman is pretty to look at. But that's about all there is to this love story. Not only is there no love chemistry or acting talent in this supposed love component, the plot while a potential master-stoke (beautiful young queen falling in love with a younger man who came into her life when he was only a boy) was rather spat out poorly.

The original star wars contained: (1) Fantastic cinematography and mood (eg Luke Skywalker pondering his future and gazing at the twin moons rising); (2) Harrison Ford; (3) Legendary characters (Darth Vader, Wookie, Ewoks); (4) Simple fun plot weaved with very cleaver storyline ("I am your father!").

AOC contains: (1) Good CGI but not good enough (many scenes looked like cartoon); (2) Fun action scenes; (3) Intriguing plot but falters somewhat; (4) Horrible horrible romance; (5)Some hideous looking Jedi knights with some getting slaughtered (deservedly).

I give AOC 6/10.

title: An uneven film with few highs, many lows
review:
While most seem to feel that this was an improvement over The Phantom Menace, I found AOTC to be much more flawed overall. Granted, there were some real highs, what I call "fanboy moments" such as the visuals, the battles, Yoda, the Fetts, and Ewan's much-improved performance as Obi-Wan. Unfortunately, the movie is filled with terrible dialogue, uneven pacing, unforgiveably bad edits, and a horribly hacked edit of a wonderful music score (make that two, since they re-used so much music from TPM).

The romance element is unconvincing, almost creepy, due to inept performances by Natalie Portman and Hayden Christensen. I can only assume that the director himself is to blame, considering that both performers have done so much better in other films, and Christensen as Anakin does have one brief shining moment late in the film.

Of course, one doesn't come to Star Wars looking for fine art. But even as a "summer blockbuster" and "come to be entertained" kind of film, sitting through the bad bits makes it hard to enjoy the great bits when they come. Nothing in the original trilogy was this bad, and even the vilified "Phantom Menace" had a fraction of the clunkers to be found in "Clones". Although there are classic moments that rank amongst the highest in the Star Wars series in AOTC, the uneven elements ultimately make it the most disappointing entry in the series.

title: Maybe The Best Science Fiction Film Ever Produced!
review: I have seen all of the Star Wars movies out and by far this episode is the best.  The production was a work of art & the fight scenes where the best yet.  You have to check out Master Jedi Yoda fighting with a light saber to understand what I am referring to.  Overall this was a great movie, my wife even loved it.  If you have not seen it then make plans to watch it!

title: Fantastic!!!
review:
SPOILERS SPOILERS SPOILERS SPOILERS SPOILERS

First of all, let me say that I was extremely sceptical after seeing the several trailers posted on the internet. I felt that Lucas was repeating himself storywise and have stated so in several BBS's all over the internet. This scepticism was of course fueled by the in many ways severely flawed Ep1:TPM. I have been a Star Wars fan from the very first hour and dreaded this next installment.

But.. and here comes an enormous BUT...

I was wrong, I apologize to George and his entire crew and cast for losing faith in them. Episode 2 made may jaw drop almost all the way through. Right from the start this rollercoaster ride rolls at a breathtaking speed through several interwoven storylines, four planets, extremely well crafted special effects, a love-story that is more credible than I thought Lucas was able to write and a big load of intrigue, fun, humor, excitement, anger and the list goes on.

Hayden is excellent and extremely dark (I say two words: Tusken Camp), his eyes and words reflect Vader in a human form. Natalie is good as always as the ever beautiful Padmé, she looks more and more like her daughter every day (that was weird saying that). Ewan takes a turn for the better in this flick by making Obi-Wan the more responsible Jedi, in a way he takes the role of Liam, he is more and more becoming the quiet hermit we see in Ep4:ANH. And then there is the rest of the excellent supporting cast: Christopher Lee as Lord Tyranus, Ian McDiarmid as Palpatine (scheming as ever), Jimmy Smits as the future foster father of Leia and of course Samuel Jackson as the ass-kicking Jedi Mace Windu. Oh and let's not forget the awesome new version of Yoda, he is absolute too ass-kicking (the whole theatre went up in cheers when he grapped his lightsaber!!!)

Is there a downside to this installment? Yes, sure there is. The dialogues are not always as solid as they should be, as are the acting performances. Some of the blending of life-action and cgi wasn't all that good. But in the end I was extremely relieved when I left the theatre.

Thank you George for bringing us back into the universe that is so dear to so many people. Despite its flaws, this is what Star Wars is about, fun movie viewing. Me and my friends were left with so many questions after the first viewing (e.g. why did Qui-Gon not disappear at the end of Ep1:TPM, it seems he wasn't all that benevolent as we thought he was.) Aargh now we have to wait another three years!!!!!!

I'd give it a 9.9, so that becomes a 10 when you round up.

Cheers George, thanks and don't disappoint us with Ep3:???.

title: Genuinely good film. Lots of good humour and action
review:
This is a great film. Lots of good action sequences, and these ones are actually relevent to the plot (unlike Episode 1). The plot never drags, though one fault I found was that it switches between simultaneous plots too quickly. All the acting is brilliant, though some of the CGI is obviously fake and this could be done better.

Another great thing about this film is that it is very self referential. There are many jokes and puns that rely on the viewer having seen episodes IV-VI, and these pleased the big starwars fans in the audience (me included). The jokes were very frequent, and there were many throw away lines that got the whole audience laughing...

A wonderfully crafted film that took the audience through all sorts of emotions... The final battle scene is incredible, and the way the movie ends is very dramatic. In this respect it suffers the same problem as The Fellowship Of The Ring, in that it is a movie that does not tell the whole story... It is not a movie within itself, but tells only part of the story, and leaves the audience waiting to find out what happens next. Overall a great film.
