Star Wars freaks will get a lot out of it, much more than episode I, and newbies who haven't seen ANY starwars film will appreciate on its own merits as well.

title: Better than Phantom Menace, but........
review:
To start things off, I'd have to say that George Lucas is a genius. He brought the first Star Wars film (now known as Episode IV- A New Hope) into our lives in 1977, The Empire Strikes Back in 1980 and Return of the Jedi in 1983 and they still remain to be the most magical, imaginative, creative, innovative & influential films of all time. Simply put, they were classics.

Then in 1999, George had an idea - to bring the prequels to the big screen. Hence, Episode I - The Phantom Menace was released, leaving everyone who saw it confused, wondering where Lucas' magic went. To soothe the scars of abuse heaped on audiences by the impotent direction and blatant racial stereotyping of Episode I - The Phantom Menace, the only criteria this installment really had to meet was: be better than its predecessor. Not a difficult task, and Attack of the Clones is an improvement over the tragedy witnessed three years ago. Alas, "better than Phantom Menace" still doesn't mean Clones is a particularly good movie. The film's central focus - the "romance" between Senator Padme and Anakin Skywalker is tediously dull. How people as boring as they are made kids as interesting as Luke and Leia is beyond me. No chemistry whatsoever, Lucas probably thought, " That's ok, the Lightsaber duels scenes are gonna save this movie". This film offers some of the strongest casting of many recent films, yet the casts are never utilized, never given material, dimension, or direction which allows them to shine. Bombarded with 90's cliche lines like, "I hate it when he does that", is truly unacceptable, especially for a Star Wars film. Even Arnold Schwarzenegger delivers punchlines more clever than that.

This film just suffocates itself so much trying to be legendary like the first trilogy but hip enough to fit the new millennium.

I guess all I have left to say is the Force may have been with George Lucas directing Episodes IV-VI, but since viewing the first two prequels, he may have turned to the Dark Side.

title: Fantastic... but overdone.
review:
This new Star Wars installment sees Lucas move into an upper echelon of special effects. But is this necessarily a good thing?

I am of the firm belief should only augment the story and not dominate it, as happens in Attack Of The Clones. The saga that began (or ended) with such a fantastically involving story, complete with such intense mythical underpinnings that Joseph Campbell (the renowned mythologist) himself looked upon it favourably. Its a pity now that it has degenerated into an orgasmic explosion for the senses.

If you have no problem with what's mentioned above, the sensory overload will no doubt appeal to you and, by all means, get out and see the film for yourself. But for any discerning film buffs who look deeper than the superficial images, for any concepts or, God forbid, even a theme, I wouldn't bother.

I seriously doubt whether Attack Of The Clones will garner the same enthusiasm in a few decades as the original trilogy currently does. The emotional depth just isn't there, as it was in A New Hope, Empire and Jedi.

title: Great look, weak writing
review: While "Clones" is much better than "Phantom Menace," it still lacks a feel for engaging dialogue.  Rick McCallum should have written it in addition to producing it. The reason that "Empire" is widely considered to be the best of the series is because Larry Kasden wrote the script.  Good writing is Everything!

title: The magic of cinema
review: Much as I wanted them to be wrong, I couldn't help but give some credit to the reviews I'd read of this movie, which at best damned it with faint praise ('well, it's better than the last one...') and at worst dismissed it completely as an unfathomable, soulless exercise in expensive FX and bad acting.  Surely, even if they were overly critical, there must be some truth to these appraisals?  I enjoyed The Phantom Menace, but had to concede some of the points made by its detractors.  Would this be just another 'fun, but flawed' piece of sci-fi fluff?  I'd hoped for so much more, especially after Lord Of The Rings had delivered so spectacularly. Well... I'm not sure exactly how to put this... but not only was this film better than Fellowship Of The Ring, it may well be the best Star Wars film of them all.  I left the cinema dizzy with elation, hairs on end as they had been throughout the last 2½ hours.  Take your pick of superlatives - awe-inspiring, epic, captivating, enchanting, riveting, breathtaking, spectacularly beautiful... it is all of these and more.  The characters are solid and often intriguing - in Ewan McGregor's Obi Wan Kenobi we have a classic action hero who could be the prototype Jedi; Hayden Christensen as Anakin Skywalker is a complex, often brooding figure for whom we can all feel some empathy.  With his innocent beginnings, the descent into the Dark Side and eventual redemption which are to come, this phase of Anakin's life completes the cycle of classic tragic hero.  Natalie Portman makes Amidala into more than just a love interest, truly convincing as the future mother of Princess Leia.  The supporting cast is crammed with memorable performances, from the (very!) animated Yoda and the righteous Mace Windu to Jango Fett and the menacingly powerful Count Dooku.  The many worlds are bustling with all manner of alien life, charming and menacing at turns. The special effects... they need no introduction, except to say they are more convincing than computer generated images have ever been before.  Nothing breaks the spell. Were there any flaws?  I suppose there must have been.  Flaws as seen in the original trilogy, and as seen in Fellowship, and a thousand other films heaped with unconditional critical praise.  The critics must have had their own agenda in slating this film - I feel most sorry for those who claimed they couldn't follow the plot.  Perhaps they need to reconsider their choice of career, because the magic of cinema can rarely have been in such evidence as it is here - if it eludes you, it's your loss.

title: the Star Wars Lovestory!!!!!
review: Star wars have always been fancy fighting with deathplanets and all that. In this episode the focus of the film is on anakin skywalker and Senator Padmé Amidala. Its a lovestory with a little bit of action and fancy details and special effects. But if you have seen all the other Star Wars episodes you will know that this film builds up for some very heavy action in the next episode. I gave it 6 out of 10 point because it could have been 30 minutes shorter and still get the story told.it got a little bit BORING

title: Could be better
review: After a disappointing Phantom Menace I tried not to set my expectations too high this time. Which is just as well. For me the script was poor at times with too many cliches and for the first hour I found myself cringing at times in my seat. The love scene was too prolonged and downright corny. The most notable performance was Christopher Lee who was his usual excellent self. The highly talented Ewan McGregor seemed to be struggling converting his Scottish accent into an upper class English accent and Hayden Christensen looked as though he had been plucked from some mediocre amateur dramatic society to fill the role. Although he does have my sympathy as the lines he was given were not exactly inspirational. Having said all that the film did improve considerably in the second half. The battle scenes and special FX were superb which was to be expected. On balance this was a good light entertainment film well worth seeing and certainly a big improvement on it's predecessor. But unfortunately, Lucas again failed to achieve the exceptionally high standards expected of him. I awarded this film 7/10. Had the script been of a higher standard with better casting I would have edged it up to a 9 or even a 10.

title: Thank the Maker!!!
review: Attack of the Clones is an excellent addition to the Star Wars saga. The film sets a much more darker, moody atmosphere reminiscent of Empire'. The film's special effects are mind blowing and my only criticism would be that at some points in the film there is so much happening on the screen you just don't have time to take it all in. I suppose that what video and DVD are for. Hayden Christiansen's portrayal of the older more unruly Anakin is very convincing. You feel different emotions for the character as the film progresses. Don't get me wrong I don't think he will get an Oscar nomination, but his older version of Anakin is what it should be. The rest of the characters pick up their parts from Phantom' and develop as the story progresses. The main flaw in Phantom' was the lack of story. This film does not fall into that trap and gives the viewer lots to think about. More references to the original trilogy are made throughout the film and this helps you once again fell as if you are back in the Star Wars universe. One nice touch are the scenes set in the homestead of Owen and Beru. Shots and camera angles are exactly the same as the original film. Once you get to the battle at the end of the film you will have forgiven George Lucas for Jar Jar and the menace that was Phantom' and see the true nature of a Star Wars film. If you haven't seen this movie yet go and enjoy the experience. It will definitely make you feel young again.

title: Most unimpressive
review:
Disclaimer: I'm not part of the target audience of the film

The Good: more action than TPM, a new Sith lord with a brain, some nice new costumes and designs, memorable love theme, some nice settings, the Anakin-Shmi scene is moving, enjoyable acting from McGregor and Lee.

The Bad: disastrous dialogue especially in the first half, inconsistent characters - or not enough character development, many plot holes, indulging in unnecessary CGI, noticeable changed and overdubbed lines, weak CGI characters ( this includes Yoda - although he was done with great detail, he was not consistent with Episode V ), unnecessary "comedic relief" from R2 and C3P0, amateur acting from Portman and Christensen - part of the blame goes naturally to Lucas who's posing as a director again.

The Ugly: seems that lot of stuff ended up on the cutting floor that would have made this movie more fluid and consistent. Having read the preliminary scripts, I see that Lucas traded off conflict and depth for action and CGI scenery. As if he is ashamed to make a nice movie - and part of me can understand him when seeing the reactions from the average fan. These people want action and toys, as if there isn't a new action movie released every week.

To summarize:

What I wanted from the movie: to tell how Anakin's most important moments in life changed his character pushing him towards the "Dark Side", and actually see those mysterious clone wars.

What I got: CGI w***fest, implausible "convenient" plot, an uninspired forgettable action flick for toy collecting 9 year olds. The PG rating seems to apply to Lucas' filmmaking skills as well.

The DVD release might remedy many of the problems I listed, I'm curious how it will turn out.

title: My favourite film outing of all time
review:
It's 3.20 am on Thursday 16th May 2002, and I'm barely in the door from just seeing a the first official showing of AOTC in Northern Ireland, and my heart is pounding and my smile is fixed. I guess this means I got to see it before you guys in the US :)

Two screens in the cinema are showing the film at the same time, and you can tell the fans booked theirs really early, as all the t-shirts, pony tails, guts and babbling conversations about a certain one on one between two masters of the Jedi art are in screen 1 - my screen. One guy dressed as Darth Vader walks in and out of the auditorium to the immense delight of the crowd, resulting in the unknown hero receiving a massive applause. As you may guess, the atmosphere is simply electric.

The film starts, the music pounds our eardrums, and we are ecstatic to see the trademark yellow story card scroll into space before our very eyes. It's been three long years...we don't know what to expect after the last drab episode.

At long last we have what we wanted - comedy, romance, mythology and lashings and lashings of cold, hard action (not to mention a great deal of irony). Shortly after two hours has passed something happens on screen that makes every single living soul in the audience shift in their seats....the legendary fight between Yoda and Dooku. I will not spoil it, but I will say that this alone was worth the price of admission.

I left the cinema fulfilled and refreshed, kind of surprising for the time of day. I say my favourite film outing of all time not just because of the film (which, admittedly, has faults), but because of the great feeling of the unspoken union between all people there watching the magic on the silver screen.

title: Star Wars is for fans only.
review:
Episode 2 goes on to confirm that the Star Wars universe can only be appreciated by fans only. I liked Episode 2. I liked Episode 1 as well. In fact I watched Ep1 3x in the cinema and never once got bored with it. I liked the characters in both Ep1 and Ep2. I didn't think Jar Jar Binks was annoying. In fact without him Ep1 would have been really dull (Ep 4,5 and 6 had C-3PO to provide the fun factor why not Jar Jar for Ep1 considering C-3PO only had a minor role in Ep1). I think the acting was good. Typical Star Wars. No nonsense, polite (compared to movies these days). The story is well told and I dare say the ending was one of the only few movies this past year that raised a few Oh I see.... Example: And I thought Count Dooku was..... Oh I didn't expect him to...... And what do you know, both sides were...... And that's why he did it. He wanted to.... This is what happened to me in the end. Truely rare. The only other movie that came close to it was Sixth Sense. I really don't understand critics these days. In fact I think people should always remember the critics name and institution he/she from when reading such critics. Why? I guarantee that the same person would have gone to the cinema and criticised 8 out of 10 movies he/she is supposed to review. It has its faults I admit but waw is that bad till some critics gave it a D???? If it got a D, then almost all other films out there should have gotten a Z. Special effects criticised. Too computer based. Well whether all the critics like it or not, this is the future of Science Fiction.

Again this is a movie strictly for fans and people who like the Star Wars type. This movie is great. Why? It brings into reality all the things fans have always wanted to see. Coruscant. The origins of Stormtroopers, the origins of Boba Fett, the origins of the Death Star!!, what was it like in the Republic times. What was the Jedi Council like and many other things. I gave it a 9/10 because in my opinion no movie can ever get 10/10. No movie is perfect so for those critics out there, if you ain't Star Wars fan, you won't understand the magic and you're missing something truly great.

title: Not as weak as the Phantom Menace but still weak...
review:
I admit it wasn't as bad as the last movie but the movie is at best mediocre. The charm of the first movie, a New Hope, was the one story line of the little band of heroes just escaping from one scrape to another and finally ending with the big Death Star climax. In Empire, we got two story lines, Han, Leia and gang and Luke and Yoda. Again, Han just escapes from one scrape to another and Luke face Vader and loses. Great stuff. Jedi had three story lines. Lando and the fleet, Han & the Ewoks, Luke and Vader on the station. It was a bit much but it worked. Weaker than its predecessors but it was still good.

Flash forward a few decades and we all greatly anticipated the great epic that was Star Wars: Jar Jar Binks. Enough said. I saw the movie three times and came away enjoying it by blocking out Jar Jar the 2nd and 3rd time.

This time I expected very little. I wasn't disappointed. The story line jumped all over the place. As soon as I got interested in someone (the bounty hunter at the beginning, Bobba Fett's dad) they're gone, just a flash in the pan. Christopher Lee should be a great villain but we don't see him until the end. Ewan McGregor just seems to be walking through his parts and leaves me not caring about Obi Wan which is sad since I was a huge Sir Alec Guiness fan. I didn't expect much from Christiensen, I mean Canadian TV to Star Wars is a bit of a stretch, so I forgave him his annoying pouty moments. I thought Portman was great, beyond the fact that she puts Carrie Fisher to shame looks wise. Yoda of course steals the show but too little, too late and any way when a puppet is the best part of a movie... hmmm...

I'll see this movie two more times. I had to do the same in order to enjoy Phantom Menace. Maybe I'll soften after a few more sittings. But I'm afraid the magic of the first three movies so many decades ago will never be recaptured by Lucas

title: Three Years for This???
review: The movie is 2 and a half hours long which is a plus nowadays, but the content sucked. It is worth going to once, but not more than that. When the Phantom Menace came out, the only reason I was excited to go, was to see Darth Maul. With the lack of a menacing villain (pun intended), the movie drags on and on. The only things worth talking about is the Jango/Boba Fett backstory and the 40 second fight between Yoda and Dooku. I'm not saying not to see this movie, I just don't recommend seeing it more than once.

title: DISAPPOINTING (STILL)... here's why:
review: What was the true attraction of the original Star Wars?  The awesome and unstoppable power of Darth Vader.  The whole story revolves (rightly) around him.  Although fairly interesting, the `creating of Darth Vader' can logically never be as riveting as the fully mature version.  Which would you prefer to watch, Macbeth in action at the peak of his career or Macbeth as a young lad unsure of where his future lies?  That's why regardless of the depths (or lack) of creative story-telling in these three 'prequels', all will fall short of the final (original) version.  At best it can be a suspense-filled build up to the full monty.

title: Eye Candy doesn't make a movie
review:
I've got really mixed feelings here. On the one hand it's Star Wars, so it must be great, but the evidence speaks otherwise. I should say that we went to see it twice, and my opinions changed a little on the second viewing. First time through, I thought it was terrible. The dialogue was atrocious-that line about sand being coarse etc. plumbed new depths. I've played video games with better dialogue. And the guy that plays Anakin is one of the worst actors I have ever seen. I guess the material doesn't help, but Harrison Ford pulled it off in Empire. The pacing is clumsy to say the least. From the first time Anakin opens his mouth you are sledgehammered with his rebellious nature, and those brooding glares he pulls at the camera every few scenes made him look constipated. He couldn't even deliver the most famous line in Star Wars history: "I've got a bad feeling about this". What's with ninja Yoda? I appreciate that he is supposed to the best with a light sabre but I thought it would be cooler if, despite his skills he never has to fight. The battle with Dooku at the end looked like leftover scenes from Willow until the light sabre battle which sort of looked good in a Hong Kong action movie sort of way, but just didn't fit right in the movie.

The scene in the droid making factory looked like a level from Sonic the Hedgehog. The arena at the end was from Gladiator, the huge battle looked like it was ripped from the Final Fantasy movie, the chase in Coruscant was from the Fifth Element and when the clones arrive, it looks like Yoda meets "Black Hawk Down". The movie looked like a re-hash from George Lucas' most recent visit to his local video store. Yoda spouts wisdom about the force, not no-brainer action movie guff. Returning for a moment to the chase in Coruscant-it was far too long, and in the end the audience is cheated out of there being any real point to it. Sure they get the dart which ultimately leads to Jango Fett, but it seemed like a poor trade for all that screen time.

And Jango Fett. . . . He acts like a reject from a grim soap opera, and little Boba running around was laughable. They took one of the most enigmatic bad guys in action movies and turned him into a brain dead lug in a cool suit.

Whenever I meet a woman I always try and be polite and charming, but this is obviously wrong. If I want to marry someone like Natalie Portman, I should really be creepy and obsessive. Chicks must dig this.

And so we come to our second viewing, which only took place after some serious thought about asking for refunds on the tickets. I guess the problem with Star Wars is that expectations are always going to be so high. By the second viewing I had no expectations, and I actually enjoyed it. Sure the dialogue still sucks and the acting is still pretty poor, but this time I just got swept up in the action and the whole feel of it. There are still some things I don't like about it. The pacing seems wrong, the love scenes are too long and the dialogue is pretty poor.

What's to like about it. . . . ? It looks amazing. The scenes at the end when Dooku meets Sidious and Anakin and Amidala get married are great-very reminiscent of Empire. The action is breath-taking and there is no other movie which so convincingly creates a complete mythology except maybe Lord of the Rings, but since that is based on a classic book it doesn't really count.

A final comment about expectations. . . . I had huge expectations about Lord of the Rings-I've played Dungeons and Dragons for almost 20 years and this was going to be the movie of my hobby-it lived up to all my expectations. ..

title: George Lucas = Bad Director!!!!!
review:
Why in the world would Lucas not entrust this film to another director? Because his ego is too big. These first three movies should have been absolute gimmes. Instead, Lucas has managed to mangle the screenplay and direction so badly in the first 90 minutes!! that AOTC can barely recover. AOTC has its moments, and some decent performances from Ewan Macgregor, Christopher Lee, Ian MacDermid and the unforgettable computer animated YODA. There is a decent battle scene and the confrontation between Dooku and the Jedis is quite good.

Unfortunately we have to endure some pretty bad dialogue and screenplay moments along the way. So very bad are these moments that they force Clones into a cinematic corner it only so barely recovers from. Truly laughable moments include but was not limited to the entire dialogue delivered throughout the movie between Natalie Portman and Hayden Christenson. This was just horrible chemistry and it was obvious that Lucas is uncomfortable with the portrayal of onscreen romance. It seemed like very defensive direction, like he was forced to include the relationship and did not know how to accomplish it without mangling it.

Padmes ability to shake off a fall from a speeding starship onto the surface of a planet was not only unbelievable but laughable in the way it was filmed. Almost like out of a comedy skit Padme is rolling around on the ground in what is assumed agony until a Stormtrooper (clone) comes to her (aide?) and asks her if she is alright....the reaction....is like uhhh yeah no problem and she gets up without any problem and RUNS off breasts a bouncing!!!! So implausible I burst out laughing.

Other unintentionally funny scenes and my personal favorite in regards to the bad things with this movie was Anakins nightmare scene. Poorly placed in the final cut of this movie it was an unnecessary scene which had already been implied several times. Well, it was so poorly done and placed just after Anakin had been rebuffed by Padme that at first glance it looks like Anakin is well.... uhhh....masterbating. I know I wasnt the only one to think this because several people in the audience started laughing at this point. I had to stifle a laugh on the verge of hysterics it was so rediculous. And it kind of went with Anakins character. Whiny and creepy. Which is too bad because it ruins the appeal of Darth Vader as a bad guy in my view. Now we all know the guy is just a whiny punk with a very bad attitude.

All in all I was disappointed in AOTC, but it had its good points which is more than Menace had. NO one is more disappointed in writing a bad Star Wars review than I. I was a huge Star Wars mark growing up.

It could have been much better George. Peter Jackson proved a fantasy epic could be done properly earlier this year. Let go of your feelings George, trust the fans and let a proper screenplay writer and director take charge. You just dont have what it takes.....

title: Finally! This movie had all that I missed in episode one.
review:
After seeing episode one I had pretty low expectations on this second episode, but after a bit slow introduction of the 'new' characters the movie really takes off and Gorge Lukas takes you for the ride of your life! The last part of the move is really breathtaking, the battle scenes has nothing more to wish for.

We also get at insight on why Anakin is drawn to the dark side and for the fans of Boba Fett there is some sweet candy in the form of Jango Fett (Boba's father) and his son (Boba).

All in all, the Attack of the Clones is a worthy member of the Star Wars Saga!

title: The Road to Hell is Paved with Good Intentions
review:
The seeds are sown for the ultimate coup for Episode 3. Like Episode 1, the Dark Side moves in shadows, with deception and lies that further his dark agenda while seeming to be in the best interests of the Republic. This time, the agenda is not to gain political power, with Darth Sideous already has, but to gain control of a military force he can use to enforce his rule on the galaxy. Separatists, including the Trade Federation are striking to rebel against Republic Control with a huge army of even more advanced battle droids. But there is a possible salvation; another huge army of clones grown at the order of a dead Jedi Knight over 10 years ago - clones grown supposedly for the Republic!

While Jedi Knight Obi-Wan Kenobi seeks to uncover the mystery, and capture the source of the clone army, a bounty hunter named Jango Fett, the Jedi council realizes how deeply the dark side is clouding their ability to use Jedi visions to foresee events.

Meanwhile, young Padawan Anakin Skywalker receives his first independent assignment: the protection of former Queen, now Senetor Padme Amadala, who, as the chief opponent of a Republic Army, finds herself the target of a plot to kill her. Unfortunately, his reunion with her stirs feelings of love and passion, which are forbidden to the Jedi. Worse still, his dreams of his mother in pain and suffering lead Anakin to return to Tattooine in a desperate attempt to find her. No more direct comments, but master Yoda stated it best. "Afraid to lose her are you? Fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. Hate leads to suffering." Some of the seeds for his descent into a Sith lord who is more machine than man are firmly planted.

Side note. It is clear that Anakin is the chosen one who will bring balance to the force. Jedi fade and the ability to become one with the force, while still retaining a sense of self was unknown to Jedi before this time, and Anakin opened the door for this, very slightly, in this episode. Obi-Won will understand it eventually, allowing himself to be struck down to allow Luke and company to escape, while still being able to guide him.

Final note. Don't underestimate Yoda. He is wise, and kindly, and a good trainer of Jedi, not to mention a master who can gain insights into the force unlike most others. However, he is a true master of the force, and if pressed, the kindly teacher of the ways of the Jedi is a dangereous and deadly opponent if forced into battle. For knowledge and defense, a Jedi uses his power for. Short he may be, but don't underestimate his ability as a Jedi.

title: Vast Improvement!
review:
Definitely a step up from Episode 1. The set ups established in the first installment are elaborated greatly, particularly Anakin's sense of discontent with the Jedis. The character's roles become more defined, particularly those of the Jedis, and for those who were asking the question, Jar Jar Binks does have a (large) part to play in the saga.

The performances are generally excellent, particularly the leads, but the support cast deserve huge praise for their efforts. Christopher Lee's Count Dooku is an intriguing character who could have benefitted from a little more introduction but who will hopefully return in Episode 3. The Fett family is introduced as having much more significance than you would have guessed from Boba's contribution to the first three movies (nothing to do with merchandising possibilities I'm sure!) There is also a dazzling array of aliens and humans all with their part to play in this installment.

Highlights include breathtaking fight scenes and a CGI Yoda displaying just why he is the master. There is little to pick fault with this time around as even a sluggish middle is important in setting the scene both for the finale and the next episode. We are left, as in Episode 5, with a calm before the inevitable storm that will be Episode 3. Only another three years to go!

title: Be warned...you won't like this
review: I would give it 1 star but for the excellent visuals, the performance of Christopher Lee and the interesting plot as it relates to Episode I. Otherwise, the acting was mostly horrible (although I'm pretty sure it was due to the ridiculous lines), the editing was poorly done, which caused the whole film to bog down, even during the "climactic" final 30 minutes, there was very little humor and what was there was so poorly done as to cause me to cringe and of course there was the PG rating.  George Lucas seems to have a big fear of losing the very young audience, but by dumbing down this and the last Star Wars films, he totally shuts out the now grown up fans of the first three films.  I hope George doesn't plan to write and direct Episode III, which should be the darkest of all six of them, because he will probably turn it into a childish "adventure."  If you see this film, don't expect too much.

title: The train is not only back on track, its speeding at 1000mph.
review: The wait is over.  When "Phantom Menace" ended, I was happy.  Happy because even though it wasn't exactly what I was hoping for, there was a lot of good in it. And happy because I knew the best was yet to come...but not for  3 long years.  For three years we have waited and today that wait is finally over: We have been absolved with Attack of the Clones. (Mr. Lucas, I never doubted you for a second ;) "Clones" is a lightspeed paced dash through the galaxy; it takes us through what should seem like a lifetime in just over two hours.  Compared to the geriatric pace of "Phantom Menace", this movie barely stops to breathe.  The characters are lovable in entirely new ways and the FX are awe-inspiring.  The dialogue can be clunky, and at times, downright silly, but there are still parts to be cherished.  I now view Star Wars in an entirely new light...it is all finally starting to make sense. "Clones" and "Menace" are not like the originals...they are not meant to be. These are not new versions of Episodes IV-VI...they are a continuation of them.  They are a completion of THE story, and when it becomes possible to understand them as equal parts in saga not and not as a bunch of suped-up sequels, nothing, not even Jar Jar Binks, can prevent you from being impressed.

title: Good-bye Jar Jar!
review:
I saw Attack of the Clones today, and what a relief! Gone are the fear and horror of seeing another Phantom Menace. This new movie is considerably more entertaining, fun, and (yes, Jar Jar) MUCH less annoying than Phantom.

I am not going to say this movie is perfect, but I enjoyed it. Many times I found myself wincing at a deeply emotional line (poorly) delivered by one of the actors, it's true. But these moments were offset by the joy of seeing a good old light saber fight or hearing strains of the theme music.

Attack fits nicely in the middle of the new trilogy, building on the characters while leaving the viewer wanting the final pieces. The love story, Annikan's rebelliousness, and the role of Senator Palpatine all pave the way for the next movie. And I welcome it.

title: Attack of the Cartoons
review:
If Count Dooku is a Jedi who is sick of the corruption in the Senate, then I'm pretty sick of the mindless corruption of this once great series. Now we have Star Wars Episode II - ATTACK OF THE CARTOONS.

I love George Lucas - he is great story teller, but oh my God, is he bad at directing and writing. There's a good story here - it the birth of the Empire, Anakin is becoming dark, and somehow, I don't know how, George Lucas manages to make it all rather dull.

***Possible Spoilers****

I felt saddened by this film, it flirts with crashing through the barrier of Lucas's banal dialogue and clunky uninspiring direction - and a few times the thrill of seeing Star Wars creeps through, but is snuffed out quickly with more terrible dialogue, or another massive special effect that cracks you over the head with it's hugeness and puts everyone in the punch drunk state that Lucas requires his audience to be in. I'm sure people will say, 'but the dialogue was cheesy in all the films' - yep, it was. But it was also fun, and sometimes poignant.

I also felt sad because people are hailing this film as one of the greatest ever. Have we really got so used to bad cinema? What should be great sequences under a better director are just plain dull - like the asteroid chase. The chase of the Bounty Hunter as the opener is floored because you can see they're just hanging in front of a blue screen and you know Anakin and Kenobi aren't in any real danger as they survive for the rest of the series. It still doens't stop Lucas from spreading this particular sequence out over about 20 minutes.

Thank God for the Yoda fight and the bit at the very end where you see the Empire beginning to form.

But in the meantime, Lucas will make his millions and take that as a sign he's doing a great job. Come on George, get a better writer and director in - Search your feelings, you know it to be true.

title: Welcome back George!
review: I had heard mixed reviews on this film. Many said that the acting was bad, that the love story is annoying and that the film was generally not a worthy prequel. I have to disagree. First of all, everyone seems to have forgotten that the acting in the first star wars films was not always top notch. But, bad acting added to its character somehow. I think that the acting in Episode II is perfect for the type of film it is, it adds character. All of you love story critics out there, are you forgetting the love story in the original three. I bet you even liked it, admit it! It is absolutely necessary in this story in order to show one of the forces pulling Annikin off track. In the original three episodes the love story was basically superfluous, so why complain about this one? It is essential to go into this film with an open mind. Forget about the magic of the original films, and forget about the disappointment of episode I and you will have a great time.

title: Has to be seen
review: Overall i really liked the film, but a quite a few scenes made me angry, especially the whole one in the robot assembly factory, WHEN THE HELL HAS R2-D2 EVER FLOWN BEFORE?? and when C3PO fell it looked stupid, as we have never seen him move in the way we saw him do so. I was also shocked behond belief with Lucas including a scene with yoda fighting. I mean i love star wars but i think that this new film and the first film are not doing the overall story credit. I for one preferred the muppit yoda cos frankly i think the computer generated one sucks. I was very pleased to see Christopher Lee in this film as i think he is a wonderful actor and i hope he is also in the 3rd film, i also was impressed with a certain scottish actor who redeems himself after a disappointing first outing as the jedi master. I thought the younger members of the cast also did well, though i found the love scenes a bit poor. Everyone should go see this film because it is good but its no where near as good as any of the originals. I think Lucas has focussed too much on using fancy special effects to wow audiences, rather than wow an audience with a good story like he did before...

title: The Force... What can I say more?
review:
This movie is da bomb. After seeing the disappointing episode I, I was afraid that Lucas would screw it up again but didn't. He made Attack of the Clones an excellent movie. Specially Yoda rocks big time.

A very big thanx to the godfather of space adventures, Mr. Lucas.

And now on to Episode III...

title: swell movie
review: I was very impressed with episode II: attack of the clones. I thought it was alot better than "the phantom menace" it was full of action and new and awesome scenes, that were nothing like any in the other StarWars flicks. I am looking forward to Episode III, only 4 years away.............

title: Don't believe the critics, this one was great!
review: Besides what the critics might have said, I loved this movie down to the very last second. While still showcasing a little choppy dialogue that is somewhat characteristic of Lucas, the movie was still a thrill to watch. The fifth installment in a series of six movies, this one managed to make good on what its predecessor didn't. One noticable improvement can be seen in Anakin Skywalker.  While still not the greatest acting ever seen, Hayden Christensen does a much better job on the character than Jake Lloyd did.  While Anakin in "The Phantom Menace" came off as poorly acted kid hero, Anakin in this movie comes off how he should, a teenager who is slowly turning to the dark side. After seeing the movie twice, I can safely say that the critics were over critical of the acting. On to the movie itself.  While some accuse the first two hours being to slow and boring, I never found that to be true.  Anytime the movie would start to drag, something exciting happened, which kept you wanting to see more. Then there is the last half hour of the movie.  One of the greatest parts of any movie I have ever seen, it gives a little taste of everything, including some humor that involves R2-D2 and C-3PO.  The last half hour also showcases some of the most amazing visual effects ever shown.  The realistic looking CGI Yoda is a testament to the time spent on making the visual effects look real.  And don't get me wrong, the effects through the first two hours are amazing too.  The sound is also done quite well, and helps to immerse in the picture even more.  I would say this movie is a shoo in for Best Visual Effects and Best Sound Editing Oscars, as have many of the other Star Wars movies.  ILM and Skywalker Sound show why the are considered to be one of the best in the business. All in all, this movie is a great one, and worth seeing many times. I've already seen it twice, and I can't wait to see it more.

title: an enjoyable feature; great surprise after Episode I
review:
An excellent Star Wars movie. I was put off by the first trailer (the love-story one) and the Episode One itself... but the movie turned out way beyond my expectations. Story, special effects are great - perhaps the characters a bit bland (although Anankin is scary at times) and acting could be better but then, it's not the heart of the movie.

Jar-Jar appears but is kept to minimum. And Yoda with a light sabre, yeah!

Enjoy!

title: Incredible!!!!
review:
Incredible!!! The second episode in George Lucas' immortal "Star Wars" saga has just been released and it has surpassed even my highest expectations. "Attack of the Clones" is an amazing, action-packed thrill ride not to be missed. I won't waste my time summarizing the plot, for fear that I might give away some plot spoilers and such, but I saw the movie on opening night and I do plan on seeing it maybe two or three more times during its theatrical run.

I've been a fan of Star Wars ever since I was a little kid, and I've been waiting for that long to see the Jedi masters in action, as described by Obi-Wan in "A New Hope". George Lucas has taken us back to the glory days of the Jedi order, before Anakin Skywalker capitulated to the Dark Side, became Darth Vader, and executed the remaining Jedi Knights. One can only hope that Episode III, due in May of 2005, portrays these events as they have been described in all the source materials and in the other films.

Once again, kudos to you, George. A terrific effort by all involved, a riveting plot, awesome visuals and sound, not to mention that Christopher Lee was pretty creepy as Count Dooku/Darth Tyranus, and finally getting an answer to the generation-old question, "What were the Clone Wars?"

title: Better than Episode I, but a far cry from Han and Chewie.
review: It was good, it wasn't great. George Lucas should strictly be an idea factory--spitting out the great, general plot lines--and leave the script writing to those who know what they're doing. There were several lines in this movie that stank of cheese--they were just plain stupid (The Christopher Lee line to Yoda at the end being the most memorable example of crap). It was George Lucas TRYING to make it cool. He can't do that. The first three movies didn't TRY, they just WERE.         GOOD NEWS: JarJar is quite scarce in this film. BAD NEWS: Believe it or not (and this may be a spoiler) but C-3PO seems to fill JarJar's void. WHAT THE...? Did anyone else notice the Sound of Music shot in the love sequence on Naboo? I think even John Williams made reference to it in the first few notes of the score. So, i give it a 7. It really was a good movie, but they just don't make 'em like they used to. And that's another thing. One of the coolest things about the first three movies was the muppets. Why use computers just because you can? The CGI Yoda doesn't even compare to the muppet. I remember when i was little, I thought Yoda was a real little creature living in the swamp on Dagobah. Now, every little kid going to see Star Wars now will spot the CGI in an instant. I personally have more respect for the skill and ingenuity of making a puppet look real than for letting a computer do all the work. Show some respect for the late Mr. Hinsen.

title: Absolutely awesome!!
review: Saw it last night and loved every minute of it.  Way better than the first one with more plot development, action, and romance.  My eyes were pretty tired by the end though, I don't think I blinked once!  You have to see this one or your going to miss a truly epic movie, so don't delay.  I'm definitely  going to see it again asap!!

title: Great piece of cinema: fun, exciting and emotional
review:
I loved this movie. I dig all the Star Wars movies, because they capture so much of what is and always has been right about epic films. The series has also managed to hold the same aura about it since 1977, and still draws huge crowds generations after the original's release. That itself is amazingly impressive.

This installment of the series, however, has drawn a complete split among critics. Some reviewers have pointed to bad dialog and weak acting, and declared this installment of the series "poor" in all regards. Some see the special effects and say that it is a grand cinematic achievement, but lacks depth. Some love the characters, but can't get into the plot. Everyone seems to have gripes about it. However, this reviewer has none.

From the moment I sat down in the theater til the end credits, I was consistently excited and thrilled about the movie. As far as popular critics gripes go, I thought the acting was on par with every other Star Wars movie, and the action and web of plots and subplots complimented each other very well. I felt that the characters were developed very well, and the job AOTC did setting up what we know of the future of the series' reality is due of note. It was a great moviegoing experience, and a great experience for me as a Star Wars fan. There were many classic moments and quotes, as well as groundbreaking scenery and action.

Why then could I, an avid moviegoer, see this movie and leave without having any real problems with it? I think that today, completely unlike the era of the original trilogy, people have a real hard time sitting down and just enjoying something. Movies like the Star Wars titles are simply for that. This saga, the India Jones trilogy, and the Superman films are all great examples of this epic, yet serialized filmmaking. It may not be Shakespeare, and it may not be wrought with masturbatory indie pretences, but its definitely a good time at the movies.

Attack of the Clones is a great popcorn flick. Its a movie that captivates you, makes you feel, and leaves you satisfied. Since when has that not been enough?

title: Star Wars is back and better than ever
review: All I have to say is wow!  I cannot believe the magic in that movie, it blew me away!  From the attention grabbing beginning to the INCREDIBLE end, it was pure star wars rush.  the stuff they do in this movie is absolutely incredible ******possible spoiler warning!!!!  YODA fighting with a lightsaber is the coolest thing ever and is hilarious as well!!!!!!!!******* end spoiler..  That alone is worth the ticket price.  I totally can't see where critics are coming from when they complain about weak acting of a stilted romance, the romance, in fact, seemed way above the "titanic" level, and was very natural, and all the dialogue fit right in with the characters and they're feelings.  A wonderful rollercoaster ride - the last hour is the best science fiction ever put on film!

title: This is a work of art.
review:
This movie was a moving work of art from start to finish. (Period)

I was totally impressed by not only the music but the overall video art.

I highly recommend this movie. I give it 9/10 stars.

title: Critics can kiss my a$$
review: Pure and simple:  I'm as big a Star Wars fan as there is without being a fanatic.  Episode I made me puke and made me leery to see Episode II.  I can honestly say that Star Wars is BACK!!!  Roger Ebert, go eat another dozen doughnuts. Great movie  9/10

title: Yoda kicks ass!
review: For the most part there is noting new in this one. You know what has to happen to get to episode 4, but they don't always take the most direct approach. But to put it mildly, the last 30 minutes turned this fine film into a beautiful action flick that the Star Wars fan has come to expect. The special effects where even better then episode 1! And master Yoda is a hellcat with a light saber!! Mr. Lucas had a story to tell, and he did another bang-up job of doing it. So if you though that The Phantom Menace was good, hang on to your hats, this is going to be a damn fine summer block buster!

title: Vastly underrated by most critics, blends well with the feel of the originals
review:
(extremely minor spoiler warning, proceed if you don't mind learning things you could get as easily from the official site)

As is my usual policy, I held off on reading critical reviews of this movie until after seeing it and developing my own opinions; from what I've read of said reviews, it doesn't seem many of the critics in question did themselves the same courtesy. At my showing I saw a room full of people having a load of fun with a highly enjoyable movie that finally begins to bring together all the loose threads of Lucas's universe, while presenting the viewer amazing visuals and stunning battle scenes along the way, and it is in that spirit that I appreciated it.

The crux of most critics' issues with this movie revolve around its dialogue, particularly in the romantic portions of the film. Frankly, I feel things would be a lot less believable if Anakin were to be a smooth-talking ladies' man; think for a moment, he's a backworld slave turned Jedi, presumably with no romantic experience, who's been obsessed with one woman for more than 10 years...in this light, his dialogue seems at least genuine for the character, although admittedly not some of the most poetic ever uttered on screen. I can't imagine it sounding any better otherwise.

What we *do* get in the rest of the movie's dialogue are plenty of the trademark Lucas one-liners (they've been there since Han Solo, don't start lamenting them now), as well as a side of Yoda that most viewers probably weren't quite prepared for. Anyone who was expecting beautiful prose out of this movie would be well advised to go review the original trilogy, and try to recall what *really* made those movies great. It wasn't stunningly lyrical dialogue of a caliber to put the greats to shame, it was the all-out scope and mythos of the movie, the emotionally genuine characters, the amazing and original visuals, the stirring of the imagination towards that galaxy far, far away, and of course the [more than] occasional bad*&$ action sequence. In all of these areas, particularly the final, Clones delivers with a vengeance, presenting the viewer with what I feel to be some of the high points of the franchise.

title: The Force is strong with this one
review:
Just seen Episode II and I got to write something to get it out of my system... (No spoilers, I promise!)

I... loved it!

It's far better than Episode I.

Plotwise it is about as complex (or non-complex, if you like) as the first prequel and the following (original) movies. Structurally it is more sound than Episode I. For instance, the climax is at the end of the movie, instead of in the middle.

Visually it is stunning. Lots of visual easter eggs to look out for, both design-wise and character-wise, to serve as tie-ins to both Episode I and the original (following) episodes. (This baby is going to run in slow motion and on repeat on my DVD when it is released!) One Swedish reviewer complained that he could discern which backgrounds where digital and that it looked like a video game. In that case I would like to have his game console, I have never seen a computer game this life like.

Well, okay, so the acting wasn't top notch. Jake Lloyd as the nine year old Anakin in The Phantom Menace is actually a better actor than Hayden Christensen as the nineteen year old jedi apprentice in Attack of the Clones. However, he whines just like Mark Hamill as Luke in Episode IV, very amusing! Jar Jar Binks is in it though, but he hardly has a minute of total screen time. The digital characters are better than ever, and even though the all-digital Yoda sometimes isn't as good as the puppet one, the audience cheered and applauded when he finally reached for the lightsaber...

Lastly, one reviewer complained that while technically brilliant this movie lacked catchy lines for fans to pick up. Not so, you just have to pay attention. I picked up one five minutes into the film: Jedi poodo!

10/10. May the force be with you.

title: well done, makes up for Phantom menace
review:
well I liked it.. I really liked it. Action scenes were phenomenal, CGI was done very well (minus a few parts), the acting was O.K. (though cheezy and poorly acted in a few places), but all in all, I walked out with a positive impression. This episode fills in alot of blanks as to how episode 4 starts off. Ewan does an awesome job as obi-wan, and yoda done as CGI looked VERY good in my opinion!

go see it! you won't be sorry!!!!!

title: Four words: Yoda is a legend
review: Episode 1 one was baaad. Episode II is good. Especially Yoda. He is my hero. See this movie, despite being nowhere near as witty scriptwise as classics like ep.V, at least there is no Jar Jar! yay for Yoda!

title: Can't wait for Episode III
review: Great movie!! Totally Star Wars!! For me, the most exciting aspect of the film is all the linkage to the original 3 movies. You know what will happen eventually, but it is cool to see how we are going to get there.  Its fun to speculate where episode III will take us. Can't wait!!

title: Straight from a skeptic: it's actually pretty good.
review:
I really didn't care to see the film right away when it came out. I ended up seeing it with a friend four days after release, because he was more anxious than I.

There's some hokey stuff going on at the beginning. Anakin is a little... strange. The point that he's immature/childish seems to be overdone. In the beginning when there aren't any action scenes, acting seems stiff. Hard to say if it's acting or directing. I don't know.

Other than that: yes there is a story. Yes it was interesting. Yes there was action. There was a lot of neat stuff going on, especially near the end. In fact, all of this was pretty good.

The only other bothersome thing is the use of cliches. There seemed to be a lot of current day phrases and jokes used which just didn't seem to fit into the film.

In other words, it was a pretty good movie with some oddities. Don't let the two oddities set you off, and you'll likely really enjoy the movie. I had thoroughly expected to hate it. 7/10. (I gave epI a 5/10).

title: This is what we were waiting for
review:
This is not just a movie many fans of Star Wars have been waiting for since Episode I, no, this movie might just be everything you could ask for in a movie in this genre. Those of you who liked the prequel to this, there are no doubts that you will love this one.

Episode II introduces magnificent new worlds, atmospheres in which the viewers will just not believe their eyes. Definitely setting new standards in digital effects, just having a look at the planet Coruscant, as well as all other created sceneries, will surely take away your doubts.

George Lucas finally took his foot off the brake and leads the viewers with Episode II into a trip which will surely stay in their minds.

This is simply a 'must see' movie, not only for fans, but for everyone who enjoys great entertainment.

title: Yoda's Comments
review: Deadly dull, this movie is. Effects though plentiful, we before have seen. Wooden and stiff is Annakin the actor. Though Padme be fair of face, her attraction to Annakin, puzzling is. Early on, pizzazzz there was; lightness of spirit, aeriness of touch. Now the heavy side of the Force afflicts us; pondrous we are, weighty with our own religion. A movie this is, in a theater to be shown - a church it is not, or should not be. Too seriously perhaps George Lucas takes himself. A clinkeroo his movie is.

title: Second Best Star Wars film ever...
review:
Relax. This film is everything you wanted The Phantom Menace to be, and if you're into lists then the top five Star Wars films of all time run like this: Empire, Clones, Hope, Jedi, Phantom.

When `A Long Time Ago, in a Galaxy Far Away.' appears on the screen, objectivity goes out of the window. Actually, the 20th Century Fox fanfare always makes me anticipate the beginning of a Star Wars film. And the logo which recedes and gives way to an opening crawl - doesn't matter what it says - is just terrific on a big screen. This is just the result of having seen the first three films on a tiny screen way too often. When the first screen full of stars slowly pans onto a huge planet you can tick of three iconoclastic cinema moments of the last thirty years and realise that someone, somewhere knows how to make a sci-fi film that'll get you going. And you're still only in the opening titles.

It is a return to form. It is spectacular. It is an effects-laden masterpiece. It is complex enough to warrant further viewing. It is a lot of fun.

title: Better than Episode I
review: Well,the wait is over.I've finally seen Attack Of The Clones.Did I expect anything? No,not after the flop of The Phantom Menace.But this time both dramatisation and visual effects are superior to the previous episode.The storyline is good and no one can badmouth about visual effects.Besides there are very good actors like Samuel L Jackson and Christopher Lee.Natalie Portman was good too.Thankfully,she didn't have to wear those horrific costumes for the most of the part.And Jar Jar's having a smaller part is a very good thing.Bad sides? Well, not much actually.I didn't like Ewan McGregor.I thought he was so reluctant playing this role.As for the dialogues,everyone knows that this movie is not about dialogues or drama.Forget about the critics, just have your popcorn and enjoy the movie!

title: Great movie, but still not up to par in my opinion.
review: George Lucas is a creative genius. He has the incredible ability to visualize and animate a whole other universe and place one of the most compelling stories of all time into that breathtaking setting. What Lucas is not as skilled at, however, is writing. This movie suffered from one of the same problems that plagued "Phantom Menace", lack of a script that does justice to Lucas' imaginative fluency. Nevertheless, I still enjoyed "Attack of the Clones," very much and place it third on the list of the best Star Wars films with "Empire" and the origional 1977 film ahead just because of the strength of the story and it's visual effects. But if Lucas could find someone to write a script that incorporated a witty, sharp diologue that featured a less blatent, robotic, cliche filled, romantic relationship such as in "Attack" (a-la Han and Leia in "Empire") this film and episode 3 would benefit greatly.

title: Wow!
review:
I've heard from the critics that this movie lacks in many areas, after seeing it myself I would say that its very hard or impossible to find as many flaws as they claim exist. I enjoyed every minute of this movie, its so much better than The Phantom Menace.

The music is beautifully composed and conducted by John Williams, he has done yet another great job of composing a theme that sounds like a `Star Wars' movie score.

Costumes by Trisha Biggar are not as over the top as they were in TPM, though they will become dated in the future, as some from the original movies did.

In the technical aspect I'd say that the editing could have been better, some scenes should have been just a little shorter.

Ewan McGregor, Natalie Portman, Hayden Christensen, & Christopher Lee did great jobs in their roles. Yoda is amazing! Just as he was about to fight, the theater went wild everyone was clapping and cheering.

Jar Jar Binks is not annoying; he doesn't have much of a role to speak of, which may not be bad.

Fight scenes are spectacular, also the chase scene in the beginning. There are a few surprising scenes (which I'm not going to say which ones) that are, in my opinion, unexpected and traditionally different that other SW movies.

I gave it 10/10.

title: "That blast came from the Death Star!"
review: A tear came to my eye as the opening words of Episode 2 began.  Ever since the ending credits of Episode had rolled off the screen, I was in zealous anticipation for this second coming of the new trilogy.  Was it good for all that wait? By God yes. It certainly was paralleled to the originals, in my opinion being just as good as the best; Empire Strikes Back.  The questions this film answers a really welcomed, we are told of where the storm troopers come from, how and why Darth Vader (Anakin Skywalker) is consumed by the evil dark side of the force, and the biggest "blast" of all, the origins and concept of the death star - this revelation was marvellous and left me in awe. And one last thing, we have always heard throughout the Star Wars Saga how great Master Jedi Yoda is. I always questioned this thinking, "this little green thing doesn't do much at all." After seeing Attack Of The Clones, you will certainly appreciate why Yoda is called "The Master." Oh, the film was spellbinding, I have to stop writing, or I may start crying...

title: Absoulutly AMAZING!!!
review: I thoroughly enjoyed this film! Being a huge star war fan, i knew the backround to each of the events. This movie has got to be one of the best! It is linking in with the original trilogy, by the ship design and plans to the origonal death star. This was a great movie and deserves 10/10!!

title: Yoda is the man
review: Downright awesome.  Here's 5 words why this movie is so fantastic:  Yoda, Yoda, Yoda, Yoda, and Yoda.  Here's some more: Mace Windu, storm troopers, Yoda, Anakin flirting with the dark side, Yoda, battle scenes, and Yoda. Lucas has definitely gotten his sea legs back.  Some people have criticized the dialog, and the slow pace of the first half but it really plays into the whole calm before the storm thing going on in this installment.  And by the way, Yoda kicks ass.  Go see it, I'm going again.

title: Enormous, awe inspiring.
review: It seems to drag at the start as the story develops but then you see why. A huge crescendo builds; the enormity is astounding.  I sense definite anime influences that have maybe been lacking from Phantom Menace and the other Episodes.  Very complicated, fast moving, a lot to get into two hours.

title: its true- this is the phantom menace's empire strikes back.
review:
if a bit overloaded with cgi at times the digital orgy eventually gives way to a compelling plot and subplot. this time it is more like we are watching dominoes collapse than a stale chess match. yoda. the fetts. anakin minus the night cries. natalie porter. 3rd kind cloning encounters. gladiator. braveheart. lucas must be brimming. all in all a great movie.

ps. i thought spiderman sucked. really.

title: It's GREAT that STAR WARS is coming back in a more "HARD WAY" ...
review:
In my opinion the best part so far was EMPIRE STRIKES BACK - EPISODE 6 . Why - because it simply does not include many "pathetic" passages as for example EPISODE 1 . I think EPISODE 1 was made for younger audience - their buying power & influence is so big we can't even imagine . That is why LUCAS played the first STARWARS NEWCOMER to be the 100% cash success - NOW he can be harder . Episode two included few scenes I would like to see made differently , but It was not so distracting as JAJAR BINGS style in EP.1 .

I want to see this movie again - YODA is really showing for the first time how good fighter he is - I think that is the best scene of this movie - you have to laugh inside your head for a few moments but than you really can see he's the biggest Jedi . The love story is not disturbing and you can see why ANAKIN is approaching the dark side - He was under pressure just he was born and it is only intensifying . His mother , Padme , death of Qui Gon , other Jedi knights > all is leading to be the reason - we can just guess what will be the last to cause his change ... I am looking forward to NEXT SW movies & hope George will continue in this style of story telling .

title: Totally awesome
review: I just got done seeing the second installment of the greatest 5 movies the planet has ever seen and this installment secures that status even more. the movie is a bit long but is more than made up for with a good story and great special effects.  The action depicted buy the Jedi Masters and their apprentices, i.e. Anakin Skywalker, are spectacular.  Yoda kicks major a!@ against Count Dooku!!!  Mace Windu show what the force can do in dire circumstances and theri are plenty of great Jedi to try to save the galaxy from the Dark Side.  Definitely a must see!!! I plan on going again to take in everything that the long movie has to include in this awesome series. Thank you George Lucas!!!!

title: The most fun I've had at a movie in years!
review: I remember the first time I saw "Star Wars" - I was 11 years old and living in small-town Iowa. The moment the closing credits music ended and the lights came up, I knew my life would never be the same. Now I'm 36 and a jaded New Yorker, but for two and a half hours early Thursday morning, I was a kid again - thrilled to be discovering a new visual vocabulary courtesy of George Lucas, and amazed to be able to just have FUN at a movie! Say what you will about some of the dialog or a few line readings, it doesn't matter. This is "Star Wars," in all its glory - action, laughs, jaw-dropping effects, and lots of good old-fashioned cheese. I wouldn't have it any other way.

title: Incredible digital effects
review: I hoped this episode would be better than first, for I consider the Trilogy the best thing in cinema ever made. Well, it was, but just for digital effects (if its possible). Really incredible, but dialogues were very boring. Terrible the falling-in-love-scenes between Anaquin and Padme, worst than a soap opera dialog. Finally, it was great seeing Yoda fighting with his sword! At the end I consider myself satisfied.

title: The Force Will Be With Us...ALWAYS!
review: When I first say the trailer for Star Wars Episode II, I said to myself "I can't believe this will be a Funny Girl meets Independence Day". Although I loved each of these films I hated the idea of turning Star Wars into a romance with a little bit of action. But this trailer is by far one of the bests I've ever seen. It shows nothing on it. It doesn't let us know what the movie is about, it doesn't let us know anything about the characters...anything. Not like the trailer of AMERICAN PIE II where you can see the whole movie in 1minute and 35 seconds. With this I mean that the movie was a total surprise for me. Not only i loved it but it was also very emotional for me...watching Amidala hugging Anakin...and the music swells, and...I think this movie was made with "The" Star Wars magic, unlike EPISODE I, which was quite boring and quite intensive...4 wars at the same time...give the Force a break. With Episode II, Star Wars rise again, with great classic touches from the original episodes, to great new adventures and a great script in my opinion. I can't deny however how sad it was, for me at least. I think the best performance on the movie is Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, played by Ian McDiarmid. What I liked the most about the film is the scenes, moments, places and language that made me remind of the old movies. It was the greatest Dejá vu moment i have ever had in the silver screen. It was indeed an amazing movie. Now I know, the force will be with us...ALWAYS!

title: The force is strong with this one!
review: To say Star Wars The Phantom Menace was a box Office smash hit would be an understatement, but to say it left only a few Star Wars fans disappointed would be a understatement as well. the Phantom menace was heavily criticised for the Disneyesque Story style and wooden characters (the less said about the annoying Jar Jar binks the better) and with movies like the Lord of the Rings and the Matrix challenging Star Wars for the title of Movie epic it seemed like the Star Wars franchise was under threat for a moment. Thankfully Star Wars: The Attack of the Clones shows George Lucas hasn¹t lost his touch,  the movie is a special effects feast, beyond anything we seen recently, mixed with plenty of battle sequences and a love story on the side. For all you non Jedi fans, a quick re cap. Episode two of the Star Wars series deals with the gradual transformation of young Anakin Skywalker, to the Dark Side of the mystical Force and turning to the evil Darth Vader. Episode two starts ten years after the The Phantom Menace,  the old Galactic Republic is going through a time of political turmoil with the danger of a civil war looming. The defenders of the old order the Jedi Knights are increasingly over stretched and opposition in the Senate (led  by Senator Amidala played by Natalie Portman) has blocked plans to make a grand Army to crush the separatists led by Count Dooku (played by Christopher Lee a Desi connection here, he played Quaid e Azam in the Movie Jinnah!). The political backdrop, with the gradual decay of the old order, the contempt for politicians, and the intent of the ruler to gradually increase his power, through emergency powers is something we often see happening in the World. Ewan Mgregor reprises his role as Obi Won Kenobi with the usual stoicism and the growing rift between him and his apprentice Anakin Skywalker played by Hayden Christenson. Hayden comes of well as an increasingly angry and bitter Anakin who has little time for the patient approach of the Jedi order. Samuel Jackson returns as Jedi Knight Mace Windau, happily in a bigger role than last time, watch out for his spectacular show down with Bounty hunter Jango Fett. Another high point is the light sabre duel between Count Dooku and Yoda. I do have a few complaints, unlike the original trilogy, there is little chemistry between the characters, Anakin and Amidala and the whole love story seems a bit contrived. Another problem is the sheer number of sub plots, it tends to distract from the characters. Despite the criticism, this is a good family movie and sets a build up for (what should be a dark) finale.

title: Better than Episode I, but still lacks that old SW magic
review: The original Star Wars trilogy had a certain magical quality to it, something that you can't quite put your finger on, but it's there. If this film is any indication of what is to come, then it can be safely said that George Lucas has lost his magic touch.   Episode II, without question, is an incredibly exciting movie to watch and, if you don't employ any critique, is a most enjoyable film. But if you do choose to employ your skills as a critic, and if you can get past the incredible special effects, you see what is essentially an average movie with very bland dialogue and monotonous acting. As a dedicated Star Wars fan, I was disappointed by this latest attempt at reviving the phenomenon. On the credit side, this film makes wonderful use of computer animation and special effects. And I must admit that I got goosebumps when Yoda pulled out that tiny lightsaber and very nearly kicked the bad guy's ass. One of the coolest movie scenes I have ever seen. 2.5 out of 5

title: Best of Star Wars
review: Though it is basically a love story, it still has all the essentials of a Star Wars movie, as well as Anakin slowly turning to the Dark Side and many other things. It is another Star Wars masterpiece, with great visual effects and acting. Though it did halve Jar-Jar in it, it is only brief but important, believe-it-or-not. The clones look like excactly like what a proto type of a Stormtrooper would. As well as the introduction to Boba Fett. The sabre-battles are excelent and the drama is top notch. Hope the 3rd one tops all the others.

title: Random Thoughts On A Barely Above Average Flick
review:
I had the rare pleasure of seeing this on a "double-bill" -- we took our 10-year-old to see it, then got lunch, then caught the early evening showing of Spider-Man. Some random observations:

-- Man, that first hour stinks.

-- As Anakin drops out of the car in the middle of the chase through Coruscant, my husband and I simultaneously said, "Who does he think he is--Peter Parker?" It would not be the first mental comparison I would make to SM as the film went along.

-- Ewan McGregor is clearly channelling Alec Guinness. This is not a bad thing.

-- Obi-Wan vs. Jango Fett on Kamino--great fight, but again the comparison to SM jumped out as OW is dangling by a line and JF is trying not to slide off the runway. ("Now Obi-Wan's channelling Peter!" my husband laughed.)

-- What the blank is wrong with the Jedis that they cannot figure out what's going on with Palpatine? Is he really that powerful or does the plot just make Jedis that stupid?

-- Anakin should have been drummed out of Jedi training a long time ago.

-- Hayden Christensen cannot act. For an example of how teen angst and unrequited love and coping with remarkable powers should be played, watch Tobey Maguire's performance in SM again and again as needed.

-- If I'm Amidala, I'm running as fast as I can from Anakin because he is clearly a paranoid obsessive/compulsive schizophrenic.

-- There isn't a believable moment in the Anakin/Amidala romance. Not one.

-- I liked meeting the Lars family on Tattooine.

-- That last hour of the film, including the battle royal, makes up for a multitude of sins. Finally, everyone's agenda begins to unfold. Finally, we get to see Jedis be Jedis. Finally, we get to see why Yoda is the master that he is. I would go see this movie again just to see that last hour.

-- But I'd probably skip the entire 1:20 proceeding it, because man, could this movie have used a good, tight editing.

-- Shockingly, the AotC showing I went to wasn't sold out. But almost every single SM showing of the day was, including the one we managed to snag the last tickets for (they put up the "Sold out" sign just as I was leaving the ticket booth). If I'm 20th Century Fox, I'm worried. If I'm Sony, I'm doing backflips.

I'd rate it above average, but just barely -- 6.5 on a scale of 1 to 10.

title: Best of the current trilogy so far!
review:
I have been a Star Wars fan since age 12 (1992), and even though I was one of the few who enjoyed Phantom Menace (except for Jar-Jar Binks, who disappointly shows up here once again), Attack of the Clones, while flawed, is much better. Non-stop action, plus a few things we've never seen in a Star Wars movie before, for example, Jedi council members Mace Windu and Yoda going to help out Obi-Wan Kenobi and getting involved with the Clone Wars. I've never been much of a stickler for the dialogue George Lucas writes, which admittedly is not that great, but what he lacks in prose, he makes up for in visualization. I mean, Yoda has a lightsaber battle in this picture for Heaven's sake! That's so original. The cute little fellow sees more action here than he has in the entire series so far!

Only real problems I have with this picture are:

1. Hayden Christensen as Anakin, who seems like he's acting in

the film just because he'll get noticed and not because of what

he can contribute, which isn't a whole hell of a lot. 2. Jar-Jar Binks returns. Admittedly, it's good that if he has to be around, his appearance is kept short and sweet, but Meesa hopes Yousa Star Wars writers write in the next picture that he was lost in the Tatooine or something.

title: Cloning Fun
review:
I'm not sure what all the negative fuss is about. It's no Casablanca but who expects it to be? Some have obviously tumbled into the wrong cinema.

I think most of us love Star Wars for what it really is: a rip-roaring romp with plenty of great special effects. Why pretend otherwise?

Brickbats:

Wooden acting by Natalie Portman

Stilted dialogue (please get Lawrence Kasdan back!)

Bouquets:

Superb performances from Ewan MacGregor, Christopher Lee & Ian McDiarmid

Yoda (highlight)

More believable chemistry between Armidala and Anakin

Fantastic light sabre sequences (more please)

Scrumptious sets

All in all a lot of fun.

title: Way To Go George!
review: When first walking into the theatre to see Star Wars Episode II I will admit I was very skeptical, I usually only like to see movies like this for the hype, but my skeptiscism (sp??) went away quickly.  The movie--though not as good as the original--was very entertaining and fun to watch.  Much much more better than Epsiode I, Episode II lived up to the original Star Wars more than E1 did.  Kudos to George Lucas for bringing us such a good movie.

title: This is one of the best Star Wars
review:
OK, Empire Strikes Back is still #1 for me. But this one is close; definitely better, in my book, than EP1 and Return of the Jedi. And I can't wait to see how EPIII (possibly the darkest of all six -- we know what must happen -- and who's going to die -- before Episode IV begins) unfolds.

The first time I saw it, I was really tired and so some of the scenes in the middle part (exposition) dragged a little, but it was still engrossing enough to keep me interested. And by the time the final battles started, it was a thrill ride all the way.

At first I was laughing with the rest of the theater audience at the corny dialogue (especially those between Anakin and Padme). But then I realized that's what Star Wars is all about. It's not NYPD Blue. This is a comic book, Sci-fi fantasy. If you have ever read a comic book, you will know that the dialogue actually fit very well. On my second viewing, they actually worked very well for me. The love story arc actually worked for the purpose. It's important to move it along, so we know that they fall madly in love (and that leads to Luke and Leia).

But we all know why we are there in the first place. It's the fantasy, the action, the mythology, the lightsabers, the Force, the machineries, the technologies, the scenery... and I believe EPII delivers. The final 40 minutes is exhilirating. I have to go back a second time to truly appreciate everything that is put on the screen (you're bound to miss a lot of details if you only see it once). The arena scenes are amazing -- a fine tribute to the original trilogy and the great Ray Harryhausen movies.

If George Lucas keeps this up, EPIII is going to kick ass.

title: Well Worth the Wait!
review:
A++ A perfect 4 stars!

For years fans have debated which Star Wars film is the best of them all. At last we have a champion. George Lucas has answered the fans call and delivered a film with a perfect blend of action and romance, dazzling special effects and a script that flows beautifully.

To anyone who walks away from this movie disappointed I must ask, what were you expecting? I was expecting the greatest Star Wars ever and this film surpassed my expectations.

I must admit I was a little surprised at how violent the film was. I have no objection to it however. I'm all for intense action sequences. It does not reach outrageous levels but it is definitely more intense than it's predecessors.

MINOR SPOILER: I don't want to reveal too much but let's just say there's a lot of lightsaber chopping and only a fraction of it is to battle droids. END SPOILER.

Whether or not you liked Phantom Menace (I loved it 4 stars!) Episode II blows it away. The title Attack Of The Clones is lousy, but the movie more than makes up for that!

Oh and the long awaited Yoda lightsaber scene: jaw droppingly excellent!

Running Time: Aprox. 142 minutes MPAA rating: PG for intense SCI-FI action violence and some minor language and sensuality

title: much better than ep 1
review:
well still no classic starwars movie, but much better than ep 1. characters looked nice (almost all of em aged well) and special effects were cool.

the first half of the film is boring, but in the end you are just stunned.

and, most important in my opinion is: the scene where yoda fights with a lightsaber :)

8/10

People throw around the term "Jaw Dropping" a lot, but by the time I walked out of that theater, my jaw was SORE. It was everything i could do to not make little squeals of joy during the more amazing points.

11/10

title: where's the heart?
review: I am an avowed fan of the original Star Wars trilogy. I watched them a thousand times, I bought the merchandise, I loved the characters. I don't understand why the two movies of the new trilogy have not affected me as much. They had too much of the techno stuff, and not enough heart.
