title: Jedi's and Politicians... ARE YOU READY TO RUMBLE?!?!!!!
review:
OH BABY! BABY! BABY!! I just got back from this 2 hour + movies and I've never been this hyped after a Star Wars film- EVER. I LOVE Return of the Jedi- now AotC has knocked RotJ down to my #2 favorite Star Wars film. Actings' great. Plot is outstanding. The graphics are far beyond your imagination. And the fighting...ooooooooh the fighting will leave you're heart craving more of the endless action!

The story line is SO MUCH MORE in depth then I think anyone could predict before seeing this movie. I am a HUGE Star Wars fan, and of course I wondered if Lucas could pull off another great SW film- and he has.

*************!!!!POSSIBLE SPOILER HERE!!! TAKE CAUTION!!**************** ! ! ! ! R E A D A T O W N R I S K ! ! ! !



The love between Padme` and Anakin really keeps your heart pounding. I'll admit, I cheated and read the VERY LAST sentence of the book( and not the rest of it. Just the last sentence) before seeing the movie. I knew everything *should* be okay at the end, but throughout the movie, it still kept me watching...and watching...and watching...wondering....

And believe me...if you've heard people already raving about Yoda's sweet battle- it's so much more than that. HE KICKS THE DONKEY'S TAIL RIGHT IN!!!!!!!!! YODA ROCKS!!!!! You have to see it to believe it.

Attack of the Clones might sound like a stupid title at first- but it really does live up to it's name in the movie.

If there's anything bad with this film- it's that it's the second to

last Star Wars film- THE AGONY OF IT ALL!!!!!

Favorite part: When Yoda rules the screen- And when all the Jedi's fought against the droids towards the end...and...heck I loved the whole film.

title: Has the Force abandoned Lucas?
review:
As a Gen-Xer, I was one of many to grow up on the Star Wars franchise. We had and actually used the lunchboxes. Wiffle bats were our lightsabers. We saw a few neighborhood girls with slightly twisted parents even try that Princess Leia spiral-pigtail-in-stereo thing on their daughters, and at the time we thought it was actually cool.

We lived through the Dark Times...the sixteen long years the Great and Terrible Emperor of Skywalker Ranch forced us to wonder why he gave us only Episodes 4 through 7. Was it a cruel trick? Was it a typo? ILM run amok? Or was there a method to the seeming madness?

After all he gave us clue after clue about what might have filled those first three episodes, didn't he? Sir Alec lamenting those "damn fool idealistic crusades" he and Luke's father (oh yes, we learned all about that twisted little family tree) went on. The existence of a Republic and the dreaded Clone Wars. Sir Alec's mistaken belief he could train Anakin "just as well as Yoda." And, of course, the fact that "I was wrong."

We were captivated by the frequent but incredibly brief exchanges of emotional innuendo between Han, Leia, and Luke which hinted at romance but never quite bogged us down with it. We revered a broken-down, 900 year old Jedi master and even spoke like him on occasion (usually after one too many libations).

We rooted for and against one of the greatest villains of all time...the "Star Wars" Vader. Of course, his stripes changed as the Episodes spun by, but we changed with him. We wanted redemption for a man whom we thought may have taken the quicker and more seductive path, only to learn that life constantly changes what we believe is easiest.

The Trilogy became part of our culture, part of our national identity. You may not like it, but you must admit it. No doubt each of us, whether you read this with a bobble head Yoda staring back at you from the top of your monitor or on a 5 minute respite from the office workday, planned out the history of the Republic. You created your own Episodes 1 - 3. You knew what would happen...you just wanted to see it. You yearned for the Great and Terrible One to bring those dreams to life...to compare notes.

And then, after those Dark Times, He granted our wish. Sort of. He gave us the Phantom Menace. He gave us Jar Jar Binks. He gave but took back Darth Maul. A fantastic marketing piece for the economic Empire. But for us, the faithful, those that created the franchise in the first place, we were handed a would-be Disney CGI event ripoff. That wasn't Episode I. It was an infomercial for "PodRacer the Game" and "Tickle-Me-Anakin."

OK, we thought. He's rusty. We'll cut him some slack. A cinematic mulligan. After all, Episode II has to be dark. It has to be better. "Empire" was. After all, they carbonized Han, hacked off Luke's hand, and wrapped it up with the nastiest family reunion this side of Springer. Episode II...he'll be back in game shape by then. A cuddly Vader? A sympathetic Emperor? An 800 year old, broken down Jedi master? Nah...something's gotta give.

But Lucas knows something about us we may be hesitant to admit. No matter what he gives us...we have to see it. HAVE to. Just like Rosemary's baby, we can't pull our eyes away. In the process, accountability vanishes. Lucas has become the Emperor. He does what he wants. Good for him. Bad for us...

I slipped in to an 8 pm showing on opening day. The 2/3 full theater (Spidey was sold out at 8pm on opening day...I was there for that, too, mind you) erupted into applause when the lights went down and the familiar and soothing rumble of brass and percussion that is John Williams finest work enveloped us in THX (a Lucasfilm trademark) sound.

Then it got quiet. Real quiet. For about and hour and a half. Well, some of those retching sounds during Lucasfilmean romance scenes did break up that monotony. Of course, Flying Yoda the Wild West SaberSlinger brought the house down. Bigtime. It did salvage the film. I suppose you can see when I'm going with this.

In short, this is not Star Wars. We were cheated. Casting was fine. Action sequences were better than average. The CGI mishmash was entertaining when you could follow it. The climax was worth 6 of the eight bucks I spent. Flying Yoda was worth the whole 8.

However, the writing was atrocious. And who spliced in 30 minutes of Intergalactic Days of Our Lives? A fireside love confession? A romp in the fields? I seriously expected Natalie Portman to start belting out "The Hills Are Alive..." Had we been spared that travesty, and instead given a 5 minute dramatic flashback near the end of the film (say, when they were about to be fed to those critters by Christopher Lee) would have gotten the job done and spared us the agony. After all, the fact that Anakin and Amidala produce Luke and Leia isn't exactly news. Efficiently accomplish it and move on.

I understand the impetus behind the attempt, but the execution was deplorable. Overall, the movie gets a 6...and 8 if they grant us the power to delete the soap scenes from the DVD.

But there is a bigger problem here. The inconsistencies between where we are and where we have to go will make Episode III a miniseries in length or require us to forget Episodes 4 through 7. And wasn't it the point of 1 through 3 to get us there?

Lucas missed an excellent opportunity to tell a new story. Create new characters. Fill in the history of the Republic. Anakin should not have even shown up until Episode II and he should have been a bit player there. There is no way Lucas can turn him into the Episode 4 Vader in the next film. The misunderstood man-child becomes the ruthless right hand of the Emperor after pouting his way through a forbidden love? He's spent too much time making him the sympathetic pawn of tired Jedi and Sith lords who simply haven't gotten enough play. Poor Anni...I feel my popcorn resurfacing...

Why? In his quest to stay in the marketable PG rating, he's abandoned all inter-character strife, all sarcasm and wit, all surprise, and anything else that might not be immediately picked up by an X-Box obsessed 7 year-old with ADHD. If all we can expect is eye candy, leave General Hospital on ABC and let Yoda and Tyranus get it on. Let Vader be Vader. Give us what we want.

Of course, like the addicted suckers we are, we'll be back for Episode III, if for no other reason that to see if the Great and Terrible one can descend from Skywalker Ranch and finally deliver the goods. But we won't be buying that lunchbox for our kids. No Amidala bare-midriff conveniently torn shirts for our 8 year old girls. No fantasies about Episodes 7 through 9. We'll take our medicine and go home. What a waste.

May the Force come back to him. Please.

title: I should have waited to see Star Wars II on DVD
review: Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones was pretty much what I expected.  I wasn't really looking forward to going to this one since I had been disappointed by the "re-makes" of episodes IV, V, and VI.  (So-called improvements to IV, V, and VI failed to eliminate artifacts and visual flaws in scenes with star patterns for example.  In those re-makes I had expected technical adaptations, not character additions).  But with Episode II - Attack of the Clones, I could not detect such imperfections (short of the tape change markers).  In my opinion, the continuity to the story could have been better; there seemed to be some jumping around from one set of characters to another.  The fact that the story takes place before episode VI limits the parameters to the extent that there was little room for expanding the story itself.  In my opinion, the movies should have begun from episode I instead of episode VI.  In any case, I managed to sit through much of the movie with some level of patience.  About the last 20 minutes contained most of the action which was (in my opinion) somewhat predictable. I emphasize somewhat.  Perhaps I would have enjoyed Attack of the Clones if I were 16 again, but I would have preferred to see it on DVD & on my 70" TV. When the movie was over, there was NO APPLAUSE. This is the first time that I have been to a Star Wars Movie when this did not occur.  The small crown could have had something to do with it...maybe.

title: Great flick!
review: Much better than Episode I.  I enjoyed the whole movie with the exception of Hayden Christensen.  His performance seemed forced and very much over the top.  He must be an alumni of the William Shatner school of acting.  The best part of the film has to be Yoda kicking some serious butt.

title: Enjoyable, but over-compensating perhaps?
review:
Minor spoilers contained within...

I would like to start by saying that I watch movies to be entertained, to be whisked away to another time and place. I do not dwell much on the acting, or the direction etc unless these are poor enough to get in the way of my enjoyment.

I enjoyed watching "Attack of the Clones", mostly.

I have no real problems with the acting and dialogue. The action was fast paced, the fight scenes impressive, but after a while I began to tire of the continual barrage of visual effects.

The galaxy it seems is a place of absolute diversity. Each planet is an amazing vista with weird and wonderful aliens. This in itself is not a bad thing, but I felt that there were no normal or everyday places, no average people going about their average lives, to keep the events and actions of the main characters in perspective.

It seems to me that George Lucas has over-compensated for the poor showing of "The Phantom Menace". The effects are continuously thrust at us, each one more fantastical then its predecessor. One example of this, during the big climactic battle, one side has these big two-wheeled missile launchers that look very impressive but don't make a lot of sense as a weapon (to me at least). Can't missiles be launched from a solid platform out of harms way to similar effect?

Finally I guess I am a little disappointed that the story doesn't seem to have got much nearer the already known conclusion. Darth Vader to me was a character of considerable power and evil, but most of all a character in total control. Annakin on the otherhand, seems to be an impetuous, spoilt brat with obvious ability but minimal self-discipline. So am I to believe that the dark-side will teach him this? Hmmm...

As for the two sides of the battles just begun, I am none the wiser as to which side is which. If everything is to be revealed in Episode 3 (as it seems it will be) then what is the point of Episode 2???

title: good, not great, just good.
review:
In the old Star Wars movies the characters had personality. Princess Leah was a bitch-on-ice, and it was great watching her interact with a sarcastic Han Solo or a naïve Luke Skywalker. Darth Vader was a nasty, evil villain and everybody wanted to be like him. Come on, admit it, he stole the show. And for the most part, the special effects were used only to help tell a clever, witty, almost inspirational, over-the-top story.

In the new films the characters are just bland shadows of the originals. They say whatever clichéd lines and dialog Lucas wrote for them. There are occasional moments of emotion and feeling, but more often the computer-animated characters are more full of life than the real humans. (Hey George, if you're going to go through all the trouble of making up a character from scratch, next time try not to make him irritating.) And worst of all, the special effects seem to take priority over the story. It's like the plot is used as an excuse to throw in more shiny-flashy-noisies. And where's the villain?

George Lucas is a very talented man, only a fool would say otherwise. But I think his strengths lean more towards the producing end. In my humble opinion he's not that great at directing or writing, at least not anymore.

title: Lucas has done it again!
review:
All us Star wars fans were all a little disappointed with "The Phantom Menace", but George Lucas has cast off all of the bad memories of his last flick with "Attack of the Clones"

While "Attack of the Clones" may not be perfect, it's not that far off. It's got everything a Star Wars flick needs to succeed, and a few new tricks thrown in for extra effect. While the Anakin/Amidala relationship is a little cliché and lame (very Titanic-like), everything else blows you away.

The storyline may not be Oscar material, but is still good by most sci-fi standards. What really makes this film great though are the action sequences. When you see 100 Jedi knights charging into battle with their lightsabers, you'll see what I mean, especially considering they are up against thousands of droids. Yoda's lightsaber battle (very Matrix-y) and Anakin's double lightsaber duel is terrific. In addition, no Star Wars movie has ever tried to do a large-scale ground assault, this one making "The Empire Strikes Back" look like a day at the beach.

The acting is surprisingly good for a Star wars movie. Jar-Jar is only slightly less annoying, but performances from Samuel L. Jackson, Christopher Lee and Ewan MacGregor cancel all that out. Jimmy Smits is only a minor character, but makes an impact, as does Temuera Morrison's Jango Fett.

A few new alien species and old faces from "The Phantom Menace" add to the film's greatness, as do shots of future Star Wars characters (errrrr......Uncle Owen, Aunt Beru). As with every Star Wars flick, there is at least one great chase/race scene, this one not letting you down. Anakin's stroll down the Dark Side also begins with among other things slaughtering a campful of Tusken Raiders (by himself).

Along with a few hint-dropping joke lines, and a few Star Wars classics slipped into the movie, it's just a great movie. Whatever George Lucas did wrong with "The Phantom Menace" he fixed in "Attack of the Clones", and based on what I saw, he did a pretty good job too. It's got everything a good Star Wars movie needs: action, lightsabers, a few corny lines, one great battle, a good villain, and Yoda. Granted it gets a little lame with the love story thing, but is still a great flick.

title: "Judge me by my size, do you?"
review:
In May of 1983 I was 13 years old when I went to the movies and saw "Return of the Jedi." Months before after hearing that it would be arriving soon my friends and I had lengthy discussions on possible plot points and certain things that we wanted to see. Two things we all agreed that we wanted was action scenes with Boba Fett and a lightsaber duel featuring Yoda. We never expected the duel with Yoda. That was a dreamers dream, but we did expect Boba Fett. When neither of these things came to light in the film I must say I was disappointed. However, I did not turn my back on the saga. I still loved the movie and didn't harp on the disappointments. I merely packed my dreams in the vault of my mind and moved on.

On May 16, 2002 that vault was opened with the release of `Attack of the Clones.' Both of my friends' dreams and mine came true. Jango Fett who is Boba Fett (or Boba Fett who is Jango Fett - see the movie and you will understand) provided action and a face to this mysterious person who has captured all of our imaginations. Most important of all Yoda drew his lightsaber and showed us why he is the best of the best. These two things alone were enough to make me love this movie, but then there was more. So much more. Plot connections to the other movies, romance, action and characters that made me reconnect to a universe that I loved and cherished as a boy.

I would recommend this movie to anyone who went to see all of the Episodes the same way that I did. With the eyes and the heart of a child. I feel that if you are there for the special effects you will not be disappointed, but you will miss out on the magic. The magic of imagination and wonder. The magic that is Star Wars.

title: Critics be darned, it's wonderful entertainment
review:
First let me say I'm one of the faithful that hopes for the best from Mr. Lucas and Co. And I also live in Marin county, and naturally pull for 'local boy makes good', and was a bit taken aback by the utter evisceration that AOTC has received from some critics. It made me wonder whether or not some critics are simply angry that Mr. Lucas is not ground-breaking and insightful as they _try_ to be in their reviews. It's almost like they're upset that they have to work so hard putting out clever reviews while George is resting on his laurels.

It's hard to always be groundbreaking and/or clever. The Beatles were almost always groundbreaking but how long did they last? And what has Quentin Tarantino done for you since Pulp Fiction? I do agree with the critique that George doesn't have to stretch his muscles with AOTC, he already has a huge audience base that is favorable for any Star Wars movie that is more than utter trash. Yet it seems playing to an audience is another thing that upsets critics.

And Star Wars doesn't have to be independent filmy sophisticated, it tells a basic story of good and evil where the lines are well drawn on what side each character is on, and the bad guys get their butts kicked (eventually) by the hero. All in a galaxy far, far away.

Original Stars Wars was ground-breaking in that it told the good vs evil in an almost transcendant way, in a context that was unique and clever, filled with esoteric and mystical undertones and background. Some have said that the original was based loosely on the Mahabarata, one of the Bibles of Hinduism. In keeping to simplicity, all the films are the fantasy of teenage boys, who want to kick some ass and impressed the chicks, teenage boys from 7 to 70. I also forgive George for the "Moichendising, moichendising" that Mel Brooks exclaims in SpaceBalls.

And there's some underlying arrogance that we're more sophisticated than the childishly simple plot of good vs. evil. But when push comes to shove, say when certain terrorists fly airplanes into buildings, were we not, at some points, filled with rage and a desire for vengeance? To the degree that sense of vengeance filled you, is the level at which you were taken by the Dark Side of the Force.

But as in the title, critics be darned, this is great entertainment. The reviews of the pro critics lowered the bar for me, but to my surprise, I thoroughly enjoyed the movie. The plot was not too simple, yet not confusing (remember the first Mission Impossible?), and the movie was of two basic parts, about half for setup and half for climax and resolution. So here are my turn on and turn offs for the movie

*** SPOILERS ***

Turn ons:

  • I thought Hayden Christiansen was excellent in mixing a believably human character with bright talents and dark faults. You can see by his character how the emperor will turn him in the next movie


  • The special effects were varied and seemingly always fresh. I looked forward to each scene portraying another fantasy use of technology.


  • Christopher Lee as Dooku. It's great to see Sauron again, zapping stuff from his finger tips!


  • The tension between Annikan and Padme. Fun watching their love and desire for each other come to life. Lots of gentle kissing.


  • Very little Jar-Jar Binks. Nuff said.


  • Natalie Portman talking normal and getting her clothes ripped just so to show off her belly button.


  • Great to see a slew of Jedi Knights, male and female, duking it out together.


  • Yoda! Yoda! Yoda! Taking care of business and kicking butt! Oh yeah!


Turn-offs:

-There were a lot of re-use and borrowing from other movies in contexts and special effects: the Fifth Element in the city scenes, the Rocketeer in the smuggler, "The Grays" of Whitley Shreiber on the water planet, Gladiator, Lord of the Rings and the Matrix efx in the coliseum creatures, the underground creature factories from Lord of the Rings

-All planets have the perfect atmosphere for humans. There are no gas planets in the universe. Everyone speaks English in the universe.

-The movie is about 15 minutes too long.

-Jimmy Smits? If Sipowicz showed up too, they'd take care of that evil emperor, no doubt.

-Samuel L. Jackson. That character was much too sedate for Samuel.

-The flat panel text setup at the beginning of the movie. It's almost cliche by now. Try something new George!

Basically, my inner teenager loved the movie, I think yours will too.

title: George, all is forgiven (warning: spoilers!)
review:
All is forgiven, George. You have redeemed yourself utterly.

From the opening sequence (which is both beautiful and shocking) Attack of the Clones is pure, perfect, vibrant Star Wars. The film provides the nervous fans with an all-too-tantalising glimpse of how richly detailed the Star Wars universe is, while developing the story and characters a hundred-fold over the pallid Phantom Menace.

Obi-wan and Anakin are perfect as the bickering but affectionate master & apprentice, and even through Obi-wan's curt orders and Anakin's frustrated outbursts the bond between them is clear. Padme Amidala is also excellent, and a whole new depth is added to her character. One sees the clear link between herself and her headstrong and beautiful daughter Leia.

The other characters are also excellent. Yoda & Windu add enormous depth to the Jedi order; Chancellor Palpatine is at his brilliantly evil best; and the wonderful and charismatic Christopher Lee gets into his role as Count Dooku with the same obvious relish as that of Saruman in Lord of the Rings.

For the casual movie-going fan, I cannot stress enough the depth that this movie brings to the Star Wars universe. It's like you have a half completed jigsaw puzzle that the final pieces don't exist for, and suddenly most of the gap is filled in. and the almost completed picture that takes shape is infinitely more richly detailed and beautiful than you had ever imagined.

There are several eerie echoes of the future in this film. One of my favourite scenes from the original trilogy was early in ANH, when Luke stood outside the settlement and looked to the horizon, a young man contemplating his future and the changes that were to come. The music swells and you just know this is one of the deepest moments of the film. When Anakin did the very same thing in AOTC I couldn't help but gape in joyous wonderment. Moments like this make AOTC far, far more than the sum of its parts.

But wonderful scenes abound. The speeder chase and bar sequence is a fantastic Bladerunner-esque glimpse of real life in Coruscant, and in the middle of a deadly pursuit Obi-wan still finds time to use the Jedi mind-trick for good in one of the film's many genuinely funny moments. And of course the final battle of the droids and the Jedi / clone armies is simply eye-popping. with Yoda as the reluctant general called to battle to win a bitter victory that is the lesser of two evils.

But to top it all, who can possibly forget the final sequence, with the insidious Palpatine, doubtful Organa at his side, surveying his vast army as they move to war. to the rising strains of the Imperial March. Bone-chilling stuff.

George, well done. You've done us proud. As for the reviewers, I haven't read a single one that knows the first thing about the Star Wars universe, so stuff 'em. You'll make a squillion, your fans love you again, and you've created an instant classic.

Now for the final piece of the puzzle.

title: The best yet of the new trilogy
review:
The new trilogy cannot in any way be compared to the first. This one is synthetic, technically-driven, and far from the innocent simplicity of the first three entries.

When "The Phantom Menace" was released in 1999, a large percentage of the Star Wars devotees fell away, and such was to be expected. The feeling of the film was different--distant, esoteric at times. But this is an entirely new set of films and entirely new sets of objectives. Now that a second entry is in the books, perhaps the animosity toward Lucas and his new creation can go away at last.

"Attack of the Clones" is startling, mystifying, dazzling, provocative, and fun through-and-through. It employs the eye-candy graphics initiated with "The Phantom Menace" and takes them to a whole new atmosphere. Even though the film is 95% computerized, one can still feel a part of the picture, another spectator in the arena. The writing was refreshingly better than that of "The Phantom Menace." Full of quirky exchanges and chilling references of things to come, the script manages to keep the movement of the film fluid while not getting too bogged down in the politics of the story. A finely crafted dialogue and delivery onto a screen filled with enough going on to thrill even the biggest skeptic.

The last half-hour of the film puts the viewer on a conveyor belt, sets the speed to hyperdrive, and throws them straight into the door leading to Episode III. After seeing the film at 12:01 on the morning of 16 May, there was a great deal of material there to sink in. I am quite confidant that this film will appeal on many, many levels and take its place gracefully on the shelf next to "The Phantom Menace." And when all is said and done for this prequel series, movie lovers will have two wonderfully unique trilogies to sink their teeth into, for many years to come I hope.

"Attack of the Clones" gets a 7.5/10

title: When it's bad, it is very bad...
review:
Final Fantasy has proven that the filmmaker can create the most dazzling special effects, and immerse the audience in an intricate virtual world, but it all comes to nought if the filmmaker doesn't draw the characters well and give them something intelligent to say.

There is much to be impressed with in Attack of the Clones. The storyline is quite ambitious and raises some more complex intrigues than the first trilogy. Lucas's politics have matured with age, preaching the virtue of democracy (albeit without much subtlety). It is also interesting to see the evolution between the two trilogies over time.

However, if Lucas is incapable of directing actors then in all fairness he should hand over the reins to someone who can. Christopher Lee excepted, the entire human cast may just as well have been animated. The characters are supremely shallow and the acting wooden. The idiotic wisecracks come along as just the wrong moments, obliterating any tension the film may have stumbled across. The comic duo R2D2 and C3PO are relied upon far too much. Portman seems supremely unsuitable for the role (during the final climax, exactly how did her jumpsuit transform itself into a crop top?)

Furthermore, Lucas, in his desire to take moviemaking from celluloid to digital, appears to have scripted the storyline in binary fashion: 1's being action, 0's being character development (development used broadly). The result is an unevenly paced film that outstays its welcome and only really succeeds in tedium and confirming what we all expected.

Bottom line: when it's good it holds the attention Â– when it's bad it is very bad indeed.

2.5 / 5

title: Sadly it lacks the "feeling" of the old Star Wars trilogy.
review:
I saw "Attack of the Clones" hoping it would be a better movie than "The Phantom Menace" and I would have to say that it is, but that does not automatically make it a good Star Wars movie. "Attack of the Clones" suffers from big problems.

The story is great. We all know what eventually is going to happen to the characters and the plot in this movie makes a good job building a deeper understanding for why things will go that way. Too bad George Lucas is unable to tell it in an interesting way.

The screenplay poorly written. Much of the dialogue in this movie really bad, with some of the romantic lines being a real disaster. The love story never gets believable and it feels like we just have to accept it, without actually believe in it.

The acting performances are often flat though the banal lines doesn't exactly make it easy for the actors to do their job well. Hayden Christensen as Anakin manages really good with the physical acting, facial expressions and so on but has problems delivering the dialogue in a believable way. Natalie Portman as Amidala tries to make the most of her part but Lucas never really gave her a fair chance. Ewan McGregor does make a much better Obi-Was this time around, more relaxed then he ever was in `Phantom Menace'. The attempts at humour in `Attack of the Clones' are in about 90 percent of the time only embarrassing and the way they use R2 and C3PO is completely unforgivable.

The visual effects are at times perfect but just as often flawed. There are still problems with some of the character animation, and some of the blue screen work are way too obvious, especially for a movie of this calibre.

Some might say that the action is the strength of this movie, I disagree. Most of the action is no more than average. There are only two action sequences that I think works. One is the space ship battle between Obi-Wan and Jango Fett, which also show how visual effects can be used right. The other is the light sabre duel against Dooku in the end of the movie. This fight is actually one of real highlights even though it should have been a bit longer. Here we also get to see a new side of Master Yoda and I must admit that I had my doubts about how that would work. It actually turned out to be well handled and not as out of character as one would have thought. The main problem with most of the action is that Lucas never even try to make us care. Instead he just throws a lot of visual effects in our faces. Just the fact that you have a lot of Jedi's waving their light sabres doesn't make it good action. Especially not when the big Jedi battle is flawed by the blue screen effect. It's just so obvious that the actors never really hit anything, you can actually see that they try to act against some piece of tape in a studio environment and that really bothers me.

The music by John Williams works fine but there is just one new theme that sticks, the love theme. Williams is apparently not what he ones was but he makes it work using themes from the previous movies, thankfully.

To sum up my thoughts about `Attack of the Clones' I can say that it is a film that have the potential of being a great chapter of the Star Wars saga. The problem is that Lucas doesn't manage to use this potential. Yes it is a better movie than `Phantom Menace'. Much in the sense that this one lets you sit though it without having to be annoyed by most of what you see on screen but `Attack of the Clones' still doesn't deliver more than a few scenes that really works and that is what makes me sad. I see George Lucas himself as the big problem of the new Star Wars movies. It is so obvious that his talent lies neither in directing nor screenwriting. The only question is why he can't let competent people take care of writing and directing. That is how `Empire Strikes Back' and `Return of the Jedi' where made and those are the movies that made Star Wars to be the incredible adventure that it's supposed to be.

What did work in "Attack of the Clones? + The Story + Some Visual FX + The Music + Yoda

What did not work in "Attack of the Clones? - The Directing - The Dialogue - The Acting - The Humour - Some Visual FX - The Action

title: George needs somebody to tell him "NO!" sometimes

title: A worthy installment of a classic series
review:
"Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones" delivers to many of the fans what they have been asking for: More jedi battles, more development of the mythology, and less Jar-Jar. And Lucas does come through in this film in full bravado. (Warning, this review contains a synopsis for the entire film! All those who wish to not know anything about this should read this after seeing the film!)

The film is about how the recent assassination attempts on Padme Amidala; who is no longer a queen, but a senator, have forced her to seek protection from former Jedi friends Obi Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker. Anakin is still in training as this film unravels, but he seems to have grown more hot-headed and rebellious to the Jedi ways. When an encounter with a bounty hunter sends Obi Wan to seek out the person who is causing these attempts on Amidala's life, Anakin and Padme retreat to Naboo. There, Amidala and Anakin share a conflict of emotions, but we also learn that the reason for Anakin's unease was due to the nightmares he's been having about his mother, who he left in Episode I to become a Jedi.

Meanwhile, Obi Wan has traced an assassin's weapon to the planet Camino (food? crappy cars?) where he learns that a clone army has been built for the Jedi council under the supervision of bounty hunter Jango Fett. As Jango Fett escapes Camino to a planet (which name escapes me), he learns that Sith jedi Count Dooku has been ordering the clone army to be built before he is captured. Upon learning of this, Senator Palpatine decides to take the army as his own legally and use it to protect the galaxy and aid the Jedi in restoring peace to the galaxy.

Troubled by the dreams he's been having, Anakin returns to Tatooine in search of his mother, who he traces back to the (dah-dah-dah-duh) Lars Homestead. Upon his arrival, he learns that his mother was kidnapped by Tuskan Raiders and immediately leaves to search for her. When he finds her, she only sees him for a moment before dying in his arms. With his rage finally reaching a boiling point, Anakin slaughters the entire tribe (in his own words: "Not just men, but women and children, too.") His descent to the dark side has apparently begun.

Anakin and Amidala leave to aid Obi-Wan and what follows after this is sheer excitement with arena battles, jedi duels, and a fantastic war sequence where a pivotal weapon is in the design stage of being constructed.

One things that the Star Wars series is notable for is the wonderful environments that Lucas creates. In Episode II, he expands on his universe, giving the audience a more in depth look at the awe-inspiring planet Coruscant, taking us inside the city's skyways and streets where we only saw the skylines. There is also an interestingly hidden planet called Camino where the planet seems to be mostly experimental facilities overtop a planet full of water. The infamous Lars homestead is even painstakingly recreated to the degree that if this film does not receive a nomination for art direction, the academy clearly does not have their eyes open.

Many will complain about how the film lacks excitement in the beginning before the end, but to me, that only seems true because the end is so grand and exciting that it's easy to overlook the chase through the skyway at Corusant, Obi-Wan's duel with Jango Fett and Slave One on Camino, and the chase through the astroid field that makes for an interesting nod to Empire (I almost expected Obi-Wan to see a crater worm, but thankfully, that hand puppet didn't appear.)

Or many other complaints will be from the dialog in the romance between Amidala and Anikan, which does contain some cheesy lines, but I challenge anyone to find lines in there that aren't as cheesy as those in Moulin Rouge or Titanic. Epic romances are supposed to have a certain amount of cheesiness to them in order to make them succeed. In the end, the chemistry isn't as strong as the aforementioned films, or even Han and Leia's, but it does work.

Though this movie has many flaws, one must remind ourself that the original trilogy is just as flawed, only it's easier to have overlooked them when we were younger than it is now as we've grown up in a more cynical and critical time. In order to enjoy this film, one must "concentrate on the moment," "stretch out with your feelings" and this installment will not disappoint. Remember, Lucas never once tried to be Bergman.

title: George Lucas finds the Force...
review:
George Lucas, after a dreadful attempt with The Phantom Menace, is back in original form with Attack of the Clones. Clones is simply the best of the Star Wars saga since The Empire Strikes Back.

Lucas uses Clones to focus on some of the characters we've grown to love. Obi-Wan is starting to look a lot like Alec Guinness. Amidala is more grown up herself, even rivaling Princess Leia for females who kick some ass. Chancellor Palpatine is even more sinister than in the first one, and you can see just how he plans to take the Republic for himself.

There are two characters that stand out in this movie. Anakin Skywalker is played by the wonderful Hayden Christiansen. He reminded me a lot of Mark Hamill playing Luke Skywalker. Unfortunately, Anakin seems to have the same whiney qualities of his son. However, Christiansen does a wonderful job portraying the emotional schism that Anakin goes through during his journey down the dark path.

Master Yoda, however, is a different story. Though Lucas was required to stray from the puppet, which is replaced by a computer image, Yoda's character gets much more love in this movie. Much like in Empire Strikes Back, Yoda is often the focus of the movie, and he seems to hold it all together. And in his much larger role, he gets to do what every Star Wars fan was curious about. We finally get to find out why he is the Master of all Jedi in his showdown with Count Dooku. Three words - Yoda kicks ass!!

What makes this movie though was the lessened role of the infamous Jar Jar Binks and an incredible fight scene on the planet Geonosis. Two words - Mace Windu. Of course viewers will have to endure some sappy love scenes between Amidala and Anakin, but we had to expect it. Lucas found his directing touch once again. The computer effects don't take too much from the movie. The foreshadowing of future events is astounding in how it prepares us for the climax that will occur in Episode III. The humor and one-liners from almost every character bring us back to the charm of Han Solo and the antics of C-3PO and R2-D2. Star Wars fans all over will not be disappointed, but left in agony knowing a 3 year wait is in store until Episode III.

title: Everyone I Know Loved it. Needless to Say, I hated it.
review:
Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones was a hard movie to stomach for me. Some had dubbed it Lucas' return to form, his return to creating a movie with passion, adventure, and most importantly, a soul. I was looking forward to this. Even though I liked Episode I to a certain extent, it was nothing compared to the epics of storytelling that comprised the original Star Wars Trilogy. When you break it down, The Phantom Menace was nothing but the depiction of a group of people wandering around trying to find some replacement parts for their ship so a bunch of stuff could explode by the movie's third act. Even though it was wholly boring at some parts and seemed directionless, I accepted its flaws because it was Star Wars. I had a hard time doing the same for Clones.

If you want to see the movie from a purely technical standpoint, it's a marvel. The special effects are astonishing and for this reason alone, the movie warrants at least one viewing. The action scenes move quickly and are well directed for the most part, which isn't surprising, because at any given moment 96.5% of the images onscreen are computer generated. It must be easy to direct a movie in front of a blue screen. But I digress, I just found myself disinterested with most of the main plot. The love between Anakin and Padme...it was bizarre...like watching an illogical soap opera. You knew they would fall in love, but weren't sure how. After watching this, I don't think Lucas knows how it happened either. The romance is poor and detracts from other interesting plotlines in the movie. It was irritating to get caught up in the tension of Obi-Wan's discovery midway through the movie, only to have that tension shelved for a bit while the two lovebirds exchange poor dialogue. As I look back on the movie, I realize that I have little clue what it was actually about. Similar to Episode I, you're watching the unfolding of events that aren't interesting. Only this time, they're all computer-generated events shown through the eyes of blank-eyed robot actors. Thrill, as Obi-Wan cannot figure out a riddle that a child easily solves. Gasp, as Padme and Obi-Wan look at things and make allusions to boring events. Chuckle, as C-3PO and R2-D2 are milked for all they are worth, including the worst pun ever conceived in any medium! "Such a drag". I wanted to kill myself.

The movie just isn't interesting for the first two hours. Sure, there are sparce moments of cool action, but otherwise it's just a series of meaningless events. I never got the sense that a story was being told. It felt more like a history class of Jedi lore. While that may excite (and possibly arouse) some people, it felt just as boring as regular history class for me. The problem with these prequels are their lack of neccessity. Whereas the original trilogy was a compelling tale with definite story elements, these new movies seem like mindless backstory. If Obi-Wan had to sit in a library to discover a planet that may or may not have something to do with an assassination attempt on a Queen who is having relationship problems with the future father of Luke Skywalker, then that's great. JUST DON'T MAKE A MOVIE ABOUT IT.

Calling this movie "Attack of the Clones" is meaningless. Relating a title to an event that barely happens in the third act...kinda misleading. I recommend a change of title to "I Was A Teenage Sith Lord." Or even better: "Yoda's Rockin' Jedi-Palooza." It's accurate, and it describes the only segment of the movie worth watching: The last 45 minutes. I suggest seeing Spider-Man, then theatre-hopping to catch the tail end of this flick. You get the fireworks with none of the gummy crud. Seeing Jedi fight an entire army is thrilling. I just wish it had something to do with ANYTHING.

At least Jar Jar's barely in it. Thank God for that.

title: Good parts sadly overshadowed
review:
It's ten years since little Anny started his training as a Jedi, and he and Obi Wan Kenobi have been sent to protect the ex-Queen Padme Amidala from separatist assassins. There are not enough Jedi these days to protect the universe from the separatist threat, so a clone army is being created.

What ensues is a very spectacular, but ridiculous affair. The love story between Anikin, who is ten years older than in Episode One, and Padme Amidala, who for some reason has not aged more than a day, is terribly acted, and unoriginally and blandly written. Many parts are so much like a kung fu movie that you wonder whether Jet Li will turn up to save the day. The special effects were nothing short of superb, but nothing much is new since the last movie.

So much could have been achieved in Episode II, but I was very disappointed in this film. Even bona fide Star Wars fans may be turned off by the bad plot and wooden acting, but Star Wars is Star Wars, and as long as there are people willing to put "Jedi" as their religion on the census form, George Lucas will churn out movies like this.

title: It's Getting Better Folks!
review:
After I had been disappointed by Episode 1, I decided to watch Episode 2 with less expectations and it paid off. I went into the cinema, preparing myself for another kiddie sci-fi comedy and this film delivered. It was largely comical and better than its predecessor in many aspects: digital/special effects were more real, better characterization, more drama, lots of limbs-flying fights and we got to see Jedi Knights in battle, lots of them.

SPOILERS

There were more chemistry between the characters and in this aspect, Lucas seemed to have taken notes that many true fans were largely disappointed with several elements in Episode 1. So scenes involving JJ Binks and Watto were short. In fact Jar Jar was relatively quiet when he did appear. Anakin on the other hand, remained as annoying and arrogant as he ever was. Christensen gave this teenage Anakin an evil edge and throughout the movie, he was more of the local-bar jerk than a promising Jedi knight. He's far from that prophesied Jedi who would bring balance to the Force, whatever that means (won't he fall to the dark side anyway?).

Jimmy Smits made a nice cameo as Senator Bail Organa, Leia's future adopting father. Temuera Morrison made an interesting John Waynesque' Jango Fett, with references to classic Western movies. As you probably know that New Zealanders played all the character of Jango Fett, Boba Fett and Captain Typho, so whenever they appeared on screen, the audience here were laughing and cheering at their opportunity to be in Star Wars, and mostly for their kiwi accent.

C3PO and R2-D2 (the real heroes of the saga) started their dynamic relationship here, with plenty of fun and laughs. Well, what can I say about Natalie Portman, she's as beautiful and intelligent as ever, and Lucas made sure the movie exploited her sexuality further (a titillation for those 12-13 years old hormones). She changed her costumes so many times that it was getting a bit ridiculous though and old Lucas was probably planning to cash in through her many toys later on. The two last costumes she wore were so sexy and exposing her 'assets' that some audience couldn't resist to say: "Oooooh! Aaaaah!" and `Rrrrrrrr.'.

The romance between Amidala and Anakin was the cheesiest scenes in Star Wars saga unfortunately. The Sound of Music' part was the funniest of all. I understand that this movie was the only chance Lucas had to emphasize on their relationship and doomed romance, but he could've done it in a way that their scenes had been sweet not cheesy. The most surprising part of their supposedly romantic escapade was Anakin having a wet dream about Padme, and when he was found out, he lied and said that he dreamt about his mother. What was Lucas thinking?

The dark part of the film had something to do with Anakin, his mother and the Tusken warriors. The revelation of what Anakin did to them had a notorious echo of his falling to the dark side. Other than that, Episode 2 is only darker than Episode 1, simply because there were more shots in night time Coruscant, rainy Kemino and the red-fiery landscape of Genosia.

I always believe that puppet/costumed animation is better than digital, but with Episode 2 Lucas had taken it to a higher level. So all the vehicles, droids, aliens, etc. were more real and especially the Coruscant cityscape (which was a reminiscent of Blade Runner).

In terms of plot, Lucas was running out of idea so he borrowed a lot from The Empire Strikes Back, among other classic movies. So expect to see vehicle-chasing scenes right at the beginning of the movie, Anakin got his right hand chopped-off and went to sleep, and lastly the last scene of Episode 2 was a complete take on Episode 5's own scene.

Christopher Lee was charismatic as the separatist leader and I was amazed at how well he fought with a light sabre (considering his age). His sultry voice and commanding presence was one of the uplifting elements in the film. The best part of the movie, which I believe will be the most memorable scenes from Episode 2, is a fight between Count Dooku and Master Yoda. Simply put, Yoda kicks ass.

There were several plot holes and narration problems that caused the story to develop incongruently, however again, the overall script was better written this time. The background music was also something new and added a different feel to Episode 2, almost Middle-Eastern in tone.

So my conclusion is that Attack of the Clones' is a much better film compared to The Phantom Menace'. It may still not worthy of the Star Wars heritage because it is simply a different movie that raised more questions and mystery than answers to Episode 1's plot holes, but overall it is genuinely entertaining, funny and better made. It's a heart-lifting comedy of galactic proportion.

Still a Star Wars fan, R.

title: Most Entertaining SW flick yet!
review:
This Star Wars film has it all: the battles, the beautiful girl in the tight suit, the fast and furious lightsaber action, and of course the easter eggs (jawas, womp rats, bounty hunters, etc.) Though Episode I may be considered a slight downfall in the series' overall progress, this one makes up for the faults in The Phantom Menace by far.

This film proves that the older Star Wars episodes have definitely met their match in the twenty-first century. Star Wars is, and remains, timeless. My children will be watching this one as soon as all six episodes come out on DVD.

Second only to The Empire Strikes Back, this film is already one of the top SW flicks of all time, as far as I'm concerned.

title: Attack the Theaters!
review:
I can't help but notice some haters here and there. Now, I concede to the fact that no movie will please every person on earth, but to some critics Episode II was already a bomb before they even saw it. One critic even when on and on about how the movie sucked, how this was done poorly, how that was not cool, ect, ect.......only to say in closing that he didn't like the Star Wars Trilogy to begin with and was never a fan! Now I don't know about you, but that only tells me that some critic's opinion was already set well before he/she saw the movie. So OF COURSE they're going to say it sucked! DUH, they don't like Star Wars to begin with! These poor reviews are nothing more than jealous belittling from a hater. H A T E R........and haters don't make for good critics.

Simple fact is Episode II was an incredibly ENTERTAINING movie. Don't believe me? An auditorium of 600 people clapping and cheering during an incredible scene right in the middle of the movie is proof enough. No movie I've ever been to stirred a crowd like this one did.............And THAT is because Episode II delivers. Attack of the Clones gets back to it's roots. It feels like Star Wars. Hard to believe that there's still more to come with Episode III, but this latest act makes you wanting more. It's only going to get better. But, in the meantime, go attack the theaters! Episode II is an excellent movie...........and this coming from an unbiased man who didn't like Episode I.

title: Fantastic!
review: If you've not yet seen this movie, you may not want to read any further... ...Fantastic! That is the best way for me to sum up this movie. I know that a lot of people were disappointed in The Phantom Menace, I was NOT one of them. But this movie is far superior. The story was better, the film was set at a faster pace and the action was spectacular. A visual masterpiece. It is indeed, as Mr. Lucas said, a darker movie than the last. But it is to be expected in the grand scheme of the Star Wars story. The first battle of the Clone Wars between the Jedi and the Republic is akin Gladiator meets..well...meets Star Wars! The final duel sequence between Count Dooku (Christopher Lee) and Yoda is breathtaking. To see the little Jedi Master movie around so swiftly and display his prowess lets the viewer know exactly why he is the Ultimate Jedi Master...he steals the movie.

title: A truly great achievement
review: Everybody knows whether they admit it or not (even the critics) that George Lucas saved American cinema from death by banality and boredom when he released his first Star Wars film and revolutionized the film industry. This installment rivals the original Star Wars in terms of innovation and excitement. It is a sweeping epic that will excite and entertain anyone who isn't brain dead or a professional movie critic (which often goes hand in hand, at least in the US). I've been to two showings and on both occasions the audience was clearly moved and everybody cheered throughout the movie. There was a huge roar of applause from people of all ages after the movie ended.  Some have criticized the acting but in my opinion that is absolutely ludicrous and has probably more to do with the fact that most of the actors are not from the USA than their talent. Hayden IS Anakin Skywalker just as Harrison Ford was Han Solo and its impossible to imagine anyone else taking their place. Ewan and Natalie play their roles well and Samuel Jackson and Christopher Lee are brilliant. I fear many of the critics that have given this movie a negative review have alternate motifs. We must bear in mind that Lucas is not a part of the Hollywood fluff machine circle that the critics move in and churns out one brainless and badly acted move after another to critical acclaim. It is interesting that in Europe AOTC has received overwhelmingly positive reports.

title: The Force Is Strong With This One
review: Sure, the critics hated it, but they hated it for all the reasons that make the Star Wars series great: cheesy acting in the leads, solid acting from supporting characters and villains, incredible special effects, well-choreographed action, and good versus evil.  If you consider yourself a Star Wars fan, you will love it. If you aren't a fan, see it anyway, so Lucas can finance Episode III

title: Here We go Again
review: Brilliant Images and terrific sound, even more so if you see it in a digital theater, help bring this film to life. Therein lies the fault. this film, despite all its wonderful technological Prowess, ultimately yields a HIGHLY unsatisfying experience for the viewer.The film's attempts at humor go overboard, and the style grows quickly stale. The History, such as it is, is presented as well as can be expected, but, there are times when I, at least, couldn't help but think that it seems as if LUCAS has tinkered with what has already been established.Looking at the story, what little there is, one YEARNS for the middle chapter of the first trilogy, one wants the WONDER of A NEW HOPE, the CAREFREE attitude of RETURN OF THE JEDI. You will not find that here. Instead, you get Anakin Skywalker, whom from the older films, we know will one day become known as DARTH Vader, reduced to a typical teen suffering the WHINIEST form of angst. Even the Defining moment in the Film, Which serves to let the Viewer see the EXACT turning point in his life, is a bit of a letdown, due mainly to the fact that HAYDEN Christensen, who portrays him, has next to no acting ability. He is in fact, as banal as Jake Lloyd, who performed the role in PHANTOM MENACE, and once more, Natalie Portman shows that, while a Beauty, she cannot overcome her surroundings, and NEVER once rises above the material or her on-screen partners. Even R2-D2 and C3po are given short shrift. Yes, they play a somewhat larger part in this, but, what screen-time they get is wasted. Christopher Lee, always a marvelously Unique actor, seems uncomfortable in his role. EVEN YODA seems to have problems....Quite a feat, considering it is an entirely DIGITAL creation. The annoying JAR JAR BINKS....and this may be considered a spoiler, it may not, plays a VASTLY reduced role....yet one cannot help but get the impression that, perhaps LUCAS, if not winking at himself, which HE COULD be, I suppose, is rather, stuffing the atrocity down our collective throats once more? but, I digress. The point is, If you love Star wars, see it. If you love Star Wars, know it is not what it used to be. There are more Problem in this film than I have room for here, but.....I was VERY MUCH LET DOWN.

title: Episode II: Accomplishment of the Clones
review: Never has a film delivered so fully upon my expectations.  Grand, grand filmmaking, brilliantly executed, imminently watchable, full of thought, full of the spirit of the enterprise.  This coming from a person who is very anti-computer generated effects, a person who believes the magic of the first movies relied on the winning formula of fantastic ideas added to real situations, resulting in a perfect movie.  With the cg effects, I felt the film would feel too cartoonish, too distant, and harder to relate to.  I still much prefer real costumes to computer imagery, but Lucas is a visionary, and he has created a brilliant film.  What is most appealing to me is the love story, despite what is being reported it is exceptionally well-done, and the dialogue is superb as well.  Some critics do not realize that Anakin and Padme are from two stern backgrounds, and their feelings of love are forbidden, so to have that kind of connection between them they respond with their hearts and their glances.  The whole series from the beginning left the largest elements in simplicity, like the force, the light and the dark, and in simplicity it is easier to relate to.  The same with their love, it is something everyone has felt, it is both a gift and a curse for them because of their situation, and we relate by how well they portray it in their dialogue and behavior.  Hayden Christensen does an exceptional job of portraying Anakin, in fact he IS Anakin.  He portrays the arrogance that leads to the dark side, and the love and compassion that make him such a tormented being, the one who eventually let's Luke know that Luke `was right' in knowing that he still had good in him.  Natalie Portman is not only beautiful, but a marvelous character in the film, who plays the stern side of politics along with the side of love and compassion exceptionally well, fitting Hayden's emotions of love and anger perfectly.  No wonder Hayden was chosen for the part, they have real chemistry on screen.  The scene where Anakin first shows some signs of his power and anger is incredible, a scene that really puts the point across, and helps us identify with his character and the grandness of Lucas' story.    Ewan McGregor is a captivating lead, one who carries the film with considerable ease, much like his predecessor the great Alec Guinness.  He is wise and powerful, yet burdened and somewhat overshadowed by his brave young Jedi apprentice. Lucas' pacing is exceptional, the transitions, the light to dark, the dark to light, the screen fades, the handling of his material: grand enough to encompass the whole galaxy, minute enough to trace the details of love between the two leads, and the disdain of a wise leader, seeing the arrogance in his young apprentice turning to something more horrible than he can possibly imagine.

title: Lucas is Back
review: Lucas has redeemed himself big after a somewhat dissapointing but still enjoyable episode 1.  This movie totally brings back the original spirit that made the original holy trilogy so great. There are many great scenes of action but the absolute best scene is where Anakin is chasing after Jango Fett's assassin.  This sequence blew me away and i loved it.  Get ready for some really cool Yoda fighitng and buckle in for this kickin ride!!!!!!

title: Better enjoyed if you know which flaws to expect
review:
ATTACK OF THE CLONES is one of the most consistently dazzling movies I have seen in years, and it was probably an okay picture until it ended. Unlike EMPIRE, which closed on a cliffhanger or two, this movie didn't bother to become climactic before it simply stopped. It was much, much better the second time, but remains flawed in some big ways.

CLONES takes itself seriously from the start, a refreshing change from its Jar-Jar laden predecessor. Very little aims to be cute. It's the most political of these films. It would help to have this realized in a more dramatic fashion given its ultimate import to the story. Padme is believable as a Senator. Yoda is well developed as the head of the Jedi order. It's easy to understand why so many rely upon in him. He's a counselor, an effective general in battle, and he's pretty cool with his lightsaber, though he gets barely a minute of time with it. Luke Skywalker's whininess is clearly an inherited trait. Anakin is nothing if not petulant. He is portrayed as headstrong, arrogant, resentful and lacking anything resembling wisdom, but otherwise he doesn't even start down the dark path.

It's slow for a Star Wars movie. Transitions between scenes are labored. A final line of dialogue is said, the shot holds before the wipe to the next one, then there is a hold before the new dialogue starts. This may seem picky, but with 178 scenes - it adds up to a sluggish picture.

Action scenes lay limp. An asteroid field chase brings no concern about anyone hitting anything. The big ending battle with the colossal ships is quite grand, but also quite short for a climax. These sequences suffer from the consistent use of master shots, spectacular on their own, but not conveying progress in the battles. While this may seem realistic, it is also anonymous, structureless, and without drama. There is no urgency, no sense of goal, just spectacular, empty fighting. Scored gloomily, CLONES' action music sometimes has a beat, but still saps the energy right out of these scenes. John Williams seems to have forgotten how to score a heroic moment, or a victory. Listening to the CD, I just assumed that there weren't any, but there are, and they're diminished by the music.

While CLONES portrays a romance, it is not in the least way romantic. Anakin's attraction is immediate and intense. Padme's is neither. Her draw to Anakin is motivated only by the needs of the story. Many scripted personal moments have been left out of the film, and I think her character needed those to make this believable from both sides. Her eventual pronouncement of love is made with clumsiness - it's not sweet, it's kind of weird. Anakin's lengthy one on Naboo is earned, but Christiansen's woodenness makes it fall flat as well.

The dialogue could have used a once-over by someone who isn't afraid to correct George Lucas. "M'Lady" is said too frequently, and never comfortably. Anakin and Kenobi say each other's names repeatedly, and not naturally, because it's unnatural to do. Obi-Wan's sarcasm seems forced, and the buddy-picture dialogue plays flat. Things are also repeated within scenes. As Padme prepares to leave Coruscant, her handmaid jokes that the security guard will be safe with her around. A minute later Anakin makes the same reversal joke about Artoo being along with he and Padme. Also, jokes are sometimes made, including three awful, awful one-liners, not worthy of a low-rent Henny Youngman - made by C-3PO. I would almost trade these in for more of Jake Lloyd's "Yipee!"'s.

SPOILER TIME

A scene with Anakin's mother is too pat. She sees him, says, "Now... I am complete" and dies. This kind of thing happened in MENACE, but there was so much talk of the will of the force, that the deus-ex-machinas worked. This plays as melodrama.

The lightsaber duel is the least dramatic or exciting since the first Star Wars movie. EMPIRE added geography and drama to its duel. JEDI's duel was fierce, and pivotal. MENACE added the speed and acrobatics of real Jedi Knights. This one represents a regression. Dooku fights Obi-Wan, Anakin and Yoda each in turn. The fights with Anakin and Obi-Wan are shot like the duel in A NEW HOPE - close-ups with swords moving past the camera until Dooku gets the better of them. Yoda makes an entrance, and the two battle with lightning, then Yoda whips out the blade. His fighting style works for his size, but the skirmish is too brief to be relished before Dooku pulls the Distract Him By Endangering His Friends trick, and skirts away while Yoda saves our heroes.

Where other movies build to a climax, even MENACE, this one concludes with our heroes getting into, and then out of, an isolated mess. The Clone War begins, but that has no import to these specific characters in the moment, as would, say, Anakin's turning to the dark side. It's interesting politically, but politics play as backdrop. CLONES ended as would have EMPIRE if it had stopped just as the Millennium Falcon landed at Cloud City. It's not that the story isn't finished, or that the film isn't self-contained, it's that neither a climax nor a breaking point were reached. Even FELLOWSHIP OF THE RING ended at a clear chapter stop. CLONES seems to end more in the middle of a chapter, with a cut straight to a quick epilogue just for form.

END SPOILERS

The problem is not with what the filmmakers did, i.e. "focusing too much on the visuals". That effort cannot be faulted. It is a constant blessing, and it has nothing to do with this movie's problems. It is what they didn't do, fixing up the dialogue, tightening, emphasizing the important story elements, and including the moments that develop Padme's love of Anakin, as well as the political dialogue. These and building to a climax - these are the problems.

title: A Fantastic Film
review: I just have to say that all the critics who gave this movie a bad review have no clue what they are talking about and have a serious lack of imagination and aesthetic vision. I think this movie is absolutely wonderful. It has all the excitement and charm of the original trilogy and the darkness of my favorite star wars film The Empire Strikes Back. George Lucas is a master story teller and continues to revolutionize film making. The visual artistry of this film is breathtaking and is to be commended. I would recommend this movie to everyone. It is a triumph not only as an installment of this epic series, but stands alone as a truly masterful film. Gotta run, I'm going to see it again. :-)

title: big step up but a long way to go
review: Surprise- Hayden Christiansen was not as bad as I feared. However, the CGI effects were as distracting as expected. In my opinion creature effects hit their pinnacle in the 80s with films like Dragonslayer and Aliens. Nothing in the past 20 years can surpass those in realism. The CGI characters in SW 2 were just not tangible or  believable. Yoda was the closest thing to a success in this area but he looked like Sonic the Hedgehog during his duel (even though that was the most entertaining sequence in the film.) Overall all SW 2 was such a vast improvement over Phantom Menace that you have to be somewhat pleased but it is still is light years behind Empire which it desperately sought to emulate (protector and princess fall in love, severed limbs, asteroid chases, etc). Maybe its the Byzantine politics instead of rag tag heroes trying to oppose the ultimate bad guy. It's hard to figure out who you should hate.

title: Much Better than "Phantom"
review:
A big Star Wars fan, I saw this movie twice in its first week, and I actually enjoyed the movie more the second time than the first. Maybe it was the theater, or the fact that I was too close to the screen the first time, or for whatever reason. Still, despite all the negative reviews of the movie, I was thoroughly entertained, and I recommend this movie to fans and critics alike.

The movie is much like the original Star Wars movies released in the 70s and 80s - but with more emphasis on the political activities of the Republic. It does an outstanding job setting the stage for the originals, and it also does very well in bridging the gap between the originals and Phantom Menace.

Most of the reviews I heard or read before watching the film said that for the first hour or so, the movie is a little slow and less exciting than the action scenes later in the movie. I did not find this to be the case, and in fact, I enjoyed the first half of the movie every bit as much or perhaps more than the second half. The story is very interesting throughout the entire movie. After watching this second prequel, I am much more excited about the next film than I was after watching Phantom Menace.

Obviously, the action scenes near the end of the movie are very exciting, and it was fun to watch Yoda and Samuel L. Jackson, though I am hoping for more action scenes from them in the next film.

The romance scenes are not that great, but they are good enough. The 'cheesiness' of these scenes could be more of a reflection of the age and inexperience of the characters, and not necessarily due to poor writing, acting or directing of the scenes. The scenes are also necessary in Anakin Skywalker's character development - they help make his eventual turn to the Dark Side of the force more apparent.

Hayden Christensen does an impressive job in his portrayal of Anakin Skywalker. He had perhaps the toughest role in the movie, needing to show pretty intense emotions at almost a moment's notice. Christensen's performance makes it easier to see how a young Jedi could tap into his hatred and anger and eventually become Darth Vader. Star Wars helped launch Harrison Ford's career, and after watching Christensen, I expect him to land some impressive roles in the future as well.

Ewan McGregor is also outstanding in this movie in a likewise tough role - all Star Wars fans are familiar enough with Obi-wan Kenobi that any of them would easily spot inconsistencies in his character, mannerisms, speaking style, wit, etc. Not only did McGregor need to adequately portray Kenobi, but he also had to do it like Alec Guiness did 20 years ago. McGregor is excellent as Kenobi - he had all of the subtleties of Guiness as well as Kenobi's style. He made what could have been a difficult task look effortless in an impressive performance.

The rest of the performances are also good, if somewhat time-limited. I suspect we'll see more from Christopher Lee as Cout Dooku and from Jackson as Mace Windu in the third prequel.

I was not impressed with Natalie Portman, however. Her performance of Padme Amidala was somewhat flat and one-dimensional. She could have done much better since it appeared she really did not sink her teeth into the role well. In some of her scenes, she appeared distracted and/or uninterested. I expect a better performance from her in Episode 3.

No review of a George Lucas film could be complete without discussing the digital effects. Though the CG effects are integrated well into the rest of the movie, they are not completely flawless, and there are at least a few examples of obvious computer creations - not the least of which is the diner cook who interacts with Obi-wan Kenobi. Despite all of the advances in computer-generated effects, they simply are not as realistic as the old 'man-in-a-rubber-suit' trick which has been with us since the 1920s. For background scenery, outer space flying scenes, and in other areas, CG effects do a good job. But when it comes to creating a character who interacts with human actors, computer-generated effects do a very poor job. In fact, if Jar Jar Binks and this diner cook represent the best we can do with creating realistic-looking CG characters to interact with human actors, I'd say it is still impossible to succeed. Makeup and latex masks are still much more realistic than any software Lucas has utilized in his movies.

John Williams outdoes even himself in the music he created for the film. I thought the music was perfect for the mood of the film - the hints of the Imperial March during some of Anakin's scenes, the underlying somber tones during some of the scenes, the upbeat music during the battle scenes - all of it was very good. This is the best Star Wars music next to Empire Strikes Back.

Overall, this is a very good film, easily in line with the original Star Wars films. The ending leaves you with a similar feeling that you have at the end of Empire. It's not an upbeat or happy film like Star Wars A New Hope was, but that's understandable considering the subject matter. Star Wars fans will be pleased - much more than at the end of Phantom Menace. And even movie fans who don't like Star Wars will likely find something about this movie to enjoy.

title: Restores your faith after the E1 slip.
review:
I am a Star Wars fan. These films captured my imagination at a very young age and, except for Episode 1, (which, IMHO was worthless outside of the lightsabre duels) have had me ever since.

I loved this film. The story was rich and satisfying. The special effects were almost perfect. The acting was very much improved. All around it was better than E1 and a worthy successor to the original trilogy. I sat down at the start of the film and didn't stop smiling (there were a few snips of dialogue, especially Anakin's that made me wince) until I went to sleep that night.

The opening battle of the clone war was so well done that I don't have the words to express how pleased I am. Truly a grand achievement for CGI story telling.

The love story didn't really work for me until the end. The rolling around in the grass scene was a little weak. And the CGI scene where Anakin rides one of the animals grazing near them was the only CGI sequence that failed.

I REALLY hope they get someone who can finally do Anakin some justice for E3. Hayden was a fair actor but, they next piece of the story will be INTENSE and they need to find someone who will suspend my disbelief better. Portman really stepped up and actually acted this time around, good for her!

Parsecs.... Jango banging his head as he boards Slave 1... homage's to famous E4 bloopers? All I know is I laughed very hard. Good for Lucas for having a sense of humor!

Yoda's fighting might not have worked the way it was intended but, it was very entertaining. And how about him picking up his walking stick after thrashing Dooku... classic! He flies around like Bruce Lee amped up on crack but then needs his walking stick just to get around??? Priceless!

So, I was VERY pleased. Hope I didn't focus on the faults too much, just trying to balance out my testament to fandom with some focus on reality. Please keep up the intensity for E3 (and PLEASE add a big fat space battle (capital ships and fighters!!!!) so this amazing story can be finished properly.

title: Star Wars is back on Track!!!
review:
Attack of the Clones puts Star Wars back on the Map!!! I thoroughly enjoyed this film. It is a very, visually stunning movie, and the plot moves along, smoother then any Star Wars movie to date. While there may not be an acting performance worthy of an Academy Award, this does not hinder the movie one bit. As with all Star Wars movies, there are bits in this movie that may get annoying at times, but there is so much more that makes you forget these small flaws.

Jar Jar Binks, the Gungan outcast that annoyed many fans in the Phantom Menace, returns to his role, though he is only given mabye ten minutes of screen time. He still has his annoying tone, which may make one cringe for a moment or two, but just as he gets under your skin, the scene changes. There are a few really goofy one liners in this movie, but again, they will be forgotten as the movie moves so quickly, you hardly notice.

After viewing this film, it makes you appreciate the Phantom Menace a lot more. I truly enjoyed The Phantom Menace, but this movie just blows it away. This movie will take several viewings, in order to catch all of the action. So much is going on during the final battle, between the Republic, and the Separatists, that you just cannot see everything. One thing I really loved, was the return of the magic between our lovable droid duo, C-3PO and R2-D2. While some of the dialogue between the two becomes a bit much, it takes us back in time to the original trilogy. After watching this movie, I am sure you will be transported back to the Star Wars universe we have come to love for the past two decades.

title: Yoda's my hero!!
review: it was awesome!! i went with no expectations whatsoever, and thoroughly enjoyed it. if you aren't expecting much when you go and see it, then i think you'll be pleasantly surprised. the special effects were awesome, Ewen McGregor's a stud, and Yoda is so my hero!!

title: Yoda is the greatest Jedi Knight!!
review:
I must admit I was afraid to go see Episode II, even though I´ve been a Star Wars fan since I was 4 years old. I had liked Episode I, but somehow didn´t expect Episode II to be any good. Boy was I wrong!!

This movie has a little bit of everything. It has romance, a lot of action, drama, spectacular special effects, and humor. At first Anakin didn't convince me, he seemed too up tight, but as the movie evolves, we can actually see darkness in his face, it's Vader in the making.

But of course, the best part of the movie is the "Yoda Scene". I don't want to spoil that for anyone, so please go ahead and see this wonderful movie. You will understand why Yoda is the best Jedi ever!!

title: Much better then Episode I
review: Lucas has once again created an excellent movie. The action in this movie is brilliant, its easy to follow and intense. Its sad that Episode I was so bad, because it kind of sabotages the saga. My vote 9/10 and the best movie of the year so far.

title: The Force is strong with this one!
review: At last! After the childish Episode I, the Star Wars saga is back on track with this one. The plot is more complex than it might appear at first glance and the dark side of the force has regained the appeal it had in The Empire Strikes Back by seducing young and handsome Anakin Skywalker. I believe that this movie can also be more appreciated by non-Star-Wars-fans for it almost does without of the "fans only" material so frequent in Episode I. My only remark is that the gravity of Anakin's seduction might not be clear enough for non fans for there is no previous discussion of the power of the dark side. Ah, and I live near lake Como where the love scenes between Anakin and Padme were shot. Please have some envy...

title: Send in the Clones
review: WOW! This movie ranks the 4th best Star Wars Series. The first is A New Hope, come on it's the original. Well anyway, Attack of the Clones Rocks! Christopher Lee plays spectacularly as the role of Count Dooku. Hayden Christiensen brings darkness and evil to the person, Anakin. Ewan McGregor plays Anakin's father-figure jedi master. But Yoda. Oh Yoda. Yoda kicks Lee's a$$, it's so funny. He's flipping and rolling and slashing at this guy. But it's so short. Another good actor is Temuera Morrison, he plays great as Jango Fett, even though he doesn't have many lines as he should, but his action parts make up for it. C-3PO is hilarious.
