Just keep your eye out. But, do yourself a favor and see this huge breakthrough in American Filmmaking. Take your kids, or your wife or girlfriend, or even take a bunch of your pals. It's one of those movies, you have a great time with. So see Star Wars - Episode II: Attack of the Clones in theaters now! Have fun! I know you will.

title: Better than Episode 1!!!
review: Aside from the brief Jar Jar occurances, and the stooges-styled antics of 3PO and  R2, the story actually did a decent job of interweaving character development against the complex political backdrop. Thank god it was better than Phantom Menace.

title: SEE IT NOW
review: The movie is excellent.  Action sequences very believable.  Doesn't suffer from the prolong sequences of CG that made parts of Episode I a little unbelievable.  The problem with critics is that they don't consider the movie in leu of the other 4 films.  In this light, the movie is nearly perfect.  Lucas fills in many of the plot and character gap and sets us up for the fall of Skywalker.  I'm sure after Episode III we will all be in amazement how Lucas crafted this space opera that has spanned 50 years on screen and 30 years in our lives.

title: Now we're getting somewhere!
review:
Despite what you may have heard, this movie is not horrible. It has a couple of low-points but they do not detract from the film nearly as much as everyone is saying. Mainly, it rocks in an Empire Strikes Back kind of way. Any true Star Wars fan will love it. And when I say any true Star Wars fan, I am not talking about the little kids who liked The Phantom Menace? I am talking about the people who have all the bad dialogue from episodes 4-6 memorized and are really happy about it. I am talking about the people who own the limited edition 1978 Boba Fett action figure. But most importantly, I am talking about the people that love Star Wars because it's truly a great story.

So let me briefly sum up what all the poop-on-my-party reviewers are saying about this movie: they are saying that the screenplay is cheesy. DUH! Did you see ANY of the other movies in this series? Or did you block out Luke's whining and C-3PO's prissy one-liners? Star Wars movies are not indie films. They do not have brilliant acting performances or Tom Stoppard writing the dialogue. They are archetypal tales of good vs. evil. They are about high-action battles and awe-inspiring special effects. They are about a time long ago in a galaxy far far away- so cool your jets and have a little fun or I'm going to turn to the dark side and use the force against you.

Let me start off the praise portion of this review by saying that Attack of the Clones contains some of the best CGI animation I have ever seen. I am pretty picky about this stuff, but I can honestly say that not one thing looked lame or cartoonish. It was just perfect. Yoda is completely CGI, and yet he is still the Yoda you know and love. In fact, seeing the Jedi master whip out his lightsaber is one of the highlights of the whole action-packed escapade. He is better than ever. Ewan McGregor and Samuel L. Jackson are both super-cool as Yoda's right-hand-men, fighting the forces of darkness with style, grace and aplomb (nice word, huh)? Hayden Christensen is cast rather perfectly in the role of the teenage Anakin. In his performance, hints of Darth Vader's cruelty and echoes of Luke's whiny "it's just not fair" attitude shine through with equal ease - and they come to the surface in a way that feels quite earnest.

The plot is infinitely more engaging than The Phantom Menace, complete with lots of hand-to-hand combat, undercover investigations, intrigue over who is going to the dark side, and the ever looming question: who is really controlling the Senate? Considering everything we already know (having seen the future in Episodes 4-6), Attack of the Clones does an incredible job of keeping us on our toes while also doing some major setup work in preparation for Episode III- which has all the potential to be the best film of all.

All that said, even I have to concede that the love story between Padme and Anakin leaves a little something to be desired. Aside from the fact that she is "in his soul, consuming him," you have to wonder what a woman like Senator Amidala sees in the hotheaded Jedi apprentice. Sure, he's got the skills that pay the bills, but even if they don't have statutory rape laws in the Republic, it's a pretty risque romance. Granted, we all love a bad boy now and then, but usually not one we used to baby-sit. But I came to terms with it as it evolved into something believable during the last hour of the film.

I'm going to stop here so as not to give anything away. But I will say that this movie is less for the masses and more for the people who are obsessed with the whole story. So although I am jumping up and down and doing the dance of joy, I do admit that I own a toy light saber (it makes the coolest noises) as well as a plethora of additional Star Wars paraphernalia such as an R2-D2 crazy straw that I just can't seem to part with. It might be a little sick, but I really couldn't care less. If you have never been bitten by the SWB (Star Wars Bug), you may not be as excited as I am. So go see Spider-Man instead, but don't ask me to respect you in the morning.

title: Solid Star Wars film. Definitely leaves you wanting more.
review: This movie was very well done and accomplished what it set out to do. Anyone who is going into this movie anticipating the best movie of all time is going to be disappointed.  After all, there can be only one "Princess Bride" in Hollywood history.  =)  Seriously, though, if you're a fan of Star Wars, this movie will leave you wanting more, and that's exactly the mark of a successful movie in a series.  Go see this movie and enjoy it for what it is--a highly entertaining action movie with a few twists and turns thrown in to keep it interesting.

title: Maybe the best of the series.
review:
After seeing it twice I can honestly say that "Attack of the Clones" might be the best Star Wars film to date. It's at the very least just as good as Empire Strikes Back which up to now was hands down my favorite Star Wars film.

Sure at times some of the performances are a bit wooden but the acting in the original trilogy wasn't exactly Oscar caliber either. The story is more intriguing than the one in "The Phantom Menace" and I found myself caring more about the characters this time around. The standout performance in this movie comes from Ewan McGregor as Obi Wan Kenobi. He was the best thing about "The Phantom Menace" and I thought that he was even better in the role this time around. Christopher Lee is also pretty effective as Count Dooku although he doesn't have much screen time.

Some may be turned off by the romantic scenes with Anakin and Padme but I actually enjoyed them even in spite of the fact that some of the dialogue was too sappy and overdramatic. The background scenery is real nice and at the same time John Williams excellent love theme helps to give these scenes a boost. I also thought it was pretty effective in how some of the music from the previous films was used during key scenes.

Some of the most spectacular moments come during the final 40 minutes when the whole Jedi Council is seen in action. And Yoda provides perhaps the most exciting two minutes out of the whole entire Star Wars saga. Yoda got a huge response from the people in the theater.

It was also nice to see C-3PO and R2-D2 together again on screen. 3PO has a few really hilarious moments. Even Jar Jar Binks was used well this time around with a brief but significant supporting role. So those who hate the character will not have to tolerate him for that long.

The ending of Episode II sort of has an Empire Strikes Back cliffhanger style ending that should leave most Star Wars fans anxiously anticipating May of 2005.

I think that most of the critics who are ripping this movie apart just don't know how to have a good time at the theater anymore.

title: Hmmmm....how do I call this one?
review:
Ok...let me start by saying that I am total Star Wars fan. I grew up with the ANH, ESB and ROTJ and LOVED them all (even ROTJ)!!!

I waited MANY, MANY years for more of the same and my prayers were finally answered with TPM. Sadly, the film did NOT live up to my hopes and dreams. Far from it!! There were good points -though not many. Darth Maul was cool but very little else shone. It set the scene I suppose but ultimately it was flat, and lifeless. The poor acting left me with NO apathy for any of the characters.

Now, here we are 3 years later and I have just seen AOTC a few hours ago. And....well....I really don't know what to make of it. I wanted to LOVE it, but cos of TPM I was scared and frankly, I approached the film with a 'its probably gonna be a let-down as well' attitude.

However...I was excited and when the film started and the title music played after the all too familiar 'A long time ago in a Galaxy far, far away...' I must admit I was tingling all over, all doubt left my mind and I waited, waited to be enthralled like I was all those many years ago.

BUT.....you know what? Something was wrong. Seriously wrong! My head is still buzzing from seeing it but I will try to sum it up in as best I can......though this could be tricky.

Good Points...

1. YODA -OH MY GOD!!!! I still can't believe how amazing he was in this. That end fight is truly one of the greatest Star Wars moments EVER!!!!

2. COUNT DOOKU -At LAST someone who can act in Star Wars!! Thank you Mr Lee. It's just a shame none of the others can match your talent.

3. THE BIG BATTLE -Well, to sum up, it was fantastic. Epic, sprawling and with, best of all, loads of Jedi fighting. Most of it was CGI and the action was so overwhelming as to be sometimes difficult to follow but it was still GREAT!! I was enthralled throughout this final battle. Great stuff!!

Bad Points...

1. The Acting -This was ABSOLUTELY AWFUL. Perhaps even worse than TPM, especially as this film had so many more poignant moments in it. They really should've done better. There is no excusing it!

2. Dialogue -For the love of GOD...why is the script so child-like AGAIN!! Almost every line could be winced at. Like Obi-wan's 'BLAST, this is why I hate flying!' Though I must admit, Yoda had a few good lines like the one about Obi-wan 'losing' his planet for example.

3. CGI - I am all for CGI and the new boundaries it gives films. BUT a film loses its warmth and feeling the more you add in. The actors have enough problems struggling with the awful dialogue without having blue screen after invisible enemy after blue screen after invisible enemy, etc to work with.

4. The 'Plot' -hmmm.....this was very worrying. How did a Star Wars storyline suddenly become so confusing to follow? I know plenty of the Star Wars Universe, but at times I was left wondering just what the hell was going on. This will be explained upon further viewings but should that need to be the case? I am CERTAIN that people new to Star Wars will be totally lost at the Political angle to this story. This is such a shame.

5. The 'love' Story -ARRGHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!! This was SOOOO painful to watch. I just CANNOT buy into this at all. It's these scenes which could prevent me from seeing again in the cinema.

So.....What does this all mean? It means I feel mixed emotions about this film. I want to LOVE it and bits of it I really do. BUT, there are SO MANY gripes and niggles that, worryingly, I cant love it.

This is such a shame....

My mark for this film will be 7 out of 10

title: It's what the fans have been wishing for.
review:
George Lucas's rustiness after a 20-year directing hiatus was evident in the clunky pacing and unnaturally stilted performances of Star Wars: Episode I: The Phantom Menace. Now, with the benefit of recent experience and the writing assistance of Jonathan Hales, Lucas has directed another masterpiece in his mythical space opera. While Phantom Menace was almost childlike in its giddiness, Attack of the Clones begins to delve into Anakin Skywalker's dark motives for turning to the dark side. This is the perversely riveting spectacle that die-hard fans have awaited for 25 years, and it foretells a descent into darkness in Episode III that should be unmatched by any of the other films in the series.

Episode II also reintroduces a few of the elements that made the original trilogy so much fun. R2D2 and C3PO are once again a comic team after their miscalculated demotion to throwaways in Episode I. Young Obi-Wan Kenobi, now played by Ewan MacGregor as though he were channeling the spirit of Sir Alec Guinness himself, shows us the adventures we always imagined he must have had as a young, eager Jedi Knight. And Yoda reveals a never-before-seen facet of himself that elicits cheers and squeals of delight from the audience.

Most critics, even those who enjoyed this installment, bemoan the dialog. Do not fear. If your ear has grown accustomed to Lucas's penchant for theatrical speech, more akin to the 19th-century stage than the 21st-century street, then you will find no surprises here. Even Natalie Portman as Padme Amidala has shed her stubborn monotone of Episode I to show that, when delivered with a little feeling, even Lucas's starched verbiage can convey the appropriate emotions. You won't be moved, but your ears won't be ringing, either.

For sheer originality, nothing will surpass the thrill of the original Star Wars trilogy. But George Lucas has managed to give us the next best thing: a film that stokes our nostalgia for the originals while adding to their mystique.

Chris Stvartak

title: StarWars is back
review:
I believed that this film still shows us that George Lucas still has a passion for this epic. His love and devotion is on course, but it would appear that he sometimes he can't "see the forest for the trees". Like many, I found the beginning rather pedantic in it's ability to draw the observer into something emotional, but rather attempted to dazzle us with effects. In my opinion, Lucas has so developed his scope and concept for the films attitude, that he forgot to allow one very special thing to happen: Allow the actors to act. I got teary-eyed at some of the action scenes rather than the development of sympathies and antipathies involving the character development. There is where the trees go in the way. The movie consisted of so many trees, that one kind of didn't see the forest till after they had digested the viewing for at least 45 minutes.

Movement from one shot to the next was breathless. I also found myself yearning for the days of the little puppet that characterized Yoda rather than the CGI - especially in the fight with Dooku. A bit much. And even though the antics of C3PO in the assembly line of Droids and his 2-sided part in the arena battle was comical, it lacked coherency with the seriousness of the moment. And yes, I do know what comic relief is.

But yet, all in all, it did not really disappoint me like The Phantom Menace. I saw it on a huge screen with a Dolby system that was, in my opinion, the best in the area. It was a true sensation, and for that I will go see it again, and probably again. And even though it didn't rank up there with "Return Of The Empire", or had the heart that "A New Hope" had, it shows that Lucas is still in love with this epic tale of good against evil.

title: Everything that we could ever ask for!
review: This movie has everything a Star Wars fan could ask for. All the cool scenes are there. Sadly, though, there are minor flaws in visuals. Like in the scene where Anakin rides one of the huge animals. The intro scene is just as it should be. It's intense and kept me on the edge of my seat the whole way through. We also learn new things. I like the scene were Kenobi "accidently" achieves knowledge on the Clone army. The movie's main theme is the "development" of Anakin Skywalker. I think the change of him and his "turning dark" is magnificently presented to us. On another note, reviews say the actors' performances are beyond poor. I must disagree. I give this movie 10/10 - Star Wars is back!

title: How things work
review:
Despite of a minor failure of the theatre's sound system, I was mostly impressed by the great sound effects in this movie. Spaceship flyby's explosions etc, really made me shiver and shake! ;)

I am glad this story really adds to the trilogy, as there are many unfoldings of the plot. If you know Episode 1 and Episode 4, Episode 2 will tell you where things got started, and how things work out.

The least bit was the part where Anakin and Padme grow to love eachother in a way "I want to love you but I can't". Ofcourse, it was supposed to happen this way, but mostly in the first part it really drags on.

I recommend this movie to all Star-Wars lovers that want to know where the roots of Episode 4 lie.

Bakmeel

title: Mostly Harmless
review:
Well part 2 has arrived. Like everyone who is going to see it for the first time I had the wonder, not the wonder of how amazing it was going to be, but the wonder of 'I wonder if it's any good'. So by I went in with mixed expectations and am glad I did. Yes over all it is better than The phantom Menace, but then again it could have been better. What stuck me most is that there are very few stand out moments, like the pod race in part one. What everyone will remember is the Yoda fight scene which is fun but short. The only other big moment was the space battle but again it seemed to short. Is it just me but has ship to ship combat which made up much of 4,5 and 6 to me so exciting almost been forgotten. The love scenes were there but apart from that they are not worth commenting on. Another thing that got me was that I have always had the idea that Jedis are hard, lightsaber welding mother f***ers, but in this film they do come over a bit wimpy.

Well was it worth the wait? No. Is it crap? No. Is it to complicated? At times. Should Mr Lucas direct ever again? Hard to say, No. Is the dialogue good? Well, I Believe that the Jedis use many many words, when one would do! So No. Is it any good. Well I enjoyed this as much as I enjoyed the Scorpion King. In fact,these films have many things in common. They have sword fights, They have lots of wonderful looking sets, they have wooden acting. They are really both fun no brainer. Maybe one of the biggest insults I have ever given to a star Wars film

title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly
review: As much as I would love to be able to say that Attack of The Clones is as good as the original three in the series, I sadly cannot.  And even more dissapointing is the realization that the prequels will never reach the type of cinematic enjoyment that the first three did. It's just not going to happen. But don't get me wrong.  Attack of The Clones is not a bad movie. It is much better then the Phantom Menace and gives us much more insight into how the Republic falls and the Empire takes over. THE GOOD:  Every scene with Palpatine is awesome.  Watching the character continue to manipulate the Jedi is fun to watch and you can tell that Ian McDiarmid is having fun playing the character. His early scene with Anakin gives us insight into the relationship the two have built since we last saw them in The Phantom Menace and when Palpatine talks about how he loves Democracy and loves the Republic it is develish evil we hear in his undertones. When Palpatine finally reveals himself as Darth Sidious in Episode III, it is going to be an awesome moment. Anakins slaughter of the Tusken Raiders camp is cool and his scene after where he tells Amidala what he did is easily the best acting scene in the Prequels.  We finally see Darth Vader in Anakins eyes and it is very compelling. Also memorable: The chase through Coruscant, Kenobi vs. Jango Fett, The Battle Scene at Geonosis, parts of the C-3PO and R2-D2 antics during the big battle scene, watching Count Dooku escape on his scooter across the desert as he is being followed by Anakin and Obi Wan (am I mistaken or did the soundtrack have undertones of the Wicked Witch of the West theme from the Wizard of Oz as Dooku is on his broom err scooter.). The BAD: The two most difficult things for a director to convey are tone and subtlety.  Lucas fails to convey both of these.  Sadly this movie that should be full of energy and emotion is dead.  Instead of experiencing the movie with the characters we are observers. This is mainly due to the weak dialogue and stale directing by Lucas.  The Flanneled One is much more interested in computer effects then he is in character development.  This is the biggest missing ingredient that seperates Episode I and II from the first three.  Also, the editing choices in the film were questionable at times.  There  is little to no tension built through out the story.  It never builds to anything emotional, it just moves on to the next scene, the next plot point.  Some scenes should have been cut out all together. The UGLY:  Anakins scene with Amidala by the fireplace is truly horrible.  The writing is sophomoric and its really quite embarrassing for both actors.  Lucas then follows this scene with what has to be the worst scene of the movie which is Anakin having a nightmare about his mother.  This scene would have worked if Lucas would have shown us a glimpse of what his dream was about and it would have served to re-aquaint the audience with Shmi before we see her death scene.  Sadly, no one mentioned this to Lucas and the scene plays horribly.  I saw the movie twice on opening day and this scene got laughs both times. All in all the movie has a lot  more good in it then bad. However I couldn't help feeling that as Palpatine and others watch the Clone Army board the Star Destroyers and The Imperial March is playing it should have been the emotional climax of the film instead of just another visual spectacle. 7.5 out of 10 but I'll round it up to 8 since it's Star Wars :-)

title: A brilliant segue into the future (past) of Star Wars...
review: I was thrilled with "Attack of the Clones". The action kept me at the edge of my seat, the cinematography was breathtaking, the comedy made me laugh out loud, and the romance - well, it is so believable. I applaud George Lucas - telling the middle of a story when everyone in the world knows how it ends - an incredible task. "Attack of the Clones" ties together so many relationships from the original 3 movies. Hayden Christensen is perfect for this role, Natalie Portman again does an outstanding job. Ewan McGregor even looks like Alec Guiness a bit. And, Yoda ROCKS! I can't wait to see it again.

title: Bring on the Clone War
review:
Well I saw the opening night at Leicester Sq london where we got some preshow entertainment from Anthony Daniels the actor for C3P0, he was pretty funny and handled the raucous post pub midnight crowd admirably! He dealt with a line up of storm troopers the curtains parted and the crowd cheered loudly. Oh and Rick McCallum also came out and told us it was Fu****** awesome!

To the movie, what a fantastic movie (not comparing at all to the others) so much colour, visual candy, action, romance, new worlds, fantastic aliens as well as the introduction of characters we already know and love!

The thing is, people are complaining about the dialogue etc and comparing it to the ep 4,5,6 but the first time you ever saw those movies most of us were just kids, what did we know about fancy dialogue (not that hollywood really delivers anything but!) so to criticise plot, dialogue etc is a bit over the top. I just sat back and soaked every minute of a brilliant movie. I dont think I have ever been in a cinema where people were actually cheering so loud (Yoda scene, when Mace Windu makes a tough entrance) and at the end deservedly so a standing ovation! Great movie, great characters, simply the best movie i have ever seen.

Long live the star wars saga because it brings out the child in us and takes us away from the real world for a couple of action packed hours!!!

Great Stuff Lucas! Cant wait for the CLone War, I cant even begin to imagine the fight scenes in that baby!

title: Disappointed with the actors & the 1st half of the movie
review: I'd been looking forward for this movie and the least i can say is that it's been disappointing.I hear people say this is the real return of Star Wars,that episode 1 wasn't very good,but for me,it was better than this one.Let's start with the good stuff:the story is really getting somewhere,we start to understand where the next episodes come from(why Anakin became Darth Vador,what the supreme chancellor plans are...),and the suspense at the end is good,which makes us wanna see episode 3.Now with the negative:the acting is really bad.Christensen doesn't seem to know what he's supposed to do:am I a good or a bad guy?Portman is more of a princess than a fighter and it shows during the big battle(even htough she is really sexy).Their love story is sometimes really ridiculous.Overall,the movie really starts after its 1st half when the talking is over and the action really begins(what's the point with the murder attempts on PadmÃ©'s life).Anyway,I'm now looking forward for the next episode:let's hope the acting will be better and the romance won't be so absurd...

title: I like the Phantom Menace Better
review: I saw this film today and was disappointed. The dialog was really bad at the beginning. Natalie Portman has done better work than this (Where The Heart Is). I didn't like Hayden Christinsen either. The fight scenes were done before and it's just ho hum now. There was nothing really that got me involved in this movie. I liked the Phantom Menace because it had Liam Neeson and he is a fine actor. If Jar Jar Binks would have not been as much in the Phantom Menace it would have been better. The Yoda fight was awesome and was the highlight of the movie. George has not made any of the movies as good as The Empire Strikes Back. He did try to do this movie like the Empire, but to me he fell short.

title: Absolutely bloody brilliant!
review:
The smile first appeared on my face when the Star Wars theme music blasted out at the very beginning. I was still smiling 2 days later when i was about to see it for the third time. All i can say is that it is most excellent.

The characterisation is incredible. Lucas has gone back to the roots and has learnt how to make you care about the characters. It breaks my heart to think that one day Anakin will become Darth-Vader, an evil sith majorly transformed from the days of his innocent youth.

The action scenes are breathtakingly good and had me on the edge of my seat throughout.

Now onto my favourite part... the music. John Williams has absolutely out-done himself once again. The thing i like most about the music from episode 2 is that it is incorporating more of the music from episodes 4, 5 and 6. The echo of the imperial march when Anakin is deeply distressed and angered is truly haunting.

I have heard many people criticise the dialogue in this movie, which i feel is justified in some areas but not in most. The only truly cringe-worthy moment is the whole business with C3-P0 and R2-D2 during the arena battle. But even that is short lived and acceptable because children will love it. There is a beautiful scene between Padme and Anakin where they question their feelings where the dialogue is perfect. Poetic without being cheesy springs to mind.

The acting was superb throughout with stand-out performances by Ewan McGregor, Hayden Christensen, Christopher Lee and of course Samuel L. Jackson.

All in all i can say that i totally understand now how people must have felt seeing "The Empire Strikes Back" and having to wait 3 years for "The Return of The Jedi". It will indeed be a painful wait but i can confidently say that it will be totally worth it.

I gave this movie a very deserved 10/10. Roll on episode 3, and in the meantime i will be eagerly awaiting the dvd release of this one.

title: A Great Movie
review: After seeing Star Wars Episode 2, I can say that I was very pleased with the entire movie. It provides plenty of action, mystery, and a love story. This segment sets up Episode 3 very well in Anakin's character development, and while people know the result of this trilogy, the means to which that is accomplished is what really brings people to the theater. Oh yeah, and the light sabers.

title: Wanted more...
review:
I've just come home from the World premier of SW 2 and what can you say.. The movie felt like it went on for only a few minutes, thanks to the plot pace was good, with a speed increase the longer into the movie you get..

Not wanting to tell anything that will ruin it for anyone else but this movie is a most.... I think it was WAY BETTER then Ep. 1 .... Too bad you have to wait another 3 years to see if they will top this...

title: Better than Episode 1
review:
My review of Attack of the Clones

My general view of the movie: Somewhat slow, but picks up the pace to finish strong. You will need to see this movie more than once, if for nothing else than to see all the stuff you couldn't take in the first time around. It is not a perfect movie, it does have it's flaws. Yet it is an improvement on Episode 1 and a worthy addition to the franchise.

Specific thoughts: **Some Spoilers Ahead** Ewan McGregor IS Obi-Wan Kenobi! Perhaps it is just the beard and the longer hair, but I could honestly believe someone miraculously de-aged Alec Guiness, he was THAT good. Hayden Christenson shines best when he gets in touch with that nasty dark side. Natalie Portman makes it obvious where Priness Leia gets her good looks from. She also wears an outfit at the end that comes close to Leia's Metal Bikini in Jedi for sex appeal. Samuel L Jackson is fine as Mace Windu, but the role really does not play to his strengths: Yelling and Jive-Talking. Nice to see R2-D2 and C3PO back at it. C3PO has some of the funniest scenes in this movie, particularly when his head is removed and mistakenly attached to a droid warrior. And Yoda.......oh, boy! Muppet no more! He's now a full on CGI character that finally shows just how much of a bad-ass Jedi he really is!

One thing I noticed the most were things that rely on the viewer's foreknowledge of what is to come to have an effect. Obi-Wan's line to Anakin, "I swear you are going to be the death of me!" would be just a throwaway by itself, but given we already know Obi-Wan's fate in episode IV, that line elicts a response from the audience. As does another line from C3PO, "R2 says he has received a message from an Obi-Wan Kenobi....", which parallels a line from Episode IV.

Like I said, the movie has it's flaws. The dialogue does seem stilted at tiimes (personal beef: Having someone with an American accent say "Milady" to me sounds EXTREMELY fake! Just say "My Lady" and it sounds SO MUCH better!), but I really do not see the beef people have with Lucas' directing style. To me, it works just fine for this movie.

As to this installment's place amongst the episode pantheon, it is close but does not quite equal any of the first three movies, but it is a solid improvement over Episode I. At any rate, it is definitely worth a look see whiole it is still in the theater. I know I will go again.

I gave this movie an 8/10.

title: Return of the magic
review:
Well hi there,

I'll make this short:

this movie brought back the magic in the SW series... where Episode 1 was a kind of prelude with some very nice bits in it (music, setup of grander schemes, saber duels, podrace), this episode really brings the magic Star Wars feeling back to the screen.

The acting was better than I expected, still soft in some spots, but, as someone said before, Star Wars is not always about the acting (Luke? Luuuuuuuuuuuuke?), but about the general magic feeling it tends to create. And Attack of the Clones really makes that happen, after a slow start (not bad start, just tempo-wise slow), the pace goes faster and faster, and I for one really like the way Anakin is potraited to succumb slowly to the dark side. Sometimes the movie is cheesy, sometimes too much CGI, but all in all, I think this one is very close to the original trilogy.

If you like Star Wars, go to this movie.

If you dont like Star Wars, just give it a try, I will guarantee that at least you will marvel at the effects, but maybe, just maybe, you will feel a bit of the magic too!

Lando

title: ===Spoiler Alert===.......great movie
review: well...this movie is a definite improvement over episode 1. The characters have some history to work from and there is not a lot of Jar Jar. Well actually he causes the rise of the empire but that's beside the point. C-3p0 and r2 again bring back humor, which I missed since the original trilogy. Attack of the clones in my opinion has a lot to do with the original trilogy than episode 1 because we meet Luke's aunt and uncle, the clone troopers will eventually become storm troopers and WE FINALLY SEE THE ORIGINS OF THE DEATH STAR...which for me was a spine tingling moment.... the death star will probably play a role in episode 3. One last thing.... yoda...yoda yoda yoda.... I just didn't see it coming...yoda with a light saber...the highlight of the star wars saga...

title: George, swallow your pride and get someone with talent already!
review:
These movies (this statement can only be said with eyes closed, hand on my shaking forehead). I cannot express how much I would respect George Lucas if he were to just stand up out of the directors seat, hand the pen and paper to someone a little more capable, and say, `Here you go, please, make me proud.' It almost makes me wish someone would slap him on the back of the head and tell him to ask for directions already, cause Georgy boy is as lost as you can get. These movies have such potential, they have so much to offer us. Can't we just get the movie so promised to us? It's almost as if Mr. Lucas is thinking, well, there is no way that this movie will not make a zillion dollars so I can go ahead and write what I want and that way I get to do it all myself.

Episode II-Attack of the Clones' takes place 10 years after the last POS we all waited on line to see 3 years ago, The Phantom Menace'. Queen Padme' Amidala (Natalie Portman) is now a senator (and still single??), Anakin Skywalker (Hayden Christensen, Life as a House') is now a grown up (in appearance only mind you, I don't know who whines more, him or my 3 ½ year old!) hotty with an ego only Padme' can love. The movie starts off with Senator Amidala's life being threatened. That is how Obi-Wan (Ewan McGregor) and his young apprentice Skywalker make their way back into Padme's life and heart. Also going on, the Republic is slowly falling apart and its up to the Jedi to help stop it. Only thing is the Jedi cannot do much to help because there aren't enough of them. Keep in mind that these are only a few of the things going on in this mess of a movie. It was mind boggling. I consider myself an intelligent person and I don't think following movies is a difficult task, but with all the different references to people we haven't met responsible for this or that catastrophe, its hard to keep up with who is good and who is bad. And the CG in this movie is very good, yes, but also too much. I don't want only eye candy George, I want a good-guy bad-guy story that will keep me interested. Don't we all? Aren't you all sick of saying, `well, it was better then Phantom'. It's supposed to be a great movie, not an acceptable movie.

These actors have so much potential. Natalie Portman is a good actress, all she needs is a little direction. You know, that thing the Director is supposed to do. And Hayden Christensen does an okay job, if he's supposed to be so whiney and overstuffed. Poor Ewan McGregor tries so hard to give his character life, but how can he with such HORRIBLE dialog. For instance, in one scene C3PO is having his head dragged along by R2D2 and Lucas actually has him say `This is such a drag'. COME ON! Are we all 12? Is this supposed to entertain us? George, move aside and let someone else make a good movie. You can still put your fancy schmancy logo in front of it, but why don't you give something for the intelligent folks to enjoy too, other then stealing our money for yet a 3rd time. The only thing 'Phantom Menace' and 'Attack of the Clones' seems to be good at is giving 'A New Hope' that the next one will be better. But I'm alreay starting to lose that.

title: 1.5 hours of boring drivel (and then some decent stuff)
review:
Ok, I am not a perfectionist - I thought Episode I was pretty enjoyable. This movie bored me to death. The first 1.5 hours is awful, Hayden as Annakin is awful, and the political plots are very difficult to follow - and I am a sci fi fan.

Overall, I was very disappointed..and I had low expectations.

5 of 10

title: Very nice effects but boring lovestory and dialogs
review: I am not big fun of SW serial but original films was for me very good and interesting. In Episode1 there was too many childish stuff and in Episode2 there is too many love stuff. Love is important for story but i didn't like how it was showed. The dialogs and some parts are like Mexican lovestory serials :(

title: Movie made for Star Wars Fans
review: While you see a lot of mixed reviews on the movie, we must not forget that this movie is made for star wars fan not the critics.  Thus if you are a fan you will enjoy it.  The effects and action are at its best and while we see very poor acting for Hayden Christianson, Natalie Portman and Ewen Mcgregor light up the screen.  What is also great about this movie is the links between this and the original trilogy. All together great film, minus Anakin Skywalker who needs up a bit more education on acting, as he lacks in his abilities to make us believe he is the next darth vader, as well he has no on screen chemistry with Natalie Portman.

title: The force is strong with this one...
review:
An amazing acheivement.

After the disappointment of The Phantom Menace, I really wasn't holding out much hope for this film. Thankfully, it exceeded my expectations and then some...

Even though you know how this story will conclude, you're still on the edge of your seat as the action unfolds. There are also some clever references to the original trilogy, at one point Obi-Wan tells Anakin "You'll be the death of me...". The characters are also slightly more developed than in the first prequel. Hayden Christensen does a good job as Anakin Skywalker, we don't know whether to cheer him or jeer him.

Then there's Yoda. Do not mess with the little dude...enough said.

In terms of spectacle, this takes the saga to new heights. In terms of story and drama however, it still cannot match The Empire Strikes Back.

Roll on 2005.

title: One Word, One Name....... YODA
review:
This was a class movie, really! I wasn't too impressed with the 'sound of music' Scenes. Although the film is basically set around Anakin Skywalkers quest of knowledge, I still felt he dominated the movie, leaving not much screentime for favourites such as Mace Windu, Jar Jar Binks (I'll get back to him later) and the almighty Yoda! He must only be in it for less than 30 mins altogether he has a cracking scene involving himself and Count Dooku, I wont give away what happens you'll have to see with your own eyes to believe it, after this scene I really think that Yoda must win best supporting actor in next years Oscars! Jar Jar Binks was really left out of this movie, he wasn't as mental as the previous movie, why does everyone keep dissin' him.

REAL QUALITY!!!

title: Why does Lucas try to direct??
review:
I'm sorry but I'm gonna have to say that this film is nothing more than average to poor! To be perfectly honest, this film would have received an even worse rating than the 5 I gave it if it wasn't part of the Starwars legend!

So, what are is my problem with Attack of the Clones? Firstly, the direction leaves a lot to be desired. Lucas chose to step back from directing the Empire Strikes Back and Return Of The Jedi and his attempts at directing Episode II should be considered a major mistake. I accept that Lucas obviously knows the most about the entire Starwars legend, but this hands on control only means that he is attempting to include too much detail that often makes the film drag. The laughable attempt at a love story is only topped in sheer badness (is that a word?) by the awful acting of the teenage Anakin - wooden is not the word!

The lack of set pieces also leaves the viewer with a bad taste in their collective mouths as the ending doesn't deliver the breath-taking climax that is considered a vital part of the starwars formula. Can you honestly say that the ending battle delivers anywhere near the action levels of any of the 4 films made before this?? Yoda revealing his powers is cool, but not nearly long enough.

I'm not a starwars boffin, but I do love the films. I rate the Phantom Menace as a better film than this and I can't say how disappointed I am. Sorry, but I just can't believe how average this film is...I'm still hoping for the dark third installment that has been promised - please let someone else direct it!

title: Hit or Miss...
review: I went to see this movie the first day it opened, the first showing as a matter of fact.. The theater was almost full, but not as full as it was when I saw Spider-Man on the first show of the first day.. I liked the movie quite a bit, as I am a fan of Star Wars.. I true fan must like it.. But it was missing something, mostly people.. See when they made episode one, most of the characters, and things around them were real, with CGI (computer generated images) over some of the make up and costumes, to make things look more real. But I found in this movie that even Yoda was 100% a CGI... And in most shots when you would think there should have been a stunt man or at least a human on blue screen, they just made the whole person a CGI.. And you could tell.. Some of the CGI's in this movie looked like an old 3DO game.. It was easy to tell that most of the actors had done complete scenes, (and most of the scenes this way) with a blue screen not knowing what was going to be put behind them later.. I thought the casting job was done well, I was glad to see they didn't try something stupid like casting big names for people such as Anakin Skywalker.. I did like his character, and the attitude they placed with him.. Other than the lack of non computer use, the movie was done to set up the next one in the series.. The clone wars has to be in the next movie, because it was not in this one.. Ok Here it is.. Ten years later, things have changed, so much in fact an hour of the movie sets up to explain everything.. After that, we see Anakin and Padmé, sort of fall in love.. I would say the movie starts with a beginning, beginning, beginning, middle, middle, and then we finally see some Jedi Fighting, and then the credits.. No one wins, in fact I would say the bad guys win in a way.. Nothing like the last movie, that movie started and then we saw fighting, and we were taken from there, one thing happened after another, until in the end we are at piece, everything worked out, there was a plot, beginning, middle and end.. Episode 2 doesn't have any of that.. Though we get to see Yoda in action for the first time!! This movie will be a great movie when the next one comes out, until than, it will just p**s you off to see it, because you will want to know what will be next!!!! I almost want to go see it again, just to see if more happens the next time around.. I give it 5 out of 10 stars.. Hit, or Miss..

title: When will balance be restored to the Force?
review:
After watching George Lucas' latest opus I am still questioning why I wasn't impressed. The major consensus between other people who have seen the film is that it is better than the disappointing Phantom Menace. Well to quote Master Yoda "Better it may be, but good it is not."

This venture out is a sweeping adventure, filled with amazing 3D computer generated environments populated with 2D characters. The eye candy in this piece is endless but when the characters open their mouths the dialogue feels flat & wooden. As a viewer I couldn't connect with them as the words spoken lacked conviction & failed to ring true with any emotional resonance.

The spectacle of the story may be laid out with schemes piled upon schemes, but it all feels like a poorly written elementary school history play. The original trilogy storyline seemed more straight forward and easier to navigate.

There were several moments where the film seemed poised to break through and present us with complex emotional scenes, but each time they fell drastically short. A spoiler free example is Anakin's scene with Shmi. It begins well but seems to end with an unintentional & uncomfortable audience laugh. Again what should have been an emotional scene seems cold.

The true breakthrough character of the film is Yoda. Moving from a static character to a dynamic CGI creation, it is now evident why everyone refers to him as a THE Jedi Master. Ewan McGregor also injects much needed life into Obi Wan Kenobi, and when it's shown it's like a glass of water on Tatooine.

Outside of the great finale & visual amazement, ATOC is still hollow at the center. I was hoping for more of a meal and less of a dessert, but with 2 down and 1 to go I won't keep my hopes up.

title: gud movie, but not as good as phantom menace
review: Before watching this movie at the theatres, i had expected it to be a moderately gud movie.  At first sight the 'cover art' remained illustrative to keep consistent with the previous movies, which i thought was best despite the age we are in with modern photography. The film started out well, but i began to have doubts as the movie progressed for numerous reasons.  I thought the acting of Anakin Skywalker by Hayden Christensen was poor, and the performace of Obi-Wan Kenobi by Ewan McGregor wasnt as consistent as it was in the Phantom Menace.  Especially in the emotional scenes, Anakins acting suffers a great deal due to lack of facial expressions and carisma.  Even when his mum dies, you can tell the fake mourning blatently. The love scenes between Anakin and Padme didnt contain any depth, again due to Anakins poor acting (Natalie Portman as Padme was passable, but again not as gud as in Phantom menace).  Obi-Wan was a much stronger character in the phantom menace, and he looses much of his acting quality due to keeping a still face for most of the movie.  I thought the young Anakin in the phantom menace was a much better actor than the older one in Attack of the clones because of convincing acting.  I thought another downfall of the movie was the dialogue, and corny jokes.  A better dialogue delivery i think was in the older versions of star wars. The soundtrack however was good, as it captured the essence of the movie which was based on love more than anything else. One thing i didnt like in the phantom menace, was the 'over-doing' of special effects, which i think was solved in this episode.  it was moderate and kept realistic, although the jedi masters gliding in the air was abit daft.  Overall a good movie, but not as gud as the phantom menace.

title: Fantastic ! Going to see it again !
review:
Just come back from the 11.45 pm showing of Episode II. When can I get my ticket for the next showing. The film was really good.

Characters were very funny, especially C3PO. Minimal amounts of Jar Jar Binks made a big difference ..... I think they got the hint from Episode I that he isn't liked.

Brilliant effects and fighting, this film had much more of a Star Wars feel than the last.

That Anakin bloke has a lot of issues ..... I feel that he could turn out to be a baddie in later films ! ;o)

title: Finally back up to par
review: I was very pleased with the new Star Wars movie.  While I didn't hate episode one it was extremely disappointing for me.  Attack of the clones finally kicks it back into gear.  I especially enjoyed the humor and the tie ins to the original three.

title: Decent film, but Lucas can't write or direct!
review:
Enjoyed the film immensely - well almost.

Story progresses well enough...bit of the Dark Side...bit of The Force, but George, for Chrissakes, leave the directing to someone else! Some of the scenes are woefully long and some are woefully short...the audience knows what's going on - we can work out the story for ourselves(it's not written by David Mamet!)...and, here comes the put down, we're not ALL American!

It would have been nice to have a little more original music as well. It's acceptable to have the main theme played, but the music from Episode 1 shouldn't have come back...it's fairly poor to begin with.

Grievances aside, it is still a very good film...let's just be thankful that there was a lot of story to progress from Episode 1!

And to everyone who moans about the acting, it's fine...this is still a sci-fi film after all...we don't expect to see the proper acting skills of an Alec Guinness for example...oops!

Hope to see more Yoda fighting in the next one.

title: It was okay, but somewhat disappointing
review: As a kid, I was a huge "Star Wars" fan and was thoroughly looking for to seeing "Attack of the Clones."  That said, after seeing the movie, I can honestly say I was somewhat disappointed.  While the movie was an improvement over "Phantom of Menace," as a film overall, it was not very enjoyable.  This latest chapter seemed to focus more on a set up for the original trilogy, rather than telling a story.  The romance between Amidala and Anikan seemed force, and Obi-Wan was made to look like a nagging shrew, harping on Anikan's every fault.  No doubt the movie will make tons of money and the truly devout "Star Wars" fans will see it over and over.  But for the general movie going public, here's my review- it okay, but somewhat disappointing.

title: Luckily no Jar-Jar and kiddie-ani, but still 3D galore and low on characters
review:
3D animation has taken quantum leaps the last few years and this film knows to use it. Not only background and starfighters are smooth and realistic, but fighting monsters and flabby bartenders are created with believability.

However, although technically superior, Lucas still suffers from the "kid in a candyshop" when it comes to animation. With no limits to what he can put on the silver screen, he *still* forgets what made the original films not only success, but cult - personality! The characters are as stereotypical and predictable as in PM, and the "scruffiness" of A New Hope has gone forever.

In my bantering, which is much a lingering grumble from the disappointment of Phantom Menace, I must say I was pleasantly surprised. Natalie Portman is sNackaLiCIOus (and also made a convincing performance with much more life than in PM). McGregor actually portrayed a young Sir Guinness well, but Christensen lacked the keenness one would expect from the great Jedi Skywalker. The film held good suspense, even better effects than the first and without spoiling too much, a scene with the venerable Yoda in the end which will surely go into history! One could also see much more progress towards the forming of the empire in the story, and the end makes you very keen on the third film.

All in all, good entertainment, and even though bereft of the edge that would push it to the top, fans will be pleased and most moviegoers will have a good time too.

title: It feels sooo good!!
review:
Well, it feels good to finally see the plot getting thicker and better. Episode 1 had left me hungry. This one makes me want to see the next one right now!! Yes, there is lot of battles and a lot of digital effects, however they never get annoying. The critics are complaining about dialogues. When it's moving and happening on the screen, how much more do you need to understand the story? Lucas never pretended he was reinventing the wheel of story telling.

Die-hard fans are criticising that some of the elements are not following the true spirit of the saga... Can anyone just watch the story and enjoy? Can Lucas just tell a story his own way?? I never called my favourite writer to tell him what to do about his next novel, what would be the point of reading it then? What would be creative?

It was a very enjoyable experience, make my eyesight and my imagination happy. The imagery was beautiful, the music magical, the characters convincing, especially Yoda and it really made the story go on a forward leap. Enjoy the ride!!

title: Great Film---Bad Dialogue
review:
The special effects were incredible. Personally, I think that the digital format is not very flattering to the actors and the make-up artists should have adapted to the medium. The story was good and the action was rather intense.

However, the love scenes were atrocious. Through no fault of Portman or Christensen, the love scenes were about the funniest parts of the movie. The script made 90210 look like Oscar winning dialogue. Please don't let Lucas write the dialogue or direct the next one! Anakin comes off whinier than Luke did, and that's saying a lot. McGregor, Jackson and Christopher Lee all give great performances, but with all of the time devoted to showing off the computerized special effects there's not much heart in this movie. The film certainly could have used some Harrison Ford and Carrie Fisher charisma and charm.

title: Nothing here for anyone but the die-hard fan, and the kids.
review:
Frankly, the average viewer will walk away from this film wondering how such a high budget and highly anticipated film could be released with such pathetic dialogue. Because 'talk' makes up such a large part of this film (filling in plot lines, etc) the cliche and wooden performances are brought to the foreground, leaving the truly impressive stuff (CGI, action sequences) to wallow alone in the back. How is it possible to assemble such quality, skilled actors, and come away with such awful performances?

Kids won't notice all this of course, and Star Wars fans will certainly see this film as an improvement over "The Phantom Menace". Yet it is far, far away from capturing the magic of "A New Hope" and "Empire Strikes Back".

title: I gotta say, I'm relieved.
review:
I mean, I was really prepared for a root-canal of a movie. Prepared to grit my teeth through the whole thing. (Jar-Jar broke my heart. I know a lot of you can relate.)

But I had a great time at this movie. Samuel Jackson, Christopher Lee, and Ewan McGregor were all top-notch (and that's not just because I find Obi-Wan way yummier than young Anakin). That Natalie just keeps getting more beautiful. Stirring music, breathtaking vistas, a whole lot o' Jedi (including girls!! and kung fu!!), Boba Fett's dad, mythic tidbits a-plenty. And as has been stated numerous times on this database, Yoda does, in fact, rock.

I'm an incredibly picky and critical moviegoer, and the fact that I only have three negative things to say about this movie is really pretty amazing.

First, consistently distributed throughout the film, I felt manipulated by gamer-logic. The special effects were gorgeous, and most of the action scenes were really exciting, but I kept getting distracted by thoughts like "Oh, that'll be a tricky part in the video game".

Second, while I'm not prepared to say that Hayden Christensen is a bad actor, I thought that most of his scenes were not written in such as way as to allow him to play them well.

And third, I thought it was incredibly cruel to have the star-crossed lovers hanging around some of the most romantic landscapes ever put on film, and for Padme's costumes to just keep getting prettier. "No, no, our love is forbidden. Let me just make my hair a little more tousled and put on a gauzier outfit."

But if you're a Star Wars fan, I'm confident you'll have a great time here. This one got me thinkin' how much fun it's going to be when all six films are out and we can have 12-hour marathon viewings of the whole cycle. 'Cause it's the only great modern myth, after all.

title: This movie is absolutely incredible!!!!!!!
review:
This may contain SPOILERS SO STOP READING NOW IF YOU HAVE NOT SEEN THIS MOVIE.

I have been eagerly awaiting this movie for the longest time and I can honestly tell you that I am completely amazed by the quality of this movie. I have no idea how people that know anything about the Star Wars story could possibly have any complaint other than they have to wait 3 year before the next installment! First of all Hayden Christensen was the perfect choice for the role of Anakin, he played the part exactly the way that it is supposed to be. His perfect mixture of young jedi in training to the rage of the future Darth Vader was right on the money. Secondly the perception that the love scenes were akward could not be farther from the truth. This is exactly the way Mr. Lucas was trying to portray it, with both Anakin and Padme unsure that what they are doing is the right thing all the while fighting the true love that lies inside both of them.

I will not completely go into detail on the incredible light saber scenes as many people have done that already. None the less there were outstanding and yes yoda does kick ass!!!!!! Bring on episode 3. Overall rating 10/10

title: Better Than Phantom Menace But Not By Much
review:
While Attack of the Clones was not the unmitigated disaster that Phantom Menace was, it is a far cry from Star Wars or Empire Strikes Back.

What was good in the film: The final battle scene. Fabulous CG and an intelligent design. Ewan McGregor was better than in Phantom Menace, maybe he's warming to the part or they wrote it better. The sequences related to the cloning process and other manufacturing were great too. Both Jango and Boba Fett shone in small roles.

What was bad in the film: Hayden Christenson might be the worst actor I have ever seen. This character as 'portrayed' by Christenson has more in common with Scooby-Doo than with Darth Vader. I guess slack-jawed androgynous pretty-boys are all the rage since Leonardo DiCaprio was inflicted on us by Hollywood. Natalie Portman's outfits and hair. What does Lucas have against female hair. First, Princess Leia and now Natalie Portman. In one scene, she has hair that makes her look like Mickey Mouse in another she looks like she's wearing a snail on her head. The outfits she wears are ridiculous. In one she's got a bare midriff like some mallrat. In another, her nipples show through her formal dress. If she's going to be a princess and a senator at least let her dress like she has a little dignity. The CG where people and CG creations were on screen together were pretty bad. They looked close to some 1950s Ray Harryhausen Grade B monster movie.

Ethnic stereotyping: I never really understood why people got upset with Jar-Jar Binks. He was annoying but I really believed he was so in a non-discriminatory fashion. However, and columnist John Leo did mention this too, the character of Waddo is right out of anti-semitic stereotyping. Anyone who has ever been to a European art museum can recognize the saucer-shaped metal hat that Waddo wears as a hat that had to be worn by Jews in medieval Germany. When you combine that with his large nose, his small body and large abdomen, his funny accent and the fact that he is a cheating junk dealer, it is clear where Lucas got the idea for the character. Lucas prides himself on his knowledge of mythology and art.

All this being said, I guess I'm looking forward to the next movie.

title: The First PG-13 Star Wars Movie
review:
This movie is awesome!!!!!! I know this is rated PG movie-but damn! This movie was intense. I'm glad all the kiddie crap is gone from TPM and ROTJ. I have a message for all the critics who bash this movie-What the hell are you guys looking for? This is just a fun movie which will be loved by fans. Was Mark Hamill that great when he cried in ANH because he couldn't hang out with his friends. The acting in the OT was not very good. How many times does Leia say, " Let's get out of here" in ROTJ. IN ESB- the dialogue seems forced- "who's scruffy looking"or "A death mark is not an easy thing to live with". The dialogue in AOTC is no different than the previous films. Granted, I do feel ESB is the best of them all. I think critics blast this film because their not Star Wars fans. I swear these critics try to find something to rip because Star Wars is not artistic. I bet if SW consisted of avant -garde Clone-troopers or a gay anakin skywalker they'd like it. Most of them are too grown up to enjoy Star Wars. Last Night I felt like a little kid. That's what these movies are all about. SPOILER- When Jango got his head cut off by Mr. Jackson I got so excited. Man-That was cool!!! Hint go into these movies with the mind set of a 12 year old- You'll love it.

Go into this movie trying to find something wrong with it- you will. This is my second favorite SW movie behind ESB. Note- THIS IS NOT A MOVIE FOR YOUNG KIDS. THERE ARE NO STUPID CHARACTERS OR STUPID HUMOR. 8.6/10- Great Movie

title: Best since Empire Strikes Back
review:
First off I would just like to say that for all the fans who didn't like this film you must be really picky and full of negativity. But its not my place to tell you to like this film. This is the way that George Lucas has made these movies so full of special effects using the latest in technology to do so. This is how Star Wars should be!

Alrighty on to my review (SPOILERS)

I loved every minute of it the acting was great the Love story was a bit corny but other then that George hit the nail on the head with this one! The speeder chase kept me on the edge of my seat and Jango Fett what can I say he really shows us what a Bounty Hunter is suppost to be.

Plus the lines were well delivered I especially liked Obi Wan's comment to Anakin "You'll Be the Death of Me" and other line "Where are you going? To get a Drink" that was great.

The Yoda/Dooku Duel this what I have been waiting for along time now. Christopher Lee really delivered in his performance as Count Dooku all I have to say about him is that's exactly what a Sith should be like.

Overall I give this film 10/10 it really delivered and yet it had enough twists to keep me begging for more. Great Job Mr. Lucas can't wait till 2005 and Episode III.

title: Lucas Again Conjures the Magic
review:
Crouching Yoda, Hidden Sith Lord could well describe Attack of the Clones. Whether conscious or not, the references to other films are several in George Lucas's latest Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones ... and it all works brilliantly. Fans of Star Wars truly have a feast before them with this latest installment of the series. Visually stunning, and chock-o-block full of action sequences that flow logically as the story progesses into a crescendo until the satisfying climax, Attack of the Clones is as good as the original Star Wars: A New Hope and The Empire Strikes Back - in fact it is like a mix of the two, with the thrills of the former and the more adult dark tones of the latter.

There are moments of the film that feel like Predator, Bladerunner, North by Northwest, 007 (any number of the Bond films), and even Lord of the Rings - and all in the best sense of homage, for these references seem effortless, as if they infused the work rather than were the basis of the particular scenes which evoke these earlier films. Lucas is at the top of his game here, and the CGI work is the best yet, and Lucas moves his camera almost constantly - taking a page from Peter Jackson. Certain vistas are works of art, and the detail and texture now possible is simply stunning - a testament to Lucas's vision and to the technology.

For those who thought the magic they felt upon the release of the original Star Wars back in 1977 would never be recaptured, I have news for you - Lucas has made lightning strike again. You will see this movie more than once.

title: Lucas Strikes Back
review: I wasn't expecting anything from Star Wars after Phantom Menace. However Lucas did a god job with attack of the Clones. The movie is definetly darker than EpisodeI . Although Haygen wasn't a good choice as Anakin Skywalker the movie was still watchable .The cinematography was amazing for Star Wars . The fight scenes were original and the plot was solid . And Yoda Ruled :))

title: Truly Amazing on so many different levels (EVEN AFTER 5 TIMES of Watching..hehehehe)
review: This film is absolutely brilliant. Whether you like Star wars or not....it doesn't matter. This film is undeniably great, not just visually but acting wise. As a Brit Ewan McGregor is fantastic, he holds the screen well and how Liam Neeson did in The Phantom Menace he pulls off being the wise Jedi very well. Obi-Wan is essential to the plot as we all should know what is going to happen but Lucas keeps us guessing how it happens. Ewan McGregor especially as he seems so strong but has this degree of humanity that when watching, the viewer can really relate to. Episode IV to VI were so brilliant because of Han Solo keeping the comic element there....were episode 1 failed is to re-create a character of comedy....they tried with Jar Jar Binks and it did work to a degree but Han Solo was really arrogant and that made him appealing..as his comic relief was essential for the whole series. In Attack of the Clones (AOTC) Hayden Christensen amazes me as his acting ability is fantastic not only does he portray Anakin as strong and arrogant but his facial expressions are fantastic and change the whole tone of the movie.....he really shows that inside Anakin is a boy who just needs to get out so he can be a man. Christensen shows this brilliant and comes across very evil at times and really keeps the viewer enthralled as he allows everyone to see how he is slowly becoming seduced by the dark side. Anakin and Obi-Wan make this film amazing to watch and u can really relate to everything that goes on. Christopher Lee in a role much like his role in Lord of The Rings is a very good bad guy and is very arrogant. He really does give Obi-wan a nemesis.....Anakin is not only battling with his feelings with the Dark Side but with Padmé...on paper a love story doesn't really fit at all into the story because Star wars seems like a guy thing...just loads of action....but how wrong we could be. Lucas doesn't over do it....but emphasises on the natural feeling between the two...and Christensen really does show how versatile he is, as an actor....the chemistry between him and Portman make the film very interesting....and like I said before abt the need for relief from an all action plot...it is a nice diversion. If you see this film you have to see it for Yoda....as Yoda is absolutely brilliant at the end....tt final scene towards the end will be remembered form years to come...as 25 years of waiting to see what Yoda can actually do is finally seen. In conclusion to this epic adventure.....Lucas stays close to the story and fuses together the fundamental key characteristics of what made Star Wars, Star Wars....he substitutes Anakins arrogance for Han Solo's comic relief....but tt alone is not enough....so he uses the diversion of a love story to ease the whole action. At the same time he runs sub-plots into the film...introducing new ideas and although the eventual ending is already known....u never quite noe where the film is going to go next. This is what George Lucas has done amazingly....Im not a person who goes to see films over and over again...but films I truly respect and love for what they do critically should be watched and watched over and over again. Star Wars and LOTR come under tt category.....but AOTC has met the hype of the two new films together....it is a joy to watch...its only friday and I have seen it 5 times.....its not sad....if you see it...you can see no matter how perceptive u r to wot is going on, on screen u always pick up on sub-plots.....and Lucas has wrote this script like a book because its so unpredictable....Jango's character should return as tt is one of the minor details tt u can only pick up on if u see this film again and again...I suggest to any1 who has seen it, to see it again even if they do not like it....give urself a chance to see how great this film is...and how it works on the five levels a film should, Sociological, philosophical, Religious, psychological and suspense...the fact AOTC is such a big budget picture and it can do this is truly amazing......if u see one film this summer see this film. Get down to the nearest theatre that shows it digitally...becasue if you see it digitally...u will just simply look in ore...of the amazing effects....in the end....ull get your money's worth even if you don't like Star Wars...its a brilliant romance...its not a Pearl Harbour romance...it has depth to it....watch it twice...because if you dunt....it will plague ur mind.

title: A good piece of heroic s-f
review:
I find the movie very good. Actually, out of episodes I, IV, V and VI, I find it the best one - it has everything the previous episodes had, but more focus on character development than on action.

Everything about special effects and battles have already been said, so I'll focus on characters and their personalities. The most controversive point is Anakin+Padme romance. People yell that it is too much focused on, getting too much on-screen time. Indeed, some parts were too heavy with Anakin's speeches, but it was probably because their relationship got TOO LITTLE time and it had to be rushed to make it tragic enough (and they had to insert certain amount of words into limited amount of time, so it turned out to be a bit too much of "Gone with the Wind" or "Titanic" style). So, if you're looking for Leia+Solo styled, crazy Jones-like or Bond-like romance, you probably won't enjoy this movie (or this part of it) - as the love story follows the "doomed lovers" style, not an cute little adventure love story.

I liked also the way Obi-Wan Kenobi was portrayed. I won't go into details as not to spoil the plot, but we have portrayed both - the generation-conflict and Anakin's feelings to him in a father-to-son-like manner. Still, I think Ewan McGregor had some problems with playing serious parts of the movie. He's good when he fights, he's good when he's mean, but when he's just to be serious and adult, he seems somehow stiff.

And, of course, Yoda is wonderful! He makes the Yoda from Original Trilogy look pale and outdated. He gets a lot of onscreen time.

Generally, I'm looking forward to seeing Ep.3 - I hope they'll manage to make an ending fulfilling the expectations created by this movie.

title: When is the last time you cheered?
review:

Is the romantic dialogue the worst game spat ever, maybe? Does the need to explain every character and plot foundation in episodes 4-6 a little tiresome by the end? Yes. Is Jar Jar Binks the anti-christ? You know the answer. But

When is the last time you jumped to your feet in a theater packed with strangers to cheer the sword fighting skills of a muppet? When is the last time a charecter saying "I killed them all...the women the children all of them..." didn't indicate a predictable heavy and actually scared you.

When is the last time a leading lady kicked as much ass as Portman and still retained such a quiet grace? When is the last time you felt 12 years old, jabbering to your friends about a film so amazing yet familer that you jumped right back in line to see it again.

This is the type of film a sequel should be. Shallow, predictable, and ultimately fun.

title: WOW.
review: I bought tickets to see Episode II at 12:01 AM and 9:30 PM, and my first thought when the film finished the first time was, "I have to wait 18 hours to see it again?!".  I LOVED this movie.  A huge SW fan since age 5, I was holding back tears as the opening theme began.  From that moment, my eyes didn't leave the screen (except for a few moments when I covered them in fear).  It seems like the "cool" trend among "real" fans is to point out as many flaws as possible, such as the movie's admittedly unremarkable dialogue, but you know what?  If loving AOTC makes me less of a fan, so be it.  The film is AMAZING.  There are at least half a dozen visually unparalleled scenes.  The plot blends just the right amount of adventure and intensity with subtle (or not-so-subtle) foreshadowing of episodes 4-6, and leaves the viewer drooling with anticipation for Episode III.  AOTC was everything I wanted it to be and more.  The Force is with us again!  I love you, George Lucas!

title: It's missing that intangible "something" that makes a great movie
review:
The story of Star Wars (episode 4) just blew me away when I first watched the movie at age 12. The subsequent movies did not disappoint. When Episode 1 came along 3 years ago I liked it while most people seemed to dislike it. I tried not to have expectations going into this showing at 8 am this morning. But, 1/2 hour into the movie I could just feel that it was missing something.

LOTR had that magic in a major way. Episode 2 misses the bulls-eye by a wide mark.

Despite the action in the beginning the movie still seems to plod along. The last 1/2 hour speeds up considerably and it is visually overwhelming.

The dialogue is as bad as the other reviews suggest. Especially, the dialogue between Anakin and Amidala. It is just horrid. The entire "courtship" is unreal. There is no chemistry. All I can figure is that this is a perfect example of why love is blind. And, the looks that Anakin gives Amidala border on creepy and she says so. Why would any woman, especially one that shows the compassion and intelligence that Amidala shows here, end up with a guy like Anakin? If there had been at least a little bit of on-screen chemistry it would have been easier to believe.

The visual are stunning. I'm sure I missed a lot of the details.

The light saber fights were great. It was also fun to finally see the other Jedi. Getting to see Yoda move and interact with other people was fun.

The light humor that R2D2 and C-3PO display are just hilarious. They have not lost their touch.

Despite my negativity toward the acting/dialogue (I know it is one of the trademarks of the Star Wars franchise) I still enjoyed watching the story unfold. I will watch this movie again and pray that George gets the magic back for the final installment.
